完全不说话，面试官只能自己盯代码猜，评估窗口基本消失。
optionExplanations_en: Announcing after every few keystrokes buries the signal in typing noise, the interviewer loses the point.
Right — about every 30 to 60 seconds is a practical rhythm that doesn't interrupt flow or go dark.
Summarizing only once everything is written means the interviewer's context arrives far too late.
Saying nothing at all leaves the interviewer guessing from the code alone — the evaluation window is gone.

q: 编码过程中，哪些时刻最值得主动说出来？（多选）
q_en: During coding, which moments are most worth saying out loud? (Select all that apply.)
options: AI 输出和你的预期不一致
每次输入一个标点符号
准备开始实现下一个功能步骤
发现需要改变算法或数据结构
why: 面试官关心决策、偏差和修正，而不是机械的输入细节。
why_en: The interviewer needs decisions, mismatches, and corrections, not keystroke-level commentary.
options_en: The AI's output doesn't match what you expected.
Every time you type a single punctuation mark.
You're about to start the next implementation step.
You realize the algorithm or data structure needs to change.
optionExplanations: 输出跟预期对不上时说出来，能让面试官看到你在核对结果，不是照单全收。
标点级别的播报没有决策信息，纯粹占用本该讲判断的时间。
开始下一步前说一声，面试官提前知道方向，跟得上你的节奏。
算法或结构要变时说清楚，能让面试官看到这是主动调整而非乱改。
optionExplanations_en: Flagging a mismatch between output and expectation shows you're checking results, not accepting them blind.
Punctuation-level narration carries zero decision value, it just eats time you could spend on judgment.
Announcing the next step before you start it keeps the interviewer ahead of your pace.
Naming an algorithm or structure change shows a deliberate adjustment, not a random edit.

scenario: 你需要安静想十几秒，确认当前算法能否覆盖边界情况。
scenario_en: You need to think quietly for ten or so seconds to confirm whether the current algorithm covers edge cases.
q: 这时最合适的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle this moment?
options: 直接沉默不说话，让面试官自己去猜你在干嘛
还没想清楚就立刻让 AI 生成新方案
说一句“想一下这个边界情况”，再停顿
跳过边界情况不想，直接往下写代码
why: 一句框定语能把沉默变成可理解的思考时间，避免面试官误以为你卡住或走神。
why_en: A short framing sentence turns silence into an understandable thinking pause instead of ambiguous dead air.
whenOtherWins: 如果你已经有可运行测试，可以边说边跑测试，用结果帮助思考。
options_en: Go completely silent and let the interviewer guess what you're doing.
Have the AI generate a new approach before you've even thought it through.
Say 'let me think about this edge case' and pause briefly.
Skip the edge case without thinking about it and just keep writing.
tradeoff: 一句框定语再沉默 vs 直接沉默不说明
optionExplanations: 完全沉默，面试官分不清你是在想、卡住了还是走神了。
还没想明白就让 AI 重新生成，容易在没想清楚的情况下越改越乱。
对，一句框定语几乎零成本，就能把沉默变成看得懂的思考停顿。
直接跳过边界情况不想，等于把风险留到后面才爆出来。
optionExplanations_en: Going fully silent leaves the interviewer unable to tell if you're thinking, stuck, or distracted.
Regenerating before you've actually thought it through risks making the mess worse, not better.
Right — one framing sentence costs almost nothing and turns silence into a legible thinking pause.
Skipping the edge case without thinking about it just pushes the risk further down the line.

scenario: 你要让 AI 实现搜索函数，需要让面试官清楚你选的是 BFS，而不是把决策交给 AI。
scenario_en: You want the AI to implement a search function, and the interviewer needs to know you chose BFS rather than handing the decision to the AI.
q: 哪组“口头说明 + 提示”最能体现你在主导决策？
q_en: Which pair of spoken framing and prompt best shows that you are driving the decision?
options: 说明：我先看看 AI 会怎么处理这道题。提示：“solve this”
说明：用 BFS 找最短路径。提示：在 Grid 实现 BFS 返回坐标路径。
说明：不说明。提示：“make it work”
说明：AI 应该知道怎么做。提示：“写一个复杂的解法”
why: 先公开你的策略，再把同一策略写进提示，能让 AI 输出贴合方案，同时向面试官展示你在做决策。
why_en: State your strategy out loud and put the same strategy in the prompt so the AI executes your decision, not its own.
whenOtherWins: 如果算法选择还没确定，可以先说明你在比较 BFS、DFS 或 Dijkstra，再决定后提示。
options_en: Framing: let's see what the AI does with it. Prompt: 'solve this.'
Framing: I'll use BFS for the shortest path. Prompt: implement BFS on Grid, return the coordinate path.
Framing: none. Prompt: 'make it work.'
Framing: the AI should already know. Prompt: 'write a complex solution.'
tradeoff: 先说策略再写进提示 vs 不说明直接丢给 AI 决定

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层从起点向外扩展，用于无权图找最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, explores a graph layer by layer from the start node and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 深度优先搜索，沿一条路径尽量往前探索，走到底再回溯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DFS, Depth-First Search, explores as far as possible along one path before backtracking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理带权图最短路径的经典算法，每次扩展当前已知代价最小的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's Algorithm finds shortest paths in a weighted graph by always expanding the lowest-known-cost node next.

optionExplanations: 只说“看看 AI 怎么处理”再丢一句空提示，算法选择权全交给了 AI。
对，先口头点名 BFS，再把同一约束写进提示，AI 输出直接落在你的方案上。
完全不说明、只给一句“make it work”，AI 可能选出你答不上来的方案。
“AI 应该知道”加一句模糊提示，等于没有给出任何可执行的约束。
optionExplanations_en: Just saying 'let's see what the AI does' plus an empty prompt hands the algorithm choice to the AI entirely.
Right — naming BFS out loud, then encoding the same constraint in the prompt, keeps the AI's output on your plan.
Giving no framing and only 'make it work' risks the AI picking an approach you can't defend.
'The AI should already know' plus a vague prompt gives it nothing executable to build from.

q: 事后解释你刚让 AI 做了什么，为什么弱于提示前先说明？
q_en: Why is explaining what you just asked the AI to do weaker than stating it before prompting?
options: 事后解释会让 AI 生成变慢
事后解释在大多数面试规则里是被禁止的
两者对面试官来说完全一样
事前说明让面试官实时看到计划，而不是事后倒推
why: 面试评估的是过程控制；事前说明能让你的意图在行动发生的同时就被看到。
why_en: Interviews evaluate process control, and explaining before you act makes your intent visible in real time.
options_en: Explaining after the fact makes the AI generate more slowly.
Explaining after the fact is against the rules in most interviews.
The two approaches are exactly the same to the interviewer.
Explaining beforehand lets the interviewer see your plan in real time, instead of reconstructing it afterward.
optionExplanations: 叙述时机跟 AI 生成速度是两回事，两者之间没有因果关系。
大多数面试其实允许事后解释，只是信号强度更弱，不是被禁止。
时机差异正是这题的关键，先说和后说对面试官的可读性完全不同。
对，事前说明能让面试官在动作发生的同时就看到你的计划，不用事后靠猜。
optionExplanations_en: Narration timing and AI generation speed are unrelated, there's no causal link there.
Most interviews actually allow after-the-fact explanation, it's just a weaker signal, not a rule violation.
The timing gap is exactly the point here — before and after read very differently to the interviewer.
Right — explaining beforehand lets the interviewer watch your plan unfold live instead of reconstructing it later.

scenario: AI 一次性输出了一大段代码，你还没有读完确认。
scenario_en: The AI produced a large block of code all at once, and you have not finished reviewing it.
q: 这时最好的口头反馈是什么？
q_en: What is the best spoken response here?
options: “应该可以，继续下一步。”
“我不需要看，直接用。”
“这段挺长，我先读一遍确认它符合计划。”
“面试官你帮我读一下吧。”
why: 承认需要审阅是好信号，说明你不会因为代码看起来完整就直接接受。
why_en: Saying you need to review a large output shows you won't accept complete-looking code blindly.
whenOtherWins: 如果输出只是一行你能立刻确认的改动，可以快速说明确认点后继续。
options_en: 'Looks fine, let's move on.'
'I don't need to look, I'll just use it.'
'This is a lot, let me read through it to confirm it matches the plan.'
'Can you read through this for me instead?'
tradeoff: 承认需要审阅 vs 假设输出直接可信
optionExplanations: “应该可以”是没核实过的猜测，面试官会当成你在盲目接受输出。
完全不看直接用，风险等到后面测试或追问时才会暴露出来。
对，主动说要先读一遍再判断，把审阅习惯摆在明面上给面试官看。
把审阅甩给面试官，本该是候选人自己的职责，显得缺乏主导。
optionExplanations_en: 'Should be fine' is an unverified guess, it reads as accepting the output blindly.
Skipping the read entirely just delays the risk until testing or a follow-up question exposes it.
Right — saying you'll read it first before continuing puts your review habit on full display.
Handing review to the interviewer is your job to begin with, it makes you look less in control.

q: 补全沟通节奏的练习方法：
q_en: Complete the practice method for building communication rhythm:
text: 用 AI 解题时录下自己，回看哪里{{沉默太久}}、哪里{{过度叙述}}，几次练习后会形成自然节奏。
why: 沟通节奏很难只靠阅读形成，录像回放能立刻暴露盲点。
why_en: Recording practice sessions exposes long silences and over-narration so you can tune your rhythm.

q: 编码过程中，哪句话属于过度叙述而非有用沟通？
q_en: During coding, which sentence is over-narration rather than useful communication?
options: “我现在要输入 function 这个单词。”
“我接下来实现 search 函数。”
“这段输出用了错误的错误处理风格，我会重提示。”
“我需要想一下这个边界情况。”
why: 有用沟通聚焦决策和状态，机械播报键盘动作只会消耗时间和注意力。
why_en: Useful narration covers decisions and state, while keystroke-level commentary just wastes time and attention.
options_en: 'I'm about to type the word function now.'
'I'm going to implement the search function next.'
'This output uses the wrong error-handling style, I'll reprompt it.'
'I need to think about this edge case for a second.'
tradeoff: 播报决策和状态 vs 播报键盘动作
optionExplanations: 对，播报到具体单词级别没有任何判断信息，纯粹是键盘动作的噪音。
宣布下一步要实现什么，是决策级信息，值得说，不算过度叙述。
指出风格冲突并打算重提示，是主动纠偏的证据，同样值得说。
提前说一句要想边界情况，把停顿变得可理解，也不算过度。
optionExplanations_en: Right — narrating down to a single word carries zero judgment, it's pure keystroke noise.
Announcing the next thing you'll implement is decision-level information, worth saying, not over-narration.
Flagging a style conflict and planning to reprompt is proof of self-correction, also worth saying.
A quick heads-up before thinking through an edge case makes the pause legible, not excessive.

q: 出问题时，哪些沟通动作能把局面拉回可评估状态？（多选）
q_en: When something goes wrong, which communication moves bring the situation back into an evaluable state? (Select all that apply.)
options: 说明当前错误或阻塞点
给出你对根因的判断
解释为什么要改变方向
静默删除大量代码，不作说明
why: 问题本身不可怕，可怕的是面试官看不到你如何诊断和调整。
why_en: When things go wrong, visible diagnosis and explicit adjustment matter more than hiding the struggle.
options_en: Name the current error or blocker.
State your judgment about the root cause.
Explain why you're changing direction.
Silently delete a large chunk of code without explanation.
optionExplanations: 把卡点具体说出来，是让面试官重新跟上进度的第一步。
给出根因判断，把“出问题了”升级成“我知道为什么”，可评估。
解释转向的理由，能把主动调整和随意乱改区分开来。
静默删除一大块代码不说明，面试官只看到混乱，判断不出你的依据。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the blocker concretely is the first step to getting the interviewer back up to speed.
Stating your root-cause judgment upgrades 'something's wrong' into something evaluable.
Explaining the reason for a pivot separates a deliberate adjustment from a random rewrite.
Silently deleting a big chunk of code with no explanation just looks like chaos to the interviewer.

scenario: 面试官已经看过很多候选人做同一道题，熟悉常见的死路在哪里。
scenario_en: The interviewer has seen many candidates solve this same problem and knows the common dead ends.
q: 你走进死路时，最应该向面试官展示什么？
q_en: When you hit a dead end, what should you most show the interviewer?
options: 永远不承认自己走错方向
继续微调错误方向直到时间用完
把责任推给 AI 的建议
尽快识别死路、说明原因并干净转向
why: 面试官不指望你避开所有死路，但会评估你发现和恢复的速度。
why_en: Interviewers don't expect you to avoid every dead end, but they do evaluate how fast you notice and recover.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是实现细节的小错，先局部修正即可；只有方向性错误才需要明确转向。
options_en: Never admit you went the wrong way.
Keep tweaking the wrong direction until time runs out.
Blame the AI's suggestion for the wrong turn.
Recognize the dead end quickly, explain why, and pivot cleanly.
tradeoff: 快速识别并转向 vs 硬撑原方向到超时
optionExplanations: 死不承认走错方向，面试官很快就能看穿，可信度反而更受损。
在错误方向上死磕到超时，是时间耗尽还没有可用方案的最差结果。
把方向判断甩给 AI 建议，决策权始终在你手里，这个借口站不住。
对，尽快认出死路、讲清原因、干净转向，正是面试官在评估的恢复速度。
optionExplanations_en: Refusing to admit a wrong turn gets seen through fast, and it costs you credibility instead of saving it.
Grinding on a broken direction until time's up is one of the worst outcomes: no usable solution left.
Blaming the AI's suggestion doesn't hold up, the decision was always yours to make.
Right — recognizing the dead end fast, explaining why, and pivoting cleanly is exactly what gets evaluated.

q: 把“AI 输出不符合项目风格”后的沟通链排好：
q_en: Put the communication chain in order after the AI output does not match the project style:
steps: 重新提示 AI 使用项目现有错误处理风格
说明你观察到它用了异常而项目用 error object
继续前先读生成的改动是否符合预期
指出这会和代码库模式冲突
why: 先说观察，再说影响，然后重定向 AI，最后审阅结果，能完整展示控制力。
why_en: The correction loop is observe, explain impact, reprompt with constraints, then review the revised output.
tradeoff: 观察+影响+重定向+复核的完整闭环 vs 直接静默重写
diagram:
flowchart LR
  BadStyle[Output off style] --> Say[Name mismatch]
  Say --> Reprompt[Reprompt with local pattern]
  Reprompt --> Review[Review diff]
  Review --> Test[Run tests]
  Test --> Explain[Explain outcome]

q: AI coding 面试进入执行阶段后，面试官最常评估的不是你打字多快，而是什么？
q_en: Once an AI coding interview reaches execution, what are interviewers really evaluating?
options: 你是否持续提示、审阅并掌控 AI 的输出
你是否让 AI 独自决定架构方案
你是否尽量避免运行和验证代码
你是否写出全场最长的一段提示
options_en: Whether you keep prompting, reviewing, and steering the AI's output.
Whether you let the AI decide the architecture entirely on its own.
Whether you avoid running and verifying the code.
Whether you write the single longest prompt in the room.
why: 执行阶段考核的是你能否按计划驱动 AI、审阅它的产出并持续掌控方向，而不是把决策权交给模型。
why_en: During execution, interviewers watch whether you keep driving, reviewing, and steering the AI instead of handing it the decisions.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> Prompt[Prompt AI]
  Prompt --> Review[Review output]
  Review --> Run[Run code]
  Run --> Adjust[Adjust]
  Adjust --> Prompt
optionExplanations: 这正是评分点：你全程在提示、审阅、纠偏，AI 只是执行你的判断。
误解：把方案决策权交给 AI，面试官反而看不到你自己的工程判断。
误解：省掉运行验证不是效率，是把错误留到后面一次性爆发。
误解：提示字数不是评分维度，提示是否精确锁定约束才是。
optionExplanations_en: Exactly the scoring signal — you're prompting, reviewing, and correcting course the whole time.
Misconception: handing the whole architecture decision to the AI hides your own engineering judgment from the interviewer.
Misconception: skipping verification isn't efficiency, it just lets errors pile up until they explode at once.
Misconception: prompt length isn't the scoring axis — precisely naming constraints is.

q: 写 AI 提示时，粒度的“甜点区”具体是什么？
q_en: What is the sweet spot for prompt granularity when coding with AI?
options: 只给原始题目，让 AI 自己决定所有方案
明确要做什么和怎么做，但让 AI 处理语法和惯用写法
逐行规定变量名和代码格式
完全不用 AI
options_en: Hand over the raw problem and let the AI pick the whole approach.
State the what and how clearly, but let the AI handle syntax and idioms.
Dictate variable names and formatting line by line.
Skip the AI entirely.
why: 太泛会让 AI 接管决策，太细又变成隔着 AI 手写代码；合适粒度是你定策略、AI 写实现。
why_en: The sweet spot is stating the what and how clearly while letting the AI handle syntax and idiomatic implementation.
tradeoff: 约束够用 vs 微管理成本 —— 提示太泛让 AI 接管决策，提示太细就变成隔着 AI 手写代码。
optionExplanations: 题目原样甩给 AI 时，你等于把方案选择权让出去，面试官看不到你的判断。
把 what/how 钉死、语法交给 AI，是省时间又保住判断权的甜点区。
连变量名都亲自口述，等于隔着 AI 手写，速度反而不如自己直接打字。
完全不用工具能保留全部判断，但放弃了它能省下的实现时间。
optionExplanations_en: Handing over the raw problem lets the AI pick the whole approach, so the interviewer never sees your call.
Pinning down the what and how while leaving syntax to the AI is the sweet spot — fast and still your judgment.
Dictating even variable names turns the AI into a typing proxy, slower than just typing it yourself.
Skipping the AI keeps every decision yours, but gives up the implementation speed it could have offered.

scenario: 你要实现前缀搜索，并已经决定使用 trie（前缀树），每个节点要保存字符和是否为单词结尾。
scenario_en: You need prefix search and have already chosen a trie, where each node stores a character and an end-of-word flag.
q: 哪条提示最符合推荐的提示粒度？
q_en: Which prompt best matches the recommended level of granularity?
options: 不给任何设计信息，只说一句“写点代码把前缀搜索功能实现掉，随便怎么做”，没有提数据结构
trie 支持 insert 和 prefix search，节点存字符、子节点和结束标记
先声明一个变量 a，再写好 for 循环，然后要求 AI 逐行照我口述的每一句代码往下写
需求只是新增一个前缀搜索方法，却要求 AI 顺带把整个项目重写成更好的分层架构
options_en: Give zero design detail — just say 'write some code for prefix search, any way you like,' naming no data structure.
A trie supporting insert and prefix search, each node storing a character, its children, and an end-of-word marker.
Declare a variable, write out a for loop, then have the AI type each line exactly as I dictate it, one by one.
Even though you only need one new method, ask the AI to rewrite the whole project into a better layered architecture.
why: 这条提示锁定了数据结构和节点字段，但把语法实现留给 AI，正好落在推荐的提示粒度上。
why_en: This prompt fixes the data structure and node fields while leaving syntax to the AI, landing right in the recommended granularity.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是改一行判断条件，自己直接写通常比提示 AI 更快。
tradeoff: 锁定方案与字段 vs 逐行口述实现 —— 提示到数据结构层就够，细到变量名就是隔着 AI 手写。
codeSample:
Implement a trie that supports insert(word) and searchByPrefix(prefix).
Each TrieNode stores: character, children map, isEndOfWord boolean.
Fit it into the existing Dictionary class; keep it concise.
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Task[Raw task] --> AI[AI decides]
  AI --> Drift[Drift risk]

flowchart LR
  You[Trie decision] --> AI[Implement methods]
  AI --> Fit[Code fits plan]

flowchart LR
  You[Line orders] --> AI[Typing proxy]
  AI --> Slow[Slow loop]

flowchart LR
  Scope[Small feature] --> Rewrite[Rewrite project]
  Rewrite --> Risk[Huge risk]

termDefinitions.meaning: 前缀树，一种按字符逐层存储字符串前缀的数据结构，适合前缀搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a prefix tree that stores strings character by character to make prefix search fast.

termDefinitions.meaning: trie 里的单个节点，通常保存一个字符、子节点集合和是否为单词结尾的标记。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TrieNode is a single node in a trie holding a character, its children, and an end-of-word flag.

termDefinitions.meaning: trie 节点上的布尔标记，标记从根到此节点的路径是否恰好是一个完整单词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: isEndOfWord is a boolean flag on a trie node marking whether the path from the root to this node spells a complete word.

optionExplanations: 不给结构信息时，AI 可能选哈希表而不是你已经定好的 trie。
锁定数据结构和字段、放开语法细节，正落在推荐的提示粒度上。
口述到每一句代码，等于隔着 AI 手写，比自己直接实现还慢。
题目只要一个方法，却引导 AI 做架构级重写，范围严重失控。
optionExplanations_en: Without any structure hint, the AI might reach for a hash map instead of the trie you already chose.
Fixing the data structure and fields while leaving syntax open lands exactly in the recommended granularity.
Dictating every line turns the AI into a typing proxy, slower than just writing it yourself.
The task only needs one method, but this steers the AI into an architecture-level rewrite — scope spirals.

scenario: 你要让 AI 实现一个复杂状态机（用状态和转移规则描述行为的模型），转移规则多且容易出错。
scenario_en: You need the AI to implement a complex state machine with many transition rules and easy-to-miss edge cases.
q: 这类任务的提示应该偏向什么风格？
q_en: What prompt style fits this kind of task?
options: 只说“实现状态机”
明确状态、转移、约束和边界行为
让 AI 自己发明状态
不要告诉 AI 任何现有接口
options_en: Just say 'implement a state machine.'
Spell out the states, transitions, constraints, and edge behavior.
Let the AI invent its own states.
Withhold every existing interface from the AI.
why: 复杂逻辑需要更具体的方向，避免 AI 用看似合理但不符合题意的状态设计。
why_en: Tricky logic needs precise states, transitions, constraints, and edge behavior so the AI implements what you actually intend.
whenOtherWins: 如果是重复样板代码，如类似的 API handler，可以用更短的提示再仔细验证。
tradeoff: 具体约束换正确率 vs 省提示时间 —— 逻辑越容易出错，越要提前说清状态和转移。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用有限个状态和转移规则描述系统行为的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state machine models behavior as a fixed set of states with rules for transitioning between them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用程序编程接口，模块之间约定好的调用方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is an Application Programming Interface, the agreed-upon way one piece of code calls another.

optionExplanations: 只给任务名不给约束，转移规则的边界情况多半会被漏掉。
状态、转移、边界都写清楚，AI 落地的状态机才会贴合你设计的规则。
状态设计权本该是你的判断，交给 AI 发明容易看似合理却偏离题意。
故意扣住现有接口只会让实现和代码库对不上，之后还要返工。
optionExplanations_en: Naming the task alone with no constraints usually means edge-case transitions get missed.
Spelling out states, transitions, and edges keeps the AI's machine matching the rules you designed.
State design should be your call — letting the AI invent its own can look plausible yet miss the intent.
Deliberately withholding the existing interfaces just makes the result clash with the codebase later.

scenario: 你需要生成五个几乎相同的 API endpoint handler（接收请求并返回响应的处理函数），项目里这种模式已经很标准。
scenario_en: You need five nearly identical API endpoint handlers, and this project already has a clear handler pattern.
q: 面对这批重复 handler，最合理的 AI 用法是什么？
q_en: What is the most reasonable way to use AI for these repetitive handlers?
options: 给短提示让 AI 生成样板，再验证是否遵守既有模式
逐行手写所有重复代码来证明打字能力
让 AI 顺带重新设计整个 API 层
生成之后跳过验证，因为样板一定正确
options_en: Give a short prompt, let the AI generate the boilerplate, then verify it follows the existing pattern.
Hand-write every repetitive line of code to prove your typing skill.
Have the AI redesign the entire API layer while it's at it.
Skip verification after generating, because boilerplate is always correct.
why: AI 很适合处理可验证的重复体力活，你仍要检查它是否照着项目模式写。
why_en: AI is useful for repetitive boilerplate that is easy to verify, as long as you still review it against the local pattern.
whenOtherWins: 如果 handler 里包含关键鉴权或事务边界，提示要更精确，不能只靠模板感生成。
tradeoff: 省时间 vs 验证成本 —— 样板交给 AI 换取速度，但你仍要核对它是否照抄了项目既有模式。
codeSample:
Generate 5 endpoint handlers: GET /orders/{id}, POST /orders, ...
Follow the existing handler pattern in OrderController exactly.
Keep error handling and response shape identical to current handlers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用程序编程接口，模块之间约定好的调用方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is an Application Programming Interface, the agreed-upon way one piece of code calls another.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理某个 API 路径请求、返回响应的函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An endpoint handler is the function that processes requests to a specific API route and returns a response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 项目里高度重复、模式固定的样板代码，比如相似的 API handler。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Boilerplate is highly repetitive, pattern-following code such as near-identical API handlers.

optionExplanations: 体量交给 AI、你负责核对模式一致性，是这类重复活的最优分工。
五个 handler 全部手打，花的时间远超 AI 方案却没有额外收益。
任务只是加 handler，让 AI 顺带重设计整层 API，范围失控。
样板也可能抄错字段或漏掉鉴权，不查一遍风险照样放行。
optionExplanations_en: Handing the volume to the AI while you check pattern consistency is the right split for this kind of repetition.
Hand-typing all five handlers takes far longer than the AI path with no extra benefit.
The task only needed handlers, and letting the AI redesign the whole layer lets scope spiral.
Boilerplate can still copy a field wrong or drop an auth check — skipping review lets that slip through.

q: 补全控制 AI 输出长度的原因：
q_en: Complete the reason for keeping AI output concise:
text: 面试里要让 AI 输出{{简洁}}，因为每一行额外代码都需要你{{审阅}}并可能被要求{{解释}}。
why: 冗长输出会增加理解、验证和辩护成本，常常比它节省的打字时间更贵。
why_en: Concise AI output matters because every extra line must be reviewed and potentially defended.

scenario: 完成代码取向（先读懂项目结构再动手）后，你知道项目已有 Dictionary 类和 TrieNode 结构，需要新增前缀搜索。
scenario_en: After orienting to the codebase, you know it already has a Dictionary class and TrieNode structure, and you need prefix search.
q: 哪条提示最可能产出贴合代码库的代码？
q_en: Which prompt is most likely to produce code that fits this codebase?
options: 不提任何类名，只笼统地说要写一个自动补全功能，别的都不管
给 Dictionary 添加 searchByPrefix，复用现有 TrieNode，返回列表
不管现有结构，让 AI 生成一个全新的 AutocompleteService 类和一套新节点结构
不管代码库现状是什么样子，随便挑一种当下最快能跑起来的写法就行
options_en: Name no existing class at all, just vaguely ask for an autocomplete feature and leave everything else unsaid.
Add searchByPrefix to Dictionary, reusing the existing TrieNode, and return a list of matches.
Ignore the existing structure and have the AI generate a brand-new AutocompleteService class with its own node structure.
Ignore whatever the codebase already looks like and pick whichever approach gets something running fastest right now.
why: 使用真实类名、方法名和数据结构会把 AI 限定在现有架构内，也向面试官展示你读懂了代码。
why_en: Using actual class names, method signatures, and data structures keeps the AI aligned with the existing architecture.
whenOtherWins: 如果现有结构确实不支持需求，应先说明缺口，再设计最小扩展。
tradeoff: 贴合现有架构 vs 生成速度 —— 引用真实类名换来能直接拼进代码库的输出，但提示要多打几个词。
codeSample:
Add searchByPrefix(String prefix) to the Dictionary class.
Reuse the existing TrieNode structure; do not create a new node type.
Return List<String> of all words matching the prefix.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Names[Real class names] --> Bound[Bound AI to repo]
  Bound --> Reuse[Reuse structures]
  Reuse --> Fit[Local fit]

termDefinitions.meaning: trie 里的单个节点，通常保存一个字符、子节点集合和是否为单词结尾的标记。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A TrieNode is a single node in a trie holding a character, its children, and an end-of-word flag.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里指开始写代码前先读懂项目结构、类和方法的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orientation is the phase before coding where you read and understand the project’s classes and structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种参数化的字符串列表类型，常见于 Java/Kotlin 风格签名。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: List<String> is a parameterized list-of-strings type common in Java- or Kotlin-style method signatures.

optionExplanations: 缺代码库词汇时，AI 只能猜结构，很容易和 Dictionary/TrieNode 脱节。
点名真实类和真实返回类型，把改动直接钉在现有架构里，改动面最小。
另起一套结构而不是复用 TrieNode，等于制造一份重复且难维护的代码。
只求先跑起来，短期能过但很可能和现有命名、类型冲突，后续要返工。
optionExplanations_en: Without codebase vocabulary, the AI can only guess the shape, likely disconnected from Dictionary/TrieNode.
Naming the real class and return type pins the change straight into the existing architecture with minimal surface.
Building a parallel structure instead of reusing TrieNode just creates a duplicate that's hard to maintain.
Optimizing for whatever runs first may pass today but likely clashes with existing naming and types later.

q: 在提示中引用代码库具体词汇有什么好处？（多选）
q_en: What are the benefits of using codebase-specific vocabulary in prompts? (Select all that apply.)
options: AI 更可能复用已有接口和数据结构
输出更容易融入现有架构
面试官能看到你完成了取向
可以完全不用审阅输出
options_en: The AI is more likely to reuse existing interfaces and data structures.
The output fits the existing architecture more naturally.
The interviewer can see that you actually did the orientation step.
You can skip reviewing the output entirely.
why: 具体词汇改善生成质量并展示上下文理解，但不能替代你对结果的验证。
why_en: Codebase-specific vocabulary improves fit and demonstrates understanding, but it does not remove the need to review.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试里指开始写代码前先读懂项目结构、类和方法的阶段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Orientation is the phase before coding where you read and understand the project’s classes and structure.

optionExplanations: 挡住的风险：AI 凭空重新发明一套接口，之后要花时间对齐。
减掉的压力：合并代码时不用再手动理顺架构冲突。
带来的信号：用词本身就让面试官看到你读懂了项目结构。
误解：具体词汇改善生成质量，但审阅这一步不能被它替代。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it blocks: the AI reinventing its own interface from scratch, which you'd later have to reconcile.
Pressure it relieves: less manual work untangling architecture conflicts when merging the result.
Signal it sends: your word choice alone shows the interviewer you actually did the orientation step.
Misconception: specific vocabulary improves generation quality, but it never replaces the review step.

scenario: 你发现只需要改一个变量名或一行条件判断，自己 30 秒能完成。
scenario_en: The change is just a variable rename or a one-line condition, and you can do it yourself in 30 seconds.
q: 这类小改动，最好的选择是什么？
q_en: What is the best choice for this tiny change?
options: 直接自己改
让 AI 生成完整补丁
先让 AI 解释变量名历史
暂停等待面试官指示
options_en: Just make the change yourself.
Ask the AI to generate a full patch.
Ask the AI to first explain the variable's history.
Pause and wait for the interviewer to tell you what to do.
why: 小修小改提示 AI 往往更慢，也会显得你离开 AI 就无法写代码。
why_en: For a tiny change you can make in seconds, writing it yourself is faster and shows you are not dependent on AI.
whenOtherWins: 如果小改牵涉多个文件或不确定副作用，可以请 AI 辅助定位影响面。
tradeoff: 自己改的速度 vs 提示 AI 的往返成本 —— 30 秒能搞定的事，提示往返通常更慢还更显得依赖 AI。
optionExplanations: 这是最快的选择：改一行判断，自己动手比写提示还省时间。
误解：为一行改动走完整提示流程，写提示、等结果的时间比手改还长。
误解：历史背景跟这一行改动无关，多问一步纯属绕路。
误解：一行小改不需要等指示，暴露的是对 AI 的依赖而非独立判断。
optionExplanations_en: The fastest call — fixing one condition by hand beats writing and waiting on a prompt.
Misconception: running a full prompt loop for a one-line change costs more time than just typing it.
Misconception: variable history has nothing to do with this edit — it's an unnecessary detour.
Misconception: a one-line fix needs no green light — waiting here signals AI dependency, not judgment.

scenario: 某段标准数据结构实现你知道方案正确，但手写要五分钟，AI 十秒可生成且容易测试。
scenario_en: You already know the standard data-structure approach is correct, but it takes five minutes to type and ten seconds for AI to generate.
q: 这类工作更适合谁来做？
q_en: Who should do this kind of work?
options: 让 AI 生成，你负责方向和验证
永远手写，避免使用 AI
让 AI 决定数据结构
跳过测试直接继续
options_en: Let the AI generate it while you own the direction and verification.
Always hand-write it and avoid AI entirely.
Let the AI decide which data structure to use.
Skip testing and move straight on.
why: AI 适合体量大、正确性可验证的实现工作；关键是方案仍由你选择。
why_en: Use AI for high-volume implementation that is easy to verify while keeping the design decision yourself.
whenOtherWins: 如果难点是算法选择或边界推理，应先自己想清楚再让 AI 实现。
tradeoff: 生成速度 vs 决策归属 —— AI 承担打字体量，但数据结构的选择仍必须是你的判断。
optionExplanations: 十秒拿到已知正确的实现，省下的五分钟能用在更难的部分。
误解：拒绝工具反而在已验证的体力活上浪费掉本可以省下的时间。
误解：数据结构的选择该是你的判断，交给 AI 后错的结构会在边界情况炸掉。
误解：跳过测试等于放弃确认正确性，哪怕方案本身没问题。
optionExplanations_en: Ten seconds for an implementation you already know is correct frees five minutes for the harder part.
Misconception: refusing the tool wastes time on grunt work that's already known to be verifiable.
Misconception: the structure choice should be yours — a wrong AI pick can break on edge cases later.
Misconception: skipping tests means giving up on confirming correctness, even for a known-good approach.

q: 补全 AI 使用原则：
q_en: Complete the principle for using AI during execution:
text: 把 AI 用在{{体量}}上，把自己用在{{判断}}上；AI 可以写得快，但方案选择和取舍要由你负责。
why: 面试要评估你的工程判断，而不是你把模型输出转发到代码库的速度。
why_en: Use AI for volume and yourself for judgment, because the interview evaluates your engineering decisions.
tradeoff: AI 出体量 vs 你出判断 —— 生成速度换不来方案责任，选择和取舍必须你来担。

q: 为什么不要连续堆叠多次 AI 生成后才第一次运行代码？
q_en: Why should you not stack several AI generations before running the code for the first time?
options: AI 会因为堆叠生成太多次而直接拒绝继续输出
多个局部正确的改动可能互相冲突，最后形成级联错误
运行代码这个动作本身会降低面试评分
面试规则规定测试只能放在最后运行
options_en: The AI will simply refuse to keep generating once you stack too many rounds.
Several locally-correct changes can conflict and surface as one cascading failure.
The act of running the code itself is what lowers your interview score.
Interview rules dictate that tests can only be run at the very end.
why: 每次有意义生成后运行能把错误隔离在最近一步，避免最后同时面对多处冲突。
why_en: Running after each meaningful generation isolates failures to the latest change instead of creating a cascade.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Gen1[Generate step 1] --> Gen2[Generate step 2]
  Gen2 --> Gen3[Generate step 3]
  Gen3 --> Fail[Mixed failure]
  Run[Run each step] -.-> Isolate[Small failure]

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个局部改动叠加后互相冲突，在最后一次运行时集中爆发的一串错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cascading errors happen when several stacked changes conflict and surface together the first time you finally run the code.

optionExplanations: 误解：AI 不会因为堆叠生成次数就拒绝工作，问题不出在它身上。
每步都局部正确，攒到最后一次运行时，冲突会同时爆发难以定位。
误解：运行验证是加分习惯，不是拉低分数的动作。
误解：测试应该跟着每一步走，攒到最后只会让早期错误被掩盖。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the AI doesn't refuse to work just because generations pile up — that's not the mechanism.
Each step looks locally fine, but stacking them means the final run has to untangle several conflicts at once.
Misconception: running code to verify is a plus habit, not something that costs you points.
Misconception: tests should track each step — saving them for the end just masks earlier errors.

q: 把增量执行循环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the incremental execution loop in the correct order:
steps: 修复本轮引入的问题
让 AI 完成一个明确小步骤
运行测试或编译检查
确认通过后进入下一步
why: 核心原则是每个有意义变更后马上验证，有问题先修，不在破损代码上继续叠新功能。
why_en: The loop is: generate one clear step, run checks, fix any breakage, then move on.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Prompt[Prompt one change] --> Review[Review diff]
  Review --> Run[Run tests]
  Run --> Decide{Pass?}
  Decide -->|yes| Next[Next step]
  Decide -->|no| Fix[Fix latest step]
  Fix --> Run

q: AI 的“训练数据偏置”（更容易给出训练语料里最常见的解法）在面试中常表现为什么？
q_en: How does training-data bias usually show up in an AI coding interview?
options: 给出教科书式解法，但不一定适合当前约束或代码库
遇到算法题会永远拒绝回答，什么也不生成
只能生成注释文字，完全不能生成任何代码
自动识别并精准套用每家公司的具体偏好
options_en: It gives a textbook solution that may not fit your specific constraints or codebase.
It will always refuse to answer any algorithm question and generate nothing.
It can only generate comment text and is completely unable to generate any code.
It automatically detects and precisely applies every company's specific preferences.
why: AI 可能给出技术上正确、策略上不合适的常见解法，你要判断它是否匹配题目约束和现有工具。
why_en: Training-data bias often gives a textbook solution that may not fit the specific constraints or codebase.

termDefinitions.meaning: AI 更容易给出训练语料里最常见的解法，而不一定是最贴合当前约束的解法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Training-data bias means the AI defaults to the most common solution in its training data, which may not fit your specific constraints.

optionExplanations: 常见解法技术上没错，但可能没用到代码库里更简单的现成方案。
误解：训练偏置指的是内容倾向，不是拒绝作答的行为。
误解：偏置和生成能力的形式无关，AI 照样能生成完整代码。
误解：AI 不会自动获得某家公司的具体偏好，这不是偏置的表现。
optionExplanations_en: The common answer is technically sound, but may skip a simpler option already available in the codebase.
Misconception: training bias is a content tendency, not a refusal to answer at all.
Misconception: bias has nothing to do with output form — the AI still generates full code.
Misconception: the AI gains no automatic awareness of a specific company's preferences from bias.

q: AI 输出过度冗长的主要代价是什么？
q_en: What is the main cost of overly verbose AI output?
options: 代码量越大就一定意味着越正确
面试官看到长代码一定会更喜欢
你需要理解、验证并解释更多不必要的抽象和注释
测试覆盖率会随着代码变长自动变全面
options_en: More code always necessarily means more correctness.
The interviewer will always end up liking longer code more.
You have to understand, verify, and defend more unnecessary abstractions and comments.
Test coverage automatically becomes more thorough simply because the code got longer.
why: 冗长代码增加审查面，也给面试官更多可追问但你未必能防守的内容。
why_en: Verbose output expands the surface you must understand, verify, and defend.
optionExplanations: 误解：行数和正确性没有必然关系，混淆了体量和质量。
误解：面试官通常更欣赏精简可控的输出，长度不是加分项。
每多一行都要能讲清楚它为什么在那，审查和答辩面被动放大。
误解：实现变长不会自动带来更全面的测试覆盖。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: line count has no necessary link to correctness — this conflates volume with quality.
Misconception: interviewers usually prefer concise, controlled output — length isn't a point-scorer.
Every extra line needs a reason you can explain on the spot, passively expanding what you must defend.
Misconception: a longer implementation doesn't automatically make test coverage more thorough.

q: 哪些是 AI 常见的设计捷径或过度设计？（多选）
q_en: Which are common AI design shortcuts or over-designs? (Select all that apply.)
options: 为两个几乎无关的类创建 BaseProcessor
不必要地引入深继承层级
把简单 if-else 包成 strategy pattern
遵守现有最小接口
options_en: Create a BaseProcessor superclass for two barely related classes.
Introduce unnecessarily deep inheritance hierarchies.
Wrap a simple if-else in a strategy pattern.
Stick to the existing minimal interface.
why: 这些抽象可能不直接破坏功能，但会显得你接受了没有必要的设计复杂度。
why_en: Unneeded base classes, deep inheritance, and strategy wrappers can signal that you accepted lazy over-engineering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 示例中 AI 为两个几乎无关的类硬造出的公共父类，是过度抽象的典型产物。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BaseProcessor is the example of an unnecessary shared superclass the AI invents for two barely related classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种把可替换算法封装成独立类、通过接口切换的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The strategy pattern wraps interchangeable algorithms in separate classes swapped through a common interface.

optionExplanations: 挡不住风险：硬造的公共父类让以后改一个类容易牵连另一个不相关的类。
带来的压力：层级越深，定位一个方法实际生效在哪一层就越难。
带来的压力：模式复杂度超过分支本身，读者要多学一层结构才看懂逻辑。
不是过度设计：接口保持最小是应保留的克制，不需要新学任何结构。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it creates: a forced shared superclass lets a later change to one class accidentally ripple into the unrelated one.
Pressure it adds: the deeper the hierarchy, the harder it is to trace which layer a method actually runs in.
Pressure it adds: pattern complexity exceeds the branch it wraps, forcing readers to learn a layer just to see the logic.
Not over-design: keeping the interface minimal is the restraint worth keeping, nothing new to learn.

q: 哪些 AI 生成行为属于严重的 correctness shortcut（掩盖而非修复真实错误的取巧做法）？（多选）
q_en: Which AI-generated behaviors are serious correctness shortcuts? (Select all that apply.)
options: 删除失败测试而不是修实现
用 any 绕过类型错误
吞掉异常或硬编码特定测试值
保留失败测试并定位根因
options_en: Delete a failing test instead of fixing the implementation.
Use `any` to bypass a type error.
Swallow exceptions or hardcode specific test values.
Keep the failing test and track down the root cause.
why: 这些做法让表面错误消失，但真实问题仍在，是面试官会追问的红旗。
why_en: Deleting tests, silencing types, or hardcoding values hides bugs instead of fixing them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为了让代码看起来通过，掩盖而非修复真实错误的取巧做法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A correctness shortcut is a trick that makes code look like it passes without actually fixing the underlying bug.

termDefinitions.meaning: TypeScript 中关闭类型检查的“万能类型”，用它能绕过编译期类型错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In TypeScript, `any` is the escape-hatch type that turns off compile-time type checking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 捕获异常的语法结构，如果 catch 块什么也不做就会把错误悄悄吞掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: try/catch is the exception-handling construct, and an empty catch block silently swallows the error.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把本该动态计算的值写死成固定值，通常只为让某个测试用例通过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hardcoding means baking in a fixed value that should be computed dynamically, often just to make one test pass.

optionExplanations: 挡不住风险：红灯变绿灯了，但底层 bug 原样留在实现里。
挡不住风险：类型系统失去保护，问题会拖到运行时才炸出来。
挡不住风险：错误被压制而不是修复，换一批输入立刻打回原形。
不是取巧：保留红灯去追根因，才是应对失败测试的正确做法。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it fails to block: the red light turns green while the underlying bug stays exactly where it was.
Risk it fails to block: the type system loses its protection until the bug surfaces at runtime instead.
Risk it fails to block: the error is suppressed rather than fixed, and resurfaces the moment inputs change.
Not a shortcut: leaving the test red and tracing the cause is the correct response to a failure.

scenario: AI 第一次输出偏离你的要求，没有使用你指定的数据结构。
scenario_en: The AI's first output drifted from your request and did not use the data structure you specified.
q: 这时最好的下一步是什么？
q_en: What is the best next step here?
options: 原样重复同一个提示，不加任何新信息
接受这次偏离，继续在上面叠功能
带更多上下文重新表述，明确必须使用的数据结构
马上切换模型，但完全不改提示内容
options_en: Repeat the exact same prompt again, adding no new information.
Accept this drift and keep layering new features on top of it.
Rephrase with more context, stating the required data structure explicitly.
Immediately switch models while leaving the prompt content completely unchanged.
why: 如果第一次没理解，重复原话通常不会改善；更清晰的上下文和约束才是有效修正。
why_en: If the AI missed the request, rephrase with clearer context and constraints rather than repeating the same prompt.
whenOtherWins: 如果偏离只是一个小局部且你能十秒改好，直接手修会更快。
tradeoff: 重提示一次的时间成本 vs 偏差累积的返工成本 —— 说清楚约束换取一次修正，好过在错误结构上继续堆功能。
codeSample:
Before: "Implement the cache eviction logic."
After: "Implement cache eviction using a doubly linked list + hash map
for O(1) LRU eviction, matching the existing Cache class fields."
optionExplanations: 没加新信息时，AI 第一次没理解的地方大概率还会同样理解错。
在已知偏差的结构上继续叠功能，返工成本会随时间放大。
补上数据结构等具体约束，是对因下药，最可能让输出对齐意图。
光换模型不改约束，没解决问题根源，还多花一份上下文重建成本。
optionExplanations_en: With no new information added, whatever the AI misunderstood the first time likely gets misunderstood again.
Building more features on a structure already known to be off just lets the rework cost grow over time.
Filling in the missing constraint, like the required data structure, targets the actual cause most directly.
Swapping models without touching the constraints skips the real fix and adds a context-rebuild cost on top.

q: 开放式面试里为什么建议频繁提交或保留回滚点（代码可运行时的一次提交）？
q_en: Why keep frequent commits or rollback points during an open-ended interview?
options: 为了在面试官面前展示自己熟悉多少条 git 命令
因为面试系统里每提交一次代码都会自动加一次分
AI 连续跑偏时，回到上一个可运行状态通常比手工拆坏改动更快
为了图省事，正好可以借口避免再写测试
options_en: To show the interviewer how many git commands you know.
Because the interview system auto-adds points for every single commit.
When the AI drifts repeatedly, returning to the last working state is usually faster than manually undoing the damage.
As a convenient excuse to avoid writing tests.
why: 坏生成叠多了会很难局部修复，干净回滚点能保护你不被错误改动拖住。
why_en: Frequent checkpoints let you return to a working state when several bad AI generations pile up.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Good[Known good] --> Commit[Checkpoint]
  Commit --> Try[AI change]
  Try --> Bad{Bad path?}
  Bad -->|yes| Back[Rollback]
  Bad -->|no| Keep[Keep going]

termDefinitions.meaning: 代码处于已知可运行状态时的一次提交，可以随时退回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A rollback point is a commit made while the code is in a known-working state that you can return to.

optionExplanations: 误解：回滚点的价值是恢复速度，不是拿来展示命令熟练度。
误解：分数不来自提交次数本身，这套自动加分机制并不存在。
AI 连续跑偏时，直接退回可运行状态，比逐处手工拆解改动快得多。
误解：回滚点和是否写测试是两件独立的事，不能拿来当借口。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: rollback points earn their value from recovery speed, not from showing off git commands.
Misconception: score doesn't come from commit count itself — no such auto-bonus mechanism exists.
When the AI drifts repeatedly, jumping back to a working state beats manually untangling each bad change.
Misconception: rollback points and writing tests are separate concerns, not an excuse to skip one for the other.

q: AI 输出“90% 正确”时，为什么手工逐行补最后 10% 常常是陷阱？
q_en: Why is hand-patching the last 10% of a mostly-right AI output often a trap?
options: 因为面试规则里明确规定手写代码永远不被允许
因为 AI 会在你不知情时主动删除你后加的改动
你可能花更久修补混乱结构，不如用更清楚的提示重新生成
因为 90% 正确这个比例本身就已经一定足够上线
options_en: Because interview rules explicitly state that hand-writing code is never allowed.
Because the AI actively deletes your later edits without you knowing.
You may spend longer patching a confused structure than reprompting clearly for a clean regeneration.
Because a 90% correct ratio is, by itself, always already good enough to ship.
why: 半 AI 半手补的代码容易变乱，如果偏差来自误解需求，清晰重提示通常更快。
why_en: Patching a mostly-wrong output can be slower than reprompting clearly because the structure may already be misaligned.
optionExplanations: 误解：手写代码从来不是被禁止的选项，陷阱不是禁令问题。
误解：AI 不会主动删掉你后加的改动，风险不来自这个机制。
半 AI 半手改的结构越补越乱，重提示往往比逐处打补丁更省时间。
误解：剩下的 10% 常常正是边界情况，不能默认它已经够用。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: hand-writing code is never off-limits — the trap here isn't about a rule.
Misconception: the AI doesn't actively delete edits you add afterward — that's not where the risk comes from.
Half-AI, half-hand-edited structure gets messier the more you patch it; a clear reprompt is usually faster.
Misconception: the missing 10% is often exactly the edge case that can't be assumed already fine.

scenario: 你已经花两分钟让 AI 写对十行逻辑，但它连续两次没理解；你自己一分钟能写完。
scenario_en: You have spent two minutes trying to get AI to write ten lines, it missed twice, and you can write them in one minute.
q: 最务实的选择是什么？
q_en: What is the most pragmatic choice?
options: 继续和 AI 纠缠直到成功
换一个无关模型继续试
停止提示，自己写这十行
放弃这个功能
options_en: Keep fighting with the AI until it finally succeeds.
Switch to an unrelated model and keep trying.
Stop prompting and write the ten lines yourself.
Give up on the feature entirely.
why: 工具的目的不是证明能用 AI，而是更快正确推进；能手写更快时就该手写。
why_en: If writing it yourself is faster than fighting the AI, do that and keep moving.
whenOtherWins: 如果实现很长但只是约束表达不清，先做一次更具体的重提示仍可能划算。
tradeoff: 继续纠缠的时间成本 vs 自己写的确定性 —— 已知一分钟能搞定时，纠缠 AI 的边际时间不再划算。
optionExplanations: 已经两次没成功，继续纠缠只是追加沉没成本，收益不确定。
换模型有上下文重建成本，问题未必出在模型本身，不一定划算。
已知一分钟能写完，直接动手是总耗时最短的选择，工具是手段不是目的。
功能本身并不难，只因工具没配合就放弃，是不必要的损失。
optionExplanations_en: Two failed attempts already spent — continuing just chases sunk cost with uncertain payoff.
Switching models costs context-rebuild time, and the problem may not even be the model itself.
Knowing it takes one minute by hand makes writing it yourself the shortest total path — the tool is a means, not the goal.
The feature itself isn't hard; giving up just because the tool didn't cooperate is an unnecessary loss.

q: 补全一条经验规则：
q_en: Complete this rule of thumb:
text: 如果 AI 第一次没写对，可以{{重提示一次}}；如果仍没对，通常应该{{自己写}}或缩小任务，而不是继续耗时。
why: 单个生成上纠缠超过几分钟，往往比直接实现或拆小问题更不划算；这是给定的经验阈值，不是靠公式推导出来的。
why_en: A practical rule of thumb is one reprompt, then write it yourself or break the task down.

q: 面试中 AI 输出不佳时，为什么切换模型通常不是首选？
q_en: When AI output is poor in an interview, why is switching models usually not the first move?
options: 切换模型这件事一定被平台规则禁止
切换模型这个动作会直接删除代码库
不同模型的输出质量其实完全一样
更具体地重提示或自己写，通常比切换上下文更快
options_en: Switching models is something the platform rules always forbid outright.
The act of switching models directly deletes the codebase.
Different models' output quality is in fact completely identical.
Reprompting more specifically or writing it yourself is usually faster than switching context.
why: 模型切换有上下文和时间成本，问题常常来自提示不清或任务太大，而不是模型名称。
why_en: Reprompting more specifically or writing it yourself is usually faster than switching models mid-interview.
tradeoff: 切换模型的上下文成本 vs 重提示/自己写的确定性 —— 换模型要重建上下文，通常比说清楚约束更慢。

termDefinitions.meaning: AI 助手在当前会话里已经了解的代码、约束和历史信息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Context is everything the AI assistant already knows in the current session — the code, constraints, and history so far.

optionExplanations: 误解：切换模型通常不是被禁止，只是时间上不划算。
误解：切换模型不会对代码库产生任何破坏性影响。
误解：不同模型的输出质量确实存在差异，不能一概而论。
重提示或自己写不需要重建上下文，通常比换模型更省时间。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: switching models usually isn't forbidden, it's just a bad time trade.
Misconception: switching models has no destructive effect on the codebase at all.
Misconception: output quality does differ across models — this can't be flattened to identical.
Reprompting or writing it yourself skips rebuilding context, usually saving time over a model switch.

q: 结构化面试里的 AI 为什么可能感觉比你平时用的工具弱？
q_en: Why might AI in a structured interview feel weaker than your everyday tools?
options: 因为公司平台一定是故意把 AI 削弱来为难候选人，这是明确规则
因为面试用的浏览器在技术上无法运行任何模型调用
因为面试题目的文本内容根本传不进 AI 的输入窗口
因为平台 AI 可能缺少日常工具里的系统提示、代码上下文和工作流集成
options_en: Because the company platform must be deliberately weakening the AI to make it hard for candidates — that's an explicit rule.
Because the interview browser is technically incapable of running any model calls at all.
Because the interview problem's text content technically can never reach the AI's input window.
Because the platform AI may lack the system prompt, code context, and workflow integration your daily tools have.
why: 不管是否故意限制，实际效果是工具能力更弱，你需要降低期待并更多依赖自己的理解。
why_en: Interview AI may feel weaker because it lacks the system prompt, context, and workflow integration of your daily tools.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在用户看不到的地方预先设定 AI 行为和上下文的隐藏指令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A system prompt is the hidden instruction that pre-configures an AI assistant’s behavior and context before the user’s own messages.

optionExplanations: 误解：是否故意本身不确定，把它断言成明确规则过于绝对。
误解：浏览器本身能正常承载模型调用，不是能力弱的原因。
误解：AI 通常能正常读到题目文本，这不是问题所在。
缺少系统提示、代码上下文和工作流集成，才是体感变弱的真正原因。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: whether it's deliberate is actually uncertain, so stating it as an explicit rule overreaches.
Misconception: a browser can carry model calls just fine — that's not what causes weaker capability.
Misconception: the AI can usually read the problem text without issue — that isn't the bottleneck.
Missing the system prompt, code context, and workflow integration is the real reason it feels weaker.

q: 遇到能力受限的面试 AI 时，适合让它做哪些事？（多选）
q_en: When interview AI is limited, what tasks are still good fits? (Select all that apply.)
options: 生成样板代码
解释陌生语法
搭建基础结构
替你做所有架构判断
options_en: Generate boilerplate code.
Explain unfamiliar syntax.
Scaffold basic structure.
Make every architecture decision for you.
why: 弱 AI 仍能加速基础工作，但难点思考和架构取舍必须由你兜住。
why_en: A limited AI can still help with boilerplate, syntax explanations, and scaffolding while you own the hard reasoning.
optionExplanations: 减掉的压力：重复模式代码交给它写，省下打字体量。
挡住的风险：语言/库用法卡壳时，靠它补齐知识空白而不是干等。
减掉的压力：先搭出骨架再填细节，起步更快，但骨架是否合理仍要你把关。
不该外包：架构取舍正是你该兜住的判断，能力受限时外包风险更高。
optionExplanations_en: Pressure it relieves: repetitive pattern code goes to it, saving typing volume.
Risk it blocks: when a syntax or library usage stalls you, it fills the knowledge gap instead of you guessing.
Pressure it relieves: a starter scaffold speeds up the beginning, though you still judge whether it's sound.
Not to outsource: architecture judgment is exactly what you must own, riskier still when the AI is limited.

q: 只用最强日常 AI 工具练习，面试时有什么风险？
q_en: What is the risk of practicing only with your strongest everyday AI tool?
options: 风险其实很小，因为不管哪个模型能力都完全一样
你会因为换了个工具就完全不会写提示了
所有结构化面试平台都会自动帮你同步日常工具的个人设置
你可能没有形成在受限 AI 只能完成一部分时继续推进的工作流
options_en: The risk is actually small because every model has exactly the same capability.
You would completely forget how to write a prompt just from switching tools.
Every structured interview platform automatically syncs your daily-tool personal settings.
You may never build a workflow for making progress when a limited AI can only get you part of the way.
why: 真实面试工具可能更慢、更弱或上下文更少，没练过受限环境会让你措手不及。
why_en: Practicing only with top-tier daily tools can leave you unprepared when interview AI is slower or less capable.
optionExplanations: 误解：不同模型能力差距是真实存在的风险，不能当成可忽略的量。
误解：换工具不会让提示能力彻底消失，这是夸大后果。
误解：结构化平台通常不会带你的个人配置，同步这件事并不存在。
真正缺的是受限工具只能完成一部分时，你怎么接着往下推进的套路。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the capability gap between models is a real risk, not something safe to write off.
Misconception: switching tools doesn't wipe out your prompting ability — this overstates the consequence.
Misconception: structured platforms usually don't carry your personal config — no such sync exists.
What's actually missing is a playbook for pushing forward once a limited AI can only get you partway.

q: 把 AI 输出不佳时的恢复链排好：
q_en: Put the recovery chain for poor AI output in the correct order:
steps: 如果仍失败且手写更快，就自己实现
识别具体偏差：算法、接口、风格或正确性
用更具体的上下文和约束重提示一次
运行或审阅确认修正是否有效
why: 恢复坏输出要先定位偏差，再重定向，再验证；持续失败时果断脱离 AI。
why_en: Recover from bad output by identifying the mismatch, reprompting with constraints, verifying, then writing it yourself if needed.
tradeoff: 重提示一次 vs 直接接管 —— 先花一次精确重提示的成本，换取避免过早放弃 AI 的效率损失；反复失败就该换成本更低的自己写。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Bad[Bad output] --> Diagnose[Name issue]
  Diagnose --> Reprompt[One focused reprompt]
  Reprompt --> Review[Review result]
  Review --> Decide{Better?}
  Decide -->|no| Manual[Take over]

scenario: AI 建议用一个新架构，但你还无法解释它为什么比原计划更适合当前题目。
scenario_en: The AI suggests a new architecture, but you cannot yet explain why it fits this problem better than your original plan.
q: 你应该怎么做？
q_en: What should you do?
options: 马上采纳，因为 AI 可能更聪明
让 AI 自己决定所有后续步骤
删除原计划
先不采纳，除非你能说明它更适合的原因
options_en: Adopt it immediately because the AI might be smarter.
Let the AI decide every subsequent step on its own.
Delete the original plan outright.
Hold off unless you can explain why it actually fits better.
why: 改变方案的理由必须来自你对题目和约束的判断，而不是 AI 提出了一个看起来高级的替代品。
why_en: You should only adopt an AI-suggested approach if you can explain why it better fits the problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果 AI 指出了你确实漏掉的约束，并且新方案能清楚解决它，那就是合理的 pivot。
tradeoff: 方案切换的潜在收益 vs 你能否为它辩护 —— 换方案的理由必须来自你的判断，不是 AI 看起来更高级。
optionExplanations: 只因来源是 AI 就采纳，被追问原因时会答不上来。
决策权本该在你，整体外包后面试官看不到任何你自己的判断。
还没确认新方案站得住就先销毁旧方案，一旦不成立就没了退路。
把采纳门槛设在能不能自己说清原因，是能在追问下站住的判据。
optionExplanations_en: Adopting it just because it came from the AI leaves you stuck when asked to justify the switch.
This decision should still be yours — outsourcing it all shows the interviewer no judgment of your own.
Destroying the old plan before confirming the new one holds up leaves you no way back if it doesn't.
Setting the bar at being able to explain the reason yourself is what survives follow-up questioning.

q: “不要在破损代码上继续叠新功能”背后的原因是什么？
q_en: Why should you avoid layering new features on top of broken code?
options: 因为破损代码上新功能一定完全写不出来
因为 AI 无法读取编译器给出的报错信息
因为面试官的规则不允许运行任何测试
你会失去错误来源，后续调试成本快速放大
options_en: Because new features simply cannot be written on broken code at all.
Because the AI is unable to read the error output the compiler gives.
Because the interviewer's rules do not allow running any tests.
You lose track of the error's source, and later debugging cost balloons.
why: 代码一旦处于未知坏状态，新错误和旧错误混在一起，AI 也更容易修错方向。
why_en: Layering features on broken code hides the source of errors and makes later debugging much more expensive.
optionExplanations: 误解：代码依然能继续写，只是新旧错误会叠加在一起。
误解：AI 通常能读到编译器报错，这不是限制的来源。
误解：运行测试通常是被鼓励的行为，不是被禁止的。
新旧错误交织在一起，回溯需要的排查时间会成倍增加。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: code can still be written on top, it's just that new and old errors stack together.
Misconception: the AI can usually read compiler error output fine — that's not the limiting factor.
Misconception: running tests is usually encouraged, not something interviewers forbid.
New and old errors tangle together, multiplying the time it takes to trace anything back.

q: 审阅 AI 输出时，应主动扫描哪些失败模式？（多选）
q_en: When reviewing AI output, which failure modes should you actively scan for? (Select all that apply.)
options: 是否换了你没同意的算法
是否引入不必要抽象
是否用类型或测试捷径掩盖问题
是否完全不需要运行
options_en: Whether it swapped in an algorithm you never approved.
Whether it introduced unnecessary abstractions.
Whether it used type or test shortcuts to hide problems.
Whether it means you never need to run the code at all.
why: 这些都是 AI 看似完成任务但实际偏离、过度设计或隐藏 bug 的常见方式。
why_en: Review AI output for unapproved algorithm changes, unnecessary abstractions, and shortcuts that hide bugs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 any 绕过类型检查、删测试或硬编码值等让代码表面通过的手法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A type or test shortcut is a trick — like using `any`, deleting tests, or hardcoding values — that makes code look correct on the surface.

optionExplanations: 挡住的风险：算法悄悄换了却没人发现，追问选择理由时答不上来。
挡住的风险：抽象层不知不觉膨胀，复杂度失控却没人察觉。
挡住的风险：any、空 catch、硬编码值让真实 bug 藏在看似通过的代码里。
误解：审阅不能替代实际运行，二者是互补关系不是替代关系。
optionExplanations_en: Risk it blocks: an algorithm swapped quietly leaves you unable to answer why it was chosen.
Risk it blocks: abstraction creeps in unnoticed and complexity spirals without anyone catching it.
Risk it blocks: `any`, empty catches, or hardcoded values let a real bug hide inside code that looks like it passes.
Misconception: review can never substitute for actually running the code — they're complementary, not interchangeable.

scenario: 你在 AI 编码面试里已经看完代码库、理清了架构和现有接口，还没打开 AI 聊天窗口。
scenario_en: In an AI coding interview, you have already read the codebase, understood the architecture and existing interfaces, and have not opened the AI chat yet.
q: 打开 AI 聊天前，你最应该先做完什么？
q_en: Before opening the AI chat, what should you finish first?
options: 跳过和面试官同步，直接开始写提示
让 AI 先把整个项目重构一遍
形成自己的实现计划，明确关键决策
把原始题目一字不改地粘给 AI
options_en: Skip syncing with the interviewer and jump straight to prompting.
Have the AI refactor the whole project first.
Form your own implementation plan and pin down the key decisions.
Paste the raw problem statement to the AI unchanged.
why: 计划让你掌握架构和算法决策，AI 只是执行者；没有计划就容易被模型的第一版输出牵着走。
why_en: Forming your own plan first keeps architecture and algorithm decisions in your hands instead of the AI's first draft.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Orient[Orientation] --> Plan[Own plan]
  Plan --> Share[Share with interviewer]
  Share --> Prompt[Guide AI]
  Prompt --> Execute[Execute steps]
optionExplanations: 跳过同步只是省了确认步骤，你手上依旧没有成型的实现计划。
把重构交给 AI，它的第一版结构就变成事实架构，关键决策没经过你手。
先想清楚要怎么做、决策点在哪，AI 才有明确目标可以执行。
原样转发题目等于把拆解问题的机会让给 AI，你自己没做任何转译。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping the sync only skips confirmation — you still haven't formed a plan of your own.
Handing the redesign to the AI turns its first draft into the real architecture, with no decision passing through you.
Nail down what you're doing and where the key decisions sit, so the AI has a clear target to execute.
Forwarding the raw prompt hands the job of breaking the problem down to the AI instead of you.

scenario: 你要在动手写代码前先把实现方案定下来，具体怎么定要看面试官对 AI 参与设计的态度。
scenario_en: Before coding, you need to settle the implementation plan, and the right way depends on how the interviewer wants AI involved in design.
q: AI 编码面试里，形成实现计划主要有哪两种方式？
q_en: In an AI coding interview, what are the two main ways to form an implementation plan?
options: 只让 AI 出计划，你全盘接受不追问
完全不做计划，边想边写
只写测试用例，不管架构
自己先设计架构，或者审阅并修改 AI 出的计划
options_en: Let the AI produce a plan and accept it fully without questioning it.
Skip planning entirely and improvise as you go.
Only write test cases and ignore the architecture.
Either design the architecture yourself, or vet and revise a plan the AI drafts.
why: 两种方式都成立：能不能用 AI 参与设计取决于面试官；无论哪种，你都要真正理解并能防守这份计划。
why_en: Either you design the architecture yourself or you vet and revise an AI-drafted plan, but you must understand and defend whichever plan you end up with.
tradeoff: 自己设计架构（慢但可控）vs AI 起草后你审阅（快但要能拆穿它）
optionExplanations: 全盘接受 AI 的计划等于放弃审查，面试官一追问原因你就答不上来。
边想边写等于没有前置计划，一旦题目涉及架构决策就容易走偏。
只盯着测试用例会把架构判断搁置一边，事后返工成本更高。
不管起草者是谁，最终计划都要经你手定稿，你要能讲清每个决策的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Accepting the AI's plan wholesale means giving up review, and you can't answer when the interviewer asks why.
Improvising with no upfront plan leaves you adrift the moment the problem has real architecture decisions.
Focusing only on test cases pushes architecture judgment aside, which costs more to fix later.
Whoever drafts it, the final plan has to pass through you, and you need to be able to explain every decision.

scenario: 面试官明确表示可以用 AI 做设计讨论，你需要快速形成实现路线。
scenario_en: The interviewer explicitly allows AI-assisted design discussion, and you need to form an implementation route quickly.
q: 此时最合适的规划方式是什么？
q_en: What planning mode fits best here?
options: 让 AI 提计划，但逐项审阅、反驳、修改后再执行
直接照 AI 计划做，不追问也不改
拒绝任何 AI 帮助，全部自己手写设计
跳过计划，先让 AI 随便写一版看效果
options_en: Have the AI draft a plan, then review, push back on, and revise it item by item before executing.
Take the AI's plan as-is without questioning or changing anything.
Refuse any AI help and hand-design everything yourself.
Skip planning and let the AI write a random first pass to see what happens.
why: 面试官已经接受 AI 参与设计，AI 辅助规划能加速；但强信号来自你审查和塑形计划，而不是盖章批准。
why_en: Since the interviewer is fine with AI-assisted design, let the AI draft fast, but the strong signal comes from you actively vetting and reshaping the plan.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官希望看你亲自设计，应先自己画出结构，再把 AI 用在实现体力活上。
tradeoff: AI 起草求快 vs 你亲自把关求可控
optionExplanations: 面试官已经放行 AI 参与设计，就让它先起草求快，但每一项都要你审、你改。
原样照做等于把设计判断交给 AI，即使这轮允许用 AI，你也没留下把关痕迹。
本题面试官已经开放 AI 参与，还坚持全手写等于白白放弃这轮明确允许的加速方式。
没有先成型的计划直接摸索，AI 第一版会隐性定型架构，你事后很难说清楚为什么这样设计。
optionExplanations_en: Since the interviewer already opened the door to AI-assisted design, let it draft fast — you still review and revise every piece.
Taking the draft as-is hands the design call to the AI, and there's no sign of your judgment even though review was allowed.
Refusing all AI help here throws away speed the interviewer explicitly said you could use.
Skipping a plan and letting the AI free-write first quietly locks in the architecture, and you'll struggle to explain it later.

scenario: 你不确定这轮面试是否允许 AI 帮你做计划，还是只希望 AI 写实现。
scenario_en: You are not sure whether this interview allows AI to help with planning, or only expects AI to write implementation code.
q: 最好的处理方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to handle this?
options: 直接假设可以用 AI 做所有设计
先问面试官对 AI 参与规划的期望
完全不用 AI，全程手写
先按自己的想法做，等面试官发现问题再解释
options_en: Just assume AI can be used for all the design work.
Ask the interviewer up front what they expect from AI in planning.
Avoid AI entirely and write everything by hand.
Do it your own way and explain only if the interviewer objects.
why: 不同公司甚至不同面试官的预期不同，提前对齐能避免把可接受的用法误判成负面信号。
why_en: Ask the interviewer directly, because expectations for AI in planning vary by company and by interviewer.
whenOtherWins: 如果规则已经在题面里写清楚，就按规则执行并简短复述你的理解即可，不必再问。
tradeoff: 先问清楚 vs 自行假设后再纠偏
optionExplanations: 凭自己猜测替面试官做了决定，一旦猜错就等于在不该用 AI 设计时用了。
边界不清时先开口确认，一句话就能把后续所有 AI 用法钉死在正确范围内。
全程手写可能白白放弃面试官本来允许的加速手段，规则还没确认就先自我设限。
先斩后奏、等被指出才补救，既被动又显得你事先没想清楚边界。
optionExplanations_en: Guessing on the interviewer's behalf means you might use AI for design exactly when you weren't supposed to.
When the boundary is unclear, one quick question locks down how you can use AI for the rest of the round.
Going fully hand-written can throw away speed the interviewer would have allowed, based on a rule you never confirmed.
Doing it your way and explaining only when caught is reactive, and signals you never thought about the boundary upfront.

q: 补全 AI 规划的分界线：
q_en: Fill in the boundary line for AI-assisted planning:
text: 理解后提出反驳和修改叫{{审阅计划}}；看不懂却点头照做叫{{橡皮图章}}。
why: 面试官看的是你是否还在控制方案：理解后提出反驳和修改是审阅计划；看不懂却点头照做是橡皮图章。
why_en: The line is vetting versus rubber-stamping: pushing back on a plan you understand is control, nodding along to one you couldn't have written is not.
tradeoff: 审阅计划（理解+修改，慢但可控）vs 橡皮图章（照单全收，快但空心）

termDefinitions.meaning: 看不懂却直接盖章通过的行为，这里指对 AI 计划不加判断就照做。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rubber-stamping means approving something without understanding it, here nodding along to an AI plan you couldn't defend.

q: 多数 AI 编码面试题为什么需要先拆分阶段？
q_en: Why do most AI coding interview problems need to be split into phases first?
options: 因为 AI 每次只能生成一行代码
因为拆分能让你跳过写测试这一步
因为问题常含修 bug、加功能、优化等多阶段
因为这类题目从来没有现成代码库
options_en: Because the AI can only generate one line of code at a time.
Because decomposition lets you skip writing tests.
Because these problems usually bundle multiple phases like fixing a bug, adding a feature, then optimizing.
Because this kind of problem never starts with an existing codebase.
why: 多阶段题需要你判断顺序和依赖，否则 AI 容易一次性生成难以验证的大块代码。
why_en: Multi-phase problems need you to decide the order and dependencies, or the AI will produce one large, hard-to-verify block of code.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  BigTask[Big task] --> Phase1[Baseline]
  BigTask --> Phase2[Core feature]
  BigTask --> Phase3[Edges]
  Phase1 --> Prompt1[Small prompt]
  Phase2 --> Prompt2[Small prompt]
optionExplanations: 这个说法不成立，AI 完全能一次输出大段代码，限制不在这里。
拆分和是否写测试无关，每个阶段该测的部分照样要测。
阶段之间彼此有顺序和依赖，你得先想清楚顺序再分步提示 AI。
很多这类面试其实带现成代码库，这不是要拆分的理由。
optionExplanations_en: That's not actually true — the AI can output a large block in one go, so that's not the real limit.
Splitting the work has nothing to do with skipping tests; each phase still needs its own checks.
The phases depend on each other in order, so you have to work out that order before prompting step by step.
Plenty of these interviews do start from an existing codebase, so that's not the real reason to decompose.

q: 开放式从零构建时，哪些顺序原则通常成立？（多选）
q_en: For open-ended greenfield builds, which ordering principles usually hold? (Select all)
options: 先建数据模型，再写依赖这些模型的逻辑
先做核心功能，再补边界情况
先修会影响后续功能的 bug，再加依赖它的新功能
先优化还不存在的代码
options_en: Model your data first, then write the logic that depends on it.
Build the core functionality before handling edge cases.
Fix bugs that block later features before adding features that depend on them.
Optimize code that doesn't exist yet.
why: 这三条顺序能减少返工；反过来先优化还没成形的代码，往往把复杂度引到错误的地方。
why_en: Model-first, core-before-edge, and fix-before-feature ordering reduce rework, while optimizing code that doesn't exist yet wastes effort.
optionExplanations: 先定好对象和关系，后续逻辑才有稳定边界可以依靠。
主路径先跑通，剩下的少数分支能逐个补，不拖累主线。
先解除卡住后续功能的坏基础，别在它上面继续叠新功能。
代码还没写出来，根本没有可测的东西能拿来调优。
optionExplanations_en: Nail down the objects and relations first, so later logic has a stable boundary to build on.
Get the main path working first, then the few edge branches can be patched in without derailing it.
Clear the blocking bug before stacking a new feature on top of a broken base.
There's no code yet to profile or tune — there's nothing to optimize.

scenario: 类似 Shopify 的开放式教程题：你从空仓库和 README 开始，要构建一个小应用。
scenario_en: In a Shopify-like open-ended tutorial task, you start from an empty repo and a README and need to build a small app.
q: 最先应该让计划解决什么？
q_en: What should your plan solve first?
options: 最终性能优化
UI 配色
让 AI 一次写完整应用
先定义核心实体和数据结构
options_en: Final performance optimization.
The UI color scheme.
Let the AI write the entire app in one shot.
Define the core entities and data structures first.
why: 数据结构先定下来，会迫使你先理解系统对象和关系，后续逻辑才有稳定边界。
why_en: Modeling entities first in greenfield work forces you to understand the system's objects and relationships before any logic is written.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目是已有代码里的单点 bug，先定位失败路径比重新建模更重要。
tradeoff: 先建数据模型求稳定边界 vs 先让 AI 快速出一版看效果
optionExplanations: 系统结构还没成形就调优，之后架构一变这些优化全部作废。
配色不影响核心逻辑对不对，不该抢在架构判断前面处理。
把整个应用交给 AI 一次写完，你之后很难解释每个类的职责为什么这样分。
空仓库起步先把对象和关系定下来，后面每一步逻辑才有依据。
optionExplanations_en: Tuning performance before the structure even exists means the work gets thrown away once the architecture shifts.
Color choices don't affect whether the core logic is correct, so they shouldn't jump ahead of the architecture call.
Letting the AI write the whole app in one shot leaves you unable to explain why each class has the responsibilities it does.
Starting from an empty repo, pin down the objects and their relations first so every later step has something to build on.

q: 缺少拆分时，AI 最容易生成什么样的代码？
q_en: Without decomposition, what kind of code is the AI most likely to generate?
options: 清晰、可验证、每步可解释的小改动
职责太杂的大块代码，需求一变就难重构
完全不包含任何实现
只包含测试
options_en: Clean, verifiable, small changes you can explain step by step.
One large block of code that covers too many responsibilities and is hard to refactor once requirements shift.
No implementation at all.
Only test code.
why: 大而泛的提示会把多个决策埋进一个输出，直到很晚才暴露错误方向。
why_en: A broad, undecomposed prompt buries many decisions inside one output, so a wrong direction only surfaces very late.
optionExplanations: 这是拆分得当时才会出现的结果，不是本题问的缺少拆分的后果。
职责混在一起，需求一变就要大改，返工成本随之升高。
AI 通常会给出实现，完全不产出代码不是常见的规划风险。
只有测试没有实现，没法验证真实行为，也不是缺少拆分的典型后果。
optionExplanations_en: That's what good decomposition produces — not the outcome of skipping it, which is what's being asked here.
Responsibilities get tangled together, so any requirement change forces a big rewrite and heavier rework.
The AI usually does produce an implementation; producing nothing at all isn't the typical risk here.
Tests with no implementation can't verify real behavior, and that's not the typical fallout from skipping decomposition either.

q: “Build the scheduler”和“Write the Task constructor”分别错在哪里？
q_en: What is wrong with “Build the scheduler” versus “Write the Task constructor”?
options: 前者太宽，后者太窄
前者太窄，后者太宽
两者都是理想粒度
两者都不能给 AI
options_en: "Build the scheduler" is too broad, and "Write the Task constructor" is too narrow.
"Build the scheduler" is too narrow, and "Write the Task constructor" is too broad.
Both prompts are the ideal granularity.
Neither prompt should ever be given to the AI.
why: 前者把多个算法和设计决策混在一个提示里；后者只是你自己可以直接手写的一行级任务。
why_en: The broad prompt bundles several algorithm and design decisions into one shot, while the narrow one is just a single line you'd type yourself.
tradeoff: 提示太宽（AI 决策过多，难验证）vs 提示太窄（你在替 AI 打字，没有价值）
codeSample:
太宽: "Build the scheduler"
太窄: "Write the Task constructor"
右粒度: 建 Task/Dependency 类型 -> 建依赖图 -> 拓扑排序 -> 处理 cycle
optionExplanations: 校准提示粒度正好卡在两者之间：一个太宽把决策全扔给 AI，一个太窄等于替它打字。
方向说反了：Build the scheduler 才是那个过宽的提示，不是过窄。
两个例子分别踩了过宽和过窄两个极端，都不是理想粒度。
两个提示都能用，只是各自需要往中间粒度调整，不是完全不能给 AI。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the calibration point in the middle: one prompt hands over every decision, the other has you typing for the AI.
The direction is flipped — "Build the scheduler" is the broad one, not the narrow one.
Each example sits at an opposite extreme, so neither is the ideal granularity.
Both prompts are usable, they just need to shift toward the middle granularity — neither is off-limits to the AI.

q: 把 task scheduler with dependencies 的合理拆分排好：
q_en: Put the reasonable decomposition for a task scheduler with dependencies in order:
steps: 用拓扑排序计算合法执行顺序
处理 cycle 情况
建 Task 和 Dependency 类型
根据输入构建依赖图
why: 先建 Task/Dependency 模型，把输入转成依赖图，再用拓扑排序求执行顺序，最后单独处理无解的 cycle。
why_en: For dependency scheduling: model tasks first, build the graph, topologically sort it, then handle the cycle case separately.
tradeoff: 一次性大提示（AI 承担全部决策）vs 按拓扑顺序拆成 4 个小步骤（你逐步验证）
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Model[Model tasks] --> Graph[Build dependency graph]
  Graph --> Ready[Find ready tasks]
  Ready --> Schedule[Assign workers]
  Schedule --> Verify[Verify order]

termDefinitions.meaning: 对有向无环图的节点排序，使每个节点排在它依赖的节点之后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Topological sort orders the nodes of a directed acyclic graph so each node comes after everything it depends on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 依赖图里出现环状依赖，导致不存在合法执行顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cycle is a circular dependency in the graph, which means no valid execution order exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 任务之间的先后依赖关系，通常建模成图中的一条有向边。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dependency is a must-come-before relationship between tasks, usually modeled as a directed edge in the graph.

scenario: 面试时长 45-60 分钟，你要把整道题拆成几个主要阶段写进计划里。
scenario_en: In a 45 to 60 minute interview, you need to split the whole problem into a few main phases in your plan.
q: 这道题的计划粒度，拆成几个阶段最匹配这个时长？
q_en: For that interview length, how many phases is the right planning granularity?
options: 只给一个笼统步骤，让 AI 自己规划全部实现
拆成三到五个可独立验证的阶段
拆成十几个逐行级别的小步骤
步骤数量不设上限，越细越好
options_en: Give the AI one vague step and let it plan the entire implementation.
Break it into three to five independently verifiable phases.
Break it into a dozen-plus line-by-line micro-steps.
Don't cap the step count at all — finer is always better.
why: 45-60 分钟 ÷ 一步一次提示-验证周期 ≈ 3-5 步；这个数字决定你该把计划切多细，也是后面判断有没有过度拆分的参照。
why_en: Divide the 45 to 60 minute interview by one prompt-and-verify cycle per step and you land on three to five steps, which sets how finely to slice your plan.
optionExplanations: 一步到底等于把全部架构决策交给 AI，45-60 分钟根本来不及逐项验证。
把 45 到 60 分钟按单步提示加验证来分配，落点刚好是三到五步。
十几个逐行步骤远超这个时长能验证的次数，变成人工盯着 AI 打字。
步骤越细耗时越多，超出面试时长就没时间跑完整个实现。
optionExplanations_en: One catch-all step hands the AI every architecture call, and 45 to 60 minutes isn't enough to verify it piece by piece.
Pace it at one prompt-and-verify cycle per step across 45 to 60 minutes and you land on three to five steps.
A dozen-plus line-by-line steps blows past how many checks that time budget can fit, turning into micromanaging.
The finer you slice it the more time it eats, and you'll run out of interview time before finishing the build.

scenario: 你已经形成计划：先修 parser bug，再用 BFS 加搜索功能，最后若需要处理加权边再优化。
scenario_en: You have a plan: fix the parser bug first, add search with BFS, then optimize for weighted edges if needed.
q: 在提示 AI 前应该做什么？
q_en: What should you do before prompting the AI?
options: 只在心里记住，不说出来
直接把三步一次性丢给 AI
把计划告诉面试官，给他们纠偏窗口
先优化再修 bug
options_en: Keep it in your head and never say it out loud.
Dump all three steps on the AI in one prompt.
Say the plan out loud to the interviewer so they get a chance to redirect you.
Optimize first, then fix the bug.
why: 说出计划展示战略思考，也给面试官一个在你走偏前就能提醒你的窗口。
why_en: Stating your plan out loud shows strategic thinking and gives the interviewer a window to redirect you before you head the wrong way.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目极小，也至少用一句话说明当前顺序和理由，而不是完全跳过。
tradeoff: 说出计划（多花十秒，换纠偏机会）vs 直接开始写（更快，但走偏了没人拦）

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层扩展、常用于求无权图的最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, or Breadth-First Search, expands level by level and is commonly used to find shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把输入文本解析成结构化数据的组件，这里指代码里已有的解析模块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parser is the component that turns raw input text into structured data.

optionExplanations: 计划只留在你脑子里，面试官没有共享上下文，后面每次提示都要重新解释背景。
三步一次性丢给 AI，三个决策被压进一次输出，容易生成难验证的大块代码。
已经形成计划时，先花几秒说给面试官听，能在你走偏前就被拦住。
parser 的 bug 还没修，后面靠它的搜索功能等于建在坏地基上。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping the plan in your head only means the interviewer has no shared context, and you re-explain the background every prompt after.
Dumping all three steps on the AI at once buries three decisions in a single output that's hard to verify.
Once you have a plan, saying it out loud gives the interviewer a few seconds to redirect you before you drift.
The parser bug is still broken, so the search feature you build next sits on a bad foundation.

q: 把计划说给面试官听有哪些作用？（多选）
q_en: What does saying your plan out loud to the interviewer accomplish? (Select all)
options: 保证 AI 输出永远正确
展示你在战略性思考
给面试官机会及时纠偏
建立共享上下文，后续提示更容易被理解
options_en: It guarantees the AI's output is always correct.
It shows you're thinking strategically.
It gives the interviewer a chance to redirect you early.
It creates shared context so your later prompts are easier to follow.
why: 计划沟通能同步方向和评估点，但仍需要你在执行时验证 AI 的结果，它不会替你保证正确性。
why_en: Sharing the plan syncs direction and gives the interviewer something to evaluate, but you still have to verify the AI's output yourself.
optionExplanations: 说出计划不能替代验证这一步，AI 仍可能跑偏或出错。
十秒话就能让面试官判断你是不是有方向，而不只是在打字。
面试官能在你投入实现前先拦住走偏的方向，省下返工时间。
后面每个提示，面试官都能对上你当前在做哪一步，少一次重新解释。
optionExplanations_en: Saying the plan out loud doesn't replace verification — the AI can still drift or get it wrong.
Ten seconds of talking lets the interviewer tell you have direction, not just that you're typing.
The interviewer can stop a wrong turn before you sink time implementing it.
Every prompt after that, the interviewer can place which step you're on, so you skip re-explaining.

scenario: 你已经决定在现有 `Grid` 类上用 BFS 找迷宫最短路径。
scenario_en: You have decided to use BFS on the existing `Grid` class to find the shortest maze path.
q: 哪条提示最能体现“用计划指导 AI”？
q_en: Which prompt best shows that you are using your plan to guide the AI?
options: 跟 AI 说 solve the maze 就行，别的不用管
在 Grid 类里用 BFS，指定入口和返回坐标路径
随便写个高效算法，思路交给 AI 决定
先把 Grid 类整个重写一遍再说
options_en: "Just tell the AI to solve the maze, nothing else specified."
"Implement BFS in the Grid class, with a named entry point and a returned coordinate path."
"Write some efficient algorithm, leave the approach up to the AI."
"Rewrite the whole Grid class first."
why: 提示把算法选择、入口对象和返回值都交代清楚，AI 负责实现细节，而不是替你决定路线。
why_en: This prompt spells out the chosen algorithm, the entry object, and the return value, so the AI implements your plan instead of choosing its own route.
whenOtherWins: 如果边权不一致，BFS 不再适合最短路径，应改用 Dijkstra 或 A*，并在提示里说明原因。
codeSample:
Implement BFS in the existing Grid class.
Start from start, stop at end, and return the shortest path as a list of coordinates.
Use the existing Cell representation; do not introduce a parallel grid model.
tradeoff: 笼统提示（AI 决定算法，快但失控）vs 精确提示（你决定算法，AI 负责落地）
optionDiagrams:
flowchart LR
  Raw[Raw prompt] --> AI[AI chooses plan]
  AI --> Drift[Drift]

flowchart LR
  Plan[Plan] --> AI[Focused implementation]
  AI --> Review[Review diff]

flowchart LR
  Vague[Vague ask] --> AI[AI guesses structure]
  AI --> Mismatch[Mismatch risk]

flowchart LR
  Rewrite[Rewrite all] --> Scope[Scope creep]
  Scope --> Risk[Risk]

termDefinitions.meaning: 广度优先搜索，按层扩展节点，能在无权图里找到最短路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS, Breadth-First Search, expands nodes level by level and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理带权最短路径的经典算法，权重非负时保证最优解。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths in weighted graphs and guarantees optimality when weights are non-negative.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 Dijkstra 基础上加启发函数、更快收敛到目标的最短路径算法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A-star adds a heuristic on top of Dijkstra's algorithm to reach the target faster.

optionExplanations: 只说 solve the maze，AI 会自己挑算法和结构，你的判断没有出现在提示里。
算法、入口对象、返回格式都写清楚了，AI 复用现有 Cell，产出能直接接进代码库。
只要求高效不指定算法，AI 可能选一个和现有 Grid/Cell 不兼容的实现。
没必要的重写会把范围扩大到 Grid 本身，偏离找最短路径这个目标。
optionExplanations_en: Just saying "solve the maze" lets the AI pick its own algorithm and structure — your judgment never makes it into the prompt.
Naming the algorithm, entry point, and return format means the AI reuses the existing Cell and the result drops straight into the codebase.
Asking only for efficiency without naming an algorithm risks the AI picking something incompatible with the existing Grid and Cell.
An unnecessary rewrite drags scope onto the Grid class itself, away from the actual goal of finding the shortest path.

q: 把原始题目直接粘给 AI，而不先转化成自己的计划，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What is the main risk of pasting the raw problem into AI instead of translating it into your own plan first?
options: AI 一定无法理解英文题目
代码会自动通过全部测试
你会因此节省验证时间
AI 给方案，但未必贴合代码库或预期
options_en: The AI definitely can't understand an English problem statement.
The code will automatically pass all the tests.
You'll end up saving time on verification.
The AI will produce a solution, but it might not fit the codebase or expectations.
why: 原题提示让模型自己决定关键路线，你也失去了展示问题拆解和选型判断的机会。
why_en: Pasting the raw problem lets the model pick the approach on its own, and you lose the chance to show your own decomposition and judgment.
optionExplanations: 现代模型理解英文题目基本没有障碍，这不是真实风险。
方案通不通过测试，跟有没有先转化成自己的计划没有必然关系。
跳过转化通常不会省验证时间，返工反而可能更多。
AI 会给出方案，但它自己选的路线可能忽略代码库结构或面试官的期待。
optionExplanations_en: Modern models have no real trouble reading an English prompt — that's not the actual risk.
Whether the code passes the tests has no direct link to whether you translated the problem into your own plan.
Skipping the translation step rarely saves verification time — it usually means more rework instead.
The AI will produce something, but the route it picks on its own can ignore the codebase's structure or what's expected.

q: 补全好提示应包含的上下文：
q_en: Fill in the context a good prompt should include:
text: 好的实现提示应说明选择的{{算法}}、要复用的{{数据结构}}，以及如何和现有{{接口}}交互。
why: 这些信息让 AI 沿你的计划写代码，而不是发明并行架构；缺一项，AI 就多一分自由决定权。
why_en: A good implementation prompt names the algorithm, the data structures to reuse, and the existing interfaces so the AI follows your plan instead of inventing its own.

q: 提示“太具体”会带来什么问题？
q_en: What problem does an overly specific prompt create?
options: 你变成逐行口述，AI 只是代打
AI 会掌握太多上下文信息
输出内容一定会变得更短
面试官会看不到你的想法
options_en: You end up dictating line by line, and the AI is just typing for you.
The AI ends up with too much context.
The output is guaranteed to be shorter.
The interviewer can no longer see your thinking.
why: 目标是指导 AI 实现你的方案，而不是把每个变量名和每行代码都口述给它。
why_en: The goal is to direct the AI to implement your approach, not to dictate every variable name and every line yourself.
tradeoff: 太具体（你在打字，AI 只是代打）vs 右粒度（你定方向，AI 处理实现体力活）
optionExplanations: 提示细到每个变量名，你花的时间跟自己打字差不多，AI 没帮你分担设计。
上下文多少不是问题所在，缺的是留给 AI 的判断空间。
输出长短不是核心问题，谁在做设计决策才是关键。
面试官反而能看到你在口述每一行，只是看到的是打字而不是判断。
optionExplanations_en: When the prompt spells out every variable name, you spend as much time as typing it yourself — the AI isn't carrying any design load.
The amount of context isn't the issue — what's missing is room for the AI to actually judge anything.
Output length isn't the core problem — who's making the design call is.
The interviewer actually sees you dictating every line, just typing instead of deciding.

q: AI 回来后偷偷把你选的算法换成另一个，应该怎么处理？
q_en: If the AI quietly swaps your chosen algorithm for another one, how should you respond?
options: 只要能编译就接受
立即放弃原计划，不解释
看理由站不站得住，站不住就纠偏
忽略测试
options_en: Accept it as long as it compiles.
Abandon your original plan immediately without asking why.
Check whether there's a good reason; if not, correct it and redirect the AI.
Ignore the tests.
why: 模型可以提供替代思路，但方案改变必须经过你判断，否则你就不再是驱动者。
why_en: The model can propose alternatives, but any change of approach must pass through your judgment, or you stop being the one driving.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Output[AI output] --> Drift{Changed algorithm?}
  Drift -->|yes| Stop[Stop and name drift]
  Stop --> Repoint[Repoint prompt]
  Repoint --> Verify[Verify against plan]
optionExplanations: 编译通过只说明语法没问题，不代表换掉的算法真的适合这道题。
不问理由直接放弃计划，如果 AI 的替代方案其实更好，你就白白丢了一个合理 pivot。
先判断替代算法有没有站得住的理由，站得住就用，站不住就纠偏重定向。
跳过测试只会让偷换算法的副作用更晚才暴露出来。
optionExplanations_en: Compiling only means the syntax is fine — it says nothing about whether the swapped algorithm actually fits this problem.
Dropping the plan without asking why means you might be throwing away a genuinely better alternative.
Check whether the swap has a solid reason first — keep it if it does, correct and redirect the AI if it doesn't.
Skipping the tests just delays when the side effects of the swapped algorithm finally show up.

q: 哪些情况是修改计划的合理理由？（多选）
q_en: Which situations are valid reasons to revise the plan? (Select all)
options: 发现新的性能约束
数据模型比取向时看到的更复杂
AI 随口建议重写一切但你说不出理由
面试官给出改变范围的提示
options_en: You discover a new performance constraint.
The data model turns out more complex than it looked during orientation.
The AI casually suggests rewriting everything and you can't say why that would help.
The interviewer drops a hint that changes the scope.
why: 计划应该随新事实变化，而不是随 AI 的每一个建议摇摆。
why_en: Revise the plan when new facts change the problem, not just because the AI suggests something different.
optionExplanations: 约束一变，原计划可能不再可行，这时候改是有依据的。
模型复杂度变了，原来的拆分粒度和接口边界可能不够用了。
没有收益说明的重写建议只是噪声，跟着走等于把方向让给了 AI。
范围一变，哪些组件还要不要做都会跟着变，计划自然要跟上。
