termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment, the editor software you normally write code in, like VS Code.

optionExplanations: 浏览器编辑器的手感和本地 IDE 不一样，提前摸熟能省掉正式面试当天的适应成本。
内置 AI 能力和提示方式都固定死了，练的就是怎么在这个限制下把话说清楚。
按阶段推题要求你按顺序管理时间和优先级，这套节奏得提前练才不生疏。
本地插件配置在结构化沙盒里根本用不上，这条属于开放式练习复刻的条件。
optionExplanations_en: The browser editor feels different from a local IDE, so getting used to it in advance saves adjustment time on the real day.
The built-in AI's capability and prompting style are fixed, so practice is really about phrasing clearly within that limit.
Working through staged problems means managing time and priority in a set order, a rhythm that needs rehearsing beforehand.
Your local plugin setup simply isn't available inside the structured sandbox — that's what open-ended practice recreates instead.

q: 开放式练习和结构化练习的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between open-ended and structured practice?
options: 开放式用自己工具，结构化用平台内置工具
开放式不需要 AI，结构化不能写代码
开放式没有时间限制，结构化没有反馈
两者完全一样
options_en: Open-ended uses your own tools, structured uses the platform's built-in tools.
Open-ended doesn't need AI at all, and structured doesn't let you write code.
Open-ended has no time limit, and structured gives no feedback.
The two are completely identical.
why: 两条通道的分界在于工具提供方：开放式用你自己的编辑器和 AI，结构化用平台锁定的浏览器沙盒和内置 AI。
why_en: The core difference is who provides the tools: open-ended uses your own editor and AI, while structured uses the platform's locked-down browser sandbox and built-in AI.
tradeoff: 复刻自带工具的真实工作流 vs 复刻平台锁定的受限环境

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 谁提供工具是真正的分界线，这条决定了你练习时该复刻自己的环境还是平台的环境。
两条通道其实都要写代码、都用得上 AI，说其中一条不需要 AI 是错的。
两条通道都设了计时和反馈机制，说哪一条没有时限或没有反馈是错的。
如果两者真的完全一样，平台压根没必要拆成两条练习通道。
optionExplanations_en: Who supplies the tools is the real dividing line, and it decides whether practice should recreate your own setup or the platform's.
Both tracks actually involve writing code and using AI — claiming one skips AI entirely is wrong.
Both tracks come with timing and feedback built in — claiming either one lacks a limit or feedback is wrong.
If the two were truly identical, there'd be no reason for the platform to split practice into two separate tracks.

scenario: 练习反馈说你代码完成了，但 AI 聊天显示你多次接受了无法解释的实现。
scenario_en: Your practice feedback says the code was completed, but the AI chat shows you repeatedly accepted implementations you could not explain.
q: 下一轮练习最该改什么？
q_en: What should you change most in the next practice round?
options: 练习每次 AI 输出后，公开复述并解释关键实现逻辑
换更简单的题目，跳过阅读 AI 生成的代码
为了赶时间，直接停用所有单元测试
把精力全部放在更快点击提交按钮上
options_en: After every AI output, practice restating and explaining the key implementation logic out loud.
Switch to easier problems and skip reading the AI-generated code.
Turn off all unit tests to save time.
Put all your effort into clicking submit faster.
why: 反馈显示的是控制力缺口：能出代码不等于你在掌控实现；下一轮要练成每次输出后立刻复述解释。
why_en: The feedback points to a control gap, since finishing the code isn't the same as owning it, so next time practice narrating and explaining every AI output immediately.
whenOtherWins: 如果反馈主要是算法思路选错，就该回去补相关算法模式，而不是只练讲解习惯。
tradeoff: 每次输出后立即复述解释 vs 全盘接受不追问
codeSample:
After each AI output, say out loud:
1. What this code does: ...
2. Why I accept or reject it: ...
3. One thing I'd verify before moving on: ...

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 把复述解释变成每次 AI 输出后的固定动作，练出来的是你能不能对任何一段代码说清它在做什么。
换更简单的题目回避了真正的问题：你现在还是没练成解释已有输出的能力。
停掉单元测试后，连一段解释不清的实现是否正确都没法验证，风险反而更大。
提交更快只是速度指标，证明不了你理解了 AI 写出来的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Making restate-and-explain a fixed step after every AI output trains whether you can actually narrate what any piece of code does.
Switching to an easier problem dodges the real gap — you still haven't built the skill of explaining output you already have.
Turning off unit tests means you can't even check correctness for an implementation you can't explain, which raises the risk.
Submitting faster is just a speed metric — it proves nothing about whether you actually understood what the AI wrote.

q: 补全准备原则：
q_en: Complete the preparation principle:
text: 准备 AI 编码面试不要只读内容；要在{{真实约束}}下练习，提交{{代码和聊天}}，再用{{反馈}}调整。

why_en: Reading alone can't teach the dual-conversation rhythm; only practicing under real constraints and reviewing both code and chat turns knowledge into an interview-day workflow.

电话初筛和现场终面说的是招聘流程的阶段先后，不是同一场编码面试里的工具环境差异。

Confuses an AI coding interview with a plain algorithm quiz — the defining trait here is AI helping you code, not solo algorithm writing.
System design and behavioral rounds are different interview types altogether, not the two format buckets inside a coding interview.

开放式题目通常从零构建、自由度更高，「题目固定、没有自由度」说的其实是结构化。
optionExplanations_en: Open-ended interviews actually require communication and encourage using your own AI — this flips both sides.
Right — familiar tools let you move faster, but with no platform to hide behind, your prompts, tool switches, and any messy steps are all visible to the interviewer.
Open-ended still needs tests to verify AI output, so 'no tests' doesn't hold.
Open-ended problems usually start from scratch with more freedom — 'fixed problem, no freedom' actually describes structured.

scenario: 开放式面试里，面试官能看到你的提示、工具切换和每一步操作。
scenario_en: In an open-ended interview, the interviewer can see your prompts, tool switching, and every step you take.
q: 这带来的主要要求是什么？
q_en: What main requirement does this create?
options: 提示、工具切换、验证和沟通都必须真的可靠
你可以完全隐藏所有决策过程
你完全不需要解释 AI 输出
你完全不用提前准备好本地环境
why: 没有平台遮挡，日常工作流本身就是评估对象，混乱的操作会直接暴露给面试官。
why_en: Because everything is visible, your prompting, tool switching, verification, and communication all need to actually hold up under scrutiny.
options_en: Your prompting, tool switching, verification, and communication all need to actually be solid.
You can completely hide all of your decision-making.
You don't need to explain AI output at all.
You don't need to prepare your local environment ahead of time at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 对，既然一切都被看到，你的提示、工具切换、验证和沟通就必须经得起当场审视。
屏幕共享下决策过程本来就无处可藏，说能隐藏正好说反了。
解释 AI 输出的能力恰恰是这类面试的评估重点，不是可以省略的部分。
环境没提前准备好，摩擦只会在面试现场暴露，准备仍是必要前提。
optionExplanations_en: Right — since everything is visible, your prompting, tool switching, verification, and communication all need to actually hold up under live scrutiny.
Under screen sharing there's nowhere for decision-making to hide — this has it backwards.
The ability to explain AI output is exactly what this round evaluates, not something you can skip.
An unprepared environment just exposes its friction live on interview day — prep is still required.

scenario: 开放式问题常常给你一个空仓库或一份 README。
scenario_en: Open-ended problems often give you an empty repo or a README.
q: 开放式问题通常更偏向什么类型的任务？
q_en: What type of task do open-ended problems usually lean toward?
options: 从空仓库或 README 从零构建应用
只在已有平台代码里改一行
只审批选择题
只口头解释理论，不动手写代码
why: 开放式题更强调你能否从零设计、建模并用 AI 加速实现，而不是在已有代码里做局部修改。
why_en: Open-ended problems typically start from an empty repo or README and ask you to build a working application from scratch.
options_en: Building an application from scratch, starting from an empty repo or README.
Changing a single line in existing platform code.
Only reviewing multiple-choice questions.
Only explaining theory verbally, without writing any code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 对，开放式题常常从一个空仓库或 README 起步，考的是从零设计和实现的能力。
改一行已有代码更接近结构化第一阶段的形态，不是开放式的典型起点。
选择题考不到实现和验证能力，和编码面试的形式不符。
不写代码就没有可运行、可评审的产出，动手编码是这类面试的核心。
optionExplanations_en: Right — open-ended problems often start from an empty repo or README, testing your ability to design and build from scratch.
Editing one existing line is closer to structured's phase-one shape, not open-ended's typical starting point.
A multiple-choice quiz can't test implementation or verification skill, which doesn't match a coding interview.
Without writing code there's no runnable, reviewable output — hands-on coding is core to this format.

scenario: 开放式面试要求你从空仓库开始设计并实现一个可运行的应用。
scenario_en: An open-ended interview asks you to design and implement a runnable app starting from an empty repo.
q: 为什么开放式 AI 编码面试会更依赖低层设计能力？
q_en: Why do open-ended AI coding interviews rely more on low-level design skill?
options: 因为 AI 不能写代码
因为可工作、可扩展的软件结构仍需你自己决定
因为开放式面试不考功能是否正确
因为只需要画 UML，不用写代码
why: 从零构建时，实体、接口和扩展点都要由你定，AI 只能帮你更快实现这些决定，不能替你做设计判断。
why_en: Open-ended interviews lean on low-level design because you must define entities, interfaces, and extensible structure yourself, even though AI accelerates implementation.
options_en: Because AI can't write code.
Because a working, extensible software structure still needs you to decide it.
Because open-ended interviews don't evaluate whether the feature works.
Because you only need to draw a UML diagram, not write code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计，指定义实体、接口和类结构的设计能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD, or low-level design, is the skill of defining entities, interfaces, and class structure.

optionExplanations: AI 恰恰能写出大量代码，只是不会替你做设计判断，这条和 AI 的真实能力相反。
对，实体、接口和扩展点都得由你自己定，AI 只加速实现，不替你做设计决定。
功能是否真的能跑起来依然是评估的一部分，不会被忽略。
画图代替不了一个真正跑起来的可运行应用，范围窄于实际要求。
optionExplanations_en: AI can actually write plenty of code — it just doesn't make design decisions for you, the opposite of what this claims.
Right — entities, interfaces, and extension points are still yours to decide; AI only speeds up implementation, not the design judgment itself.
Whether the feature actually works is still part of the evaluation, not something skipped.
A diagram can't substitute for a genuinely runnable application — narrower than what's actually required.

scenario: 同样叫开放式格式，不同公司在 AI 使用要求和推进方式上可能不一样。
scenario_en: Even when the format is called open-ended, companies can differ in AI-use requirements and how the task progresses.
q: 开放式格式在不同公司之间可能有哪些具体差异？（多选）
q_en: What concrete differences can open-ended formats have across companies? (Select all that apply.)
options: 有些公司要求必须用 AI 并显式打分
所有公司的开放式面试完全一样，细节不需要确认
有些公司按测试用例逐步加功能
有些公司按团队从结构化 DSA 到开放仓库工作不等
why: 不同公司的开放式细节不同：比如 Canva 强制打分、Rippling 按测试用例递进，所以必须向 recruiter 逐项确认。
why_en: Open-ended details vary by company, from mandated and scored AI use to incremental test-driven builds to team-specific formats, so confirm specifics with the recruiter.
options_en: Some companies require AI use and score it explicitly.
All companies run open-ended interviews identically, with no details to confirm.
Some companies add features incrementally against test cases.
Some companies vary by team, from structured DSA to open repo work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 对，比如强制打分 AI 使用率的公司确实存在，练习时要把提示过程做成可展示的动作。
错，后面三条列出的都是真实存在的公司差异，「完全一样」和它们矛盾。
对，按测试用例递增加功能的公司存在，练习该拆成小步提交而不是一次性完成。
对，同一家公司不同团队的格式也可能不同，必须单独向 recruiter 确认这个团队的做法。
optionExplanations_en: True — some companies really do mandate and explicitly score AI use, so practice needs a demonstrable prompting habit.
False — the other three options list real variations that exist, contradicting 'identical, nothing to confirm'.
True — some companies add features incrementally against test cases, so practice should be small commits, not one big push.
True — format can even vary by team within the same company, so confirm that specific team's approach separately.

q: 补全首先要问 recruiter 的格式问题：
q_en: Fill in the first format question to ask the recruiter:
text: 先确认这是 {{Structured}} 还是 {{Open-Ended}}，以及是否有{{starter code}}或要从零开始。
why: 这两个答案直接决定你接下来该练平台适应，还是练本地从零构建的完整流程。

q: 如果是结构化面试，应该问 recruiter 哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: If it is a structured interview, what should you ask the recruiter? (Select all that apply.)
options: 使用哪个平台：CoderPad 还是 HackerRank
是否有 practice environment 可以提前熟悉
我应该穿什么颜色衣服
面试有几个阶段
why: 平台、练习环境和阶段数量直接影响工具准备和当天的时间分配，是结构化面试该确认的核心信息。
why_en: For structured interviews, ask about the platform, practice-environment availability, and number of phases, since those drive tool prep and pacing.
options_en: Which platform: CoderPad or HackerRank.
Whether there's a practice environment to try beforehand.
What color clothes I should wear.
How many phases the interview has.

termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

optionExplanations: 该问，知道平台才能去对应网站提前注册练习，不会练错工具。
该问，有练习环境就该用掉，提前踩坑，正式面试就不用再踩。

optionExplanations_en: Worth asking — knowing the platform lets you register and practice on the right site instead of the wrong tool.
Worth asking — use the practice environment if one exists, so quirks get hit ahead of time instead of on the day.
Not worth asking — clothing color has no real bearing on tool prep or pacing.
Worth asking — knowing the phase count lets you plan roughly how much time to leave for each one.

q_en: If it is an open-ended interview, what should you ask the recruiter? (Select all that apply.)

AI 工具是否有限制
公司是否偏好某个工具，比如 Cursor
是否需要 push 到仓库，还是屏幕共享即可
why: 开放式的关键风险在环境准备和交付方式，提前问清 AI 工具限制、偏好和交付形式，能避免当天卡在工具或权限上。
why_en: For open-ended interviews, clarify AI-tool restrictions, tool preferences, and whether code must be pushed, since environment and delivery are the real risks.
options_en: Whether the interviewer will just hand over the final answer.
Whether there are restrictions on AI tools.
Whether the company prefers a specific tool, like Cursor.
Whether you need to push to a repository, or screen share is enough.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

Worth asking — if there are restrictions, swap your practice to a tool that's actually allowed, avoiding a banned tool on the day.
Worth asking — if the company prefers a specific tool, installing it ahead saves setup time on interview day.
Worth asking — if a push is required, confirm repo access in advance so you don't get stuck requesting permissions on the day.

scenario: recruiter 对「AI-enabled」说得很模糊，你想问出具体准备要求。
scenario_en: The recruiter is vague about AI-enabled, and you want to ask for concrete preparation requirements.
q: 哪句话最容易得到有用信息？

options: 这次面试整体难度大吗？
能不能直接把答案告诉我？
这次的 AI 会不会特别聪明？
面试前机器该提前装好设置好什么？
why: 询问机器准备会自然带出平台、工具限制、仓库和屏幕共享等具体信息，比直接问「难不难」更容易得到可执行的答案。
why_en: Asking what to set up on your machine tends to surface concrete platform and tool details, more useful than asking how hard the interview is.
whenOtherWins: 如果 recruiter 能直接回答格式，就先问「structured 还是 open-ended」更省一轮往返。
tradeoff: 问具体准备动作换取可执行信息 vs 问笼统难度换不到细节
options_en: Is this interview overall pretty hard?
Can you just tell me the answer directly?
Will the AI for this round be especially smart?
What should I have set up on my machine before the interview?

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during the interview or practice.

optionExplanations: 问难度换来的多半是「还好」之类的主观评价，转化不成具体的准备动作。
recruiter 不会也不该提供最终答案，这类问题问不出准备信息。
AI 聪明与否和你该怎么准备没有关系，答不到点子上。
对，问机器设置会倒逼对方说出平台、权限、工具这些具体细节，直接换来可执行的准备清单。
optionExplanations_en: A difficulty question usually gets a vague 'not too bad', which never converts into a concrete action.
Recruiters won't and shouldn't hand over the final answer, so this yields no prep information.
Whether the AI is smart has nothing to do with how you should prepare — it misses the point.
Right — asking about machine setup forces out concrete platform, access, and tool details, converting directly into an actionable prep checklist.

scenario_en: You need to send a short email confirming the AI coding interview format so you can choose the right practice environment.
q: 哪段问题清单最贴近文章建议？

options: 只问对方能不能直接透露标准答案
问清赛制、起点、平台阶段、AI 限制和交付方式
只问 AI 会不会直接替我顺利通过面试
只问这轮面试整体难度到底如何
why: 这组问题覆盖格式、起点、平台阶段、AI 限制和交付方式，能直接转化成一份具体的练习计划。
why_en: This question list covers format, starter code, platform, phases, AI restrictions, and delivery, turning directly into a concrete prep plan.
whenOtherWins: 如果邮件要更短，至少确认格式和需要提前设置的环境。

codeSample:

Ask about format, starting point, platform phases, AI restrictions, and delivery.
Only ask whether the AI will get me straight through the interview.
Only ask how hard this round is overall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中协助你写代码的编程助手模型。

optionExplanations: recruiter 不会透露标准答案，这类问题问不出任何可用的准备信息。

AI 的角色是加速实现，评估的仍是你的判断和控制力，这个问题误解了它的作用。
只问难度得到的是主观感受，换不到具体该练什么环境或工具。
optionExplanations_en: The recruiter won't reveal the standard answer, so this yields no usable prep information.
Right — this list hits every axis that decides your practice target: format, starting point, platform stage, AI limits, and how you'll deliver work, nothing left unasked.
AI's role is accelerating implementation; your judgment and control are still what's evaluated, so this misreads AI's role.
Asking only about difficulty gets a subjective impression, not concrete direction on which environment or tools to practice.

q: 把根据格式调整准备的决策链排好：
q_en: Put the decision chain for format-based preparation in order:
steps: 结构化：练浏览器平台、内置 AI、阶段节奏
从邀请或 recruiter 确认格式

why_en: Confirm the format first, then match practice to it: rehearse platform pacing for structured, or your own tools and delivery flow for open-ended.
tradeoff: 先确认格式再匹配练习 vs 不分格式统一刷题
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Confirm[Confirm format] --> Match[Match practice]
  Match --> Tools[Set tool constraints]

options_en: Structured practices adapting to a constrained platform; open-ended practices showing a real workflow.

optionExplanations: 对，结构化的备战重点是适应受限平台的手感和节奏，开放式则要练到能在全程可见下展示真实的设计与工作流。
