termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 这是编出来的情节——题目里没有厨师请假这回事，PREP 也没有闲置。
Pasta 的 chop 排在 Salad 后面才轮到，等它做完时 grill 已经空等了 30 秒，这正是浪费所在。
题目没有说哪个厨师不会用某个 station，这个说法没有依据。
同时段安排多个 step 给同一厨师本身就违反约束，greedy 根本不会这样排。
optionExplanations_en: This is invented -- nothing in the setup says a chef is off shift, and PREP isn't sitting idle here.
Pasta's chop only gets its turn after Salad's, so by the time it's ready the grill has already sat empty for 30 seconds -- that's the waste.
Nothing in the setup says any chef can't run a given station, so this claim has no basis.
Double-booking one chef on two steps at once would break the constraint outright, which greedy never does.

q: 为什么说“问题不在换个更好的 chef”？
q_en: Why is the problem not simply picking a better chef?
options: 所有 chef 的速度参数其实完全一样，无论换成谁来做都没有任何区别
station 完全没有任何容量限制，可以同时让好几位厨师并行处理
greedy 已用 specialists，浪费来自 step 顺序排空 grill
makespan 这个最终指标根本就不受 step 排列顺序变化的影响
options_en: Every chef's speed factor is actually exactly the same, so it makes no difference at all who does it.
A station has no capacity limit whatsoever and can let several chefs work on it in parallel.
Greedy already uses the specialists; the waste comes from step order leaving the grill idle.
The final makespan metric is not affected by changes to step ordering in any way.
why: Pasta 晚到 grill 不是因为 chef 慢，而是因为 Pasta 的上一步排晚了，需要优化的是 ordering。
why_en: The bottleneck is step ordering, not a failure to pick the station specialists.
tradeoff: 把浪费归因于 chef 选择 vs 把浪费归因于 step 顺序（ordering）

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 station 上速度是 0.5 factor 的 chef，比其余 1.5 factor 的 chef 快三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialist is the one chef who runs a given station at half the base time, three times faster than a non-specialist there.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

optionExplanations: 厨师速度并不相同——specialist 比 non-specialist 快三倍，这不是这题的病因。
station 恰恰是稀缺资源，同一时间只能服务一位厨师，并不能并行。
greedy 挑的已经是各 station 最快的厨师，真正的浪费出在 Pasta 排队排晚了，问题在 ordering 不在 chef。
顺序恰恰决定了 makespan——本题的 30 秒差距就是顺序调整消掉的。
optionExplanations_en: Chef speeds aren't equal at all -- specialists run three times faster than non-specialists, so that's not the culprit here.
A station is exactly the scarce resource -- it serves one chef at a time and can't run in parallel.
Greedy already assigns the fastest chef per station; the real waste is that Pasta's turn comes too late -- the fix is ordering, not chef choice.
Order absolutely drives makespan -- the 30-second gap in this example disappears once the order is fixed.

scenario: 你想停止按 dish 输入顺序一路走到底，而是允许不同 dish 的 ready steps 交错。
scenario_en: You want to stop walking dishes strictly in input order and allow ready steps from different dishes to interleave.
q: 第二版 dispatch 策略是什么？
q_en: What is the second dispatch strategy?
options: 继续按输入顺序做完第一个 dish 再做第二个 dish
随机选一个未完成的 step，完全不管前置关系
每轮从所有 dish 的 ready step 里选最早完成者提交
一次性把所有 step 都提前排给同一个 chef
options_en: Keep finishing dishes one at a time in strict input order.
Pick a random unfinished step while ignoring precedence entirely.
Each round, commit whichever ready step across all dishes finishes earliest.
Assign every step to the same single chef up front.
why: dispatch 延后了承诺时间，可以 interleave dishes，但仍是单向 greedy，不能撤销已选步骤。
why_en: Dispatch chooses the earliest-finishing ready step across dishes each round.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标只需要简单合法排程，dish-order greedy 更短；如果需要最优，dispatch 仍不够。
tradeoff: 延后承诺、按 ready step 交错 vs 提前锁定 dish 顺序
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[All unfinished dishes] --> B[Collect one ready step each]
B --> C[Score earliest finish]
C --> D[Pick best ready step]
D --> E[Commit and update resources]
E --> A

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 dish 里下一个可以开始的 step，因为它前面的 step 都已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is a dish's next step, eligible to run once every earlier step in that dish is done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

optionExplanations: 这其实还是第一版 dish-order greedy 的做法，没有做出交错。
无视前置关系随便选步骤会直接产出非法 schedule，不是 dispatch 的策略。
每一轮从所有未完成 dish 的 ready step 里挑一个能最早完成的提交，让不同 dish 得以交错——这就是 dispatch。
把所有 step 提前塞给一个厨师，既不合法也没法体现多厨师协作。
optionExplanations_en: That's actually just the first dish-order greedy pass again -- no interleaving happens there.
Picking a step at random while ignoring precedence would produce an illegal schedule, not what dispatch does.
Each round it grabs whichever ready step, across all dishes, finishes earliest and commits it -- letting dishes interleave. That's dispatch.
Front-loading every step onto one chef is both illegal and throws away multi-chef parallelism.

q: 填空：任一时刻，每个未完成 dish 最多只有 {{一个}} ready step，也就是它的 {{下一道}} recipe step。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: at any time, each unfinished dish has at most {{one}} ready step, its {{next}} recipe step.
text: 任一时刻，每个未完成 dish 最多只有 {{一个}} ready step，也就是它的 {{下一道}} recipe step。
why: 同一 dish 内部步骤不能并行，后续 step 要等前一步完成，搜索候选只需要看每个 dish 的 next_step。
why_en: Each unfinished dish exposes only its next recipe step as a ready candidate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 dish 里下一个可以开始的 step，因为它前面的 step 都已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is a dish's next step, eligible to run once every earlier step in that dish is done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一道 dish 内部固定顺序的 station step 链，后一步必须等前一步完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recipe is a dish's fixed chain of station steps, where each step must wait for the previous one to finish.

scenario: dispatch 每轮有多个 ready step 候选，每个候选也要试所有 chefs。
scenario_en: In dispatch, each round has multiple ready-step candidates, and each candidate still tries all chefs.
q: `key = (end, start, index)` 的作用是什么？
q_en: What is `key = (end, start, index)` doing?
options: 计算这一整批 dish 剩余全部工作量的全局安全下界数值是多少
判断这份 recipe 的文本内容里是否出现了重复片段
按完成时间、开始时间、dish index 做确定性 tie-break
强制只挑选这批候选厨师里速度最慢的那一个来做
options_en: Compute exactly what the global safe lower bound is over this whole batch of dishes' remaining work.
Check whether this recipe's text content contains a repeated fragment somewhere.
Sort by finish time, start time, then dish index as a deterministic tie-break.
Force the selection of whichever candidate chef in this batch is the slowest.
codeSample:
key = (end, start, index)
if best_key is None or key < best_key:
    best_key = key
    best_move = (index, dish, step_index, station, chef, start, end)
why: dispatch 仍然是局部最早完成规则，tie-break 只是让输出稳定，它没有全局 lookahead。
why_en: The dispatch key chooses the locally earliest-finishing ready step with deterministic tie-breaking.
whenOtherWins: 如果改成 branch-and-bound，候选排序只是搜索顺序，不能直接提交第一个。
tradeoff: 局部最早完成规则 vs 全局 lookahead/下界剪枝（dispatch 没有后者）

termDefinitions.meaning: 当多个候选的主要排序键相同时，用来确定唯一顺序的次要比较规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tie-break is a secondary comparison rule that produces one order when candidates are equal on the main sort key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 这段 key 不是在算安全下界，dispatch 阶段还没有这个概念。
这跟 recipe 内容是否重复完全无关，key 里没有比较菜谱文本。
先比完成时间，再比开始时间，最后用 dish index 兜底，让并列候选有唯一确定的排序——这就是这个 key 的作用。
代码选的是结束时间最小的候选，不是刻意挑最慢的厨师。
optionExplanations_en: This key isn't computing any safe lower bound -- that concept doesn't exist yet at the dispatch stage.
It has nothing to do with recipe content repeating; the key never compares recipe text.
It compares finish time first, then start time, then falls back to dish index so tied candidates get one deterministic order -- that's what this key does.
The code keeps the candidate with the smallest finish time, not a deliberate pick of the slowest chef.

scenario: 你要评估 dispatch 在更大规模 order 上是否还跑得动。
scenario_en: You need to estimate whether dispatch still runs on larger orders.
q: dispatch 的复杂度如何描述？
q_en: How should dispatch complexity be described?
options: O(total steps!)，阶乘级增长
O(total steps * dishes * chefs)，三者相乘
O(stations only)，只由 station 数决定
O(1)，常数时间不随输入变化
options_en: O of total steps factorial, growing extremely fast.
O of total steps times dishes times chefs.
O of stations only, ignoring steps and chefs.
O of 1, constant time regardless of input.
why: 每放一个 step，都扫描所有 dish 的 ready step，并为每个候选试 chefs；仍然是多项式单向 pass。
why_en: Dispatch scans ready steps across dishes and tries chefs for each placed step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

optionExplanations: 阶乘增长意味着排列穷举，但 dispatch 每轮只做一次局部挑选，没有穷举排列。
复杂度来自三层嵌套：外层是步数，中间是逐一比对的候选 dish，内层还要试遍每个厨师。
只按 station 数算显然漏掉了 dish 数和 chef 数对运行时间的影响。
常数时间不成立——dish 越多、chef 越多，dispatch 要做的比较就越多。
optionExplanations_en: Factorial growth implies enumerating permutations, but dispatch just makes one local pick per round, no permutation search.
The cost stacks three layers: the step count on the outside, comparing candidate dishes in the middle, and trying every chef on the inside.
Counting only stations misses how much dish count and chef count also drive the runtime.
Constant time doesn't hold -- more dishes and more chefs both mean more comparisons for dispatch to make.

q: dispatch 为什么仍然错过所有 targets？
q_en: Why does dispatch still miss all targets?
options: 它每次都会生成不满足约束的非法 schedule
它禁止任何两个不同 dish 互相交错执行
它完全忽视不同 chef 之间的速度差异
它每轮局部提交，无法撤销挡住后续关键资源的选择
options_en: It always produces an illegal schedule that breaks the constraints.
It forbids any two different dishes from interleaving at all.
It completely ignores the speed differences between chefs.
It commits locally each round and cannot undo a pick that later blocks a key resource.
why: dispatch 比按 dish 顺序聪明，但仍是单步 greedy，需要搜索 ordering 才能处理后悔成本。
why_en: Dispatch still commits greedily without lookahead or undo.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

optionExplanations: dispatch 产出的一直是合法 schedule，问题不在违反约束。
dispatch 恰恰允许不同 dish 交错，这点它比第一版 greedy 强。
dispatch 是拿完成时间做比较的，并没有无视厨师速度差异。
dispatch 每轮一旦提交就不能反悔，如果这个选择后来挡住了关键 station，它没法回头重排。
optionExplanations_en: Dispatch always outputs a legal schedule -- the problem isn't broken constraints.
Dispatch is exactly what lets different dishes interleave -- that's its edge over the first greedy pass.
Dispatch compares finish times directly, so it isn't ignoring how fast each chef is.
Once dispatch commits a step each round it can't take it back, so if that pick later blocks a key resource, there's no way to reorder.

q: 填空：busy orders 上 dispatch 有改善，例如 six-dish 从 {{225}} 降到 {{210}}，nine-dish 从 {{285}} 降到 {{255}}。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: on busy orders, dispatch improves six-dish from {{225}} to {{210}} and nine-dish from {{285}} to {{255}}.
text: busy orders 上 dispatch 有改善，例如 six-dish 从 {{225}} 降到 {{210}}，nine-dish 从 {{285}} 降到 {{255}}。
why: dispatch 通过交错 dish 改善了忙碌 order，但仍没达到目标，说明只靠更聪明的单向规则还不够。
why_en: Dispatch improves busy schedules but still misses the optimal targets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

scenario: 两个 greedy 都生成合法但不够快的 schedule，真正难点是 step ordering。
scenario_en: Both greedy schedulers produce legal but too-slow schedules; the hard part is step ordering.
q: 第三版应该搜索什么？
q_en: What should the third version search over?
options: 搜索 ready step 顺序，配合 branch-and-bound 剪枝
搜索所有 chef 名字按字母顺序排列出的各种组合方式
搜索所有 station 名字用不同拼写方式写出的组合方式
只搜索第一个 dish 内部各个 step 之间可能存在的排列顺序
options_en: Search over ready-step orderings, pruned with branch-and-bound.
Search over every possible alphabetical arrangement of the chef names.
Search over every combination of alternate spellings used for station names.
Search only over the possible orderings of steps within the very first dish alone.
why: 每个搜索节点选择一个 ready step，递归到剩余步骤；bound 负责砍掉不可能超过当前 best 的分支。
why_en: The optimal scheduler searches over ready-step orderings and prunes with branch-and-bound.
whenOtherWins: 如果 greedy 已满足 makespan target，完整搜索的复杂度可能不值得。
tradeoff: 对 step 排列做剪枝搜索 vs 继续用单向 greedy 规则
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Partial schedule] --> B[Generate ready steps]
B --> C[Try one candidate]
C --> D[Recurse]
D --> E[Complete schedule]
D --> F[Prune by bound]

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 dish 里下一个可以开始的 step，因为它前面的 step 都已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is a dish's next step, eligible to run once every earlier step in that dish is done.

optionExplanations: 在每个节点尝试一个 ready step、递归剩余部分，再用下界剪掉没希望的分支——这就是第三版要搜索的对象。
厨师名字的字母顺序跟调度质量毫无关系，不是搜索的目标。
station 名字怎么拼跟排程结果无关，同样不是搜索对象。
只搜第一道菜内部顺序漏掉了其余 dish 之间怎么交错，覆盖不了真正的优化空间。
optionExplanations_en: At each node it tries one ready step, recurses on what's left, and prunes hopeless branches with a bound -- that's what the third version searches over.
Alphabetizing chef names has nothing to do with schedule quality, so it isn't the search target.
How a station's name is spelled has no bearing on the schedule, so that isn't the search target either.
Searching only the first dish's internal order misses how the other dishes could interleave, so it doesn't cover the real optimization space.

q: 填空：branch-and-bound 的 lower bound 必须是 {{乐观}} 估计，不能 {{高估}} 任何可完成 schedule 的最优 makespan。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: a branch-and-bound lower bound must be {{optimistic}} and must not {{overestimate}} the best possible makespan.
text: branch-and-bound 的 lower bound 必须是 {{乐观}} 估计，不能 {{高估}} 任何可完成 schedule 的最优 makespan。
why: 只有安全下界才能用于剪枝；如果下界可能高估，就可能剪掉真正更优的 schedule。
why_en: A pruning lower bound must be optimistic so it never discards a potentially optimal completion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

q: Kitchen Orders 的 lower bound 由哪些部分取最大值？
q_en: Which components are maxed together to form the Kitchen Orders lower bound?
options: 当前所有 chef/station 已忙到的最晚时间
每个 station 当前空闲时间 + 该 station 剩余最快工作量
每个 dish 当前 ready time + 该 dish 剩余最快 tail
随机选择的一个完整 schedule makespan
options_en: The latest time any chef or station is already busy until.
Each station's current free time plus its remaining fastest-chef workload.
Each dish's current ready time plus its remaining fastest-chef tail.
The makespan of a randomly chosen complete schedule.
why: 三个部分分别从资源占用、station 序列化和 dish precedence 给出乐观下界；取最大值仍是安全下界。
why_en: The bound combines resource occupancy, per-station remaining work, and per-dish remaining tails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 已经排定的工作不可撤销，makespan 起码要等到当前最晚占用的资源腾出来。
同一 station 的剩余工作必须排队做完，空闲时间加上最快完成量就是它的乐观估计。
同一 dish 的剩余 step 得按顺序做，ready time 加上最快能做完的时长就是它的乐观估计。
随便挑一个跑出来的完整 schedule 只是某个解，不是对所有可能解的乐观估计，不能当下界。
optionExplanations_en: Already-committed work can't be undone, so makespan can't finish before the latest currently occupied resource frees up.
Remaining work on one station has to queue up, so its free time plus the fastest possible duration is an optimistic estimate.
A dish's remaining steps must run in order, so its ready time plus the fastest possible tail gives an optimistic estimate.
A randomly generated complete schedule is just one solution, not an optimistic estimate over all possible ones, so it can't serve as a bound.

q: station 下界为什么安全？
q_en: Why is the station lower bound safe?
options: station 完全可以同时并行处理它所有剩余的 step 工作
同一 station 的剩余 step 不能重叠，最快 chef 估算也要串行
station 下界为了保险起见，故意往偏大的方向去估计
station 到底什么时候空闲出来，完全不影响最终的 makespan
options_en: A station can perfectly well process all its remaining step work in parallel.
The same station's remaining steps cannot overlap, so even fastest-chef estimates must queue serially.
The station bound is deliberately padded toward a larger estimate just to be safe.
Exactly when a station becomes free has no effect whatsoever on the final makespan.
why: 把剩余工作都按最快 chef 算已经很乐观，但 station 独占约束仍要求这些工作排队完成。
why_en: Even with fastest-chef durations, remaining work for one station must be serialized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: station 恰恰不能并行——它一次只能服务一位厨师，这是这题的硬约束。
即便假设都找最快的厨师来做，同一 station 的剩余工作还是得排队完成、不能重叠，这才是下界安全的原因。
下界是要保持乐观、不高估，故意往大估反而会破坏它的安全性。
station 什么时候空出来直接决定后续工作能多早开始，怎么会没有影响。
optionExplanations_en: A station can't run in parallel at all -- it only serves one chef at a time, and that's a hard constraint here.
Even assuming the fastest possible chef for each, the same station's remaining steps still have to queue and can't overlap -- that's exactly why the bound is safe.
A bound needs to stay optimistic and never overestimate; padding it upward would break that safety property.
When a station frees up directly determines how soon later work can start, so it obviously does matter.

q: dish tail 下界为什么安全？
q_en: Why is the dish-tail lower bound safe?
options: 同一 dish 里所有剩余的 step 都可以完全并行地一起执行完
tail 计算时故意专挑最慢的那个 chef，让它变成一个上界
dish 的 ready time 在算下界的时候其实完全可以直接忽略掉不管
dish 剩余 step 需串行，ready time 加最快 tail 就是乐观下界
options_en: All of a dish's remaining steps can run entirely in parallel with one another.
The tail calculation deliberately picks the slowest chef, turning it into an upper bound.
A dish's ready time can be dropped outright and simply ignored when computing the bound.
A dish's remaining steps must run serially, so ready time plus the fastest tail gives an optimistic bound.
why: dish 内部 precedence 是硬约束；即使每一步都找最快 chef，也不能早于这个 tail 总时长完成。
why_en: A dish cannot finish before its current ready time plus the fastest possible duration of its remaining ordered steps.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一道 dish 内部固定顺序的 station step 链，后一步必须等前一步完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recipe is a dish's fixed chain of station steps, where each step must wait for the previous one to finish.

optionExplanations: 把这些剩余步骤同时摊开做是不可能的，dish 内部本来就有严格先后关系。
算下界要用最快的厨师而不是最慢的，用最慢厨师算出来的会变成上界而不是下界。
ready time 恰恰是起点，忽略它会让估计失真、不再安全。
同一道菜的剩余 step 得按顺序做，用 ready time 加上假设全用最快厨师的时长，就是一个乐观但安全的下界。
optionExplanations_en: Spreading these remaining steps out to run at once isn't possible -- a dish's steps have a strict order to begin with.
The bound should use the fastest chef, not the slowest -- using the slowest would turn it into an upper bound instead.
Ready time is exactly the starting point; dropping it would make the estimate inaccurate and unsafe.
A dish's remaining steps must run in order, so its ready time plus the duration if every step got the fastest chef gives an optimistic, safe bound.

q: 搜索中为什么可以在 `bound >= best_makespan` 时剪枝？
q_en: Why can search prune when `bound >= best_makespan`?
options: 乐观下界追不上当前 best，此分支不可能更优
下界越大代表 schedule 质量越好
best_makespan 是一个随机生成的数字
剪枝会跳过所有候选，但仍保证得到新的 best
options_en: Even the optimistic bound cannot beat the current best, so this branch cannot produce a better complete schedule.
A larger bound always means a better-quality schedule.
best_makespan is just a randomly generated number.
Pruning skips every candidate but still guarantees a new best.
why: 目标是最小化 makespan；下界已经不小于当前最优时，继续搜索只会浪费时间。
why_en: If the optimistic bound cannot beat the incumbent, no completion in that branch can improve the answer.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Partial state] --> B[Compute optimistic bound]
B --> C{Can beat best?}
C -->|yes| D[Search children]
C -->|no| E[Prune branch]

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索过程中当前已知的最好完整解，后续分支要击败它才有意义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The incumbent is the best complete solution found so far, and later branches only matter if they can beat it.

optionExplanations: 下界是这条分支最好也只能做到的程度，连这个乐观值都追不上已知最好解，继续往下搜纯属浪费。
下界大小只是估计值，跟排出来的 schedule 好不好没有必然关系。
best_makespan 是搜索过程中实际找到的最好解，不是随便生成的数字。
剪枝只是跳过没希望的分支，不会凭空产出新的更好解，也不保证一定找到 new best。
optionExplanations_en: The bound is the best this branch could possibly reach, and if even that optimistic value can't beat the known best, searching further just wastes time.
A bigger bound value is just an estimate -- it doesn't mean the resulting schedule is actually better.
best_makespan is the best solution actually found during the search, not some arbitrary number.
Pruning only skips hopeless branches; it doesn't conjure a better solution out of nowhere or guarantee a new best.

scenario: 示例 chef 速度中，每个 station 都有一个 0.5 factor specialist，其他人是 1.5 factor。
scenario_en: In the sample chef speeds, each station has one 0.5-factor specialist while the others run at a 1.5 factor.
q: 搜索版如何利用这个结构降低分支？
q_en: How does the search version use this structure to reduce branching?
options: 为每个 step 依然枚举所有可能的 chef 和 station 组合方式
把 chef 固定为该 station 的 specialist，只搜索 step 顺序
随机挑一个手速较慢的 non-specialist 厨师顶上去做这一步
让唯一一个厨师一个人包办这整单里的所有 step 工作
options_en: Still enumerate every combination of chef and station for each step.
Pin each step's chef to that station's specialist, and search only the step order.
Randomly substitute in whichever non-specialist chef happens to be slower.
Let a single chef single-handedly take on every step in the whole order.
why: 在这些实例里 non-specialist 慢三倍且不值得用，chef 维度可以折叠，真正的选择留给 ordering。
why_en: The specialist structure collapses chef choice so the search can focus on ordering.
whenOtherWins: 如果非 specialist 在排队压力下可能比等待 specialist 更早完成，就必须重新把 chef choice 纳入搜索。
tradeoff: 把 chef 折叠成 specialist、只搜 ordering vs 每步都枚举 chef+station

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 station 上速度是 0.5 factor 的 chef，比其余 1.5 factor 的 chef 快三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialist is the one chef who runs a given station at half the base time, three times faster than a non-specialist there.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在给定结构下必然不比另一个候选更优，可以直接排除而不影响最优解的选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dominated choice can never beat another option given the problem's structure, so it can be excluded without affecting optimality.

optionExplanations: 还枚举每个 chef 和 station 没有利用这个结构，分支数量没有被压缩。
厨师选择在本例里没有悬念，把它钉死在专精厨师上，搜索树就只剩下步骤怎么排这一个维度。
随便换成一个不擅长这个 station 的厨师，等于主动引入一个已知更慢的选择，没有道理这么做。
让一个厨师包办所有 step 会违反同一时刻只能做一件事的约束，根本不合法。
optionExplanations_en: Still enumerating every chef and station doesn't exploit this structure at all -- branching stays just as large.
Chef choice has no suspense in this example -- pin it to the specialist, and the search tree shrinks down to just step ordering.
Swapping in whichever chef is weaker at this station deliberately picks a choice already known to be worse, with no upside.
Letting one chef handle every step would break the one-step-at-a-time constraint and simply isn't legal.

scenario: order 里有多个 dish 使用相同 recipe，且它们处在相同步骤、相同 ready time。
scenario_en: The order has multiple dishes with the same recipe, the same step progress, and the same ready time.
q: 搜索如何避免重复等价分支？
q_en: How does search avoid repeated equivalent branches?
options: 把所有重复 recipe 的 dish 全部跳过不排入 schedule
随意改动其中一个 dish 的 recipe 内容
只探索一个代表，跳过 recipe/进度/ready time 全同的候选
把这些 dish 强行合并成一个更大的 dish
options_en: Delete every dish that shares a repeated recipe and never schedule it.
Randomly change one of the duplicate dishes' recipe.
Explore only one representative, skipping candidates identical in recipe, progress, and ready time.
Force these dishes to merge into one larger dish.
why: 这些 dish 在未来搜索中可互换，尝试每一个会产生同构子树；symmetry cut 保留一个代表即可。
why_en: Interchangeable dishes lead to identical subtrees, so the search only needs one representative.
whenOtherWins: 如果两个 dish 虽 recipe 相同但 deadline、优先级或 ready time 不同，就不能合并。
tradeoff: symmetry cut：只探索一个代表 vs 把每个可互换 dish 都单独搜索一遍

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一道 dish 内部固定顺序的 station step 链，后一步必须等前一步完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recipe is a dish's fixed chain of station steps, where each step must wait for the previous one to finish.

optionExplanations: 把这些菜整个跳过不排，等于漏掉了它们必须完成的工作，会产出不完整的 schedule。
随意改动其中一份菜谱会破坏这道菜原本的定义，跟对称剪枝没关系。
recipe、进度、ready time 完全相同的候选会展开出结构一样的子树，只探索其中一个代表、跳过其余等价候选——这就是 symmetry cut。
把几道菜强行并成一道会丢掉它们本该分别完成、分别计入 makespan 的事实。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping these dishes entirely would mean their required work never gets scheduled, producing an incomplete schedule.
Randomly editing one duplicate's recipe would break that dish's actual definition, unrelated to symmetry pruning.
Candidates identical in recipe, progress, and ready time expand into structurally identical subtrees, so exploring just one representative and skipping the rest is exactly what a symmetry cut does.
Forcibly merging several dishes into one would lose the fact that each must finish separately and count separately toward makespan.

q: branch-and-bound 的 memo 用来跳过什么？
q_en: What does the branch-and-bound memo skip?
options: 所有未完成的搜索状态
所有 makespan 比当前更小的状态
所有包含 Pasta 的搜索状态
已经以同等或更好下界见过的等价状态
options_en: Every unfinished search state.
Every state whose makespan is smaller than the current one.
Every state that happens to include Pasta.
Equivalent states already seen with an equal or better bound.
why: 如果同一 canonical 状态曾以更好下界出现，当前分支不会带来新希望；memo 减少重复搜索。
why_en: The memo skips repeated states already reached with an equal or better bound.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A[Canonical state key] --> B[Seen before?]
B -->|no| C[Store bound and search]
B -->|yes| D{Old bound no worse?}
D -->|yes| E[Skip state]
D -->|no| C

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存已搜索过的等价状态与当时的下界，命中时跳过重复搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memo caches equivalent states already searched along with the bound seen then, so the search can skip duplicate work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 跳过所有还没搜完的状态会把还有希望的分支也一起丢掉，这不是 memo 该做的事。
makespan 更小的状态往往正是更值得继续搜的，跳过它们反而会漏掉更优解。
题目里没有专门针对某道具体菜的规则，这个说法是编出来的。
同一个 canonical 状态如果之前已经以同等或更好的下界出现过，现在这个分支就不会有新发现，memo 跳过的正是这些重复状态。
optionExplanations_en: Skipping every unfinished state would throw away branches that still have promise -- that's not what a memo does.
States with a smaller makespan are often exactly the ones worth continuing to search, so skipping them risks missing a better answer.
There's no rule here specific to any one dish -- that claim is made up.
If the same canonical state was already seen with an equal or better bound, this branch can't offer anything new, and that's exactly what the memo skips.

scenario: 你在 search 中计算了当前状态的 lower bound，并准备查 memo。
scenario_en: In search, you computed the current state's lower bound and are about to check the memo.
q: `memo.get(key, inf) <= bound` 为什么可以剪？
q_en: Why can `memo.get(key, inf) <= bound` prune?
options: 同状态曾以不差的下界搜过，此分支无新信息
下界越大越好，越大越优先探索
key 只记录了 dish 的名字
memo 只用来给最终输出排序
options_en: The same state was already searched with a bound at least as good, so this branch adds nothing new.
A bigger bound is always better and should be explored first.
The key only records the dish names.
The memo is only used to sort the final output.
codeSample:
key = (canonical(next_step, dish_ready), chef_free, station_free)
if memo.get(key, float("inf")) <= bound:
    return
memo[key] = bound
why: memo 记录到达等价状态时见过的最好下界，更差或相同下界的重复状态不用再展开。
why_en: The memo prunes duplicate states when an equal or stronger bound has already been explored.
whenOtherWins: 如果 key 缺少资源空闲时间等关键状态，剪枝会不安全。
tradeoff: 命中 memo 直接剪枝 vs 每次都重新展开等价状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存已搜索过的等价状态与当时的下界，命中时跳过重复搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memo caches equivalent states already searched along with the bound seen then, so the search can skip duplicate work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可互换的 dish 排序归一化后得到的状态标识，让 memo 能识别对称状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A canonical key normalizes interchangeable dishes into one sorted form so the memo can recognize symmetric states.

optionExplanations: 同一状态之前已经以不差的下界出现过，再展开一次不会挖到新信息，这行代码剪的就是这种重复。
下界只是乐观估计，越大不代表越好，反而可能意味着这个分支希望更小。
key 里还包含了 chef_free、station_free 这些资源信息，不只是 dish 名字。
memo 是用来剪枝、避免重复搜索的，不是给最终结果排序用的。
optionExplanations_en: This state was already seen before with a bound at least as good, so expanding it again adds nothing -- that's exactly the duplicate this line prunes.
A bound is just an optimistic estimate; a larger value doesn't mean better, if anything it can mean the branch has less promise.
The key also carries chef_free and station_free, not just dish names.
The memo exists to prune and avoid repeated search, not to order the final output.

scenario: 重复 recipe 的 dish 可以互换，但原始 dish index 不同。
scenario_en: Dishes with repeated recipes are interchangeable, but their original dish indexes differ.
q: `canonical(next_step, dish_ready)` 为什么要排序 signature、step、ready time？
q_en: Why does `canonical(next_step, dish_ready)` sort by signature, step, and ready time?
options: 让 schedule 按 dish 名字字母序输出
把可互换 dish 的进度归一化成同一个状态 key
计算每个 station 的 fastest chef
删除 dish 之间的前置关系
options_en: Sort the schedule output alphabetically by dish name.
Normalize interchangeable dishes' progress into one shared state key.
Compute the fastest chef for each station.
Delete the precedence relationship between dishes.
codeSample: return tuple(sorted((signature[d], next_step[d], dish_ready[d]) for d in range(len(dishes))))
why: 不同 dish index 但同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time 的状态等价；排序后 memo 能命中这些对称状态。
why_en: Canonicalizing interchangeable dishes lets the memo recognize symmetric states.
whenOtherWins: 如果 dish 有不同订单 id 约束或不同 deadline，canonical key 需要保留这些差异。
tradeoff: canonical key 归一化对称 dish vs 保留每个 dish 独立的原始 index

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可互换的 dish 排序归一化后得到的状态标识，让 memo 能识别对称状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A canonical key normalizes interchangeable dishes into one sorted form so the memo can recognize symmetric states.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

optionExplanations: 这行代码跟最终怎么打印 schedule 没关系，它服务的是搜索内部的状态识别。
把 recipe、进度、ready time 排序打包成一个 key，让原本 dish index 不同但其实等价的状态归到同一个 key 下，方便 memo 命中——这就是它的作用。
计算每个 station 最快厨师是另一套逻辑，跟这里的排序无关。
dish 之间的前置关系还在别处继续生效，这行代码并没有把它删掉。
optionExplanations_en: This line has nothing to do with how the final schedule gets printed -- it's about recognizing state equivalence inside the search.
Sorting recipe, progress, and ready time into one key lets states that differ only by dish index but are otherwise identical collapse into the same key -- exactly what lets the memo hit them.
Figuring out each station's fastest chef is separate logic, unrelated to this sorting step.
Precedence between dishes still holds elsewhere in the search; this line doesn't remove it.

q: branch-and-bound 里为什么还要把 candidates 按 `(end, d)` 排序？
q_en: Why does branch-and-bound still sort candidates by `(end, d)`?
options: 候选排序本身就足以证明这份 schedule 是最优的
不做排序就完全无法生成一份合法的 schedule
先试早完成候选，更快找到好 incumbent，加强剪枝
候选排序会彻底替代 lower bound 该起的作用
options_en: The ordering of candidates by itself is enough to prove the schedule is optimal.
Without sorting candidates, the search cannot produce a legal schedule at all.
Trying earlier-finishing candidates first finds a good incumbent sooner, strengthening later pruning.
Sorting candidates would entirely replace the role the lower bound is supposed to play.
why: 搜索顺序不改变正确性，但影响多快找到好的 best；好的 incumbent 会让 bound 剪更多分支。
why_en: Candidate ordering helps find a good incumbent early, making bound pruning more effective.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索过程中当前已知的最好完整解，后续分支要击败它才有意义。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The incumbent is the best complete solution found so far, and later branches only matter if they can beat it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 排序本身不能证明任何东西，最优性是靠下界和穷举覆盖来保证的。
不排序候选顺序仍然可以产出合法 schedule，只是找到好解可能更慢。
先试完成得早的候选，能更快拿到一个不错的 incumbent，后面的下界比较就能更早剪掉更多分支。
排序只是影响探索顺序，下界该算还是要算，两者不能互相替代。
optionExplanations_en: Sorting by itself proves nothing -- optimality still comes from the bound plus exhaustive coverage.
Leaving candidates unsorted would still produce a legal schedule, it would just likely take longer to find a good one.
Trying earlier-finishing candidates first gets a decent incumbent sooner, so later bound comparisons can prune more branches earlier.
Sorting only changes exploration order; the bound still has to be computed regardless -- one doesn't replace the other.

scenario: 你要实现 lower bound 的 station 部分。
scenario_en: You are implementing the station component of the lower bound.
q: lower bound 里这段 station 循环代码在表达什么？
q_en: What does this station loop in the lower bound express?
options: station 至少要等到空闲时间，再串行做完剩余工作
每个 station 可以并行完成所有剩余工作
这段代码直接就是当前 best schedule
remaining 越大，makespan 反而越小
options_en: Each station must wait at least until it is free, then serially finish its remaining work.
Each station can finish all its remaining work in parallel.
This code snippet directly is the current best schedule.
A larger remaining value makes the makespan smaller.
codeSample:
for st in stations:
    bound = max(bound, station_free[i] + remaining[st])
why: station 独占约束提供了强下界；即使使用最快 chef，属于同一 station 的剩余工作也不能重叠。
why_en: The station component bounds completion time by current station availability plus its remaining fastest work.
whenOtherWins: 如果 station 没有独占限制，这个下界项就不成立。
tradeoff: 把 station 剩余工作当串行下界 vs 假设 station 能并行处理

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。

The number of chefs alone doesn't determine how big the search tree gets -- the orderings do.

String prefix matching is a completely different kind of problem, with no equivalence to this one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

optionExplanations: 去掉一个紧的 lower bound，搜索就失去了大部分剪枝能力，最大用例会直接超时。
去掉 memo，等价状态会被反复展开，重复搜索的开销会迅速拖垮它。
完全不检查 station 约束会直接产出非法 schedule，这不是优化项，是正确性底线。
把专精厨师直接钉死、再跳过对称重复的分支，这两条规则会在骨架优化之外继续往下削减分支数量。
optionExplanations_en: Drop a tight lower bound and the search loses most of its pruning power, timing out on the largest case.
Drop the memo and equivalent states get expanded over and over, and that repeated work quickly overwhelms the search.
Skipping the station check entirely would produce an illegal schedule -- that's not an optimization, it's a correctness floor.
Pinning the specialist chef and skipping symmetric duplicate branches both trim the branch count further, on top of the core optimizations.

why: 搜索先用 bound 排除无望状态，再展开候选；完整 schedule 才能更新 incumbent。

tradeoff: 试探+可撤销+剪枝搜索 vs 一次性贪心提交且不可回头

flowchart TD

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 搜索过程中当前已知的最好完整解，后续分支要击败它才有意义。

q: dish-order greedy 和 dispatch 的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the difference between dish-order greedy and dispatch?
options: dispatch 会对已经提交的每一个选择做完整回溯撤销
greedy 把 dish 顺序锁死；dispatch 每轮改选局部最早的 ready step
greedy 执行完毕就能证明自己达到了全局最优解
dispatch 调度的整个过程里其实完全不维护 station_free 这个状态量
options_en: Dispatch performs a full backtrack and undoes every choice it already committed.
Greedy locks in dish order; dispatch instead picks the locally earliest ready step each round.
Greedy can prove it reaches the global optimum simply by finishing execution.
Across the entire dispatch process, station_free as a piece of state is never tracked at all.
why: dispatch 延迟了承诺并允许 interleaving，但仍没有搜索；两者都可能被局部选择卡住。
why_en: Dispatch interleaves dishes by choosing among ready steps, but it remains a greedy one-pass scheduler.
tradeoff: 一次性锁定 dish 顺序 vs 每轮重新挑 ready step（都不做搜索/回溯）

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

optionExplanations: dispatch 提交后同样不能反悔，它并没有做完整回溯这件事。
greedy 一上来就锁死 dish 顺序按顺序推进；dispatch 更灵活，每一轮都在所有 dish 的 ready step 里挑一个最早完成的提交，能让 dish 交错。
greedy 只保证合法，完全没有做穷举或剪枝，谈不上证明全局最优。
dispatch 同样要维护 station_free 才能算出每个候选的合法开始时间，不可能不管它。
optionExplanations_en: Dispatch can't undo a commitment either -- it never does full backtracking.
Greedy locks in dish order up front and marches through it; dispatch is more flexible, picking whichever ready step across all dishes finishes earliest each round, letting dishes interleave.
Greedy only guarantees legality -- it never enumerates or prunes, so it can't claim to prove global optimality.
Dispatch still has to track station_free to compute each candidate's legal start time, so it can't be ignoring it.

q: dispatch 和 branch-and-bound search 的关键区别是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between dispatch and branch-and-bound search?
options: dispatch 立即提交局部最优；search 试探候选并靠剪枝放弃分支
search 会无视 dish 内部固定的 recipe 顺序
dispatch 执行完就能保证达到全局最优解
search 完全不需要任何形式的 lower bound
options_en: Dispatch immediately commits the locally best ready step; search tries candidates, recurses, and can abandon branches via pruning.
Search ignores the fixed recipe order inside each dish.
Dispatch is guaranteed to reach the global optimum.
Search needs no lower bound of any kind.
why: search 的价值在于不把局部看起来好的选择当成不可撤销事实；bound 让这种搜索可运行。
why_en: Search explores alternative ready-step orderings instead of committing to one greedy choice.
tradeoff: 立即提交、不可撤销 vs 试探+递归+剪枝可撤销

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: dispatch 每轮选完就直接提交、不能反悔；search 会尝试一个候选、递归下去，行不通或没希望时靠剪枝放弃这条分支——这是两者的关键区别。
search 依然要遵守 dish 内部的 recipe 顺序，只是在这个约束下搜索更好的排列。
dispatch 只是局部规则，跑完并不能证明达到全局最优。
没有 lower bound，搜索就没法剪枝，指数级的分支会直接跑不完。
optionExplanations_en: Dispatch commits the locally best pick immediately; search tries a candidate, recurses, and can abandon a branch via pruning if it's hopeless -- that's the key difference.
Search still has to respect the fixed recipe order inside each dish; it just searches for a better ordering within that constraint.
Dispatch is only a local rule -- finishing it proves nothing about reaching the global optimum.
Without a lower bound, search would have no way to prune, and the exponential branching would never finish.

options: 一上来就写复杂搜索，完全不先验证基本合法性
先做合法 schedule 基线，再用 benchmark 找瓶颈
忽略 station 约束，直接把 step 排给最快的 chef
只返回一个空的 schedule，草草交差应付了事
options_en: Jump straight into writing complex search without validating basic legality first.
Build a valid baseline schedule first, then use benchmarks to find the bottleneck.
Ignore the station constraint entirely and just assign steps to the fastest chef.
Just return an empty schedule and call the whole thing done.
why: 文章的 takeaways 明确区分 make it valid 和 make it good；合法基线帮助定位真正瓶颈。
why_en: The pragmatic path is to build a valid scheduler first, then optimize the makespan.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目直接要求证明最优且输入很小，也可以更早引入搜索。
tradeoff: 先做合法基线、再优化 vs 一开始就上复杂搜索

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 还没弄清楚问题结构就直接上复杂搜索，容易连基本合法性都没保证，风险很高。
先写一个能满足所有约束的合法排程，再用 benchmark 数据找出真正的瓶颈在哪，这是最务实的起步方式。
跳过 station 约束会直接产出非法排程，不是能接受的简化。
什么都不排显然不满足题目要求，只是在逃避问题。
optionExplanations_en: Diving into complex search before understanding the problem risks not even guaranteeing basic legality -- too risky to start with.
Writing a legal scheduler that satisfies every constraint first, then using benchmark data to find where the real bottleneck is, is the most pragmatic way to start.
Skipping the station constraint would produce an illegal schedule outright -- not an acceptable shortcut.
Scheduling nothing at all obviously fails the requirements -- it's just avoiding the problem.

scenario: 你想加入一个更激进的剪枝估计，但它偶尔会高估剩余最短完成时间。
scenario_en: You want to add a more aggressive pruning estimate, but it sometimes overestimates the shortest remaining completion time.
q: 为什么这不适合作为 branch-and-bound 的 lower bound？
q_en: Why is this unsuitable as a branch-and-bound lower bound?
options: 高估会让搜索直接变成 O(1) 且仍然正确
lower bound 只要越大越好，不管准不准
高估只会影响打印的顺序，无关正确性
高估可能把真正最优的分支剪掉，破坏最优性保证
options_en: Overestimating makes the search O(1) and still correct.
A lower bound just needs to be as large as possible, regardless of accuracy.
Overestimating only affects print order, not correctness.
Overestimating can prune away the truly optimal branch, breaking the optimality guarantee.
why: branch-and-bound 的正确性依赖下界不超过真实可达最优；激进但不安全的估计只能用于排序启发，不能用于硬剪枝。
why_en: An unsafe bound can prune the optimal branch, so it cannot be used for correctness-preserving pruning.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是启发式求近似解而不要求最优，非安全估计可以用于优先级排序。
tradeoff: 安全（从不高估）的 lower bound vs 激进但可能高估的估计

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

optionExplanations: 高估不会让搜索突然变成常数时间，反而会破坏它原本该有的正确性保证。
下界要的是「不超过真实最优」这条安全线，光是数值大没有意义，甚至有害。
高估影响的不只是打印顺序，它会直接改变哪些分支被剪掉。
如果这个估计偶尔比真实可达的最优值还大，就可能把包含真正最优解的分支提前剪掉，最优性保证也就没了。
optionExplanations_en: Overestimating doesn't magically make the search O(1); it breaks the correctness guarantee the bound is supposed to provide.
What a bound needs is to never exceed the true achievable optimum -- being merely large is meaningless, even harmful.
Overestimating affects far more than print order; it directly changes which branches get cut.
If this estimate sometimes exceeds the true achievable optimum, it can prune away the branch holding the actual best schedule, breaking the optimality guarantee.

q: 为什么 station_free 和 chef_free 都要跟踪？
q_en: Why do we need to track both station_free and chef_free?
options: 只要 chef 空闲，就能在同一 station 上并行处理
station_free 这个状态只用来控制界面输出的颜色
step 同时占用一个 chef 和一个 station，任一未空闲都不能开始
chef_free 和 station_free 这两个状态永远完全相同
options_en: As long as the chef is free, work can run on the station in parallel.
The station_free state is only used to control the color of the output display.
A step occupies one chef and one station together, and neither can be busy for it to start.
chef_free and station_free are always exactly identical.
why: chef 和 station 是两套独立资源约束，最早开始时间必须同时满足它们。
why_en: Each step requires both a chef and a station to be available.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 厨师空闲不代表 station 也空闲，两者是各自独立的资源，不能只看一个。
station_free 直接参与最早开始时间的计算，跟输出怎么显示没关系。
一个 step 要同时占住一位厨师和一个 station，任何一个还没空出来，这一步都开始不了。
厨师和 station 是两套互不相关的资源状态，它们的空闲时间没有理由必须相等。
optionExplanations_en: A chef being free doesn't mean the station is -- they're two independent resources, and you can't just check one.
station_free feeds directly into computing the earliest start time; it has nothing to do with how output gets displayed.
A step needs to hold both one chef and one station at the same time, and if either isn't free yet, the step can't start.
Chef and station are two unrelated resource states, and there's no reason their free times would always match.

scenario: 你在为 branch-and-bound 设计递归状态，需要决定保留哪些字段。
scenario_en: You are designing the recursive state for branch-and-bound and need to decide which fields to keep.
q: search 状态里哪些数组或元组是必要的？
q_en: Which arrays or tuples are necessary in the search state?
options: next_step：每个 dish 走到第几步
dish_ready：每个 dish 下一步最早可开始时间
chef_free 和 station_free：资源空闲时间
随机数生成器状态，决定合法性
options_en: next_step: how far each dish has progressed.
dish_ready: the earliest a dish's next step can start.
chef_free and station_free: when each resource becomes available.
A random-number generator's state, which decides legality.
why: 这些状态共同决定当前可选 steps 和每个候选的开始/结束时间；随机数不是调度语义的一部分。
why_en: The search state must capture dish progress, dish readiness, and resource availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 dish 里下一个可以开始的 step，因为它前面的 step 都已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is a dish's next step, eligible to run once every earlier step in that dish is done.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: next_step 记录每道菜走到第几步，决定接下来哪个 step 是 ready 的。
dish_ready 是这道菜下一步最早能开始的时间，算候选开始时间少不了它。
chef_free 和 station_free 分别记录两类资源什么时候空出来，是算合法开始时间的另外两个必要条件。
调度的合法性和最优性跟随机数毫无关系，这个状态不该出现在这里。
optionExplanations_en: next_step tracks how far each dish has progressed, which determines which step is ready next.
dish_ready is the earliest this dish's next step could start, and it's essential to computing candidate start times.
chef_free and station_free each record when their resource frees up -- the other two ingredients needed for a legal start time.
Legality and optimality of the schedule have nothing to do with a random number generator, so this state has no place here.

q: lower bound 的“当前资源最晚忙到时间”项为什么必要？
q_en: Why does the lower bound need the latest currently busy resource time?
options: 它会高估所有还没被安排进 schedule 里的剩余工作总量
schedule 不会早于已安排的 chef/station 完成时间结束
它替代了对 dish 内部前置关系所要做的完整检查流程
它只是用来给最终排出的结果做 tie-break 排序而已，没别的用
options_en: It overestimates the total amount of work not yet placed into the schedule.
The schedule cannot finish earlier than its already-committed chef and station work.
It replaces the need for a full dish-precedence check.
It's only ever used to tie-break the ordering of the final printed result, nothing more.
why: 已有 partial schedule 的资源占用已经不可逆，makespan 至少要等当前最晚的已安排工作完成。
why_en: The final makespan cannot be earlier than the latest currently occupied resource time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 这一项只看已经排定、不可撤销的工作，跟还没安排的部分没关系，谈不上高估未排工作。
已经安排好的厨师和 station 工作不能撤销，最终 makespan 不可能早于这些已提交工作的完成时间。
dish 前置关系是单独一项检查，这一项管的是资源占用，两者互不替代。
它是下界计算的一部分，直接参与判断分支要不要剪，不只是拿来排序展示。
optionExplanations_en: This term only looks at already-committed, irreversible work, not anything unscheduled, so it isn't overestimating future work.
Already-committed chef and station work can't be undone, so the final makespan can never finish earlier than that committed work completes.
Dish precedence is checked separately; this term is about resource occupancy, and one doesn't substitute for the other.
It's part of the bound calculation and directly decides whether a branch gets pruned, not just something used for display ordering.

scenario: 订单很小、target 很宽松，只要求尽快交一个合法排程。
scenario_en: The order is small, the target is loose, and you only need to return a legal schedule quickly.
q: 哪种方案可能最合适？
q_en: Which approach is likely the best fit?
options: 简单的 dish-order greedy 或 dispatch 就够用
上完整的 branch-and-bound 搜索找最优
手动建模成 integer programming 交给求解器
跳过 recipe 顺序检查，直接乱序排
options_en: Plain dish-order greedy or dispatch is enough.
Run a full branch-and-bound search for the optimum.
Model it as integer programming and hand it to a solver.
Skip the recipe-order check and schedule in any order.
why: 简单 greedy 能快速产出合法 schedule；只有当 makespan target 紧或 greedy 结构性失败时，搜索成本才合理。
why_en: A greedy scheduler is pragmatic when feasibility matters more than optimal makespan.
whenOtherWins: 在本文硬 benchmarks 中，greedy 和 dispatch 都 miss targets，必须用 bounded search。
tradeoff: 简单合法但可能不是最优 vs 保证最优但实现/运行成本更高

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把调度约束写成整数变量的约束，交给通用求解器求最优的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Integer programming encodes the scheduling constraints as integer-variable constraints and hands them to a general-purpose solver for the optimum.

optionExplanations: 订单小、目标又宽松时，简单的 greedy 或 dispatch 几步就能给出合法排程，不值得多花实现和运行成本。
完整搜索能保证最优，但对这种小规模宽松场景是杀鸡用牛刀，调优成本换不来收益。
接入通用求解器的建模和运维成本更高，对一个宽松、快出解的场景没必要。
跳过 recipe 顺序检查会直接产出非法排程，不管场景多宽松都不能这么做。
optionExplanations_en: When the order is small and the target loose, plain greedy or dispatch produces a legal schedule in a few steps -- not worth the extra implementation and runtime cost of more.
Full search guarantees optimality, but for a small, loose-target case that's overkill -- the tuning cost doesn't pay for itself here.
Wiring up a general-purpose solver adds modeling and operational overhead that a loose, fast-turnaround case doesn't need.
Skipping the recipe-order check produces an illegal schedule outright, no matter how loose the target is -- never acceptable.

scenario: 改版后 non-specialist 只比 specialist 慢一点，而且 station specialist 排队很严重。
scenario_en: After a rule change, non-specialists are only slightly slower than specialists, and station specialists have long queues.
q: 原来的“只用 fastest chef”剪枝可能有什么问题？
q_en: What can go wrong with the original fastest-chef-only pruning?
options: 这条剪枝规则在新条件下依旧永远能保持绝对安全，不受影响
可能错过稍慢 chef 反而更早完成、makespan 更低的 schedule
会让 lower bound 变得更紧一些，且完全不会影响最优性保证
会自动切换成枚举所有 chef 组合方式的更慢搜索模式
options_en: This pruning rule stays perfectly safe under the new conditions no matter what, unaffected.
It could miss a legal schedule where a slightly slower chef actually finishes earlier and lowers makespan.
It makes the lower bound tighter without affecting optimality.
It automatically switches to enumerating every chef combination.
why: specialist rule 是利用本文具体速度结构的 dominated-choice 剪枝；速度结构变了，就要重新验证是否安全。
why_en: The fastest-chef simplification is only safe when non-specialists are truly dominated.
whenOtherWins: 在原文三倍慢的 chef 配置下，折叠 chef choice 可以显著减小搜索树。
tradeoff: 折叠 chef 选择、只搜 ordering vs 重新把 chef 选择纳入搜索空间

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个 station 上速度是 0.5 factor 的 chef，比其余 1.5 factor 的 chef 快三倍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A specialist is the one chef who runs a given station at half the base time, three times faster than a non-specialist there.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在给定结构下必然不比另一个候选更优，可以直接排除而不影响最优解的选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dominated choice can never beat another option given the problem's structure, so it can be excluded without affecting optimality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 这条剪枝之所以安全，靠的是「non-specialist 永远慢很多」这个前提，前提一变就不能再假设它永远成立。
如果 non-specialist 只慢一点、specialist 又排长队，稍慢的厨师反而可能更早接手，把它剪掉就会漏掉更优的 schedule。
剪枝本身不会让下界自动变紧，它是直接排除了一部分候选，跟下界计算是两回事。
剪枝规则不会自己感知场景变化去切换策略，得由人重新判断并调整代码。
optionExplanations_en: This pruning rule is only safe because non-specialists were always assumed much slower -- once that premise changes, it can't be assumed to hold anymore.
If non-specialists are only slightly slower and specialists have long queues, a slightly slower chef could actually pick up the step sooner, and pruning it away would miss a better schedule.
Pruning doesn't automatically tighten the bound -- it just excludes some candidates outright, a different mechanism from bound computation.
A pruning rule doesn't sense the scenario changing and switch strategies on its own -- someone has to re-verify it and adjust the code.

q: symmetry cut 如果把 ready time 不同的相同 recipe dishes 合并，会有什么风险？
q_en: What is the risk if a symmetry cut merges same-recipe dishes with different ready times?
options: 只会让搜索的正确性更有保障
会让 station_free 的计算变得更准确
它们并不等价，可能剪掉更优 schedule 的分支
对结果完全没有任何影响
options_en: It can only make the search's correctness more solid.
It makes the station_free calculation more accurate.
They are not truly equivalent, so it may prune away a better schedule.
It has absolutely no effect on the result at all.
why: 可互换性要求 recipe、step index 和 ready time 等状态都相同；少一个条件就可能错误合并。
why_en: Symmetry pruning is safe only when the dishes are identical in all state relevant to future scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

optionExplanations: 少了 ready time 这个条件，合并出来的候选其实并不等价，正确性反而会被破坏。
这个剪枝跟 station_free 怎么算没有关系，它管的是要不要展开某个分支。
recipe 相同但 ready time 不同意味着两道菜其实不可互换，把它们当等价剪掉，可能正好剪掉了藏着更优解的那条分支。
合并了不该合并的状态会实实在在改变搜索结果，不是没有影响。
optionExplanations_en: Dropping the ready-time condition means the merged candidates aren't actually equivalent, and that breaks correctness rather than helping it.
This pruning has nothing to do with how station_free gets computed -- it's about whether to expand a branch at all.
Same recipe but different ready times means the dishes aren't truly interchangeable, and treating them as equivalent can prune away exactly the branch holding the better schedule.
Merging states that shouldn't be merged genuinely changes the search outcome -- it's not a no-op.

q: 填空：prep_bottleneck_seven 的 target 是 {{195}}，greedy {{255}}，dispatch {{240}}，search {{195}}。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: prep_bottleneck_seven has target {{195}}, greedy {{255}}, dispatch {{240}}, and search {{195}}.
text: prep_bottleneck_seven 的 target 是 {{195}}，greedy {{255}}，dispatch {{240}}，search {{195}}。
why: dispatch 从 255 降到 240 仍未达标，只有 search 命中 195 的目标，说明瓶颈是 ordering，不是局部规则不够聪明。
why_en: On prep_bottleneck_seven, dispatch improves but still misses the target, and only search reaches the optimum of 195.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到最后一个 step 完成的总耗时，是要最小化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time from the start of scheduling until the last step finishes, and it's the value being minimized.

q: Kitchen Orders 的主要 takeaways 有哪些？
q_en: What are the main takeaways from Kitchen Orders?
options: 先区分合法 schedule 和好 schedule
当 ordering 是瓶颈时，单向 greedy 往往不够
安全 lower bound、memo、dominated choices、symmetry 可以让指数搜索可用
只要选最快 chef，就一定全局最优
options_en: First separate a valid schedule from a good one.
When ordering is the bottleneck, a one-pass greedy rule usually is not enough.
A safe lower bound, a memo, dominated choices, and symmetry make exponential search usable.
Just always picking the fastest chef guarantees the global optimum.
why: 最快 chef 是必要但不充分；文章真正的经验是用结构化剪枝把 ordering 搜索控制住。
why_en: The lesson is to turn a hard ordering problem into a bounded search using safe pruning and problem structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存已搜索过的等价状态与当时的下界，命中时跳过重复搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A memo caches equivalent states already searched along with the bound seen then, so the search can skip duplicate work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在给定结构下必然不比另一个候选更优，可以直接排除而不影响最优解的选项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dominated choice can never beat another option given the problem's structure, so it can be excluded without affecting optimality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跳过与已探索状态等价（同 recipe、同进度、同 ready time）的候选分支。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symmetry cut skips a candidate branch that is equivalent to one already explored -- same recipe, progress, and ready time.

optionExplanations: 先保证排程合法，再谈怎么排得更好，这是文章反复强调的第一原则。
当瓶颈出在 ordering 上时，不管规则设计得多聪明，单向不可撤销的 greedy 往往追不上真正的最优解。
安全下界砍掉没希望的分支、memo 避免重复搜索、dominated choice 折叠 chef 维度、symmetry cut 去掉对称子树——四者一起才把指数级搜索压到能跑的规模。
永远选最快厨师只是必要条件，不足以保证全局最优——本题的 30 秒差距恰恰来自顺序，不是厨师选择。
optionExplanations_en: Get the schedule legal first, then worry about making it good -- the article keeps coming back to this as the first principle.
When the bottleneck is ordering, a one-pass, no-undo greedy rule usually can't catch up to the true optimum, no matter how cleverly it's designed.

A safe lower bound cuts hopeless branches, a memo avoids repeated search, dominated choices collapse the chef dimension, and a symmetry cut removes duplicate subtrees -- together they bring exponential search down to a runnable size.
Always picking the fastest chef is necessary but not sufficient for global optimality -- this example's 30-second gap comes from ordering, not chef choice.

scenario: 你要把这个题归到 Backtracking 模式。
scenario_en: You need to classify this problem under the Backtracking pattern.
q: 最准确的解释是什么？
q_en: What is the most accurate explanation?
options: 因为整个调度问题从头到尾只需要一次排序操作就能结束
每次选一个 ready step 递归剩余，再用 bound 剪掉无望子树
因为它本质上其实等价于对一张无向图做一次 BFS 广度优先遍历
因为它只靠一个哈希集合做去重处理就已经完全足够了
options_en: Because the whole scheduling problem finishes from start to end with just a single sort.
It picks one ready step, recurses on what remains, and prunes hopeless subtrees with a bound.
Because it is, in essence, equivalent to running a single BFS traversal over an undirected graph.
Because a single hash set for deduplication is already completely sufficient on its own.
why: 第三版就是搜索解空间树：尝试一个选择，进入更小问题，用剪枝控制爆炸；这是典型 backtracking/branch-and-bound。
why_en: The final scheduler is backtracking over ready-step choices with branch-and-bound pruning.
whenOtherWins: 如果一个局部规则已经能保证目标，greedy pattern 会更轻。
tradeoff: 递归试探+剪枝（backtracking） vs 一次排序/BFS 之类的单趟算法

termDefinitions.meaning: 尝试一个选择、递归到更小问题、行不通就撤销再试下一个候选的搜索模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking tries one choice, recurses into the smaller remaining problem, and undoes the choice to try the next candidate when a branch fails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 dish 里下一个可以开始的 step，因为它前面的 step 都已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ready step is a dish's next step, eligible to run once every earlier step in that dish is done.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某个部分方案能达到的最优 makespan 的乐观估计，从不高估，用来判断分支是否还值得搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lower bound is an optimistic, never-overestimating estimate of the best makespan a partial schedule could reach, used to decide whether a branch is worth exploring.

optionExplanations: 一次排序解决不了排程问题，makespan 取决于组合选择，不是一个静态顺序就能定的。
每次从 ready step 里选一个、砍掉不可能更优的分支、递归解决剩下的子问题，这正是这版调度器的搜索方式。
这里没有图遍历意义上的节点和边，BFS 这个说法不成立。
光靠一个哈希集合去重解决不了要不要展开某个分支这个问题，还需要下界配合。
optionExplanations_en: A single sort can't solve this scheduling problem -- makespan depends on combinatorial choices, not a static order.
Pick one ready step, cut any branch that can't possibly beat the best, and recurse on what's left -- that's how this scheduler searches.
There's no graph of nodes and edges being traversed here, so calling it BFS doesn't hold up.
A hash set for deduplication alone can't decide whether to expand a branch -- that still needs the bound working alongside it.

q: “make it valid”和“make it good”在本文中分别对应什么？
q_en: What do “make it valid” and “make it good” mean in this problem?
options: valid 专指整个排程必须用 Alice；good 专指必须用 Bob 这个 chef
valid 满足 recipe/chef/station 三类约束；good 要把 makespan 压到达标
valid 是指直接返回一个完全空的 schedule；good 是指干脆无视 station 约束
两者其实完全同义，只是文章换了一种说法表达而已
options_en: Valid specifically means the whole schedule must use Alice; good specifically means it must use Bob.
Valid satisfies the recipe, chef, and station constraints; good pushes makespan down to the targets.
Valid here means returning a completely empty schedule; good means simply ignoring the station constraint.
They mean exactly the same thing, just different wording in the article.
why: 前两个 greedy 都能 make it valid，但 misses targets；search 负责 make it good。
why_en: A valid schedule respects constraints, while a good one minimizes makespan enough to meet targets.
tradeoff: valid（约束合法）vs good（makespan 达标/最优）

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到最后一个 step 完成的总耗时，是要最小化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time from the start of scheduling until the last step finishes, and it's the value being minimized.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一道 dish 内部固定顺序的 station step 链，后一步必须等前一步完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recipe is a dish's fixed chain of station steps, where each step must wait for the previous one to finish.

termDefinitions.meaning: PREP/CHOP/GRILL 之类的加工资源，同一时间只能被一个 chef 占用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A station -- PREP, CHOP, or GRILL -- is a processing resource that only one chef can occupy at a time.

optionExplanations: 题目里没有规定谁必须用某个具体厨师，这个说法是编造的。
valid 指满足 recipe、chef、station 这些约束，good 指把 makespan 压到达标甚至最优，两者是完全不同的两条标准。
空 schedule 或忽略约束都直接违反 valid 的要求，跟这两个概念的定义对不上。
两者标准明显不同——前两版 greedy 已经做到 valid，却依然 miss targets，说明 good 是更高的一层要求。
optionExplanations_en: Nothing in the setup requires any specific chef to be used -- that claim is invented.
Valid means satisfying the recipe, chef, and station constraints; good means pushing makespan down to meet or beat the targets -- two entirely different bars.
An empty schedule or ignoring a constraint both directly violate what 'valid' requires, so this doesn't match either definition.
The two clearly differ -- both earlier greedy passes already achieve valid, yet still miss the targets, which is exactly why good is a higher bar.

scenario: 你看完全部 benchmark 结果，要用一句话总结三种调度器的整体表现。
scenario_en: After reviewing all benchmark results, you need to summarize the three schedulers in one sentence.
q: benchmark 总结哪项正确？
q_en: Which benchmark summary is correct?
options: dispatch 命中每一个 target，而 search 反而全部超时失败
greedy/dispatch 全错过 target；search 全中，约 928ms
greedy 单独一个就已经命中了所有 case 的 target
三种方法在所有 case 上都统一输出 105 这个结果
options_en: Dispatch hits every single target while search times out on all of them instead.
Greedy and dispatch miss every target; search hits all of them in about 928ms.
Greedy alone already hits the target on every case.
All three methods output 105 on every single case.
why: 表格的结论是更好的 one-pass rule 仍不够；只有 branch-and-bound search 在所有 case 上达到目标。
why_en: The benchmark shows that only branch-and-bound search reaches every makespan target.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 dish 输入顺序推进、每步交给能最早完成它的 chef 的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dish-order greedy walks dishes in input order and assigns each step to whichever chef finishes it earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每轮从所有未完成 dish 的下一个 ready step 里挑局部最早完成者提交的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dispatch is a scheduler that each round commits whichever ready step, across all dishes, can finish earliest.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在排序的解空间树上搜索、用安全下界剪掉不可能超过当前最优的分支的算法框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Branch-and-bound searches the tree of possible orderings while using a safe lower bound to prune any branch that cannot beat the current best.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从调度开始到最后一个 step 完成的总耗时，是要最小化的目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Makespan is the total time from the start of scheduling until the last step finishes, and it's the value being minimized.

optionExplanations: 这个说法把结果说反了——真正全部超时的从来不是 search。
两版 greedy 每个用例都没达标，唯独搜索版全部命中，哪怕是最大规模也只要约 928 毫秒就能跑完。
greedy 在多个用例上其实是没达标的，deep_nine 就明显超出目标。
105 秒只是三道菜用例的目标，其它规模的用例目标各不相同，不会到处都是 105。
optionExplanations_en: This has it backwards -- it's never search that times out here.
Both greedy passes fall short on every case, but the search version nails all of them, finishing even the largest in about 928 milliseconds.
Greedy actually falls short on several cases, deep_nine being the clearest miss.
105 seconds is only the target for the three-dish case -- other sizes have their own different targets, not 105 everywhere.

q: Maximize Unique Characters 的合法解必须满足什么条件？
q_en: What condition must a valid Maximize Unique Characters solution satisfy?
options: 选出的所有单词按字典序连续
任意两个被选单词不能共享任何字符
只能选择长度相同的单词
必须覆盖完整字母表
why: 目标是最大化合并后的字符覆盖，但前提是被选单词之间没有字符冲突；完整覆盖字母表只是可能的早停条件，不是必须条件。
why_en: The subset is legal only when no two chosen words share a character, and the objective is to maximize covered unique characters.
optionExplanations: 错：题目不要求字典序连续，这是无关的排序性质。
对：这是合法子集的唯一硬性约束——两两字符不相交。
错：单词长度可以不同，长度不是合法性条件。
错：覆盖全部字母表只是可能的最优结果，不是必须满足的前提。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the problem never requires alphabetical adjacency.
Correct: pairwise disjoint characters is the only hard legality rule.
Wrong: words can have different lengths; length is not a constraint.
Wrong: full alphabet coverage is a possible optimum, not a requirement.
options_en: The chosen words must appear consecutively in alphabetical order.
No two chosen words are allowed to share any character.
Only words of the same length can be chosen.
The chosen words must cover the entire alphabet.

scenario: 每个单词只有「选」或「不选」两个动作，选了以后会约束后面哪些单词还能选。
scenario_en: Each word has only two actions, include or skip, and including it constrains which later words can still be chosen.
q: 最自然的第一版搜索框架是什么？
q_en: What is the most natural first search framework?
options: 按字符做 BFS
对每个单词做 include/skip 回溯
把单词排序后贪心全选最长
动态规划枚举所有 26 位 mask 状态
why: 每个单词都是二叉决策，且做出选择后要递归、撤销、再试另一支，这是回溯的典型形状。
why_en: Each word creates an include-or-skip branch, so recursive backtracking matches the decision structure directly.
whenOtherWins: 如果输入已经满足区间贪心或有可证明的最优子结构，贪心或 DP 才更合适；这里冲突组合没有这种简单性质。
optionDiagrams:
flowchart TD
  Word[i] --> Skip[skip]
  Word[i] --> Include{disjoint}
  Include -->|yes| Next[i plus 1]
  Include -->|no| Prune[no include]

flowchart LR
  Masks[All masks] --> DP[full DP space]
optionExplanations: 错：字符间没有图的边关系，BFS 无法表达冲突约束。
对：每个单词恰好是二元决策，天然匹配回溯的分支结构。
错：贪心选最长词无法证明全局最优，冲突关系会被忽略。
错：状态数达 2^26，本题规模下枚举所有 mask 太浪费。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: characters have no graph edges for BFS to traverse.
Correct: each word is a binary decision, the exact shape backtracking handles.
Wrong: greedily taking the longest words cannot prove global optimality.
Wrong: enumerating all 2^26 mask states is wasteful at this problem's scale.
options_en: Run BFS over individual characters.
Backtrack over an include-or-skip decision for each word.
Sort words and greedily take the longest ones first.
Enumerate all 26-bit mask states with dynamic programming.
tradeoff: 回溯穷举搜索 vs 贪心/DP 需要的额外结构性质

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统地尝试一个选择、递归探索后果，再撤销选择去尝试别的分支的搜索方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking is a search method that tries a choice, recurses on its consequences, then undoes it to try another branch.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按层展开、先访问最近节点的图搜索方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BFS explores a graph level by level, visiting the nearest nodes first.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每一步只看当前最优选择、不回头验证全局最优的算法策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A greedy algorithm makes the locally best choice at each step without reconsidering it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把问题拆成重叠子问题、用状态表存已算结果来避免重复计算的算法方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dynamic programming breaks a problem into overlapping subproblems and caches results in a state table.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个整数的每个二进制位表示某个元素是否存在的编码方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A bitmask encodes membership using each binary bit of an integer to mark presence.

q: 补全朴素回溯携带的核心状态：
q_en: Fill in the core state carried by plain backtracking.
text: 递归帧通常携带当前位置 {{i}}、当前已选单词列表 {{current}}、已经占用的字符集合 {{used}}，以及全局最优 {{best}}。
why: 这些状态分别回答「处理到哪」「选了什么」「还能不能选当前词」和「目前最好答案是什么」。
why_en: The recursive state tracks index, current pick, used characters, and the best solution seen so far.

q: 在朴素 include/skip 回溯中，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: In plain include/skip backtracking, which statements are correct?
options: skip 分支永远合法
include 分支必须先确认当前单词字符与 used 不相交
include 后必须在返回前撤销 current 和 used 的修改
到叶子节点时不需要更新 best
why: 跳过单词不会破坏合法性；选择单词必须无冲突，并且所有就地修改都要对称撤销，叶子或改进点都要维护 best。
why_en: Skip is always legal, include requires disjoint characters, and every mutation must be undone after the recursive call.
optionExplanations: 对：跳过不修改任何状态，不可能违反约束。
对：字符集合有交集时 include 非法，必须先判断。
对：current/used 是共享可变状态，退出前必须复原对称。
错：叶子或任何改进点都要检查并更新 best，否则丢最优解。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: skipping mutates nothing, so it can never break legality.
Correct: overlapping characters make the include illegal, so check first.
Correct: current and used are shared mutable state and must be restored.
Wrong: every leaf or improvement must update best or the optimum is lost.
options_en: The skip branch is always legal.
The include branch must first confirm the word's characters are disjoint from used.
After including, current and used must be restored before returning.
There is no need to update best at a leaf node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个集合没有任何共同元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two sets are disjoint when they share no common elements.

scenario: 回溯当前已经使用字符为 `used`，准备尝试把 `word` 加入当前选择。
scenario_en: The backtracking state already has used characters in `used`, and it is about to try adding `word` to the current pick.
q: 哪段 Python 判断最直接表达「word 与已用字符没有冲突」？
q_en: Which Python check best says that word has no conflict with used?
options: if set(word) <= used:
if used.isdisjoint(set(word)):
if len(word) > len(used):
if word not in used:
why: 合法 include 的条件是两个字符集合交集为空，`isdisjoint` 正好表达这个判断。
why_en: The include branch is legal exactly when the word's character set is disjoint from the used-character set.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态已经是整数 bitmask，就应该用按位与判断，而不是再构造 set。
codeSample:
word_chars = set(word)
if used.isdisjoint(word_chars):
    current.append(word)
    used.update(word_chars)
    recurse(i + 1)
    current.pop()
    used.difference_update(word_chars)
optionExplanations: 错：子集关系判断方向反了，且未处理相等的边界。
对：两个集合没有交集，用 isdisjoint 一次调用直接表达。
错：长度比较和字符冲突无关，无法判断是否合法。
错：`word not in used` 是判断整词是否为成员，语义完全不同。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: the subset direction is backwards and misses the disjoint check.
Correct: isdisjoint directly expresses zero character overlap.
Wrong: comparing lengths says nothing about character conflicts.
Wrong: `word not in used` checks whole-word membership, not character overlap.
options_en: Check whether word's character set is a subset of used.
Check whether used and word's character set are disjoint.
Check whether the word is longer than the used set.
Check whether word as a whole is a key in used.
tradeoff: 集合 isdisjoint 判断 vs 后续 bitmask 按位与判断

termDefinitions.meaning: Python 集合方法，判断两个集合是否没有交集。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: isdisjoint is a Python set method that checks whether two sets share no elements.

q: 回溯 include 分支中忘记 `current.pop()` 或忘记从 `used` 移除刚加入字符，最直接的后果是什么？
q_en: What happens if the include branch forgets current.pop() or removing new chars from used?
options: 只会影响运行时间，不影响答案
兄弟分支会看到不属于自己的选择，导致错误剪枝或错误答案
递归深度会自动变浅
Python 会自动回滚局部变量
why: 回溯依赖「进入分支前后状态一致」；撤销不完整会污染兄弟分支，让后续合法选择被误判成冲突。
why_en: If mutations are not undone, sibling branches inherit stale state and the search can reject legal combinations or return a wrong result.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Parent[used is ab] --> Include[add cd]
  Include --> Return[return without undo]
  Return --> Sibling[sibling sees abcd]
  Sibling --> Wrong[legal word pruned]
optionExplanations: 错：脏状态会让别的分支误判冲突，答案本身会错，不只是变慢。
对：没撤销的字符残留在 used 里，后续分支会误判成冲突。
错：状态没清理和递归深度无关，深度由 i 决定。
错：`used`/`current` 是可变对象，Python 不会自动帮你撤销。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: stale state corrupts correctness, not just speed.
Correct: leftover characters in used make sibling branches see false conflicts.
Wrong: recursion depth is driven by index i, unrelated to cleanup.
Wrong: used and current are mutable objects; Python never auto-restores them.
options_en: It only affects running time, not correctness.
Sibling branches inherit stale state, causing wrong pruning or a wrong answer.
Recursion depth automatically becomes shallower.
Python automatically rolls back local variables.

q: 把朴素回溯的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the plain backtracking decision chain in the right order.
steps: 到达叶子或发现更大 used 时更新 best
对当前单词先尝试 skip 分支
若字符不冲突，加入当前单词并递归 include 分支
返回 include 分支后撤销加入的单词和字符
递归状态从第 i 个单词和当前 used 集合开始
why: 朴素搜索围绕同一状态展开两个分支，任何 include 的状态修改都要在回到父帧前恢复。
why_en: Plain backtracking branches from the current state, tries skip and legal include paths, restores mutations, and updates the best solution at terminal or improved states.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统地尝试一个选择、递归探索后果，再撤销选择去尝试别的分支的搜索方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Backtracking is a search method that tries a choice, recurses on its consequences, then undoes it to try another branch.

q: 朴素 include/skip 回溯的最坏时间复杂度最接近哪一个？
q_en: What is the closest worst-case time complexity for plain include/skip backtracking?
options: O(n log n)
O(m · 2^n)，m 是单词长度量级
why: n 个单词各有选或不选两种分支，最坏有 2^n 个组合；每帧还要做与单词长度相关的集合检查或更新。
why_en: The worst case has two branches per word, producing 2^n combinations with per-frame work proportional to word length.
optionExplanations: 错：这是排序级复杂度，回溯树的分支数不是 n log n。
对：n 个二元决策给出 2^n 组合，每帧还有 O(m) 的集合操作。
错：26 是字母表大小的常数，和单词数 n 的搜索树无关。
错：n^3 是多项式，掩盖了每个单词二元分支带来的指数增长。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong: that is sort-level complexity, not a branching search tree.
Correct: n binary decisions give 2^n combinations, each frame doing O(m) set work.
Wrong: 26 is the constant alphabet size, unrelated to the search tree over n words.
Wrong: n cubed is polynomial and hides the exponential branching per word.
scenario: 词表里有 n 个单词，每个单词长度约 m；你要预估朴素 include/skip 回溯在最坏输入下的运行时间量级，判断这套方案能不能扛住较大的 n。
scenario_en: The word list has n words of length about m; you need the worst-case runtime scale for plain include/skip backtracking to judge whether it can handle a larger n.
options_en: O(n log n).
O(m times 2 to the n), where m is the word-length scale.
O(26 squared).
O(n cubed).

termDefinitions.meaning: 描述算法运行时间随输入规模增长的渐进上界记法，O(2^n) 表示指数级增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Big-O notation describes the asymptotic upper bound on running time; O(2^n) denotes exponential growth with input size.

q: 为什么包含大量二三字母短词的数据集会让朴素回溯变慢？
q_en: Why do many two- or three-letter words make plain backtracking slow?
options: 短词冲突少，合法分支能扎得很深
短字符串同样能转换成 set
短词字符少，通常覆盖不了全部字母
短词长度不会让递归失败返回
why: 冲突本身是朴素回溯唯一的自然剪枝；短词互相冲突少，就会保留大量深层分支。
why_en: Short words collide with few others, so conflict-based pruning leaves many deep legal branches alive.
optionExplanations: 对：冲突是唯一的自然剪枝，短词冲突少，深层分支大量存活。
错：任何长度的字符串都能用 set() 转换，和这无关。
错：短词字符少，远达不到覆盖完整字母表。
错：递归返回由函数结构决定，跟单词长短无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: conflict is the only natural pruning, and short words rarely conflict.
Wrong: any string converts to a set() regardless of length.
Wrong: short words have few characters and rarely cover the full alphabet.
Wrong: recursion always returns based on control flow, unrelated to word length.
options_en: Short words rarely conflict, so legal branches can go deep.
Short strings convert into a set just as well as long ones.
Short words have few characters and rarely cover the full alphabet.
Word length has no effect on whether recursion returns.

q: 这组基准数字最支持哪些设计判断？（多选）
