why: 每 3–4 分钟跑一遍五个诊断问句，正好卡在组件之间的自然过渡点上，所以不打断表达。这不是公式算出来的，而是「一个组件讲完就自检一次」的经验节奏。
why_en: Run the five diagnostic questions every 3-4 minutes, which lands on the natural transition between components so it doesn't break your flow.
options: 每 3–4 分钟、在组件之间的自然过渡点跑一遍五个诊断问句
只在面试官皱眉或打断时才检查，其余时间闷头往下讲
每讲完一句话就自查一次，确保任何时刻都没跑偏
只在面试最后 5 分钟一次性回顾，看有没有漏掉的失败模式
options_en: Every 3-4 minutes, at the natural transition between components, run the five diagnostic questions.
Only check when the interviewer frowns or interrupts, and otherwise push straight ahead.
Self-check after every single sentence so you are never off-track for a moment.
Do one retrospective in the last 5 minutes to see which failure modes you missed.
optionExplanations: 对；3–4 分钟一次刚好对齐组件切换，抓到走偏又不打断节奏，是可持续的自监控频率。
等面试官反应才检查就晚了——失败模式往往在他开口前就已经扣了分。
每句都自查会让你结巴、丢掉连贯表达，反而制造新的负面信号。
留到最后才回顾等于事后诸葛，跑偏的那 10 分钟已经无法挽回。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — every 3-4 minutes aligns with component switches, catching drift without breaking rhythm; it's a sustainable self-monitoring frequency.
Waiting for the interviewer's reaction is too late — the failure mode has usually already cost you before they speak.
Self-checking every sentence makes you stutter and lose coherence, creating a new negative signal.
A retrospective at the end is hindsight; the 10 drifted minutes are already unrecoverable.

termDefinitions.term: 五个诊断问句 / five diagnostic questions
termDefinitions.meaning: 对应五大失败模式的自查问句：我是不是钻牛角尖了？只广不深？丢了业务指标？没报任何数字？没讲取舍？
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The five diagnostic questions map to the five failure modes: am I rabbit-holing, breadth-only, ignoring the business metric, citing no numbers, or hiding trade-offs?

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 复盘手册把资深候选人反复踩的自毁行为归纳成一张五行表，每行配一个诊断信号和自救脚本。
scenario_en: The debrief playbook groups the self-sabotage habits senior candidates repeat into a five-row table, each with a diagnosis signal and a recovery script.
q: 以下哪些是文中总结的「五大自毁行为模式」？(多选)
q_en: Which of these are among the five self-sabotage failure modes? (multiple)
why: 五大模式：钻牛角尖(Rabbit Hole)、只广不深(Shallow Survey)、丢业务(Context Dropout)、不报数字(NFR Blind Spot)、不讲取舍(Silent Trade-off)。「澄清过度」不在其列——反而问需求是被鼓励的行为。
why_en: The five modes are rabbit hole, shallow survey, context dropout, NFR blind spot, and silent trade-off; over-clarifying is not one — asking about requirements is a rewarded behavior.
options: Rabbit Hole 钻牛角尖：卡在一个组件里出不来
Shallow Survey 只广不深：组件全点到但没有任何一个讲透
NFR Blind Spot 不报数字：全程不提延迟/QPS/成本任何量级
Over-Clarifying 澄清过度：一直问需求、迟迟不动手设计
options_en: Rabbit Hole: getting stuck deep inside one component.
Shallow Survey: naming every component but going deep on none.
NFR Blind Spot: citing no numbers at all (latency / QPS / cost).
Over-Clarifying: endlessly asking about requirements and never starting the design.
optionExplanations: 对；钻牛角尖是第一大模式——压力把专长激活，你误把深度当成严谨。
对；只广不深读起来像背课本，缺少动手过的痕迹（内部机制与取舍）。
对；一个数字都不报会显得你只懂学术精度、不懂生产约束。
错；这不是五大模式之一。适度澄清需求恰恰是被奖励的资深行为，只有多到面试官要打断你才算问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the rabbit hole is the first mode: pressure activates your expertise and you mistake depth for rigor.
Correct — a shallow survey reads like textbook recitation, missing the fingerprints of hands-on work (internals and trade-offs).
Correct — citing zero numbers signals you only know academic accuracy, not production constraints.
Incorrect — this is not one of the five. Sensible requirement clarification is a rewarded senior behavior; only asking so much that the interviewer must redirect you is a problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统必须满足的运行约束，如延迟、吞吐(QPS)、成本、可解释性，而非「系统做什么」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An NFR (Non-Functional Requirement) is an operating constraint the system must meet — latency, throughput (QPS), cost, explainability — rather than what the system does.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求/预测数，衡量吞吐量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures throughput as requests or predictions handled each second.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 你已经花 8 分钟调 HNSW 索引的 ef_construction 和距离度量，而 ranking、serving、业务指标一个都还没提。
scenario_en: You've spent 8 minutes tuning the HNSW index's ef_construction and distance metric, while ranking, serving, and the business metric are still untouched.
q: 此刻最该做的一步是什么？
q_en: What's the single best move right now?
why: 钻牛角尖的信号是 >3 分钟卡在一个组件、不回连整条 pipeline。自救三拍：承认刚才太深→说要 zoom out→真的画出端到端流程再一起选深挖点。面试官持续奖励这种自我纠偏。
why_en: The rabbit-hole signal is over three minutes on one component without linking back to the pipeline; the fix is to acknowledge, zoom out, and jointly pick where to go deep.
whenOtherWins: 如果是面试官明确点名要你深入这个索引组件，那继续深挖才是对的——此时不该 zoom out。
options: 继续深挖索引参数，把这块讲到极致，用深度证明专业度
主动 zoom out，先画出端到端流程，再和面试官一起决定哪个组件值得深挖
默默跳到另一个组件，不解释为什么换，继续往下讲
承认跑偏后就停住，把「深挖哪一块」的决定完全甩给面试官
options_en: Keep drilling the index parameters and cover them exhaustively, using depth to prove expertise.
Zoom out on your own initiative, sketch the end-to-end flow, then jointly decide with the interviewer which component deserves the deep dive.
Silently jump to another component without explaining the switch and carry on.
Acknowledge the drift, then stop and hand the 'which part to go deep on' decision entirely to the interviewer.
optionExplanations: 越深挖越坐实钻牛角尖：8 分钟不回连 pipeline，读作你不会管理范围。
对；主动 zoom out 展示端到端判断力，再共同选深挖点，把失控扳回受控。
无声跳走没有承认这一拍，面试官只看到你飘忽不定，仍不知你有没有全局观。
承认之后要自己给出修正路线；把决定全甩给面试官等于放弃主导权。
optionExplanations_en: Drilling deeper cements the rabbit hole: 8 minutes without linking back reads as an inability to manage scope.
Correct — zooming out shows end-to-end judgment, and jointly picking the deep dive turns loss of control back into control.
Silently jumping skips the acknowledge beat; the interviewer just sees you wander and still can't tell if you have a global view.
After acknowledging you must offer the correction yourself; handing the whole decision over abandons your leadership of the session.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种近似最近邻(ANN)图索引，用于向量检索的快速召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is an approximate-nearest-neighbor graph index used for fast vector retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 建图时的搜索宽度参数：越大图质量越高、构建越慢，属于很细的调参项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ef_construction is HNSW's build-time search width: larger gives a higher-quality graph but slower construction — a very fine-grained tuning knob.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 压力上来时，你本能地往一个熟悉的组件里越钻越深，感觉「我在很严谨地设计」。
scenario_en: Under pressure you instinctively drill deeper into a familiar component, and it feels like 'I'm designing rigorously.'
q: 为什么这种「感觉很扎实」的深挖反而是高危信号？
q_en: Why is this 'feels solid' deep dive actually a high-risk signal?
why: 压力会激活你的专长，让你把深度误当成严谨——但对面看到的是你 3 分钟不回连 pipeline、没有端到端判断力。自我纠偏（zoom out）才是持续被奖励的行为。
why_en: Pressure activates your expertise and you mistake depth for rigor, but the interviewer sees three minutes without linking back and no end-to-end judgment; self-correction is what's consistently rewarded.
options: 深挖一定是好事，越细越能拿高分，感觉扎实就说明方向对
危险在于压力把专长激活、让你误把深度当严谨，却丢掉了端到端判断力这个真正被考的信号
危险在于深挖会用光时间，但只要最后赶紧把别的组件也点一遍就没事
这其实不是问题，面试官更喜欢一头扎进单点、把一个组件讲到底的候选人
options_en: Deep diving is always good — the finer the higher the score, and feeling solid means the direction is right.
The danger is that pressure activates your expertise and you mistake depth for rigor, while losing the end-to-end judgment that is actually being assessed.
The danger is only that deep diving burns time, but as long as you quickly name the other components at the end it's fine.
It isn't really a problem — interviewers prefer candidates who dive into one point and exhaust a single component.
optionExplanations: 「感觉扎实」正是陷阱：它像自信和推进感，却掩盖了你没在展示全局判断。
对；根因是压力触发专长，把深度当严谨；被考的其实是你能否管理范围、回连业务。
补一遍别的组件治标不治本，会滑向另一个失败模式（只广不深）。
说反了：一头扎到底、不回连 pipeline，正是资深面试里最常见的扣分点。
optionExplanations_en: 'Feels solid' is exactly the trap: it mimics confidence and momentum while hiding that you're not showing global judgment.
Correct — the root cause is pressure triggering expertise, mistaking depth for rigor; what's tested is whether you manage scope and reconnect to the business.
Tacking the other components on at the end treats the symptom and slides you into the other failure mode (shallow survey).
Backwards: diving to the bottom without reconnecting to the pipeline is one of the most common deductions in senior interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从特征、召回、排序到 serving、反馈的完整链路；钻牛角尖就是长时间不回连这条链。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The pipeline is the full chain from features, retrieval, ranking to serving and feedback; rabbit-holing is going too long without reconnecting to it.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 你一口气点了 feature store、embedding、检索、排序、重排、serving、日志、A/B 八个组件，每个只讲了一两句。
scenario_en: You've named eight components in a row — feature store, embeddings, retrieval, ranking, re-ranking, serving, logging, A/B — one or two sentences each.
q: 此刻最该做的一步是什么？
q_en: What's the single best move right now?
why: 只广不深的信号是点了 >5 个组件却没讲透任何一个，读作背课本。自救：承认已铺完高层架构→挑「取舍最有意思」的那个组件→真的走进去讲内部机制和权衡。
why_en: The shallow-survey signal is naming over five components without going deep on any; the fix is to acknowledge the architecture is outlined, pick the component with the most interesting trade-offs, and actually walk through it.
whenOtherWins: 在开场刚要建立高层蓝图、面试官也想先看全景时，先快速铺一遍所有组件是对的——广度阶段本就该点名。
options: 再补充几个之前没提到的组件，把架构图铺得更全面
承认已铺完高层架构，挑出取舍最有意思的一个组件，走进去讲内部机制和权衡
从头把八个组件按顺序再讲一遍，这次每个多说几句
直接问面试官想听哪个，自己不做取舍判断
options_en: Add a few more components you haven't mentioned to make the architecture diagram even more complete.
Acknowledge the high-level architecture is outlined, pick the one component with the most interesting trade-offs, and walk through its internals and trade-offs.
Go through all eight components again in order, this time saying a few more sentences on each.
Just ask the interviewer which one they want to hear, without making the trade-off judgment yourself.
optionExplanations: 再加组件只会加深「只广不深」，把背课本的印象坐得更实。
对；主动收敛到一个高取舍组件深挖，用一次真正的深入证明你动过手、有判断力。
重讲一遍还是浅——多说几句不等于讲透内部机制和权衡。
全甩给面试官等于放弃「挑最有价值组件」这个恰恰在被考的判断。
optionExplanations_en: Adding components deepens the shallow survey and cements the textbook-recitation impression.
Correct — converging on one high-trade-off component and going deep proves with a single real dive that you've done the work and have judgment.
Re-listing is still shallow — a few more sentences each is not the same as exhausting internals and trade-offs.
Handing it entirely to the interviewer abandons the very judgment being tested: picking the most valuable component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一存储和服务模型特征的系统，保证训练与线上取到一致特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally stores and serves model features so training and serving read consistent values.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在初排结果上再用更重的模型/规则做二次排序，通常只作用于少量候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-ranking applies a heavier model or rules to reorder an already-ranked shortlist, usually over few candidates.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 从只广不深里自救时，你要挑「取舍最有意思」的组件深挖，题目是一个对延迟极敏感的广告排序系统。
scenario_en: Recovering from a shallow survey, you must pick the component with the most interesting trade-offs to go deep on; the problem is a latency-sensitive ads-ranking system.
q: 在延迟敏感的广告排序里，应该深挖哪个组件？
q_en: In latency-sensitive ads ranking, which component should you go deep on?
why: 「最有意思」= 被业务问题约束最紧的那个组件。延迟敏感的广告排序里，serving/ranking 层承受 50ms 级 SLA 的压力，取舍最密集；离线特征管线不在这条关键路径上。
why_en: 'Most interesting' means the component most constrained by the business problem; for latency-sensitive ads ranking that's the serving/ranking layer under a tight SLA, not the offline feature pipeline.
whenOtherWins: 如果瓶颈其实在数据侧（如特征新鲜度决定成败、召回质量差），那离线特征管线才是该深挖的高取舍组件。
options: 离线特征管线，因为它数据量最大、工程最复杂
日志与监控，因为它和最终指标直接相关
serving/ranking 层，因为它被延迟 SLA 约束最紧、取舍最密集，正是业务问题的痛点所在
A/B 实验框架，因为所有决策最后都要靠它验证
options_en: The offline feature pipeline, because it has the most data and the most engineering complexity.
Logging and monitoring, because it's directly tied to the final metrics.
The serving/ranking layer, because it's most tightly bound by the latency SLA and packed with trade-offs — exactly where the business problem bites.
The A/B testing framework, because every decision ultimately gets validated there.
optionExplanations: 离线管线不在延迟关键路径上，工程再复杂也不是这道题的痛点。
日志重要但不是延迟敏感排序的核心取舍点，深挖它显示不出你抓主要矛盾。
对；把深挖对准业务约束最紧的层，才是从只广不深里救回来的正确落点。
A/B 是验证手段，不是这道延迟题里取舍最密集、最该深挖的组件。
optionExplanations_en: The offline pipeline isn't on the latency-critical path; however complex, it's not this problem's pain point.
Logging matters but isn't the core trade-off of latency-sensitive ranking; diving there doesn't show you grasp the main tension.
Correct — pointing the deep dive at the layer most constrained by the business is the right landing spot when recovering from a shallow survey.
A/B is a validation mechanism, not the most trade-off-dense component to deep-dive in this latency-bound problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对外承诺的服务指标（如响应延迟上限），未达标有后果；这里指广告拍卖的延迟上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed service target such as a maximum response latency, here the ad auction's latency ceiling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 线上实时给请求打分、返回结果的推理服务，直接承受延迟约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The serving layer is the online inference service that scores requests and returns results in real time, directly bearing the latency constraint.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 你已经连着讲了 5 分钟一个很优雅的欺诈检测 GNN 架构，全程在优化 AUC，但没提过任何业务指标或用户影响。
scenario_en: You've spent 5 minutes on an elegant fraud-detection GNN architecture, all about optimizing AUC, with no mention of any business metric or user impact.
q: 此刻最该做的一步是什么？
q_en: What's the single best move right now?
why: 丢业务的信号是最近 5 分钟没提任何业务指标或用户影响。自救：把设计显式接回业务目标——「我选它是因为它优化了[业务指标]，而这重要是因为[原因]」。在 Staff+，业务对齐和技术深度同等加权。
why_en: The context-dropout signal is five minutes with no business metric or user impact; the fix is to explicitly reconnect the design to the business goal, since at Staff+ business alignment is weighted as heavily as technical depth.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官刚明确要求你只讲纯技术实现细节（如模型结构），那暂时聚焦技术、稍后再接回业务是合理的。
options: 继续把 GNN 的消息传递和采样策略讲得更深，技术足够强业务自然不重要
把设计显式接回业务目标：我选它是因为它优化了漏报带来的资金损失，这对支付方最关键
换个话题聊聊模型部署和监控，绕开业务不谈
反问面试官这道题的业务目标到底是什么，把定义责任推回去
options_en: Keep going deeper on the GNN's message passing and sampling, since strong enough tech makes the business irrelevant.
Explicitly reconnect the design to the business goal: I chose it because it minimizes the money lost to false negatives, which matters most to the payment provider.
Switch topics to deployment and monitoring, steering around the business entirely.
Ask the interviewer what the business objective even is, pushing the definition back onto them.
optionExplanations: 技术再强也救不了丢业务：Staff+ 把业务对齐和技术深度同等加权，只讲技术等于丢一半分。
对；一句「优化了什么业务指标、为什么重要」就把技术接回价值，正是自救的执行拍。
换话题是继续回避业务，信号不会消失，只会拖到结尾坐实。
开场就该澄清业务；讲了 5 分钟才反问，暴露你一直没带着业务目标设计。
optionExplanations_en: No amount of tech saves a context dropout: Staff+ weights business alignment as heavily as depth, so tech-only loses half the score.
Correct — one line naming the business metric optimized and why it matters reconnects tech to value; that's the execute beat of the recovery.
Switching topics keeps dodging the business; the signal doesn't vanish, it just cements by the end.
The business should be clarified up front; asking after 5 minutes reveals you were never designing toward a business goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在图结构上做消息传递学习节点/边表示的模型，常用于欺诈检测里的关系建模。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A GNN (Graph Neural Network) learns node/edge representations by passing messages over a graph, common for relational modeling in fraud detection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分类器排序能力的离线指标，衡量把正样本排在负样本前的概率；它是技术指标，不等于业务价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline ranking metric — the probability a positive is scored above a negative — a technical metric, not business value.

termDefinitions.meaning: Staff 及以上工程师级别，面试要求业务对齐与技术深度并重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staff+ denotes staff-level and above engineers, where interviews weight business alignment alongside technical depth.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 一个技术上很漂亮的欺诈 GNN，全程只优化 AUC，从没讨论漏报(FN)和误报(FP)各自的美元代价。
scenario_en: A technically beautiful fraud GNN optimizes AUC throughout and never discusses the dollar cost of false negatives versus false positives.
q: 在 Staff+ 评估里，这样一个「优雅但不谈业务」的设计会怎样？
q_en: In a Staff+ assessment, how does this 'elegant but business-blind' design fare?
why: 漏报和误报的美元代价通常极不对称——放过一笔欺诈亏的钱，和误拦一个好用户造成的流失，代价差很多，这决定阈值和损失函数。只优化 AUC 而不谈这笔账，在 Staff+ 会因业务对齐缺失而扣掉一半分。
why_en: The dollar costs of false negatives and false positives are usually very asymmetric, which should set the threshold and loss; optimizing AUC alone ignores that ledger and loses heavily on business alignment at Staff+.
options: 会拿高分，因为 AUC 高就代表模型好，业务细节可以留给产品团队
无所谓，反正 Staff+ 只看架构是否新颖优雅
会明显扣分：FN 与 FP 的美元代价高度不对称、本应决定阈值与损失函数，只谈 AUC 暴露业务对齐缺失
只会小扣一点，业务对齐在 Staff+ 权重很低
options_en: It scores high, because a high AUC means a good model and business details can be left to the product team.
It doesn't matter, since Staff+ only cares whether the architecture is novel and elegant.
It's clearly penalized: FN and FP dollar costs are highly asymmetric and should set the threshold and loss, so AUC-only exposes missing business alignment.
It's only lightly penalized, since business alignment carries little weight at Staff+.
optionExplanations: AUC 高不等于赚钱：不谈 FN/FP 代价，模型可能优化了一个和收益错位的目标。
说反了：Staff+ 恰恰把业务对齐抬到和技术深度同等的高度。
对；把漏报/误报换算成钱，才能定阈值和损失函数——这正是资深候选人该主动交代的账。
低估了权重：在 Staff+，业务对齐和技术深度同等加权，缺它会实打实扣一大块。
optionExplanations_en: High AUC doesn't mean profit: without FN/FP costs the model may be optimizing an objective misaligned with revenue.
Backwards: Staff+ specifically raises business alignment to the same level as technical depth.
Correct — converting false negatives/positives into money is what sets the threshold and loss, exactly the ledger a senior candidate should volunteer.
It underestimates the weight: at Staff+ business alignment is weighted equally with depth, and missing it costs real points.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把真欺诈判成正常，放过一笔欺诈，直接造成资金损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false negative (FN) labels real fraud as normal, letting fraud through and causing direct money loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把正常交易判成欺诈，误拦好用户，造成体验损失与流失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive (FP) labels a legitimate transaction as fraud, blocking a good user and causing friction and churn.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 你为搜索页设计了一个把相关性提升 +3% 的重排模型，但整场没报过任何延迟数字，而搜索页 p99 延迟 SLO 大约是 200ms。
scenario_en: You designed a re-ranker that lifts search relevance by +3%, but cited no latency numbers all session, while the search page's p99 latency SLO is around 200ms.
q: 这个「不报数字」的习惯为什么可能让整个设计作废？
q_en: Why can this 'no numbers' habit invalidate the whole design?
why: NFR 是首要设计驱动：一个 +3% 相关性的重排，如果把 p99 顶过 200ms SLO，用户根本等不到它、等于白做。面试不要求精确 SLO，给合理量级即可——如「搜索 <200ms p99」「广告 serving ~50K QPS」。
why_en: NFRs are primary design drivers: a +3% re-ranker that pushes p99 past the 200ms SLO is useless because users never wait for it; rough estimates like search <200ms p99 or ad serving ~50K QPS are enough.
options: 不会有问题，相关性 +3% 是硬收益，延迟慢一点用户会愿意等
因为面试必须报出精确到毫秒的官方 SLO，报不出就算失败
因为 NFR 是首要约束：+3% 相关性若把 p99 顶过 200ms SLO 就等于不可用，报个合理量级(如搜索 <200ms)即可
因为数字只在给出精确成本预算时才有意义，延迟不影响模型是否可用
options_en: No problem — +3% relevance is a hard gain, and users will happily wait a bit longer for it.
Because interviews require citing the exact official SLO down to the millisecond, and failing to means failure.
Because NFRs are the primary constraint: a +3% re-ranker that pushes p99 past the 200ms SLO is effectively unusable; a rough magnitude like search <200ms suffices.
Because numbers only matter when giving an exact cost budget; latency doesn't affect whether the model is usable.
optionExplanations: 用户不会等：搜索页超时的模型分数来得太晚，+3% 相关性也救不了不可用。
过头了：不需要精确官方 SLO，合理量级估计就够——重点是有没有用数字约束设计。
对；先把延迟/QPS 量级钉下来，才能判断这个重排到底能不能上线，这正是 NFR 作为首要驱动的意义。
延迟本身就决定可用性：一个 200ms SLO 的搜索页装不下拖慢它的重排。
optionExplanations_en: Users won't wait: a model whose score arrives after the search page times out can't be saved by +3% relevance.
Overshoot: you don't need the exact official SLO; a reasonable magnitude is enough — the point is whether you constrain the design with numbers.
Correct — pinning latency/QPS magnitudes first tells you whether the re-ranker is even deployable, which is what makes NFRs a primary driver.
Latency itself decides usability: a search page with a 200ms SLO can't absorb a re-ranker that slows it down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求都比这个延迟快；比均值更能反映最慢那批用户的体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value 99% of requests come in under, reflecting the slow tail of user experience better than the mean.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内部设定的服务目标（如 p99<200ms），是给定目标而非公式推导结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is an internal service target like p99 under 200ms — a given goal, not a value derived from a formula.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在初排后用更重的模型对少量候选再排序，提升相关性但增加延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A re-ranker reorders a small candidate shortlist with a heavier model, lifting relevance at the cost of latency.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 被问召回架构时你直接说「我会用 two-tower 双塔模型」，没说它换来什么、牺牲了什么。
scenario_en: Asked about the retrieval architecture, you flatly say 'I'd use a two-tower model,' without stating what it gains or gives up.
q: 此刻最该补上的一句是什么？
q_en: What's the one line you most need to add right now?
why: 沉默取舍的信号是「我会用 X」却不说得失，在资深级读作在瞎猜。自救：一句话点名取舍轴——双塔换来 serving 高效（物品向量可预计算），代价是丢掉 cross-encoder 那种细粒度 query-item 交互。
why_en: The silent-trade-off signal is 'I'd use X' with no gain/loss, which reads as guessing at senior level; the fix is one line naming the axis — two-tower buys serving efficiency but gives up fine-grained query-item interaction.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经和你一起确认过这个取舍、只想快速推进到下一步，就不必每次都重复展开得失。
options: 补一句更自信的话：双塔是业界标准做法，选它准没错
补一句取舍：双塔换来 serving 高效（物品向量可预计算），代价是丢掉 cross-encoder 的细粒度 query-item 交互
补充双塔的训练细节，比如用了哪种负采样
改口说其实哪个模型都行，避免被追问得失
options_en: Add a more confident line: two-tower is the industry standard, so picking it can't be wrong.
Add the trade-off: two-tower buys serving efficiency (item vectors are precomputable) at the cost of the fine-grained query-item interaction a cross-encoder captures.
Add training details of the two-tower, like which negative sampling you used.
Backpedal and say any model would do, to avoid being pressed on gains and losses.
optionExplanations: 「业界标准」不是取舍，反而更像在背模板；资深级要的是你能说出得与失。
对；一句「gives us…costs us…」点名取舍轴，把瞎猜变成有依据的决策。
训练细节是另一层深度，回答不了「你为什么选它、放弃了什么」这个取舍问题。
改口说都行是最差的：既没取舍又显得没主见，直接坐实沉默取舍。
optionExplanations_en: 'Industry standard' isn't a trade-off and sounds like reciting a template; senior level wants the gain and the loss.
Correct — one 'gives us... costs us...' line names the trade-off axis and turns a guess into a grounded decision.
Training details are a different depth and don't answer why you chose it and what you gave up.
Backpedaling to 'any works' is worst: no trade-off and no conviction, cementing the silent trade-off.

termDefinitions.meaning: query 和 item 各用一个塔编码成向量，靠向量内积匹配；物品向量可离线预计算，serving 快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model encodes query and item with separate towers into vectors matched by dot product; item vectors can be precomputed offline for fast serving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 query 和 item 拼在一起同时编码，能捕捉细粒度交互但无法预计算、serving 贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder jointly encodes query and item together, capturing fine-grained interaction but can't be precomputed, making serving expensive.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 双塔(two-tower)和 cross-encoder 都能给 query 和 item 打匹配分，你要一句话说清为什么召回阶段常选双塔。
scenario_en: Both two-tower and cross-encoder score query-item match; you must state in one line why retrieval usually picks two-tower.
q: 召回阶段选双塔而非 cross-encoder，换来什么、牺牲什么？
q_en: Choosing two-tower over a cross-encoder for retrieval — what's gained and what's lost?
why: 双塔换来 serving 高效：物品向量可离线预计算、线上只算一次 query 向量再做近邻检索，能在毫秒级从千万级物品里召回。代价是塔各自独立编码，丢掉了 cross-encoder 那种把 query 和 item 拼在一起才能捕捉的细粒度交互。
why_en: Two-tower buys serving efficiency — item vectors are precomputed so only the query is encoded online — at the cost of the fine-grained query-item interaction a cross-encoder captures by joint encoding.
tradeoff: 双塔(可预计算、serving 快) vs cross-encoder(细粒度交互强、但每对都要现算、serving 贵)
options: 双塔更快但更不准，cross-encoder 又快又准，只是工程复杂所以少用
双塔换来 serving 高效（物品向量可预计算），牺牲了 cross-encoder 的细粒度 query-item 交互精度
两者完全等价，只是命名不同，选哪个不影响延迟和精度
cross-encoder 可预计算所以 serving 更快，双塔必须每对现算所以慢
options_en: Two-tower is faster but less accurate; cross-encoder is both fast and accurate and only rarely used because it's complex.
Two-tower buys serving efficiency (item vectors precomputable) at the cost of the fine-grained query-item interaction accuracy of a cross-encoder.
They're fully equivalent, just named differently, and the choice affects neither latency nor accuracy.
The cross-encoder is precomputable so it serves faster, while two-tower must score each pair live and is slower.
optionExplanations: cross-encoder 并非又快又准：它精度高但每个 query-item 对都要现算，在千万级候选上 serving 扛不住。
对；双塔的可预计算换来毫秒级大规模召回，代价是牺牲了拼接编码才有的细粒度交互。
并不等价：可预计算与否直接决定能否在延迟内从海量物品召回，精度侧也有差。
说反了：可预计算的是双塔（物品向量离线算好），cross-encoder 才是每对现算的那个。
optionExplanations_en: A cross-encoder isn't both fast and accurate: it's accurate but must score every query-item pair live, which can't scale to tens of millions of candidates.
Correct — two-tower's precomputability buys millisecond large-scale retrieval, at the cost of the fine-grained interaction only joint encoding gives.
Not equivalent: precomputability decides whether you can retrieve from a huge corpus within latency, and accuracy differs too.
Backwards: two-tower is the precomputable one (item vectors computed offline); the cross-encoder scores each pair live.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  subgraph TwoTower["双塔 two-tower"]
    Q1["query 塔"] --> V1["query 向量"]
    I1["item 塔(离线预计算)"] --> V2["item 向量库"]
    V1 --> M1["内积/ANN 匹配"]
    V2 --> M1
  end
  subgraph Cross["cross-encoder"]
    QI["query+item 拼接"] --> ENC["联合编码"] --> S["匹配分(每对现算)"]
  end

termDefinitions.meaning: 在向量空间里快速找最接近 query 向量的物品，用近似换速度，支撑双塔的大规模召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search quickly finds items closest to the query vector, trading exactness for speed to power large-scale two-tower retrieval.

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 你在准备资深级面试，想知道哪一个习惯性动作对评分的正向影响最大。
scenario_en: Preparing for senior interviews, you want to know which single habit most positively affects your score.
q: 在 senior/Staff+ 面试里，单个最高信号的行为是什么？
q_en: What is the single highest-signal behavior in senior/Staff+ interviews?
why: 显式的取舍推理是 senior/Staff+ 单个最高信号的行为。光说「我会用 X」在资深级读作瞎猜；把每个决策说成「换来什么、牺牲什么、为什么在本情境下我选它」，才证明你在做工程判断而非套模板。
why_en: Explicit trade-off reasoning is the single highest-signal behavior at senior/Staff+; a bare 'I'd use X' reads as guessing, while naming gain, loss, and why-here proves engineering judgment.
options: 把尽可能多的组件都点到，展示知识面广
显式的取舍推理：每个决策都说清换来什么、牺牲什么、为什么本情境选它
在一个熟悉的组件上钻得越深越好，证明技术硬
尽量用最新的模型架构名词，显得紧跟前沿
options_en: Name as many components as possible to show breadth of knowledge.
Explicit trade-off reasoning: for each decision state what's gained, what's lost, and why it fits here.
Drill as deep as possible into one familiar component to prove technical strength.
Drop the newest model-architecture terms to seem on the cutting edge.
optionExplanations: 点满组件正是「只广不深」失败模式，广度本身不是高信号。
对；取舍推理直接展示工程判断，是资深级评分权重最高的单个动作。
钻太深是「钻牛角尖」失败模式，深度不回连全局并不加分。
堆名词不等于判断力，反而容易在被追问得失时露馅。
optionExplanations_en: Maxing out components is the shallow-survey failure mode; breadth alone isn't high signal.
Correct — trade-off reasoning directly displays engineering judgment, the single most heavily weighted behavior at senior level.
Drilling too deep is the rabbit-hole failure mode; depth that never reconnects to the whole doesn't score.
Piling on terms isn't judgment and tends to collapse when you're pressed on gains and losses.
category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 为了即使紧张也能强制自己讲取舍，文中给了一个句法习惯。
scenario_en: To force yourself to state trade-offs even when nervous, the lesson gives a syntactic habit.
q: 把每个设计决策都说成含哪两个短语的句子，就能逼出取舍表达？
q_en: Framing every design decision as a sentence containing which two phrases forces trade-off articulation?
text: 把每个设计决策说成一句同时含「{{gives us}}」（换来什么）和「{{costs us}}」（牺牲什么）的话——这个句法习惯即使在紧张时也能逼你把取舍讲出来。
text_en: Frame every design decision as a sentence containing both '{{gives us}}' and '{{costs us}}' — this syntactic habit forces trade-off articulation even when you're nervous.
why: 「gives us / costs us」是一个可随身携带的句法钩子：句子结构本身要求你填上得与失，于是紧张时也不会漏讲取舍，直接对治沉默取舍这个失败模式。
why_en: 'Gives us / costs us' is a portable syntactic hook whose very structure demands you fill in the gain and the loss, so trade-offs survive even nerves.
category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 复盘手册说，失败模式自救脚本和之前学的「4 步 pushback 框架」是互补的两套工具。
scenario_en: The playbook says the failure-mode recovery scripts and the earlier '4-step pushback framework' are two complementary tools.
q: pushback 恢复和失败模式恢复，触发来源有什么区别？
q_en: How do pushback recovery and failure-mode recovery differ in what triggers them?
why: pushback 恢复应对面试官发起的约束变更（他改了规模/延迟/需求），是被动接招；失败模式恢复是你自己发起的临场纠偏（发现钻牛角尖就 zoom out），是主动自救。两者合起来才是完整的抗压工具箱。
why_en: Pushback recovery answers interviewer-initiated constraint changes, while failure-mode recovery is self-initiated course correction; together they form the full resilience toolkit.
tradeoff: pushback 恢复(面试官发起、被动接招) vs 失败模式恢复(自己发起、主动纠偏)
options: 两者都是面试官发起的，只是一个改约束、一个改题目
pushback 恢复是面试官发起的约束变更；失败模式恢复是你自己发起的临场纠偏，二者互补
两者都是候选人自己发起的，只是话术不同
pushback 恢复只在编码轮用，失败模式恢复只在系统设计轮用
options_en: Both are interviewer-initiated; one changes constraints and the other changes the problem.
Pushback recovery handles interviewer-initiated constraint changes; failure-mode recovery is self-initiated course correction — the two are complementary.
Both are candidate-initiated and differ only in wording.
Pushback recovery is only for coding rounds and failure-mode recovery only for system design rounds.
optionExplanations: 混淆了触发源：失败模式恢复不是面试官发起的，是你自己察觉走偏后主动做的。
对；一个应对外部约束变更、一个应对自己走偏，触发源正好相反，合起来覆盖两类风险。
说反了一半：pushback 是面试官发起的，不是候选人自己发起。
两套工具跨轮次通用，不限定编码或系统设计。
optionExplanations_en: Confuses the trigger: failure-mode recovery isn't interviewer-initiated; you do it after noticing your own drift.
Correct — one answers external constraint changes and one answers your own drift; opposite triggers that together cover both risk types.
Half-backwards: pushback is interviewer-initiated, not candidate-initiated.
Both tools apply across rounds and aren't limited to coding or system design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应对面试官临场改约束（改规模/延迟/需求）的 4 步应对法，属被面试官发起的恢复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The pushback framework is a 4-step method for handling interviewer-initiated constraint changes (scale/latency/requirement shifts).

category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 官方给的自救话术念起来不像你平时说话，你想改成自己的口吻。
scenario_en: The official recovery scripts don't sound like how you normally talk, and you want to adapt them to your own voice.
q: 个性化自救话术时，哪一点绝不能动？
q_en: When personalizing a recovery script, what must you never change?
why: 措辞可以改成你自己的口吻、更自然，但必须保住三拍结构：承认偏了→说出怎么纠→真的执行。丢掉承认这一拍会显得遮掩，丢掉执行会变空话，结构才是话术起作用的骨架。
why_en: Adapt the wording to your own voice, but preserve the three-beat structure — acknowledge, name the correction, execute — because the structure, not the phrasing, is what makes the script work.
whenOtherWins: 如果某个场景天然只需要一步（比如只是补一个数字），可以压缩表达，但仍要保留「承认+执行」的最小闭环。
options: 必须一字不差背原话，任何改写都会削弱效果
措辞可自由改成自己的口吻，但要保住「承认→纠正→执行」三拍结构
只要保留执行这一拍就行，承认和说纠正都可以省
把话术改得越长越正式越好，显得准备充分
options_en: Recite the exact wording verbatim, since any rewrite weakens it.
Freely adapt the wording to your own voice, but preserve the three-beat structure (acknowledge, correct, execute).
Keep only the execute beat; acknowledging and naming the correction can be dropped.
Make the script as long and formal as possible to seem well-prepared.
optionExplanations: 背原话反而僵硬、像念稿；自然口吻更可信，可改的正是措辞。
对；骨架（三拍）保住、血肉（措辞）随你，这样既自然又不丢自救的有效结构。
省掉承认会显得遮掩、省掉说纠正会突兀，三拍缺一恢复就不完整。
越长越正式反而显得在背模板，简短自然的三拍才有效。
optionExplanations_en: Verbatim recital sounds stiff and scripted; a natural voice is more credible, and wording is exactly what you may change.
Correct — keep the skeleton (three beats), let the flesh (wording) be yours, staying natural without losing the effective structure.
Dropping acknowledge looks evasive and dropping name-the-correction feels abrupt; missing any beat leaves the recovery incomplete.
Longer and more formal reads as reciting a template; a short, natural three-beat is what works.
category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 五大失败模式各有一个可当场自查的诊断阈值，用来判断自己是不是踩进去了。
scenario_en: Each of the five failure modes has a self-checkable diagnostic threshold to tell whether you've fallen in.
q: 补全钻牛角尖和只广不深的两个诊断阈值：
q_en: Fill in the two diagnostic thresholds for rabbit hole and shallow survey:
text: 钻牛角尖(Rabbit Hole)的信号：在一个组件上停留超过 {{3}} 分钟却没回连 pipeline；只广不深(Shallow Survey)的信号：点了超过 {{5}} 个组件却没讲透任何一个的内部机制与取舍。
text_en: Rabbit-hole signal: over {{3}} minutes on one component without linking back to the pipeline; shallow-survey signal: naming more than {{5}} components without going deep on any one's internals and trade-offs.
why: 这两个是可当场数的阈值：单组件 >3 分钟、或点名 >5 个组件都没讲透，就该触发自救。它们不是硬定律，而是让你在压力下快速自查的经验红线。
why_en: These are countable in-room thresholds — over three minutes on one component, or more than five named without depth — that trigger recovery; they're rules of thumb, not hard laws.
category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 你想理解为什么学术背景强的候选人特别容易犯「不报数字(NFR Blind Spot)」这个失败模式。
scenario_en: You want to understand why academically strong candidates are especially prone to the NFR-blind-spot failure mode.
q: 「不报数字」这个失败模式的根因通常是什么？
q_en: What's the usual root cause of the NFR-blind-spot failure mode?
why: 根因是学术训练把重心放在模型精度上、很少练运维约束，所以答题时本能盯着 accuracy/AUC，忘了延迟、QPS、成本这些生产里真正决定可行性的量级。对治办法是开场就主动锚定 NFR。
why_en: The root cause is that academic training emphasizes accuracy over operational constraints, so candidates fixate on accuracy/AUC and forget the latency, QPS, and cost magnitudes that decide feasibility in production.
options: 候选人故意不报数字，想藏住自己不会估算
学术训练强调模型精度、少练运维约束，所以本能忽略延迟/QPS/成本这些生产量级
因为面试题从不提供任何数字，报了也没依据
因为报数字属于高级技巧，初级候选人还没资格用
options_en: Candidates deliberately cite no numbers to hide that they can't estimate.
Academic training emphasizes model accuracy over operational constraints, so latency/QPS/cost magnitudes get instinctively ignored.
Because interview prompts never provide any numbers, so any figure would be unfounded.
Because citing numbers is an advanced skill juniors aren't yet qualified to use.
optionExplanations: 多数不是故意藏拙，而是训练重心让人根本没想到要报运维数字。
对；学术偏精度、轻运维的惯性，让人盯着 AUC 忘了延迟/QPS/成本这些首要约束。
题目常故意不给 NFR，正是要考你主动补——不给数字不等于没约束。
报数字不是资历门槛，恰恰是资深级被期待的基本动作。
optionExplanations_en: It's usually not deliberate hiding but a training bias that never prompts operational numbers.
Correct — the accuracy-over-ops habit from academia makes people watch AUC and forget latency/QPS/cost, the primary constraints.
Prompts often omit NFRs on purpose to test if you surface them — no numbers given doesn't mean no constraints.
Citing numbers isn't a seniority gate; it's precisely the baseline move expected at senior level.
category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 你想在模拟面试里系统性地练掉这五个失败模式，而不只是靠自己感觉。
scenario_en: You want to systematically train away the five failure modes in mock interviews, not just by feel.
q: 文中推荐的「搭档辅助练习」具体怎么做？
q_en: What is the recommended partner-assisted practice method?
why: 让模拟搭档在你答题时安静地记录出现了哪些失败模式，结束后对着那张五模式表逐条复盘。第三方视角能抓到你自己察觉不到的走偏，比闷头自练更快看到盲区。
why_en: Have a mock partner silently track which failure modes appear while you answer, then debrief against the five-mode table; an outside view catches drift you can't see yourself.
options: 让搭档全程打断你、每犯一个错就立刻纠正
让搭档安静记录你出现了哪些失败模式，结束后对着五模式表逐条复盘
让搭档替你回答，你在旁边看他怎么做
两人各自练，练完只对比谁用的模型更新
options_en: Have the partner interrupt you throughout and correct each mistake the instant it happens.
Have the partner silently track which failure modes appear, then debrief against the five-mode table afterward.
Have the partner answer for you while you watch how they do it.
Practice separately and afterward only compare who used the newer model.
optionExplanations: 全程打断会毁掉表达连贯性，也练不出你在真实无干预下的自我纠偏。
对；安静观察+事后对表复盘，既保留真实答题状态，又拿到第三方视角标出的盲区。
看搭档答替代不了你自己练，抓不到你个人的走偏习惯。
比谁模型新完全跑题，练的是失败行为不是模型选型。
optionExplanations_en: Interrupting throughout destroys your flow and never trains the self-correction you'd need without intervention.
Correct — silent observation plus a table-based debrief keeps your answering authentic while giving an outside view of your blind spots.
Watching the partner answer can't replace your own reps and misses your personal drift habits.
Comparing whose model is newer misses the point; you're training failure behaviors, not model selection.
category: Common Failure Modes And Live Recovery Scripts

scenario: 面试官抛出一句「给 Airbnb 设计一个搜索排序系统」，没有任何约束，等你开口。
scenario_en: The interviewer drops 'design a search ranking system for Airbnb' with no constraints and waits for you to start.
q: 什么是「问题形式化(problem formulation)」，为什么它决定成败？
q_en: What is 'problem formulation,' and why does it decide success?
why: 问题形式化 = 把模糊的业务命题翻译成一个精确、可解的 ML 问题。形式化对了，后面每个决策都容易被追问时自证；形式化错了，架构再精巧也是在解错的问题。
why_en: Problem formulation is translating a vague business prompt into a precise, solvable ML problem; get it right and every downstream decision is easy to justify, get it wrong and even a sophisticated architecture solves the wrong problem.
diagram:
flowchart LR V["模糊业务命题
(intentionally vague)"] -->|结构化探索
problem formulation| P["精确可解的
ML 问题"] P --> D["每个下游决策
都可追溯自证"]
options: 问题形式化就是选定模型架构，越早定下用哪个模型越好
问题形式化 = 把模糊业务命题翻译成精确可解的 ML 问题；错了则架构再精巧也在解错问题
问题形式化是最后写评估指标的步骤，放在设计末尾即可
问题形式化是把需求写成代码接口，主要是工程活
options_en: Problem formulation means choosing the model architecture, and the earlier you fix the model the better.
Problem formulation is translating a vague business prompt into a precise, solvable ML problem; get it wrong and even a sophisticated architecture solves the wrong problem.
Problem formulation is the final step of writing evaluation metrics, fine to leave for the end of the design.
Problem formulation is turning requirements into code interfaces — mostly an engineering task.
optionExplanations: 过早锁模型正是要避免的锚定：形式化是先定义问题，不是先选模型。
对；先把模糊命题收敛成一个精确 ML 问题，后面的架构、指标才有对的靶子。
指标是形式化的产物之一，但形式化本身发生在最前面，不是收尾步骤。
写接口是工程实现；形式化解决的是「到底要解哪个 ML 问题」这个更前置的判断。
optionExplanations_en: Locking the model early is exactly the anchoring to avoid: formulation defines the problem first, not the model.
Correct — converging the vague prompt into a precise ML problem first gives the architecture and metrics a correct target.
Metrics are an output of formulation, but formulation itself happens up front, not as a wrap-up step.
Writing interfaces is implementation; formulation answers the earlier question of which ML problem to solve at all.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 面试才刚开始几分钟，你在纠结要先展示哪个高级模型来抓住面试官。
scenario_en: Only a few minutes in, you're deciding which advanced model to showcase first to impress the interviewer.
q: 面试官对候选人的评估，权重最高的往往是哪个阶段？
q_en: Which phase carries the most weight in how interviewers assess candidates?
why: 面试官很大程度上看你开场那几分钟的结构化问题探索——这段早期 framing 往往比后面任何单个建模选择更影响评分。开局把问题框对，比秀一个高级模型更值钱。
why_en: Interviewers weigh the first few minutes of structured problem exploration heavily, and that early framing often matters more than any single modeling choice.
options: 开场几分钟的结构化问题探索——早期 framing 比后面任何单个建模选择都更影响评分
中段选用的模型架构，越前沿越能决定评分
结尾的评估与监控方案，是打分的主要依据
全程的编码实现细节，写得越完整分越高
options_en: The first few minutes of structured problem exploration — early framing matters more than any single later modeling choice.
The mid-session model architecture — the more cutting-edge, the higher the score.
The closing evaluation and monitoring plan is the main basis for scoring.
The coding implementation details throughout — the more complete, the higher the score.
optionExplanations: 对；开局的框定质量最能预示后面所有决策的可辩护性，权重自然最高。
秀前沿模型若没框对问题，反而暴露锚定；架构不是评分的重心。
评估重要，但它是形式化的下游产物，不是被最先、最重看的阶段。
编码完整度不是系统设计面的主要信号，判断力才是。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the quality of the opening framing predicts the defensibility of every later decision, so it carries the most weight.
Showcasing a cutting-edge model without framing the problem exposes anchoring; architecture isn't the scoring focus.
Evaluation matters but is a downstream product of formulation, not the first and most heavily weighted phase.
Coding completeness isn't the main signal in a system design round; judgment is.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 面试官给的命题「给 Airbnb 设计搜索排序」故意含糊，你不确定他是不是漏说了细节。
scenario_en: The prompt 'design search ranking for Airbnb' is deliberately vague, and you're unsure if the interviewer just left out details.
q: 「问题形式化 gap」指什么？含糊的命题是疏忽还是有意？
q_en: What is the 'problem-formulation gap,' and is a vague prompt an oversight or intentional?
why: 形式化 gap = 面试官那句「有意含糊」的命题，和你最终要解的那个具体 ML 问题之间的距离。含糊是故意的，用来考你导航歧义的能力——同一句命题会因优化目标、用户情境、延迟预算、冷启动比例分叉成完全不同的系统。
why_en: The formulation gap is the distance between the interviewer's intentionally ambiguous prompt and the specific ML problem you end up solving; the vagueness is deliberate, testing how you navigate ambiguity.
options: 指命题写得不够详细，属于面试官的疏忽，你应假设一个默认场景直接开做
指模型和数据之间的差距，靠加特征就能补上
指有意含糊的命题与你要解的具体 ML 问题之间的距离；含糊是故意的，考你导航歧义
指线上和线下指标的差距，属于评估阶段的问题
options_en: It means the prompt lacks detail due to the interviewer's oversight, so assume a default scenario and just start building.
It means the gap between model and data, closable by adding features.
It's the distance between the intentionally ambiguous prompt and the specific ML problem you solve; the vagueness is deliberate, testing ambiguity navigation.
It means the gap between online and offline metrics, an evaluation-stage concern.
optionExplanations: 把含糊当疏忽、直接假设默认场景，正是被考的反面——你会解到错的问题上。
这是把 gap 误当技术差距；形式化 gap 是命题到问题定义的距离，不是特征问题。
对；含糊是刻意设计的考点，你要主动把命题收敛成一个具体问题，而不是接受表面。
线上线下 gap 是另一个概念，不是命题到问题定义之间的这段形式化距离。
optionExplanations_en: Treating vagueness as oversight and assuming a default is exactly what's tested against — you'll solve the wrong problem.
This mistakes the gap for a technical gap; the formulation gap is prompt-to-problem-definition distance, not a feature issue.
Correct — the vagueness is a deliberate test, and you must actively converge the prompt into a specific problem rather than accept the surface.
The online-offline gap is a different concept, not this prompt-to-definition formulation distance.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 同一句「Airbnb 搜索排序」，业务目标定为「预订转化率」时，你要选一种建模形式。
scenario_en: For the same 'Airbnb search ranking,' with the business objective set to booking conversion, you must pick a modeling form.
q: 当优化目标是预订转化时，最直接的形式化是什么？
q_en: When the objective is booking conversion, what's the most direct formulation?
why: 优化目标决定形式化。目标是预订转化 → learning-to-rank，用「完成预订」当正样本标签排序。若目标换成长期房东满意度，就要变成多目标（预订率+评价分+房东留存），形式完全不同。
why_en: The optimization target drives formulation: booking conversion maps to learning-to-rank with completed bookings as the positive label, while long-term host satisfaction becomes a multi-objective problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务目标改成长期房东满意度，就该用多目标（预订率+评价分+房东留存），而不是单一预订转化的 LTR。
options: 多目标优化，同时平衡预订率、评价分和房东留存
learning-to-rank，用「完成预订」作为正样本标签来排序
无监督聚类，把房源分组后按组推荐
回归预测每个房源的绝对价格，价高者排前
options_en: Multi-objective optimization balancing booking rate, review scores, and host retention at once.
Learning-to-rank, using completed bookings as the positive label to order listings.
Unsupervised clustering that groups listings and recommends by group.
Regression predicting each listing's absolute price, ranking higher-priced first.
optionExplanations: 多目标是「长期房东满意度」那个目标的形式化，对预订转化这个单目标是过度复杂化。
对；预订转化是明确的正/负信号，用完成预订当正标签的 LTR 直接对齐这个目标。
聚类没有利用预订这个监督信号，答不了「哪个更可能被订」。
预测绝对价格与「被预订概率」错位，价高不等于转化高。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-objective is the formulation for the host-satisfaction target; it over-complicates the single booking-conversion goal.
Correct — booking conversion is a clear positive/negative signal, so LTR with completed bookings as the positive label aligns directly.
Clustering ignores the booking supervision signal and can't answer which listing is more likely booked.
Predicting absolute price is misaligned with booking probability; higher price isn't higher conversion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 直接学习候选集的排序（而非独立打分）的一类方法，常用成对或列表损失，正样本是被点击/预订的项。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learning to rank (LTR) learns to order a candidate set directly, often with pairwise or listwise loss, using clicked or booked items as positives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时优化多个可能冲突的目标（如预订率、评价、房东留存），需要加权或帕累托权衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Multi-objective optimization jointly optimizes several possibly conflicting goals (booking rate, reviews, host retention) via weighting or Pareto trade-offs.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 同一个排序问题，延迟预算被确认为极紧的 50ms（对比另一场景是宽松的 500ms）。
scenario_en: For the same ranking problem, the latency budget is confirmed as a tight 50ms (versus a generous 500ms in another scenario).
q: 50ms 的延迟预算会把形式化推向什么，和 500ms 有何不同？
q_en: How does a 50ms budget steer the formulation, versus 500ms?
why: 延迟预算直接砍掉整类模型。50ms → 只能上轻量模型 + 预计算特征，来不及做重推理；500ms → 装得下更重的 re-ranking 阶段。同一个问题，预算不同就分叉成不同架构。
why_en: The latency budget prunes whole model classes: 50ms forces lightweight models with precomputed features, while 500ms leaves room for heavier re-ranking stages.
whenOtherWins: 如果预算是 500ms（如非首屏、可异步的场景），就能负担更重的 re-ranking，不必压到纯轻量模型。
options: 50ms 和 500ms 没本质区别，模型选型主要看精度而非延迟
50ms 允许更重的模型，因为预算紧反而要靠大模型一次算准
50ms → 只能用轻量模型 + 预计算特征；500ms → 装得下更重的 re-ranking
50ms 意味着必须离线批处理，不能做在线推理
options_en: 50ms and 500ms are essentially the same; model choice depends on accuracy, not latency.
50ms allows heavier models, because a tight budget means you need one big model to get it right in one shot.
50ms forces lightweight models plus precomputed features; 500ms leaves room for a heavier re-ranking stage.
50ms means you must go offline batch and can't do online inference.
optionExplanations: 延迟恰恰是硬约束：它决定哪类模型根本来不及跑，不能只看精度。
说反了：预算越紧越用不起重模型，只能靠轻量模型+预计算把在线开销压下来。
对；50ms 逼你把重活挪到离线（预计算特征），线上只留轻量打分。
50ms 依然是在线推理，只是必须是轻量的；不等于退化成离线批处理。
optionExplanations_en: Latency is precisely the hard constraint: it decides which model classes can't run in time, not just accuracy.
Backwards: a tighter budget means you can't afford heavy models and must push cost offline with lightweight scoring.
Correct — 50ms forces the heavy work offline (precomputed features), leaving only lightweight scoring online.
50ms is still online inference, just lightweight; it doesn't degrade to offline batch.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 澄清时你得知：Airbnb 每季度有约 40% 是全新房源（冷启动），而非稳定不变的存量。
scenario_en: You learn that about 40% of Airbnb listings each quarter are brand-new (cold-start), rather than stable inventory.
q: 40% 季度新房源这个事实，会怎样改变你的形式化？
q_en: How does 40% new listings per quarter change your formulation?
why: 40% 的季度新房源意味着大量物品没有交互历史，纯协同过滤会把它们冷落。它逼你做和稳定存量完全不同的特征工程：重内容特征（描述、图片、位置）而非依赖行为信号，否则新房源永远排不上去。
why_en: 40% new listings each quarter means many items have no interaction history, so you need content-based feature engineering rather than relying on behavioral signals, unlike a stable inventory.
options: 没影响，新房源和老房源用同一套行为特征排序即可
意味着大量物品无交互历史，逼你做重内容特征的冷启动工程，而非依赖行为信号
意味着直接把新房源全部排到最后，等它们攒够点击再说
意味着改用回归预测房源价格，绕开冷启动
options_en: No impact — rank new and old listings with the same behavioral features.
It means many items have no interaction history, forcing content-heavy cold-start feature engineering instead of relying on behavioral signals.
It means simply ranking all new listings last until they accumulate enough clicks.
It means switching to regression on listing price to sidestep cold-start.
optionExplanations: 同一套行为特征对无历史的新房源是空的，40% 库存会被系统性埋没。
对；冷启动比例这么高，特征工程必须重内容侧（文本/图片/位置）来给新房源打分。
把新房源全排最后会伤害供给侧和用户体验，也不是解决冷启动的办法。
换回归改的是任务类型，回避不了「新房源没有信号」这个冷启动核心。
optionExplanations_en: The same behavioral features are empty for history-less new listings, systematically burying 40% of inventory.
Correct — with a cold-start ratio this high, feature engineering must lean on content (text/images/location) to score new listings.
Ranking all new listings last hurts supply and user experience and doesn't solve cold-start.
Switching to regression changes the task type but doesn't address the core cold-start issue of no signal for new listings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 新用户或新物品缺乏历史交互，协同信号为空，需靠内容特征或探索来补。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cold-start is when new users or items lack interaction history, so collaborative signals are empty and you rely on content features or exploration.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 澄清「搜索」的用户情境时，发现同一个搜索框既服务想订周末游的房客，也服务查看竞品定价的房东。
scenario_en: Clarifying the 'search' user context, you find the same box serves guests planning a weekend trip and hosts checking competitor pricing.
q: 为什么必须先分清「房客搜索」和「房东查竞品」这两种情境？
q_en: Why separate a guest's trip search from a host checking competitors first?
why: 两种用户意图完全不同：房客要可预订、匹配日期的房源，房东要的是竞品价格情报。意图不同 → 特征不同、指标不同，甚至是两个系统。不澄清就默认一种，等于赌一半概率解错问题。
why_en: Guest and host intents differ entirely — one wants bookable listings, the other wants competitor pricing — so features and metrics differ, and assuming one without asking risks solving the wrong problem.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确只做房客侧搜索，就可以把房东情境显式排除在范围外，聚焦单一意图。
options: 不用分，搜索框只有一个，两类用户可以共用同一排序逻辑
因为两种意图不同（可预订房源 vs 竞品价格情报），特征、指标乃至系统都不同
因为房东用户更重要，应该优先只服务房东
因为要按用户地理位置分区，和意图无关
options_en: No need — there's one search box, so both user types can share the same ranking logic.
Because the two intents differ (bookable listings vs competitor pricing intel), so features, metrics, and even the system differ.
Because host users matter more and should be served first and exclusively.
Because you should partition by user geography, unrelated to intent.
optionExplanations: 共用一套逻辑会两头不讨好：给房客的可预订排序满足不了房东的比价需求。
对；先分清意图，才知道该建哪套特征、用哪个指标，避免解错问题。
谁更重要是范围决策，但前提是先把两种意图分开、显式取舍。
地理分区是另一维度，回避不了「这是给房客还是房东用」这个意图问题。
optionExplanations_en: One shared logic satisfies neither: a guest's bookable ranking can't meet a host's price-comparison need.
Correct — separating intent first tells you which features and metric to use, avoiding solving the wrong problem.
Which matters more is a scoping decision, but only after explicitly separating the two intents.
Geographic partitioning is a different dimension and doesn't resolve the guest-vs-host intent question.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 命题刚说完，你的第一句话就在定调——面试官正据此判断你的级别。
scenario_en: Right after the prompt, your very first sentence sets the tone — the interviewer is already gauging your level.
q: 初级和资深候选人，对模糊命题的第一反应有何差别？
q_en: How do junior and senior candidates differ in their first response to a vague prompt?
why: 初级第一反应是报一个模型（「我会用 two-tower」）；资深第一反应是问业务目标和成功指标。先问目标的人才能把问题框对，报模型只是提前锚定。
why_en: A junior's first move is to name a model ('I'd use a two-tower'), while a senior first asks about the business objective and success metric.
tradeoff: 先报模型(显得果断但提前锚定) vs 先问目标/指标(慢半拍但框对问题)
options: 初级先问业务目标，资深先报一个模型架构
两者第一反应一样，只是资深讲得更流利
初级先报一个模型（如 two-tower），资深先问业务目标与成功指标
初级先问延迟预算，资深先谈数据分布
options_en: Juniors first ask the business objective, seniors first name a model architecture.
Both respond the same way; seniors just say it more fluently.
Juniors first name a model (e.g. two-tower); seniors first ask about the business objective and success metric.
Juniors first ask about the latency budget, seniors first discuss data distribution.
optionExplanations: 说反了：先问目标是资深行为，先报模型是初级的提前锚定。
第一反应的方向恰恰不同，这正是级别信号所在，不只是流利度。
对；先问目标与指标，后面所有决策才有可追溯的靶子，这是资深的开局。
延迟和数据是后续维度，第一反应的分水岭是「先报模型 vs 先问目标」。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: asking the objective first is the senior move; naming a model first is the junior's premature anchoring.
The direction of the first response is exactly what differs — that's the level signal, not just fluency.
Correct — asking objective and metric first gives every later decision a traceable target; that's the senior opening.
Latency and data are later dimensions; the dividing line at the first response is 'name a model vs ask the objective.'
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 设计到一半，面试官挑战你：「为什么这里用两阶段而不是一把梭？」
scenario_en: Mid-design, the interviewer challenges: 'why two stages here instead of one pass?'
q: 被挑战时，初级和资深在「设计可辩护性」上差在哪？
q_en: When challenged, how do junior and senior differ in design defensibility?
why: 资深能把每个决策追溯回形式化阶段确立的某条需求（「我们定了 200ms 预算、100M 物品，所以排除一次过重打分」）；初级在被挑战时讲不出所以然，因为决策没锚在需求上。
why_en: A senior traces every decision back to a requirement set during formulation, while a junior can't justify choices when challenged because they weren't anchored to requirements.
tradeoff: 决策锚在需求上(可被追溯自证) vs 决策靠直觉/惯例(被挑战即失守)
options: 初级能追溯到需求，资深只会说这是常见模式
资深把决策追溯回形式化时确立的需求，初级被挑战时讲不出理由
两者都能自证，只是资深用词更专业
初级更敢坚持己见，所以更能辩护
options_en: Juniors trace to requirements, seniors just say it's a common pattern.
Seniors trace decisions back to requirements set during formulation, while juniors can't justify when challenged.
Both can justify; seniors just use more professional wording.
Juniors are more willing to hold their ground, so they defend better.
optionExplanations: 说反了：靠「常见模式」搪塞是初级，追溯需求才是资深。
对；决策一开始就锚在需求上，被追问时才能一句话把它拎回约束、自证成立。
关键不是用词，而是有没有可追溯的需求链；这决定了能不能真正辩护。
嘴硬不是辩护；没有需求支撑的坚持一被挑战就塌。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: falling back on 'common pattern' is junior; tracing to requirements is senior.
Correct — anchoring decisions to requirements from the start lets you pull them back to a constraint in one line when pressed.
The point isn't wording but whether there's a traceable requirement chain; that's what enables real defense.
Stubbornness isn't defense; conviction without a requirement basis collapses under challenge.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 被问「你打算用什么离线指标衡量这个排序系统」时，你的答法暴露级别。
scenario_en: Asked 'what offline metric will you use for this ranker,' your answer reveals your level.
q: 在指标定义上，初级和资深候选人的差别是什么？
q_en: How do junior and senior candidates differ on metric definition?
why: 初级默认套 accuracy 或 AUC；资深把离线指标绑定到一个业务 KPI，并会讨论校准(calibration)。离线指标脱离业务 KPI，就算离线涨了线上也未必赚钱。
why_en: A junior defaults to accuracy or AUC, while a senior ties the offline metric to a business KPI and discusses calibration.
tradeoff: 默认 accuracy/AUC(离线好看但可能脱离业务) vs 绑定业务 KPI + 校准(离线涨对应线上赚)
options: 初级绑定业务 KPI，资深只看 accuracy
两者都用 AUC，只是资深会多画一条 PR 曲线
初级默认 accuracy/AUC；资深把离线指标绑定业务 KPI 并讨论校准
资深只关心线上 A/B，从不看离线指标
options_en: Juniors tie to a business KPI, seniors only watch accuracy.
Both use AUC; seniors just add a PR curve.
Juniors default to accuracy/AUC; seniors tie the offline metric to a business KPI and discuss calibration.
Seniors only care about online A/B and never look at offline metrics.
optionExplanations: 说反了：默认 accuracy 是初级，绑定 KPI 是资深。
多画曲线不是重点，重点是离线指标有没有对齐业务 KPI。
对；离线指标要能代理业务 KPI，还要校准，才能保证离线涨=线上有价值。
资深两者都看：离线快速迭代、线上最终验证，不是二选一。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: defaulting to accuracy is junior; tying to a KPI is senior.
Adding a curve isn't the point; the point is whether the offline metric aligns with the business KPI.
Correct — the offline metric must proxy the business KPI and be calibrated, so an offline gain means online value.
Seniors watch both: offline for fast iteration, online for final validation — not either/or.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量分类器把正样本排在负样本前的能力的离线指标，是技术指标不等于业务价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline metric of a classifier's ability to rank positives above negatives — technical, not business value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型预测的概率与真实发生频率一致的程度（说 0.7 就真有约 70% 发生）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibration is how well predicted probabilities match real frequencies — a 0.7 prediction should occur about 70% of the time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量业务成败的核心指标（如转化率、留存），离线指标应对齐它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) is a core business success metric like conversion or retention, which the offline metric should align to.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 一听到「欺诈检测」，你脑子立刻蹦出一套背好的架构：XGBoost + 规则兜底 + 流式处理，感觉很顺。
scenario_en: Hearing 'fraud detection,' your brain instantly surfaces a memorized stack: XGBoost + rule fallback + streaming, and it feels smooth.
q: 这种「秒出架构」的锚定为什么危险？
q_en: Why is this instant-architecture anchoring dangerous?
why: 锚定偏差让你把之后所有推理都拿来「合理化最初那个选择」，于是当面试官探一个你未验证假设覆盖不到的边缘情况时，你无法转向。更坏的是它感觉像自信和推进，不像犯错，所以最难自察。
why_en: Anchoring bias makes you filter all later reasoning to justify the initial choice, so you can't pivot when the interviewer probes an edge case your unvalidated assumptions miss — and it feels like confidence, not a mistake.
diagram:
flowchart TD P["听到'欺诈检测'"] --> A["秒出背好的架构
XGBoost+规则+流式"] A --> F["之后所有推理
都在合理化它"] F --> E["面试官探边缘情况"] E --> X["无法转向 → 失守"]
options: 危险在于 XGBoost 太老，应该锚定一个更新的模型
不危险，秒出架构说明你准备充分、反应快
锚定偏差让你后续只为合理化初始选择，边缘情况被探时无法转向；且它像自信而非错误、最难自察
危险仅在于流式处理太贵，换成批处理就没问题
options_en: The danger is that XGBoost is too old; anchor on a newer model instead.
Not dangerous — an instant architecture shows you're well-prepared and quick.
Anchoring bias makes you only rationalize the initial choice, so you can't pivot when an edge case is probed; and it feels like confidence, not error, so it's hardest to self-detect.
The danger is only that streaming is expensive; switch to batch and it's fine.
optionExplanations: 问题不在模型新旧，而在你还没框问题就锁死了方案。
秒出架构恰恰是锚定信号：快不等于框对了问题。
对；锚定的坏处是锁死推理方向、无法转向，且伪装成自信让你察觉不到。
换批处理没触及根因：根因是过早锁定、丧失转向能力，不是某个组件贵。
optionExplanations_en: The issue isn't the model's age but locking a solution before framing the problem.
An instant architecture is exactly the anchoring signal: fast doesn't mean you framed the problem right.
Correct — anchoring locks your reasoning direction and kills the ability to pivot, disguised as confidence so you don't notice.
Switching to batch misses the root cause: premature lock-in and lost pivot ability, not one expensive component.

termDefinitions.meaning: 过早认定一个方案后，把后续所有信息都往合理化它的方向解读，丧失转向能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Anchoring bias is fixating on an early choice and interpreting all later information to justify it, losing the ability to pivot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种梯度提升树模型，表格数据上强、可解释、上线快，常被当欺诈检测的默认选择。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: XGBoost is a gradient-boosted tree model, strong and interpretable on tabular data, often a default choice for fraud detection.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 你意识到自己一听命题就想秒出架构，想在开局就防住锚定这个最贵的失败模式。
scenario_en: You notice the urge to blurt an architecture on hearing the prompt, and want to guard against anchoring — the costliest failure mode — from the start.
q: 开局对抗锚定，最有效的做法是什么？
q_en: What's the most effective way to counter anchoring at the opening?
why: 锚定最贵是因为它感觉像自信和推进，而不像错误，所以最难当场察觉。对治办法是刻意延后锁定方案：先花 5–8 分钟做需求工程、把问题框清楚，让方案从需求里长出来，而不是反过来用需求合理化预设方案。
why_en: Anchoring is costly because it feels like confidence, not a mistake, so the counter is to deliberately delay committing — spend 5-8 minutes on requirements first and let the solution emerge from them.
whenOtherWins: 如果命题本身极窄、约束已给全（罕见），确实可以更快进入方案，但这种情况在开放式面试里几乎不出现。
options: 一想到架构就赶紧说出来，抢在忘记前把它讲完
刻意延后锁定方案：先做 5–8 分钟需求工程，让方案从需求里长出来
把脑中第一个架构默认当对的，再倒推需求去支持它
同时抛出三四个架构，让面试官帮你选
options_en: Say the architecture the instant it comes to mind, before you forget it.
Deliberately delay committing: do 5-8 minutes of requirements engineering first and let the solution emerge from them.
Treat the first architecture in your head as correct and back-fill requirements to support it.
Throw out three or four architectures at once and let the interviewer pick.
optionExplanations: 抢着说出来正是锚定：一旦出口，你后面会不自觉地只为它辩护。
对；先做需求工程、延后锁定，方案由约束推导而来，天然可辩护也能随探问转向。
倒推需求支持预设方案就是锚定的定义，最危险。
一次抛多个方案不是框问题，是把选择权外包，仍没做形式化。
optionExplanations_en: Blurting it out is anchoring itself: once said, you'll unconsciously only defend it.
Correct — doing requirements first and delaying commitment makes the solution derive from constraints, naturally defensible and able to pivot.
Back-filling requirements to fit a preset solution is the definition of anchoring — the most dangerous.
Throwing out several at once isn't framing the problem; it outsources the choice and still skips formulation.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 你想把开局的探索控制在一个合理时长，既框清问题又不至于问到面试官打断。
scenario_en: You want to time-box the opening exploration so you frame the problem without the interviewer having to cut you off.
q: 资深候选人通常把开局多长时间当作「需求工程阶段」？
q_en: How long do senior candidates treat as the 'requirements engineering' phase up front?
why: 资深把开局约 5–8 分钟当成需求工程阶段，先探索再承诺架构。这是经验时长而非公式：太短会漏约束、太长会被面试官叫停；它决定了你留给后续架构/建模的时间预算。
why_en: Seniors treat roughly the first 5-8 minutes as a requirements-engineering phase, exploring before committing to architecture — a rule-of-thumb window, not a formula.
options: 整场的一半时间，约 20 分钟，越久越稳
约 5–8 分钟，先做需求工程探索再承诺架构
开局 1 分钟就够，问一两句立刻进方案
不设时长，想到哪问到哪直到面试官满意
options_en: Half the session, about 20 minutes — the longer the safer.
About 5-8 minutes of requirements-engineering exploration before committing to architecture.
One minute is enough — ask a question or two and jump straight into the solution.
No time box — keep asking whatever comes to mind until the interviewer is satisfied.
optionExplanations: 20 分钟太久，会挤掉架构和深挖的时间，面试官多半会叫停。
对；5–8 分钟够把五个维度探一遍，又给后面 35+ 分钟留出架构与建模空间。
1 分钟框不清问题，容易漏掉决定性约束，滑向锚定。
无时长控制会被面试官打断，反而暴露你不会管理节奏。
optionExplanations_en: 20 minutes is too long, crowds out architecture and deep dives, and the interviewer will likely stop you.
Correct — 5-8 minutes covers the five dimensions while leaving 35+ minutes for architecture and modeling.
One minute can't frame the problem, misses decisive constraints, and slides into anchoring.
No time box gets you interrupted and reveals poor pacing control.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 同是欺诈类问题：一个场景 chargeback 标签 24 小时内到，另一个欺诈要 90 天才被确认。
scenario_en: Two fraud-like problems: in one, chargeback labels arrive within 24 hours; in another, fraud is confirmed only after 90 days.
q: 标签延迟从 24 小时变成 90 天，为什么会变成「两个不同的问题」？
q_en: Why does a label delay of 24 hours versus 90 days make it 'two different problems'?
why: 标签延迟决定训练能拿到什么监督信号。24 小时到的标签近乎实时可训；90 天才确认意味着你训练时手里全是「还没盖棺」的样本，必须按延迟反馈来设计（等待期、代理标签、样本重加权），是完全不同的形式化。
why_en: Label delay decides what supervision you have at training time: 24-hour labels are near-real-time, while 90-day confirmation forces delayed-feedback design (waiting windows, proxy labels, reweighting).
whenOtherWins: 如果标签很快且可靠（24 小时到位），就不必上延迟反馈那套复杂设计，直接用近实时监督即可。
options: 标签延迟只影响上线速度，不改变问题的形式化
90 天延迟意味着训练时样本大多未盖棺，必须按延迟反馈设计，和 24 小时是两个问题
延迟越长数据越干净，所以 90 天的问题反而更简单
只要多雇标注员，90 天延迟就能压到 24 小时
options_en: Label delay only affects deployment speed, not the problem's formulation.
A 90-day delay means most training samples aren't yet finalized, forcing delayed-feedback design — a different problem from 24 hours.
Longer delay means cleaner data, so the 90-day problem is actually simpler.
Just hire more annotators and the 90-day delay compresses to 24 hours.
optionExplanations: 延迟不只是上线快慢：它改变你训练时能拿到多少确定标签，直接重塑形式化。
对；90 天意味着大量样本标签未定，得设计等待期/代理标签/重加权，是另一套问题。
延迟长不等于更干净，反而带来大量未定标签，问题更难不是更简单。
chargeback 的 90 天是业务确认周期，加人也压不动，这不是标注人力问题。
optionExplanations_en: Delay isn't just deployment speed: it changes how many confirmed labels you have at training time, reshaping the formulation.
Correct — 90 days means many samples are unresolved, needing waiting windows/proxy labels/reweighting — a different problem.
Longer delay isn't cleaner; it brings many unresolved labels, making the problem harder, not simpler.
The 90-day chargeback is a business confirmation cycle; more headcount can't compress it — it's not a labeling-labor issue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持卡人向银行申诉撤销一笔交易，常作为欺诈的延迟真值标签。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chargeback is a cardholder disputing a transaction with the bank, often used as a delayed ground-truth fraud label.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签在预测很久之后才到达，训练必须处理大量暂时无标签或标签会翻转的样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delayed feedback is when labels arrive long after prediction, so training must handle many temporarily unlabeled or later-flipping samples.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 需求探索阶段，你在纠结要不要花一个问题去确认「现在线上有没有一套规则系统在跑」。
scenario_en: During exploration you're debating whether to spend a question confirming 'is there already a rule-based system in production.'
q: 为什么该问「现有 baseline 是什么」？它揭示了什么？
q_en: Why ask 'what's the current baseline,' and what does it reveal?
why: 问现有 baseline（比如已有规则系统）揭示了「增量改进」长什么样：你的模型不是从零证明价值，而是要打败一条现有基线。它决定成功标准、A/B 对照组，甚至要不要先复刻规则再叠加 ML。
why_en: Asking about the current baseline (e.g. an existing rule system) reveals what incremental improvement looks like — your model must beat a baseline, which sets the success bar and the A/B control.
whenOtherWins: 如果确认是全新产品、线上无任何 baseline，那成功标准就变成绝对值（如首次达到某召回/精度），而非相对提升。
options: 不必问，反正 ML 模型一定比规则强，直接替换即可
它揭示增量改进的样子：模型要打败一条现有基线，决定成功标准与 A/B 对照
问它只是礼貌，对设计没有实际影响
它主要用来估算数据量，和成功标准无关
options_en: No need to ask — an ML model always beats rules, so just replace it.
It reveals what incremental improvement looks like: your model must beat an existing baseline, setting the success bar and A/B control.
Asking is just politeness with no real design impact.
It's mainly for estimating data volume, unrelated to the success bar.
optionExplanations: 「一定更强」是危险假设：很多规则系统很强，ML 未必稳赢，忽视 baseline 会定错成功标准。
对；有 baseline，成功就变成相对提升，直接决定对照组、指标门槛和上线策略。
它有实打实的设计影响：没有它你都不知道要打败什么、涨多少才算成功。
它首先决定成功标准（要超过基线多少），估数据量是次要的。
optionExplanations_en: 'Always stronger' is a dangerous assumption: many rule systems are strong, ML may not win, and ignoring the baseline sets the wrong success bar.
Correct — with a baseline, success becomes a relative lift, directly setting the control group, metric threshold, and rollout strategy.
It has real design impact: without it you don't even know what to beat or how much lift counts as success.
It primarily sets the success bar (how much you must beat the baseline); estimating data volume is secondary.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 面试官问「你为什么用两阶段 retrieval-ranking，而不是一次过打分？」你要展示一条从约束到方案的追溯链。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'why two-stage retrieval-ranking instead of one-pass scoring?' and you must show a constraint-to-decision trace.
q: 把「探索模式」候选人追溯这个决策的推理链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the exploration-mode candidate's reasoning chain for this decision:
steps: 所以选两阶段：先轻量 retrieval 缩小候选，再重模型 ranking
形式化时已确立约束：200ms 预算、100M 物品
被挑战时能一句话追溯回约束，决策站得住
推出：一次过用重模型给 1 亿物品打分，装不进 200ms
why: 探索模式的力量在于每个决策都能倒放回一条既定约束：200ms + 100M 物品 → 一次过重打分不可行 → 两阶段 → 被挑战时可自证。解决方案模式的候选人只能说「这是常见套路」，一挑就塌。
why_en: Exploration mode lets every decision replay back to a stated constraint — 200ms plus 100M items rules out one-pass heavy scoring, forcing two stages, so it holds up when challenged.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["约束: 200ms + 100M 物品"] --> R["一次过重打分
装不进 200ms"] R --> T["两阶段: retrieval → ranking"] T --> D["被挑战可追溯自证"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量模型从海量物品召回少量候选(retrieval)，再用重模型对候选精排(ranking)，兼顾规模与精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-stage retrieval-ranking first recalls a small candidate set from a huge corpus with a light model, then precisely ranks it with a heavy model, balancing scale and accuracy.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 面对「为什么两阶段？」这个追问，探索模式和解决方案模式的候选人给出的答法截然不同。
scenario_en: To the follow-up 'why two stages,' exploration-mode and solution-mode candidates answer very differently.
q: 「探索模式」和「解决方案模式」候选人的答法差在哪？
q_en: How do exploration-mode and solution-mode candidates' answers differ?
why: 探索模式答：「我们定了 200ms 预算、100M 物品，所以排除一次过重打分」——把决策接回约束。解决方案模式只能答「这是常见模式」——没有可追溯的理由，一被追问就露怯。
why_en: Exploration mode answers by tracing the decision to a constraint ('we set a 200ms budget with 100M items, ruling out one-pass heavy scoring'), while solution mode can only say 'it's a common pattern.'
tradeoff: 追溯到约束(可自证、抗追问) vs 诉诸常见模式(无理由、一挑即塌)
options: 探索模式说「这是常见模式」，解决方案模式追溯到约束
两者答案一样，只是语气不同
探索模式把决策追溯回 200ms+100M 约束；解决方案模式只能说「这是常见模式」
解决方案模式答得更详细，所以更有说服力
options_en: Exploration mode says 'it's a common pattern,' solution mode traces to constraints.
Both answers are the same, differing only in tone.
Exploration mode traces the decision to the 200ms+100M constraint; solution mode can only say 'it's a common pattern.'
Solution mode answers in more detail, so it's more convincing.
optionExplanations: 说反了：追溯约束是探索模式，「常见模式」是解决方案模式。
答案的实质不同：一个有约束支撑、一个没有，这才是关键。
对；能把「两阶段」拎回 200ms+100M 的人，才在展示真正的形式化功力。
「常见模式」再详细也没有理由链，追问下反而更快露馅。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: tracing to constraints is exploration mode; 'common pattern' is solution mode.
The substance differs: one is constraint-backed and one isn't — that's the crux.
Correct — pulling 'two stages' back to 200ms+100M is what shows real formulation skill.
'Common pattern' has no reasoning chain no matter how detailed, and collapses faster under follow-up.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 你想要一份可复用的探索清单，保证开局 5–8 分钟不漏掉决定性维度。
scenario_en: You want a reusable exploration checklist so the opening 5-8 minutes never misses a decisive dimension.
q: 结构化探索清单包含哪些维度？(多选)
q_en: Which dimensions belong to the structured exploration checklist? (multiple)
why: 五维清单：业务目标、ML 任务定义、数据全景、系统约束、范围决策。每一维都会改写下游设计——漏掉任一维，就留下一个日后要付昂贵中途返工代价的盲点。「选哪家云厂商」不是形式化维度。
why_en: The five dimensions are business objective, ML task definition, data landscape, system constraints, and scope decision; each reshapes the downstream design.
options: 业务目标：主 KPI、次级指标、干系人优先级
ML 任务定义：分类/排序/生成，单任务还是多目标，在线还是离线推理
系统约束：延迟 SLA、吞吐 QPS、成本预算、容错
选哪家云厂商：AWS 还是 GCP 更便宜
options_en: Business objective: primary KPI, secondary metrics, stakeholder priorities.
ML task definition: classification/ranking/generation, single-task vs multi-objective, online vs offline inference.
System constraints: latency SLA, throughput QPS, cost budget, fault tolerance.
Which cloud vendor: whether AWS or GCP is cheaper.
optionExplanations: 对；业务目标塑造损失函数和评估框架，是清单第一维，必须最先探。
对；任务类型决定损失、指标和 serving 架构，是形式化的核心一维。
对；延迟/吞吐/成本/容错这些系统约束能直接砍掉整类模型。
错；选云厂商是实现层采购决策，不改变问题形式化，不属于探索维度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the business objective shapes the loss and eval framework; it's the first dimension and must be explored first.
Correct — the task type sets loss, metric, and serving architecture, a core formulation dimension.
Correct — latency/throughput/cost/fault-tolerance constraints can cut whole model classes.
Incorrect — picking a cloud vendor is an implementation-layer procurement choice that doesn't change the formulation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 明确哪些功能纳入、哪些显式排除，以及先做 MVP 还是完整系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A scope decision fixes what's in, what's explicitly excluded, and whether to build an MVP or the full system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签可得性、特征来源、数据新鲜度与体量的整体盘点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The data landscape is the overall picture of label availability, feature sources, data freshness, and volume.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 你在某处选了最终一致性而非强一致性，面试官问「凭什么？」，系统需要 50K TPS 且亚 100ms 延迟。
scenario_en: You chose eventual over strong consistency somewhere, and the interviewer asks 'on what basis?' — the system needs 50K TPS at sub-100ms.
q: 为什么「50K TPS @ 亚 100ms」这条约束能让「选最终一致性」变得可辩护？
q_en: Why does '50K TPS at sub-100ms' make choosing eventual consistency defensible?
why: 强一致性要跨节点协调（CAP 里的一致性），协调开销会顶破亚 100ms 的延迟 SLA。把「选最终一致性」追溯到 50K TPS + 亚 100ms 这条已定约束，它就从「拍脑袋」变成「被约束逼出来的必然」，可自证。
why_en: Strong consistency needs cross-node coordination whose overhead (CAP) breaks the sub-100ms SLA, so tracing 'eventual consistency' back to the 50K TPS at sub-100ms constraint makes it a forced, defensible choice.
options: 因为最终一致性永远比强一致性好，和约束无关
因为强一致性的跨节点协调开销(CAP)会顶破亚 100ms SLA，追溯到 50K TPS+亚100ms 就自证成立
因为 TPS 越高就必须用强一致性，这里数字不够所以退而求其次
因为一致性只影响存储成本，不影响延迟
options_en: Because eventual consistency is always better than strong, independent of constraints.
Because strong consistency's cross-node coordination overhead (CAP) breaks the sub-100ms SLA, so tracing to 50K TPS + sub-100ms makes it self-justifying.
Because higher TPS forces strong consistency, and here the numbers are too low so you settle for less.
Because consistency only affects storage cost, not latency.
optionExplanations: 没有「永远更好」：最终一致性是被延迟约束逼出来的，脱离约束就不成立。
对；把决策接回具体约束，理由从「个人偏好」升级为「约束下的必然」，这就是可辩护。
说反了：高吞吐+低延迟恰恰逼你放弃强一致性的协调开销。
一致性直接影响延迟：强一致要等跨节点确认，正是它顶破 SLA 的原因。
optionExplanations_en: There's no 'always better': eventual consistency is forced by the latency constraint and doesn't hold without it.
Correct — tracing the decision to a concrete constraint upgrades the reason from preference to a constraint-forced necessity, which is defensibility.
Backwards: high throughput plus low latency is exactly what forces you to drop strong consistency's coordination overhead.
Consistency directly affects latency: strong consistency waits for cross-node acknowledgment, which is what breaks the SLA.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分区发生时，一致性与可用性不可兼得；追求强一致要付跨节点协调延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CAP theorem says under a network partition you can't have both consistency and availability; strong consistency costs cross-node coordination latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒事务数，衡量系统吞吐；这里 50K TPS 是给定的规模约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TPS (Transactions Per Second) measures throughput; here 50K TPS is a given scale constraint.

category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 探索时你确认了一堆需求，但担心讲到后面会忘、或面试官看不出你在用它们。
scenario_en: You've confirmed a pile of requirements during exploration but worry you'll forget them or the interviewer won't see you using them.
q: 探索阶段确认的需求，最该怎么处理？
q_en: What's the best thing to do with requirements confirmed during exploration?
why: 把需求当场写下来（编号需求清单/共享文档），后面显式回指它们。这条可见的「决策审计轨迹」既帮你自己不跑偏，也让面试官看到你每个决策都挂在需求上——是面试官会主动奖励的行为。
why_en: Write requirements down as you confirm them and refer back to them explicitly; that visible decision audit trail is a behavior interviewers reward.
options: 记在脑子里就好，写下来会浪费宝贵的白板空间
当场写成编号需求清单，后面显式回指——形成面试官奖励的可见审计轨迹
只在最后总结时一次性列出来，中途不用提
全部交给面试官记录，自己专注讲方案
options_en: Just keep them in your head; writing wastes precious whiteboard space.
Write them as a numbered requirements list and refer back explicitly — forming the visible audit trail interviewers reward.
List them only in the final summary and don't mention them mid-way.
Let the interviewer record everything while you focus on the solution.
optionExplanations: 只记脑子里，讲到后面容易漏、也让面试官看不见你在用需求。
对；写下来+回指，把「我在按需求做决策」变成可见证据，这正是被奖励的审计轨迹。
只在结尾列不产生中途的追溯效果，决策与需求的挂钩看不见。
让面试官记录等于放弃主导权，你应自己维护这条轨迹。
optionExplanations_en: Head-only means you'll drop some later and the interviewer won't see you using them.
Correct — writing plus referring back turns 'I'm deciding by requirements' into visible evidence, the rewarded audit trail.
Listing only at the end gives no mid-session traceability; the decision-to-requirement link stays invisible.
Letting the interviewer record cedes leadership; you should maintain the trail yourself.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 你在犹豫要不要花时间探索——毕竟直接进方案感觉更快、更能展示技术。
scenario_en: You hesitate to spend time exploring — jumping to the solution feels faster and more technical.
q: 结构化探索为什么能实打实降低「设计风险」？
q_en: Why does structured exploration actually reduce 'design risk'?
why: 探索先把关键约束确认清楚，就避免了那种最贵的中途返工：设计到一半发现某个假设的约束是错的，被迫推倒重来。前期多花 5–8 分钟，省掉的是中段大改的时间和信任崩塌。
why_en: Exploration confirms key constraints up front, avoiding the expensive mid-interview pivot where an assumed constraint turns out wrong and forces a rebuild.
options: 因为探索能让你显得更资深，和设计风险无关
因为它先确认关键约束，避免设计到一半发现假设错误、被迫推倒重来的昂贵中途返工
因为探索时间越长，最终模型精度越高
因为探索能替代后面的评估阶段，省掉一步
options_en: Because exploration makes you look more senior, unrelated to design risk.
Because it confirms key constraints first, avoiding the expensive mid-interview pivot when an assumed constraint turns out wrong.
Because the longer you explore, the higher the final model accuracy.
Because exploration replaces the later evaluation phase, saving a step.
optionExplanations: 显得资深是副产品；降低设计风险的实质是提前排掉错误假设。
对；把约束验在前面，就不会在中段因假设崩塌被迫大改，这才是省风险的机制。
探索不直接提精度，它降低的是「解错问题/中途返工」的风险。
探索和评估是不同阶段，前者不替代后者。
optionExplanations_en: Looking senior is a byproduct; the real risk reduction is ruling out wrong assumptions early.
Correct — validating constraints up front prevents a mid-session rebuild when assumptions collapse, which is the risk-saving mechanism.
Exploration doesn't directly raise accuracy; it lowers the risk of solving the wrong problem or a mid-course pivot.
Exploration and evaluation are different phases; the former doesn't replace the latter.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 你把开局的形式化做得很扎实，后面偶尔出了个小口误或小疏漏。
scenario_en: You nailed the opening formulation, then later made a small slip or minor omission.
q: 扎实的开局探索，对面试官的「信任」有什么复利效应？
q_en: What compounding effect does a solid opening have on interviewer trust?
why: 扎实的形式化会建立信任，而信任会复利：一旦面试官相信你有判断力，后面偶尔的小失误他更愿意放过、当作口误而非能力问题。开局赢下信任，等于给后半场买了容错额度。
why_en: A solid formulation builds trust that compounds — once the interviewer trusts your judgment, they forgive later minor missteps as slips rather than gaps.
options: 没有影响，面试官对每个失误都同等扣分
信任会复利：开局建立信任后，面试官更愿把后面的小失误当口误而非能力问题
开局越强，面试官后面越会故意刁难来找平衡
信任只在行为面有用，技术面不看这个
options_en: No effect — the interviewer deducts equally for every mistake.
Trust compounds: after a strong opening builds trust, the interviewer forgives later minor slips as misstatements rather than gaps.
The stronger the opening, the more the interviewer nitpicks later to rebalance.
Trust only helps in behavioral rounds, not technical ones.
optionExplanations: 并非同等扣分：面试官对已建立信任的候选人更宽容，这是人评的现实。
对；信任是复利资产，开局赢下它，后半场的小失误更容易被放过。
强开局不会招来刁难，反而降低后面被抓小辫子的概率。
技术面同样是人在评：信任照样影响他如何解读你的失误。
optionExplanations_en: Not equal deductions: interviewers are more lenient toward candidates who've earned trust — a reality of human evaluation.
Correct — trust is a compounding asset; winning it early makes later small slips easier to forgive.
A strong opening doesn't invite nitpicking; it lowers the chance of being caught out later.
Technical rounds are still judged by humans: trust still shapes how they read your mistakes.
category: Why Problem Formulation Is Where Interviews Are Won

scenario: 澄清约束时得知系统要在 50ms 内、以 100K QPS 服务在线请求（对比另一条路是可离线批处理）。
scenario_en: You learn the system must serve online at 50ms within 100K QPS (versus an alternative batch path).
q: 「50ms @ 100K QPS」这组数字对形式化的直接作用是什么？
q_en: What does '50ms at 100K QPS' directly do to the formulation?
why: 50ms @ 100K QPS 是给定的服务约束（SLO/规模），不是公式推出的。它直接砍掉整类模型：大 transformer 逐条推理既进不了 50ms、也扛不住 10 万 QPS，于是形式化被逼向轻量模型+预计算+水平扩展；若允许离线批处理，这些约束大部分消失。
why_en: 50ms at 100K QPS is a given serving constraint that eliminates whole model classes — a big transformer can't meet 50ms at that volume — pushing you toward lightweight models with precompute and horizontal scaling.
options: 它只影响服务器数量，不改变模型选型
它是给定服务约束，直接砍掉整类模型（大 transformer 逐条推理进不了 50ms/扛不住 100K QPS），逼向轻量+预计算+水平扩展
它意味着必须用最大的模型才能扛住 100K QPS
它只在离线训练时相关，在线服务不受它约束
options_en: It only affects server count, not model choice.
It's a given serving constraint that eliminates whole model classes (a big transformer can't hit 50ms at 100K QPS), forcing lightweight models plus precompute and horizontal scaling.
It means you must use the largest model to withstand 100K QPS.
It only matters for offline training; online serving is unconstrained by it.
