q_en: With a 100M+ parameter model and constrained devices, edge or cloud?
why: 选云:100M+ 参数需要云端 GPU/TPU 的内存和算力,受限的手机 NPU/边缘 TPU 装不下、跑不动。边缘只适合小模型(移动 NPU 在小模型上正逐步逼近云)。模型大小因素主导时优先云。
why_en: Pick cloud: 100M+ parameters need cloud GPU/TPU memory and compute that constrained mobile NPUs can't fit or run, while edge suits small models.
tradeoff: 云(能跑大模型,加网络延迟) vs 边缘(省往返,装不下大模型)
whenOtherWins: 如果模型能被量化/蒸馏/剪枝压到小模型规模,且延迟或隐私要求强,边缘就重新可行——先压小再上端。
options: 选边缘:手机 NPU 也能硬跑 100M+ 大模型,省网络最重要
选云:100M+ 参数需要云 GPU/TPU 的内存与算力,受限设备装不下跑不动;边缘只适合小模型
两者都行:模型大小不影响边缘/云选择
选边缘并加大手机内存:堆内存就能在端上跑任意大模型
options_en: Pick edge: a mobile NPU can brute-force a 100M+ model, and saving the network matters most.
Pick cloud: 100M+ parameters need cloud GPU/TPU memory and compute that constrained devices can't fit or run; edge suits only small models.
Either works: model size doesn't affect edge/cloud choice.
Pick edge with more phone RAM: piling on memory runs any large model on-device.
optionExplanations: 受限手机 NPU 装不下也跑不动 100M+ 大模型,省网络也无从谈起。
对;大模型需要云端算力/内存,模型大小主导时选云。
模型大小恰是五因素之一,大模型直接排除受限边缘设备。
手机内存有物理与功耗上限,堆内存无法承载任意大模型。
optionExplanations_en: A constrained mobile NPU can neither fit nor run a 100M+ model, so saving the network is moot.
Correct — big models need cloud compute/memory; when model size dominates, choose cloud.
Model size is exactly one of the five factors; a big model rules out constrained edge devices.
Phone RAM has physical/power limits; piling memory can't carry any large model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 移动/边缘设备上的神经网络加速芯片,算力/内存受限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NPU (Neural Processing Unit) is a neural accelerator on mobile/edge devices with limited compute/memory.

scenario: 机器人/野外设备经常没有稳定网络,但仍必须持续做推理决策。
scenario_en: Robots/field devices often lack stable connectivity yet must keep making inference decisions.
q: 设备需要在无网络时仍能推理,边缘还是云?
q_en: When devices must infer offline without connectivity, edge or cloud?
why: 选边缘:本地模型让设备在离线/弱网时仍能持续推理(机器人、野外设备);云则每次请求都依赖可靠网络,断网即停摆。连接性因素主导时必须边缘。
why_en: Pick edge: a local model keeps a device inferring offline (robots, field devices), while cloud needs reliable connectivity per request and stalls when offline.
tradeoff: 边缘(离线可用、自治,更新难) vs 云(需稳定网络,断网即停)
whenOtherWins: 如果设备始终在稳定网络下(如数据中心内服务),云的集中更新与强算力更省事,离线能力用不上。
options: 选云:断网时云会自动缓存请求,恢复后补算,等价于离线可用
选边缘:本地模型让设备离线/弱网也能持续推理;云每请求依赖网络,断网即停摆
两者都行:现代设备网络都很稳,不用考虑离线
选云并加重试:断网时不停重试直到联网即可
options_en: Pick cloud: it auto-caches requests during outages and computes on reconnect, equivalent to offline.
Pick edge: a local model keeps the device inferring offline/weak-network; cloud needs connectivity per request and stalls offline.
Either works: modern devices always have stable networks, so ignore offline.
Pick cloud with retries: keep retrying during outages until connectivity returns.
optionExplanations: 缓存请求不是实时推理;断网时需要当场决策,缓存补算救不了。
对;边缘本地模型是离线/弱网持续推理的唯一解,连接性主导。
机器人/野外设备恰恰常断网,离线能力是硬需求。
重试期间设备无决策可用,断网场景下重试等于停摆。
optionExplanations_en: Caching requests isn't real-time inference; offline you need an on-the-spot decision that deferred compute can't provide.
Correct — a local edge model is the only way to keep inferring offline/weak-network, with connectivity dominating.
Robots/field devices frequently lose connectivity, so offline capability is a hard requirement.
During retries the device has no decision available; offline, retrying equals stalling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 设备是否有稳定网络;边缘部署可在离线/弱网下自治推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Connectivity is whether a device has a stable network; edge deployment allows autonomous inference offline/weak-network.

scenario: 评估规模成本:边缘部署到百万设备 vs 云端集中服务,成本结构不同。
scenario_en: Assessing cost at scale: deploying to millions of edge devices vs centralized cloud serving, with different cost structures.
q: 边缘和云在「规模成本」上结构有何不同?
q_en: How do edge and cloud differ structurally on cost at scale?
why: 边缘=固定的单设备成本、无需服务基础设施,但更新要推权重到每台设备。云=成本随 QPS 变动,但基础设施共享、更新集中、监控统一。规模成本是取舍:设备极多时边缘边际成本低,但更新/监控是负担。
why_en: Edge is a fixed per-device cost with no serving infra but costly weight pushes to every device, while cloud cost varies with QPS but shares infra with centralized updates and monitoring.
tradeoff: 边缘(固定单机成本、无服务基建,更新难) vs 云(随 QPS 变动,基建共享+集中更新监控)
options: 边缘和云成本结构完全一样,都是随 QPS 线性变动
边缘=固定单设备成本、无服务基建(但更新要推权重到每台);云=随 QPS 变动、基建共享+集中更新监控
边缘一定更便宜、云一定更贵,与规模无关
云=固定成本、边缘=随 QPS 变动,和实际相反
options_en: Edge and cloud have identical cost structures, both varying linearly with QPS.
Edge = fixed per-device cost, no serving infra (but weight pushes to every device); cloud = varies with QPS, shared infra plus centralized updates/monitoring.
Edge is always cheaper and cloud always pricier, regardless of scale.
Cloud = fixed cost and edge = varies with QPS — the reverse of reality.
optionExplanations: 两者成本结构本质不同:边缘固定单机、云随 QPS,不是都随 QPS。
对;边缘固定单机成本但更新难,云随 QPS 但基建共享集中更新,是结构性取舍。
谁更便宜取决于规模与更新频率,不是绝对的。
说反了:边缘才是固定单机成本,云随 QPS 变动。
optionExplanations_en: Their structures fundamentally differ: edge fixed per-device, cloud varies with QPS — not both QPS-varying.
Correct — edge is fixed per-device but hard to update, cloud varies with QPS but shares infra with central updates, a structural tradeoff.
Which is cheaper depends on scale and update frequency, not absolute.
Reversed: edge is the fixed per-device cost, cloud varies with QPS.

termDefinitions.term: cost at scale / 规模成本
termDefinitions.meaning: 大规模下的总拥有成本结构:边缘按设备固定,云随流量变动。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cost at scale is the total cost structure at large volume: edge fixed per device, cloud varying with traffic.

scenario: 手机银行反欺诈:多数交易要实时评分且注重隐私,但少数可疑交易需要更深的分析。
scenario_en: Mobile banking fraud: most transactions need real-time private scoring, but a few suspicious ones need deeper analysis.
q: 手机银行反欺诈,边缘/云怎么混合才合理?代价是什么?
q_en: For mobile banking fraud, how do you sensibly mix edge and cloud, and at what cost?
why: 混合:设备上跑轻量模型做实时评分(低延迟+隐私),定期推权重更新;把少数可疑/模糊交易路由到云端大模型做深度分析。既得端上隐私实时,又保住难例的深度。代价:向数百万设备每周推权重很贵。
why_en: Hybrid: a lightweight on-device model scores in real time (low latency + privacy) with periodic weight pushes, routing ambiguous cases to a cloud model for deeper analysis, at the cost of expensive weekly weight pushes to millions of devices.
tradeoff: 混合(端上实时隐私+云端深度,推权重贵) vs 纯云(易更新,牺牲隐私/延迟)
whenOtherWins: 如果所有交易都需要同等深度分析、或设备无法承载任何本地模型,纯云更简单;若完全无需深度分析,纯边缘即可。
options: 全部交易都传云端大模型评分,简单统一,不在设备上跑任何模型
设备跑轻量模型实时评分(低延迟+隐私)+定期推权重,可疑交易路由到云端大模型深度分析;代价是向百万设备推权重贵
全部在设备上跑,连可疑交易也不上云,彻底不联网最省事
边缘和云各跑一份完全相同的大模型,互为备份
options_en: Send every transaction to a cloud model, uniform and simple, running no model on-device.

Run a lightweight on-device model for real-time scoring (low latency + privacy) with periodic weight pushes, routing suspicious cases to a cloud model for deeper analysis; the cost is expensive weight pushes to millions of devices.
Run everything on-device, keeping even suspicious cases off the cloud — fully offline is simplest.
Run identical large models on both edge and cloud as mutual backups.
optionExplanations: 全传云牺牲了端上的实时性和隐私,与反欺诈的低延迟/隐私诉求冲突。
对;端上轻模型保实时隐私、云端大模型啃难例,是经典混合,代价是推权重贵。
全在端上跑不动深度分析,难例得不到云端更强算力。
两端跑相同大模型不现实(设备装不下),也没发挥混合分工的意义。
optionExplanations_en: All-cloud sacrifices on-device real-time and privacy, conflicting with fraud's low-latency/privacy needs.
Correct — a light on-device model keeps real-time privacy while the cloud model handles hard cases, the classic hybrid, costing weight pushes.
All-on-device can't run deep analysis, so hard cases miss the cloud's stronger compute.
Identical big models on both ends is impractical (devices can't fit it) and wastes the hybrid division of labor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把更新后的模型权重推送到每台边缘设备;设备极多时成本高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A weight push sends updated model weights to every edge device, costly when devices number in the millions.

q: 把 INT8 PTQ 量化的正确流程排好序:
q_en: Order the correct workflow for INT8 PTQ quantization:
steps: 在留出的生产样本上核对 Top-1 准确率是否可接受
准备一份覆盖真实分布(含离群激活)的代表性校准集
拿训练好的 FP32 模型作为量化输入
跑校准集观察各层激活范围、设每层缩放因子转成 INT8
why: 流程:FP32 成品→备好有代表性的校准集→跑校准定每层缩放并转 INT8→在生产样本上验 Top-1。校准集不具代表性会在最后一步暴露掉点,所以验证不可省。
why_en: Take the trained FP32 model, prepare a representative calibration set, run calibration to set per-layer scaling into INT8, then validate Top-1 on production samples.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不参与校准的独立生产样本,用来客观验证量化后精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A held-out sample is independent production data not used in calibration, for objectively validating post-quantization accuracy.

q: 填空:量化各精度的加速与精度损失锚点。
q_en: Fill in the speedup and accuracy anchors for quantization precisions.
text: FP16 相对 FP32 约 {{2}}× 吞吐(Tensor Cores),精度损失 <{{0.1}}%;INT8 约 {{2-4}}× 提速,精度损失依校准而定(PTQ 约 0.5-2%,QAT <0.3%);四轴总体可降本降延迟 {{2-4}}× 且多数免重训。
text_en: FP16 gives about {{2}}x throughput (Tensor Cores) with <{{0.1}}% accuracy loss; INT8 gives about {{2-4}}x speedup with calibration-dependent loss (PTQ ~0.5-2%, QAT <0.3%); the four axes cut cost/latency {{2-4}}x, mostly without retraining.
why: 记住量化阶梯:FP16 稳赚 2× 几乎无损,INT8 更省 2-4× 但看校准,QAT 把 INT8 掉点压到 <0.3%。这些数决定默认先上 FP16、成本更紧再上 INT8。
why_en: Anchor the quantization ladder: FP16 a safe near-lossless 2x, INT8 a bigger 2-4x depending on calibration, QAT pushing INT8 loss under 0.3%.

termDefinitions.meaning: 32 位浮点,训练与调试的基线精度,推理时可量化到 FP16/INT8。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FP32 is 32-bit floating point, the training/debugging baseline, quantizable to FP16/INT8 for inference.

scenario: 通用的量化/剪枝/编译能加速单次前向,但把 LLM 服务到生产会撞上一个根本不同的瓶颈。
scenario_en: Generic quantization/pruning/compilation speed up a single forward pass, but serving an LLM in production hits a fundamentally different bottleneck.
q: 让 LLM 生产服务可行的四项关键创新是哪些?
q_en: What four innovations make production LLM serving viable?
why: 四项:KV 缓存、PagedAttention、投机解码、连续批处理。它们都针对 LLM 特有的「自回归解码 + 内存带宽受限」瓶颈,分别优化显存效率或摊薄逐 token 顺序解码的成本。
why_en: The four are KV caching, PagedAttention, speculative decoding, and continuous batching, all targeting the LLM-specific autoregressive, memory-bandwidth-bound bottleneck.
diagram:
flowchart TB L["LLM 生产服务"] --> K["KV 缓存
免重算历史K/V"] L --> P["PagedAttention
分页省显存"] L --> S["投机解码
草稿+并行验证"] L --> C["连续批处理
逐步调度"]
options: 数据增强、超参搜索、模型集成、知识蒸馏——都是训练调参手段
KV 缓存、PagedAttention、投机解码、连续批处理
分库分表、读写分离、主从复制、消息队列——经典数据库水平扩展组合
量化、剪枝、编译、边缘部署——上一课讲的通用推理加速手段
options_en: Data augmentation, hyperparameter search, model ensembling, and knowledge distillation — all training-time tuning tricks.
KV caching, PagedAttention, speculative decoding, and continuous batching.
Database sharding, read-write splitting, primary-replica replication, and message queues — classic DB horizontal-scaling combo.
Quantization, pruning, compilation, and edge deployment — last lesson's generic inference-acceleration levers.
optionExplanations: 这些是训练/调参手段,不解决 LLM 自回归服务的显存瓶颈。
对;这四项专门对付 LLM 的自回归+内存带宽受限瓶颈。
传统数据层扩展手段,和 LLM 逐 token 解码无关。
量化/剪枝/编译是上一课的通用手段,不是 LLM 服务的四项专属创新。
optionExplanations_en: These are training/tuning methods, not fixes for the LLM autoregressive serving bottleneck.
Correct — these four specifically address the LLM autoregressive, memory-bandwidth-bound bottleneck.
Classic data-tier scaling, unrelated to LLM token-by-token decoding.
Quantization/pruning/compilation are last lesson's generic levers, not the four LLM-specific innovations.

termDefinitions.meaning: LLM 一次生成一个 token,每步都把已生成序列喂回去预测下一个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Autoregressive decoding generates one token at a time, feeding the sequence so far back in to predict the next.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存各层注意力的 key/value 张量,避免每步重算历史 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The KV (Key-Value) cache stores per-layer attention key/value tensors to avoid recomputing prior tokens each step.

scenario: ResNet 推理是固定输入、单次前向、算力密集;GPT 式模型每步只产一个 token 却要重载全部注意力参数。
scenario_en: ResNet inference is fixed-input, single-pass, compute-heavy; a GPT-style model reloads all attention params each step to produce just one token.
q: 为什么说 LLM 推理是「内存带宽受限」而非「算力受限」?
q_en: Why is LLM inference memory-bandwidth-bound rather than compute-bound?
why: 解码每步要从显存重载全部注意力参数,却只产出一个 token→算术运算相对搬运的字节数很少(arithmetic-to-bytes 比值低),浮点单元闲着、内存总线吃紧。所以瓶颈是显存带宽而非算力,GPU-hours 主要花在等数据搬运。
why_en: Each decode step reloads all attention params from GPU memory but produces only one token, so the arithmetic-to-bytes ratio is low — FP units idle while the memory bus is the bottleneck.
tradeoff: 算力受限(ResNet:一次前向密集算) vs 内存带宽受限(LLM 解码:重载参数产一 token)
options: 因为 LLM 参数太多,FP 单元算力不够用,是纯算力瓶颈,和内存搬运无关
解码每步重载全部参数只产一 token,算术/字节比低,FP 单元闲、显存带宽吃紧
因为 LLM 只在 CPU 上跑,GPU 完全用不上,瓶颈在 CPU 主频
因为 LLM 推理受磁盘 IO 限制,把权重放在 SSD 上导致频繁换入换出
options_en: Because LLMs have too many parameters and FP units run out — a pure compute bottleneck unrelated to data movement.
Each decode step reloads all params to produce one token, so the arithmetic-to-bytes ratio is low — FP units idle, memory bus strained.
Because LLMs run only on CPU, GPUs go entirely unused, and the bottleneck is CPU clock speed.
Because LLM inference is disk-IO-bound, caused by keeping weights on SSD and swapping them in and out.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反:FP 单元是闲着的,瓶颈不是算力不够而是数据搬不动。
对;重载参数只产一 token 让算术/字节比很低,显存带宽成为瓶颈。
LLM 主要在 GPU 上服务,不是 CPU-only。
权重驻显存不在磁盘;瓶颈是显存带宽不是磁盘 IO。
optionExplanations_en: Opposite: FP units are idle; the bottleneck is not compute but moving data.
Correct — reloading params for one token gives a low arithmetic-to-bytes ratio, making memory bandwidth the bottleneck.
LLMs are served mainly on GPUs, not CPU-only.
Weights live in VRAM not disk; the bottleneck is memory bandwidth, not disk IO.

termDefinitions.meaning: 瓶颈在从显存搬数据的速度,而非计算单元的算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memory-bandwidth-bound means the bottleneck is data movement from memory, not compute capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每搬运一字节数据做多少次运算;比值低说明大量时间在等数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The arithmetic-to-bytes ratio is how many ops run per byte moved; a low ratio means most time is spent waiting on data.

scenario: ResNet 的计算量固定可预测;而一个 GPT 回复可能只要 10 步、也可能要 500 步前向,事先不知道。
scenario_en: A ResNet's compute is fixed and predictable, while a GPT reply may need 10 or 500 forward passes, unknown in advance.
q: 自回归解码给 LLM 服务带来什么根本困难?
q_en: What fundamental difficulty does autoregressive decoding pose for LLM serving?
why: 输出长度不可预知:一条回复可能 10 步也可能 500 步前向,事先不知道。这让显存占用、批处理调度、延迟都变得不确定——不能像 ResNet 那样按固定计算量静态规划,是连续批处理与 PagedAttention 要解决的根源。
why_en: Output length is unknown in advance (10 or 500 forward passes), making memory, batch scheduling, and latency all variable, unlike a ResNet's fixed compute.
options: 输出长度固定可预知,所以调度很简单,和 ResNet 没本质区别,不需要额外设计
输出长度不可预知(10 步或 500 步),使显存/批调度/延迟都不确定,不能静态规划
每步必须重新加载训练数据到显存里,导致解码逐步变慢
每个 token 生成都要访问外部数据库做查询,受网络往返限制
options_en: Output length is fixed and predictable, so scheduling is trivial — no different from a ResNet, no extra design needed.
Output length is unknown in advance (10 vs 500 passes), making memory/batch-scheduling/latency variable — can't plan statically.
Each step must reload the training data into VRAM, causing decoding to slow down over time.
Each token generation queries an external database, limited by network round-trip time.
optionExplanations: 输出长度恰恰不可预知,这正是难点所在。
对;长度不定让显存和调度无法静态规划,是 LLM 服务的核心难题。
解码不重载训练数据,重载的是注意力参数与 KV 缓存。
解码是本地显存计算,不必每 token 查外部数据库。
optionExplanations_en: Output length is precisely unknown, which is the difficulty.
Correct — variable length prevents static memory/scheduling planning, the core LLM-serving challenge.
Decoding doesn't reload training data; it reloads attention params and the KV cache.
Decoding is local VRAM compute, not an external DB query per token.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型对当前输入算一次输出;LLM 解码要跑多次,次数随回复长度变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A forward pass computes one output from the current input; LLM decoding runs many, varying with reply length.

scenario: 生成第 200 个 token 时,注意力需要用到前 199 个 token 的 key/value。
scenario_en: Generating token 200, attention needs the key/value tensors of all 199 prior tokens.
q: 没有 KV 缓存会怎样?KV 缓存把复杂度从多少降到多少?
q_en: What happens without a KV cache, and from what to what does it cut complexity?
why: 没有缓存,生成第 200 token 要为前 199 个重算 K/V,整段生成累计是 O(n²)。KV 缓存把每层每 token 的 K/V 存下来跨步复用,只需为新 token 算 K/V,总量降到 O(n)。代价是缓存本身吃显存。
why_en: Without caching, token 200 recomputes K/V for all 199 prior tokens, giving O(n²) total; the KV cache retains them for reuse so only new tokens are computed, dropping to O(n) at the cost of memory.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["生成第n个token"] --> B{有KV缓存?} B -->|否| C["重算前n-1个K/V
累计O(n²)"] B -->|是| D["复用历史K/V
只算新token → O(n)"]
options: 没缓存也一样快,重算历史 K/V 完全不花时间,KV 缓存只省内存不省任何计算量
没缓存要为历史 token 重算 K/V,累计 O(n²);缓存复用历史、只算新 token,降到 O(n),代价是吃显存
KV 缓存把复杂度从 O(n) 升到 O(n²),是为了换取更高准确率
KV 缓存实际缓存的其实是模型最终生成出来的每一个 token 的文本本身,和内部的 K/V 张量完全没有关系
options_en: It's equally fast without caching — recomputing prior K/V costs no time at all; the KV cache only saves memory, not compute.
Without caching you recompute K/V for prior tokens, O(n²) total; the cache reuses history, computing only new tokens, dropping to O(n), at the cost of memory.
The KV cache raises complexity from O(n) to O(n²) in exchange for higher accuracy.
The KV cache actually stores each of the model's own final generated token texts as-is, with nothing to do with the internal K/V tensors.
optionExplanations: 没缓存要反复重算历史 K/V,计算量是 O(n²),明显更慢。
对;缓存历史 K/V 把总量从 O(n²) 降到 O(n),代价是缓存占显存。
方向反了:缓存是把 O(n²) 降到 O(n),不是升,也不为了准。
KV 缓存存的是 key/value 张量,不是 token 文本。
optionExplanations_en: Without caching you repeatedly recompute prior K/V — O(n²) and clearly slower.
Correct — caching prior K/V drops the total from O(n²) to O(n), at the cost of cache memory.
Reversed: the cache cuts O(n²) to O(n), not up, and not for accuracy.
The KV cache stores key/value tensors, not token text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 注意力机制里代表每个 token 的两组向量,后续 token 需读取它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Key/value tensors are the two vectors representing each token in attention, read by later tokens.

scenario: LLM 推理分两阶段:先处理整个 prompt,再一个一个吐 token。
scenario_en: LLM inference has two phases: first process the whole prompt, then emit tokens one by one.
q: prefill 和 decode 两阶段各是什么瓶颈?
q_en: What is the bottleneck of each of the prefill and decode phases?
why: prefill 并行处理整段 prompt、一次填满 KV,像普通前向一样算力密集;decode 每步只产一 token 却要加载整份缓存,是内存带宽受限。
why_en: Prefill processes the whole prompt in parallel and fills the KV cache at once, compute-bound like a normal forward pass; decode emits one token per step loading the full cache with little new math, memory-bandwidth-bound.
tradeoff: prefill(并行、compute-bound) vs decode(逐 token、memory-bandwidth-bound)
options: 两阶段都是算力受限,prefill 和 decode 的处理方式完全没有区别
prefill 并行填满 KV,算力密集;decode 逐 token 加载缓存,新算很少,带宽受限
prefill 是逐 token 处理、decode 才是并行处理整段 prompt,和实际情况正好相反
两阶段都只受磁盘 IO 限制,和算力、显存带宽这些指标都完全无关
options_en: Both phases are compute-bound, and prefill and decode are handled in exactly the same way.
Prefill fills the KV cache in parallel, compute-heavy; decode loads the cache per token with little new math, bandwidth-bound.
Prefill processes token by token and decode processes the whole prompt in parallel — the reverse of reality.
Both phases are limited only by disk IO, entirely unrelated to compute or memory-bandwidth metrics.
optionExplanations: 两阶段瓶颈不同:prefill 算力密集,decode 带宽受限。
对;prefill 像普通前向密集算,decode 是带宽受限的逐 token 生成。
说反了:prefill 才是并行,decode 才是逐 token。
两阶段都在显存内计算,瓶颈是算力/带宽而非磁盘。
optionExplanations_en: Their bottlenecks differ: prefill compute-heavy, decode bandwidth-bound.
Correct — prefill is compute-heavy like a normal pass, decode is bandwidth-bound token-by-token generation.
Reversed: prefill is the parallel one, decode is token-by-token.
Both compute in VRAM; the bottleneck is compute/bandwidth, not disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并行处理整个 prompt,一次性填满所有 prompt token 的 KV 缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Prefill processes the whole prompt in parallel, filling the KV cache for all prompt tokens at once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐个生成 token,每步把新 K/V 追加进缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Decode generates tokens one by one, appending each new K/V to the cache.

scenario: 要估算一个 7B 模型、2048 token 上下文、FP16 下,单个请求的 KV 缓存占多少显存。
scenario_en: Estimate the KV-cache VRAM for one request on a 7B model, 2048-token context, in FP16.
q: 7B/2048 token/FP16 下,单请求 KV 缓存有多大?这个数字决定了什么?
q_en: How big is the KV cache for one 7B/2048-token/FP16 request, and what does that number decide?
why: 约 1GB。它是显存(而非 FLOPs)成为绑定约束的直接证据:一张 80GB A100 装完权重后剩下的显存,除以每请求 1GB 就是最大并发数。所以 KV 缓存大小直接决定最大并发。
why_en: About 1GB, and it's why VRAM (not FLOPs) is the binding constraint: an 80GB A100's leftover memory divided by ~1GB per request gives max concurrency, so KV-cache size directly sets max concurrency.
options: 1KB 左右,这点显存占用完全可以忽略不计,显存从来都不是服务的瓶颈所在
1GB 左右,让显存(非 FLOPs)成为绑定约束,剩余显存÷每请求 KV≈最大并发
1TB 左右,单个请求就装不下 80GB 显存,必须上分布式
大小固定不变,和上下文 token 数、模型精度这些因素都完全无关
options_en: About 1KB, an amount small enough to ignore entirely — VRAM is never the serving bottleneck.
About 1GB, making VRAM (not FLOPs) the binding constraint: leftover VRAM ÷ per-request KV ≈ max concurrency.
About 1TB, so a single request alone won't fit in 80GB VRAM and you must go distributed.
Its size is fixed, entirely independent of context length or model precision.
optionExplanations: 1KB 严重低估;7B/2048/FP16 的 KV 约 1GB,显存正是瓶颈。
对;每请求约 1GB,剩余显存除以它就是最大并发,KV 大小=并发上限。
1TB 高估;单请求约 1GB,不至于单请求就要分布式。
KV 随上下文 token 数线性增长,不是固定的。
optionExplanations_en: 1KB grossly underestimates; 7B/2048/FP16 KV is ~1GB and VRAM is the bottleneck.
Correct — ~1GB per request, and leftover VRAM ÷ it is max concurrency, so KV size = concurrency ceiling.
1TB overstates; one request is ~1GB, not requiring distributed for a single request.
KV grows linearly with context tokens, not fixed.

termDefinitions.meaning: GPU 同时服务的请求数;受剩余显存÷每请求 KV 缓存限制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Concurrency is how many requests a GPU serves at once, limited by leftover VRAM ÷ per-request KV cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: NVIDIA 数据中心 GPU,常见 80GB 显存型号用于 LLM 服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The A100 is an NVIDIA data-center GPU, commonly the 80GB model used for LLM serving.

scenario: 一张 80GB A100 服务某模型,发现能同时处理的请求数远低于预期,怀疑是 KV 缓存吃满了显存。
scenario_en: An 80GB A100 serves a model but handles far fewer concurrent requests than expected, suspected to be KV cache filling VRAM.
q: 要提高单卡最大并发,最该动哪个变量?
q_en: To raise a single GPU's max concurrency, which variable should you target?
why: 最大并发≈(总显存−权重)÷每请求 KV 缓存,所以最该压 KV 缓存占用——降精度(FP16→更低)、缩上下文、或用 PagedAttention 消除碎片。堆更多 FLOPs 没用,因为约束是显存不是算力。
why_en: Max concurrency ≈ (total VRAM − weights) ÷ per-request KV cache, so shrink KV-cache footprint (lower precision, shorter context, or PagedAttention), because the constraint is memory, not FLOPs.
tradeoff: 压 KV 缓存(提并发,可能损上下文/精度) vs 加算力(对显存约束无效)
whenOtherWins: 如果瓶颈其实是 prefill 阶段的算力(超长 prompt、compute-bound),那才该优化算力/并行,而非只压 KV 缓存。
options: 加更多 GPU 算力(FLOPs),算力足了并发自然会升高
压 KV 缓存占用(降精度/缩上下文/PagedAttention),因为并发受显存约束
把 batch size 强行设成 1,让单个请求占用尽量最省的那份显存资源
换成参数更多的更大模型来服务,权重变多了并发反而会更高
options_en: Add more GPU compute (FLOPs); with enough compute concurrency naturally rises.
Shrink KV-cache footprint (lower precision / shorter context / PagedAttention), because concurrency is memory-bound.
Force batch size down to 1, so a single request uses the smallest possible slice of VRAM.
Switch to serving with a bigger model with more parameters — supposedly more weights raise concurrency.
optionExplanations: 并发受显存约束,堆 FLOPs 不增加能同时装下的请求数。
对;直接压每请求 KV 占用,才能在固定显存里塞更多并发请求。
batch=1 反而把并发限成 1,与提高并发相反。
更大模型权重更占显存、KV/token 更大,并发只会更低。
optionExplanations_en: Concurrency is memory-bound; adding FLOPs doesn't fit more simultaneous requests.
Correct — shrinking per-request KV lets more concurrent requests fit in fixed VRAM.
Batch=1 caps concurrency at 1, the opposite of raising it.
A bigger model uses more VRAM for weights and larger KV/token, lowering concurrency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单卡能同时服务的请求上限,约等于剩余显存÷每请求 KV 缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Max concurrency is the ceiling of simultaneous requests per GPU, roughly leftover VRAM ÷ per-request KV cache.

scenario: 同一张 80GB A100 上,7B 模型每请求 KV 约 1GB 能并发~80,而 70B 模型每请求约 5GB。
scenario_en: On the same 80GB A100, a 7B model's ~1GB-per-request KV supports ~80 concurrent, while a 70B model is ~5GB per request.
q: 从 7B 到 70B,单卡最大并发大致怎么变?为什么?
q_en: From 7B to 70B, how does per-GPU max concurrency roughly change, and why?
why: 并发从~80 骤降到~16:模型越大,权重占显存更多、每 token 的 K/V 也更大(70B 每请求约 5GB),留给并发的显存少、每份又更贵,双重挤压。所以大模型服务成本高的根源在 KV 缓存把并发压死。
why_en: Concurrency drops from ~80 to ~16: bigger models use more VRAM for weights and larger per-token K/V (~5GB/request at 70B), squeezing concurrency from both sides.
options: 并发基本不变,模型参数量大小并不影响能同时装下多少个请求
并发从~80 降到~16:权重更占显存、每 token K/V 更大(70B 约 5GB/请求)
并发反而升高,因为大模型的 KV 缓存实际上更小
并发直接降到 1,因为单个 70B 请求本身的显存占用就已经装不满整张 80GB 显卡
options_en: Concurrency stays roughly the same; a model's parameter count doesn't affect how many requests fit at once.
Concurrency drops from ~80 to ~16: bigger weights use more VRAM and per-token K/V is larger (~5GB/request at 70B).
Concurrency rises instead, because a bigger model actually has a smaller KV cache.
Concurrency drops straight to 1, because a single 70B request's own VRAM footprint already can't fill an 80GB card.
optionExplanations: 模型越大权重和 KV 都更占显存,并发必然下降,不会不变。
对;权重+每 token K/V 双重变大,把 80GB 上的并发从~80 压到~16。
大模型 KV/token 更大,不是更小,并发只会更低。
70B 单请求约 5GB 能装下,不至于降到 1。
optionExplanations_en: Bigger models use more VRAM for both weights and KV, so concurrency must fall, not stay flat.
Correct — larger weights plus larger per-token K/V squeeze 80GB concurrency from ~80 to ~16.
A bigger model has larger KV/token, not smaller, lowering concurrency.
A single 70B request is ~5GB and fits, so concurrency isn't 1.

termDefinitions.term: KV per token / 每 token KV
termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 token 在所有层的 key/value 占用;随模型层数与隐藏维增大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KV per token is the key/value footprint of one token across all layers, growing with model depth and hidden dimension.

scenario: 朴素显存分配为每个请求预留一整块「按最大可能序列长度」的连续显存;结果一条 50 token 的回复也占着 2048 token 的空间。
scenario_en: Naive allocation reserves one contiguous block per request sized for the max possible sequence; a 50-token reply still holds space for 2048.
q: 朴素连续分配 KV 显存会造成什么问题?类比是什么?
q_en: What problem does naive contiguous KV allocation cause, and what's the analogy?
why: 内存碎片:按最大序列长度预留连续块,短回复也占满 2048 的坑,浪费 60-80% 显存。类比虚拟内存前的固定分区 OS——坑开太大,大量空间被占着不用,并发被白白拉低。
why_en: Fragmentation: reserving a contiguous max-length block means a short reply still holds the full 2048 slot, wasting 60-80% of VRAM — like fixed-size OS partitions before virtual memory.
options: 没有问题,预留最大长度的做法最安全,完全不会浪费任何显存
内存碎片:短回复也占满按最大长度预留的坑,浪费 60-80% 显存
会导致模型精度下降,因为显存对齐方式影响数值计算
会让解码变慢,但完全不浪费显存空间,纯粹只是个延迟问题
options_en: No problem; reserving max length is the safest approach and wastes no VRAM at all.
Fragmentation: a short reply still holds the max-length slot, wasting 60-80% of VRAM.
It lowers model accuracy, because memory-alignment layout affects the numerical computation.
It slows decoding down, but wastes no VRAM space at all — purely a latency issue.
optionExplanations: 预留最大长度恰恰浪费显存:短回复占满大坑,碎片高。
对;按最大长度预留连续块造成 60-80% 浪费,类比固定分区 OS。
碎片是显存利用率问题,不影响数值精度。
碎片主要浪费显存、压低并发,不是纯延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Reserving max length is exactly what wastes VRAM: short replies hold big slots, high fragmentation.
Correct — contiguous max-length blocks waste 60-80%, analogous to fixed-partition OS.
Fragmentation is a utilization issue, not numerical accuracy.
Fragmentation mainly wastes VRAM and lowers concurrency, not pure latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分配单元过大导致大量已占但未用的显存,拉低有效利用率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memory fragmentation is wasted, reserved-but-unused memory from oversized allocation units, lowering effective utilization.

scenario: vLLM 借用操作系统的分页思想来管理 KV 缓存显存,解决碎片问题。
scenario_en: vLLM borrows the OS paging idea to manage KV-cache memory and solve fragmentation.
q: PagedAttention 是怎么工作的?借鉴了什么?
q_en: How does PagedAttention work, and what does it borrow?
why: 借鉴 OS 分页:把显存切成固定大小的小页,每个请求的 KV 缓存映射到一组不连续的物理页(靠 block table 记录映射),页按需随序列增长分配、请求结束即释放。于是不必预留连续大块,碎片几乎消失。
why_en: It borrows OS paging: split VRAM into small fixed-size pages, map each request's KV cache to non-contiguous pages via a block table, allocate on demand as the sequence grows, and free on completion.
diagram:
flowchart LR Req["请求KV缓存"] --> BT["block table
逻辑→物理映射"] BT --> P1["物理页1"] BT --> P3["物理页3(不连续)"] BT --> P7["物理页7"] G["序列增长→按需加页
结束→释放"] -.- BT
options: 把每个请求的 KV 预留成一整块连续显存,做法和朴素分配一样
借鉴 OS 分页:显存切小页,KV 映射到不连续物理页(block table),按需分配
把 KV 缓存全部搬到磁盘上存放,靠分页文件做换入换出
取消 KV 缓存这个设计,让解码的每一步都重新计算一遍全部历史,靠算力去换显存
options_en: Reserve each request's KV as one contiguous VRAM block, the same as naive allocation.
Borrow OS paging: split VRAM into small pages, map KV to non-contiguous physical pages via a block table, allocate on demand.
Move the whole KV cache onto disk storage and page it in and out of a swap file.
Drop the KV cache design entirely, recompute all history from scratch at every single decode step, trading compute for memory.
optionExplanations: 连续大块正是 PagedAttention 要取代的朴素做法。
对;分页+block table 让 KV 用不连续小页按需分配,消除碎片。
分页在显存内进行,不是搬到磁盘换入换出。
PagedAttention 是更好地管理 KV 缓存,不是取消它。
optionExplanations_en: Contiguous blocks are exactly the naive approach PagedAttention replaces.
Correct — paging plus a block table lets KV use non-contiguous pages on demand, removing fragmentation.
Paging happens in VRAM, not swapping to disk.
PagedAttention manages the KV cache better, not removes it.

termDefinitions.meaning: vLLM 提出的 KV 显存管理法,借 OS 分页把缓存映射到不连续小页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PagedAttention is vLLM's KV-memory scheme borrowing OS paging to map the cache to non-contiguous pages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录请求 KV 逻辑位置到物理页的映射,类似 OS 页表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A block table maps a request's logical KV positions to physical pages, like an OS page table.

scenario: 对比朴素连续分配和 PagedAttention 的显存浪费。
scenario_en: Comparing memory waste between naive contiguous allocation and PagedAttention.
q: PagedAttention 把显存浪费从多少降到多少?带来什么下游收益?
q_en: From what to what does PagedAttention cut memory waste, and what downstream gain?
why: 浪费从 60-80% 降到 4% 以下。省下的显存直接变成并发:同一张 80GB GPU 能多服务 2-4× 的请求,单 token 成本随之下降。这是 PagedAttention 的核心价值——把碎片浪费转成吞吐。
why_en: Waste drops from 60-80% to under 4%, and the freed memory becomes concurrency: the same 80GB GPU serves 2-4x more requests, lowering cost per token.
options: 从 4% 降到 0.1%,起点数字本来就低,几乎没有实际收益可言
从 60-80% 降到 4% 以下,省下的显存变并发:同卡多服务 2-4× 请求
从 10% 升到 50%,是用显存换取推理速度的做法
浪费比例完全不变,PagedAttention 这项技术只影响延迟指标
options_en: From 4% down to 0.1%, starting already low, with almost no practical gain to speak of.
From 60-80% down to under 4%, and freed memory becomes concurrency: the same GPU serves 2-4x more requests.
From 10% up to 50%, trading memory for faster inference.
The waste ratio stays entirely unchanged; PagedAttention only affects the latency metric.
optionExplanations: 起点是 60-80% 浪费而非 4%,收益是巨大的并发提升。
对;60-80%→<4% 的显存回收直接换来 2-4× 并发和更低单 token 成本。
方向反了:是把浪费降下去,不是升上去。
浪费显著降低,并发和吞吐随之提升,不是只影响延迟。
optionExplanations_en: The start is 60-80% waste, not 4%, and the gain is a large concurrency boost.
Correct — 60-80%→<4% reclaims memory into 2-4x concurrency and lower cost per token.
Reversed: waste goes down, not up.
Waste drops significantly, raising concurrency and throughput, not just latency.

termDefinitions.term: cost per token / 单 token 成本
termDefinitions.meaning: 生成每个 token 的摊薄成本;提高并发/吞吐即降低它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cost per token is the amortized cost to generate one token; higher concurrency/throughput lowers it.

scenario: 并行采样或 beam search 时,多条生成共享同一段 prompt 前缀。
scenario_en: In parallel sampling or beam search, multiple generations share the same prompt prefix.
q: PagedAttention 怎么处理共享的 prompt 前缀?靠什么机制?
q_en: How does PagedAttention handle shared prompt prefixes, and via what mechanism?
why: 共享前缀的多条生成可以指向同一批物理页,不必各存一份,靠写时复制(copy-on-write):读时共享同一页,某条要写新内容时才复制出自己的页。这进一步省显存,是分页带来的额外红利。
why_en: Generations sharing a prefix reference the same physical pages via copy-on-write: they share pages while reading and only copy a page when one needs to write, saving more memory.
options: 每条生成都完整复制一份属于自己的前缀 KV,彼此之间互不共享
共享前缀指向同一批物理页,靠写时复制:读时共享,要写才复制自己的页
把共享的前缀直接丢弃重算,靠多花算力去省显存空间
共享前缀被单独存到磁盘上,各条生成分别从磁盘里读取出来
options_en: Each generation fully copies its own prefix KV, sharing nothing at all with the others.
Generations sharing a prefix point to the same physical pages via copy-on-write: shared while reading, copied only when one writes.
Discard the shared prefix and recompute it, trading extra compute to save memory.
The shared prefix is stored separately on disk, with each generation reading it back from disk.
optionExplanations: 各存一份浪费显存,分页的价值正是共享物理页。
对;copy-on-write 让共享前缀只存一份,写时才分叉,省显存。
共享前缀不必重算,分页让它被多条生成共享。
共享在显存内的物理页完成,不是走磁盘。
optionExplanations_en: Copying each wastes VRAM; paging's value is sharing physical pages.
Correct — copy-on-write stores the shared prefix once and forks only on write, saving memory.
The shared prefix needn't be recomputed; paging lets generations share it.
Sharing happens on VRAM physical pages, not via disk.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多方共享同一份数据,只有当某方要修改时才复制出独立副本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Copy-on-write shares one copy among parties and only duplicates when one needs to modify it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时保留多条候选生成路径的解码策略,常共享 prompt 前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Beam search keeps several candidate generation paths at once, often sharing the prompt prefix.

scenario: PagedAttention 用 block table 做一层间接映射,面试官问它有没有代价。
scenario_en: PagedAttention adds a block-table indirection layer, and the interviewer asks whether it has a cost.
q: PagedAttention 的间接映射有什么代价?为什么仍值得?
q_en: What's the cost of PagedAttention's indirection, and why is it still worth it?
why: 代价是每次注意力要经 block table 查物理页,增加一点点间接开销。但换来碎片从 60-80% 降到 <4%、并发 2-4×,吞吐收益远大于这点开销,所以是稳赚的权衡。
why_en: The cost is minor per-attention overhead from block-table lookups, but the throughput gain (fragmentation 60-80%→<4%, 2-4x concurrency) far outweighs it.
tradeoff: PagedAttention(略增 block table 间接开销,大幅提并发) vs 连续分配(无间接但碎片巨大)
options: 没有任何代价,PagedAttention 这项技术是完全免费的显存优化手段
每次注意力要经 block table 查物理页,增加一点间接开销,但吞吐收益远大于它
代价是精度会下降,因为分页会改变注意力的计算结果
代价是必须先重新训练一遍模型,才能用上这套分页机制
options_en: No cost at all — PagedAttention is a completely free memory-optimization technique to adopt.
Each attention adds minor overhead from block-table lookups, but the throughput gain far outweighs it.
The cost is lower accuracy, since paging changes the attention computation's result.
The cost is that you must retrain the model from scratch before this paging mechanism can be used.
optionExplanations: 有间接开销,只是很小;说完全免费不准确。
对;block table 查页的微小开销远小于并发翻倍带来的吞吐收益。
分页只改显存布局不改数值,注意力结果不变。
PagedAttention 是推理期显存管理,不需重训模型。
optionExplanations_en: There is indirection overhead, just small; calling it free is inaccurate.
Correct — the tiny block-table lookup cost is far below the throughput gain from doubled concurrency.
Paging changes memory layout not the numbers; attention results are unchanged.
PagedAttention is inference-time memory management, needing no retrain.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过一层映射表访问真实位置,增加一点查表开销换取灵活性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Indirection accesses the real location through a mapping table, adding lookup cost for flexibility.

scenario: 逐 token 顺序解码很慢(如 30ms/token × 200 token = 6s),想攻击这个顺序延迟。
scenario_en: Sequential token-by-token decoding is slow (30ms/token × 200 = 6s), and you want to attack that sequential latency.
q: 投机解码(speculative decoding)的「草稿-验证」机制是怎么运作的?
q_en: How does speculative decoding's draft-then-verify mechanism work?
why: 小草稿模型先猜 K 个候选 token(便宜);大模型一次并行前向验完,匹配的接受、首个分歧处回退到大模型预测——一次前向能确认多个 token。
why_en: A small fast draft model (e.g. 1B) autoregressively guesses K candidate tokens cheaply, the large model verifies all K in one parallel forward pass, accepting tokens matching its distribution and falling back at the first divergence.
options: 大模型自己逐 token 生成,草稿模型只在事后打分校验
小草稿模型先猜 K 个候选,大模型一次并行验完,匹配的接受、首个分歧回退
两个规模相近的大模型互相投票,取多数一致的 token
把 prompt 拆成 K 段发去不同 GPU,各自独立生成一段结果
options_en: The large model generates token by token itself, and the draft model only scores afterward.
A small draft model guesses K candidates, the large model verifies all in one parallel pass, accepting matches and falling back at the first divergence.
Two similarly sized large models vote and take whichever token the majority agrees on.
Split the prompt into K parts sent to different GPUs, each independently generating one part.
optionExplanations: 草稿模型是先猜 token 不是事后打分,大模型是并行验证不是逐 token。
对;小模型猜、大模型一次并行验,是投机解码的核心。
投机解码用一小一大两个不同规模模型,不是两个大模型投票。
它加速的是顺序解码延迟,不是把 prompt 拆段并行生成。
optionExplanations_en: The draft model guesses tokens, not scores afterward, and the large model verifies in parallel, not token by token.
Correct — the small model guesses and the large model verifies K in one parallel pass, the core of speculative decoding.
It uses one small and one large model, not two large models voting.
It accelerates sequential decode latency, not by splitting the prompt across GPUs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 小草稿模型先猜多个 token,大模型一次并行验证,加速顺序解码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Speculative decoding has a small draft model guess several tokens that the large model verifies in one parallel pass, speeding sequential decoding.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个小而快的模型,负责先生成候选 token 供大模型验证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The draft model is a small fast model that generates candidate tokens for the large model to verify.

scenario: 大验证模型一次前向验 1 个还是 K 个候选 token,成本几乎一样。
scenario_en: The large verification model's cost is nearly the same whether it verifies 1 or K candidate tokens in a pass.
q: 为什么投机解码里「验证几乎是免费的」?
q_en: Why is verification 'nearly free' in speculative decoding?
why: 因为大模型前向的成本主要花在把权重从显存加载进来(内存带宽受限),这份加载成本无论处理 1 个还是 K 个 token 几乎不变。所以一次前向顺带验 K 个 token 近乎免费,接受率高时一次就确认多个 token。
why_en: The large model's forward cost is dominated by loading weights from memory (memory-bandwidth-bound), which is nearly constant whether processing 1 or K tokens, so verifying K in one pass is almost free.
options: 因为草稿模型独自承担了全部计算,大模型完全不用再算一遍
大模型前向成本主要在加载权重(带宽受限),1 个或 K 个 token 几乎不变
因为验证根本不需要大模型参与,只是一次查表操作
因为 K 个候选 token 一定会全部被接受,所以根本不需要真的验证
options_en: Because the draft model handles all the compute by itself, and the large model doesn't compute again at all.
The large model's forward cost is dominated by loading weights (bandwidth-bound), nearly constant for 1 or K tokens.
Because verification doesn't need the large model at all, it's just a table lookup.
Because all K candidate tokens are always accepted anyway, so no real verification is needed at all.
optionExplanations: 大模型仍要做验证前向,只是这份成本被加载权重主导。
对;加载权重是主成本且与 token 数无关,所以并行验 K 个几乎不加成本。
验证正是靠大模型的一次并行前向,不是查表。
接受率不一定 100%,首个分歧就回退,但验证本身仍近乎免费。
optionExplanations_en: The large model still runs a verification pass; that cost is just dominated by loading weights.
Correct — loading weights is the main cost and token-count-independent, so verifying K in parallel adds almost nothing.
Verification is exactly the large model's one parallel pass, not a table lookup.
Acceptance isn't always 100% — it falls back at the first divergence — but verification itself is still nearly free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 草稿 token 被大模型接受的比例;越高一次前向确认的 token 越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Acceptance rate is the fraction of draft tokens the large model accepts; higher means more tokens confirmed per pass.

scenario: 团队用投机解码后,单条回复更快了,但想当然以为整机吞吐也会翻倍。
scenario_en: After adopting speculative decoding, single replies are faster, but the team assumes aggregate throughput will also double.
q: 投机解码降低的是延迟还是吞吐?这对何时该用它意味着什么?
q_en: Does speculative decoding lower latency or throughput, and what does that mean for when to use it?
why: 它降的是单请求延迟,不是整机吞吐:大模型每接受一个 token 做的总工作量没变,还多养了一个草稿模型。所以它适合「延迟 SLA 紧、但有算力冗余」的场景;若目标是最大化吞吐/降成本,它帮不上甚至更费。
why_en: It lowers per-request latency, not aggregate throughput — the large model does the same work per accepted token plus a draft model — so it fits tight latency SLAs, not throughput/cost maximization.
tradeoff: 投机解码(降单请求延迟,不增吞吐、还多养草稿模型) vs 连续批处理(提吞吐)
options: 同时大幅提升延迟和吞吐,是一项完全没有代价的纯双赢技术
只提吞吐、不降延迟,适合追求高吞吐的离线批处理场景
降的是单请求延迟不是吞吐,大模型每 token 工作量不变还多养草稿模型
既不降低延迟也不提升吞吐,只是顺带省了那么一点点显存空间而已
options_en: It boosts both latency and throughput at once — a purely costless win-win technique.
It raises throughput but not latency, suited to high-throughput offline batch scenarios.
It lowers per-request latency, not throughput — the large model's work per token is unchanged, plus a draft model to feed.
It lowers neither latency nor throughput, only incidentally saves just a small bit of memory.
optionExplanations: 不是双赢:大模型总工作量没变,吞吐不增,还多了草稿模型开销。
方向反了:它降延迟不提吞吐。
对;延迟↓吞吐持平,适合延迟敏感且有算力冗余,是 SLA vs 成本讨论的关键。
它确实降单请求延迟,不是只省显存。
optionExplanations_en: Not win-win: the large model's total work is unchanged, throughput doesn't rise, and a draft model adds cost.
Reversed: it lowers latency, not raises throughput.
Correct — latency down, throughput flat, fitting latency-sensitive cases with spare compute, key to the SLA-vs-cost discussion.
It does lower per-request latency, not merely save memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 整机单位时间产出的 token 总量;投机解码不提升它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Aggregate throughput is total tokens produced per unit time across the system; speculative decoding doesn't raise it.

scenario: 草稿模型接受率 70%、每步猜 5 个候选 token。
scenario_en: A draft model with 70% acceptance rate, 5 candidates per step.
q: 70% 接受率、每步 5 个候选,投机解码的主要收益是什么?
q_en: With 70% acceptance and 5 candidates per step, what's speculative decoding's primary benefit?
why: 主要收益是单请求延迟下降:大模型一次并行前向能确认多个(常 2-3 个)token,而非逐个 30ms 顺序出。接受率越高,一次前向确认的 token 越多。但整机吞吐不变——收益在延迟不在吞吐。
why_en: The primary benefit is lower per-request latency: the large model confirms several tokens in one parallel pass instead of one-per-step, and higher acceptance means more tokens per pass, while throughput is unchanged.
options: 整机吞吐会直接翻倍,而单个请求的延迟完全不受影响
单请求延迟下降:一次并行前向确认多个 token,接受率越高确认越多
显存占用直接下降一半,和延迟指标完全无关
模型准确率也会有所提升一些,因为验证的过程会顺带纠正错误
options_en: Aggregate throughput doubles right away, and per-request latency is entirely unaffected.
Per-request latency drops: one parallel pass confirms several tokens, and higher acceptance confirms more.
Memory footprint drops by half outright, entirely unrelated to the latency metric.
Model accuracy also improves a little, since the verification process happens to correct errors along the way.
optionExplanations: 吞吐不会翻倍;收益在单请求延迟。
对;这就是那道 quiz 的答案——一次前向确认多 token,延迟降、吞吐平。
投机解码不省显存,它省的是顺序解码的等待时间。
验证保证与大模型分布一致,不是提升准确率的纠错。
optionExplanations_en: Throughput doesn't double; the gain is per-request latency.
Correct — the quiz answer: multiple tokens per pass lowers latency with flat throughput.
Speculative decoding doesn't save memory; it saves sequential-decode wait time.
Verification guarantees matching the large model's distribution, not accuracy-improving correction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 草稿模型每步预测出的、待大模型验证的 token。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A candidate token is one the draft model predicts each step, pending large-model verification.

scenario: 一个 batch 里既有 20 token 的短回复,也有 500 token 的长回复。
scenario_en: A batch contains both a 20-token short reply and a 500-token long reply.
q: 静态批处理和连续批处理在处理变长输出上有什么本质区别?
q_en: How do static and continuous batching fundamentally differ on variable-length outputs?
why: 静态批必须等整批都完成才返回,短回复干等长回复、GPU 空转;连续批以单步为粒度调度,完成即退、新请求即进,GPU 始终饱和。
why_en: Static batching runs the whole batch through the full decode loop and waits for every request to finish, so a 20-token reply idles for a 500-token one; continuous batching schedules per decode step, letting finished requests exit and new ones enter each iteration to keep the GPU saturated.
tradeoff: 静态批处理(实现简单,短请求被长请求拖、GPU 空转) vs 连续批处理(逐步调度、GPU 饱和,实现复杂)
diagram:
flowchart TB subgraph St[静态批处理] A["整批一起跑完"] --> B["短请求干等长请求
GPU空转"] end subgraph Co[连续批处理] C["逐解码步调度"] --> D["完成即退出
新请求即进入 → GPU饱和"] end
options: 两者完全一样,都是要等整批请求一起完成才返回结果
静态批整批等完成(短请求陪长请求空等);连续批逐步调度,完成即退、新请求即进
静态批其实才是逐步调度、连续批才要整批等待,和它们的名字正好相反
静态批只用在模型训练阶段、连续批只用在离线评估阶段
options_en: They're exactly the same — both wait for the whole batch to finish before returning results.
Static waits for the whole batch (short idles alongside long); continuous schedules per step, exit and entry happen immediately.
Static is actually the one that schedules per step, and continuous the one that waits for the whole batch — reversed.
Static is used only during model training and continuous only during offline evaluation.
optionExplanations: 连续批处理不必等整批完成,这正是它优于静态的关键。
对;逐步调度让完成的请求立即退出、新请求补入,GPU 不空转。
说反了:静态才是整批等待,连续才是逐步调度。
两者都是推理服务的批处理策略,不是训练/评估之分。
optionExplanations_en: Continuous batching needn't wait for the whole batch, exactly its edge over static.
Correct — per-step scheduling lets finished requests exit and new ones enter, no GPU idling.
Reversed: static waits for the whole batch, continuous schedules per step.
Both are serving-time batching strategies, not a training/eval split.

termDefinitions.meaning: 固定一批请求一起跑完整个解码循环,等全部完成才返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Static batching runs a fixed batch through the whole decode loop and returns only when all finish.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以单个解码步为粒度调度,完成的请求退出、新请求随时加入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous batching schedules at the granularity of a decode step, with finished requests exiting and new ones joining anytime.

scenario: 变长输出的 LLM 服务从静态批处理换成连续批处理。
scenario_en: An LLM service with variable-length outputs switches from static to continuous batching.
q: 连续批处理相比静态批处理大致能提多少吞吐?靠什么拿到?
q_en: Roughly how much throughput does continuous batching add over static, and how?
why: 变长负载下约 2-5× 吞吐,靠消除静态批的空转——完成即腾位、新请求即补入,GPU 始终饱和。它天然配合 PagedAttention,共同构成 vLLM 骨架。
why_en: About 2-5x throughput under variable-length loads, from eliminating static batching's idling — finished requests free slots immediately and new ones enter, keeping the GPU saturated.
options: 约 2-5× 吞吐,靠消除静态批空转:完成即腾位、新请求即补入
约 100× 吞吐,靠把所有在线请求硬合并成一个超大 batch 一起跑
吞吐不变,只降延迟,和批处理策略换成哪种无关
吞吐反而下降,连续批处理更慢但确实更省显存
options_en: About 2-5x throughput, by eliminating static idling: finished slots free up and new requests fill in immediately.
About 100x throughput, by forcibly merging all live requests into one giant batch to run together.
Throughput is unchanged, it only lowers latency, regardless of which batching strategy you switch to.
Throughput actually drops; continuous batching is slower but does save more memory.
optionExplanations: 对;2-5× 来自 GPU 不再空转等长请求,短请求腾位后立即被补上。
100× 夸大;实际量级是 2-5×,靠调度而非无限增大 batch。
它主要提吞吐(也顺带改善尾延迟),不是吞吐不变。
连续批处理提吞吐,不是下降。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 2-5x comes from the GPU no longer idling on long requests, with freed slots refilled immediately.
100x overstates; the real magnitude is 2-5x, via scheduling not an unbounded batch.
It mainly raises throughput (and improves tail latency), not unchanged.
Continuous batching raises throughput, not lowers it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在每个解码步做批调度决策,即连续批处理的实现方式(又称 in-flight batching)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Iteration-level (in-flight) scheduling makes batch decisions at each decode step, how continuous batching is implemented.

scenario: 要给一个 LLM 服务后端选批处理策略,线上请求的输出长度差异很大(有的几十 token,有的上千)。
scenario_en: Choosing a batching strategy for an LLM backend where output lengths vary widely (tens to thousands of tokens).
q: 变长输出的 LLM 服务后端,该默认用哪种批处理?为什么不用静态?
q_en: For a variable-length LLM backend, which batching to default to, and why not static?
why: 默认连续批处理:逐步调度让 GPU 在变长负载下保持饱和,短请求不被长请求拖住。静态批处理在变长输出下失效——短请求被迫补贴长请求、GPU 在拖尾者上空转。只有输出长度几乎一致时静态才勉强够用。
why_en: Default to continuous batching: per-step scheduling keeps the GPU saturated under variable lengths so short requests aren't held hostage, whereas static batching fails when short requests subsidize long ones and the GPU idles on stragglers.
tradeoff: 连续批处理(变长下 GPU 饱和,实现复杂) vs 静态批处理(简单,变长下短补贴长、GPU 空转)
whenOtherWins: 如果所有请求输出长度几乎相同(如固定长度分类/打分任务),静态批处理实现更简单,连续批的调度复杂度用不上。
options: 默认静态批处理:实现简单,应对变长输出也完全没问题
默认连续批处理:逐步调度让变长负载下 GPU 饱和,短请求不被长请求拖住
两者都不用,逐个请求单独跑、不做任何批处理才最公平
默认静态批,把所有请求都填充 padding 到相同长度就行了
options_en: Default to static batching: simple to implement, and handles variable output just fine.
Default to continuous batching: per-step scheduling keeps the GPU saturated under variable loads, short requests aren't held hostage.
Use neither; run each request alone with no batching at all — that's the fairest.
Default to static and just pad every request out to the same length.
optionExplanations: 静态批在变长输出下正是会失效:短请求被长请求扣住、GPU 空转。
对;连续批处理是变长 LLM 服务的默认解,GPU 保持饱和。
不批处理会让 GPU 利用率极低,吞吐远不如批处理。
填充到相同长度浪费算力(短请求算了一堆 padding),不如逐步调度。
optionExplanations_en: Static batching fails precisely under variable output: short requests are held by long ones and the GPU idles.
Correct — continuous batching is the default for variable-length LLM serving, keeping the GPU saturated.
No batching leaves GPU utilization very low, far below batched throughput.
Padding to equal length wastes compute on padding; per-step scheduling is better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 批中最慢完成的长请求,在静态批处理下拖住整批。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A straggler is the slowest long request in a batch, holding the whole batch under static batching.

scenario: PagedAttention 和连续批处理常被一起提及,构成主流 LLM 服务引擎的核心。
scenario_en: PagedAttention and continuous batching are often mentioned together as the core of mainstream LLM serving engines.
q: PagedAttention 和连续批处理为什么天然搭配?它们构成了哪些引擎的骨架?
q_en: Why do PagedAttention and continuous batching pair naturally, and which engines do they form the backbone of?
why: 两者都以「请求为独立单元」运作:PagedAttention 让每个请求的显存页按需独立分配/释放,连续批处理让请求逐步独立进出批次——一个管显存、一个管调度,严丝合缝。它们共同构成 vLLM 和 TensorRT-LLM 的骨架。
why_en: Both operate per independent request: PagedAttention allocates/frees each request's pages on demand, continuous batching lets requests enter/exit the batch per step — memory and scheduling align, forming the backbone of vLLM and TensorRT-LLM.
options: 它们互相冲突,在生产环境的服务引擎里不能同时启用
两者都按请求独立运作(分页管显存、连续批管调度),共同构成 vLLM 骨架
它们其实是同一个机制,只是叫法不同而已
它们只能用于模型训练框架内部这一个场景,和线上推理服务完全无关
options_en: They conflict with each other and can't both be enabled in a production serving engine.
Both operate per independent request (paging for memory, continuous batching for scheduling), together forming vLLM's backbone.
They're actually the same mechanism, just called by two different names.
They can only be used inside the model-training-framework scenario, entirely unrelated to online inference serving.
optionExplanations: 两者恰恰互补:页独立分配 + 请求独立进出,是天然搭配。
对;分页管显存、连续批管调度,都以请求为独立单元,构成 vLLM/TensorRT-LLM。
它们是两种不同机制:一个是显存管理、一个是调度策略。
它们是推理服务的核心机制,不是训练框架。
optionExplanations_en: They're complementary: independent page allocation plus independent request entry/exit — a natural pair.
Correct — paging for memory and continuous batching for scheduling, both per-request, form vLLM/TensorRT-LLM.
They're two different mechanisms: memory management vs scheduling.
They're core inference-serving mechanisms, not training frameworks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开源高吞吐 LLM 服务引擎,以 PagedAttention + 连续批处理为核心。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: vLLM is an open-source high-throughput LLM serving engine built on PagedAttention plus continuous batching.

termDefinitions.meaning: NVIDIA 的 LLM 推理引擎,集成分页 KV 与 in-flight 批处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TensorRT-LLM is NVIDIA's LLM inference engine integrating paged KV and in-flight batching.

q: 把 KV 缓存驱动的一次解码步生命周期排好序:
q_en: Order the steps of one KV-cache-driven decode iteration:
steps: 读取整份历史 KV 缓存,与当前 token 做注意力
prefill 阶段并行处理 prompt,填满所有 prompt token 的 KV
把新 token 的 K/V 追加进缓存,供下一步复用
模型输出下一个 token
why: 先 prefill 一次性填满 prompt 的 KV;之后每个解码步:读整份缓存做注意力→产出下一 token→把它的 K/V 追加进缓存。追加让下一步无需重算历史,复杂度保持 O(n)。
why_en: Prefill fills the prompt KV once, then each decode step reads the full cache for attention, emits the next token, and appends its K/V so the next step needn't recompute history.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把新生成 token 的 K/V 加到缓存末尾,是解码步维持 O(n) 的关键动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append adds the new token's K/V to the cache end, the key action keeping decode at O(n).

q: 填空:LLM 服务的关键显存/吞吐锚点。
q_en: Fill in the key memory/throughput anchors for LLM serving.
text: 7B/2048 token/FP16 单请求 KV 缓存约 {{1}}GB,80GB A100 上约 {{80}} 并发;PagedAttention 把碎片从 60-80% 降到 <{{4}}%,并发提 {{2-4}}×;连续批处理在变长负载下提吞吐约 {{2-5}}×。
text_en: A 7B/2048-token/FP16 request's KV cache is about {{1}}GB, ~{{80}} concurrent on an 80GB A100; PagedAttention cuts fragmentation from 60-80% to <{{4}}% for {{2-4}}x concurrency; continuous batching adds ~{{2-5}}x throughput under variable loads.
why: 四个锚点串起 LLM 服务成本模型:KV≈1GB 定并发基数,PagedAttention 去碎片×2-4 并发,连续批×2-5 吞吐。它们都指向同一句话:LLM 服务是显存与调度效率之争。
why_en: These anchors chain the LLM serving cost model: KV≈1GB sets the concurrency base, PagedAttention 2-4x concurrency, continuous batching 2-5x throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用于 LLM 服务的 GPU 规格,显存 80GB 决定能装多少 KV/并发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The 80GB A100 is a common LLM-serving GPU whose 80GB VRAM sets how much KV/concurrency fits.

scenario: 面试官让你脱口说出 LLM 服务的几个关键显存/吞吐锚点数字,检验你是否真的建立了量级直觉。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to recite the key LLM-serving memory/throughput anchor numbers on the spot, to check whether you've internalized the magnitudes.

q: 填空:LLM 服务的统一原则。
q_en: Fill in the unifying principle of LLM serving.
text: LLM 推理是{{内存带宽}}受限而非{{算力}}受限;每个优化要么提升{{显存}}效率(KV 缓存、PagedAttention),要么摊薄{{顺序解码}}成本(投机解码、连续批处理)。
text_en: LLM inference is {{memory-bandwidth}}-bound, not {{compute}}-bound; every optimization either improves {{memory}} efficiency (KV cache, PagedAttention) or amortizes {{sequential-decode}} cost (speculative decoding, continuous batching).
why: 一句话收束全课:瓶颈是显存带宽,所以四项创新分两组——省显存 vs 摊薄顺序解码。面试时先讲这条原则,再挂上四项手段,逻辑最清晰。
why_en: One line ties the lesson together: the bottleneck is memory bandwidth, so the four innovations split into saving memory vs amortizing sequential decode.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逐 token 一个接一个生成,天然串行,是 LLM 延迟的主因。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sequential decode generates tokens one after another, inherently serial, the main driver of LLM latency.

scenario: 一张 80GB A100 服务 13B 模型,KV 缓存碎片严重(短回复占满按最大长度预留的坑),并发上不去,想在不换硬件、不掉精度下提并发。
scenario_en: An 80GB A100 serves a 13B model with severe KV fragmentation (short replies hold max-length slots), and you want higher concurrency without new hardware or accuracy loss.
q: 碎片严重导致并发低,不换硬件不掉精度,最该上哪项?
q_en: With fragmentation capping concurrency and no hardware/accuracy budget, which technique first?
why: 上 PagedAttention:它专治 KV 碎片,把浪费从 60-80% 降到 <4%,同卡并发提 2-4×,且不改数值(不掉精度)、不用换硬件。降精度会掉点、加卡要花钱,都不满足约束;投机解码降的是延迟不是并发。
why_en: Use PagedAttention: it directly cures KV fragmentation (60-80%→<4%) for 2-4x concurrency on the same GPU with no numerical change and no new hardware, unlike lowering precision or adding GPUs.
tradeoff: PagedAttention(去碎片提并发,略增间接开销) vs 降精度(提并发但掉点) vs 加卡(提并发但花钱)
whenOtherWins: 如果碎片已经很低、瓶颈是权重本身太占显存,则该转向量化(降精度)或张量并行分卡,而非再去优化碎片。
options: 把权重量化到 INT8:确实能提并发,但会掉精度,违反给定约束
上 PagedAttention:专治 KV 碎片(60-80%→<4%),同卡并发提 2-4×,不掉精度
加一张 A100 卡扩容:确实能直接提高单卡最大并发上限,但要额外花不少钱采购硬件,违反给定约束
上投机解码:它降低的是单个请求的延迟,帮不上并发或碎片问题
options_en: Quantize weights to INT8: it does raise concurrency, but drops accuracy, violating the given constraint.
Use PagedAttention: directly cures KV fragmentation (60-80%→<4%) for 2-4x concurrency on the same GPU, no accuracy loss.
Add another A100 card: it does directly raise the per-GPU concurrency ceiling itself, but costs real extra money to procure hardware, violating the constraint.
Use speculative decoding: it lowers a single request's latency, doesn't help with concurrency or fragmentation.
optionExplanations: INT8 能提并发但掉精度,违反「不掉精度」约束。
对;PagedAttention 直接消碎片、同卡提并发 2-4×,不掉精度不换硬件,正中约束。
加卡违反「不换硬件」;而且碎片没解决,新卡也照样浪费。
投机解码优化的是延迟,对碎片和并发没帮助。
optionExplanations_en: INT8 raises concurrency but drops accuracy, violating no-accuracy-loss.
Correct — PagedAttention removes fragmentation for 2-4x concurrency on the same GPU, no accuracy loss or new hardware, hitting the constraints.
Adding a GPU violates no-new-hardware, and unaddressed fragmentation wastes the new card too.
Speculative decoding optimizes latency, not fragmentation or concurrency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 130 亿参数的中型 LLM,每请求 KV 约 1.56GB,并发比 7B 低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A 13B model has 13 billion parameters, ~1.56GB KV per request, with lower concurrency than 7B.

scenario: 面试官问：ML 模型上线管线和传统软件的 CI/CD 有什么本质不同。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how an ML deployment pipeline fundamentally differs from a traditional software CI/CD pipeline.
q: ML 部署管线为什么不能照搬传统 CI/CD？
q_en: Why can't an ML deployment pipeline just reuse traditional CI/CD?
why: 传统 CI/CD 假设确定性构建（同代码→同二进制），ML 还要验证数据分布和模型质量这两个随机量。管线要解决三件事：拦坏数据、拦坏模型、支持带回滚的安全流量迁移。
why_en: Traditional CI/CD assumes deterministic builds, but ML must also validate stochastic data distributions and model quality, so the pipeline blocks bad data, blocks bad models, and enables safe traffic migration with rollback.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["代码提交"] --> D["数据验证门"]
  D --> M["模型验证门"]
  M --> P["性能门"]
  P --> R["灰度上线+可回滚"]
options: 两者无差别，代码单测通过、构建产物一致即可上线，不必额外验证数据或模型质量
传统 CI/CD 靠确定性构建，ML 还要验证随机的数据分布与模型质量，并拦坏数据/坏模型、支持回滚
ML 只需在训练时保证模型质量达标，上线管线只做代码构建和打包，不必再检查数据分布或漂移
唯一差别是 ML 管线跑得更慢，验证的内容和传统 CI/CD 完全一样，没有本质区别
options_en: No difference; if unit tests pass and the build artifact is consistent, the model can ship, with no extra data or model-quality validation.
Traditional CI/CD relies on deterministic builds; ML must also validate stochastic data distributions and model quality, blocking bad data/models and supporting rollback.
ML only needs to hit its quality bar at training time; the pipeline just does code build and packaging and skips checking data distribution or drift.
The only difference is the ML pipeline runs slower; the validation content is identical to traditional CI/CD, with no real difference.
optionExplanations: 代码单测只覆盖确定性逻辑，覆盖不了「数据分布漂了、模型在新分布上乱来」这类随机风险。
对；ML 的输入（数据）和产物（模型）都是随机量，必须额外设门验证，还要能秒级回滚。
模型质量依赖上线时的真实数据分布，训练时保证不了，上线仍须验证。
不只是慢：ML 多出数据验证和模型验证两类传统 CI/CD 根本没有的检查。
optionExplanations_en: Unit tests cover deterministic logic only, not stochastic risks like a drifted distribution making the model misbehave.
Correct — both ML inputs (data) and outputs (model) are stochastic, needing extra validation gates plus fast rollback.
Model quality depends on the live distribution and cannot be guaranteed at training time, so it must be validated at deploy.
It is not just slower: ML adds data and model validation, checks that traditional CI/CD lacks entirely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持续集成/持续交付：自动构建、测试、发布代码的流水线，假设构建确定性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CI/CD (Continuous Integration / Continuous Delivery) is the automated build-test-release pipeline for code, assuming deterministic builds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同样的代码总是产出同样的二进制产物，可复现、可测试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deterministic build always produces the same binary from the same code, so it is reproducible and testable.

scenario: 一个模型离线 AUC 高达 0.92，上线后在生产分布上却行为不稳、时好时坏。
scenario_en: A model scores 0.92 AUC offline but behaves erratically once live on the production distribution.
q: 「离线 0.92 AUC，上线却不稳」体现的是什么问题？
q_en: What problem does 'high offline AUC but erratic in production' illustrate?
why: 这是欠定问题（underspecification）：离线指标只反映训练/评测分布，多个模型能拿到同样高分却在生产的偏移分布上表现迥异。所以不能只信离线分，必须上性能门和灰度实测。
why_en: This is the underspecification problem — offline metrics reflect only the eval distribution, so equally-scoring models can diverge on a shifted production distribution, which is why you cannot trust offline scores alone.
options: 说明离线 AUC 算错了，重新算一遍分数、换个工具复核就会和线上一致
欠定问题：离线高分只在评测分布成立，生产分布一偏移，同分模型行为可能天差地别
说明模型参数量不够大，只要加大模型、堆更多层，线上就会自然稳定
说明该换一个更高的 AUC 阈值，把阈值调高一些线上自然就稳了
options_en: The offline AUC was miscomputed; recomputing it with a different tool will match production.
Underspecification: a high offline score only holds on the eval distribution, so once production shifts, equally-scoring models can behave very differently.
The model isn't large enough; just scale it up with more layers and production will naturally stabilize.
Just raise the AUC threshold a bit higher and production will naturally stabilize.
optionExplanations: 分数没算错，问题在离线分布≠生产分布，重算同一批数据不会揭示这个差距。
对；离线只约束了评测集上的表现，生产分布偏移时行为不受约束，这正是欠定的含义。
加大模型不解决分布偏移，欠定与容量无关，大模型照样能在偏移分布上乱来。
调高阈值只改判定点，不改分布偏移这个根因，线上照样不稳。
optionExplanations_en: The score is not wrong; the gap is offline distribution vs production, which recomputing on the same data will not reveal.
Correct — offline only constrains behavior on the eval set, leaving it unconstrained when production shifts, which is exactly underspecification.
Scaling the model does not fix distribution shift; underspecification is unrelated to capacity.
Raising the threshold only moves the decision point, not the distribution-shift root cause.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个模型在离线评测上同样好，但在生产偏移分布上表现各异，离线指标无法唯一确定线上行为。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Underspecification is when many models score equally offline yet behave differently on a shifted production distribution, so offline metrics do not pin down live behavior.

termDefinitions.meaning: ROC 曲线下面积，衡量分类器排序/区分正负样本的能力，与概率校准无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) measures a classifier's ranking/discrimination ability, independent of probability calibration.

q: 把 ML 上线的三道验证门按正确的先后顺序排列：
q_en: Order the three ML deployment validation gates correctly:
steps: 模型验证门：训练后对比 champion 的离线指标、公平性、产物完整性
性能门：在镜像生产硬件的 staging 压测 p99 延迟、吞吐、内存
数据验证门：训练前查 schema、分布漂移、标签泄漏
why: 顺序是数据门（训练前拦坏数据）→模型门（训练后对比 champion 拦坏模型）→性能门（staging 压测拦超延迟）。每道门守一个阶段，前门不过后门没必要跑，不能跳。
why_en: The order is data gate before training, then model gate after training versus champion, then performance gate in staging, each guarding one stage with no shortcuts.
diagram:
flowchart LR D["数据门
训练前"] --> M["模型门
训练后 vs champion"] M --> P["性能门
staging 压测"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 当前在生产服务的基线模型，新模型（challenger）要与它对比才能上线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The champion is the model currently serving in production, against which a new challenger is compared before shipping.

termDefinitions.meaning: 镜像生产硬件和流量的环境，用来在真上线前压测性能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Staging mirrors production hardware and traffic to load-test performance before real deployment.

scenario: 训练前，一批新到的训练数据里某列缺失、或某列的空值率异常高。
scenario_en: Before training, an incoming batch has a missing column or an abnormally high null rate on one column.
q: 数据验证门里哪一项检查专门拦这种问题？
q_en: Which data-gate check catches this specific problem?
why: schema 一致性检查（schema conformance）：核对期望的列、类型、取值范围是否都在，缺列或空值率异常就直接 block，避免把结构损坏的数据喂进训练。
why_en: Schema conformance checks that expected columns, types, and value ranges are present, blocking a missing column or abnormal null rate before it enters training.
tradeoff: schema 检查（拦结构损坏） vs 分布漂移检查（拦数值统计偏移）
options: 分布漂移检查：拿每个特征的当前统计分布和参考集历史分布做对比，看均值方差有没有整体偏移
schema 一致性检查：核对期望列/类型/取值范围是否齐全，缺列或空值率异常即 block
标签泄漏检测：专门查有没有把答案特征、或者与答案强相关的衍生特征悄悄混进了输入
公平性检查：在不同人群或不同地区的切片上分别对比 AUC，看有没有哪个群体的指标明显掉分
options_en: Distribution-drift check: compare each feature's current statistics against the reference set's historical distribution for an overall mean/variance shift.
Schema conformance: verify expected columns/types/value ranges are present, blocking a missing column or abnormal null rate.
Leakage detection: specifically checks whether the answer feature, or a feature strongly correlated with the answer, quietly slipped into the inputs.
Fairness check: compare AUC separately across different demographic or regional slices to see if any group's metric clearly dropped.
whenOtherWins: 如果列都在、类型也对，只是某特征的数值分布整体偏移（如均值漂了一档），那就该由分布漂移检查而非 schema 检查来拦。
whenOtherWins_en: If columns and types are all present but a feature's numeric distribution shifted as a whole, the drift check, not schema conformance, is the one that should catch it.
optionExplanations: 分布漂移看的是数值统计偏移，缺列/类型错这种结构问题不归它管。
对；schema 一致性专门守结构层——列、类型、取值范围，缺列和空值率异常正是它的职责。
标签泄漏查的是输入里混进了答案，与缺列/空值率无关。
公平性检查在模型验证门、对比切片指标，管不到训练前的数据结构。
optionExplanations_en: Drift looks at numeric statistical shifts, not structural issues like a missing column or wrong type.
Correct — schema conformance guards the structural layer (columns, types, ranges), exactly where a missing column and abnormal nulls belong.
Leakage detection checks for answers leaking into inputs, unrelated to missing columns or null rates.
Fairness lives in the model gate comparing slice metrics, not the pre-training data structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 校验数据的列、类型、取值范围是否符合预期结构，守训练数据的结构完整性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Schema conformance verifies that a dataset's columns, types, and value ranges match the expected structure.

scenario: 某特征历史上稳定在 2% 空值率，本批数据里这个特征的空值率突然变成 40%。
scenario_en: A feature historically has a 2% null rate, but this batch arrives at a 40% null rate.
q: 「2% → 40% 空值率」这个数字在数据门里怎么用？
q_en: How is the '2% to 40% null rate' number used at the data gate?
why: 它不是要背的数，而是分布漂移检查的触发信号：对比本批与参考集，某特征偏离基线（2%→40%，20 倍）超阈值就 reject。多半是上游管线坏了，放进去训练会静默毁掉模型。
why_en: The number is not trivia but a drift-check trigger: comparing this batch to a reference baseline, a 20x jump past threshold rejects the batch, usually signaling an upstream pipeline break that would silently corrupt training.
options: 40% 是要死记硬背的硬指标，本题考点就是背下这个具体阈值数字
分布漂移触发信号：特征偏离基线超阈值即 reject，多半是上游管线坏了
空值多其实是好事，模型能借机学到更多缺失模式，不该被拦下来
40% 只会推高存储成本，跟这批数据能不能训练完全无关
options_en: 40% is a hard number you're meant to memorize; the point is recalling this exact threshold.
A drift trigger: the feature deviates from baseline past threshold, so reject — usually an upstream break.
Lots of nulls is actually good, since the model learns more missing patterns, so don't block it.
40% only drives up storage cost, unrelated to whether this batch can be trained on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 特征的数值统计分布相对参考基线发生偏移，可能因上游数据管线故障导致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distribution drift is a shift in a feature's statistical distribution versus a reference baseline, often from an upstream pipeline failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 作为基线的历史数据分布，新批次与它对比来判断有没有漂移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reference dataset is the baseline historical distribution against which new batches are compared to detect drift.

optionExplanations: 这不是要死记的固定数字，阈值因每个特征自己的基线而异，换个特征换个数。
对；跳变本身就是拒收信号，这类跳变多半意味着上游管线出了故障。
空值飙升是异常信号，不是有用的缺失模式，学进去只会带偏模型。
空值率是训练数据质量信号，不只是存储开销，这批数据大概率不能用。
optionExplanations_en: This isn't a fixed number to memorize — the threshold moves with each feature's own baseline.
Correct — the jump itself is the reject signal, and a jump like that usually means an upstream break.
A null spike is an anomaly, not richer signal; training on it only skews the model.
Null rate signals data quality, not just storage cost — this batch likely isn't fit to train on.

scenario: 一个 Uber ETA 模型的训练批次里，`trip_duration`（实际行程时长）被当成输入特征喂了进去。
scenario_en: In an Uber ETA model's training batch, `trip_duration` (the actual trip time) was fed in as an input feature.
q: 把 `trip_duration` 当输入特征会引发什么后果，靠什么拦？
q_en: What happens if `trip_duration` is used as an input feature, and what catches it?
why: 这是标签泄漏：`trip_duration` 就是要预测的答案，模型离线会得到虚高分，上线时这个特征根本拿不到，精度崩塌。靠数据门的泄漏检测（leakage detection）在训练前 flag 掉。
why_en: This is label leakage — `trip_duration` is the answer itself, so the model scores artificially high offline but collapses in production where the feature is unavailable, caught by the data gate's leakage detection.
options: 无害，多一个强特征只会让模型学得更准更好，训练和上线都不用额外拦截它
标签泄漏：把答案当输入→离线虚高分→上线拿不到该特征→精度崩塌；靠泄漏检测拦
只会让训练跑起来变慢一点，纯粹属于性能开销问题，交给性能门处理就行
属于 schema 问题，只要这一列都齐全在场，就说明数据完全没有问题
options_en: Harmless — an extra strong feature only makes the model learn better, no need to block it in training or at deploy.
Label leakage: the answer used as input inflates offline scores, then the feature is unavailable in production and accuracy collapses; leakage detection catches it.
It only slows training down a bit — purely a performance overhead issue, hand it to the performance gate.
It's a schema issue; as long as that column is fully present, the data is completely fine.
optionExplanations: 它不是普通强特征，而是答案本身，离线虚高、上线归零，是典型的泄漏陷阱。
对；答案当输入让离线分骗人，生产拿不到就崩，必须在数据门用泄漏检测提前 flag。
泄漏不是速度问题，性能门查延迟/内存，抓不到答案混入输入。
列在不代表没泄漏，schema 检查不判断某列是否本质上是答案。
optionExplanations_en: It is not an ordinary strong feature but the answer itself — inflated offline, zeroed in production, the classic leakage trap.
Correct — the answer as input fakes offline scores and collapses in production, so the data gate must flag it via leakage detection.
Leakage is not a speed issue; the performance gate checks latency/memory and cannot catch answers leaking into inputs.
Columns being present does not rule out leakage; schema checks do not judge whether a column is essentially the answer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把与标签强相关或本就是答案的特征混进输入，导致离线虚高、上线失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Label leakage feeds a feature that is (or closely reveals) the answer into inputs, inflating offline scores while failing in production.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预计到达时间，Uber 等要预测的目标量；行程实际时长是它的答案不能当输入。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival) is the target to predict, so the actual trip duration is its answer and must not be an input.

scenario: 训练数据被上游悄悄污染了，但用来评测的 eval 集来自同一批数据、带着同样的污染。
scenario_en: Training data is silently corrupted upstream, but the eval set comes from the same batch and carries the same corruption.
q: 为什么说数据验证失败是最危险的「静默杀手」？
q_en: Why is a data-validation failure the most dangerous 'silent killer'?
why: 因为 eval 集和训练集共享同一污染，坏模型能顺利通过模型验证门——离线分看着正常。污染在数据门没拦住就一路潜行到生产才发作，所以数据门必须最先、最严。
why_en: Because the eval set shares the same corruption as training, a bad model sails through the model gate with normal-looking offline scores, so corruption slips silently to production unless the data gate catches it first.
options: 污染的训练集和 eval 集同源，坏模型能骗过模型门，静默潜行到生产才发作
数据验证失败会立刻报错崩溃，一眼就能看到，所以反而最容易排查修复
数据验证只影响训练花的时间，不会影响最终模型的质量好坏
污染数据一定会被模型验证门百分百拦下，数据门可有可无、可以省略
options_en: The corrupted training and eval sets are same-source, so a bad model fools the model gate and slips silently to production.
A data-validation failure crashes loudly right away and is easy to spot, so it's actually the easiest to debug and fix.
Data validation only affects how long training takes, not the final model's quality.
Corrupted data is always caught by the model gate without fail, so the data gate is optional and can be skipped.
optionExplanations: 对；同源污染让离线评测也被污染，模型门看不出异常，这正是它「静默」的原因。
恰恰相反：它不崩不报，离线分正常，静默才是它最危险的地方。
污染直接毁掉模型学到的东西，不是速度问题。
eval 与训练同源污染时模型门根本拦不住，所以数据门不可省。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — same-source corruption also corrupts the eval set, so the model gate sees nothing wrong, which is why it's 'silent'.
Opposite: it does not crash and offline scores look normal; the silence is precisely the danger.
Corruption ruins what the model learns; it is not a speed issue.
When eval and training share corruption the model gate cannot catch it, so the data gate is not optional.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练后用来算离线指标的数据集；若与训练集同源污染，会掩盖数据质量问题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The eval set is data used to compute offline metrics after training; if it shares the training set's corruption, it masks data-quality problems.

scenario: 训练出一个新模型（challenger），要判断它值不值得替换当前在线的 champion。
scenario_en: You've trained a challenger and must decide whether it should replace the currently-serving champion.
q: 模型验证门里，判断新模型能否上线的核心检查是什么？
q_en: At the model gate, what is the core check for whether a new model may ship?
why: 离线指标对比：在标准化 eval 集上把 challenger 的 AUC/RMSE/NDCG 和 champion 比，回退超过阈值就 block。这样保证新模型至少不比现役差，才有资格进下一道门。
why_en: Offline metric comparison — on a standardized eval set, compare the challenger's AUC/RMSE/NDCG to the champion and block any regression past threshold, ensuring the new model is no worse than the incumbent.
tradeoff: 对比 champion（有基线、防回退） vs 只看绝对分（没参照、可能悄悄退步）
options: 查训练数据的 schema 是否完整、列和类型对不对、空值率是否正常，这是训练前该做的事
在 staging 环境里对新模型压测 p99 延迟，看负载下是否超过约定的 SLA 门槛值
在标准 eval 集上对比 challenger 与 champion 的指标，回退超阈值就 block
统计一下模型一共有多少层、多少个参数，参数量越大就说明它越应该被优先上线
options_en: Check the training data's schema — are columns and types correct, is the null rate normal — that's a pre-training task.
Load-test p99 latency for the new model in staging, checking whether it exceeds the agreed SLA threshold.
On a standard eval set, compare challenger and champion metrics, and block if the regression exceeds threshold.
Count how many layers and parameters the model has; more parameters means it should be prioritized to ship.
whenOtherWins: 如果没有可比的 champion（全新任务、首个模型），就无法做回退对比，只能退回到看绝对指标是否达到预设的业务门槛。
whenOtherWins_en: If there is no comparable champion (a brand-new task with the first model), you cannot do regression comparison and must fall back to whether absolute metrics clear a preset business bar.
optionExplanations: schema/空值率是数据门训练前的事，模型门查的是训好之后的质量。
延迟压测在性能门，不衡量模型的离线质量。
对；有 champion 做基线，逐指标对比才能保证新模型不带回退地替换。
参数量不代表质量，堆参数不能作为上线判据。
optionExplanations_en: Schema/null rates belong to the pre-training data gate, not the post-training model gate.
Latency load-testing is the performance gate, not offline model quality.
Correct — with the champion as baseline, per-metric comparison ensures the new model replaces without regression.
Parameter count is not quality; piling on parameters is no ship criterion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 均方根误差，回归任务的误差指标，越小越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RMSE (Root Mean Squared Error) is a regression error metric; lower is better.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累计增益，按排位加权的排序质量指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a rank-weighted ranking-quality metric.

scenario: 一个模型整体 AUC 达标，但在某个地理区域切片上 AUC 比 champion 掉了 3%。
scenario_en: A model's overall AUC is fine, but on one geographic slice its AUC drops 3% versus champion.
q: 为什么整体达标的模型会因为「某切片掉 3%」被拦？
q_en: Why can a model with fine overall AUC be blocked by a '3% drop on one slice'?
why: 模型门要做公平性/切片检查：整体平均会掩盖某个人群或地区的退步，单个切片 AUC 掉 3% 就可能意味着对该群体系统性变差，够格 block，避免上线一个对部分用户有偏的模型。
why_en: The model gate runs fairness/slice checks because a healthy average hides a group's regression, so a 3% AUC drop on one slice can signal systematic harm to that group and is grounds to block.
options: 整体数据都达标就该直接放行，单个切片掉 3% 只是正常范围内的统计噪声，可以忽略不管
公平性/切片检查：整体平均会掩盖某群体退步，单切片掉 3% 可能是系统性偏差，够格 block
3% 只是延迟这类系统指标的正常波动范围，跟公平性完全无关，该交给性能门处理
切片检查只需要在模型训练之前统一做一次就够了，上线阶段完全没必要再重复检查
options_en: If the overall data is fine, ship it; a 3% drop on one slice is just normal statistical noise, ignore it.
Fairness/slice check: the average hides a group's regression, so a 3% slice drop can be systematic bias and grounds to block.
3% is just normal fluctuation in a system metric like latency, unrelated to fairness — hand it to the performance gate.
Slice checks only need to run once before training; there's no need to repeat them at deploy time.
optionExplanations: 整体平均正是问题所在——它把一个群体的系统性退步平均没了，不能只看整体。
对；按切片评估才能暴露对特定人群的偏差，单切片显著回退就该拦。
3% 是切片上的 AUC 回退，不是延迟，属于模型门的公平性范畴。
公平性检查恰恰在模型门（训练后）做，是上线前的关键一环。
optionExplanations_en: The average is the problem — it washes out a group's systematic regression, so overall alone is not enough.
Correct — slice-based evaluation exposes bias toward a specific group, and a significant single-slice regression warrants a block.
The 3% is a slice AUC regression, not latency, squarely in the model gate's fairness scope.
Fairness checks are precisely at the model gate (post-training), a key pre-launch step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按人群、地区等子集分别评估指标，暴露整体平均掩盖的局部退步或偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slice-based evaluation measures metrics per subgroup (demographic, region) to expose regressions the overall average hides.

scenario: 一个模型离线指标全部达标，但在镜像生产硬件的 staging 里，负载下 p99 推理延迟冲到 65ms，而 SLA 是 50ms。
scenario_en: A model passes all offline metrics, but in staging on prod-mirroring hardware its p99 inference latency hits 65ms under load against a 50ms SLA.
q: 这个模型该在哪道门、因为什么被拦？
q_en: At which gate and for what reason should this model be blocked?
why: 性能门：它在镜像生产硬件/流量的 staging 里测 p50/p99 延迟、吞吐、内存。离线再好，负载下 p99 超 50ms SLA 就在这里 block，防止上线后超时、体验退化。
why_en: The performance gate measures p50/p99 latency, throughput, and memory in prod-mirroring staging, so exceeding the 50ms p99 SLA under load blocks it here regardless of offline quality.
tradeoff: 性能门（在 staging 拦超延迟） vs 直接上线（省一步但可能生产超时）
options: 性能门：staging 压测 p99/吞吐/内存，负载下 p99 超 50ms SLA 就 block
数据门：因为延迟偏高，说明训练用的原始数据本身存在质量问题，该回头重新查数据
模型门：因为它的离线 AUC 这类质量指标本身相对 champion 早就已经明显退步没达标
不用拦，只要离线各项指标全部达标，风险就已经排除干净，可以直接跳过压测全量上线
options_en: Performance gate: staging load-tests p99/throughput/memory, and exceeding the 50ms p99 SLA under load blocks it.
Data gate: high latency means the raw training data itself has a quality problem, so go back and recheck the data.
Model gate: because its offline AUC-type quality metric had already clearly regressed below champion.
No block needed; once all offline metrics pass, the risk is already cleared, so skip load-testing and go straight to full rollout.
whenOtherWins: 如果延迟没超但离线指标相对 champion 回退，那问题在模型门而非性能门；两道门守的是不同维度。
whenOtherWins_en: If latency is within budget but offline metrics regress against champion, the block belongs at the model gate, not the performance gate — they guard different dimensions.
optionExplanations: 对；延迟/吞吐/内存是性能门在 staging 的职责，p99 超 SLA 正是它拦的典型。
延迟高是服务性能问题，不代表训练数据坏，数据门管不到。
题设离线指标全达标，AUC 没问题，不是模型门拦的。
离线达标不等于扛得住生产负载，跳过性能门会导致线上超时。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — latency/throughput/memory are the performance gate's job in staging, and p99 over SLA is exactly what it blocks.
High latency is a serving issue, not proof of bad training data; the data gate does not cover it.
The prompt says offline metrics all pass, so AUC is fine and the model gate is not the blocker.
Passing offline does not mean surviving production load; skipping the performance gate causes live timeouts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的请求延迟低于该值，衡量尾部延迟，比平均更能反映最差体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 latency is the value below which 99% of requests fall, capturing tail latency and worst-case experience better than the mean.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务水平协议：对外承诺的延迟/可用性目标，超了就算违约。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed latency/availability target that a breach violates.

scenario: 面试官让你把三道门讲清楚：各在什么时机、查什么、跳过它的代价。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to lay out the three gates: when each runs, what it checks, and the cost of skipping it.
q: 数据门 / 模型门 / 性能门在时机与检查内容上如何分工？
q_en: How do the data / model / performance gates divide by timing and checks?
why: 数据门在训练前查 schema/漂移/泄漏，模型门在训练后对比 champion 的指标/公平性/产物完整性，性能门在 staging 查 p99/吞吐/内存。三门顺序串联，各守一段，跳哪个坏哪一段。
why_en: The data gate checks schema/drift/leakage before training, the model gate checks metrics/fairness/integrity after training versus champion, and the performance gate checks p99/throughput/memory in staging.

rows: 拿坏数据训练、静默退化
对比 champion/公平性/完整性
有偏或退步的模型上线

options: 三门查的其实是完全同一件事，只是先后运行的顺序不同而已，跑最后一道门验证就已经够了
数据门守训练前、模型门守训练后比 champion、性能门守 staging 压测，各管一段
三门其实都是在正式上线之后才开始运行的，本质上属于监控而不是上线前的门禁流程
三门里只有性能门是真正必须要跑的，数据门和模型门其实都只是可选的加分项而已
options_en: The three gates check the exact same thing, just in a different order; running only the last one is already enough.
Data gate guards pre-training, model gate guards post-training vs champion, performance gate guards staging load tests — each covers one stage.
All three gates actually only run after launch; they're essentially monitoring, not pre-launch gates.
Of the three, only the performance gate is truly required; the data and model gates are just optional bonus checks.
optionExplanations: 三门查的是不同维度（数据、模型、性能），互不覆盖，不能只跑最后一道。
对；按训练前/训练后/staging 三个时机各守数据、模型、性能，顺序串联缺一不可。
它们是上线前的门禁，不是上线后监控，时机在部署之前。
三门各拦一类风险，少一门就漏一段，都不可省。
optionExplanations_en: The three check different dimensions (data, model, performance) with no overlap, so the last one cannot cover the rest.
Correct — by pre-training/post-training/staging timing they guard data, model, and performance in series.
They are pre-launch gates, not post-launch monitoring; the timing is before deployment.
Each gate blocks a distinct risk, so dropping one leaves a gap; none is optional.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查序列化模型文件格式正确、输入输出张量形状对、可从记录的训练配置复现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Artifact integrity checks the serialized model file format, correct I/O tensor shapes, and reproducibility from the logged training config.
