optionExplanations_en: Highest score only optimizes the model objective, ignoring diversity and policy, so raw scores derail.
The issue is experience and compliance, not latency: bubbles, monotony, and violating content are not latency effects.
Correct — these three problems map to re-ranking's two constraint types: soft (diversity) plus hard (policy) post-processing.
Recall is an upstream retrieval concern; the raw top list's problems are diversity and policy, not insufficient recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序打分之后的后处理层，注入多样性并施加硬性政策过滤。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-ranking is a post-processing layer after scoring that injects diversity and applies hard policy filters.

scenario: 重排要同时处理「多样性」和「政策合规」两类需求，但它们的强制程度不同。
scenario_en: Re-ranking handles both diversity and policy compliance, but they differ in how absolute they are.
q: 重排里的软约束和硬约束有什么本质区别？
q_en: What is the essential difference between soft and hard constraints in re-ranking?
why: 软约束(多样性)可与分数权衡，用 MMR/标量化实现，允许被高相关性盖过；硬约束(政策合规)是不可协商的确定性过滤，模型分数无论多高都不能覆盖。
why_en: Soft constraints (diversity) trade off against score via MMR/scalarization and can be outweighed; hard constraints (policy) are non-negotiable deterministic filters that no score can override.
tradeoff: 软约束(可与分数权衡) vs 硬约束(确定性、分数不可覆盖)
options: 软约束和硬约束都靠给分数加权实现，只是权重大小不同
软约束是确定性过滤、硬约束可被高分覆盖
软约束(多样性)可与分数权衡、允许被盖过；硬约束(政策)是确定性过滤、分数不可覆盖
软约束只在离线训练用、硬约束只在离线用，都不进在线服务
options_en: Both soft and hard constraints work by weighting the score, differing only in weight magnitude.
Soft constraints are deterministic filters and hard constraints can be overridden by a high score.
Soft constraints (diversity) trade off against score and can be outweighed; hard constraints (policy) are deterministic filters no score can override.
Soft constraints are used only in offline training and hard only offline; neither reaches online serving.
optionExplanations: 硬约束不是加权：它必须一票否决，加权再大也可能被更高分盖过，不满足「绝不出现」。
说反了：确定性过滤是硬约束的特征，软约束才可被高分盖过。
对；关键区分在能否被模型分数覆盖——软的可以权衡，硬的绝不能被覆盖。
两者都在在线服务的重排阶段生效，不是离线专用。
optionExplanations_en: Hard constraints are not weighting: they must veto absolutely, and any weight can still be outscored, failing 'never appears'.
Backwards: deterministic filtering is the hard constraint's hallmark; only soft constraints can be outweighed.
Correct — the key distinction is whether a model score can override it: soft trades off, hard can never be overridden.
Both act in the online re-ranking stage; they are not offline-only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 偏好性目标(如多样性)，可与相关性分数权衡，不是绝对。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A soft constraint is a preference (e.g. diversity) that trades off against the relevance score, not absolute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不可协商的规则(如政策合规)，用确定性逻辑强制，模型分数不能覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hard constraint is a non-negotiable rule (e.g. policy compliance) enforced by deterministic logic that no model score can override.

scenario: 重排要在保持相关性的同时避免连续推很像的视频。
scenario_en: Re-ranking must keep relevance while avoiding a run of very similar videos.
q: MMR(Maximal Marginal Relevance)是怎么做多样化的？
q_en: How does MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) achieve diversification?
why: MMR 贪心地逐个挑下一项，用「相关性 − 与已选集合的相似度」打分：太像已选内容的会被惩罚，从而在相关和多样之间平衡。
why_en: MMR greedily picks the next item by 'relevance minus similarity to already-chosen', penalizing items too similar to what is selected, balancing relevance and diversity.
options: 逐个挑下一项，用相关性减去与已选集合的相似度打分，惩罚太相似的
把所有候选随机打乱，用随机性制造多样
只保留每个类目分数最高的一个，其余全部丢弃
训练时给相似样本加权，推理时不做任何处理
options_en: Iteratively pick the next item scored as relevance minus similarity to the already-chosen set, penalizing too-similar items.
Randomly shuffle all candidates, using randomness to create variety.
Keep only the single highest-scored item per category and discard the rest.
Up-weight similar samples during training and do nothing at inference.
optionExplanations: 对；MMR 的核心就是这条边际收益公式，贪心地在相关性和与已选的差异之间权衡。
随机打乱破坏相关性，不是有控制的多样化，MMR 恰恰要保住相关性。
每类只留一个太激进会大量丢相关内容；MMR 是惩罚不是硬性去重。
多样化是在线重排的推理期动作，训练加权解决不了「本次列表太雷同」。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — MMR's core is this marginal-gain formula, greedily trading relevance against difference from what is chosen.
Random shuffle destroys relevance and is not controlled diversification; MMR keeps relevance.
Keeping one per category is too aggressive and drops relevant items; MMR penalizes rather than hard-dedupes.
Diversification is an inference-time re-ranking action; training-time weighting cannot fix 'this list is too samey'.

termDefinitions.meaning: 贪心重排法，按相关性减去与已选集合的相似度来逐项挑选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MMR (Maximal Marginal Relevance) is a greedy re-ranking method that picks items by relevance minus similarity to the already-chosen set.

scenario: 两种多样化算法都想让最终列表更分散，但机制不同。
scenario_en: Two diversification algorithms both spread out the final list, but by different mechanisms.
q: 多样化里 MMR 和 DPP(行列式点过程)的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between MMR and DPP (Determinantal Point Process) for diversity?
why: MMR 是贪心逐项挑选、显式用相关性减相似度；DPP 是概率模型，给「整体更不相似的子集」更高被选中概率，从集合层面建模多样性。
why_en: MMR is greedy per-item, explicitly relevance-minus-similarity; DPP is a probabilistic model that assigns higher probability to more dissimilar whole subsets, modeling diversity at the set level.
tradeoff: MMR 贪心逐项(简单直观) vs DPP 概率集合级(全局多样但更重)

rows: 相关性−相似度 贪心
概率给不相似子集更高概率

options: MMR 是概率集合模型，DPP 是贪心逐项挑选
两者完全一样，只是名字不同
MMR 贪心逐项(相关性减相似度)；DPP 是概率模型，给整体更不相似的子集更高概率
MMR 用于硬性政策过滤，DPP 用于训练损失
options_en: MMR is a probabilistic set model and DPP is greedy per-item picking.
They are identical, only differently named.
MMR is greedy per-item (relevance minus similarity); DPP is probabilistic, giving more dissimilar whole subsets higher probability.
MMR is for hard policy filtering and DPP is for the training loss.
optionExplanations: 说反了：贪心逐项是 MMR，概率集合模型是 DPP。
机制不同：一个贪心逐项、一个概率建模整个子集，不是同一算法换名。
对；关键区分是粒度——MMR 一项一项挑，DPP 直接对整个子集的多样性建概率。
两者都是软性多样化手段，不做硬政策过滤，也不是训练损失。
optionExplanations_en: Backwards: greedy per-item is MMR; the probabilistic set model is DPP.
The mechanisms differ: one greedy per-item, one probabilistic over whole subsets, not the same algorithm renamed.
Correct — the key distinction is granularity: MMR picks item by item, DPP models the diversity of the whole subset probabilistically.
Both are soft diversification tools, not hard policy filters or a training loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种概率模型，用行列式度量子集内部多样性，给更不相似的子集更高概率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DPP (Determinantal Point Process) is a probabilistic model that uses a determinant to measure within-subset diversity, favoring more dissimilar subsets.

scenario: YouTube/TikTok 想保证每屏都出现一些新创作者或小众类目，而不是全被热门霸屏。
scenario_en: YouTube/TikTok want to guarantee each screen shows some new creators or niche categories rather than all popular content.
q: slot-based diversity(槽位多样性)是怎么保证多样性的？
q_en: How does slot-based diversity guarantee variety?
why: 槽位多样性预留固定 feed 位置给欠代表的类目或新创作者，是一种确定性配额，保证它们一定出现，而不是靠软打分去竞争。
why_en: Slot-based diversity reserves fixed feed positions for underrepresented categories or new creators—a deterministic quota that guarantees they appear rather than competing on soft score.
options: 训练时给小众类目样本加权，推理时不干预
预留固定 feed 位置给欠代表类目/新创作者，保证它们一定出现
把所有候选按相似度聚类后只留每簇一个
对整个列表做概率采样，让分散子集概率更高
options_en: Up-weight niche-category samples in training and never intervene at inference.
Reserve fixed feed positions for underrepresented categories/new creators so they are guaranteed to appear.
Cluster all candidates by similarity and keep only one per cluster.
Probabilistically sample the whole list so dispersed subsets are more likely.
optionExplanations: 训练加权改变不了单次列表的位置分配，也不保证欠代表内容一定出现。
对；槽位是确定性配额，直接把位置留出来，强保证曝光，不靠打分竞争。
按簇只留一个是去重不是留位；槽位是主动预留位置给特定群体。
概率采样是 DPP 的思路，不是槽位；槽位是确定性的位置预留。
optionExplanations_en: Training-time weighting cannot change position allocation in a single list nor guarantee underrepresented content appears.
Correct — slots are a deterministic quota that carves out positions, hard-guaranteeing exposure rather than competing on score.
Keeping one per cluster is dedup, not reservation; slots proactively reserve positions for a specific group.
Probabilistic sampling is the DPP idea, not slots; slots are deterministic position reservations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在 feed 里预留固定位置给欠代表类目或新创作者的确定性配额法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Slot-based diversity is a deterministic quota that reserves fixed feed positions for underrepresented categories or new creators.

scenario: 有内容违反政策(未成年人不宜、错误信息)，但排序模型偏偏给它打了很高的分。
scenario_en: A piece of content violates policy (age-restricted, misinformation), yet the ranker gives it a very high score.
q: 硬性政策合规该放在哪一层、怎么实现，才能保证不被模型分数覆盖？
q_en: Where and how should hard policy compliance be enforced so a model score can never override it?
why: 政策合规是硬约束，要用重排层里确定性的过滤逻辑强制移除，模型分数无论多高都不能覆盖；把它做成标量化里的负权重是软的，会被更高分盖过。
why_en: Policy compliance is a hard constraint enforced by deterministic filter logic in re-ranking that no score can override; folding it into scalarization as a negative weight is soft and can be outscored.
tradeoff: 确定性硬过滤(绝对但一刀切) vs 标量化负权重(灵活但可能被高分盖过)
options: 用重排层里确定性的硬过滤逻辑移除，模型分数不可覆盖
在标量化打分里给违规内容加一个大负权重，让它自然排到后面
训练时把违规样本标成负例，靠模型自己学会不推
交给召回层，用 ANN 相似度阈值把违规内容挡在候选之外
options_en: Enforce it with deterministic hard-filter logic in the re-ranking layer that no model score can override.
Add a large negative weight to violating content in the scalarized score so it naturally sinks.
Label violating samples as negatives in training and rely on the model to learn not to push them.
Delegate to retrieval, using an ANN similarity threshold to keep violating content out of candidates.
whenOtherWins: 若约束只是「倾向少推」而非「绝不出现」(如轻度降低争议内容)，用标量化里的软性降权更灵活。
optionExplanations: 对；只有确定性硬过滤能保证「绝不出现」，模型分数再高也一票否决。
负权重是软的：一个足够高的相关性分数仍可能把它顶上来，达不到绝不出现。
模型是概率的，学到的偏好不是保证；总有漏网样本被打高分推出去。
召回相似度阈值抓不住政策语义，会误杀也会漏放，不是合规的可靠闸门。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — only a deterministic hard filter guarantees 'never appears', vetoing regardless of how high the score is.
A negative weight is soft: a high enough relevance score can still surface it, failing the never-appear rule.
The model is probabilistic; a learned preference is not a guarantee, and some samples still score high and slip through.
A retrieval similarity threshold cannot capture policy semantics—it both over-blocks and leaks, an unreliable compliance gate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由明确规则(而非模型概率)判定是否移除，结果可复现、可审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deterministic filter removes items by explicit rules rather than model probability, giving reproducible, auditable outcomes.

scenario: 突发新闻期间，平台希望把权威新闻源顶到 feed 前列，压过普通推荐分数。
scenario_en: During breaking news, the platform wants authoritative news sources boosted to the top of the feed, overriding ordinary recommendation scores.
q: 「突发事件加权权威来源」最该怎么实现？
q_en: How should 'boost authoritative sources during breaking events' be implemented?
why: 这是硬约束里的 position override：用确定性规则在重排阶段把权威来源强制置顶，不依赖模型重新学习或重训，才能即时、可控地响应突发事件。
why_en: This is a hard-constraint position override: deterministic re-ranking rules force authoritative sources to the top, not relying on model retraining, giving immediate controllable response.
tradeoff: 确定性 position override(即时可控) vs 重训模型(慢且不精确)
options: 紧急重训模型，把权威来源的历史点击率调高再上线
在标量化里临时给新闻类目加正权重，等事件过去再撤
用重排阶段的确定性规则把权威来源强制置顶(position override)
扩大召回候选集，多召回一些新闻视频交给排序自然处理
options_en: Urgently retrain the model with authoritative sources' historical CTR boosted, then redeploy.
Temporarily add a positive weight to the news category in scalarization and remove it after the event.
Use deterministic rules in re-ranking to force authoritative sources to the top (position override).
Widen the retrieval candidate set to pull in more news videos and let ranking handle it naturally.
whenOtherWins: 若不是突发、而是长期想略微提升某类内容，用标量化里的软加权更平滑，不必硬置顶。
optionExplanations: 重训要数小时到数天，突发新闻等不起，且历史 CTR 反映不了刚发生的事件。
软加权可能被更高相关性盖过，也不保证权威来源一定置顶，响应不够确定。
对；position override 是确定性硬规则，能即时、可控、可审计地在突发时置顶权威来源。
多召回不保证排到前面，排序仍按分数走，达不到「突发时强制置顶」。
optionExplanations_en: Retraining takes hours to days—breaking news cannot wait—and historical CTR does not reflect a just-happened event.
A soft weight can be outscored by higher relevance and does not guarantee the top slot, too uncertain a response.
Correct — a position override is a deterministic hard rule that pins authoritative sources immediately, controllably, auditably during breaking events.
More candidates does not guarantee top placement; ranking still follows score, failing the forced-top requirement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用确定性规则强制某类内容占据指定位置，覆盖模型打分排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A position override forces certain content into designated positions via deterministic rules, overriding model-scored order.

scenario: 历史参与度数据里多数群体创作者互动更多，模型直接学这份数据。
scenario_en: Historical engagement data has majority-demographic creators interacting more, and the model learns straight from it.
q: 把历史参与度偏差自我强化、伤害欠代表创作者的循环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the loop by which historical engagement bias self-reinforces and harms underrepresented creators:
steps: 模型放大偏差：欠代表创作者被打更低分
低分导致更少曝光(impressions)
更少曝光带来更少互动数据
数据更稀疏使下一轮打分更低，形成强化环
why: 偏差循环：模型放大历史偏差→欠代表创作者打分低→曝光少→数据更少→打分更低。它是自我强化的，所以公平必须在设计期就介入，不能事后审计。
why_en: The bias loop: the model amplifies historical bias, underrepresented creators score lower, get fewer impressions, generate less data, and score even lower—self-reinforcing, so fairness must be designed in, not audited later.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["模型放大偏差
欠代表创作者低分"] --> B["更少曝光"] B --> C["更少互动数据"] C --> D["数据更稀疏→打分更低"] D --> A

termDefinitions.meaning: 历史互动数据偏向多数群体，模型学后进一步放大不平等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Engagement bias is historical interaction data favoring majority groups, which the model then amplifies into greater inequality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条内容被展示给用户一次，是分配注意力的基本单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An impression is one display of content to a user, the basic unit of attention allocation.

scenario: 欠代表创作者质量与他人相当，却因历史偏差长期曝光不足，想在系统里纠正。
scenario_en: Underrepresented creators are comparable in quality but chronically under-exposed due to historical bias, and you want to correct it in-system.
q: 曝光公平(exposure fairness)该在哪里、怎么落地？
q_en: Where and how should exposure fairness be implemented?
why: 在重排阶段加曝光公平约束：按目录占比(catalog share)或约定标准分配曝光份额，而不是纯按预测参与度分配，这样能主动打破「低分→少曝光」的强化环。
why_en: Add an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking that allocates impression share by catalog share (or an agreed criterion) rather than purely by predicted engagement, breaking the reinforcing loop.
tradeoff: 按目录占比分配曝光(长期生态健康) vs 纯按预测参与度(短期指标高但强化偏差)
options: 在重排里按目录占比分配曝光份额，而不是纯按预测参与度
在损失函数里删掉所有涉及创作者人群的特征，做到「不看即公平」
维持纯参与度排序，等偏差自己随时间消失
只在年度审计时手工提一批欠代表创作者的排名
options_en: In re-ranking, allocate impression share by catalog share rather than purely by predicted engagement.
Delete every creator-demographic feature from the loss to be 'fair by blindness'.
Keep pure engagement ranking and wait for the bias to fade on its own over time.
Manually bump a batch of underrepresented creators' ranks only during the annual audit.
whenOtherWins: 若某群体是因内容质量真的差而非历史偏差被压，强行按占比给曝光会推低质内容，此时该先修质量信号而非配额。
optionExplanations: 对；曝光公平约束在重排主动分配份额，直接打断「少曝光→少数据→更低分」的强化环。
删特征做不到公平：偏差藏在相关代理特征里，「不看」反而失去纠偏和审计的抓手。
偏差是自我强化的，放任只会越来越糟，不会自己消失。
年度手工提名不可扩展、不可复现，纠不了每天数十亿次的曝光分配。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking actively allocates share, directly breaking the 'less exposure → less data → lower score' loop.
Deleting features is not fairness: bias hides in correlated proxy features, and blindness loses the lever to correct and audit.
Bias is self-reinforcing; leaving it alone makes it worse, not better on its own.
Annual manual nominations do not scale and are irreproducible, unable to fix billions of daily impression allocations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让不同创作者群体获得与其目录占比或约定标准相称的曝光份额。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exposure fairness gives creator groups an impression share proportional to their catalog share or an agreed criterion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某群体内容在全站可推物料中所占的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Catalog share is the fraction of the recommendable corpus that a group's content makes up.

scenario: 要检查模型是否系统性低估某些创作者群体，而不只看整体指标。
scenario_en: You need to check whether the model systematically under-scores certain creator groups, not just look at aggregate metrics.
q: 公平性的 calibration audit(校准审计)具体查什么？
q_en: What exactly does a fairness calibration audit check?
why: 校准审计按创作者人群(性别/地域/语言)切片看预测分：在质量可比时若某群体分数被系统性压低，就是模型放大了偏差，需要纠偏。
why_en: It slices predictions by creator demographic (gender/geography/language) and checks whether a group's scores are systematically lower despite comparable quality.
options: 只看全站平均观看时长有没有上涨
按创作者人群切片看预测分，检查质量可比时是否被系统性压低
统计模型总参数量是否超过部署预算
检查 ANN 索引的召回率是否达标
options_en: Just check whether site-wide average watch time went up.
Slice predictions by creator demographic and check if scores are systematically lower despite comparable quality.
Count whether total model parameters exceed the deployment budget.
Check whether the ANN index's recall meets target.
optionExplanations: 全站均值会掩盖群体间差异——总量涨了也可能某群体被系统性压低。
对；切片对比是发现「同质量不同分」的唯一办法，正是校准审计的核心动作。
参数量是部署成本问题，和群体公平无关。
召回率是召回质量指标，查不出创作者群体间的打分偏差。
optionExplanations_en: A site-wide mean masks between-group gaps—the total can rise while one group is systematically suppressed.
Correct — sliced comparison is the only way to spot 'same quality, different score', the heart of a calibration audit.
Parameter count is a deployment-cost concern, unrelated to group fairness.
Recall is a retrieval-quality metric and cannot reveal scoring bias across creator groups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按人群切片对比预测分，检查是否在质量可比时系统性偏低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A calibration audit slices predictions by group to check for systematically lower scores at comparable quality.

scenario: 团队争论公平性该是上线前跑一次的审计，还是持续监控的一等指标。
scenario_en: The team debates whether fairness is a one-off pre-launch audit or a continuously monitored first-class metric.
q: Staff+ 会怎么对待公平性在系统里的地位？
q_en: How would a Staff+ engineer position fairness in the system?
why: 把公平当作被监控的 SLO：一块 dashboard 同时看参与度(观看时长/CTR)和公平(按人群的曝光份额、校准曲线)，配告警。公平是持续监控对象，不是上线后一次性审计。
why_en: Treat fairness as a monitored SLO: one dashboard tracks engagement (watch time/CTR) and fairness (impression share by demographic, calibration curves) side by side with alerts, not a one-off audit.
tradeoff: 公平作为持续监控 SLO(可及时纠偏) vs 一次性上线审计(易回退失守)
options: 上线前做一次公平审计，通过后就不再监控
把公平当被监控的 SLO：dashboard 同时看参与度和公平指标并配告警
只在用户投诉时临时查一次相关群体的排名
把公平完全交给法务合规，工程侧不设指标
options_en: Do one fairness audit before launch and stop monitoring once it passes.
Treat fairness as a monitored SLO: a dashboard tracks engagement and fairness metrics side by side with alerts.
Only spot-check some group's ranking when users complain.
Hand fairness entirely to legal compliance, with no engineering metric.
whenOtherWins: 若产品还在 MVP、量级极小且无公平风险敞口，可先只做上线前抽查，等规模上来再建持续监控。
optionExplanations: 一次性审计会随模型迭代和数据漂移失守，偏差会悄悄回来却没人发现。
对；持续监控 + 告警才能在偏差回潮时及时发现纠正，公平是活的指标不是一次通过。
等投诉太被动，很多被压制的群体根本没有发声渠道，问题长期隐藏。
公平既是合规也是工程问题，没有工程指标就无法监控和迭代。
optionExplanations_en: A one-off audit lapses as the model iterates and data drifts; bias quietly returns unnoticed.
Correct — continuous monitoring plus alerts catches bias regressions in time; fairness is a live metric, not a one-time pass.
Waiting for complaints is too passive; many suppressed groups have no channel to speak up and the problem stays hidden.
Fairness is both a compliance and an engineering problem; without an engineering metric you cannot monitor or iterate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对某项指标设定的目标阈值，持续监控并在越界时告警。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a target threshold for a metric, continuously monitored with alerts on breach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击数除以曝光数，衡量内容吸引点击的比例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is clicks divided by impressions, measuring how often content is clicked.

scenario: A/B 显示纯观看时长排序器 +12% 观看时长，但 +15% 用户不满(dissatisfaction，来自不喜欢/调查)。
scenario_en: An A/B shows a watch-time-only ranker gains +12% watch time but +15% dissatisfaction (from dislikes/surveys).
q: 面对这个结果，最该做的一步改动是什么？
q_en: Given this result, what is the single best change to make?
why: 观看时长涨但不满也涨，是典型单目标 cannibalization。最直接的修法是加一个满意度预测头(如点赞率/调查分)并把它并入标量化打分，用满意度对冲纯观看时长。
why_en: Rising watch time with rising dissatisfaction is classic single-objective cannibalization; add a satisfaction prediction head and fold it into the scalarized score to offset raw watch time.
tradeoff: 加满意度头对冲(牺牲一点观看时长换满意) vs 只追观看时长(短期指标高但用户流失)
options: 加一个满意度预测头并并入标量化打分，用满意度对冲纯观看时长
直接上线这个版本，因为观看时长是主指标、+12% 够好
把观看时长权重再调高，让指标涨得更多
彻底放弃观看时长目标，只用点赞率排序
options_en: Add a satisfaction prediction head and fold it into the scalarized score to offset raw watch time.
Ship this version, since watch time is the primary metric and +12% is good enough.
Raise the watch-time weight further so the metric climbs even more.
Abandon the watch-time objective entirely and rank by like rate only.
whenOtherWins: 若不满上升只是新鲜效应(novelty)导致的短期噪声、跑满 1–2 周后回落，则可能无需加头，先观察再决定。
optionExplanations: 对；加满意度头把「人不满」变成可优化信号并入打分，正面对冲观看时长的副作用。
+15% 不满会侵蚀长期留存，只看主指标上线等于放任 cannibalization。
调高观看时长权重会让不满更严重，方向完全反了。
只用点赞率会丢掉观看深度信号，从一个极端跳到另一个极端。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a satisfaction head turns 'users are dissatisfied' into an optimizable signal folded into scoring, directly offsetting watch time's side effect.
+15% dissatisfaction erodes long-term retention; shipping on the primary metric alone lets cannibalization run.
Raising the watch-time weight worsens dissatisfaction—exactly the wrong direction.
Ranking by like rate alone drops watch-depth signal, swinging from one extreme to the other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化一个指标系统性拖垮另一个，如观看时长涨但满意度掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cannibalization is when optimizing one metric systematically degrades another, e.g. watch time up but satisfaction down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对任何新东西短期都更爱互动，会误导 A/B 结论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users engaging more with anything new short-term, which can mislead A/B conclusions.

scenario: 把「从单目标排序升级到多目标排序」这个决策讲成一条完整链路。
scenario_en: Explain the decision to upgrade from single- to multi-objective ranking as one complete chain.
q: 把多目标排序的决策链排成正确顺序(需求→性质→选择→代价→缓解)：
q_en: Order the multi-objective ranking decision chain (requirement → property → choice → cost → mitigation):
steps: 需求：不能只追观看时长，要同时兼顾满意度/新鲜度/多样性
关键性质：需要显式、可优化的满意度信号来对冲
选择：共享 backbone + 多预测头，用标量化合成一个分
代价：多个权重不是常数、难人工设定
缓解：用在线 A/B 按 surface 调权，并设 guardrail 监控
why: 链路：先说需求(别单极)→点出关键性质(要显式满意度信号)→选多头+标量化→承认代价(权重难定)→给缓解(A/B 调权 + guardrail)。面试里这样一条链能体现取舍思维。
why_en: The chain: state the requirement (no single objective), name the property (need an explicit satisfaction signal), choose multi-head plus scalarization, admit the cost (weights are hard to set), and mitigate with per-surface A/B tuning plus guardrails.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不被直接优化但不能恶化的指标(如不喜欢率)，越线就叫停实验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is not optimized directly but must not regress (e.g. dislike rate); breaching it kills the experiment.

scenario: 排序模型已给几百候选打好分，要经过重排后处理再展示。
scenario_en: The ranker has scored a few hundred candidates; they pass through re-ranking post-processing before display.
q: 把重排后处理的执行顺序排对：
q_en: Put the re-ranking post-processing steps in the correct order:
steps: 拿到排序模型的标量化分数列表
注入软性多样性(MMR / 槽位规则)重新组织顺序
施加硬性政策/安全过滤，移除违规内容
输出最终展示列表
why: 顺序：先拿排序分→软性多样化(MMR/槽位)调整顺序→硬性政策/安全过滤兜底移除→出最终列表。软的可权衡放前面，硬的一票否决放最后确保没有违规漏出。
why_en: Order: take the scored list, inject soft diversity (MMR/slots), apply hard policy/safety filters, then output; soft trade-offs go first and the hard veto goes last to guarantee nothing violating slips through.
diagram:
flowchart LR S["排序分数列表"] --> D["软性多样化
MMR/槽位"] D --> P["硬性政策/安全过滤"] P --> O["最终展示列表"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 重排末端的确定性关卡，移除违规/不安全内容，模型分数不可覆盖。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A safety filter is a deterministic gate at the end of re-ranking that removes violating/unsafe content, unoverridable by model score.

scenario: 除了算法层的多样化，产品侧也能给用户直接的控制权来减小信息茧房。
scenario_en: Beyond algorithmic diversity, the product side can hand users direct controls to reduce filter bubbles.
q: 哪种产品侧手段能直接让用户减小自己的信息茧房深度？
q_en: Which product-side lever lets users directly reduce their own filter-bubble depth?
why: 用户控制项(「少推这类」按钮、话题滑块)让用户显式表达不想看什么，直接降低茧房深度，是算法多样化之外的产品杠杆。
why_en: User controls ('show me less of this', topic sliders) let users explicitly say what they don't want, directly reducing filter-bubble depth alongside algorithmic diversity.
options: 把所有用户的推荐权重设成一样，抹平个性化
提供「少推这类」按钮和话题滑块，让用户显式调整想看的内容
把召回候选集缩小，减少可选内容
关闭个性化，改成纯热门榜
options_en: Set all users' recommendation weights identical, flattening personalization.
Offer a 'show me less of this' button and topic sliders so users explicitly adjust what they see.
Shrink the retrieval candidate set to reduce available content.
Turn off personalization and switch to a pure trending chart.
optionExplanations: 抹平个性化会损害相关性，也不是「让用户控制」，方向不对。
对；用户控制项把多样化的选择权交给用户本人，直接、可解释地减小茧房。
缩小候选集反而减少多样性来源，与目标相反。
纯热门榜牺牲个性化且未必更多样，不是给用户控制权。
optionExplanations_en: Flattening personalization hurts relevance and is not 'user control', the wrong direction.
Correct — user controls hand the diversification choice to the user, directly and interpretably shrinking the bubble.
Shrinking candidates reduces diversity sources, the opposite of the goal.
A pure trending chart sacrifices personalization and is not necessarily more diverse, nor does it give users control.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让用户显式表达偏好的产品功能，如「少推这类」按钮、话题滑块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: User controls are product features letting users state preferences explicitly, like a 'show less' button or topic sliders.

scenario: 视频推荐要在总延迟 <200ms 内，从数百万视频里选出并排好一屏推荐。
scenario_en: Video recommendation must select and order a screen of recommendations from millions of videos within <200ms total latency.
q: 在线服务的两阶段流水线由哪几段组成，各自的量级延迟是多少？
q_en: What stages make up the two-stage serving pipeline, and roughly how much latency does each take?
why: 三段：候选生成(~20ms，ANN 召回~500个)→排序(~50ms，W&D/DCN 精排)→重排(~10ms，多样性+硬过滤)。核心计算约 80ms，留余量给网络/特征拉取，凑成 <200ms 预算。
why_en: Three stages: candidate generation (~20ms, ANN pulls ~500), ranking (~50ms, Wide&Deep/DCN), re-ranking (~10ms, diversity + hard filters), about 80ms of core compute inside the <200ms budget.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["用户请求"] --> C["候选生成
~20ms · ANN→~500"] C --> R["排序
~50ms · W&D/DCN"] R --> RR["重排
~10ms · 多样性+过滤"] RR --> F["返回一屏"]
options: 单阶段：一个大模型直接对数百万视频逐个打分排序
两阶段：先排序精算全量、再召回粗筛，最后不做重排
候选生成(~20ms)→排序(~50ms)→重排(~10ms)，共约 80ms 核心计算，落在 <200ms 预算内
召回→排序→召回→排序 反复迭代直到收敛，不设延迟预算
options_en: Single stage: one big model scores and orders all millions of videos directly.
Two stages: rank the full corpus first, then coarse-retrieve, with no re-ranking.
Candidate generation (~20ms) → ranking (~50ms) → re-ranking (~10ms), ~80ms core compute inside the <200ms budget.
Retrieve → rank → retrieve → rank repeatedly until convergence, with no latency budget.
optionExplanations: 对数百万逐个跑重模型远超 200ms，正是两阶段漏斗要避免的；必须先召回缩小候选。
顺序反了：先召回粗筛把数百万压到几百，再排序精算；且生产系统一定有重排。
对；漏斗把重计算限制在几百候选上，各段延迟相加还留出网络/特征的余量。
反复迭代无界会爆延迟；在线服务是单向漏斗且有硬延迟预算。
optionExplanations_en: Running a heavy model over millions blows past 200ms—exactly what the two-stage funnel avoids; retrieve first to shrink candidates.
Order is reversed: retrieval coarse-filters millions to hundreds first, then ranking; production always has re-ranking.
Correct — the funnel confines heavy compute to a few hundred candidates, and the summed stage latencies leave headroom for network/features.
Unbounded iteration explodes latency; online serving is a one-way funnel with a hard latency budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务第一阶段，用 ANN 从数百万里召回约 500 个候选，追求召回和吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is stage one: ANN pulls ~500 candidates from millions, optimizing recall and throughput.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 要评估候选生成阶段本身好不好，而不是评估最终排序。
scenario_en: You need to evaluate the candidate-generation stage itself, not the final ordering.
q: Recall@K 衡量的是什么？
q_en: What does Recall@K measure?
why: Recall@K = 从数百万里检索出的 top-K 中，真正相关视频所占的比例。它只看「有没有被召回进 top-K」，不看排序顺序，是候选生成阶段的核心指标。
why_en: Recall@K is the fraction of truly relevant videos captured in the top-K retrieved from millions; it measures coverage, not ordering, and is the candidate-generation metric.
options: top-K 检索结果里真正相关视频所占的比例，衡量候选生成的覆盖率
把相关视频排在越靠前得分越高的位置加权质量
用户看完一个视频后的平均观看时长
模型推理一次的平均延迟
options_en: The fraction of truly relevant videos in the top-K retrieved, measuring candidate-generation coverage.
A position-weighted quality that scores relevant videos higher when ranked earlier.
The average watch time after a user finishes a video.
The average latency of one model inference.
optionExplanations: 对；Recall@K 只问「相关的有没有进 top-K」，是覆盖率指标，忽略顺序。
位置加权是 NDCG@K 的定义，不是 Recall@K；Recall 不看顺序。
观看时长是在线参与度指标，不是离线召回覆盖率。
延迟是服务性能指标，和召回覆盖率无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — Recall@K only asks whether the relevant items made the top-K; it is a coverage metric ignoring order.
Position weighting defines NDCG@K, not Recall@K; recall ignores order.
Watch time is an online engagement metric, not offline retrieval coverage.
Latency is a serving-performance metric, unrelated to retrieval coverage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索出的前 K 个里，真正相关物料所占的比例，衡量召回覆盖率。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@K is the fraction of truly relevant items among the top-K retrieved, measuring retrieval coverage.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 候选生成的 Recall@K 很低，很多真正相关的视频根本没进召回结果。
scenario_en: Candidate generation has low Recall@K—many truly relevant videos never make it into the retrieved set.
q: 低 Recall@K 会对整条流水线产生什么后果？
q_en: What does a low Recall@K do to the whole pipeline?
why: 召回是漏斗上游：没被召回的视频，排序永远看不到，也就没机会被推。低 Recall@K 会「饿死」整条流水线，再强的排序也救不回漏掉的候选。
why_en: Retrieval is the funnel's top: videos not retrieved are never seen by the ranker, so low Recall@K starves the whole pipeline, and no ranker can recover missed candidates.
options: 没影响，排序模型会自动补回漏掉的相关视频
排序永远看不到漏掉的候选，整条流水线被饿死，强排序也救不回
只会略微增加延迟，推荐质量不变
会提高多样性，因为候选更少更集中
options_en: No impact, the ranker automatically recovers missed relevant videos.
The ranker never sees missed candidates, starving the whole pipeline, and even a strong ranker cannot recover them.
It only slightly increases latency, with unchanged recommendation quality.
It improves diversity because fewer, more focused candidates remain.
optionExplanations: 排序只能给召回给它的东西排序，看不到没召回的，补不回来。
对；这是漏斗的硬约束——上游漏了，下游无从弥补，Recall@K 决定天花板。
问题不是延迟而是覆盖率：好内容根本没进候选，质量直接受损。
漏掉相关视频不是多样性，是覆盖缺口，会降低相关性而非提升多样性。
optionExplanations_en: The ranker can only order what retrieval hands it; it cannot see or recover what was never retrieved.
Correct — this is the funnel's hard constraint: what the top misses, downstream cannot fix; Recall@K sets the ceiling.
The issue is coverage, not latency: good content never entered candidates, directly hurting quality.
Missing relevant videos is a coverage gap, not diversity; it lowers relevance rather than raising diversity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上游召回漏掉的候选，下游排序永远拿不到，质量被上游封顶。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pipeline starvation is when candidates missed by upstream retrieval never reach downstream ranking, capping quality.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 要评估排序阶段的好坏，且第 1 位的相关视频应该比第 10 位的更值钱。
scenario_en: You need to evaluate the ranking stage, where a relevant video at position 1 should count far more than at position 10.
q: NDCG@K 相比 Recall@K 多考虑了什么？
q_en: What does NDCG@K account for that Recall@K does not?
why: NDCG@K 是位置加权的相关性：排在前面的相关视频得分远高于排在后面的，模拟用户注意力随位置衰减。Recall@K 只看在不在 top-K，不看顺序。
why_en: NDCG@K is position-weighted relevance—a relevant video ranked earlier scores far higher, mirroring attention decay—whereas Recall@K ignores order.
options: 只看相关视频有没有进 top-K，忽略顺序
衡量模型推理延迟随位置的变化
统计用户对每个位置的绝对打星数
位置加权的相关性：越靠前的相关视频得分越高，模拟注意力衰减
options_en: Only whether relevant videos entered the top-K, ignoring order.
How inference latency varies by position.
Users' absolute star ratings at each position.
Position-weighted relevance: earlier relevant videos score higher, modeling attention decay.
optionExplanations: 只看在不在 top-K 是 Recall@K；NDCG 的关键增量正是位置权重。
延迟是服务指标，NDCG 是排序质量指标，不相关。
NDCG 用的是隐式反馈标签，不是绝对打星；且它按位置加权而非计星。
对；位置折扣是 NDCG 的核心，让「把相关的排前面」得到奖励。
optionExplanations_en: Whether items are in the top-K is Recall@K; NDCG's added value is exactly the position weighting.
Latency is a serving metric; NDCG is a ranking-quality metric, unrelated.
NDCG uses implicit-feedback labels, not absolute stars, and weights by position rather than counting stars.
Correct — the position discount is NDCG's core, rewarding putting relevant items earlier.

termDefinitions.fullName: Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at K
termDefinitions.meaning: 位置加权的排序质量指标，越靠前的相关结果贡献越大，再对理想排序归一化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG@K (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain at K) is a position-weighted ranking metric where earlier relevant results contribute more, normalized to the ideal order.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 离线评估要同时衡量「召回够不够全」和「排得好不好」，需要两个不同指标。
scenario_en: Offline evaluation must measure both 'did retrieval cover enough' and 'is the order good', needing two different metrics.
q: Recall@K 和 NDCG@K 分别评估哪个阶段、有何互补？
q_en: Which stage does each of Recall@K and NDCG@K evaluate, and how are they complementary?
why: Recall@K 评候选生成，只看覆盖率、不看顺序；NDCG@K 评排序，位置加权看顺序质量。前者定天花板、后者定天花板内的排列质量，两者互补。
why_en: Recall@K evaluates candidate generation (coverage, order-agnostic); NDCG@K evaluates ranking (position-weighted order quality)—one sets the ceiling, the other the ordering quality within it.
tradeoff: Recall@K 管覆盖(不看序) vs NDCG@K 管排序质量(看序)
options: 两者都评排序阶段，只是 K 取值不同
Recall@K 评排序、NDCG@K 评候选生成
Recall@K 评候选生成(看覆盖率)，NDCG@K 评排序(看位置加权质量)，互补定天花板与排列质量
两者都评候选生成，NDCG 只是 Recall 的归一化版本
options_en: Both evaluate the ranking stage, differing only in the value of K.
Recall@K evaluates ranking and NDCG@K evaluates candidate generation.
Recall@K evaluates candidate generation (coverage), NDCG@K evaluates ranking (position-weighted quality), complementary as ceiling vs ordering quality.
Both evaluate candidate generation, and NDCG is just a normalized version of Recall.
optionExplanations: 两者评的是不同阶段(召回 vs 排序)，不是同指标换 K。
说反了：Recall 管召回覆盖、NDCG 管排序顺序。
对；覆盖率定上限，位置加权质量定上限内的好坏，正好互补。
NDCG 不是 Recall 的归一化；它引入位置折扣、评的是排序阶段。
optionExplanations_en: They evaluate different stages (retrieval vs ranking), not the same metric with a different K.
Backwards: Recall covers retrieval coverage, NDCG covers ranking order.
Correct — coverage sets the ceiling and position-weighted quality sets the goodness within it, complementary.
NDCG is not a normalized Recall; it introduces a position discount and evaluates the ranking stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用历史数据(不上线)衡量模型质量，如 Recall@K、NDCG@K。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offline evaluation measures model quality on historical data without deploying, e.g. Recall@K, NDCG@K.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 要为 NDCG@K 构造 ground-truth 相关性标签，但用户几乎不会显式打星，且打星样本极少。
scenario_en: You must build ground-truth relevance labels for NDCG@K, but users rarely give explicit star ratings and such samples are scarce.
q: 相关性标签该用显式打星还是隐式反馈来构造？
q_en: Should relevance labels come from explicit stars or implicit feedback?
why: 用隐式反馈(观看时长分桶、点赞、转发)构造标签：显式打星稀疏、有偏、大多数用户不打。隐式信号量大、覆盖全，但要小心它也带偏差(如标题党骗点)。标签构造本身就是设计决策。
why_en: Build labels from implicit feedback (watch-time buckets, likes, shares): explicit stars are sparse and biased since most users never rate, while implicit signals are abundant but carry their own biases—label construction is itself a design choice.
tradeoff: 隐式反馈(量大全覆盖但有偏) vs 显式打星(直接但稀疏有偏)
options: 用显式打星，因为它最直接反映用户真实评价
用隐式反馈(观看时长分桶、点赞、转发)构造标签，因显式打星稀疏且大多不打
随机采样一批视频人工标注，忽略用户行为
只用视频元数据(时长、分辨率)推断相关性
options_en: Use explicit stars, since they most directly reflect the user's true evaluation.
Build labels from implicit feedback (watch-time buckets, likes, shares) because explicit stars are sparse and mostly unrated.
Randomly sample videos for human annotation, ignoring user behavior.
Infer relevance only from video metadata (duration, resolution).
whenOtherWins: 若产品本身有强显式评分文化(如电影评分站、明确 1-5 星)且样本充足，显式标签更干净、可直接当 ground truth。
optionExplanations: 显式打星虽直接但极稀疏、只有少数活跃用户打，样本量撑不起训练。
对；隐式反馈量大覆盖全，是主流做法；但要意识到它带偏差，标签构造是设计决策。
人工标注不可扩展、且脱离真实用户偏好，不适合数百万视频规模。
元数据不反映相关性——分辨率高不等于用户想看，信号错位。
optionExplanations_en: Explicit stars are direct but extremely sparse—only a few active users rate—so the sample size cannot support training.
Correct — implicit feedback is abundant and full-coverage, the mainstream approach; but recognize its bias, and label construction is a design choice.
Human annotation does not scale and detaches from real user preference, unfit for millions of videos.
Metadata does not reflect relevance—high resolution does not mean the user wants it, a mismatched signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户行为(观看时长、点赞、转发)间接推断偏好，无需用户主动评分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Implicit feedback infers preference from behavior (watch time, likes, shares) without users actively rating.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被当作正确答案的参考标签，这里由隐式反馈构造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ground truth is the reference label treated as correct, here built from implicit feedback.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 团队只跑离线指标(Recall@K、NDCG@K)就想直接上线新模型。
scenario_en: The team wants to ship a new model based on offline metrics (Recall@K, NDCG@K) alone.
q: 为什么离线指标是「必要但不充分」，必须再做在线评估？
q_en: Why are offline metrics 'necessary but not sufficient', requiring online evaluation?
why: 离线指标只衡量与历史行为的相关性，抓不住新颖性、多样性、长期满意度。历史标签里没有的行为(如用户对全新内容的反应)离线看不到，必须靠在线 A/B 才能测真实因果影响。
why_en: Offline metrics only measure correlation with historical behavior and miss novelty, diversity, and long-term satisfaction, so real causal impact must be tested with online A/B.
options: 离线指标只衡量与历史行为的相关性，抓不住新颖性/多样性/长期满意，需在线 A/B 测真实影响
离线指标已经覆盖一切，在线评估纯属浪费流量
在线评估只是为了测延迟，和推荐质量无关
离线指标不可信，应完全弃用，只看在线
options_en: Offline metrics only measure correlation with historical behavior, missing novelty/diversity/long-term satisfaction, so online A/B is needed for real impact.
Offline metrics already cover everything, so online evaluation just wastes traffic.
Online evaluation only tests latency and is unrelated to recommendation quality.
Offline metrics are untrustworthy and should be dropped entirely in favor of online only.
optionExplanations: 对；离线是历史相关性，抓不到新颖/多样/长期满意这些只有真实上线才暴露的维度。
离线看不到用户对全新内容的反应，也测不了长期满意，覆盖不了一切。
在线评估的核心是真实用户行为的因果影响，不只是延迟。
离线便宜、能快速筛掉坏模型，是必要的第一道关，不该弃用。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — offline is historical correlation and misses novelty/diversity/long-term satisfaction, dimensions only real deployment exposes.
Offline cannot see how users react to brand-new content nor measure long-term satisfaction, so it does not cover everything.
Online evaluation is about causal impact on real user behavior, not just latency.
Offline is cheap and quickly filters bad models, a necessary first gate, not to be discarded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推荐内容对用户的新鲜程度，离线历史标签无法衡量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Novelty is how fresh recommended content is to the user, which offline historical labels cannot measure.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 新排序模型通过了离线评估，要在真实流量上验证，但不想拿全量用户冒险。
scenario_en: A new ranker passed offline evaluation and needs live validation, but you don't want to risk all users.
q: A/B 测试初期该怎么设置对照/实验组和流量比例？
q_en: How should you set up control/treatment and traffic split for an early A/B?
why: 对照组看现网模型、实验组看候选模型，随机分流，初期只放 1–5% 小流量灰度。小比例把风险控制住，出问题只影响少数用户，指标稳了再逐步放量。
why_en: Control sees the production model, treatment sees the candidate, split randomly, ramping only 1–5% initially so a bad model hits few users before scaling up.
tradeoff: 小流量灰度(风险可控但样本慢) vs 大流量(统计快但风险大)
options: 直接全量切到新模型，最快拿到统计显著结果
对照和实验各占 50%，一上来就对半分
只在内部员工账号上测，不放任何真实用户
对照看现网、实验看候选，随机分流，初期只放 1–5% 小流量灰度
options_en: Switch all traffic to the new model at once for the fastest significant result.
Split control and treatment 50/50 right from the start.
Test only on internal employee accounts, exposing no real users.
Control sees production, treatment sees the candidate, split randomly, ramping only 1–5% initially.
whenOtherWins: 若改动极小、风险低且需要尽快达到统计功效(如微小 UI 文案)，可直接用较大比例甚至对半分加速实验。
optionExplanations: 全量切换一旦模型坏了会伤害所有用户，风险太大，违背灰度原则。
初期就对半分暴露过多用户，坏模型影响面太大；应先小流量确认安全。
只测员工样本无代表性、样本量小，测不出真实用户的行为差异。
对；小流量灰度是标准做法——先小规模验证安全和信号，再逐步放量。
optionExplanations_en: Full switch harms all users if the model is bad—too risky, against ramp-up principle.
A 50/50 split up front exposes too many users; confirm safety at small traffic first.
Employee-only samples are unrepresentative and too small to detect real user differences.
Correct — small-traffic ramp is standard: validate safety and signal at small scale, then scale up.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对照组用现网模型、实验组用候选模型，随机分流后比较指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Control uses the production model and treatment the candidate; users are split randomly and metrics compared.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从小流量比例开始逐步扩大实验组，控制风险。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A ramp gradually grows the treatment traffic from a small percentage to control risk.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: A/B 里既有想拉高的指标，也有绝不能恶化的红线指标。
scenario_en: An A/B has both metrics to lift and red-line metrics that must never regress.
q: 在线 A/B 的 primary metric 和 guardrail metric 有什么区别？
q_en: What distinguishes a primary metric from a guardrail metric in online A/B?
why: Primary(观看时长/session、满意度代理)是主动优化目标；guardrail(不喜欢率、举报、退订、session 放弃)不直接优化，但不能越过阈值恶化——越线就叫停实验，无论参与度涨多少。
why_en: Primary metrics (watch time/session, satisfaction proxies) are actively optimized; guardrail metrics (dislike, report, unsubscribe, abandonment) are not optimized but must not regress past a threshold—breach kills the experiment regardless of engagement gains.
tradeoff: primary(要拉高) vs guardrail(只守不恶化，越线即叫停)
options: primary 和 guardrail 都是要最大化的目标，只是优先级不同
primary 是要主动优化拉高的目标；guardrail 不优化但不能越阈值恶化，越线即叫停实验
guardrail 是主动优化目标，primary 只是背景监控
两者都只在离线评估用，在线不看
options_en: Both primary and guardrail are metrics to maximize, differing only in priority.
Primary is actively optimized to rise; guardrail is not optimized but must not regress past a threshold—breach kills the experiment.
Guardrail is the actively optimized metric and primary is just background monitoring.
Both are used only in offline evaluation, not online.
optionExplanations: guardrail 不是要最大化的，而是「不能变坏」的红线，二者角色不同。
对；primary 拉高、guardrail 守底线，guardrail 越线即杀实验是硬安全网。
说反了：guardrail 只守不优化，primary 才是主动拉高的目标。
两者都是在线 A/B 的核心指标，恰恰是上线前的真实检验。
optionExplanations_en: Guardrails are not to be maximized but are a red line that 'must not worsen'; the roles differ.
Correct — primary rises, guardrail holds the floor, and a guardrail breach kills the experiment as a hard safety net.
Backwards: guardrails only hold and are not optimized; primary is the metric actively lifted.
Both are core online A/B metrics, exactly the real pre-launch test.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不被直接优化但不能恶化的红线指标(不喜欢率、退订、放弃率)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A guardrail metric is a red-line metric that is not optimized directly but must not regress (dislike, unsubscribe, abandonment).

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在一次会话中提前离开的比例，是护栏指标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session abandonment is the rate at which users leave a session early, one guardrail metric.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: A/B 结果：观看时长 +3%，但不喜欢率 +15%、7 天回访 −2%(护栏指标越过阈值)。
scenario_en: A/B result: watch time +3%, but dislike rate +15% and 7-day return −2% (guardrails past threshold).
q: 这个实验该怎么处理？
q_en: How should this experiment be handled?
why: 护栏(不喜欢、7 天回访)已越阈值恶化，无论观看时长涨多少都该叫停。+3% 参与度换 +15% 不喜欢、−2% 回访是净亏，护栏就是拦这种「短期涨、长期崩」的安全网。
why_en: Guardrails (dislike, 7-day return) regressed past threshold, so kill the experiment regardless of the +3% watch time—it is a net loss and guardrails exist to block short-term-up long-term-down trades.
tradeoff: 护栏越线即叫停(护长期) vs 只看主指标上线(赚短期赔长期)
options: 上线：观看时长涨了 +3%，主指标为正就够了
把不喜欢阈值调宽，让实验通过后再上线
叫停实验：护栏(不喜欢、7 天回访)越阈值恶化，参与度增益不足以抵消
延长实验到 3 个月，等护栏指标自己回落
options_en: Ship it: watch time rose +3%, a positive primary metric is enough.
Widen the dislike threshold so the experiment passes, then ship.
Kill the experiment: guardrails (dislike, 7-day return) regressed past threshold, and the engagement gain does not offset it.
Extend the experiment to 3 months and wait for guardrails to recover on their own.
whenOtherWins: 若护栏波动只是新鲜效应导致的短期噪声、且在 1–2 周内回到阈值内，可继续观察而非立即杀掉。
optionExplanations: 只看主指标会放任 cannibalization：+3% 观看时长换来 +15% 不喜欢和回访下降，得不偿失。
为通过而放宽护栏是自欺欺人，护栏的意义正是拦住这种交易。
对；护栏越线即杀是硬安全网，短期参与度增益盖不住长期满意度崩塌。
拖 3 个月既伤害用户又浪费流量，护栏恶化不会因为等待而自愈。
optionExplanations_en: Looking at the primary metric alone lets cannibalization run: +3% watch time for +15% dislike and lower return is a bad trade.
Widening guardrails to pass is self-deception; guardrails exist precisely to block this trade.
Correct — breach-kill is a hard safety net; short-term engagement gains cannot cover long-term satisfaction collapse.
Dragging on 3 months harms users and wastes traffic; a guardrail regression will not self-heal by waiting.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在 7 天内再次回来的比例，是长期满意度的护栏代理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 7-day return rate is the share of users who come back within 7 days, a guardrail proxy for long-term satisfaction.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 有人想把 A/B 只跑 2 天就下结论，因为实验组观看时长立刻大涨。
scenario_en: Someone wants to conclude an A/B after just 2 days because treatment watch time jumped immediately.
q: A/B 一般要跑多久，为什么不能只跑两天？
q_en: How long should an A/B usually run, and why not just two days?
why: 典型跑 1–2 周(经验值，非公式)来吸收新颖效应——用户对任何新东西头几天都更爱互动，过早下结论会把这段虚高当成真实收益，得到误导性的「假赢」。
why_en: Run 1–2 weeks (a rule of thumb, not a formula) to absorb novelty effects—users engage more with anything new in the first days, so cutting short mistakes that spike for real gains, a misleading false win.
options: 典型 1–2 周，用来吸收新颖效应，避免把头几天的虚高当真实收益
只需几小时，指标一出现好转波动就能立刻下结论，不必等待
至少要跑一整年，运行时间短于一年的实验结果都不可信
必须跑到样本量正好凑够 100 条为止，和运行了多久完全无关
options_en: Typically 1–2 weeks, to absorb novelty effects and avoid mistaking a first-days spike for real gains.
Just a few hours — once the metric shows any positive blip you can conclude immediately, no need to wait.
At least a full year is required; any experiment run for less than a year is untrustworthy.
Must run until the sample size hits exactly 100, entirely independent of how long it ran.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对任何新东西头几天都更爱互动的短期现象，会虚高实验指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The novelty effect is users engaging more with anything new in its first days, transiently inflating experiment metrics.

optionExplanations: 对，这是常见经验做法——留出十来天时间，让用户对新鲜事物的短暂热情自然褪去，再看数据是否真的站得住。
错，几小时连新鲜感尖峰都还没退，此时看到的正向数字大概率只是噪声或凑巧的短期波动。
错，一整年既拖慢迭代节奏，又让业务变化和季节因素混进来，反而让对比失真。
错，样本量当然要看，但只认一个固定数字、不管时间窗口，照样会被新鲜效应带偏。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — running about ten days to two weeks lets the initial novelty spike fade before you trust the numbers.
Wrong — a few hours isn't enough for the novelty spike to fade, so an early positive reading is likely just noise.
Wrong — a full year both stalls iteration and lets seasonal shifts creep in, distorting the comparison.
Wrong — a fixed sample size ignoring the time window still lets novelty bias skew the result.
category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 早期迭代流量有限，想更快、用更小样本比较两个排序模型的相对优劣。
scenario_en: Early iterations have limited traffic, and you want a faster, smaller-sample comparison of two rankers.
q: 流量有限的早期迭代，interleaving 相比标准 A/B 有什么优势？
q_en: For early iterations with limited traffic, what advantage does interleaving have over standard A/B?
why: Interleaving 把对照和实验的排序在同一次会话里交错混排，让同一用户直接比较两者，控制了用户异质性，所以用更小样本就能得出偏好，适合流量有限的早期迭代。
why_en: Interleaving mixes control and treatment rankings within one session so the same user directly compares both, controlling user heterogeneity and needing smaller samples—good for early low-traffic iterations.
tradeoff: interleaving(同人对比·省样本·比相对偏好) vs A/B(分人对比·需大样本·测绝对指标)
options: interleaving 能测长期留存这种绝对指标，A/B 不能
interleaving 把两模型排序在同一会话交错，同一用户直接比较，样本更小就能定偏好
interleaving 不需要现网模型做对照，直接单独跑候选
interleaving 完全取代 A/B，任何阶段都优于分组实验
options_en: Interleaving can measure absolute metrics like long-term retention, which A/B cannot.
Interleaving mixes both rankings within one session so the same user compares directly, needing smaller samples to settle preference.
Interleaving needs no production model as control and just runs the candidate alone.
Interleaving fully replaces A/B and beats split experiments at every stage.
whenOtherWins: 若要测长期留存、收入这类绝对业务指标或需要护栏监控，标准 A/B 更合适——interleaving 只给相对排序偏好。
optionExplanations: 反了：绝对指标(长期留存)是 A/B 的强项，interleaving 给的是相对偏好。
对；同一用户内对比消除了个体差异，统计功效高，小样本即可比出谁更好。
interleaving 恰恰是把对照和实验混在一起比较，仍需两个排序来源。
interleaving 只测相对偏好、盖不了绝对指标和护栏，不能全面取代 A/B。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed: absolute metrics (long-term retention) are A/B's strength; interleaving gives relative preference.
Correct — within-user comparison removes individual variance, giving high power so a small sample settles which is better.
Interleaving specifically mixes control and treatment for comparison; it still needs both ranking sources.
Interleaving only measures relative preference and cannot cover absolute metrics or guardrails, so it cannot fully replace A/B.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个模型的排序在同一会话交错混排，让同一用户直接比较，样本效率高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interleaving mixes two models' rankings within one session so the same user compares both, giving high sample efficiency.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 端到端延迟预算是 <200ms，要分配给候选生成、排序、重排三段。
scenario_en: The end-to-end budget is <200ms, split across candidate generation, ranking, and re-ranking.
q: <200ms 是怎样的预算，各阶段大致怎么分，对模型有什么约束？
q_en: What kind of budget is <200ms, how is it split, and what does it constrain?
why: <200ms 是给定的产品/SLO 目标(不是公式推出来的)。核心分配约候选生成 ~20ms + 排序 ~50ms + 重排 ~10ms，其余留给网络和特征拉取。它直接约束排序模型大小——大到跑不进预算就得压缩。
why_en: The <200ms is a given product/SLO target (not derived), split roughly ~20ms candidate gen + ~50ms ranking + ~10ms re-rank with the rest for network/features, and it directly caps the ranker's size.
options: 候选生成~20ms+排序~50ms+重排~10ms，其余留给网络特征，直接约束模型大小
这是训练阶段允许的时长上限，跟线上请求的响应延迟完全无关
把全部 200ms 时间都只分给排序阶段，召回和重排两个环节完全不占用时间
它衡量的是模型准确率必须达到的下限指标，不是对响应延迟的约束
options_en: ~20ms candidate gen + ~50ms ranking + ~10ms re-rank, rest for network/features — it directly caps the ranker's size.
This is a training-time duration ceiling, unrelated to the online request's response latency.
All 200ms goes only to the ranking stage; retrieval and re-ranking take up no time at all.
It measures the minimum accuracy threshold the model must hit, not a constraint on response latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 端到端允许的最大响应时间，超了会增加会话放弃，是给定 SLO 而非算出来的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency budget is the max end-to-end response time allowed; exceeding it raises abandonment, and it is a given SLO rather than a computed value.

optionExplanations: 对，这套~20/50/10ms 的分配把重计算限制在预算内，模型大小和推理速度也因此被这条硬线卡死。
错，训练时长你想跑多久都行，跟在线一次请求要多快返回完全是两回事。
错，全部时间只给排序，召回和重排就没法运作，漏斗式流水线也就散架了。
错，这是响应速度的硬性上限，不是拿来衡量模型准不准的门槛。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — that ~20/50/10ms split keeps the heavy compute inside budget, and it's exactly what caps how big and slow the ranker is allowed to be.
Wrong — training can take as long as you like; that's unrelated to how fast one online request must return.
Wrong — giving all the time to ranking leaves nothing for retrieval or re-ranking, so the funnel pipeline falls apart.
Wrong — this is a hard ceiling on response speed, not a bar for how accurate the model has to be.
category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 候选生成要在 ~20ms 内从数百万视频里选出 ~500 个候选。
scenario_en: Candidate generation must select ~500 candidates from millions of videos within ~20ms.
q: 候选生成为什么能在 ~20ms 内跑完，在线主要花在哪？
q_en: How does candidate generation finish in ~20ms, and where does its online cost go?
why: 视频 embedding 离线预计算好、建成索引，在线只需把用户上下文编码成 query embedding，再用 ANN 查最近邻。在线成本 = 一次 query 编码 + 一次索引查找，所以能压到 ~20ms，优先保召回和吞吐。
why_en: Video embeddings are precomputed offline into an index, so online cost is just encoding the user context into a query embedding plus one ANN lookup, keeping it near ~20ms while prioritizing recall and throughput.
tradeoff: 视频侧离线预计算(在线只查) vs 在线实时算视频 embedding(准但太慢)
options: 在线对每个视频实时重算 embedding，再逐个和用户比对
视频 embedding 离线预计算成索引，在线只做 query 编码 + ANN 查找
把数百万视频全量灌进排序模型逐个打分
在数据库里用 SQL 关键词匹配标题挑候选
options_en: Recompute each video's embedding online in real time and compare with the user one by one.
Video embeddings are precomputed offline into an index; online does only query encoding plus an ANN lookup.
Feed all millions of videos into the ranking model to score each one.
Use SQL keyword matching on titles in the database to pick candidates.
whenOtherWins: 若物料库极小或视频特征高频变化到无法预计算，才考虑在线实时算 embedding；一般规模下预计算+ANN 才跑得进预算。
optionExplanations: 在线实时算数百万 embedding 远超 20ms，正是预计算要避免的。
对；预计算把重活挪到离线，在线只剩编码+查找，才压得进 ~20ms。
全量灌排序模型是数百万次重推理，秒级都不止，违背两阶段设计。
关键词匹配抓不到语义相似，召回质量差，也不是 embedding 检索。
optionExplanations_en: Computing millions of embeddings online far exceeds 20ms—exactly what precomputation avoids.
Correct — precomputation moves the heavy work offline, leaving only encode plus lookup online to fit ~20ms.
Feeding all into the ranker is millions of heavy inferences, seconds not ms, violating the two-stage design.
Keyword matching misses semantic similarity, giving poor recall, and is not embedding retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户上下文编码成的向量，用它在视频索引里做 ANN 最近邻查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A query embedding encodes the user context into a vector used for ANN nearest-neighbor lookup in the video index.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 排序阶段的 Wide&Deep/DCN 模型要在 ~50ms 内给几百候选打分，模型大小被延迟卡住。
scenario_en: The ranking-stage Wide&Deep/DCN must score hundreds of candidates within ~50ms, its size capped by latency.
q: 哪些技术能让排序模型在延迟预算内跑得动？(多选)
q_en: Which techniques help the ranking model fit within the latency budget? (multiple)
why: 压延迟的三招：模型蒸馏(小学生模型模仿大老师)、量化(FP32→INT8 减算力)、embedding table distribution(把稀疏 embedding 表分片到多机并行查)。加大 batch 上限不是降延迟手段。
why_en: Three levers: model distillation (small student mimics big teacher), quantization (FP32→INT8), and embedding-table distribution (shard sparse tables across machines for parallel lookup); raising the batch cap is not a latency reducer.
options: 模型蒸馏：小学生模型模仿大老师，参数更少推理更快
量化：把权重从 FP32 降到 INT8，减少算力和内存
embedding table distribution：把稀疏 embedding 表分片到多机，并行查找
把推理 batch 上限调大，让单次处理更多请求
options_en: Model distillation: a small student mimics a big teacher, fewer params and faster inference.
Quantization: drop weights from FP32 to INT8, cutting compute and memory.
Embedding-table distribution: shard sparse embedding tables across machines for parallel lookup.
Raise the inference batch cap so one pass handles more requests.
optionExplanations: 对；蒸馏用小模型逼近大模型精度，直接砍推理成本，是压延迟主力。
对；INT8 让每次乘加更快、内存更省，是常见的推理加速手段。
对；YouTube 规模稀疏表装不下单机，分片并行查是必需，也带来分布式推理的容错课题。
错；加大 batch 提高吞吐但通常增加单请求延迟(等凑批)，不是降延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — distillation approximates the big model's accuracy with a small one, directly cutting inference cost, a primary latency lever.
Correct — INT8 makes each multiply-add faster and saves memory, a common inference speedup.
Correct — at YouTube scale sparse tables cannot fit one machine, so sharded parallel lookup is required, introducing distributed-inference fault-tolerance concerns.
Wrong — a larger batch raises throughput but usually increases per-request latency (waiting to fill the batch), not reduces it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把模型权重从高精度(FP32)降到低精度(INT8)，减少算力和内存、略损精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers model weights from high precision (FP32) to low (INT8), cutting compute and memory with slight accuracy loss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练一个小的学生模型去模仿大的老师模型输出，换取更快推理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model distillation trains a small student model to mimic a large teacher's outputs for faster inference.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: YouTube 规模的稀疏特征 embedding 表(数亿 ID)大到一台机器的内存装不下。
scenario_en: At YouTube scale, sparse-feature embedding tables (hundreds of millions of IDs) are too big for one machine's memory.
q: 稀疏 embedding 表装不下单机时，怎么在服务里处理？代价是什么？
q_en: When sparse embedding tables don't fit one machine, how is this handled at serving, and at what cost?
why: 把 embedding 表分片(shard)到多台机器，推理时并行查各分片再汇总(分布式推理)。代价：跨机通信增加延迟，且引入容错问题——某个分片机器挂了要有降级/副本，否则查不到那部分特征。
why_en: Shard the embedding table across machines and do parallel lookups gathered at inference (distributed inference); the cost is added cross-machine latency plus fault-tolerance concerns if a shard host fails.
tradeoff: 分片分布式推理(装得下大表但加通信+容错) vs 单机(简单但装不下)
options: 把 embedding 表分片到多机、并行查找汇总；代价是跨机通信延迟 + 容错问题
把稀疏 ID 全哈希进一个小表，接受大量冲突以塞进单机
干脆不用稀疏特征，只留稠密特征以缩小模型
把整张表复制到每台机器上，靠冗余提速
options_en: Shard the embedding table across machines with parallel gathered lookups; the cost is cross-machine latency plus fault tolerance.
Hash all sparse IDs into one small table, accepting heavy collisions to fit one machine.
Just drop sparse features and keep only dense ones to shrink the model.
Replicate the whole table onto every machine for redundancy-based speedup.
whenOtherWins: 若稀疏表小到能装进单机内存，就别上分布式——单机查找没有跨机通信和分片容错开销，更简单更快。
optionExplanations: 对；分片+分布式推理是装下大表的标准解，代价是通信延迟和分片容错，Staff+ 要点名。
全哈希进小表冲突严重、信息大量丢失，损精度换空间不是这里的正解。
丢掉稀疏特征会损失关键个性化信号，是削足适履。
整表复制到每机内存翻倍更装不下，也不解决单机放不下的根本问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — sharding plus distributed inference is the standard way to fit a large table; the cost is communication latency and shard fault tolerance, a Staff+ point.
Hashing everything into a small table causes heavy collisions and information loss, trading accuracy for space, not the fix here.
Dropping sparse features loses key personalization signal, cutting the foot to fit the shoe.
Replicating the whole table onto every machine doubles memory and still cannot fit, not solving the root problem.

termDefinitions.term: embedding table distribution / embedding 表分布
termDefinitions.meaning: 把巨大的稀疏 embedding 表分片到多台机器，推理时并行查找。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding-table distribution shards a huge sparse embedding table across machines for parallel lookup at inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推理跨多台机器协同完成，带来通信延迟和容错需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Distributed inference splits one inference across machines, adding communication latency and fault-tolerance needs.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 团队一路加大观看时长权重，指标持续上涨，但用户自报满意度悄悄下滑。
scenario_en: The team keeps raising the watch-time weight and the metric keeps climbing, but self-reported satisfaction quietly slips.
q: 指标相食(metric cannibalization)最典型的一对是什么，本质是什么问题？
q_en: What is the canonical cannibalization pair, and what kind of problem is it fundamentally?
why: 最典型是观看时长 vs 长期满意度：最大化观看时长会顶起自动播放友好的煽动内容，人一直看却不满意；YouTube 自己的研究证实纯参与度优化拉低了自报满意度。它没有银弹，是需要持续校准的问题，不是一次性可解。
why_en: The canonical pair is watch time vs long-term satisfaction: maximizing watch time surfaces autoplay-friendly sensational content that keeps users watching yet dissatisfied, a continuous calibration problem with no silver bullet.
options: 延迟 vs 吞吐：压低延迟必然降吞吐，属硬件权衡
召回 vs 精度：多召回必然掉精度，靠调 K 解决
观看时长 vs 长期满意度：最大化观看时长顶起煽动内容、人看却不满，需持续校准
训练成本 vs 推理成本：省训练必然贵推理
options_en: Latency vs throughput: cutting latency must lower throughput, a hardware tradeoff.
Recall vs precision: more recall must drop precision, fixed by tuning K.
Watch time vs long-term satisfaction: maximizing watch time surfaces sensational content that users watch yet dislike, needing continuous calibration.
Training cost vs inference cost: saving training must raise inference.
optionExplanations: 延迟-吞吐是资源权衡，不是「优化一个业务指标拖垮另一个业务指标」的相食。
召回-精度是检索权衡，不涉及长期满意度被短期参与度侵蚀。
对；观看时长顶起煽动内容侵蚀长期满意，是相食的教科书案例，需持续校准。
训练-推理成本是工程成本权衡，不是指标相食。
optionExplanations_en: Latency-throughput is a resource tradeoff, not one business metric systematically degrading another.
Recall-precision is a retrieval tradeoff and does not involve long-term satisfaction eroded by short-term engagement.
Correct — watch time surfacing sensational content that erodes long-term satisfaction is the textbook cannibalization case, needing continuous calibration.
Training-inference cost is an engineering-cost tradeoff, not metric cannibalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 优化一个指标系统性地拖垮另一个，如观看时长涨但长期满意度掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Metric cannibalization is when optimizing one metric systematically degrades another, e.g. watch time up but long-term satisfaction down.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 已知观看时长在蚕食长期满意度，要在建模和部署层面缓解。
scenario_en: Given that watch time is cannibalizing long-term satisfaction, you need modeling and deployment-level mitigations.
q: 缓解指标相食有哪些正当手段？(多选)
q_en: Which are legitimate ways to mitigate metric cannibalization? (multiple)
why: 四类缓解里的三类：多目标标量化(加满意度头、按 surface 调权)、长视野奖励建模(预测 N 天回访、用 RL 处理延迟奖励)、护栏门控部署(满意度护栏恶化就不上线)。「删掉满意度指标」是掩耳盗铃，不是缓解。
why_en: Three legitimate levers: multi-objective scalarization (satisfaction heads, per-surface weights), long-horizon reward modeling (predicted N-day return, RL for delayed rewards), and guardrail-gated deployment; deleting the satisfaction metric is not a mitigation.
options: 多目标标量化：加满意度预测头、按 surface 调权
长视野奖励建模：预测 N 天回访率，用 RL 处理延迟奖励
护栏门控部署：满意度护栏(不喜欢、放弃率)恶化就不上线
干脆不再统计满意度指标，眼不见为净
options_en: Multi-objective scalarization: add satisfaction heads and tune weights per surface.
Long-horizon reward modeling: predict N-day return rate and use RL for delayed rewards.
Guardrail-gated deployment: do not ship if satisfaction guardrails (dislike, abandonment) regress.
Just stop tracking the satisfaction metric to keep it out of sight.
optionExplanations: 对；标量化加满意度头把长期满意变成可优化信号，是最直接的缓解。
对；长视野奖励把 N 天回访纳入目标，缓解只看即时观看时长的短视。
对；护栏门控是硬安全网，满意度恶化直接拦下上线。
错；停统计不解决问题，只是让相食无人察觉，是反面做法。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — scalarization with satisfaction heads turns long-term satisfaction into an optimizable signal, the most direct mitigation.
Correct — long-horizon rewards fold N-day return into the objective, easing the short-sightedness of raw watch time.
Correct — guardrail gating is a hard safety net that blocks shipping when satisfaction regresses.
Wrong — not tracking it solves nothing and just lets cannibalization go unnoticed, an anti-pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 N 天回访等延迟结果纳入优化目标，对抗只看即时观看的短视。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A long-horizon reward folds delayed outcomes like N-day return into the objective to counter short-term myopia.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 一部分用户出现明显不满信号(打开频率下降、不喜欢上升)，另一部分仍很活跃满意。
scenario_en: Some users show clear dissatisfaction (declining frequency, rising dislikes) while others remain active and satisfied.
q: 怎么用「按用户分群调权」缓解这部分用户的相食？
q_en: How does per-user-segment weight tuning mitigate cannibalization for these users?
why: 对出现不满信号的分群提高满意度目标的权重、压低纯观看时长权重，让排序对他们更保守；满意用户维持原权重。分群调权把全局一刀切换成因人而异的校准。
why_en: Raise the satisfaction weight (and lower raw watch-time weight) for the dissatisfied segment so ranking is gentler for them, while keeping other segments' weights, turning a global knob into per-segment calibration.
tradeoff: 按分群调权(精准但更复杂) vs 全局一套权重(简单但对不满用户失灵)
options: 给出现不满信号的分群提高满意度权重、降低观看时长权重，其余分群维持原权重
对所有用户统一把观看时长权重再调高，摊平差异
把不满用户直接从推荐系统里剔除，不再服务
只按用户地理位置分群，与满意信号无关
options_en: For the segment showing dissatisfaction, raise the satisfaction weight and lower the watch-time weight, keeping other segments as is.
Uniformly raise the watch-time weight for all users to flatten differences.
Remove dissatisfied users from the system entirely and stop serving them.
Segment only by geography, unrelated to the satisfaction signal.
whenOtherWins: 若各分群的不满模式差别不大、或分群带来的复杂度/数据稀疏得不偿失，一套全局权重反而更稳更好维护。
optionExplanations: 对；对不满分群定向加满意度权重，是把校准做到人群粒度，正对相食。
全局再调高观看时长权重会让不满用户更糟，方向反了。
剔除用户是放弃而非缓解，还会流失用户，不是调权手段。
只按地理分群抓不到「谁在不满」，与缓解相食的目标脱节。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — targeting the dissatisfied segment with a higher satisfaction weight brings calibration down to the segment level, directly addressing cannibalization.
Raising the watch-time weight globally makes dissatisfied users worse—the wrong direction.
Removing users is giving up, not mitigating, and churns users, not a weighting lever.
Segmenting by geography alone cannot capture who is dissatisfied, detached from the mitigation goal.

termDefinitions.term: per-segment weight tuning / 分群调权
termDefinitions.meaning: 对不同用户分群使用不同的目标权重，对不满群体加大满意度权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-segment weight tuning uses different objective weights for different user segments, boosting satisfaction weight for dissatisfied groups.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 一次在线请求进来，要在 <200ms 内走完两阶段服务并返回一屏推荐。
scenario_en: One online request arrives and must traverse two-stage serving within <200ms to return a screen.
q: 把在线服务一次请求的处理步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the steps of serving one online request correctly:
steps: 把用户上下文编码成 query embedding
用 ANN 查预计算的视频索引，召回 ~500 候选
排序模型对候选算多目标分并排序
重排注入多样性并施加硬性政策过滤，返回一屏
why: 顺序：编码 query→ANN 召回~500→排序精算打分→重排(多样性+硬过滤)出屏。前两步是候选生成(~20ms)、第三步排序(~50ms)、第四步重排(~10ms)，合计核心~80ms 落进 <200ms。
why_en: Order: encode query, ANN-retrieve ~500, rank with multi-objective scores, then re-rank (diversity + hard filters), i.e. ~20ms + ~50ms + ~10ms of core compute inside <200ms.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["编码 query embedding"] --> A["ANN 召回 ~500"]
  A --> R["排序多目标打分"]
  R --> RR["重排+硬过滤→出屏"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选生成(召回)+排序(精排)的在线漏斗，末端加重排，整体受延迟预算约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two-stage serving is the online funnel of candidate generation (retrieval) plus ranking, with re-ranking at the end, all under a latency budget.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 同一道视频推荐题，L4、L5、Staff+ 候选人的答法差在哪。
scenario_en: For the same video-rec question, how do L4, L5, and Staff+ answers differ.
q: 区分 Staff+ 与更初级答案的核心是什么？
q_en: What core thing separates a Staff+ answer from more junior ones?
why: Staff+ 的差异不是「知道更多事实」，而是能跨整个生命周期(训练→服务→评估→迭代)做取舍推理：把系统框成持续校准回路，讲相食缓解、embedding 表分布、评估里的公平监控。L4 只认出两阶段+基本指标。
why_en: The Staff+ differentiator is not knowing more facts but reasoning about trade-offs across the whole lifecycle (training, serving, evaluation, iteration) and framing the system as a continuous calibration loop.
tradeoff: Staff+ 全生命周期取舍推理 vs L4 罗列组件与指标
options: 背下更多算法名词和公式细节
能跨训练/服务/评估/迭代全生命周期做取舍推理，把系统框成持续校准回路
把两阶段流水线和 NDCG/Recall 名字说全就够
画出最复杂的架构图，组件越多越好
options_en: Memorizing more algorithm names and formula details.
Reasoning about trade-offs across the full training/serving/evaluation/iteration lifecycle, framing the system as a continuous calibration loop.
Just naming the two-stage pipeline and NDCG/Recall.
Drawing the most complex architecture with as many components as possible.
optionExplanations: 多背名词是知识堆砌，Staff+ 看的是判断和取舍，不是词汇量。
对；全生命周期的取舍推理 + 持续校准框架，才是 Staff+ 的分水岭。
认出两阶段和基本指标是 L4 层次，还谈不上取舍深度。
组件堆得多不等于想得深，复杂度不是信号，取舍才是。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing terms is knowledge stacking; Staff+ is judged on judgment and trade-offs, not vocabulary.
Correct — full-lifecycle trade-off reasoning plus a continuous-calibration framing is the Staff+ divide.
Naming the two stages and basic metrics is the L4 level, not yet trade-off depth.
More components is not deeper thinking; complexity is not the signal, trade-offs are.

termDefinitions.term: continuous calibration loop / 持续校准回路
termDefinitions.meaning: 把推荐系统当作永远在调、never done 的反馈优化过程，而非一次性交付。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A continuous calibration loop treats the recommender as never-done, always being retuned rather than a one-off delivery.

category: Video Recommendation Evaluation Serving Trade Offs

scenario: 面试题「给 LinkedIn/Facebook 设计 feed 排序」，它和纯视频/内容推荐共享排序原理，但多了几个独有维度。
scenario_en: The prompt 'design feed ranking for LinkedIn/Facebook' shares ranking principles with pure content rec but adds several unique dimensions.
q: 社交 feed 排序相比纯内容推荐，独有的三个新维度是什么？
q_en: What three dimensions does social feed ranking add beyond pure content recommendation?
why: 社交 feed 多了：社交图谱(纯内容推荐没有的关系信号)、以小时计的新鲜度(不是天)、异构内容(文本/图片/转发/投票/插播广告)争夺同一个视口。这三点决定了它的数据、延迟和建模都不同。
why_en: Social feed adds a social graph (relationship signals absent in content rec), freshness in hours not days, and heterogeneous content (text/images/reshares/polls/ads) competing for one viewport.
diagram:
flowchart TB F["社交 feed 排序"] --> G["社交图谱
关系信号"] F --> H["小时级新鲜度
near-real-time"] F --> C["异构内容
争一个视口"]
options: 更大的模型、更多的 GPU、更长的训练时间
更高的分辨率、更好的编码、更快的 CDN
社交图谱关系信号、小时级新鲜度、异构内容争夺同一视口
更多的广告位、更高的出价、更精的定向
options_en: A bigger model, more GPUs, longer training.
Higher resolution, better encoding, faster CDN.
Social-graph relationship signals, hour-scale freshness, heterogeneous content competing for one viewport.
More ad slots, higher bids, tighter targeting.
optionExplanations: 模型大小/算力是通用工程量，不是社交 feed 相对内容推荐的独有维度。
分辨率/编码/CDN 是视频分发问题，与社交 feed 的关系信号无关。
对；关系图谱、小时级新鲜、异构内容争视口正是社交 feed 的三个独有维度。
广告是可显式划为范围外的子问题，不是 feed 排序的独有新维度。
optionExplanations_en: Model size/compute is generic engineering, not a dimension unique to social feed vs content rec.
Resolution/encoding/CDN is a video-delivery concern, unrelated to social feed's relationship signals.
Correct — the relationship graph, hour-scale freshness, and heterogeneous content competing for one viewport are social feed's three unique dimensions.
Ads are a sub-problem you can explicitly scope out, not a unique new dimension of feed ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录用户之间关注/好友/互动关系的图，是 feed 排序独有的高信息量信号源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A social graph records follow/friend/interaction relationships between users, a high-signal source unique to feed ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户屏幕上一次能看到的内容区域，各种异构内容都要争这块位置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The viewport is the content area visible on screen at once, which all heterogeneous content competes to occupy.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 面试开场要先讲清 feed 排序在优化哪些业务目标。
scenario_en: Opening the interview, you must state which business objectives feed ranking optimizes.
q: 社交 feed 排序的三个核心业务指标是哪些？(多选)
q_en: What are the three core business metrics of social feed ranking? (multiple)
why: 三大业务指标是参与度、有意义连接、创作者公平——它们互相拉扯，应先全摆出来再问面试官优先哪个，这是产品成熟度的信号。
why_en: The three are engagement, meaningful connections, and creator equity; they pull against each other, so state all three then ask which to prioritize.
options: 参与度(engagement)：会话时长、点击、评论、转发
有意义的连接(meaningful connections)：回复、私信、熟人间评论串
创作者公平(creator equity)：跨粉丝层级的公平曝光份额
CDN 缓存命中率：静态资源分发效率
options_en: Engagement: session time, clicks, comments, reshares.
Meaningful connections: replies, DMs, comment threads between mutuals.
Creator equity: fair impression share across follower tiers.
CDN cache hit rate: static-asset delivery efficiency.
optionExplanations: 对；参与度最可测，是默认优化目标，但过头会放大标题党。
对；有意义连接关联长期留存，是 FB 2018 年重心转移的目标。
对；创作者公平保证内容供给侧不至于赢家通吃，是双边市场的一极。
错；这是纯运维指标，跟参与度/连接/公平这三个业务目标不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — engagement is most measurable and the default target, but over-doing it amplifies clickbait.
Correct — meaningful connections correlate with long-term retention, the target of Facebook's 2018 pivot.
Correct — creator equity keeps the supply side from winner-take-all, one pole of the two-sided market.
Wrong — that is a pure ops metric, not one of the three business objectives (engagement/connections/equity).

termDefinitions.meaning: 让不同粉丝量级的创作者获得公平曝光份额，避免赢家通吃、供给枯竭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator equity gives creators of different follower tiers a fair impression share, avoiding winner-take-all and supply starvation.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 参与度是最可测、最常被当默认优化目标的业务指标。
scenario_en: Engagement is the most measurable business metric and the default optimization target.
q: 参与度常用什么 ML 代理目标，主要风险是什么？
q_en: What ML proxy objective does engagement use, and what is its main risk?
why: 参与度用 P(click) 或 E[dwell time](停留时长)当代理，它最可测、直接关联广告收入和黏性。但纯追它会放大标题党，把煽动/浅层内容顶上来，侵蚀更深层的连接。
why_en: Engagement proxies as P(click) or E[dwell time]—most measurable, tied to ad revenue and stickiness—but chasing it amplifies clickbait, surfacing sensational shallow content.
options: 代理目标是 P(click)/E[dwell time]，风险是放大标题党/煽动内容
代理目标是曝光公平约束，风险是短期参与度下降
代理目标是 P(meaningful interaction)，风险是标签稀疏难测
代理目标是 CDN 命中率，风险是缓存失效
options_en: Proxy is P(click)/E[dwell time]; the risk is amplifying clickbait/sensational content.
Proxy is an exposure-fairness constraint; the risk is lower short-term engagement.
Proxy is P(meaningful interaction); the risk is sparse, hard-to-measure labels.
Proxy is CDN hit rate; the risk is cache invalidation.
optionExplanations: 对；参与度最可测，代理是 P(click)/E[dwell]，代价是易被标题党套利。
曝光公平约束是创作者公平的代理，不是参与度的。
P(meaningful interaction) 是有意义连接的代理，标签稀疏是它的风险，非参与度。
CDN 命中率是基础设施指标，不是参与度的 ML 代理。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — engagement is most measurable, proxied by P(click)/E[dwell], at the cost of clickbait arbitrage.
An exposure-fairness constraint is the proxy for creator equity, not engagement.
P(meaningful interaction) is the meaningful-connections proxy, with sparse labels as its risk, not engagement's.
CDN hit rate is an infrastructure metric, not an ML proxy for engagement.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在一条内容上停留的时间，是参与度的常用代理信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dwell time is how long a user lingers on a piece of content, a common engagement proxy.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 参与度和有意义的连接是两个不同的业务目标，可测性和风险都不一样。
scenario_en: Engagement and meaningful connections are two different objectives with different measurability and risks.
q: 参与度和「有意义的连接」在可测性与风险上如何对比？
q_en: How do engagement and meaningful connections contrast on measurability and risk?
why: 参与度最可测(点击/停留)、风险是标题党；有意义连接(回复/私信/评论串)关联长期留存但标签稀疏、难测。前者好优化易走偏，后者难测却更保长期，两者常反向拉扯。
why_en: Engagement is highly measurable (clicks/dwell) but risks clickbait; meaningful connections (replies/DMs/threads) correlate with long-term retention but have sparse, hard-to-measure labels, and they pull against each other.
tradeoff: 参与度(好测·易被标题党套利) vs 有意义连接(难测·更护长期留存)
options: 两者的可测性和风险其实完全一样，只是换了个说法而已
说反了：其实有意义连接才最好测，参与度反而是难测的那个
参与度其实是靠曝光公平约束来衡量的，有意义连接反而靠点击衡量
参与度好测但易被标题党套利；有意义连接难测但更护长期留存
options_en: Both are equally measurable with identical risk, just described using different names.
It's backwards: meaningful connections are actually the most measurable, and engagement is the hard one.
Engagement is actually measured by an exposure-fairness constraint, while meaningful connections are measured by clicks.
Engagement is measurable but clickbait-prone; meaningful connections are hard to measure but protect long-term retention.
optionExplanations: 两者可测性和风险明显不同，不是同物换名。
说反了：参与度最好测，有意义连接标签稀疏最难测。
代理搞混了：曝光公平是创作者公平的代理，点击是参与度的代理。
对；这条对比正是产品要权衡的核心——好测的易走偏，难测的更护长期。
optionExplanations_en: Their measurability and risk clearly differ; not the same thing renamed.
Backwards: engagement is most measurable while meaningful connections have sparse labels and are hardest to measure.
Proxies mixed up: exposure fairness proxies creator equity, and clicks proxy engagement.
Correct — this contrast is the core product trade-off: the measurable one drifts, the hard one protects the long term.

termDefinitions.term: meaningful connections / 有意义的连接
termDefinitions.meaning: 由内容触发的回复、私信、熟人间评论串，关联长期留存但标签稀疏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Meaningful connections are content-triggered replies, DMs, and threads between mutuals, tied to long-term retention but sparsely labeled.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: Facebook 2018 年做过一次著名的排序重心调整。
scenario_en: Facebook made a famous ranking re-weighting in 2018.
q: Facebook 2018 年的「meaningful social interactions」调整改了什么？
q_en: What did Facebook's 2018 'meaningful social interactions' shift change?
why: 它把排序权重从「原始参与度」重新分配到「有意义的社交互动」——更看重评论串深度、熟人回复，而非被动点赞/浏览。目的是保长期留存，代价是可能压低短期参与量。
why_en: It re-weighted ranking from raw engagement toward meaningful social interactions—favoring comment-thread depth and replies between mutuals over passive likes—to protect long-term retention.
options: 把整个排序逻辑完全交给广告竞价系统，价高者直接置顶
从原始参与度重新加权到有意义社交互动，护长期留存
取消所有个性化，改成纯粹按时间倒序排列的 feed
只保留视频内容，把文本和图片帖全部下线
options_en: Handed the entire ranking logic to an ad-auction system, pinning the highest bidder.
Re-weighted from raw engagement toward meaningful social interactions, protecting long-term retention.
Removed all personalization and switched to a purely reverse-chronological feed.
Kept only video content and retired all text and image posts.
optionExplanations: MSI 调整是重排业务目标，不是把 feed 交给广告出价。
对；核心是把权重从被动参与移到有意义互动，赌的是长期留存而非短期量。
MSI 不是取消个性化，反而是更精细地重排目标权重。
MSI 与内容类型下线无关，改的是目标权重不是内容池。
optionExplanations_en: The MSI shift re-weighted business objectives, not handed the feed to ad bids.
Correct — the core was moving weight from passive engagement to meaningful interaction, betting on long-term retention over short-term volume.
MSI did not remove personalization; it re-weighted objectives more finely.
MSI has nothing to do with retiring content types; it changed objective weights, not the content pool.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facebook 2018 排序重心：更看重评论串深度与熟人回复，而非被动点赞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSI (Meaningful Social Interactions) is Facebook's 2018 ranking focus favoring thread depth and replies between mutuals over passive likes.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 如果只按参与度排序、完全不管创作者曝光是否公平。
scenario_en: If you rank purely by engagement and ignore whether creator exposure is fair.
q: 缺少创作者公平会让 feed 生态出什么问题？
q_en: What happens to the feed ecosystem without creator equity?
why: 没有公平约束，曝光会向头部集中形成赢家通吃：小创作者拿不到曝光→内容供给侧枯竭→多样性下降。创作者是双边市场的供给侧，饿死供给会反噬整个平台。
why_en: Without a fairness constraint, exposure concentrates into winner-take-all: small creators starve of impressions, the supply side dries up, and diversity degrades.
options: 曝光向头部集中、赢家通吃，小创作者供给枯竭、多样性下降
所有创作者的曝光会自动变得均等，完全不需要任何人为干预
只会影响广告收入，跟内容供给侧完全没有关系
短期和长期指标会同时一起上升，完全没有任何代价
options_en: Exposure concentrates into winner-take-all, starving small creators and degrading supply and diversity.
All creators' exposure automatically becomes equal, with no human intervention needed at all.
It would only affect ad revenue, with no relationship to the content supply side at all.
Short- and long-term metrics would rise together all at once, with no cost whatsoever.
optionExplanations: 对；纯参与度排序自我强化头部，饿死供给侧，是双边市场的核心风险。
自动均等是幻想：参与度排序天然向头部集中，不干预只会更不均。
供给侧枯竭直接减少可推内容和多样性，不只是广告问题。
赢家通吃短期或许好看，长期供给枯竭会反噬，绝非没有代价。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — pure engagement ranking self-reinforces the top and starves the supply side, the core two-sided-market risk.
Automatic equality is fantasy: engagement ranking naturally concentrates at the top, and no intervention worsens it.
Supply starvation directly reduces recommendable content and diversity, not just ad revenue.
Winner-take-all may look fine short-term, but long-term supply starvation bites back—hardly costless.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时服务消费者(看)和创作者(供给)的平台，供给侧枯竭会拖垮整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-sided market serves both consumers (viewers) and creators (supply); starving the supply side drags the whole platform down.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 面试开场,你识别出参与度、有意义连接、创作者公平三个目标彼此拉扯,但不知道该主推哪个。
scenario_en: Opening the interview, you spot that engagement, meaningful connections, and creator equity pull against each other but don't know which to prioritize.
q: 面对三个互相冲突的目标,开场该怎么处理?
q_en: Facing three conflicting objectives, how should you handle the opening?
why: 先把三个目标都点出来、说清它们互相拉扯,再显式问面试官优先哪个——真实系统就是要做刻意的取舍。默认闷头只优化参与度会显得没有产品思维。
why_en: State all three objectives and their tension explicitly, then ask the interviewer which to prioritize, because real systems make deliberate trade-offs.
tradeoff: 先陈述三目标再问优先级(显产品成熟) vs 默认只优化参与度(缺取舍视角)
options: 直接默认优先优化参与度,因为它最可测,完全不必多问
自己随便挑一个目标就闷头去做,做完了才说
彻底回避目标冲突,只谈技术架构、绝口不提业务权衡
把三个目标都陈述清楚、点明它们互相拉扯,再问面试官优先哪个
