options_en: Default straight to prioritizing engagement since it's most measurable, no need to ask at all.
Pick one objective arbitrarily and build heads-down, only mentioning it once it's done.
Thoroughly avoid the objective conflict and discuss only technical architecture, never the business trade-offs.
State all three objectives, point out their tension, then ask the interviewer which to prioritize.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官已在题面明确指定主目标(如「就最大化参与度」),则不必再问,直接据此展开设计更高效。
optionExplanations: 默认参与度会错过面试官想考的取舍,也暴露缺产品视角。
随便挑一个不沟通,可能整道题都朝错误优先级做。
回避业务权衡恰恰丢掉了这道题最核心的考点。
对;陈述三目标+主动问优先级,是展示产品成熟度的标准开场。
optionExplanations_en: Defaulting to engagement misses the trade-off the interviewer wants and shows a lack of product view.
Picking one without communicating risks building the whole answer on the wrong priority.
Avoiding the business trade-off drops the very thing this question tests.
Correct — stating the three and asking the priority is the standard opening that signals product maturity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在多个互相冲突的业务目标里,和干系人确认先优化哪个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Objective prioritization is confirming with stakeholders which of several conflicting business goals to optimize first.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 监控发现:每日参与度持续上升,但 30 天留存却在下降。
scenario_en: Monitoring shows daily engagement rising while 30-day retention declines.
q: 「日参与涨、30 天留存跌」最可能说明什么?
q_en: What does 'daily engagement up but 30-day retention down' most likely indicate?
why: 这是在以有意义互动为代价换取浅层参与:排序顶起了能骗即时点击/停留但让人后悔的内容,短期数字好看、长期用户慢慢流失。信号就是短期参与与长期留存背离。
why_en: It signals optimizing for shallow engagement at the expense of meaningful interactions—content that farms immediate clicks but erodes long-term retention.
options: 这是模型欠拟合的表现,应该加大模型继续堆参与度
在以有意义互动为代价换取浅层参与,短期数字好但长期留存被侵蚀
这纯属随机噪声波动,不用理会,过阵子自己会恢复
说明创作者公平约束做得太强,压低了整体参与度
options_en: It shows the model underfitting; scale it up and keep piling on engagement.
It trades meaningful interaction for shallow engagement—good short-term numbers but eroding long-term retention.
This is pure random noise; ignore it, it will recover on its own after a while.
It means the creator-equity constraint is too strong and is suppressing overall engagement.
optionExplanations: 加大模型继续堆参与度只会加剧浅层化,方向反了。
对;短期参与与长期留存背离,是浅层参与蚕食有意义互动的典型信号。
30 天留存持续下降不是噪声,是系统性趋势,必须响应。
留存下降的锅在浅层参与,不是创作者公平;后者一般压的是短期参与不是留存。
optionExplanations_en: Scaling up to pile on engagement worsens shallowness—the wrong direction.
Correct — short-term engagement diverging from long-term retention is the classic sign of shallow engagement cannibalizing meaningful interaction.
A sustained 30-day retention decline is not noise but a systematic trend that must be addressed.
The retention drop is on shallow engagement, not creator equity, which typically suppresses short-term engagement rather than retention.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户在 30 天窗口内是否仍活跃,是长期健康的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 30-day retention is whether users remain active within a 30-day window, a core long-term health metric.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 约 20 亿日活,每次刷新要从好友/群组/主页/广告里汇聚几百到几千条候选帖。
scenario_en: About 2B DAU; each refresh must assemble hundreds to thousands of candidate posts from friends/groups/pages/ads.
q: feed 排序里的「fan-out 问题」指的是什么?
q_en: What is the 'fan-out problem' in feed ranking?
why: fan-out 问题是:一条帖子要分发到大量关注者的 feed、或一次刷新要从大量来源汇聚候选,在 20 亿日活规模下,分发/汇聚的存储与计算成本爆炸,必须选 fan-out on write / read / 混合策略。
why_en: The fan-out problem is distributing a post to many followers' feeds (or assembling candidates from many sources) at 2B-DAU scale, where the write/read cost explodes and forces a fan-out-on-write/read/hybrid choice.
diagram:
flowchart LR P["一条新帖"] --> W{"如何送达
关注者 feed?"} W -->|写时分发| A["预推进每个粉丝 feed"] W -->|读时汇聚| B["请求时拉取合并"]
options: 模型 fan-out 太多导致过拟合的正则问题
一条帖要分发到大量关注者、或一次刷新要汇聚大量来源,规模下存储/计算成本爆炸
GPU 显存不足导致 batch 无法 fan-out 的硬件问题
CDN 边缘节点无法 fan-out 静态资源的分发问题
options_en: A regularization problem where the model fans out too much and overfits.
Distributing one post to many followers (or assembling many sources per refresh), where storage/compute cost explodes at scale.
A hardware problem where GPU memory is too small to fan out the batch.
A delivery problem where CDN edge nodes cannot fan out static assets.
optionExplanations: fan-out 不是模型正则概念,而是 feed 分发/汇聚的系统扩展问题。
对;核心是海量关注者/来源下的分发与汇聚成本,决定写扩散还是读扩散。
不是 GPU 显存问题,是 feed 存储/计算的扩展权衡。
不是 CDN 静态分发,而是社交关系图上的 feed 分发。
optionExplanations_en: Fan-out is not a model-regularization concept but a systems-scaling problem of feed distribution/assembly.
Correct — the core is distribution and assembly cost under massive followers/sources, deciding write vs read fan-out.
Not a GPU memory issue but a feed storage/compute scaling trade-off.
Not CDN static delivery but feed distribution over the social graph.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一条帖子分发到众多关注者 feed(写扩散)或请求时从众多来源汇聚(读扩散)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out is distributing a post to many followers' feeds (on write) or assembling from many sources at request time (on read).

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数,这里约 20 亿,是估算分发/汇聚规模的基数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU (Daily Active Users), here ~2 billion, is the base for sizing distribution/assembly scale.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 普通用户粉丝不多、写帖不频繁,但读 feed 要极低延迟。
scenario_en: An ordinary user has few followers and posts infrequently, but reading the feed needs very low latency.
q: 对普通用户,fan-out on write 为什么合适,代价是什么?
q_en: For ordinary users, why does fan-out on write fit, and at what cost?
why: 写扩散在发帖时就把帖子预推进每个关注者的 feed 存储,读 feed 时直接取、延迟极低。代价是存储放大+写放大;粉丝越多写扩散越贵,到百万粉就是「名人问题」。普通用户粉丝少,写扩散划算。
why_en: Fan-out on write pre-pushes a post into every follower's feed store at creation, so reads are ultra-low-latency; the cost is storage and write amplification, which explodes for millions of followers (the celebrity problem), so it fits low-follower ordinary users.
tradeoff: 写扩散(读快·但写/存放大) vs 读扩散(省写·但读时现算慢)
options: 发帖时预推进关注者 feed,读快;代价是存储写放大,粉丝越多越贵
请求时才现场从各个来源拉取全部数据现算,代价是读延迟明显变得很高
完全不做任何预计算,只靠一层缓存兜底,代价是容易出现缓存穿透问题
把帖子只存在作者本地节点上,代价是所有关注者都读不到这条帖
options_en: Pre-push into each follower's feed at post time, fast reads; the cost is storage/write amplification that grows with follower count.
Assemble and rank on the fly at request time by pulling from every source live; the cost is noticeably higher read latency.
Do no precomputation at all and rely purely on one cache layer; the cost is a higher chance of cache-penetration issues.
Store the post only on the author's local node; the cost is that every follower ends up completely unable to read it.
whenOtherWins: 当账号粉丝到百万级(名人),写扩散的存储/写放大变得不可承受,该改用 fan-out on read 请求时汇聚。
optionExplanations: 对;写扩散把成本前置到写路径换极快读,普通用户粉丝少写放大可控,划算。
请求时现拉是 fan-out on read 的特征,不是写扩散。
不预计算靠缓存不是写扩散的定义;写扩散恰恰是主动预推。
只存作者本地根本没做扩散,关注者读不到帖,不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — fan-out on write front-loads cost to the write path for very fast reads; ordinary users' low follower count keeps write amplification manageable.
On-the-fly assembly is fan-out on read's trait, not write.
Relying on cache without precompute is not the write-fan-out definition; write fan-out actively pre-pushes.
Storing only on the author's node does no fan-out at all, so followers cannot read—invalid.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发帖时就把内容推进每个关注者的 feed 存储,读时直接取,读快但写/存放大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on write pushes a post into every follower's feed store at creation, making reads fast but amplifying writes/storage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次写操作触发大量下游写(推进百万粉丝 feed),放大写成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is one write triggering many downstream writes (into millions of feeds), inflating write cost.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 某名人账号有上千万粉丝,一条帖若写扩散要推进上千万个 feed。
scenario_en: A celebrity account has tens of millions of followers; a single post would push into tens of millions of feeds under write fan-out.
q: 对超高粉丝账号,为什么 fan-out on read 更合适,代价是什么?
q_en: For very high-follower accounts, why does fan-out on read fit better, and at what cost?
why: 读扩散不预推,请求时才把该名人的帖拉进候选池合并,避免了写扩散推进千万 feed 的爆炸写放大。代价是读路径要在紧预算内实时汇聚+排序,对低延迟推理要求高。
why_en: Fan-out on read does not pre-push; it pulls the celebrity's posts into the candidate pool at request time, avoiding the explosive write amplification, at the cost of needing low-latency assembly and ranking on the read path.
tradeoff: 读扩散(避免名人写爆炸·但读时现算) vs 写扩散(读快·但名人写放大爆炸)
options: 预先推进上千万个粉丝的 feed 存储里,代价只是读的时候会很快
直接把名人发的帖子全部删掉不推,代价是粉丝完全看不到内容
只给名人单独建一个独立的数据库,代价是这样反而无法排序
请求时才把名人帖拉进候选池合并,避免写爆炸;代价是读路径要低延迟实时汇聚
options_en: Pre-push into tens of millions of follower feed stores ahead of time; the only cost is that reads become fast.
Directly delete all of the celebrity's posts and never push them; the cost is followers can't see any content.
Give the celebrity their own separate database; the cost is that this actually makes ranking impossible.
Pull the celebrity's posts into the candidate pool at request time, avoiding the write explosion; the cost is low-latency real-time assembly.
whenOtherWins: 对粉丝很少的普通账号,读扩散每次现拉反而浪费,写扩散预推、读时直接取更省更快。
optionExplanations: 预推千万 feed 正是要避免的写爆炸,是写扩散不是读扩散。
删帖不推是放弃分发,不是读扩散策略。
独立库不解决扩散问题,也不是「无法排序」;偷换概念。
对;读扩散把名人帖延后到请求时汇聚,避开写放大,代价是读路径实时算的延迟压力。
optionExplanations_en: Pre-pushing millions of feeds is exactly the write explosion to avoid—that's write fan-out, not read.
Deleting posts is abandoning distribution, not a read-fan-out strategy.
A separate DB does not solve fan-out and does not make ranking impossible; a bait-and-switch.
Correct — read fan-out defers celebrity posts to request-time assembly, dodging write amplification at the cost of real-time read-path latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不预推,请求时才把关注对象的帖拉进候选池合并排序,省写但读时现算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fan-out on read skips pre-pushing and assembles a follower's posts into the candidate pool at request time, saving writes but computing on reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 超高粉丝账号发帖若写扩散,要推进千万级 feed,写放大不可承受。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The celebrity problem is that a very-high-follower account's post under write fan-out must push into millions of feeds, an unbearable write amplification.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 既有海量普通用户(粉丝少),也有少数百万粉名人,单一 fan-out 策略两头不讨好。
scenario_en: There are many ordinary users (few followers) and a few million-follower celebrities; a single fan-out strategy serves neither well.
q: 生产系统怎么用混合 fan-out 兼顾两类账号?
q_en: How does production use hybrid fan-out to serve both account types?
why: 混合:普通用户走写扩散(读快、写放大可控);高粉丝名人走读扩散(避免写爆炸),请求时拉进候选池合并。中间放一层 feed cache 缓存已排好的结果,减少重复排序调用。
why_en: Hybrid: ordinary users fan out on write (fast reads, manageable amplification); high-follower accounts fan out on read (avoid the write explosion), merged into the candidate pool at request time, with a feed cache in between to cut redundant ranking.
tradeoff: 混合(按账号类型分策略·最优但更复杂) vs 单一策略(简单但对另一类账号失灵)
options: 所有账号不分类型统统写扩散,连名人也要预推进千万级 feed
所有账号不分类型统统读扩散,普通用户也得请求时才现算
普通用户走写扩散、名人走读扩散,请求时合并,加 cache 减少重复排序
随机给每个账号分配写扩散或读扩散,单纯只是想借此均摊负载
options_en: Fan out on write for every account regardless of type, pre-pushing even celebrities into tens of millions of feeds.
Fan out on read for every account regardless of type, forcing ordinary users to compute on the fly too.
Write fan-out for ordinary users, read fan-out for celebrities, merged at request time, with a cache layer cutting redundant ranking.
Randomly assign write fan-out or read fan-out to each account, purely hoping to spread the load that way.
whenOtherWins: 若平台没有名人级账号(粉丝分布均匀且都不大),纯写扩散更简单,不必上混合的复杂度。
optionExplanations: 全写扩散在名人处触发写爆炸,正是混合要规避的。
全读扩散让普通用户每次读都现算,浪费本可预推的低延迟。
对;按账号类型分策略是生产标准解,feed cache 再砍掉重复排序开销。
随机分配无视账号粉丝规模,既不省名人写也不快普通读,没有依据。
optionExplanations_en: All-write triggers the write explosion at celebrities, exactly what hybrid avoids.
All-read makes ordinary users compute on every read, wasting the low latency a pre-push would give.
Correct — splitting strategy by account type is the production standard, and a feed cache further cuts redundant ranking.
Random assignment ignores follower scale, saving neither celebrity writes nor speeding ordinary reads—unfounded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 普通用户写扩散、高粉丝账号读扩散,请求时合并,兼顾读延迟与写成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid fan-out uses write for ordinary users and read for high-follower accounts, merged at request time, balancing read latency and write cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选池与最终 feed 之间的缓存层,存已排好的结果,减少重复排序调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feed cache sits between the candidate pool and served feed, holding ranked results to cut redundant ranking calls.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: feed 内容的半衰期以小时计,一条 12 小时前的帖子可能已经过时。
scenario_en: Feed content has a half-life in hours; a 12-hour-old post may already be stale.
q: 小时级新鲜度这个硬约束,对系统架构提出了什么要求?
q_en: What does the hour-scale freshness hard constraint demand of the architecture?
why: 新鲜度是硬约束:feed 是近实时系统不是批处理。模型要有时间衰减信号;服务要有近实时特征更新——最近的互动计数必须是当前的,不能是几小时前批处理跑出来的旧值。
why_en: Freshness is a hard constraint making feed a near-real-time system, not batch: the model needs time-decay signals and serving needs near-real-time feature updates so recent engagement counts are current, not hours-old batch values.
tradeoff: 近实时特征(新鲜准确·但流式基础设施重) vs 纯批处理(简单·但特征滞后数小时)
options: feed 是近实时系统:要时间衰减信号+近实时特征更新,互动计数不能是几小时前的旧值
feed 其实是批处理系统:每天只需要跑一次特征就够,新鲜度问题靠离线慢慢补
只要把缓存 TTL 调大一些,让旧内容多留一会儿即可解决
新鲜度这件事只影响前端 UI 排版,完全不影响模型和特征
options_en: Feed is near-real-time: it needs time-decay signals plus near-real-time feature updates, and engagement counts cannot be hours-old.
Feed is actually a batch system: a daily feature run is enough, with freshness patched offline over time.
Just turn up the cache TTL a bit, keeping old content around longer, and that solves it.
Freshness only affects the front-end UI layout, and has no effect on the model or features at all.
whenOtherWins: 对更新极慢的特征(如社交图谱拓扑、用户长期画像),用每日批处理就够,不必上流式;只有快变的互动信号才需近实时。
optionExplanations: 对;小时级半衰期逼着整条链近实时,时间衰减+新鲜特征是硬要求。
批处理特征滞后数小时,会系统性错过正在爆发的内容,不满足新鲜度。
加大 TTL 是留住旧内容,恰恰和新鲜度背道而驰。
新鲜度直接决定模型特征时效,不只是 UI 排版。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — an hour-scale half-life forces the whole chain near-real-time; time-decay plus fresh features are hard requirements.
Batch features lag hours and systematically miss trending content, failing freshness.
Raising TTL keeps old content around, the opposite of freshness.
Freshness directly governs feature timeliness for the model, not just UI layout.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容的时效性,feed 半衰期以小时计,要求近实时特征与时间衰减信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Freshness is content timeliness; feed half-life is in hours, demanding near-real-time features and time-decay signals.

termDefinitions.term: time-decay signal / 时间衰减信号
termDefinitions.meaning: 让越新的内容得分越高、越旧越衰减的特征,兑现新鲜度约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A time-decay signal scores newer content higher and decays older content, honoring the freshness constraint.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 端到端 feed 延迟预算 <200ms,例:检索 ~50ms、排序 ~80ms、重排 ~40ms、feed cache TTL 失效 ~10ms。
scenario_en: End-to-end feed latency budget <200ms, e.g. retrieval ~50ms, ranking ~80ms, re-ranking ~40ms, feed cache TTL invalidation ~10ms.
q: <200ms 是什么性质的约束,超了会怎样?
q_en: What kind of constraint is <200ms, and what happens if you exceed it?
why: <200ms 是给定的产品目标(SLO),不是算出来的。它是检索+排序+重排各段之和的封顶,例值 50+80+40+10≈180ms;超预算会增加会话放弃(用户等不及就走)。所以每段延迟都要卡在预算内。
why_en: The <200ms is a given product SLO, not a computed value; it caps the sum of retrieval+ranking+re-ranking (e.g. 50+80+40+10≈180ms), and exceeding it raises session abandonment.
options: 它是衡量模型准确率高低的下限指标,跟延迟预算完全无关
它是限制离线训练时长的一个上限,和线上服务完全无关
它是给定的产品 SLO,是各段延迟之和的封顶;超了会增加会话放弃
它是限制缓存能存多大的一个上限,一旦超过就会直接 OOM
options_en: It measures a lower bound on model accuracy, entirely unrelated to the latency budget.
It is a ceiling limiting offline training time, entirely unrelated to online serving.
It is a given product SLO capping the sum of stage latencies; exceeding it raises session abandonment.
It is a ceiling limiting how large the cache can grow; exceeding it causes an immediate OOM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户因加载太慢而提前离开的比例,延迟超预算会推高它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session abandonment is the share of users who leave early due to slow loading, which rises when latency exceeds budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对延迟等指标设定的目标阈值,这里是端到端 <200ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a target threshold for a metric like latency, here end-to-end <200ms.

optionExplanations: 错；这是模型质量指标，跟延迟预算不是一回事，200ms 管的是响应快慢。
错；训练时长是离线成本，不受制于在线请求的这条 200ms 时钟。
对；<200ms 是产品给定的 SLO，把检索+排序+重排各段加起来封顶，超了用户等不及就走。
错；缓存大小超限是内存问题，跟一次请求要多快返回没关系。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — that describes model quality, not the latency budget; the 200ms clock is about response speed.
Wrong — training time is an offline cost, not bound by this per-request 200ms clock.
Correct — <200ms is a given product SLO capping the sum of retrieval+ranking+re-ranking; blow it and users abandon the session.
Wrong — running out of cache space is a memory issue, unrelated to how fast one request must return.
category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: Staff+ 面试想听你怎么框定整个 feed 系统的最高层视角。
scenario_en: A Staff+ interview wants to hear how you frame the whole feed system at the top level.
q: Staff+ 会把 feed 系统框成什么,并因此把什么当一等目标?
q_en: How does a Staff+ candidate frame the feed system, and what becomes a first-class objective?
why: 框成双边市场(消费者+创作者):不只优化看的人,还要维护创作者供给侧。因此创作者公平成为一等目标,配可度量的公平 SLO;还要考虑组织取舍(排序权重归 ML 还是产品团队)和二阶效应(参与农场)。
why_en: Frame it as a two-sided marketplace (consumers + creators), making creator equity a first-class objective with measurable fairness SLOs, plus org trade-offs and second-order effects.
tradeoff: 双边市场框架(护供给侧+公平 SLO) vs 单边消费者视角(只优化看的人·长期饿死供给)
options: 只框成一个纯消费者系统,一门心思只优化看的人的参与度指标
框成双边市场,创作者公平是一等目标,配可度量的公平 SLO
框成一个纯广告竞价的系统,谁出价最高谁就能拿到全部曝光
框成一个纯批处理的离线系统,彻底忽略掉所有实时性要求
options_en: Frame it purely as a consumer-only system, single-mindedly optimizing only viewers' engagement metric.
Frame it as a two-sided marketplace, with creator equity as a first-class objective and a measurable fairness SLO.
Frame it as a pure ad-auction system where the single highest bidder takes all the exposure.
Frame it as a purely batch offline system, completely ignoring every real-time requirement.
whenOtherWins: 若产品明确只做消费侧、内容全由自家 PGC 供给(没有第三方创作者生态),单边消费者框架就够,不必上双边市场。
optionExplanations: 只优化消费者会长期饿死创作者供给,缺了双边视角。
对;双边市场+创作者公平 SLO 是 Staff+ 的框架高度,兼顾供需两侧长期健康。
纯竞价忽略了内容质量和长期生态,不是 feed 排序的正确框架。
纯批处理违背 feed 的小时级新鲜度硬约束。
optionExplanations_en: Optimizing only consumers starves creator supply long-term, missing the two-sided view.
Correct — a two-sided marketplace plus creator-equity SLOs is the Staff+ framing altitude, balancing long-term health on both sides.
Pure auction ignores content quality and long-term ecosystem, not the right frame for feed ranking.
Pure batch violates feed's hour-scale freshness hard constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把创作者曝光公平设成可监控的目标阈值,越线告警,而非事后审计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A fairness SLO makes creator exposure fairness a monitored target threshold with alerts, not a post-hoc audit.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 排序若奖励浅层互动,创作者会学着迎合算法而非做好内容。
scenario_en: If ranking rewards shallow interactions, creators learn to game the algorithm rather than make good content.
q: 「参与农场(engagement-farming)」是什么二阶效应?
q_en: What second-order effect is 'engagement-farming'?
why: 参与农场是创作者为迎合排序而刻意制造浅层互动(比如「评论区扣 1」「点赞抽奖」)来刷曝光,内容质量反而下降。这是激励结构被排序目标带偏的二阶效应,Staff+ 要能预见。
why_en: Engagement-farming is creators deliberately manufacturing shallow interactions (e.g. 'comment 1 below', like-giveaways) to game exposure, degrading content quality—a second-order effect of misaligned incentives that Staff+ should anticipate.
options: 创作者主动提升内容质量以换取用户的自然互动,是一种正向效应
这是平台向第三方批量购买真实用户互动的一种商业模式
这只是一种给创作者按互动量发月薪的普通激励机制
创作者刻意制造浅层互动来刷曝光,内容质量下降,是激励被带偏的二阶效应
options_en: Creators actively improving content quality to earn users' organic interaction, a positive effect.
A business model where the platform bulk-buys real user interactions from a third party.
Just an ordinary incentive scheme that pays creators a monthly salary based on interaction volume.
Creators manufacturing shallow interactions to game exposure, degrading quality—a second-order effect of misaligned incentives.
optionExplanations: 参与农场是刷浅层互动的负向套利,不是提升质量的正向效应。
不是买互动的商业模式,而是创作者为迎合算法的行为扭曲。
和发工资无关,是激励结构导致的内容退化。
对;它是排序目标错配诱发的创作者套利行为,预见它是 Staff+ 的系统思维。
optionExplanations_en: Engagement-farming is negative arbitrage of shallow interactions, not a positive quality lift.
Not a model of buying interactions but a behavioral distortion by creators gaming the algorithm.
Nothing to do with salaries; it is content degradation driven by the incentive structure.
Correct — it is creator arbitrage induced by a misaligned ranking objective, and anticipating it is Staff+ systems thinking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 创作者刻意制造浅层互动(评论区扣1、点赞抽奖)迎合排序刷曝光,内容质量下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Engagement-farming is creators manufacturing shallow interactions to game ranking for exposure, at the cost of content quality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统改动引发参与者行为改变后产生的间接后果,常被忽视。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A second-order effect is an indirect consequence arising after participants change behavior in response to a system change.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: feed 排序题的前 5-8 分钟,要用一套开场把问题框清楚。
scenario_en: In the first 5-8 minutes of a feed-ranking question, frame the problem with a structured opener.
q: 把 feed 排序面试开场的 5 步排成推荐顺序:
q_en: Order the 5 steps of a feed-ranking interview opener:
steps: 澄清平台(LinkedIn 职场 / Facebook 社交 / Twitter 实时),内容与新鲜度不同
陈述业务目标(参与度/有意义连接/创作者公平),再问优先哪个
厘清规模数字(DAU、每日帖数、候选池大小、延迟预算)
点出 fan-out 取舍(普通写扩散、高粉读扩散,并解释为什么)
声明范围外(先排除广告排序、通知、搜索),防止范围蔓延
why: 开场顺序:先澄清平台(决定内容/新鲜度基调)→陈述业务目标并问优先级→厘清规模数字→点出 fan-out 取舍→声明范围外。这套顺序体现产品思维,也防止一上来就跳进架构细节。
why_en: Opener order: clarify the platform, state objectives and ask priority, scope the scale numbers, identify the fan-out trade-off, then declare out-of-scope—showing product thinking and avoiding jumping straight into architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面试中问题范围不断扩大导致答不完,靠开场声明范围外来控制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Scope creep is the problem expanding until you can't finish; declaring out-of-scope up front controls it.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 把「为什么用混合 fan-out」讲成一条需求到缓解的完整链路。
scenario_en: Explain 'why hybrid fan-out' as one requirement-to-mitigation chain.
q: 把混合 fan-out 的决策链排成正确顺序(需求→性质→选择→代价→缓解):
q_en: Order the hybrid fan-out decision chain (requirement → property → choice → cost → mitigation):
steps: 需求:20 亿日活,读 feed 要低延迟,同时有百万粉名人
关键性质:普通用户适合预推,名人预推会写爆炸
选择:普通用户写扩散、名人读扩散,请求时合并候选池
代价:两条路径+读时现算增加系统复杂度和读延迟
缓解:中间加 feed cache 缓存已排结果,减少重复排序调用
why: 链路:先摆需求(低延迟读+名人存在)→点出关键性质(名人写扩散会爆炸)→选混合(普通写、名人读、合并)→承认代价(双路径+读延迟)→给缓解(feed cache 砍重复排序)。这条链能一口气讲清取舍。
why_en: The chain: state the requirement (low-latency reads plus celebrities), name the property (celebrity write fan-out explodes), choose hybrid (write for ordinary, read for celebrities, merged), admit the cost (dual paths + read latency), and mitigate with a feed cache.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  N["需求: 低延迟读+名人"] --> P["名人写扩散会爆炸"]
  P --> C["混合: 普通写/名人读/合并"]
  C --> K["代价: 双路径+读延迟"]
  K --> M["缓解: feed cache"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次请求要排序的帖子集合,由写扩散预推的和读扩散现拉的合并而成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The candidate pool is the set of posts to rank for one request, merged from write-fanned-out and read-fanned-out sources.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 同一道 feed 排序题,L4、L5、Staff+ 的作答范围不同。
scenario_en: For the same feed-ranking question, L4, L5, and Staff+ scope their answers differently.
q: L5 相比 L4,在作答范围上主要多了什么?
q_en: What does an L5 answer add in scope over an L4 answer?
why: L4 澄清主目标、内容类型、基本规模,定 1-2 个 ML 目标即可,不要求 fan-out 策略。L5 要多目标取舍、论证混合 fan-out、定离线+在线指标、识别数据源。
why_en: L4 clarifies the primary objective, content types, basic scale, defines 1-2 ML objectives and acknowledges latency; L5 adds multi-objective trade-offs, a justified hybrid fan-out, offline+online metrics, and data sources.
tradeoff: L5 多目标取舍+fan-out 策略+指标体系 vs L4 单目标+基本规模+认识延迟
options: 只是把同样的内容讲得更快一点、口条更流利一点而已
多目标取舍、论证混合 fan-out、定离在线指标、找数据源
只是额外多画了一张看起来更复杂一点的架构图
只是额外多背了几个听起来很厉害的算法名词而已
options_en: Just delivering the same content a bit faster with a bit more fluent delivery.
Multi-objective trade-offs, a justified hybrid fan-out, offline+online metrics, and data sources.
Just drawing one extra architecture diagram that looks a bit more complex.
Just memorizing a few extra algorithm names that happen to sound impressive.
optionExplanations: 讲得快不是层级差异,内容深度和取舍才是。
对;L5 的增量正是取舍+fan-out 论证+指标体系+数据源,比 L4 的单目标更完整。
架构图复杂度不等于范围深度,取舍论证才是。
多背名词是知识堆砌,不是 L5 要求的取舍能力。
optionExplanations_en: Speaking faster is not the level difference; content depth and trade-offs are.
Correct — L5's increment is trade-offs plus a justified fan-out plus a metric system plus data sources, more complete than L4's single objective.
Diagram complexity is not scope depth; trade-off reasoning is.
Memorizing terms is knowledge stacking, not the trade-off ability L5 requires.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量排序模型区分正负样本能力的离线指标,越接近 1 越好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AUC (Area Under the ROC Curve) is an offline metric of how well a ranker separates positives from negatives, closer to 1 is better.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: feed 排序题很容易被广告排序、通知、搜索这些相邻子系统带偏,时间不够用。
scenario_en: A feed-ranking question easily drifts into ad ranking, notifications, and search, and you run out of time.
q: 开场为什么要显式声明范围外(广告排序/通知/搜索)?
q_en: Why explicitly declare out-of-scope (ad ranking/notifications/search) in the opening?
why: 显式声明「除非被要求,先不做广告排序、通知、搜索」是防止范围蔓延:把有限时间聚焦在核心 feed 排序上,而不是被相邻子系统拖散。这是主动的范围管理,不是回避。
why_en: Explicitly saying 'unless asked, exclude ad ranking, notifications, search' prevents scope creep, focusing limited time on core feed ranking rather than adjacent subsystems.
tradeoff: 显式声明范围外(聚焦核心·控时间) vs 不声明(被相邻子系统拖散·答不完)
options: 只是为了显得自己什么子系统都懂,借此炫耀一下知识面
因为这些相邻子系统在技术上根本没法实现,必须被排除掉
防止范围蔓延,把有限时间聚焦核心排序,不被相邻子系统拖散
因为面试官事先明确下令禁止提到广告排序这件事
options_en: Just to look like you know every adjacent subsystem, showing off breadth for its own sake.
Because these adjacent subsystems are technically impossible to build at all, so they must be excluded.
To prevent scope creep and focus limited time on core ranking, not get dragged into adjacent subsystems.
Because the interviewer explicitly ordered beforehand that ad ranking must never be mentioned.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官明确说「就想听你怎么把广告插进 feed」,那广告排序就进范围,不该再排除。
optionExplanations: 声明范围外是为聚焦不是炫耀;罗列子系统反而分散注意力。
这些子系统技术上完全可做,排除是时间取舍不是不可行。
对;主动声明范围外是控时间的范围管理,把火力集中在核心问题。
面试官没禁止;是你主动划范围以聚焦,必要时可被要求纳入。
optionExplanations_en: Declaring out-of-scope is for focus, not showing off; listing subsystems scatters attention.
These subsystems are entirely feasible; excluding them is a time trade-off, not infeasibility.
Correct — proactively declaring out-of-scope is time-managing scope control, concentrating fire on the core.
The interviewer does not forbid it; you scope proactively to focus, and it can be pulled in if requested.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开场主动排除相邻子系统(广告/通知/搜索),聚焦核心问题、控时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An out-of-scope declaration proactively excludes adjacent subsystems (ads/notifications/search) to focus on the core and manage time.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 把三个业务目标映射到可训练的 ML 代理目标。
scenario_en: Map the three business objectives to trainable ML proxy objectives.
q: 下列「业务目标 → ML 代理」的映射,哪些是对的?(多选)
q_en: Which 'business objective → ML proxy' mappings are correct? (multiple)
why: 参与度→P(click)/E[dwell];有意义连接→P(meaningful interaction);创作者公平→重排里的曝光公平约束。三者代理不同、可测性不同,不能用同一个信号糊弄。
why_en: Engagement→P(click)/E[dwell]; meaningful connections→P(meaningful interaction); creator equity→an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking—distinct proxies with distinct measurability.
options: 参与度 → P(click) / E[dwell time]
有意义连接 → P(meaningful interaction)
创作者公平 → 重排里的曝光公平约束
创作者公平 → 最大化 P(click)
options_en: Engagement → P(click) / E[dwell time].
Meaningful connections → P(meaningful interaction).
Creator equity → an exposure-fairness constraint in re-ranking.
Creator equity → maximize P(click).
optionExplanations: 对;点击/停留是参与度最直接的可测代理。
对;有意义互动概率专门刻画回复/私信/评论串这类深度连接。
对;创作者公平不是打分头而是重排里的约束,分配曝光份额。
错;最大化点击恰恰会向头部集中、伤害创作者公平,方向相反。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — clicks/dwell are engagement's most direct measurable proxy.
Correct — meaningful-interaction probability specifically captures deep connections like replies/DMs/threads.
Correct — creator equity is not a scoring head but a re-ranking constraint allocating impression share.
Wrong — maximizing clicks concentrates at the top and harms creator equity, the opposite direction.

termDefinitions.term: exposure-fairness constraint / 曝光公平约束
termDefinitions.meaning: 在重排阶段按目录占比等标准分配曝光份额,兑现创作者公平。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An exposure-fairness constraint allocates impression share by criteria like catalog share in re-ranking, realizing creator equity.

category: Social Feed Ranking Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 为社交 feed 排序设计特征,要先确定最有价值的数据源。
scenario_en: Designing features for social feed ranking, you must first identify the most valuable data sources.
q: 社交 feed 排序的三大数据支柱是什么,社交图谱为何既宝贵又敏感?
q_en: What are the three data pillars for social feed ranking, and why is the social graph both valuable and sensitive?
why: 三大支柱:图谱结构、互动历史、内容元数据。社交图谱编码人际关系,所以信息量极高、预测力极强;但同样因为编码真实关系,它天然隐私敏感,是价值与风险的同源。
why_en: The three pillars are graph structure, interaction history, and content metadata; the social graph encodes human relationships, making it extraordinarily predictive yet uniquely privacy-sensitive—value and risk from the same source.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  D["feed 数据支柱"] --> G["图谱结构"]
  D --> I["互动历史"]
  D --> C["内容元数据"]
  G -.编码人际关系.-> R["高信息量 & 高隐私风险"]
options: GPU、CPU、内存三种硬件资源
图谱结构、互动历史、内容元数据;图谱编码人际关系,信息量高但隐私敏感
视频、图片、文本是三种内容模态,不是三大数据支柱,也和隐私敏感无关
训练集、验证集、测试集三种数据划分
options_en: GPU, CPU, and memory as three hardware resources.
Graph structure, interaction history, content metadata; the graph encodes relationships, high-signal but privacy-sensitive.
Video, image, and text are three content modalities — not the three data pillars, and unrelated to privacy sensitivity.
Train, validation, and test splits of the data.
optionExplanations: 硬件资源不是特征数据源,答非所问。
对;三支柱是数据侧的骨架,而图谱的高价值与高敏感同根同源。
模态是内容元数据的一部分,不是三大支柱,也漏了图谱和互动。
数据划分是训练流程概念,不是特征数据源。
optionExplanations_en: Hardware resources are not feature data sources, off-topic.
Correct — the three pillars are the data-side skeleton, and the graph's high value and high sensitivity share one root.
Modalities are part of content metadata, not the three pillars, and this misses the graph and interactions.
Data splits are a training-process concept, not feature data sources.

termDefinitions.meaning: 帖子的属性:类型、媒体、文本长度、话题标签,在发帖时生成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Content metadata is a post's attributes—type, media, text length, hashtags—generated at post creation.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 初级候选人一上来就罗列几十个特征名,面试官想看的是数据战略。
scenario_en: A junior candidate lists dozens of feature names immediately, but the interviewer wants a data strategy.
q: L5+ 在讲特征前应该先做什么?
q_en: What should an L5+ candidate do before listing features?
why: 先把原始数据源映射到业务目标(哪个源服务参与度/有意义连接/创作者公平),再据此推导特征。直接罗列特征名没有战略,显不出为什么选这些、它们各服务什么目标。
why_en: First map raw data sources to business objectives (which source serves engagement/meaningful connections/creator equity), then derive features—listing feature names without that mapping shows no strategy.
tradeoff: 先映射源→目标再推特征(有战略) vs 直接罗列特征名(无战略·说不清为什么)
options: 先把模型架构定死,再倒推需要什么特征
先把原始数据源映射到业务目标,再据此推导特征
先随便列尽可能多的特征,越多越显专业
先选好特征存储的数据库,再谈特征本身
options_en: Fix the model architecture first, then back out what features are needed.
First map raw data sources to business objectives, then derive features accordingly.
List as many features as possible first—more looks more professional.
Pick the feature-store database first, then discuss features themselves.
whenOtherWins: 若面试官已明确锁定单一目标和数据源(例如「只用互动历史优化参与度」),可跳过全量映射,直接深入该源的特征。
optionExplanations: 先定架构再倒推特征本末倒置,数据战略应先于架构。
对;源→目标映射是数据战略的核心动作,让每个特征都有归属和理由。
罗列越多越显得没重点,反而暴露缺少战略。
先选数据库是实现细节,不是数据战略;战略先于存储选型。
optionExplanations_en: Fixing architecture then backing out features is backwards; data strategy precedes architecture.
Correct — source-to-objective mapping is the core data-strategy move, giving each feature a home and a reason.
Listing more shows less focus and exposes a lack of strategy.
Choosing a database first is an implementation detail; strategy precedes storage choice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在列特征前,先把数据源映射到业务目标,让特征选择有依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Data strategy maps data sources to business objectives before listing features, giving feature choices a rationale.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 社交图谱特征可以在不同粒度上抽取。
scenario_en: Social-graph features can be extracted at different granularities.
q: 社交图谱特征通常在哪些粒度上抽取?(多选)
q_en: At which granularities are social-graph features typically extracted? (multiple)
why: 三种粒度:节点(度数、关注/被关注比)、边(共同好友、连接时长)、邻域(共同社区、聚类系数)。它们从「这个人多活跃」「这两人多熟」到「他们所在社区多紧密」层层刻画关系。
why_en: Three granularities: node (degree, follower/following ratio), edge (mutual friends, time since connection), and neighborhood (shared community, clustering coefficient).
options: 节点级:度数、关注/被关注比
边级:共同好友数、连接建立时长
邻域级:共同社区、聚类系数
像素级:图片每个像素的 RGB 值
options_en: Node level: degree, follower/following ratio.
Edge level: mutual friends, time since connection.
Neighborhood level: shared community, clustering coefficient.
Pixel level: RGB values of each image pixel.
optionExplanations: 对;节点级刻画单个用户的图谱地位(多活跃、多受关注)。
对;边级刻画两个用户之间关系的强弱与历史。
对;邻域级刻画用户所在局部社区的结构紧密度。
错;像素 RGB 是图像内容特征,不属于社交图谱粒度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — node level captures a single user's graph standing (how active, how followed).
Correct — edge level captures the strength and history of a relationship between two users.
Correct — neighborhood level captures the structural tightness of a user's local community.
Wrong — pixel RGB is an image-content feature, not a social-graph granularity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量一个节点的邻居之间彼此也相连的紧密程度,反映社区结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The clustering coefficient measures how tightly a node's neighbors are also connected to each other, reflecting community structure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被关注数除以关注数,是节点级的图谱地位特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The follower/following ratio is followers divided by following, a node-level graph-standing feature.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 两个用户之间只有「是否好友」这个二元边太粗,想刻画关系强弱。
scenario_en: The binary 'are they friends' edge between two users is too coarse; you want relationship strength.
q: 互动历史怎么把二元的社交边变成连续的关系强度信号?
q_en: How does interaction history turn a binary social edge into a continuous relationship-strength signal?
why: 把每对「浏览者-发帖者」的点赞/评论/转发/私信/主页访问/故事浏览在 1d/7d/28d 滑动窗口上聚合。二元边(是否好友)因此变成随时间演化的连续强度,还能识别衰减中的关系(仍连着但不再互动→降权)。
why_en: Aggregate each viewer-poster pair's likes/comments/reshares/DMs/profile visits over 1d/7d/28d sliding windows, turning a binary edge into a time-evolving continuous strength and exposing decaying relationships.
options: 按 1d/7d/28d 窗口聚合互动,二元边变成随时间演化的连续强度
只记录两人是否曾经互动过这一件事,完全不看频率、时间与近因
把所有互动类型合并成一个总数,不分时间窗口
只用最近一次互动的时间戳,不做任何窗口聚合
options_en: Aggregate interactions over 1d/7d/28d sliding windows, turning the binary edge into a time-evolving continuous strength.
Record only whether the pair ever interacted once, ignoring frequency, time, and recency entirely.
Merge all interaction types into one total, with no time windows.
Use only the timestamp of the last interaction, with no windowed aggregation at all.
optionExplanations: 对;多窗口滑动聚合是把关系从「有无」升级成「多强、趋势如何」的关键。
只记有无又退回二元,丢掉了频率和近因,刻画不了强度。
合并成一个总数丢了时间维度,看不出关系在增强还是衰减。
只用最近时间戳丢了频率,单点信息不足以刻画关系强度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — multi-window sliding aggregation upgrades a relationship from 'exists' to 'how strong, trending which way'.
Recording only existence reverts to binary, dropping frequency and recency, so it can't capture strength.
Merging into one total loses the time dimension, hiding whether the relationship is strengthening or decaying.
Using only the last timestamp loses frequency; a single point is insufficient for relationship strength.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在固定时间跨度(1d/7d/28d)上聚合事件,随时间滚动更新的统计口径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sliding window aggregates events over a fixed span (1d/7d/28d), rolling forward as time advances.

termDefinitions.meaning: 由多窗口互动聚合得到的连续信号,替代二元好友边刻画亲疏。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relationship strength is a continuous signal from multi-window interaction aggregation, replacing the binary friend edge.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 一次评论和一次被动点赞、一条私信和一次转发,携带的关系信息量并不相同。
scenario_en: A comment vs a passive like, a DM vs a reshare—each carries different relationship information.
q: 构造互动特征时,不同互动类型该怎么处理?
q_en: How should different interaction types be handled when building interaction features?
why: 不能一视同仁:评论比被动点赞更强,私信比转发更亲密。应给不同互动类型显式加权,让模型知道深度互动携带更强的关系信号(这正是 FB MSI 看重评论串深度的思路)。
why_en: Don't weight them equally: a comment outweighs a passive like and a DM implies more intimacy than a reshare, so weight interaction types explicitly, as Facebook's MSI favored comment-thread depth.
tradeoff: 按互动深度显式加权(信号更准) vs 所有互动等权(简单但糊平强弱)
options: 所有互动类型等权求和,简单统一
只统计点赞,忽略评论和私信,因为点赞最多
随机给互动类型分配权重,增加多样性
按互动深度显式加权:评论>被动点赞、私信>转发
options_en: Sum all interaction types with equal weight for simplicity.
Count only likes and ignore comments and DMs, since likes are most frequent.
Assign random weights to interaction types to add variety.
Weight by interaction depth explicitly: comment > passive like, DM > reshare.
whenOtherWins: 若某产品的互动类型极单一(几乎只有点赞)或数据太稀疏撑不起分类型权重,等权聚合起步更稳,等信号够了再细分。
optionExplanations: 等权把强弱信号糊平,评论和点赞被当一回事,损失关系区分度。
只看点赞丢掉了最强的深度互动信号(评论/私信),明显欠采。
随机权重不可解释也不可优化,不是加权而是加噪。
对;按深度加权让深互动携带更强关系信号,是 MSI 式的正确做法。
optionExplanations_en: Equal weight smears strength signals, treating comments and likes alike and losing relationship discrimination.
Counting only likes drops the strongest deep-interaction signals (comments/DMs), clearly under-sampling.
Random weights are neither interpretable nor optimizable—adding noise, not weighting.
Correct — weighting by depth makes deep interactions carry stronger relationship signal, the MSI-style approach.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按互动深度(评论>点赞、私信>转发)给不同类型赋不同权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Interaction weighting assigns different weights by depth—comment > like, DM > reshare.

termDefinitions.meaning: Facebook 提出的排序目标,强调评论串深度等深度互动信号,而非被动点赞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MSI (Meaningful Social Interactions) is Facebook's ranking objective favoring deep-interaction signals like comment-thread depth over passive likes.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 要为数十亿条社交边各维护多窗口互动计数器。
scenario_en: You must maintain multi-window interaction counters for billions of social edges.
q: 给数十亿条边存互动计数器,会带来什么工程约束?
q_en: What engineering constraint arises from storing interaction counters for billions of edges?
why: 边数是数十亿量级,若每条边都长期保留全量事件,存储会爆。必须做聚合(只存窗口统计而非原始事件)+ TTL 过期(旧计数自动清理),把存储控制在可持续范围。
why_en: Billions of edges make storing raw events per edge explode, so you must aggregate (keep window stats, not raw events) and let old counters lapse via TTL to keep storage sustainable.
options: 边数很少,直接全量存原始事件即可,无需优化
只能为最近一条边保留计数器,其余边的历史事件全部丢弃
数十亿边直接存储会爆,需聚合窗口统计 + TTL 清理旧计数
计数器必须强一致,任何延迟都不可接受
options_en: Edges are few, so just store all raw events with no optimization.
Only the most recent edge can keep a counter; every other edge's history is discarded entirely.
Billions of edges would explode storage, so aggregate window stats plus TTL-based cleanup of old counters.
Counters must be strongly consistent; any delay is unacceptable.
optionExplanations: 数十亿边全量存原始事件正是会爆的做法,必须优化。
只存一条边是荒谬项,系统要为所有活跃边维护计数。
对;聚合+TTL 是把海量边计数控制在可持续存储的标准手段。
互动计数容忍最终一致(见后续卡),强一致是过度要求,反而拖慢。
optionExplanations_en: Storing raw events for billions of edges is exactly what explodes; it must be optimized.
Storing only one edge is absurd; the system must maintain counters for all active edges.
Correct — aggregation plus TTL is the standard way to keep massive edge counters within sustainable storage.
Interaction counts tolerate eventual consistency (see later card); strong consistency is over-engineering that slows things down.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给存储项设过期时间,到点自动清理,控制海量计数器的存储增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL (Time To Live) sets an expiry on stored items so old counters auto-purge, bounding storage growth.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 特征管线只用每 24 小时跑一次的批处理,一条帖子在创建 10 分钟后突然爆火。
scenario_en: The feature pipeline is batch-only, refreshing every 24h; a post goes viral 10 minutes after creation.
q: 只用日级批处理特征,这条刚爆火的帖会遇到什么失败模式?
q_en: With batch-only daily features, what failure mode hits this just-viral post?
why: 帖子的互动计数特征还停留在上次批处理跑出来的~0(创建才 10 分钟,没进批),模型据此系统性地把这条正在爆发的帖低排——恰好错过它最关键的分发窗口。所以快变信号必须走近实时流式。
why_en: Its engagement-count feature still reflects the last batch run's ~0 (only 10 min old, missed the batch), so the model systematically under-ranks the trending post during its critical distribution window.
options: 模型会正确识别爆火,因为批处理足够快
模型据~0 的旧计数把它系统性低排,错过关键分发窗口
帖子会被重复推给所有人,因为计数太高
陈旧计数只会拖慢存储层读写,不会波及排序结果的高低
options_en: The model correctly spots the viral post because batch is fast enough.
Using the stale ~0 count, the model systematically under-ranks it, missing the critical distribution window.
The post gets pushed to everyone repeatedly because the count is too high.
A stale count only slows storage reads/writes; it never spills over into ranking results.
optionExplanations: 24 小时批处理根本追不上 10 分钟的爆发,不可能及时识别。
对;旧计数~0 让模型低估这条帖,正好在它最该被分发时压住它。
计数还停在~0 不是过高,不会被重复狂推,方向反了。
特征陈旧直接决定排序低估,不只是存储问题。
optionExplanations_en: A 24h batch cannot keep up with a 10-minute burst and cannot spot it in time.
Correct — the stale ~0 count makes the model underestimate the post, suppressing it exactly when it should be distributed.
The count is still ~0, not too high, so it won't be over-pushed—the opposite direction.
Stale features directly cause ranking underestimation, not just a storage issue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一条帖子刚发布、最有传播潜力的短暂时段,错过就难再起量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The distribution window is the brief early period when a post has the most spread potential; missing it caps its reach.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 特征有的慢变(图谱拓扑、用户画像),有的快变(点赞数、评论速度、转发爆发),要用一套管线覆盖。
scenario_en: Some features change slowly (graph topology, user profiles), some fast (like counts, comment velocity, reshare bursts); one pipeline must cover both.
q: 怎么设计特征管线同时覆盖慢变和快变特征?
q_en: How do you design a feature pipeline covering both slow and fast features?
why: 双管线:批处理(Spark + Airflow,日级)算慢变特征(图谱拓扑、用户聚合);流式(Flink + Kafka,实时)算快变特征(点赞数、评论速度、转发爆发)。用哪条按特征的变化速度分,不是一刀切。
why_en: A dual pipeline: batch (Spark + Airflow, daily) for slow features (graph topology, user aggregates) and streaming (Flink + Kafka, real-time) for fast features (like counts, comment velocity, reshare bursts).
tradeoff: 双管线按变化速度分工(各取所长) vs 全批处理(简单但快变滞后)/全流式(实时但慢变浪费)
options: 全部用批处理日级跑,连快变的点赞评论计数也跟着每天才更新一次
全部用流式实时跑,连慢变的图谱拓扑和用户画像也跟着每秒重算
把所有原始特征一股脑塞给模型,寄望它自己慢慢学会区分时效,完全不做批流管线拆分
双管线:批处理(Spark+Airflow)算慢变,流式(Flink+Kafka)算快变
options_en: Run everything in daily batch, so even fast-changing like/comment counts only update once a day.
Run everything in streaming, recomputing even slow-changing graph topology and user profiles every second.
Dump all raw features into the model and hope it slowly learns timeliness on its own, with no batch/streaming split at all.
Dual pipeline: batch (Spark+Airflow) for slow features, streaming (Flink+Kafka) for fast ones.
whenOtherWins: 若产品所有关键特征都慢变(如纯静态画像推荐),纯批处理就够,不必上流式的运维复杂度。
optionExplanations: 全批处理让快变计数滞后一天,爆火帖会被低排,不满足新鲜度。
全流式对慢变的图谱拓扑每秒重算是巨大浪费,拓扑一天变不了多少。
让模型自学时效解决不了特征本身陈旧的问题,数据进来就已经旧了。
对;按变化速度分工,慢的走批省成本,快的走流保新鲜,是标准双管线。
optionExplanations_en: All-batch lags fast counts by a day, under-ranking viral posts and failing freshness.
All-streaming recomputing slow graph topology every second is huge waste; topology barely changes in a day.
Letting the model self-learn timeliness cannot fix stale input; the data is already old when it arrives.
Correct — splitting by change speed (slow via batch to save cost, fast via streaming to stay fresh) is the standard dual pipeline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Spark+Airflow 定期(日级)批量算慢变特征,吞吐高但时效低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A batch pipeline uses Spark+Airflow to periodically (daily) compute slow features in bulk—high throughput, low freshness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Flink+Kafka 实时算快变特征(点赞数、评论速度),低延迟但运维重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A streaming pipeline uses Flink+Kafka to compute fast features (like counts, comment velocity) in real time—low latency, heavier ops.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 批处理和流式两条管线算出的特征,推理时要统一取用。
scenario_en: Features computed by the batch and streaming pipelines must be served uniformly at inference.
q: feature store 怎么统一批处理和流式两路特征?
q_en: How does a feature store unify batch and streaming features?
why: feature store 做统一层:批处理写离线存储再同步到在线存储;流式直接写在线存储并带 TTL 过期。推理时排序服务从在线存储(Redis/DynamoDB)读流式计数 + 批处理特征,一次取齐。
why_en: The feature store unifies both: batch writes to an offline store synced to the online store, streaming writes directly to the online store with TTL, and at inference the ranker reads streaming counters plus batch features from the online store (Redis/DynamoDB).
options: 批处理写离线存储同步在线;流式直接写在线带 TTL;推理一次读齐
两路特征各存各的系统,推理时要分别查询两边再自己手动拼接
只保留流式特征,丢弃批处理特征以简化
只保留批处理特征,流式特征仅用于监控
options_en: Batch writes an offline store synced online; streaming writes online directly with TTL; inference reads both in one shot.
Each pipeline stores its own system; at inference query both separately and stitch them together yourself.
Keep only streaming features and drop batch features to simplify.
Keep only batch features; streaming features are for monitoring only.
optionExplanations: 对;特征存储的价值就是统一读口,推理一次从在线存储取齐两路特征。
各存各的、推理时自己拼,正是特征存储要消除的碎片化。
丢批处理特征就失去慢变的图谱/画像信号,削足适履。
丢流式特征就回到批处理滞后问题,爆火帖被低排。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the feature store's value is a unified read path, fetching both feature sets from the online store in one inference call.
Storing separately and stitching at inference is exactly the fragmentation the feature store removes.
Dropping batch features loses slow graph/profile signals, cutting the foot to fit the shoe.
Dropping streaming features returns to batch lag, under-ranking viral posts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一管理离线/在线特征的系统,推理时提供低延迟点查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store manages offline/online features uniformly and serves low-latency point lookups at inference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低延迟键值存储(Redis/DynamoDB),供推理实时读取特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The online store is a low-latency key-value store (Redis/DynamoDB) that serves features to inference in real time.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 互动计数只要大致新鲜就行,但拉黑名单(block list)绝不能让被拉黑内容漏出来。
scenario_en: Engagement counts only need to be roughly fresh, but a block list must never let blocked content slip through.
q: 哪些特征容忍最终一致,哪些必须强一致?
q_en: Which features tolerate eventual consistency, and which require strong consistency?
why: 互动计数容忍最终一致(晚个 10 秒无所谓,排序不会因此崩);但隐私敏感的拉黑/限制名单必须强一致——被拉黑的内容一旦漏出就是隐私事故。按「错了有多严重」区分一致性等级。
why_en: Engagement counters tolerate eventual consistency (10s stale is fine), but privacy-sensitive block/restricted lists must be strongly consistent, since blocked content leaking is a privacy incident.
tradeoff: 计数最终一致(省成本·可容忍旧) vs 拉黑名单强一致(必须·漏出即事故)
options: 所有特征都强一致,宁慢勿错
所有特征都最终一致,包括拉黑名单也可容忍延迟
计数容忍最终一致(10s 旧无妨);拉黑名单必须强一致(漏出即隐私事故)
一致性等级按特征类型随机分配,靠随机化均摊整个系统的读写压力
options_en: All features strongly consistent—better slow than wrong.
All features eventually consistent, including block lists tolerating delay.
Counters tolerate eventual consistency (10s stale is fine); block lists must be strongly consistent (a leak is a privacy incident).
Assign consistency levels randomly by feature type, using randomness to spread the whole system's read/write load.
optionExplanations: 对计数强一致是过度设计,徒增延迟和成本,计数晚一点不影响排序质量。
对拉黑名单最终一致是危险的:延迟窗口里被拉黑内容会漏出,是隐私事故。
对;按错误后果分级——计数错一点无所谓,拉黑漏出不可接受,所以强一致。
随机分配一致性无视语义,既可能过度也可能失守,毫无依据。
optionExplanations_en: Strong consistency for counters is over-engineering that adds latency and cost; a slightly stale count doesn't hurt ranking.
Eventual consistency for block lists is dangerous: during the delay blocked content leaks, a privacy incident.
Correct — grade by consequence: a slightly wrong count is fine, but a block-list leak is unacceptable, so strong consistency.
Random consistency ignores semantics, risking both over-engineering and failure—baseless.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许短暂不一致、最终收敛,适合容忍轻微滞后的互动计数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency permits brief inconsistency that converges later, fitting engagement counts that tolerate slight lag.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写后立即对所有读可见,拉黑名单等安全关键特征需要它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strong consistency makes a write immediately visible to all reads, required for safety-critical features like block lists.

whenOtherWins: 若某类看似普通的特征一旦出错会牵连合规或金钱损失(不只是隐私),就该按更高一致性对待,不能只按「隐私漏出」一条线分级。
category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 流式管线要把一个互动事件变成可供排序读取的特征,存在端到端时延。
scenario_en: The streaming pipeline turns an interaction event into a feature readable by ranking, with an end-to-end delay.
q: 流式特征的典型 SLA(事件→特征可用)是多少,它约束什么?
q_en: What is the typical streaming SLA (event→feature availability), and what does it constrain?
why: 典型 30–60 秒(给定的产品 SLA,不是公式)。它是「一个点赞发生」到「这个计数能被排序读到」的端到端时延上限,决定了快变信号能多快反映到排序里——爆火帖能多快被识别就受它约束。
why_en: Typically 30–60 seconds (a given product SLA, not a formula), the end-to-end delay from an interaction happening to its count being readable by ranking, bounding how fast trending signals reach ranking.
options: 约 24 小时,和批处理刷新周期一样慢
约 30–60 秒,约束快变信号多快能反映到排序里
约 10 毫秒,等于模型推理延迟
约 7 天,等于最长互动窗口
options_en: About 24 hours, as slow as the batch refresh cycle.
About 30–60 seconds, bounding how fast trending signals reach ranking.
About 10 milliseconds, equal to model inference latency.
About 7 days, equal to the longest interaction window.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事件发生到特征可被读取的端到端时延目标,典型 30–60 秒。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The streaming SLA is the target end-to-end delay from event to feature availability, typically 30–60 seconds.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 只用「发帖者单独」或「浏览者单独」的特征,抓不住这一对具体的人之间有多熟。
scenario_en: Poster-alone or viewer-alone features miss how close this specific pair of people are.
q: 为什么「发帖者×浏览者」交叉特征信号最强?
q_en: Why are poster×viewer cross-features the highest-signal?
why: 交叉特征刻画的是「这个浏览者对这个发帖者」的具体关系——频率、近因、互惠、社区重叠的复合,比任何一方单独的特征都更能预测这条帖对这个人是否相关。关系是成对的,单方特征丢了配对信息。
why_en: Cross-features capture this specific viewer's relationship to this poster—a composite of frequency, recency, reciprocity, and community overlap—predicting relevance better than either side alone, because relationships are pairwise.
tradeoff: 交叉特征(成对·最强信号·但最贵) vs 单方特征(便宜·但丢配对关系)
options: 因为发帖者单独的粉丝数最能预测相关性
因为浏览者单独的历史点击率最能预测相关性
因为交叉特征参数最少、算得最快,比单方特征更省计算资源和存储空间
因为它刻画这一对人的具体关系(频率/近因/互惠),比单方特征更能预测相关性
options_en: Because the poster's follower count alone best predicts relevance.
Because the viewer's historical CTR alone best predicts relevance.
Because cross-features have the fewest params and compute fastest, using less compute and storage than single-side features.
Because they capture this pair's specific relationship (frequency/recency/reciprocity), predicting relevance better than either side alone.
whenOtherWins: 若某对用户之间历史互动极稀疏(冷启动、新关注),成对交叉特征无数据可算,这时只能退回单方特征起步。
optionExplanations: 发帖者粉丝数是单方特征,抓不到「他和你」的具体关系。
浏览者历史点击率也是单方特征,同样丢了配对信息。
交叉特征恰恰最贵(要成对算),不是最省算力,搞反了。
对;成对关系是最强预测信号,单方特征无论多强都丢了配对维度。
optionExplanations_en: Poster follower count is a single-side feature and misses the specific 'them and you' relationship.
Viewer historical CTR is also single-side, likewise losing the pairing information.
Cross-features are actually the most expensive (computed per pair), not the cheapest—reversed.
Correct — pairwise relationship is the strongest predictive signal; single-side features, however strong, drop the pairing dimension.

termDefinitions.meaning: 刻画某浏览者与某发帖者具体关系的成对特征,信号最强但最贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A poster×viewer cross-feature captures a specific viewer-poster relationship, the highest-signal but most expensive feature.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互动是单向还是双向,衡量关系是否对等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Reciprocity is whether interaction is one-sided or mutual, gauging relationship symmetry.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 要为「发帖者×浏览者」这一对具体人构造复合交叉特征。
scenario_en: You need composite cross-features for a specific poster×viewer pair.
q: 下列哪些是合理的「发帖者×浏览者」交叉特征?(多选)
q_en: Which are reasonable poster×viewer cross-features? (multiple)
why: 四个合理特征各刻画这对人关系的一面:互动强度/互惠/共同兴趣/衰减;全站 DAU 是与具体人无关的全局标量,不算成对特征。
why_en: Each valid feature captures one facet of this pair's relationship — intent, reciprocity, shared interest, or decay — while site-wide DAU is a global scalar unrelated to any specific pair.
options: viewer_poster_comment_count_7d:7 天内该浏览者评论该发帖者的次数
reciprocal_interaction_ratio:双方互动的互惠比例
time_since_last_interaction:距上次互动的时间,刻画关系衰减
全站总 DAU:平台当天的日活总数
options_en: viewer_poster_comment_count_7d: the viewer's 7-day comment count on the poster.
reciprocal_interaction_ratio: the mutual share of their interactions.
time_since_last_interaction: time since their last interaction, capturing decay.
Site-wide total DAU: the platform's daily active user count.
optionExplanations: 对;7 天评论计数是最直接的成对互动意图信号。
对;互惠比例区分单向关注和双向互动,是关系对称性信号。
对;距上次互动的时间刻画关系是否在衰减,是近因维度。
错;全站 DAU 是全局标量,对所有帖都一样,区分不了任何一对具体关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 7-day comment count is the most direct pairwise interaction-intent signal.
Correct — the reciprocity ratio distinguishes one-sided follows from mutual interaction, a symmetry signal.
Correct — time since last interaction captures whether the relationship is decaying, a recency dimension.
Wrong — site-wide DAU is a global scalar identical for all posts and cannot distinguish any specific pair.

termDefinitions.meaning: 浏览者对该发帖者主打内容格式(视频/文本)的历史点击倾向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: content_type_affinity is the viewer's historical CTR tendency toward the poster's dominant content format.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 交叉特征要按(浏览者,发帖者)成对算,一次请求有几百个候选帖,全对预计算不现实。
scenario_en: Cross-features are computed per (viewer, poster) pair, hundreds of candidate posts per request, and precomputing all pairs is infeasible.
q: 既然全对预计算不可行,交叉特征在服务时怎么算?
q_en: Since all-pairs precompute is infeasible, how are cross-features computed at serving time?
why: 两条路:请求时只为候选集现算交叉特征,或缓存每个浏览者互动最多的 top-K 发帖者。都避开 N×N 全对预计算的组合爆炸,换成候选规模的按需计算。
why_en: Either compute cross-features on the fly for the candidate set, or cache each viewer's top-K most-interacted posters — both avoid the N×N all-pairs explosion.
tradeoff: 请求时按候选集现算(省存储·加读时算) vs 缓存 top-K 发帖者(读快·但覆盖有限)
options: 把所有用户对的交叉特征全部预计算好存下来
干脆不用交叉特征,只保留发帖者和浏览者各自的单方特征
对每条帖随机采样几对用户算交叉特征
请求时只为候选集现算,或缓存浏览者互动最多的 top-K 发帖者
options_en: Precompute and store cross-features for all user pairs.
Drop cross-features entirely and keep only the poster's and viewer's separate single-side features.
Randomly sample a few user pairs per post to compute cross-features.
Compute on the fly only for the candidate set, or cache the top-K most-interacted posters per viewer.
whenOtherWins: 若浏览者的候选发帖者高度集中在少数熟人(如强社交圈产品),缓存 top-K 发帖者就能覆盖大部分请求,比每次现算更快。
optionExplanations: 全对预计算是 N×N 组合爆炸,数十亿用户根本存不下,正是不可行项。
丢掉交叉特征等于放弃最强信号,是因噎废食。
随机采样用户对算出的特征和当前候选无关,对排序没用。
对;只算召回候选或缓存 top-K 发帖者,把计算量从 N×N 降到候选规模,可行。
optionExplanations_en: All-pairs precompute is an N×N explosion; billions of users cannot be stored—exactly the infeasible option.
Dropping cross-features abandons the strongest signal, throwing the baby out with the bathwater.
Random user pairs yield features unrelated to the current candidates, useless for ranking.
Correct — computing only for retrieved candidates or caching top-K posters cuts work from N×N to candidate scale, feasible.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按精确键(viewer_id, poster_id)在特征存储里 O(1) 取一条特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A point lookup fetches one feature by an exact key (viewer_id, poster_id) in O(1) from the feature store.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 计算「A 和 B 的共同好友」要同时读 A 和 B 的好友列表,但 B 把好友列表设成了私密。
scenario_en: Computing 'mutual friends of A and B' reads both A's and B's friend lists, but B set their friend list private.
q: 图谱遍历算共同好友,可能造成什么隐私泄露?
q_en: What privacy leak can graph traversal for mutual friends cause?
why: 算共同好友要读双方好友列表,若 B 是私密的,这次遍历就间接暴露了 B 的部分关系——用户没同意公开的连接被泄露。所以隐私安全特征必须服务端算,绝不把原始图谱暴露给模型。
why_en: Computing mutual friends reads both friend lists, so if B is private, the traversal leaks part of B's connections the user never consented to expose—hence compute privacy-safe features server-side and never expose the raw graph.
options: 会泄露 B 未同意公开的部分关系,因为遍历读了 B 的私密好友列表
不会有任何泄露,共同好友是公开信息
只会泄露 A 单方的关系信息,私密设置的 B 完全不受影响
只影响计算延迟,不涉及隐私
options_en: It leaks part of B's connections B never consented to expose, because the traversal read B's private friend list.
No leak at all—mutual friends are public information.
It only leaks A's own relationships; B, who set it private, is completely unaffected.
It only affects compute latency, no privacy concern.
optionExplanations: 对;遍历读了 B 的私密列表,共同好友结果会反推出 B 未公开的连接,是隐私泄露。
B 已设私密,共同好友并非公开信息,断言无泄露是错的。
遍历读的是双方列表,泄露的正是私密方 B 的关系,不是只泄露 A。
这是实打实的关系泄露,不只是延迟问题。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the traversal read B's private list, and the mutual-friends result can reveal B's undisclosed connections, a leak.
B set it private, so mutual friends are not public; claiming no leak is wrong.
The traversal reads both lists, and the leak is precisely the private party B's relationships, not only A's.
This is a real relationship leak, not just a latency concern.

termDefinitions.meaning: 沿社交图的边访问相邻节点(如读好友列表)来算特征,可能触及私密关系。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Graph traversal walks the social graph's edges (e.g. reading friend lists) to compute features, potentially touching private relationships.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 想用图谱特征提升排序,又要保证无法从模型反推出任何单个用户的关系。
scenario_en: You want graph features to improve ranking while guaranteeing no single user's relationship can be inferred from the model.
q: 差分隐私(differential privacy)怎么在图谱特征上保护隐私,ε 起什么作用?
q_en: How does differential privacy protect graph features, and what role does ε play?
why: 差分隐私往特征里加校准过的噪声,使得任何单条数据在不在都无法被反推。隐私预算由 ε 控制:ε 越小噪声越大、隐私越强,但排序质量越差。生产常用 ε 在 1–10 之间权衡。
why_en: Differential privacy adds calibrated noise so no single data point's presence is inferable, with the privacy budget controlled by ε—lower ε means more noise and stronger privacy but worse ranking, commonly 1–10 in production.
tradeoff: 小 ε(隐私强·噪声大·排序差) vs 大 ε(排序好·隐私弱)
options: 加校准噪声使单条数据不可反推;ε 越小隐私越强但排序越差
把所有图谱特征删掉,靠不用即隐私
把特征整体加密存储,推理时再解密使用,由 ε 决定密钥长度
只给管理员看图谱特征,普通模型不用
options_en: Add calibrated noise so no single data point is inferable; a smaller ε means stronger privacy but worse ranking.
Delete all graph features and rely on non-use as privacy.
Encrypt features at rest and decrypt them at inference time, with ε determining the key length.
Show graph features only to admins; ordinary models don't use them.
whenOtherWins: 若某特征根本不涉及可反推的个体关系(如纯内容元数据),不必上差分隐私加噪,直接用原值排序更准。
optionExplanations: 对;差分隐私用加噪 + ε 预算做隐私-效用权衡,是保图谱隐私的标准手段。
删掉全部图谱特征会丢最强信号,是过度的一刀切,不是差分隐私。
ε 是隐私预算,不是密钥长度;差分隐私靠加噪不是加密。
只给管理员看不解决模型使用时的反推风险,答非所问。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — differential privacy trades privacy for utility via added noise and an ε budget, the standard way to protect graph privacy.
Deleting all graph features drops the strongest signal, an over-broad measure, not differential privacy.
ε is a privacy budget, not key length; differential privacy adds noise, not encryption.
Admin-only viewing doesn't address inference risk during model use, off-topic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往数据/特征加校准噪声,使任何单条记录在不在都无法被反推。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Differential privacy adds calibrated noise so the presence or absence of any single record cannot be inferred.

termDefinitions.meaning: 差分隐私的隐私预算,越小噪声越大、隐私越强、效用越低;生产常用 1–10。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ε (epsilon) is the differential-privacy budget: smaller means more noise, stronger privacy, lower utility, commonly 1–10.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 差分隐私和 k-匿名是两种不同的图谱隐私保护思路。
scenario_en: Differential privacy and k-anonymity are two different graph-privacy approaches.
q: 差分隐私和 k-匿名(k-anonymity)在机制上有何区别,各自的代价是什么?
q_en: How do differential privacy and k-anonymity differ mechanically, and what is each one's cost?
why: 差分隐私靠加校准噪声让单点不可反推,代价是噪声降低排序质量;k-匿名要求每种子图模式至少匹配 k 个用户,代价是匿名化可能破坏关系特征依赖的社区结构。两者都是隐私↔质量的权衡,方式不同。
why_en: Differential privacy adds calibrated noise so single points aren't inferable (cost: noise hurts ranking); k-anonymity requires every subgraph pattern to match ≥k users (cost: anonymization can destroy the community structure features rely on).
tradeoff: 差分隐私(加噪·损精度) vs k-匿名(泛化子图·毁社区结构)

rows: 加校准噪声,ε 控预算

options: 两者机制相同,只是 k 和 ε 是同一个参数的两种叫法
差分隐私加噪(代价降精度);k-匿名要求子图模式≥k 人(代价毁社区结构)
差分隐私要求任意子图模式匹配≥k 人;k-匿名则改成靠加噪声实现
两者都无代价,能同时做到完美隐私和完美排序
options_en: Same mechanism—k and ε are two names for one parameter.
Differential privacy adds noise (cost: lower accuracy); k-anonymity requires subgraph patterns to match ≥k users (cost: destroys community structure).
Differential privacy requires any subgraph pattern to match ≥k users; k-anonymity instead relies on adding noise.
Both are cost-free, achieving perfect privacy and perfect ranking at once.
optionExplanations: k 和 ε 是不同机制的参数,一个是匿名集大小、一个是隐私预算,不是同一个。
对;加噪 vs 泛化子图是两种机制,代价分别是精度损失和社区结构破坏。
说反了:加噪是差分隐私,≥k 人是 k-匿名。
隐私保护必有代价(噪声/结构损失),无代价完美是幻想。
optionExplanations_en: k and ε are parameters of different mechanisms—anonymity-set size vs privacy budget—not the same thing.
Correct — adding noise vs generalizing subgraphs are two mechanisms, costing accuracy loss and community-structure destruction respectively.
Backwards: adding noise is differential privacy, and ≥k users is k-anonymity.
Privacy protection always has a cost (noise/structure loss); cost-free perfection is fantasy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让每种子图模式至少匹配 k 个用户,使个体不可单独识别,但会破坏社区结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: k-anonymity ensures every subgraph pattern matches at least k users so individuals can't be singled out, but it can destroy community structure.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 拉黑/限制名单属于隐私安全约束,被拉黑内容绝不能通过任何特征间接漏给用户。
scenario_en: Block/restricted lists are a privacy-safety constraint; blocked content must never leak to the user through any feature.
q: 拉黑名单在特征系统里该怎么处理,才能保证不通过交叉特征泄露?
q_en: How should block lists be handled in the feature system so they never leak through cross-features?
why: 拉黑名单要强一致(见前卡),且隐私安全特征在服务端计算、绝不把原始图谱暴露给模型——避免被拉黑关系通过交叉特征间接渗出。名单是硬约束,不是软信号,漏一次就是隐私事故。
why_en: Block lists must be strongly consistent, and privacy-safe features are computed server-side with the raw graph never exposed to the model, so blocked relationships can't seep through cross-features—a hard constraint where one leak is an incident.
tradeoff: 服务端算隐私安全特征+强一致名单(绝不泄露·更重) vs 把原始图谱喂模型(方便·会漏拉黑关系)
options: 把原始好友图直接喂给模型,让它自己学会避开拉黑内容
拉黑名单用最终一致即可,延迟窗口内漏一点没关系
只在前端过滤拉黑内容,后端特征照常包含
名单强一致,隐私安全特征服务端算,绝不把原始图谱暴露给模型
options_en: Feed the raw friend graph to the model and let it learn to avoid blocked content.
Use eventual consistency for block lists; a small leak within the delay is fine.
Filter blocked content only on the frontend; backend features include it as usual.
Keep the list strongly consistent, compute privacy-safe features server-side, and never expose the raw graph to the model.
whenOtherWins: 若某类内容并非隐私安全约束、只是「倾向少看」的偏好(如降低某话题),就不必上强一致名单,用软性降权即可。
optionExplanations: 把原始图喂模型正是泄露源头,模型可能通过特征间接暴露拉黑关系。
最终一致给了泄露窗口,拉黑是硬约束,漏一次就是隐私事故。
只在前端过滤,后端特征仍携带拉黑关系,交叉特征照样能渗出。
对;强一致名单 + 服务端算安全特征 + 不暴露原始图,才能堵住交叉特征泄露。
optionExplanations_en: Feeding the raw graph to the model is the leak source; the model can indirectly expose blocked relationships through features.
Eventual consistency opens a leak window; blocking is a hard constraint where one leak is an incident.
Frontend-only filtering leaves backend features carrying blocked relationships, which cross-features can still seep out.
Correct — a strongly consistent list plus server-side safe features plus not exposing the raw graph seals cross-feature leakage.

termDefinitions.term: block/restricted list / 拉黑限制名单
termDefinitions.meaning: 用户拉黑或限制的对象集合,隐私安全硬约束,内容绝不能漏出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A block/restricted list is the set a user blocked or restricted, a hard privacy-safety constraint whose content must never leak.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 对图谱特征做了差分隐私加噪或匿名化后,想知道排序质量掉了多少。
scenario_en: After applying differential privacy or anonymization to graph features, you want to know how much ranking quality dropped.
q: 怎么量化隐私变换对特征有用性的损害?
q_en: How do you quantify the damage a privacy transform does to feature usefulness?
why: 用信息损失指标(information-loss metrics):对比隐私变换前后特征的重要性/排序质量,量化掉了多少。Staff+ 会设定一个 ε 范围并持续追踪加噪后特征重要性的退化,把隐私-质量权衡变成可监控的数字。
why_en: Use information-loss metrics: compare feature importance/ranking quality before and after the privacy transform to quantify the drop, and Staff+ tracks feature-importance degradation across an ε range.
options: 只看隐私是否达标,不管排序质量掉多少
用信息损失指标对比变换前后的特征重要性/排序质量,量化退化
假设加噪不影响质量,不做任何测量
只等到用户投诉隐私问题时,才回头检查排序质量退化
options_en: Only check whether privacy is met, ignoring how much ranking quality drops.
Use information-loss metrics to compare feature importance/ranking quality before and after the transform, quantifying degradation.
Assume noise doesn't affect quality and measure nothing.
Only revisit ranking-quality degradation after users complain about privacy.
optionExplanations: 只看隐私不看质量,无法在隐私-效用之间做知情权衡。
对;信息损失指标把加噪/匿名的质量代价量化出来,支撑 ε 的选择。
假设加噪无害是危险的,噪声确实会降特征重要性,必须测。
等投诉太被动,质量退化早在投诉前就发生了。
optionExplanations_en: Checking privacy without quality can't make an informed privacy-utility trade-off.
Correct — information-loss metrics quantify the quality cost of noise/anonymization, supporting the choice of ε.
Assuming noise is harmless is dangerous; noise really lowers feature importance and must be measured.
Waiting for complaints is too passive; quality degradation happens well before complaints.

termDefinitions.term: information-loss metric / 信息损失指标
termDefinitions.meaning: 对比隐私变换前后特征重要性或排序质量,量化隐私带来的效用损失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An information-loss metric compares feature importance or ranking quality before and after a privacy transform to quantify utility loss.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 一个点赞事件要在 30–60 秒内变成排序可读的新鲜特征。
scenario_en: A like event must become a fresh, ranking-readable feature within 30–60s.
q: 把互动事件经流式管线变成可用特征的步骤排序:
q_en: Order the steps by which an interaction event becomes a usable feature via the streaming pipeline:
steps: 用户点赞产生互动事件,写入 Kafka
Flink 实时消费事件,更新窗口互动计数
计数带 TTL 写入在线存储(Redis/DynamoDB)
排序服务推理时点查该计数 + 批处理特征
why: 流式链路:事件进 Kafka→Flink 消费更新计数→带 TTL 写在线存储→排序推理时点查。整条要压在 30–60 秒 SLA 内,快变信号才能及时进排序,爆火帖才不被低排。
why_en: Streaming flow: event into Kafka, Flink updates the count, write to the online store with TTL, then ranking point-looks it up at inference—all within the 30–60s SLA so fast signals reach ranking in time.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  E["点赞事件→Kafka"] --> F["Flink 更新窗口计数"]
  F --> S["带 TTL 写在线存储"]
  S --> R["排序推理点查"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式事件流平台,承接海量互动事件供流式管线消费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed event-streaming platform that ingests massive interaction events for the streaming pipeline.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理引擎,实时消费事件、维护窗口聚合(如互动计数)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a stream-processing engine that consumes events in real time and maintains windowed aggregates like interaction counts.

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 把 feed 特征系统的三层设计讲成一条从慢到快再到隐私的完整叙事。
scenario_en: Explain the feed feature system's three-layer design as one narrative from slow to fast to privacy.
q: 把 feed 特征系统的三层设计按讲述顺序排好:
q_en: Order the feed feature system's three-layer design as you would present it:
steps: 批处理层:Spark+Airflow 日级算慢变的图谱/画像特征
流式层:Flink+Kafka 30–60s 算快变的参与/近因特征
隐私层:限定可行遍历 + 匿名化/差分隐私保护图谱
交叉特征最强但最贵、最敏感,喂给下一课的多任务模型
why: 三层叙事:批处理(慢变)→流式(快变)→隐私层(可行遍历+匿名化),最后点出交叉特征信号最强但最贵最敏感,承上启下接入多任务模型。这条链体现「先数据战略后建模」的成熟度。
why_en: Three-layer narrative: batch (slow) → streaming (fast) → privacy layer (permissible traversals + anonymization), closing on cross-features being highest-signal but most expensive and sensitive, feeding the multi-task model.

termDefinitions.term: three-layer feature design / 三层特征设计
termDefinitions.meaning: 批处理(慢变)+流式(快变)+隐私层(可行遍历与匿名化)的组合架构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The three-layer feature design combines batch (slow), streaming (fast), and a privacy layer (permissible traversals and anonymization).

category: Social Feed Ranking Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 设计社交 feed 排序：一个模型要同时预测 P(点击)、P(转发)、P(有意义评论)、P(长停留) 和创作者公平分。
scenario_en: Designing social feed ranking: one model must jointly predict P(click), P(reshare), P(meaningful comment), P(long dwell), and a creator-equity score.
q: feed 排序模型的核心形态和三大支柱是什么？
q_en: What is the core shape and three pillars of the feed-ranking model?
why: 核心是一个模型对每个「观看者-发帖者-内容」三元组联合预测多个目标头（点击/转发/评论/停留/创作者公平）。三大支柱：多任务学习(MTL) 联合优化、专家混合(MoE) 处理内容异质、损失设计对抗指标蚕食。
why_en: The core is one model jointly predicting multiple heads (click/reshare/comment/dwell/creator equity) per viewer-poster-content triple, resting on three pillars: multi-task learning, mixture-of-experts for content heterogeneity, and loss design against cannibalization.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  F["特征: 三元组"] --> S["共享表示"]
  S --> MTL["多任务头"]
  MTL --> C["点击"]
  MTL --> R["转发"]
  MTL --> M["有意义评论"]
  MTL --> D["长停留"]
  MTL --> E["创作者公平"]
options: 每个目标各训一个独立模型，互不共享
一个模型联合预测多目标头(点击/转发/评论/停留/公平)，三支柱=MTL+MoE+抗蚕食损失设计
只预测点击一个目标，其他都不管
用纯规则打分，不用任何模型
options_en: Train a separate model per objective with no sharing.
One model jointly predicts multiple heads (click/reshare/comment/dwell/equity); three pillars = MTL + MoE + anti-cannibalization loss design.
Predict only click and ignore the rest.
Score purely by rules with no model.
optionExplanations: 独立模型浪费算力、丢失共享表示，正是本设计要避免的。
对；联合多头+MTL/MoE/损失设计三支柱，是 feed 排序的主流架构。
只预测点击会诱导 clickbait，忽略转发/评论/停留/公平等多目标。
纯规则无法个性化，也表达不了多目标权衡。
optionExplanations_en: Separate models waste compute and lose shared representation — exactly what this design avoids.
Correct — joint multi-head plus the MTL/MoE/loss-design trio is the mainstream feed-ranking architecture.
Predicting only click invites clickbait and ignores reshare/comment/dwell/equity.
Pure rules can't personalize or express multi-objective tradeoffs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务学习：一个模型共享表示同时优化多个目标，比每目标单独训模型更省且能互相受益。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTL (Multi-Task Learning) trains one model with shared representation to optimize several objectives at once, cheaper than separate models and mutually beneficial.

termDefinitions.meaning: 衡量分发是否公平覆盖不同创作者的分数，作为防止只追参与的护栏目标之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Creator equity scores whether distribution fairly reaches diverse creators, a guardrail objective against pure engagement-chasing.

scenario: 有人主张给点击、转发、评论各训一个独立模型，分开上线打分。
scenario_en: Someone proposes training separate models for click, reshare, and comment and scoring them independently.
q: 为什么用一个多任务模型联合优化，而不是每任务一个独立模型？
q_en: Why one multi-task model instead of a separate model per task?
why: feed 排序本质多目标。分开训既浪费算力（重复造底座），又丢掉共享表示——会转发的用户通常先点了击，任务间有强相关信号，共享底座能互相受益。MTL 一个模型学共享表示 + 各任务头，更省也更准。
why_en: Feed ranking is inherently multi-objective, and separate models both waste compute and miss shared representation, since users who reshare usually clicked first, so a shared backbone lets tasks benefit each other.
tradeoff: MTL 共享底座（省算力+共享信号） vs 每任务独立模型（零干扰但重复造底座、丢共享）
options: 独立模型互不干扰，任何情况下都更好
feed 本质多目标，独立训浪费算力且丢共享表示（转发者常先点击），MTL 共享底座更省更准
MTL 只是为了省钱，精度一定更差
任务之间毫无关联，共享表示没有意义
options_en: Separate models never interfere and are always better.
Feed is inherently multi-objective; separate training wastes compute and loses shared representation (resharers usually clicked first), so MTL's shared backbone is cheaper and more accurate.
MTL is only about saving money and is always less accurate.
Tasks are unrelated, so shared representation is meaningless.
whenOtherWins: 如果两个任务本质完全无关（用户预测 vs 一个毫不相干的内容审核任务），强行共享底座反而互相污染，这时分开独立模型更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: If two tasks are truly unrelated (user prediction vs a wholly unrelated moderation task), forcing a shared backbone mutually pollutes them, and separate models fit better.
optionExplanations: 独立模型确实零干扰，但重复造底座、丢共享信号，多数相关任务下更差。
对；相关任务共享底座能互相受益，还省算力，是 feed 多目标的标准解。
共享相关信号常常提升而非降低精度，不是纯省钱。
feed 任务高度相关（点击/转发/评论同源），共享很有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Separate models are interference-free but rebuild backbones and lose shared signal, worse for most related tasks.
Correct — related tasks sharing a backbone benefit each other and save compute, the standard feed multi-objective solution.
Sharing related signal often raises accuracy, not lowers it — not just cost.
Feed tasks are highly related (click/reshare/comment same-source), so sharing is meaningful.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务共用的底层特征表示，让相关任务的信号互相增强、避免重复学习。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A shared representation is the common bottom feature layer across tasks, letting related signals reinforce each other and avoid relearning.

scenario: 多任务底座有两种：所有任务共用一个底座，或每个任务用自己的门控在一组专家上加权。
scenario_en: Two MTL backbones: all tasks share one bottom, or each task uses its own gating over a set of experts.
q: shared-bottom 和 MMoE 的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What's the core difference between shared-bottom and MMoE?
why: shared-bottom：一个共享 embedding+交互层 → 各任务塔，简单便宜，但目标冲突时会互相拖累（clickbait 拉高点击却害了深度评论）。MMoE：一组专家子网络，每个任务有自己的门控网络对专家做 softmax 加权，选择性共享、减少干扰、不用整模型复制。
why_en: Shared-bottom uses one shared bottom into task towers — simple and cheap but breaks on conflict — while MMoE gives each task its own gating network softmax-weighting a set of shared experts for selective sharing with less interference.
tradeoff: shared-bottom（简单便宜但冲突时互拖） vs MMoE（选择性共享、减干扰但参数多、更难调）

rows: 每任务门控加权共享专家

options: shared-bottom 单一共享底座简单但冲突时互拖；MMoE 每任务门控加权共享专家、选择性共享减干扰
两者完全相同，只是叫法不同
shared-bottom 每任务一套专家，MMoE 只有一个底座
MMoE 不共享任何东西，等于独立模型
options_en: Shared-bottom's single bottom is simple but interferes on conflict; MMoE lets each task gate-weight shared experts for selective sharing with less interference.
They're identical, just different names.
Shared-bottom has per-task experts; MMoE has one bottom.
MMoE shares nothing, equivalent to separate models.
optionExplanations: 对；一个是硬共享一个底座、一个是每任务门控软性挑专家，正是二者分野。
两者共享机制不同，不是叫法差异。
说反了：shared-bottom 是单底座，MMoE 才是多专家+每任务门控。
MMoE 共享的是专家池，只是门控各异，不等于独立模型。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — one hard-shares a single bottom, the other lets each task softly gate experts, the dividing line.
Their sharing mechanisms differ; it's not naming.
Backwards: shared-bottom has one bottom, MMoE has multiple experts + per-task gates.
MMoE shares the expert pool with per-task gates — not separate models.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组共享专家子网络，每个任务用独立门控网络对专家做 softmax 加权，实现选择性知识共享。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MMoE (Multi-gate Mixture-of-Experts) has shared expert sub-networks, each task using its own gating network to softmax-weight experts for selective sharing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 所有任务共用一个 embedding+交互层，再接各任务塔，最简单的 MTL 结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Shared-bottom has all tasks share one embedding+interaction layer feeding task-specific towers, the simplest MTL structure.

scenario: 一个 feed 内容类型单一、任务也不多且基本不冲突，团队想要最省算力、最好调的多任务结构。
scenario_en: A feed with homogeneous content, few tasks, and little conflict, wanting the cheapest, easiest-to-tune MTL structure.
q: 这种场景该选哪种多任务结构，为什么？
q_en: Which MTL structure fits this case, and why?
why: 选 shared-bottom：任务少、不冲突、内容同质时，一个共享底座就够，简单、低算力、好调。只有当目标开始互相冲突（clickbait 拉点击伤评论）时，才值得升级到 MMoE 的选择性共享。
why_en: Choose shared-bottom: with few non-conflicting tasks and homogeneous content, one shared bottom suffices — simple, cheap, easy to tune — upgrading to MMoE only when objectives start conflicting.
tradeoff: shared-bottom（任务少不冲突时最省最好调） vs MMoE（目标冲突时才值得的复杂度）
options: 选 MMoE，越复杂越好
选 shared-bottom：任务少、不冲突、内容同质时一个共享底座够用，简单低算力好调
选每任务独立模型，最稳
选稀疏 MoE，专为同质内容而生
options_en: Choose MMoE; more complex is better.
Choose shared-bottom: with few non-conflicting tasks and homogeneous content, one shared bottom suffices — simple, cheap, easy to tune.
Choose separate per-task models; most stable.
Choose sparse MoE, built for homogeneous content.
whenOtherWins: 一旦任务目标明显冲突（点击 vs 有意义评论互相拉扯），shared-bottom 的硬共享会互相污染，这时 MMoE 的每任务门控选择性共享更合适。
whenOtherWins_en: Once objectives clearly conflict (click vs meaningful comment tug against each other), shared-bottom's hard sharing pollutes tasks, and MMoE's per-task gating fits better.
optionExplanations: 任务不冲突时上 MMoE 是过度工程，白增参数和调试成本。
对；同质少冲突场景 shared-bottom 最省最好调，是恰当的简单解。
独立模型丢共享、重复造底座，不是这里的最优。
稀疏 MoE 是为异质内容设计的，同质场景用不上。
optionExplanations_en: Using MMoE with non-conflicting tasks is over-engineering, adding params and tuning cost.
Correct — for homogeneous low-conflict cases shared-bottom is cheapest and easiest, the right simple solution.
Separate models lose sharing and rebuild backbones — not optimal here.
Sparse MoE is built for heterogeneous content, unneeded when homogeneous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多任务共享参数时，一个任务的更新损害另一个任务表现，尤其在目标冲突时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task interference is when shared-parameter updates for one task hurt another's performance, especially under conflicting objectives.

scenario: 点击有海量标签、有意义评论的标签却很稀疏，两者共用一个底座训练。
scenario_en: Clicks have abundant labels while meaningful-comment labels are sparse, and both share one backbone.
q: 标签量悬殊的任务共享底座会怎样，怎么缓解？
q_en: What happens when tasks with lopsided label counts share a backbone, and how to mitigate?
why: 标签多的强势任务（点击）会劫持共享层：梯度里它压倒性主导，把共享表示往自己方向拽，稀疏任务（评论）学不好。缓解：用同方差不确定性加权自动校准各任务影响，并给稀疏任务设权重下限，别让点击独吞底座。
why_en: The label-rich dominant task (clicks) hijacks the shared layers, dominating gradients and pulling the representation its way so the sparse task learns poorly — mitigated by uncertainty weighting and lower bounds on sparse tasks.
options: 标签多的点击任务劫持共享层、稀疏评论学不好；用不确定性加权+给稀疏任务设权重下限缓解
毫无影响，两任务自动平衡
稀疏任务会自动主导，压过点击
只影响训练速度，不影响各任务质量
options_en: The label-rich click task hijacks shared layers so sparse comments learn poorly; mitigate with uncertainty weighting + lower bounds on sparse tasks.
No effect; the two auto-balance.
The sparse task auto-dominates and overrides clicks.
It only affects training speed, not per-task quality.
optionExplanations: 对；强势任务主导梯度会拽偏共享表示，需自动加权+下限保护稀疏任务。
标签量悬殊不会自动平衡，点击天然占主导。
稀疏任务信号弱，不可能自动压过标签海量的点击。
这是学到的表示被拽偏的质量问题，不只是速度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the dominant task's gradients skew the shared representation, needing auto-weighting plus lower bounds to protect the sparse task.
Lopsided labels don't auto-balance; clicks naturally dominate.
The sparse task's weak signal can't override label-rich clicks.
It's a quality issue of a skewed representation, not just speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标签多或损失大的任务在共享层梯度中压倒其他任务，劫持共享表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Task dominance is when a label-rich or high-loss task overwhelms others in shared-layer gradients, hijacking the shared representation.

scenario: 多任务损失里，点击和评论标签量、噪声都不同，你不想手工反复调各任务的固定权重。
