why_en: Log-loss governs calibration (absolute probability) and AUC-ROC governs ranking (relative order); the auction multiplies by bid using absolute probability, so calibration is core.

termDefinitions.meaning: log-loss 的别名,衡量预测概率分布与真实标签的差距,直接反映校准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-entropy is another name for log-loss, measuring the gap between predicted probabilities and true labels and reflecting calibration.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 你要为 CTR 系统列一组指标,分别覆盖平台营收、模型质量、广告主和用户。
scenario_en: You are listing metrics for a CTR system covering platform revenue, model quality, advertiser, and user.
q: 以下哪些是合适的 CTR 系统评估指标?(多选)
q_en: Which are appropriate CTR system evaluation metrics? (multiple)
why: 合适的四个:总 eCPM/每千次曝光收入(平台营收)、log-loss(离线校准)、AUC-ROC(离线排序)、每次转化成本(广告主 ROI)。「模型参数量」是模型规模不是评估指标,不该混进来。
why_en: Appropriate: total eCPM (platform revenue), log-loss (offline calibration), AUC-ROC (offline ranking), cost per conversion (advertiser ROI); parameter count is model size, not a metric.
options: 总 eCPM / 每千次曝光收入——平台营收效率
log-loss 与 AUC-ROC——离线的校准与排序质量
每次转化成本——广告主花费效率与信任
模型参数量——模型有多少个权重
options_en: Total eCPM / revenue per 1K impressions — platform monetization efficiency.
Log-loss and AUC-ROC — offline calibration and ranking quality.
Cost per conversion — advertiser spend efficiency and trust.
Model parameter count — how many weights the model has.
optionExplanations: 对;总 eCPM 是平台营收效率的直接度量。
对;log-loss 管校准、AUC-ROC 管排序,是两个不能互相替代的离线质量指标。
对;每次转化成本反映广告主 ROI,差了会让预算缩水、伤长期营收。
错;参数量是模型规模,不衡量业务或质量效果,不是评估指标。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — total eCPM directly measures platform monetization efficiency.
Correct — log-loss governs calibration and AUC-ROC ranking, two non-substitutable offline quality metrics.
Correct — cost per conversion reflects advertiser ROI; a bad one shrinks budgets and hurts long-term revenue.
Wrong — parameter count is model size, measuring no business or quality outcome, so not an evaluation metric.

termDefinitions.term: revenue per 1K impressions / 每千次曝光收入
termDefinitions.meaning: 平台每展示一千次广告获得的收入,即 eCPM 的营收视角度量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Revenue per 1K impressions is what the platform earns per thousand ad shows, the revenue-side view of eCPM.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 从广告请求到返回胜出创意,整条管线必须在 100ms 内完成——这是 UX 和发布商合约给定的硬约束。
scenario_en: From ad request to returning the winning creative, the whole pipeline must finish under 100ms — a hard constraint from UX and publisher contracts.
q: 这个 <100ms 是怎么来的,它对架构意味着什么?
q_en: Where does the <100ms come from, and what does it mean for architecture?
why: <100ms 是 UX + 发布商合约给定的目标,不是算出来的。它是端到端墙钟预算,逼出一连串取舍:排除大 ensemble、把贵特征预计算进特征库、用两段式检索→排序,让重模型只打少量候选。
why_en: The <100ms is a given target from UX and publisher contracts, and as an end-to-end budget it rules out big ensembles, forces precomputed features, and motivates two-stage retrieval-then-ranking.
options: <100ms 是模型 FLOPs 算出的物理下限
<100ms 是 UX+发布商合约给定的目标,作为端到端预算逼出:排除大 ensemble、预计算特征、两段式架构
<100ms 只是监控告警线,不影响架构设计
<100ms 只覆盖模型推理一段,和特征检索、拍卖无关
options_en: <100ms is the physical lower bound computed from model FLOPs.
<100ms is a given target from UX and publisher contracts, an end-to-end budget forcing: no big ensembles, precomputed features, two-stage architecture.
<100ms is just a monitoring alert line and does not shape architecture.
<100ms covers only the model-inference stage, unrelated to feature retrieval or the auction.
optionExplanations: 它不是算力推导,而是商务/体验给定的目标;架构要反向适配这个目标。
对;<100ms 是给定 SLO,端到端拆开后每一步都被压缩,直接导出排除大模型、预计算、两段式这些设计决策。
它是硬约束不是单纯告警线——正因为要卡 100ms,才决定了整套架构形态。
<100ms 是端到端预算,涵盖网络+渲染、特征检索、推理、拍卖序列化全部。
optionExplanations_en: It is not compute-derived but a business/experience target the architecture must fit backward.
Correct — <100ms is a given SLO; splitting it end-to-end squeezes every step, directly yielding no-big-model, precompute, and two-stage decisions.
It is a hard constraint, not a mere alert line — the 100ms cap shapes the whole architecture.
<100ms is an end-to-end budget spanning network+render, feature retrieval, inference, and auction serialization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告平台与展示广告的网站/App 之间的协议,常规定广告必须在多少 ms 内返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A publisher contract is the agreement between the ad platform and the site/app showing ads, often mandating the ad return within a latency bound.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 把 <100ms 的端到端预算拆到各阶段,你要说清每段大概花多少。
scenario_en: Splitting the <100ms end-to-end budget across stages, you must say roughly how much each takes.
q: 100ms 大致怎么分给各阶段,留给模型推理多少?
q_en: How is 100ms roughly split, and how much is left for model inference?
why: 大致:网络往返+渲染 ~60ms、特征检索 ~20ms、模型推理只剩 10-20ms、拍卖逻辑+序列化 ~10ms。推理窗口这么窄正是为什么要预计算特征、用两段式,把重模型省到只打几百个候选。
why_en: Roughly network+render ~60ms, feature retrieval ~20ms, inference only 10-20ms, auction+serialization ~10ms, and that tiny inference window forces precompute and two-stage.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  N["网络+渲染 ~60ms"] --> F["特征检索 ~20ms"]
  F --> M["模型推理 10-20ms"]
  M --> A["拍卖+序列化 ~10ms"]
options: 模型推理独占 80ms,其余全部环节挤在 20ms 内
网络+渲染 ~60ms、特征检索 ~20ms、模型推理只剩 10-20ms、拍卖+序列化 ~10ms
全部 100ms 都留给模型推理,网络和特征不占时间
特征检索占 60ms,推理占 30ms,网络忽略不计
options_en: Model inference alone takes 80ms and everything else squeezes into 20ms.
Network+render ~60ms, feature retrieval ~20ms, model inference only 10-20ms, auction+serialization ~10ms.
All 100ms goes to model inference; network and features take no time.
Feature retrieval takes 60ms, inference 30ms, network is negligible.
optionExplanations: 推理拿不到 80ms;网络+渲染就吃掉约 60ms,推理只剩十几毫秒。
对;网络+渲染最重(~60ms)、特征检索~20ms、拍卖~10ms,推理被挤到 10-20ms,这决定了模型必须轻。
网络往返和渲染真实存在且占大头,不可能忽略。
特征检索约 20ms 不是 60ms;吃掉大头的是网络+渲染。
optionExplanations_en: Inference does not get 80ms; network+render alone eats ~60ms, leaving inference just over ten ms.
Correct — network+render dominates (~60ms), feature retrieval ~20ms, auction ~10ms, squeezing inference to 10-20ms, which forces a light model.
Network round-trip and rendering are real and dominant; they cannot be ignored.
Feature retrieval is ~20ms not 60ms; the dominant slice is network+render.

termDefinitions.meaning: 端到端预算里留给模型打分的时间(这里 10-20ms),窄到必须排除大 ensemble。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The inference window is the slice of the end-to-end budget left for model scoring (here 10-20ms), too narrow for big ensembles.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 模型推理只有 10-20ms 就要给几百个候选广告打分。有人想用一个大 ensemble 追求最高 AUC。
scenario_en: Inference has only 10-20ms to score hundreds of candidate ads. Someone wants a big ensemble for maximum AUC.
q: 大 ensemble 在这里为什么行不通?
q_en: Why won't a big ensemble work here?
why: 大 ensemble 单次推理慢,10-20ms 内给几百个候选打分根本跑不完,直接违反 <100ms 硬约束。serving 阶段要的是能在预算内打完全部候选的轻量模型,ensemble 的精度收益换不来超时的代价。
why_en: A big ensemble is too slow to score hundreds of candidates within 10-20ms, breaching the <100ms constraint, so serving needs a light model that finishes within budget.
options: ensemble 精度太低,不如单模型准
ensemble 单次推理太慢,10-20ms 内给几百候选打分跑不完,违反 <100ms 硬约束
ensemble 无法校准,永远不能用于拍卖
ensemble 只能离线训练,不能在线部署
options_en: Ensembles have too low accuracy, worse than a single model.
Ensembles are too slow to score hundreds of candidates within 10-20ms, breaching the <100ms constraint.
Ensembles cannot be calibrated and can never be used in an auction.
Ensembles can only be trained offline and never deployed online.
optionExplanations: ensemble 通常精度更高,问题不在精度而在延迟。
对;serving 卡 10-20ms 打几百候选,ensemble 的重推理跑不完,精度再高也超时,所以被排除。
ensemble 可以做校准,排除它的原因是延迟不是校准。
ensemble 可以在线部署,只是这里的延迟预算容不下它。
optionExplanations_en: Ensembles are usually more accurate; the issue is latency, not accuracy.
Correct — serving caps 10-20ms to score hundreds, and an ensemble's heavy inference cannot finish, so it is ruled out despite accuracy.
Ensembles can be calibrated; they are excluded for latency, not calibration.
Ensembles can be deployed online; here the latency budget simply cannot fit one.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把多个模型的预测组合起来的方案,精度常更高但单次推理更慢,难满足严苛延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ensemble combines several models' predictions for higher accuracy but slower inference, hard to fit tight latency budgets.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 一个强特征是用户过去 30 天的点击历史聚合,但在线现算它要扫大量日志,远超 20ms 的特征检索预算。
scenario_en: A strong feature is the user's aggregated 30-day click history, but computing it online scans huge logs, far beyond the 20ms retrieval budget.
q: 这类昂贵特征该怎么在线提供?
q_en: How should such expensive features be served online?
why: 把 30 天点击历史这类需要历史聚合的贵特征离线/流式预计算好,存进带 p99 保证的特征库,在线只做一次快速查表。请求路径上现算聚合会超时,预计算把重活挪到线下、在线只读。
why_en: Precompute expensive aggregations like 30-day click history into a feature store with p99 guarantees, so online serving is a fast lookup rather than an on-request scan.
tradeoff: 预计算进特征库(在线快查、但有新鲜度延迟) vs 在线现算(最新但超时,违反预算)
whenOtherWins: 如果一个特征完全由当前请求就能得出(如设备类型、时段),就该在线实时取,没必要预计算。
options: 预计算进带 p99 保证的特征库,在线只做快速查表,把聚合的重活挪到线下
每次请求现算 30 天聚合,靠加 CPU 硬扛,保证绝对最新
干脆不用这个特征,凡是贵的特征都丢弃
把 30 天历史塞进请求payload让客户端上传
options_en: Precompute into a feature store with p99 guarantees and do a fast lookup online, moving the aggregation work offline.
Compute the 30-day aggregation on every request, brute-forcing with more CPU for absolute freshness.
Just drop the feature; discard any expensive feature.
Stuff the 30-day history into the request payload for the client to upload.
optionExplanations: 对;历史聚合无法在 20ms 内现算,预计算存进特征库、在线快查,用 p99 保证读延迟,是标准解法。
现算聚合扫日志必然超时,加 CPU 也压不进 20ms 预算,代价和延迟都失控。
丢弃强特征白白损失精度;贵不等于该弃,预计算就是为了留住它。
让客户端上传 30 天历史不现实(数据量、隐私、可信度),也不是特征服务的路径。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a 30-day aggregation cannot be computed in 20ms, so precompute into a feature store and fast-lookup online with p99-guaranteed reads.
On-request aggregation scans logs and inevitably times out; more CPU cannot fit the 20ms budget, blowing cost and latency.
Dropping a strong feature forfeits accuracy; expensive does not mean discard — precompute keeps it.
Uploading 30-day history from the client is unrealistic (volume, privacy, trust) and is not the feature-serving path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集中存储预计算特征、供在线低延迟读取的系统,常带 p99 读延迟保证(<5-10ms)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store centrally holds precomputed features for low-latency online reads, often with a p99 read guarantee (<5-10ms).

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 每次广告请求有上千个候选,但推理只有 10-20ms,不可能用重模型给上千个都打分。
scenario_en: Each ad request has thousands of candidates, but inference is only 10-20ms — no way to score thousands with a heavy model.
q: 该用什么架构,各阶段分工是什么?
q_en: What architecture fits, and what does each stage do?
why: 两段式:轻量检索先用便宜信号把上千候选收窄到几百个,重排序模型再用更丰富特征给这几百个打分。它把昂贵计算限制在小候选集上,让整条管线卡进 <100ms。
why_en: Two-stage: lightweight retrieval narrows thousands to a few hundred with cheap signals, then a heavier ranking model scores the reduced set with richer features.
tradeoff: 两段式(重模型只打几百候选、进得了预算) vs 单段重模型(打上千候选、必超时)
whenOtherWins: 如果候选本来就只有几十个(小广告库、强定向),一段式重模型直接打完更简单也更准,不必两段。
diagram:
flowchart LR T["上千候选"] --> R["轻量检索
便宜信号收窄"] R --> H["几百候选"] H --> K["重排序模型
丰富特征打分"]
options: 单段:用一个重模型直接给上千候选全部打分,追求一次到位
两段式:轻量检索把上千收窄到几百,重排序模型再对这几百打分
随机采样几十个候选打分,其余全丢,省掉检索
把上千候选全发给客户端,让客户端本地排序
options_en: One stage: score all thousands of candidates with one heavy model for a one-shot result.
Two stages: lightweight retrieval narrows thousands to hundreds, then a heavier ranking model scores those.
Randomly sample a few dozen candidates to score and drop the rest, skipping retrieval.
Send all thousands to the client and let it rank locally.
optionExplanations: 重模型打上千候选在 10-20ms 内跑不完,单段方案直接违反延迟预算。
对;检索用便宜信号粗筛到几百,重模型只打这小集合,昂贵计算被限制住,整管线进得了 100ms。
随机采样会误杀好候选,粗筛应按信号保留最有希望的,不是靠运气。
客户端排序拿不到全量特征也无法保证一致与可信,不是可行架构。
optionExplanations_en: A heavy model over thousands cannot finish in 10-20ms; the one-stage plan breaches the budget.
Correct — retrieval coarse-filters to hundreds with cheap signals and the heavy model scores only that small set, fitting 100ms.
Random sampling kills good candidates; screening keeps the most promising by signal, not luck.
Client-side ranking lacks full features and consistency/trust — not a viable architecture.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先用轻量检索把候选从上千收窄到几百,再用重排序模型精打分,兼顾延迟与精度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-stage architecture narrows candidates from thousands to hundreds via light retrieval, then scores them with a heavier ranker, balancing latency and accuracy.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 用户在 2:00 看到广告,可能 2:15 才点、也可能永远不点。你在 2:05 用当时的标签重训模型。
scenario_en: A user sees an ad at 2:00, may click at 2:15 or never. You retrain at 2:05 using the labels available then.
q: 延迟反馈会让模型犯什么系统性错误?
q_en: What systematic error does delayed feedback cause?
why: 点击往往晚于曝光到达,近期曝光的正标签还没来,训练时被当成「没点击」。于是模型系统性低估近期曝光的 CTR,拍卖被扭曲,直到标签补齐才纠正。这是生产里的首要失效模式。
why_en: Clicks arrive after impressions, so recent positives are missing and counted as non-clicks, making the model systematically underestimate CTR for recent impressions until labels catch up.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  I["2:00 看到广告"] --> T["2:05 重训:标签未到"]
  T --> U["近期曝光被当未点击"]
  U --> B["系统性低估近期 CTR"]
  C["2:15 才点击"] -.补齐.-> B
options: 模型系统性高估近期曝光的 CTR,因为把未来点击提前算进来了
模型系统性低估近期曝光的 CTR,因为迟到的点击还没来、被当成没点击
模型完全不受影响,标签迟早会到、不影响当下训练
模型只在离线评估虚高,线上拍卖不受任何影响
options_en: The model systematically overestimates recent CTR by counting future clicks early.
The model systematically underestimates recent CTR because late clicks have not arrived and are treated as non-clicks.
The model is unaffected; labels arrive eventually and do not affect current training.
The model only looks inflated offline, with no effect on live auctions.
optionExplanations: 方向反了:迟到的是正标签(点击),缺失会让模型低估而非高估。
对;近期曝光的点击还在路上,训练时被记成负例,CTR 被系统性压低,直到标签补齐,拍卖期间被扭曲。
会影响:用不完整标签训练就是在用错误的负例,当下预测就偏了。
低估直接改变 pCTR→eCPM,线上分配一定受影响,不只是离线数字。
optionExplanations_en: Direction reversed — the late labels are positives (clicks), and their absence makes the model underestimate, not overestimate.
Correct — recent impressions' clicks are still in transit and counted as negatives, systematically depressing CTR until labels catch up, distorting the auction.
It does affect training: using incomplete labels means training on false negatives, biasing current predictions.
Underestimation changes pCTR→eCPM and definitely affects live allocation, not just an offline number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击/转化标签晚于曝光到达,近期曝光的正标签暂缺,使模型系统性低估近期 CTR。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Delayed feedback is click/conversion labels arriving after impressions, so recent positives are missing and the model underestimates recent CTR.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 广告分布和用户兴趣快速变化,再叠加延迟反馈,一个训练好就不动的模型很快过时。
scenario_en: Ad distributions and user interests shift fast, and with delayed feedback a train-once model quickly goes stale.
q: 训练节奏该怎么定,为什么?
q_en: How should the training cadence be set, and why?
why: 小时级/天级持续重训:分布漂移快加上延迟反馈的标签补齐,都要求模型频繁吸收最新数据。太久不训,近期 CTR 低估和分布漂移会持续扭曲拍卖;频率过高则成本和不稳。
why_en: Retrain hourly/daily continuously, because fast distribution shift plus delayed-feedback label catch-up require frequently absorbing fresh data to keep the auction accurate.
tradeoff: 小时/天级重训(跟上漂移与标签补齐、但成本高) vs 训练一次不动(便宜但迅速过时、拍卖失真)
whenOtherWins: 如果某个广告场景分布极稳、几乎无新广告进入,拉长重训周期(如每周)可以省成本,不必小时级。
options: 训练一次永久部署,分布不会变,重训是浪费
小时级/天级持续重训,跟上快速分布漂移和延迟反馈的标签补齐
只在 AUC 掉到某阈值以下才重训,平时不动
每分钟重训一次,越频繁一定越好、无副作用
options_en: Train once and deploy forever; distributions do not change, so retraining is waste.
Retrain continuously hourly/daily to keep up with fast distribution shift and delayed-feedback label catch-up.
Retrain only when AUC drops below a threshold, otherwise leave it.
Retrain every minute; more frequent is always better with no downside.
optionExplanations: 广告分布和兴趣快速变化,训练一次很快过时,拍卖会被漂移和低估持续扭曲。
对;小时/天级重训让模型不断吸收最新数据和补齐的标签,是应对漂移+延迟反馈的标准节奏。
等 AUC 掉了才训是被动的,近期 CTR 低估在拍卖里已造成损失,应主动持续训练。
每分钟训成本高、易受噪声,过频不稳,小时/天级是成本与新鲜度的平衡点。
optionExplanations_en: Ad distributions and interests shift fast; a one-time model goes stale and the auction stays distorted by drift and underestimation.
Correct — hourly/daily retraining keeps absorbing fresh data and caught-up labels, the standard cadence for drift plus delayed feedback.
Waiting for AUC to drop is reactive; recent-CTR underestimation already costs the auction, so retrain proactively.
Per-minute retraining is costly and noise-prone; hourly/daily balances cost and freshness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按小时或天级节奏不断用最新数据重训模型,以跟上分布漂移和延迟反馈的标签补齐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Continuous training retrains on fresh data at hourly/daily cadence to track distribution shift and delayed-feedback label catch-up.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 模型 AUC 不错,但预测概率整体偏高,拍卖里 eCPM 被系统性抬升。你要在几乎不加延迟的前提下修正校准。
scenario_en: The model has decent AUC but globally over-predicts, inflating eCPM in the auction. You must fix calibration with almost no added latency.
q: 该用什么后处理校准方法(L5 常见答案)?
q_en: Which post-hoc calibration method fits (a common L5 answer)?
why: 用 Platt scaling:在校准集上对模型 logits 拟合一个逻辑回归 p=σ(A·z+B),把整体偏移拉回对角线。它对单调型偏差有效、serving 只多一次 sigmoid,几乎零延迟,是默认首选。
why_en: Use Platt scaling — fit a logistic regression on the logits on a held-out set to pull predictions back to the diagonal, adding just one sigmoid at serving.
tradeoff: Platt scaling(单调偏差、几乎零延迟、默认) vs 复杂重训(更强但慢、常无必要)
whenOtherWins: 如果偏差是非单调的、Platt 拉不直,再上 isotonic regression(非参数单调阶梯),代价是更多数据和一张查表。
options: 重新从头训练一个更大的模型,直到概率自然校准
Platt scaling:在校准集上对 logits 拟合逻辑回归,serving 多一次 sigmoid,几乎零延迟
直接把所有 pCTR 乘一个固定常数,不用任何拟合
放弃校准,反正 AUC 高就够了
options_en: Retrain a bigger model from scratch until probabilities are naturally calibrated.
Platt scaling: fit a logistic regression on the logits on a held-out set, adding one sigmoid at serving with near-zero latency.
Just multiply all pCTR by a fixed constant with no fitting.
Skip calibration since high AUC is enough.
optionExplanations: 重训大模型成本高、也不保证校准,校准问题该用轻量后处理专门修。
对;Platt 在留出集上拟合 σ(A·z+B),把单调偏移拉回对角线,serving 只加一次 sigmoid,是默认低成本解。
乘固定常数不是拟合,救不了随分数变化的非线性偏移,还可能把概率推出 [0,1]。
AUC 高不代表校准好,拍卖乘 bid 用绝对概率,不校准会系统性错配 eCPM。
optionExplanations_en: Retraining a bigger model is costly and does not guarantee calibration; the fix should be a lightweight post-hoc step.
Correct — Platt fits σ(A·z+B) on a held-out set to pull monotonic bias back to the diagonal, adding just one sigmoid — the default low-cost fix.
A fixed constant is not a fit, cannot fix score-dependent nonlinear bias, and may push probabilities outside [0,1].
High AUC does not imply calibration; the auction multiplies by bid using absolute probability, so uncalibrated systematically misprices eCPM.

termDefinitions.meaning: 后处理校准:在留出集上对模型 logits 拟合逻辑回归 p=σ(A·z+B),修单调型偏差,几乎零延迟。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Platt scaling is post-hoc calibration fitting a logistic regression p=σ(A·z+B) on logits over a held-out set, fixing monotonic bias at near-zero latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 过 sigmoid 之前的原始分数,Platt scaling 就作用在它上面。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A logit is the raw score before the sigmoid; Platt scaling operates on it.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 同一道 CTR 预测题,L4 和 Staff+ 的答案在框架深度上差别很大。
scenario_en: For the same CTR problem, L4 and Staff+ answers differ greatly in framing depth.
q: Staff+ 答案比 L4/L5 多出哪些框架要素?
q_en: What framing elements does a Staff+ answer add over L4/L5?
why: L4 定义问题、选离线指标、提 LR/简单 NN;L5 加延迟-精度权衡、两段式、持续训练、校准(Platt)。Staff+ 再加业务指标层级与利益冲突、端到端基建、失效模式(延迟反馈/分布漂移)、监控护栏、组织级权衡(共享模型平台 vs 各面独立模型)。
why_en: Staff+ adds the business-metric hierarchy and stakeholder tensions, end-to-end infra, failure modes (delayed feedback, distribution shift), monitoring guardrails, and org trade-offs.
tradeoff: L4(定义+离线指标+基础模型) vs Staff+(业务层级+基建+失效模式+监控+组织权衡)
options: Staff+ 只是把 L4 的模型换成更大的网络,别无区别
Staff+ 加业务指标层级与利益冲突、端到端基建、失效模式、监控护栏、组织级权衡
Staff+ 只多讲用什么编程语言和框架
Staff+ 反而省略框架,直接上代码实现
options_en: Staff+ just swaps L4's model for a bigger network, nothing else.
Staff+ adds the business-metric hierarchy and stakeholder tensions, end-to-end infra, failure modes, monitoring guardrails, and org trade-offs.
Staff+ only adds which programming language and framework to use.
Staff+ skips framing and jumps straight to code.
optionExplanations: 差别不在模型大小,而在框架的广度与深度——业务、基建、失效、监控、组织。
对;Staff+ 的加分点是把技术决策接到业务利益冲突、失效模式、监控与组织权衡上,体现端到端 ownership。
语言/框架选型不是分级依据,考的是系统性推理。
Staff+ 恰恰更重 framing(可占 45 分钟的 10-15 分钟),不是跳过。
optionExplanations_en: The gap is not model size but framing breadth and depth — business, infra, failures, monitoring, org.
Correct — Staff+ ties technical choices to business conflicts, failure modes, monitoring, and org trade-offs, showing end-to-end ownership.
Language/framework choice is not a leveling criterion; systematic reasoning is tested.
Staff+ weights framing more (10-15 of 45 minutes), not less.

termDefinitions.meaning: 组织级选择:用一个共享 CTR 模型平台服务所有广告位,还是每个广告面各训一个模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An org trade-off is choosing a shared CTR model platform for all surfaces versus separate per-surface models.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 很多候选把 45 分钟几乎全花在画架构上,framing 一带而过。
scenario_en: Many candidates spend almost the whole 45 minutes on architecture and rush through framing.
q: 在 Staff+ 的 CTR 面试里,framing 大概该占多少时间,说明什么?
q_en: In a Staff+ CTR interview, roughly how much time should framing take, and what does that signal?
why: Staff+ 面试里光 framing 就可能占 45 分钟里的 10-15 分钟(经验目标,不是硬公式)。这说明评委看重「把问题定清楚」的能力:auction 数学、业务指标冲突、延迟约束,比急着画大架构更能体现级别。
why_en: Framing alone can take 10-15 of the 45 minutes (a rule of thumb), signaling that clearly defining the problem — auction math, business tensions, latency — matters more than rushing to architecture.
options: framing 应压到 1-2 分钟,把时间全留给架构图
framing 可占 45 分钟里的 10-15 分钟,体现定义问题的能力(auction 数学/业务冲突/延迟)
framing 应占满 40 分钟,几乎不谈架构
framing 时间由抽签决定,和级别无关
options_en: Framing should be squeezed to 1-2 minutes, leaving all time for architecture diagrams.
Framing can take 10-15 of the 45 minutes, showing the ability to define the problem (auction math, business tensions, latency).
Framing should fill 40 minutes with almost no architecture.
Framing time is decided by lottery and unrelated to level.
optionExplanations: 压到 1-2 分钟正是多数人的失误——跳过 framing 会暴露对问题理解的浅薄。
对;10-15 分钟的 framing(经验值)让你讲清 auction 数学、业务指标冲突和延迟约束,这才是 Staff+ 的加分处。
40 分钟只 framing 又走极端,架构与深挖同样重要,要平衡。
时间分配反映候选人的判断,不是随机,framing 深度与级别正相关。
optionExplanations_en: Squeezing to 1-2 minutes is exactly most people's mistake — skipping framing exposes shallow problem understanding.
Correct — 10-15 minutes of framing (a rule of thumb) lets you cover auction math, business conflicts, and latency, the Staff+ plus.
40 minutes of only framing is the other extreme; architecture and deep-dives matter too, so balance.
Time allocation reflects the candidate's judgment, not randomness; framing depth correlates with level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在动手设计前先讲清目标、指标、约束和取舍,是高级别面试最被看重的环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Framing is clarifying goals, metrics, constraints, and trade-offs before designing, the most valued phase in senior interviews.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Problem Framing Requirements

scenario: 面试官让你先把 CTR 模型的特征按来源和更新方式分门别类,再谈存储与服务。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants you to categorize CTR features by source and update pattern before discussing storage and serving.
q: CTR 特征通常分成哪四大家族?
q_en: What are the four feature families for CTR?
why: 四大家族:用户(user_id、CTR 等,基数达十亿)、广告(ad_id、类目等)、上下文(时段/设备,来自请求、实时)、交叉(user×类目,基数极高需 embedding)。来源、基数、更新频率不同,决定各自存储与服务方式。
why_en: User, Ad, Context, and Cross features — each differs in source, cardinality, and update frequency, which dictates how each is stored and served.
diagram:
flowchart TD F["CTR 特征"] --> U["用户
基数~十亿, 时/天更新"] F --> A["广告
基数~百万"] F --> C["上下文
来自请求, 实时"] F --> X["交叉
基数极高, 预计算/embedding"]
options: 训练集、验证集、测试集、线上集
用户特征、广告特征、上下文特征、交叉特征
数值特征、文本特征、图像特征、音频特征
整型、浮点、字符串、布尔四种数据类型
options_en: Training set, validation set, test set, online set.
User features, Ad features, Context features, Cross features.
Numeric, text, image, audio features.
Integer, float, string, boolean data types.
optionExplanations: 数据集划分不是特征家族,答非所问。
对;按语义来源分成用户/广告/上下文/交叉四类,每类的基数、来源、更新频率不同,直接决定存储与服务策略。
模态划分对广告 CTR 不合适,主体是类别与数值特征,不是图像音频。
数据类型是底层表示,不是按业务来源分的特征家族。
optionExplanations_en: Dataset splits are not feature families — off target.
Correct — by semantic source into User/Ad/Context/Cross, each with distinct cardinality, source, and update frequency driving storage and serving.
Modality splits do not fit ad CTR, which is mostly categorical and numeric, not image/audio.
Data types are low-level representations, not business-source feature families.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户对某广告类目的历史偏好强度,是需历史聚合的预计算用户特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Category affinity is a user's historical preference strength for an ad category, a precomputed user feature needing history aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个类别特征可取的不同值的总数,如 user_id 基数可达十亿。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is the number of distinct values a categorical feature can take, e.g. user_id cardinality reaching a billion.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 单看用户特征和广告特征,模型抓不到「某类用户特别爱点某类广告」这种交互效应。
scenario_en: User and Ad features alone miss interaction effects like 'this user type especially clicks this ad type'.
q: 交叉特征解决什么问题,又带来什么代价?
q_en: What do cross features solve, and at what cost?
why: 交叉特征(如 user_id×广告主类目)捕捉单个家族看不到的交互效应,在 Wide & Deep 里是主要的记忆(memorization)机制。代价是它把特征空间组合式炸开、基数极高,这正是要用 embedding 去压的原因。
why_en: Cross features capture interaction effects individual families miss and are the main memorization mechanism in Wide & Deep, but they explode the feature space combinatorially, motivating embeddings.
tradeoff: 交叉特征(抓交互、强记忆) vs 组合爆炸(基数极高、需 embedding 压缩)
whenOtherWins: 如果两个字段之间没有真实交互(相互独立),硬造交叉只会加剧稀疏、白占空间,不如不做。
options: 交叉特征把 user_id 和广告主类目合并成一个联合 ID,借此降低整体基数,是节省存储的压缩手段
交叉特征捕捉家族间交互效应,是 Wide & Deep 的记忆机制,代价是特征空间组合式爆炸
交叉特征只把卷积网络提取的图像像素块编码进模型,只用于图像输入,和类别特征毫无关系
交叉特征只是加快了梯度反向传播、让模型更快收敛,不会带来任何额外的存储代价
options_en: Cross features merge user_id and advertiser_category into one joint ID, lowering overall cardinality — a storage-saving compression technique.
Cross features capture cross-family interaction and are Wide & Deep's memorization mechanism, at the cost of combinatorial explosion.
Cross features only encode convolutional image patches into the model, applying only to image inputs, unrelated to categorical features.
Cross features merely speed up gradient backpropagation for faster convergence, with no storage cost at all.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反,交叉特征把基数组合式放大,是空间爆炸的来源不是压缩。
对;它抓「A 类用户 × B 类广告」这类交互,是 Wide 侧记忆的核心,但组合爆炸迫使我们用 embedding 压维。
交叉特征正是类别特征的组合,和图像无关。
它带来的是空间爆炸而非零代价,收敛速度不是它的核心作用。
optionExplanations_en: Opposite — cross features multiply cardinality and are the source of the explosion, not compression.
Correct — they capture 'user type × ad type' interactions, the core of Wide-side memorization, but the explosion forces embeddings.
Cross features are exactly combinations of categoricals, unrelated to images.
They cause an explosion, not zero cost, and convergence speed is not their core role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个类别特征的组合(如 user_id×广告主类目),捕捉单特征看不到的交互效应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross feature is a combination of two categoricals (e.g. user_id × advertiser_category) capturing interactions single features miss.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型直接记住训练中见过的具体特征共现模式(如某用户点某广告主),对应 Wide 侧。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memorization is the model directly recalling specific feature co-occurrences seen in training (a user clicking an advertiser), the Wide side.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: user_id 有十亿量级。若把它 one-hot 编码喂给模型,每个样本的这一维就是一个十亿长的 0/1 向量。
scenario_en: user_id is on the order of a billion. One-hot encoding it makes this one feature a billion-long 0/1 vector per sample.
q: 为什么 one-hot 高基数 ID 会崩,说明该怎么办?
q_en: Why does one-hot encoding a high-cardinality ID collapse, and what does it imply?
why: 十亿维 one-hot 每个样本约 4GB(10 亿 × 4 字节),而且极稀疏(每样本只有一个 1)、绝大多数 ID 每批很少出现。存不下也没法学,这正是要用 embedding 把每个 ID 映射成低维稠密向量的原因。
why_en: A billion-dim one-hot is ~4GB per sample and extremely sparse, so it neither fits nor trains — which is exactly why IDs are mapped to low-dim dense embeddings.
options: one-hot 编码后每个样本这一维其实只占几 KB,完全没问题,不需要为任何高基数类别 ID 做改动
one-hot 十亿维每样本约 4GB 且极稀疏,存不下也难学,所以要用 embedding 映射成低维稠密向量
one-hot 崩溃单纯是因为它把数值特征也一起做了编码,和类别 ID 本身的基数高低完全没有关系
one-hot 完全没问题,真正的瓶颈只在于模型的隐藏层不够深,把网络往深处再加几层就能彻底解决
options_en: After one-hot encoding this one dimension per sample actually takes only a few KB and is fine, needing no change for any high-cardinality categorical ID.
A billion-dim one-hot is ~4GB per sample and extremely sparse, so it neither fits nor trains — hence embeddings mapping IDs to low-dim dense vectors.
One-hot collapses simply because it also encodes numeric features together, entirely unrelated to how high the categorical cardinality happens to be.
One-hot is entirely fine; the real bottleneck is just the model's hidden layers not being deep enough, and stacking a few more layers fully fixes it.
optionExplanations: 十亿维远不止几 KB,10 亿×4 字节≈4GB,单样本就压垮内存。
对;高基数+稀疏让 one-hot 每样本约 4GB 且几乎全零,既存不下又学不动,embedding 把它压成 16-64 维稠密向量。
崩的根因是类别基数太高,不是把数值也编码进来。
加深模型救不了输入表示爆炸,根子在 one-hot 的维度。
optionExplanations_en: A billion dims is far more than a few KB; 1B×4 bytes ≈ 4GB crushes memory for a single sample.
Correct — high cardinality plus sparsity makes one-hot ~4GB per sample and nearly all zeros, so embeddings compress it into 16-64 dense dims.
The collapse is from high categorical cardinality, not from also encoding numerics.
Deepening the model cannot fix an exploded input representation; the root is one-hot dimensionality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个类别值编码成只有对应位为 1、其余全 0 的向量;高基数时维度爆炸。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: One-hot encoding represents a category as a vector with a single 1 and the rest 0; at high cardinality the dimension explodes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在任一批数据里绝大多数取值都不出现的特征(如某个 user_id),向量几乎全零。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sparse feature is one whose values rarely appear in any batch (like a given user_id), making the vector nearly all zeros.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 你要把十亿量级的 user_id、百万量级的 ad_id 这类高基数类别特征喂进模型,又不能用 one-hot。
scenario_en: You must feed high-cardinality categoricals like billion-scale user_id and million-scale ad_id into the model without one-hot.
q: 该用什么表示,它凭什么既省空间又有用?
q_en: What representation should you use, and why is it both compact and useful?
why: 用 embedding:训练时把每个类别 ID 映射成一个 16-64 维的稠密向量,点击模式相近的 ID 学到相近的向量。它把十亿维稀疏压成几十维稠密,既存得下又让模型能在连续空间里泛化到相似 ID。
why_en: Use embeddings — map each ID to a learned 16-64-dim dense vector where similar click patterns give similar vectors, compressing billions of sparse dims into dozens of dense ones while enabling generalization.
tradeoff: embedding(几十维稠密、可泛化、需存表) vs one-hot(十亿维稀疏、存不下、不泛化)
whenOtherWins: 如果类别基数很低(如设备类型只有几种),直接 one-hot 更简单,没必要为它训 embedding。
options: 继续用 one-hot,只是把总维度从十亿粗暴砍到一百万,靠这种硬截断而不是学习出来的表示来解决
用 embedding:把每个 ID 映射成 16-64 维稠密向量,相似点击模式→相似向量,压维且能泛化
把 ID 直接当成一个普通整数标量喂进模型,省掉编码这一步,指望模型自己去学习其中的规律
对每一个 ID 都单独训练出一个专属的小模型,再把海量小模型各自的输出结果做集成打分
options_en: Keep one-hot but crudely truncate the dimension from a billion down to a million, via this hard truncation instead of a learned dense representation.
Use embeddings: map each ID to a 16-64-dim dense vector, similar click patterns giving similar vectors — compact and generalizing.
Feed the ID directly as a plain integer scalar, skipping encoding entirely, hoping the model learns the underlying pattern on its own.
Train a separate dedicated small model for every single ID, then ensemble the individual outputs of that massive collection of models.
optionExplanations: 砍到一百万维仍是巨大稀疏 one-hot,没解决存储和泛化问题。
对;embedding 学出低维稠密表示,相似 ID 靠近,既把十亿维压到几十维,又让模型能对没怎么见过的 ID 泛化。
把 ID 当整数标量会强加一个虚假的大小顺序(id=5 不比 id=3「大」),模型学不到语义。
每个 ID 一个模型不可行(十亿个模型),embedding 才是可扩展表示。
optionExplanations_en: A million-dim one-hot is still huge and sparse, solving neither storage nor generalization.
Correct — embeddings learn low-dim dense representations where similar IDs sit close, compressing billions to dozens and generalizing to rarely-seen IDs.
Feeding the ID as an integer imposes a false ordinal (id=5 is not 'bigger' than id=3), so the model learns no semantics.
One model per ID is infeasible (a billion models); embeddings are the scalable representation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练中为每个类别 ID 学到的低维(16-64)稠密向量,相似 ID 向量相近,替代 one-hot。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a learned low-dim (16-64) dense vector per categorical ID where similar IDs are close, replacing one-hot.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 你给十亿个用户各训一个 64 维 float32 的 embedding,要估算光这张表占多少内存。
scenario_en: You train a 64-dim float32 embedding for each of a billion users and must estimate the table's memory.
q: 这张用户 embedding 表的原始大小怎么算、约多少?
q_en: How do you compute the raw size of this user embedding table, and roughly how much?
why: 公式:行数 × 维度 × 每数字字节数 = 10 亿 × 64 × 4 字节(float32)= 256 GB。这是压缩前的原始基数,直接说明光一张用户 embedding 表就装不进单机内存,必须压缩+分片。
why_en: Rows × dims × bytes = 1B × 64 × 4 (float32) = 256 GB, the raw base showing one user embedding table alone won't fit a single node and needs compression plus sharding.
options: 按行数 × 维度 × 字节数换算:10 亿 × 64 × 4 字节 = 256 GB,这是压缩前的原始大小
按行数 × 维度 × 位数换算:10 亿 × 64 × 4 位 ≈ 32 GB,这就是这张表的原始大小
只按行数和字节数换算,不算维度:10 亿 × 4 字节 = 4 GB,这张表的维度不影响总大小
只算单条向量本身的大小:64 × 4 字节 = 256 字节,这就是整张表需要的空间
options_en: Rows × dims × bytes: 1B × 64 × 4 bytes = 256 GB, the raw size before compression.
Rows × dims × bits: 1B × 64 × 4 bits ≈ 32 GB, taken as the table's raw size.
Rows × bytes only, skipping dims: 1B × 4 bytes = 4 GB, treating dims as not affecting total size.
Only a single vector's own size: 64 × 4 bytes = 256 bytes, taken as the space the whole table needs.
optionExplanations: 对;256 GB = 10 亿行 × 64 维 × 4 字节,这是压缩前基数,说明单机装不下、要量化+分片。
float32 是 4 字节不是 4 位,算成位少了 8 倍。
维度当然影响大小,漏乘 64 维少算了 64 倍。
总大小随用户数线性增长,不能只算单个向量。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 256 GB = 1B rows × 64 dims × 4 bytes, the pre-compression base showing it won't fit one node and needs quantization plus sharding.
float32 is 4 bytes not 4 bits; using bits undercounts by 8×.
Dimensions do affect size; omitting the ×64 undercounts by 64×.
Total size grows linearly with users; you cannot count just one vector.

termDefinitions.meaning: 32 位(4 字节)单精度浮点数,embedding 默认的数值格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: float32 is a 32-bit (4-byte) single-precision floating-point number, the default numeric format for embeddings.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存放所有类别 ID 各自 embedding 向量的大表,行数=基数,可达数百 GB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding table stores every categorical ID's embedding vector, with rows equal to cardinality, reaching hundreds of GB.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: user_id 的 embedding 表有几十亿行,存不下。你想用一种不需要维护 ID→行号 映射表的办法把行数砍下来。
scenario_en: The user_id embedding table has billions of rows and won't fit. You want to shrink rows without maintaining an ID-to-row lookup.
q: 特征哈希(feature hashing)怎么压,代价是什么?
q_en: How does feature hashing compress, and at what cost?
why: 特征哈希用一个哈希函数把多个 ID 映射进同一个桶,把几十亿行压到几百万行(约 100:1),不用存 ID→行 的映射表。代价是哈希碰撞:不同 ID 共享一个 embedding 引入噪声,但量级可控。
why_en: Feature hashing maps many IDs into the same bucket via a hash, shrinking billions of rows to millions (~100:1) without a lookup table, at the cost of collisions that add manageable noise.
tradeoff: 特征哈希(免映射表、行数骤降) vs 哈希碰撞(不同 ID 共享向量、引入噪声)
whenOtherWins: 如果 ID 数量本就不多、且每个 ID 都需要独立表示不能混淆(如关键广告主),直接用完整 embedding 表更准,不必哈希。
options: 给每个 ID 分配唯一行号并维护一张映射表,行数完全不变但查得快
用哈希函数把多个 ID 映进同一桶,行数压到约 1/100,代价是碰撞引入噪声
把 embedding 维度从 64 硬降到 1,靠减维而不是减行来压表
只保留当前批次出现过的 ID,其余全部删掉,遇到没见过的就直接报错
options_en: Assign each ID a unique row and keep a full lookup table; rows stay unchanged but reads are faster.
Hash many IDs into the same bucket, shrinking rows ~100:1, at the cost of collisions adding noise.
Cut embedding dimension from 64 down to 1, shrinking columns instead of rows.
Keep only IDs seen in the current batch and delete the rest, erroring on any unseen ID.
optionExplanations: 维护完整映射表行数没减,存不下的问题依旧,而且要额外存映射。
对;哈希把 ID 折叠进固定桶数,约 100:1 压缩且免映射表,碰撞让少数 ID 共享向量、引入可控噪声。
降维压的是列不是行;十亿行的问题靠减维解决不了,且 1 维几乎没表达力。
只留见过的 ID 无法应对新 ID,也没有系统性压缩比,不是哈希的做法。
optionExplanations_en: A full lookup table does not cut rows, so the fit problem persists and you also store the mapping.
Correct — hashing folds IDs into a fixed bucket count (~100:1) without a lookup, and collisions make a few IDs share vectors with manageable noise.
Reducing dims shrinks columns not rows; a billion-row problem is not solved by dims, and 1 dim has almost no expressiveness.
Keeping only seen IDs cannot handle new IDs and gives no systematic compression ratio — not hashing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用哈希函数把多个 ID 映射进固定数量的桶,免维护映射表地把 embedding 行数大幅压缩,代价是碰撞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Feature hashing maps many IDs into a fixed number of buckets via a hash, shrinking embedding rows without a lookup table at the cost of collisions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个不同 ID 被哈希到同一个桶,被迫共享一个 embedding,引入噪声。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hash collision is two distinct IDs hashing to the same bucket and sharing one embedding, introducing noise.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 少数高频 ID(热门广告主、活跃用户)贡献大部分曝光,长尾里海量 ID 各自只出现几次。你想把 embedding 的容量花在刀刃上。
scenario_en: A few high-frequency IDs (popular advertisers, active users) drive most impressions, while a huge long tail each appears a few times. You want to spend embedding capacity wisely.
q: 混合维度 embedding 怎么分配容量?
q_en: How do mixed-dimension embeddings allocate capacity?
why: 混合维度:给高频 ID 分配更大维度(如 64 维),给稀有 ID 分配小维度(如 16 维)。因为高频 ID 数据多、值得更强表示,长尾 ID 数据少、给大维度也学不满还浪费空间,把容量按频率分配。
why_en: Give frequent IDs larger dimensions (e.g. 64) and rare IDs smaller ones (e.g. 16), allocating capacity where data volume justifies it.
tradeoff: 混合维度(容量按频率分、省空间) vs 统一大维度(表达强但长尾浪费、表更大)
whenOtherWins: 如果 ID 频率分布很均匀、没有明显的头部和长尾,统一维度更简单,混合维度带来的复杂度不划算。
options: 所有 ID 一律给最大维度,不管出现频率,只求表达力最强
高频 ID 给大维度(64)、稀有 ID 给小维度(16),按频率分配容量
反过来分配:高频 ID 给小维度、稀有 ID 给大维度,把容量让给冷门 ID
所有 ID 一律砍到 1 维,极致压缩、完全不看出现频率
options_en: Give every ID the largest dimension regardless of frequency, for maximum expressiveness.
Give frequent IDs large dims (64) and rare IDs small dims (16), allocating capacity by frequency.
Reverse the allocation: give frequent IDs small dims and rare IDs large dims, favoring cold ones.
Cut every ID down to 1 dim for extreme compression, ignoring frequency entirely.
optionExplanations: 统一大维度让海量长尾 ID 都占大空间却学不满,浪费内存。
对;高频 ID 数据多值得大维度,长尾 ID 数据少给小维度即可,容量随频率分配,省空间又不丢主力表达。
反了:稀有 ID 数据少,给大维度学不满、纯浪费,该把大维度给高频。
全 1 维丢掉了高频 ID 应有的表达力,过度压缩伤精度。
optionExplanations_en: Uniform large dims make the vast long tail occupy big space it cannot fill, wasting memory.
Correct — frequent IDs have data justifying large dims and rare IDs get small dims, allocating capacity by frequency to save space without losing the main expressiveness.
Reversed — rare IDs have little data, so large dims are wasted; large dims belong to frequent IDs.
All-1-dim strips frequent IDs of needed expressiveness, over-compressing and hurting accuracy.

termDefinitions.term: mixed-dimension embeddings / 混合维度嵌入
termDefinitions.meaning: 按 ID 频率分配 embedding 维度:高频给大维、稀有给小维,把容量花在数据多的 ID 上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mixed-dimension embeddings assign dims by ID frequency — large for frequent, small for rare — spending capacity where data is abundant.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 用户 embedding 表 float32 下约 256 GB,你想在几乎不改结构的前提下把它塞进更少内存。
scenario_en: The user embedding table is ~256 GB in float32, and you want to fit it in less memory with almost no structural change.
q: 量化(quantization)怎么压,256 GB 能降到多少?
q_en: How does quantization compress, and what does 256 GB drop to?
why: 量化把数值从 float32 降精度到 float16 或 int8,存储砍 2-4 倍:256 GB 用 int8 降到约 64 GB(1/4)。代价是精度略损,但 CTR embedding 通常能容忍,是最省事的压缩手段之一。
why_en: Quantization drops numeric precision from float32 to float16/int8, cutting storage 2-4×, so 256 GB becomes ~64 GB with int8 at a small accuracy cost.
tradeoff: 量化(存储砍 2-4 倍、精度略损) vs 保 float32(精度满、内存吃紧)
options: 量化其实是把 embedding 维度从 64 硬降到 16,靠减维而不是降精度让 256 GB 变成 64 GB
量化把数值从 float32 降到 int8,存储砍约 4 倍,256 GB → 约 64 GB,精度略损
量化把表里的行数直接强行减少 4 倍,256 GB → 64 GB,精度完全不受影响
量化反而把数值精度提升到 float64,256 GB → 512 GB,用双倍体积换更高准确率
options_en: Quantization is actually cutting the embedding dimension from 64 to 16, shrinking columns instead of precision, turning 256 GB into 64 GB.
Quantization drops values from float32 to int8, cutting storage ~4×, 256 GB → ~64 GB, with a small accuracy cost.
Quantization forcibly cuts the table's row count directly by 4×, 256 GB → 64 GB, with accuracy fully unaffected.
Quantization instead raises numeric precision to float64, 256 GB → 512 GB, trading double the size for higher accuracy.
optionExplanations: 降维是另一种手段(改列数),量化改的是每个数字的位宽不是维度。
对;float32→int8 每数字从 4 字节降到 1 字节,存储 1/4,256 GB→64 GB,代价是可容忍的精度损失。
量化不减行数(ID 还是那么多),减的是每个数值的精度位宽。
量化是降精度省空间,不是升到 float64,方向反了。
optionExplanations_en: Reducing dims is a different technique (columns); quantization changes each number's bit width, not dims.
Correct — float32→int8 drops each number from 4 bytes to 1, so storage is 1/4, 256 GB → 64 GB, at a tolerable accuracy cost.
Quantization does not cut rows (the IDs remain); it reduces each value's precision width.
Quantization lowers precision to save space, not raising to float64 — reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数值从 float32 降精度到 float16/int8,存储砍 2-4 倍,精度略损。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers numeric precision from float32 to float16/int8, cutting storage 2-4× at a small accuracy cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 8 位(1 字节)整数格式,量化常用,相比 float32 省 4 倍空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: int8 is an 8-bit (1-byte) integer format common in quantization, 4× smaller than float32.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 十亿级 embedding 表超过了服务节点内存,你要列出可用的压缩手段。
scenario_en: A billion-scale embedding table exceeds serving-node memory, and you list the available compression techniques.
q: 以下哪些是压缩 embedding 表的有效手段?(多选)
q_en: Which are effective techniques to compress an embedding table? (multiple)
why: 四种有效手段:特征哈希(约 100:1)、混合维度(按频率分维)、量化(float32→int8)、知识蒸馏(大 teacher 迁移到小 student)。「加大 batch size」是训练超参,不压 embedding 表。
why_en: Feature hashing, mixed-dimension embeddings, quantization, and knowledge distillation all shrink the table, while increasing batch size is a training hyperparameter that does not.
options: 特征哈希——多个 ID 共享桶,约 100:1 压行数
混合维度 embedding——高频 ID 大维、稀有 ID 小维
量化——float32→int8 省 2-4 倍存储
加大训练 batch size——一次喂更多样本
options_en: Feature hashing — many IDs share a bucket, ~100:1 row shrink.
Mixed-dimension embeddings — frequent IDs large dims, rare IDs small dims.
Quantization — float32→int8 saves 2-4× storage.
Increase training batch size — feed more samples at once.
optionExplanations: 对;哈希把几十亿行折到几百万桶,约 100:1,是行数压缩主力。
对;混合维度按频率分配容量,长尾不再占大维,省列空间。
对;量化降位宽,int8 直接把表砍到 1/4。
错;batch size 是训练吞吐超参,和 embedding 表大小无关,不压表。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — hashing folds billions of rows into millions of buckets (~100:1), the main row compressor.
Correct — mixed dims allocate capacity by frequency so the long tail no longer takes big dims, saving columns.
Correct — quantization lowers bit width, and int8 cuts the table to 1/4.
Wrong — batch size is a training-throughput hyperparameter unrelated to table size and does not compress it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大 teacher 模型的 embedding 知识迁移到更小的 student,以便在服务节点内存里放得下。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Knowledge distillation transfers a large teacher model's embedding knowledge to a smaller student so it fits serving-node memory.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: LinkedIn 的 CTR 系统实践发现:不压缩 embedding,表就超出单个服务节点的内存。
scenario_en: LinkedIn's CTR system found that without compression the embedding table exceeds a single serving node's memory.
q: embedding 压缩为什么不是「锦上添花」而是「非做不可」?
q_en: Why is embedding compression a must, not a nice-to-have?
why: 不压缩,embedding 表放不进服务节点内存,实时推理就直接做不了——每次打分要查 embedding,查不到就没法在 10-20ms 内出 pCTR。压缩是让在线服务成为可能的前提,不是可选优化。
why_en: Without compression the table won't fit serving-node memory, so real-time inference is impossible — every score needs an embedding lookup — making compression a prerequisite, not an optional tweak.
options: 只是为了省一点云成本,不压缩表也完全能正常上线服务用户
不压缩表就放不进服务节点内存,实时推理直接做不了,压缩是在线服务的前提
压缩纯粹是为了提高模型的预测精度,和内存大小、能否服务都无关
压缩只影响离线训练阶段的速度,对线上实时服务完全没有影响
options_en: It only saves a bit of cloud cost; serving still works fine online for users even without it.
Without compression the table won't fit serving-node memory, so real-time inference is impossible — compression is a serving prerequisite.
Compression is purely for the model's prediction accuracy, unrelated to memory size or whether serving is possible.
Compression only affects offline training-phase speed, with no effect on live online serving at all.
optionExplanations: 不是省钱那么轻——放不进内存,服务根本起不来。
对;推理每次都要查 embedding,表超内存就查不了,10-20ms 出 pCTR 无从谈起,所以压缩是可行性前提。
压缩首先解决的是能不能放进内存、能不能服务,不是提精度。
它直接决定线上能否加载和查表服务,不只是训练速度。
optionExplanations_en: It is not mere cost saving — if it won't fit memory, serving cannot even start.
Correct — inference needs an embedding lookup each time, and an over-memory table cannot be queried, so 10-20ms pCTR is impossible, making compression a feasibility prerequisite.
Compression first addresses fitting memory and serving at all, not accuracy.
It directly determines whether the table can be loaded and served online, not just training speed.

termDefinitions.term: serving-node memory / 服务节点内存
termDefinitions.meaning: 承载在线推理的机器的内存容量,embedding 表必须放得下才能实时查表打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Serving-node memory is the RAM of the machine running online inference; the embedding table must fit for real-time lookup scoring.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 特征检索只有约 20ms 预算,你要给每个特征判定是预计算还是实时取。
scenario_en: Feature retrieval has only ~20ms, and you must classify each feature as precomputed or real-time.
q: 把「一个特征该预计算还是实时取」的判定推理排成正确顺序:
q_en: Order the reasoning for deciding whether a feature is precomputed or real-time:
steps: 问:这个特征需要跨会话/历史聚合吗(如用户 30 天 CTR)?
若需要历史聚合→预计算进特征库,在线只做 p99 <5-10ms 的快查
若能从当前请求直接得出(时段/设备/槽位)→实时从请求 payload 取,无需外部查
介于两者之间要秒/分钟级新鲜→用流式(Kafka+Flink)做中间地带
why: 判定原则:超出当前会话、要历史聚合的→预计算(在线快查);当前请求就能算出的→实时取(无外部查);要分钟级新鲜的→流式管线兜中间。这样把 20ms 预算花在必要的快查上,不在请求路径现算重聚合。
why_en: Aggregation beyond the current session is precomputed for fast lookup, request-derivable features are real-time with no lookup, and minute-fresh needs go through streaming as the middle ground.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  Q{"需历史聚合?"} -->|是| P["预计算→特征库快查"]
  Q -->|否, 请求可得| R["实时从 payload 取"]
  Q -->|需分钟级新鲜| S["流式 Kafka+Flink"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Kafka+Flink 近实时聚合特征,延迟分钟级,是预计算(时/天)与纯实时之间的中间地带。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A streaming pipeline (Kafka+Flink) aggregates features in near-real-time (minutes), the middle ground between batch precompute and pure real-time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户一次连续使用的时段;会话内的状态可实时取,跨会话的历史需预计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A session is one continuous usage period; in-session state is real-time while cross-session history is precomputed.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 用户 30 天历史 CTR、类目亲和、user×广告主计数这类特征都要跨历史聚合,而在线只有 20ms 检索预算。
scenario_en: Features like user 30-day CTR, category affinity, and user×advertiser counts need history aggregation, but online retrieval has only 20ms.
q: 这类需历史聚合的特征该怎么在线服务?
q_en: How should such history-aggregation features be served online?
why: 预计算进特征库、在线只做 p99 读延迟 <5-10ms 的快查。批处理管线小时/天级刷新它们,若要分钟级新鲜(比如 3 分钟前点过某广告),用 Kafka+Flink 流式补齐。请求路径上绝不现算历史聚合。
why_en: Precompute into a feature store with a p99 read <5-10ms, refreshed by batch (hourly/daily) and bridged by streaming (Kafka+Flink) for minute-fresh needs, never aggregating history on the request path.
tradeoff: 预计算进特征库(在线 <5-10ms 快查、有新鲜度延迟) vs 请求路径现算聚合(最新但超 20ms 预算)
whenOtherWins: 如果特征完全由当前请求得出(设备、时段),就实时取、不进特征库;预计算只用于跨历史聚合量。
options: 每次请求都现场扫描这个用户全部的历史行为日志、重新完整算一遍聚合结果,以此保证数据绝对最新不过期
预计算进特征库、在线 p99 <5-10ms 快查,批处理刷新,分钟级新鲜用 Kafka+Flink 流式补
把这些需要跨历史聚合的特征全部直接丢弃不用,只依赖当前请求自带的那一小份上下文特征来打分
让模型在每一次推理的这一刻都直接连上后端数据库,现场跑一遍完整的历史聚合查询语句之后再打分
options_en: Rescan this user's entire behavioral history log and fully recompute the aggregate live on every single request, guaranteeing absolute freshness.
Precompute into a feature store with p99 <5-10ms lookup, refreshed by batch, and use Kafka+Flink streaming for minute-fresh needs.
Drop every single feature that needs cross-history aggregation and score using only the tiny set of context features the current request carries.
Have the model connect straight to the backend database at every single moment of inference and run a full historical aggregation query before scoring.
optionExplanations: 请求路径现算历史聚合必然超 20ms 预算,扫日志根本来不及。
对;预计算+特征库快查守住延迟,批处理管日常刷新,Kafka+Flink 流式兜分钟级新鲜,分层解决新鲜度。
丢弃强历史特征白损精度;预计算就是为了既留住它又满足延迟。
推理时现跑聚合查询等于把重活放回请求路径,必超时。
optionExplanations_en: Aggregating history on the request path inevitably blows the 20ms budget; scanning logs cannot finish in time.
Correct — precompute plus feature-store lookup holds latency, batch handles routine refresh, and Kafka+Flink streaming covers minute-fresh, layering the freshness solution.
Dropping strong history features forfeits accuracy; precompute keeps them while meeting latency.
Running aggregation queries at inference puts heavy work back on the request path and must time out.

termDefinitions.term: p99 read latency / p99 读延迟
termDefinitions.meaning: 99% 的读请求都比这个值快,特征库常保证 <5-10ms 以守住在线预算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 read latency is the value 99% of reads beat; a feature store often guarantees <5-10ms to hold the online budget.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 时段、设备类型、广告位、槽位位置、以及本次会话已展示过哪些广告——这些信息在请求发生的一刻就都有了。
scenario_en: Time of day, device type, placement, slot position, and which ads were already shown this session — all available the moment the request happens.
q: 这类实时特征该怎么取,为什么不用预计算?
q_en: How are such real-time features obtained, and why not precompute?
why: 直接从请求 payload 和会话状态里取,无需任何外部查表。因为它们由当前请求就能得出、不需要跨历史聚合,预计算反而增加延迟和陈旧风险。原则:请求可得的实时取,跨历史的才预计算。
why_en: Take them straight from the request payload and session state with no external lookup, because they are derivable from the current request and need no history aggregation.
options: 预计算进特征库,和用户 30 天历史 CTR 走一样的批处理流程
直接从请求 payload 和会话状态取,无需外部查,因为当前请求就能得出
从 30 天的历史日志里聚合出来,每小时定时刷新一次
让客户端先把这些字段上传、回写数据库,下一次请求才能用上
options_en: Precompute into the feature store, going through the same batch pipeline as user 30-day CTR.
Take them directly from the request payload and session state with no lookup, since the current request yields them.
Aggregate them from 30 days of history logs, refreshed on an hourly schedule.
Have the client upload these fields first, write them back to the database, and only use them next request.
optionExplanations: 上下文特征当前请求就有,预计算它们纯属多此一举还引入陈旧。
对;时段/设备/槽位/会话状态都在请求里,直接读、零外部查,是延迟最省的实时特征。
这些不是历史聚合量,没必要从日志算,预计算反而更慢更旧。
回写再用引入一整轮延迟,当前请求就能取的信息没理由绕这么大圈。
optionExplanations_en: Context features are already in the current request; precomputing them is redundant and adds staleness.
Correct — time/device/slot/session state are in the request, read directly with zero lookup — the lowest-latency real-time features.
These are not history aggregations, so computing from logs is needless and precompute is slower and staler.
Write-back-then-use adds a whole round-trip of latency for info the current request already has.

termDefinitions.meaning: 广告请求本身携带的数据(时段、设备、广告位、槽位),实时特征直接从中读取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The request payload is the data the ad request carries (time, device, placement, slot); real-time features read straight from it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 本次会话内的即时状态(已展示广告、上次点击),实时可得、无需外部查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Session state is the in-session status (ads already shown, last click), available in real time with no external lookup.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 用户 3 分钟前刚点过某类广告,这个信号对 pCTR 很有价值。批处理特征每小时才刷一次,拿不到这么新的信息;请求路径又没法现算历史聚合。
scenario_en: A user clicked an ad type 3 minutes ago — valuable for pCTR. Batch features refresh hourly (too stale) and the request path cannot aggregate history live.
q: 怎么在延迟预算内拿到这种分钟级新鲜的聚合特征?
q_en: How do you get such minute-fresh aggregated features within budget?
why: 用流式管线(Kafka+Flink)做中间地带:它近实时地增量聚合最新事件,几分钟延迟就能反映「3 分钟前点过」,写进特征库供在线快查。它填补了批处理(小时/天,太旧)和纯请求实时(算不了历史聚合)之间的空档。
why_en: Use a streaming pipeline (Kafka+Flink) as the middle ground — it incrementally aggregates fresh events with minutes of delay into the feature store, bridging batch (too stale) and request-time real-time (can't aggregate history).
tradeoff: 流式(分钟级新鲜、增量聚合、多一套管线) vs 批处理(小时/天、简单但太旧)
whenOtherWins: 如果特征本身天级更新就够(如用户长期类目亲和),用便宜的批处理即可,不必上流式的复杂度。
options: 把批处理刷新频率硬生生提到每分钟一次,单纯靠更频繁的全量重算来解决这个棘手的新鲜度问题
用流式管线(Kafka+Flink)近实时增量聚合,分钟级写进特征库,填批处理和请求实时之间的空档
在请求路径上现场扫描全部原始日志,当场重新算出这 3 分钟窗口内的完整聚合结果给模型用
干脆放弃这个只有 3 分钟新鲜度的珍贵信号不要,只用现成的小时级批处理特征凑合着用
options_en: Force batch refresh up to once per minute, relying purely on more frequent full recomputation to solve this thorny freshness problem on its own.
Use a streaming pipeline (Kafka+Flink) to incrementally aggregate near-real-time, writing minute-fresh into the feature store, bridging batch and request-time.
Scan the entire raw logs live on the request path and freshly recompute the full 3-minute window aggregate result for the model to use.
Just give up on this valuable 3-minute-freshness signal entirely and make do with the existing hourly batch features instead.
optionExplanations: 把批处理压到每分钟成本极高且仍是全量重算,不如增量流式高效。
对;Kafka+Flink 增量聚合最新事件,分钟级延迟写入特征库,在线快查即可,是批与纯实时之间的标准中间地带。
请求路径现算历史窗口必超 20ms 预算,正是流式要替代的做法。
放弃有价值的新鲜信号会损失精度,流式本可低成本拿到它。
optionExplanations_en: Compressing batch to per-minute is very costly and still full recompute, less efficient than incremental streaming.
Correct — Kafka+Flink incrementally aggregate fresh events into the feature store with minutes' delay for online lookup, the standard middle ground.
Live window aggregation on the request path blows the 20ms budget — exactly what streaming replaces.
Dropping a valuable fresh signal costs accuracy that streaming could capture cheaply.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式事件流平台,承载点击/曝光等实时事件,供 Flink 消费聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed event-streaming platform carrying real-time events like clicks/impressions for Flink to consume and aggregate.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式流处理引擎,对 Kafka 事件做近实时增量聚合,产出分钟级新鲜特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Flink is a distributed stream-processing engine that incrementally aggregates Kafka events into minute-fresh features.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 规模假设:10 亿用户、1000 万活跃广告、峰值 500K QPS。你要估算特征总存储。
scenario_en: Scale: 1B users, 10M active ads, 500K QPS peak. You estimate total feature storage.
q: 量化后特征总存储大概多少,怎么落地部署?
q_en: Roughly what is total feature storage after quantization, and how is it deployed?
why: 量化后总量约 270 GB:用户 embedding 64GB + 用户画像 200GB + 广告部分约 8GB。放不进单机,要用分片 Redis 集群 + 副本承载。
why_en: About 270 GB after quantization (user embeddings 64 GB int8, user profiles 200 GB, ad embeddings 2.56 GB, ad metadata 5 GB), too big for one node, so a sharded Redis cluster with replication.
options: 只把用户 embedding 单独一项拿来估算:约 4 GB,单台机器内存就能全部放下
各分项相加合计约 270 GB(量化后),放不进单机,要用分片 Redis 集群 + 副本承载
把用户和广告的全部原始特征都算进去:约 10 TB,必须全部落盘、彻底放弃内存服务
只统计用户 embedding 这一项:约 256 GB,广告与画像部分不计入这次估算
options_en: Estimating from the user-embedding item alone: about 4 GB, fitting entirely in one machine's memory.
Summing all parts gives about 270 GB after quantization, too big for one node, served by a sharded Redis cluster with replication.
Counting every raw user and ad feature in full: about 10 TB, forcing everything onto disk and abandoning in-memory serving.
Counting only the user-embedding item: about 256 GB, leaving the ad and profile parts out of this estimate.
optionExplanations: 4 GB 远远不够,光量化后的用户 embedding 就 64 GB,加画像 200 GB。
对;各项相加约 270 GB,超单机内存,分片 Redis + 副本既扩容量又保可用,是标准落地。
10 TB 高估了,量化后是几百 GB 量级,仍可内存分片服务不必全落盘。
用户画像 200 GB 同样是大头,不能只算 embedding 忽略其余。
optionExplanations_en: 4 GB is far too little; quantized user embeddings alone are 64 GB plus 200 GB of profiles.
Correct — the parts sum to ~270 GB, over one node's memory, so a sharded Redis cluster with replicas scales capacity and availability — the standard deployment.
10 TB overestimates; after quantization it is hundreds of GB, still shardable in memory without going all-disk.
User profiles at 200 GB are also a big share; you cannot count only embeddings.

termDefinitions.term: sharded Redis cluster / 分片 Redis 集群
termDefinitions.meaning: 把特征数据按 key 切分到多台 Redis 节点,突破单机内存上限,加副本保可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sharded Redis cluster splits feature data by key across nodes to exceed single-machine memory, with replicas for availability.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 峰值 500K QPS,每次广告请求平均要向特征库发约 3 次查询。
scenario_en: At 500K QPS peak, each ad request issues about 3 feature-store lookups.
q: 特征库要扛多大读吞吐,这个数怎么算、用来做什么?
q_en: What read throughput must the feature store sustain, how is it computed, and what for?
why: 公式:500K QPS × 3 次查询 = 150 万次读/秒;每次约 300 字节 → 约 450 MB/s。这个吞吐是估读侧规模的基数——据此推出需要约 10 节点的 Redis 集群配读副本才扛得住。
why_en: 500K QPS × 3 lookups = 1.5M reads/sec, ~300 B each → ~450 MB/s, the read-scale base that sizes the cluster (about 10 Redis nodes with read replicas).
options: 约 5 万次读/秒,单个最普通的 Redis 节点就绰绰有余,完全不需要做任何分片处理和扩容准备
约 150 万次读/秒(500K×3),约 450 MB/s,据此配约 10 节点 Redis + 读副本
约 500 次读/秒,把读吞吐和请求 QPS、每请求查询次数都当成两件完全无关的独立事情来看
约 5 亿次读/秒,认为再怎么扩大集群规模、加多少台机器都扛不住,只能彻底放弃特征库这条路
options_en: About 50K reads/sec, comfortably handled by one plain Redis node with absolutely no sharding or scaling preparation needed at all.
About 1.5M reads/sec (500K×3), ~450 MB/s, sizing about 10 Redis nodes with read replicas.
About 500 reads/sec, treating read throughput and request QPS or lookups-per-request as two entirely separate, unrelated things to consider.
About 500M reads/sec, deemed unbearable no matter how many machines the cluster scales to, so the feature store must be abandoned altogether.
optionExplanations: 5 万远远低估,500K×3 就是 150 万次/秒,单节点扛不住。
对;150 万读/秒、约 450 MB/s 是读侧规模基数,直接推出约 10 节点 Redis + 读副本的部署。
500 次/秒完全脱离规模,QPS×每请求查询数才是真实吞吐。
5 亿是把量级夸大百倍,150 万/秒经分片副本完全可承载。
optionExplanations_en: 50K badly underestimates; 500K×3 is 1.5M/sec, beyond a single node.
Correct — 1.5M reads/sec and ~450 MB/s is the read-scale base, directly sizing ~10 Redis nodes with read replicas.
500/sec ignores scale entirely; QPS × lookups-per-request is the real throughput.
500M inflates by 100×; 1.5M/sec is fully serviceable via sharding and replicas.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数;这里峰值 500K QPS,乘以每请求查询数得到特征库读吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) is requests per second; here 500K QPS times lookups-per-request gives feature-store read throughput.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主节点数据的只读拷贝,用来分摊读吞吐、提高可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read replica is a read-only copy of a primary's data used to spread read throughput and improve availability.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 峰值 500K QPS,若每次请求都要给约 200 个候选广告用完整模型打分。
scenario_en: At 500K QPS peak, if each request scores about 200 candidate ads with the full model.
q: 这会产生多大的打分量,推出什么架构决策?
q_en: How many scores does this produce, and what architectural decision follows?
why: 500K QPS × 200 候选 = 每秒 1 亿次模型打分。这个量级下不可能对所有候选都跑重模型,正是为什么必须两段式:先便宜检索把上千候选收窄,只对约 200 个跑排序模型。
why_en: 500K QPS × 200 candidates = 100M model scores/sec, which no heavy model can serve for all candidates — exactly why two-stage retrieval-then-ranking is essential.
options: 每秒约 50 万次打分,认为单个重模型自己就能轻松扛住、完全不需要两段式架构
每秒约 1 亿次打分(500K×200),重模型扛不住全部,所以必须两段式只排约 200 候选
每秒约 200 次打分,认为打分量和请求 QPS、每次候选数量都完全没有关系
每秒约 1000 亿次打分,认为任何硬件规模都绝不可能扛住,只能干脆放弃 CTR 排序
options_en: About 500K scores/sec, judged easily handled by a single heavy model on its own with no two-stage architecture needed at all.
About 100M scores/sec (500K×200), unbearable for a heavy model on all, so two-stage ranking of ~200 candidates is essential.
About 200 scores/sec, treating score volume as having nothing to do with either request QPS or the candidate count per request.
About 100 billion scores/sec, judged absolutely impossible for any hardware scale, so CTR ranking must simply be dropped.
optionExplanations: 50 万漏乘了候选数,真实是 500K×200=1 亿次/秒,单模型全量打分扛不住。
对;1 亿次/秒的打分逼出两段式——检索先粗筛,重模型只打约 200 个候选,才进得了延迟与算力预算。
200 次/秒完全脱离规模,QPS×候选数才是真实打分量。
1000 亿高估了三个数量级,1 亿次/秒经两段式完全可行。
optionExplanations_en: 500K omits the candidate factor; the real figure is 500K×200=100M/sec, beyond one model scoring all.
Correct — 100M scores/sec forces two-stage: retrieval coarse-filters and the heavy model scores only ~200, fitting latency and compute.
200/sec ignores scale; QPS × candidates is the real score count.
100 billion overstates by three orders; 100M/sec is feasible via two-stage.

termDefinitions.term: model scores per second / 每秒打分量
termDefinitions.meaning: QPS × 每请求候选数,衡量推理侧总负载,过高时逼出两段式检索-排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model scores per second is QPS times candidates-per-request, the inference-side load that forces two-stage retrieval-ranking when high.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 面试官抛出杀手锏追问:「你怎么给十亿用户在 20ms 内提供用户特征?」
scenario_en: The interviewer drops the killer follow-up: 'How do you serve user features for a billion users under 20ms?'
q: 该怎么组织这套回答的骨架?
q_en: How do you structure the backbone of this answer?
why: 骨架三件套:①历史聚合特征预计算进特征库快查、②高基数 embedding 用哈希/量化压进内存、③分片 Redis + 副本扛吞吐;上下文特征实时取。用「预计算+压缩+分片」正面回答延迟与规模。
why_en: Precompute history features into a low-latency feature store, compress high-cardinality embeddings (hashing/quantization) to fit serving memory, and shard Redis with replicas for throughput — while context features come real-time from the request.
tradeoff: 预计算+压缩+分片(20ms 内可服务十亿用户) vs 请求路径现算(简单但必超时)
whenOtherWins: 如果用户量只有百万级、特征也不大,单个内存 KV 直接查就够,不必上分片+压缩这套重装。
options: 每次请求都现场重新算一遍这个用户的完整历史聚合,单纯靠不断堆机器硬把延迟压到 20ms 以内不超时
预计算进特征库快查 + 压缩 embedding 进内存 + 分片 Redis 配副本扛吞吐,上下文特征实时取
把十亿用户的全部历史特征都直接烘焙进模型权重里存起来,推理时完全不查任何外部存储系统
让每一次用户请求都同步训练出一个专属这个用户自己的小模型,训练完成之后再拿这个小模型来打分
options_en: Recompute this user's entire history aggregation live on every single request, relying purely on piling on more and more machines to hit 20ms without timing out.
Precompute into a fast feature store + compress embeddings into memory + sharded Redis with replicas for throughput, with context features real-time.
Bake every one of a billion users' entire history features directly into the model's weights so inference queries no external store system at all.
Synchronously train a small model dedicated to each individual user on every single request, then use that freshly trained small model to score.
optionExplanations: 现算历史聚合扫日志必超 20ms,加机器也压不进请求路径的重聚合。
对;预计算+压缩+分片三管齐下,把历史特征快查、embedding 放进内存、吞吐用副本扛,正面解掉延迟与规模。
把十亿用户特征塞进权重不现实,模型会爆炸且无法更新用户级信息。
每请求训模型完全不可行,延迟和成本都无穷大。
optionExplanations_en: Live history aggregation scans logs and must exceed 20ms; machines cannot fit heavy aggregation on the request path.
Correct — precompute + compress + shard together fast-lookup history, fit embeddings in memory, and sustain throughput via replicas, directly solving latency and scale.
Baking a billion users' features into weights is unrealistic; the model explodes and cannot update user-level info.
Per-request model training is infeasible, with unbounded latency and cost.

termDefinitions.term: feature serving under latency / 低延迟特征服务
termDefinitions.meaning: 在几十毫秒内为海量用户提供特征的能力,靠预计算、压缩和分片三者组合实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Low-latency feature serving is delivering features for massive user bases within tens of ms, achieved by combining precompute, compression, and sharding.

category: Ad Ctr Prediction Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 设计广告 CTR 预测：输入是稀疏类别 embedding + 稠密数值，要在 sub-100ms 内出预测。
scenario_en: Designing ad CTR prediction: input is sparse categorical embeddings plus dense numerics, predicted within sub-100ms.
q: CTR 模型设计的核心张力和三个关键决策是什么？
q_en: What is the core tension and three key decisions in CTR model design?
why: 核心张力是记忆(memorization：记住特征共现，如 user_id×advertiser_id) vs 泛化(generalization：预测没见过的组合)。三个关键决策：架构（Wide&Deep/DCN/DLRM）、校准（pCTR 要准）、多任务（CTR/CVR/LTV 联合）。选/校不好直接伤广告收入和体验。
why_en: The core tension is memorization (recalling feature co-occurrences like user_id x advertiser_id) versus generalization (predicting unseen combos), and the three decisions are architecture, calibration, and multi-task learning.
diagram:
flowchart LR M["记忆
记住共现"] --- T["核心张力"] G["泛化
预测新组合"] --- T T --> D1["架构"] T --> D2["校准"] T --> D3["多任务"]
options: 核心是模型参数量 vs 学习率，三决策是数据/框架/机房
核心张力=记忆(记共现) vs 泛化(预测新组合)；三决策=架构、校准、多任务
核心是前端 vs 后端，三决策是配色/字体/布局
没有张力，堆大模型就能同时做到记忆和泛化
options_en: Core is params vs learning rate; three decisions are data/framework/datacenter.
Core tension = memorization (recall co-occurrences) vs generalization (predict new combos); three decisions = architecture, calibration, multi-task.
Core is frontend vs backend; three decisions are colors/fonts/layout.
No tension; a big model does both memorization and generalization.
optionExplanations: 参数量/学习率是训练细节，不是 CTR 设计的核心张力与决策。
对；记忆 vs 泛化是主轴，架构/校准/多任务是三大设计决策。
前后端与 CTR 建模的记忆-泛化张力无关。
记忆和泛化有内在取舍，不是堆大模型就能免费兼得。
optionExplanations_en: Params/learning rate are training details, not CTR's core tension and decisions.
Correct — memorization vs generalization is the axis, with architecture/calibration/multi-task the three decisions.
Frontend/backend is unrelated to the memorization-generalization tension.
Memorization and generalization inherently trade off; a big model doesn't get both for free.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率：展示中被点击的比例，广告排序的核心预测目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions clicked, the core prediction target in ad ranking.

termDefinitions.term: memorization vs generalization / 记忆 vs 泛化
termDefinitions.meaning: 记忆=记住特征共现(user×advertiser)，泛化=预测没见过的组合，两者需在架构里平衡。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Memorization recalls feature co-occurrences (user x advertiser); generalization predicts unseen combos — balanced in the architecture.

scenario: 面试官让你讲 Wide & Deep（Google 2016）怎么同时兼顾记忆和泛化。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how Wide & Deep (Google 2016) balances memorization and generalization.
q: Wide & Deep 的 wide 侧和 deep 侧各干什么？
q_en: What do the wide and deep sides of Wide & Deep each do?
why: wide 侧是线性模型，吃原始特征+人工交叉特征，负责记忆（记住 user_id×advertiser_id 这类强共现）；deep 侧是前馈 NN，吃稠密 embedding，负责泛化（推没见过的组合）。两侧联合训练、合成一个 logistic loss。
why_en: The wide side is a linear model over raw plus manual cross features that memorizes strong co-occurrences (user_id x advertiser_id), while the deep side is a feedforward NN over dense embeddings that generalizes, jointly trained with a combined logistic loss.
diagram:
flowchart TB R["原始+人工交叉特征"] --> W["wide 线性
记忆"] E["稠密 embedding"] --> D["deep NN
泛化"] W --> J["联合 logistic loss"] D --> J
options: wide 侧线性吃人工交叉特征做记忆，deep 侧 NN 吃 embedding 做泛化，联合训练合成 logistic loss
wide 和 deep 都做泛化，没有记忆能力
wide 侧是深层 NN，deep 侧是线性模型
两侧完全独立训练，各出各的分不合并
options_en: Wide is linear over manual crosses (memorization), deep is an NN over embeddings (generalization), jointly trained with a combined logistic loss.
Both wide and deep generalize with no memorization.
Wide is a deep NN and deep is a linear model.
The two sides train fully independently and never combine.
optionExplanations: 对；wide 记忆强共现、deep 泛化新组合，联合 logistic 训练，兼顾两端。
wide 侧的人工交叉正是为记忆而设，不是没有记忆。
说反了：wide 是线性、deep 才是 NN。
两侧联合训练共享一个 loss，不是各出各的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — wide memorizes strong co-occurrences, deep generalizes new combos, jointly logistic-trained.
The wide side's manual crosses exist for memorization — it's not memoryless.
Backwards: wide is linear, deep is the NN.
The two sides jointly train on one loss, not separately.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 2016 的 CTR 架构：wide 线性记忆人工交叉，deep NN 泛化 embedding，联合训练。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Wide & Deep (Google 2016) is a CTR architecture: a wide linear side memorizes manual crosses and a deep NN generalizes embeddings, jointly trained.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把两个类别特征组合成一个（如 user_id×advertiser_id），捕捉共现，Wide&Deep 里靠人工构造。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross feature combines two categorical features (e.g. user_id x advertiser_id) to capture co-occurrence, hand-crafted in Wide & Deep.

scenario: 随着特征空间越来越大，Wide & Deep 的 wide 侧要靠工程师手工列出所有重要的交叉特征。
scenario_en: As the feature space grows, Wide & Deep's wide side needs engineers to hand-enumerate all important cross features.
q: Wide & Deep 的主要局限是什么？
q_en: What is Wide & Deep's main limitation?
why: wide 侧的记忆能力全靠人工构造的交叉特征——特征空间一大，工程师根本枚举不完所有有用组合，这成了特征工程瓶颈。DCN 正是为自动学交叉、绕开这个瓶颈而生。
why_en: The wide side's power depends on hand-crafted crosses, so as the space grows engineers can't enumerate all useful combinations, creating a feature-engineering bottleneck that DCN was built to remove.
options: wide 侧无法记忆任何共现，是纯泛化模型
wide 侧记忆全靠人工交叉特征，特征空间一大枚举不完，成特征工程瓶颈
Wide & Deep 无法联合训练，两侧必须分开
它只能处理稠密数值，处理不了类别特征
options_en: The wide side can't memorize any co-occurrence — it's pure generalization.
The wide side's memorization depends on manual crosses, unenumerable as the space grows — a feature-engineering bottleneck.
Wide & Deep can't be jointly trained; the sides must be separate.
It only handles dense numerics, not categorical features.
optionExplanations: wide 侧恰恰靠人工交叉做记忆，不是纯泛化。
对；人工枚举交叉在大特征空间不可行，正是 DCN 要自动化解决的瓶颈。
Wide&Deep 本来就是联合训练，这不是它的局限。
它处理类别特征（靠 embedding+交叉），不是只能稠密数值。
optionExplanations_en: The wide side memorizes via manual crosses — not pure generalization.
Correct — manual cross enumeration is infeasible in a large space, the bottleneck DCN automates.
Wide & Deep is jointly trained by design — not a limitation.
It handles categoricals (via embeddings + crosses), not only dense numerics.

termDefinitions.term: feature-engineering bottleneck / 特征工程瓶颈
termDefinitions.meaning: 模型能力依赖人工构造特征，特征空间增大后人力枚举跟不上，成为扩展瓶颈。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature-engineering bottleneck is when model power depends on hand-crafted features that humans can't enumerate as the space grows.

scenario: 你不想再人工枚举交叉特征，希望模型自动学到特征之间的高阶交互，且不引发组合爆炸。
scenario_en: You want the model to learn feature interactions automatically without manual crosses or combinatorial explosion.
q: 该选哪种架构，它靠什么替代人工交叉？
q_en: Which architecture fits, and what replaces manual crosses?
why: 选 DCN：cross network 每层做 x_{l+1}=x0·x_l^T·w+b+x_l，随层数显式学多项式阶交互，不用手工枚举也不组合爆炸。deep 侧仍是普通 MLP。
why_en: Choose DCN: a cross network computes x_{l+1}=x0 x_l^T w + b + x_l per layer, learning explicit polynomial-order interactions without manual enumeration or explosion. The deep side stays a plain MLP.
tradeoff: DCN cross network（自动学交叉、低特征工程） vs Wide&Deep 人工交叉（要手工枚举、特征工程重）
options: 选 Wide & Deep，继续靠人工把更多有效的交叉特征一个个列举出来补齐
选 DCN：cross network 每层显式学多项式阶交互替代人工交叉，不组合爆炸
选纯线性回归，只要模型结构足够简单、参数足够少就够用了
选只做 embedding 查表、完全不建模任何特征之间交互关系的模型
options_en: Choose Wide & Deep, and keep hand-enumerating even more effective cross features one by one by hand to fill every gap.
Choose DCN: a cross network learns explicit polynomial interactions per layer, replacing manual crosses without explosion.
Choose pure linear regression, as long as the model stays simple with as few parameters as possible.
Choose a model that only does embedding lookups and models absolutely no interaction between any of the input features at all.
whenOtherWins: 如果你其实已经知道少数几个极强的交叉（如某垂类里 user×advertiser 就是决定性的），直接用 Wide & Deep 手工放进 wide 侧更简单直接，不必上 cross network。
whenOtherWins_en: If you already know a few dominant crosses (user x advertiser decisive in a vertical), placing them in Wide & Deep's wide side is simpler than a cross network.
optionExplanations: 人工列更多交叉正是要避免的特征工程瓶颈，这条路只会越走越窄。
对：显式多项式交互随层数自动生长，省掉了人工枚举那一步。
纯线性只能给一次线性组合，学不到特征之间的交互效应。
只查表没有交互步骤，会丢掉 CTR 最关键的特征共现信号。
optionExplanations_en: Enumerating more crosses by hand is exactly the feature-engineering trap this choice should avoid.
Correct — interaction depth grows layer by layer on its own, with no manual list-building required.
Pure linear only gives one linear combination and can't learn feature interactions at all.
Lookup-only skips the interaction step, dropping CTR's most important co-occurrence signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 cross network 自动学显式多项式特征交互（x_{l+1}=x0·x_l^T·w+b+x_l）替代人工交叉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN (Deep & Cross Network) uses a cross network to automatically learn explicit polynomial feature interactions, replacing manual crosses.

termDefinitions.meaning: DCN 的核心层，逐层做特征外积与残差，显式建模到层数的多项式交互，无组合爆炸。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The cross network is DCN's core, applying feature outer products with residuals per layer to model polynomial interactions up to its depth without explosion.

scenario: DCN 的 cross layer 用一个向量权重 w，你想要更强的交互表达力。
scenario_en: DCN's cross layer uses a vector weight w, and you want more interaction expressiveness.
q: DCN-v2 相对原始 DCN 改了什么？
q_en: What does DCN-v2 change versus original DCN?
why: DCN-v2 把 cross layer 里的向量权重 w 换成矩阵 W：向量权重只能给每维一个标量缩放，矩阵能建模维度之间更丰富的交互组合，表达力更强，代价是参数更多。
why_en: DCN-v2 replaces the cross layer's vector weight w with a matrix W, so instead of a per-dimension scalar it models richer cross-dimension interactions with more expressiveness at the cost of more parameters.
options: 把向量权重 w 换成矩阵 W，建模更丰富的维度间交互，表达力更强
彻底删掉 cross network，只保留 deep 侧
把 deep 侧从 MLP 换成线性模型
去掉残差项，让每层不再累加 x_l
options_en: Replaces vector weight w with a matrix W for richer cross-dimension interactions and more expressiveness.
Removes the cross network entirely, keeping only the deep side.
Changes the deep side from an MLP to a linear model.
Drops the residual so layers no longer add x_l.
optionExplanations: 对；向量→矩阵权重让 cross layer 表达维度间更复杂的交互。
DCN-v2 强化的正是 cross network，不是删掉它。
deep 侧仍是 MLP，v2 改的是 cross layer 权重。
残差是 cross network 稳定训练的关键，v2 没去掉它。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — vector to matrix weight lets the cross layer express more complex cross-dimension interactions.
DCN-v2 strengthens the cross network, not removes it.
The deep side stays an MLP; v2 changes the cross-layer weight.
The residual is key to stable cross-network training; v2 keeps it.

termDefinitions.meaning: DCN 的改进版，把 cross layer 的向量权重 w 升级为矩阵 W，提升交互表达力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN-v2 upgrades DCN's cross-layer vector weight w to a matrix W for greater interaction expressiveness.

scenario: 面试官让你讲 DLRM（Meta 2019）的数据流：稀疏和稠密特征分别怎么走。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to trace DLRM's (Meta 2019) data flow for sparse and dense features.
q: DLRM 的结构和数据流是什么？
q_en: What is DLRM's structure and data flow?
why: DLRM：稠密特征走 bottom MLP；稀疏特征走 embedding 查表；两者所有 pairwise dot-product 交互 → 与 bottom MLP 输出拼接 → top MLP 出预测。它为超大 embedding 表而生，天然对应模型并行服务（表分片到多 GPU）。
why_en: DLRM sends dense features through a bottom MLP and sparse features through embedding lookups, takes all pairwise dot-product interactions, concatenates with the bottom MLP, and passes through a top MLP.
diagram:
flowchart TB
  D["稠密特征"] --> B["bottom MLP"]
  S["稀疏特征"] --> L["embedding 查表"]
  B --> X["pairwise 点积交互"]
  L --> X
  X --> T["top MLP → pCTR"]
options: 稠密走 bottom MLP、稀疏走 embedding 查表，所有 pairwise 点积交互→拼接→top MLP 出预测
所有特征都直接线性相加，不做任何交互
只用稀疏特征，稠密数值一律丢弃
稠密和稀疏各训一个独立模型不合并
options_en: Dense through a bottom MLP, sparse through embedding lookups, all pairwise dot-product interactions, concatenate, then a top MLP.
All features are just linearly summed with no interactions.
Only sparse features are used; dense numerics are discarded.
Dense and sparse train separate models that never merge.
optionExplanations: 对；DLRM 的核心是稠密 MLP+稀疏 embedding+pairwise 点积交互，再过 top MLP。
线性相加学不到特征交互，不是 DLRM。
DLRM 稠密数值走 bottom MLP，不丢弃。
稠密和稀疏在交互层合并，不是各自独立。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — DLRM's core is dense MLP + sparse embeddings + pairwise dot-product interactions, then a top MLP.
Linear summation learns no interactions — not DLRM.
DLRM sends dense numerics through the bottom MLP, not discarded.
Dense and sparse merge at the interaction layer, not independent.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 2019 架构，为超大 embedding 表设计：稠密走 MLP、稀疏走查表、pairwise 点积交互后过 top MLP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DLRM (Deep Learning Recommendation Model, Meta 2019) is built for massive embedding tables: dense via MLP, sparse via lookups, pairwise dot-product interactions, then a top MLP.

scenario: 你的 CTR 系统里 embedding 表大到几百 GB，装不进单张 GPU 显存。
scenario_en: Your CTR system's embedding tables are hundreds of GB, too big for one GPU.
q: 这种「embedding 表主导体量」的场景该选哪种架构，怎么服务？
q_en: For 'embedding tables dominate size', which architecture fits, and how to serve?
why: 选 DLRM：它就是为超大 embedding 表设计的，天然对应模型并行服务——把 embedding 表按 key 分片到多张 GPU，各存一部分、查表时并行取。当表到几百 GB、单卡放不下时，这是必需的部署形态。
why_en: Choose DLRM: built for massive embedding tables and mapping naturally to model-parallel serving, where tables are sharded across GPUs so each holds part and lookups run in parallel — necessary when tables reach hundreds of GB.
tradeoff: DLRM+模型并行（扛几百 GB embedding 表） vs 单卡稠密模型（表放不下、无法服务）
options: 选 Wide & Deep，人工交叉能压缩表大小
选纯线性模型，不需要 embedding
选 DLRM+模型并行：embedding 表分片到多 GPU 各存一部分、并行查表，扛几百 GB
把 embedding 表全塞进一张 GPU，加显存条即可
options_en: Choose Wide & Deep; manual crosses shrink the tables.
Choose a pure linear model needing no embeddings.
Choose DLRM + model parallelism: shard embedding tables across GPUs, each holding part with parallel lookups, handling hundreds of GB.
Cram the tables into one GPU; just add VRAM.
whenOtherWins: 如果 embedding 表其实不大、能装进单卡，模型体量由别处主导，那用 DCN 等更简单的标准服务架构就够，不必上模型并行的复杂度。
whenOtherWins_en: If embedding tables are small and fit one GPU, and size is dominated elsewhere, simpler standard-serving architectures like DCN suffice without model-parallel complexity.
optionExplanations: 人工交叉不能把几百 GB 的 embedding 表压小，答非所问。
纯线性没有 embedding 表达力，处理不了海量稀疏特征。
对；DLRM 对应模型并行，把大表分片到多 GPU，是几百 GB 表的标准部署。
几百 GB 超过单卡显存物理上限，加显存条也塞不下。
optionExplanations_en: Manual crosses can't shrink hundreds-of-GB embedding tables — misses the point.
Pure linear lacks embedding power and can't handle massive sparse features.
Correct — DLRM maps to model parallelism, sharding big tables across GPUs, the standard deployment for hundreds of GB.
Hundreds of GB exceed one GPU's physical VRAM; adding sticks won't fit it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一个模型（这里是超大 embedding 表）分片到多张 GPU，各存一部分、并行计算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Model parallelism shards one model (here huge embedding tables) across GPUs, each holding part and computing in parallel.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存所有类别特征取值向量的大表，稀疏特征查表取向量，海量类别时可达几百 GB。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding table stores vectors for all categorical values; sparse features look up vectors, reaching hundreds of GB with huge cardinality.

scenario: 面试官让你横向比较 Wide&Deep、DCN、DLRM 在记忆、特征工程量、服务上的差异。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks you to compare Wide & Deep, DCN, and DLRM on memorization, feature-eng effort, and serving.
q: 三种 CTR 架构在特征工程量和服务上的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What are the core differences among the three CTR architectures on feature-eng effort and serving?
why: Wide&Deep 人工交叉→工程高；DCN 自动学交叉→工程低；DLRM 靠点积交互+超大表→工程中、需模型并行。选哪个看你有没有已知强交叉、表体量多大。
why_en: Wide&Deep's manual crosses mean high feature-eng, DCN's auto-learned crosses mean low, and DLRM's dot-product interactions with huge tables mean medium feature-eng but model-parallel serving.
options: 特征工程从高到低：Wide&Deep 人工交叉最重、DCN 自动学习最省；DLRM 大表需模型并行
三者的特征工程量和服务方式其实完全一样，选哪一个架构都无所谓没差别
说反了：DCN 特征工程量号称最高最麻烦，Wide&Deep 反而号称最低最省事、几乎不用调
三者不管选哪个，据说都需要模型并行服务，彼此完全没有区别可言
options_en: Feature-eng ranks high to low: Wide&Deep manual crosses heaviest, DCN auto-learning lightest; DLRM needs model parallelism for its huge tables.
All three actually have identical feature-eng effort and serving setup; it doesn't matter which one you pick at all.
