options_en: It is a formula result obtained by summing the four stages' measured latencies and back-deriving.
As long as accuracy is high enough, the budget can be exceeded freely; latency is never a hard constraint.
It is a given SLO: query understanding 10-30, retrieval 50-100, ranking 30-60, rendering 20-40ms.
The budget constrains only the retrieval stage, with no cap on the other three stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标：产品/体验定的性能红线（这里 sub-200ms），是给定目标不是推导结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a product-set performance target (here sub-200ms), a given goal rather than a derived number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把端到端延迟红线拆分到各阶段的分配，约束每阶段模型能多重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency budget splits the end-to-end latency ceiling across stages, capping how heavy each stage's model can be.

optionExplanations: 错；SLO 是产品/体验先定的红线，不是拿实测延迟反推出来的公式结果，因果说反了。
错；sub-200ms 是硬约束，超了会被生产评审拒，不是可以随便突破的软指标。
对；这就是给定的服务级目标，四段粗分 10–30/50–100/30–60/20–40ms，约束每阶段模型能多重。
错；四个阶段各有自己的份额，渲染、排序、理解一样要卡在预算内，不是只管检索。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — the SLO is a product/UX target set in advance, not a formula back-derived from measured latencies; this reverses cause and effect.
Wrong — sub-200ms is a hard constraint that prod review rejects breaches of, not a soft number you can freely exceed.
Correct — it's a given service-level target broken into four rough slices (10-30 / 50-100 / 30-60 / 20-40ms), and that division caps model weight per phase.
Wrong — every stage gets its own slice; rendering, ranking, and the query stage are just as bounded as retrieval, not exempt.

scenario: 延迟预算里，检索（ANN over dense embeddings）分到 50–100ms，是四个阶段里最大的一块。
scenario_en: In the latency budget, retrieval (ANN over dense embeddings) gets 50-100ms, the largest of the four stages.
q: 为什么检索阶段既是最大延迟块、又最容易出漂移？
q_en: Why is retrieval both the largest latency chunk and the most drift-prone stage?
why: 检索要在十亿级向量上做 ANN 召回，天生是四阶段里最重的一块（50–100ms）；同时它依赖 query encoder 和 doc 向量在同一空间，一旦重训编码器就会 embedding drift，两端不兼容、召回退化。所以它既吃延迟又吃漂移风险。
why_en: Retrieval runs ANN over billions of vectors, inherently the heaviest stage (50-100ms), and depends on query and doc vectors sharing one space, so retraining the encoder causes embedding drift and degraded recall — carrying both latency and drift risk.
options: 因为渲染要等检索返回，检索只是被动背锅，本身既不慢也不会漂移
它在十亿级向量上做 ANN 天生最重；又依赖查询和文档同空间，重训编码器就漂移
因为检索阶段跑的是最贵的 cross-encoder 精排模型，所以才最慢
因为检索每次都要重新训练模型，训练时间被算进了这 50–100ms
options_en: Because rendering waits on retrieval, retrieval is just a passive scapegoat and is neither slow nor drift-prone.
ANN over billions is inherently heaviest, and it depends on query/doc sharing one space, so retraining the encoder drifts it.
Because retrieval runs the most expensive cross-encoder re-ranking model, which is why it is slowest.
Because retrieval retrains a model each time, and the training time is counted in this 50-100ms.
optionExplanations: 检索不是背锅：在十亿向量上做 ANN 本身就最重，且编码器漂移直接砸在它头上。
对；规模让它最耗时，同空间依赖让它对 embedding drift 最敏感，两个风险叠在一个阶段。
cross-encoder 是排序阶段的事，不在检索里；检索用的是双塔向量召回。
检索是在线召回，不含训练；重训是离线的事，不占这 50–100ms 的服务延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Retrieval is no scapegoat: ANN over billions is inherently heaviest, and encoder drift lands squarely on it.
Correct — scale makes it slowest, and shared-space dependence makes it most drift-sensitive; both risks stack on one stage.
The cross-encoder is the ranking stage, not retrieval; retrieval uses two-tower vector recall.
Retrieval is online recall with no training; retraining is offline and does not occupy this 50-100ms serving latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重训查询编码器后新向量与旧文档向量落到不同区域、不兼容，召回退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift: after retraining the query encoder, new vectors land in a different region than old doc vectors, becoming incompatible and degrading recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档编码成同一空间的稠密向量，按相似度召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dense embeddings encode query and doc into one space of dense vectors, recalled by similarity.

scenario: 一个新排序模型 NDCG 更高，但排序阶段多花 +50ms，会把端到端顶破 sub-200ms 的 SLO。
scenario_en: A new ranking model has higher NDCG but adds +50ms to ranking, breaching the end-to-end sub-200ms SLO.
q: 排序更准但要 +50ms，生产评审该怎么判？
q_en: More accurate ranking but +50ms — how should the prod review rule?
why: SLO 是硬红线：NDCG 再高，只要 +50ms 顶破 sub-200ms，端到端就违约，生产评审会拒。质量和延迟是显式取舍——要么把这 50ms 从别处省回来（更快召回/剪枝），要么压缩模型，否则不上。
why_en: The SLO is a hard line: however high NDCG, +50ms breaching sub-200ms violates end-to-end latency and prod review rejects it, forcing you to reclaim the 50ms elsewhere or compress the model.
tradeoff: 更高 NDCG（排序更准）vs sub-200ms SLO（延迟红线，超了就拒）
whenOtherWins: 如果这 50ms 能在别的阶段省回来（如渲染优化、召回剪枝），端到端仍在 200ms 内，那更高 NDCG 的模型就能上。
options: 直接上线：NDCG 是北极星，排序质量优先，延迟超一点无所谓
直接上线：sub-200ms 只是建议值，生产不会真因为延迟拒模型
把 SLO 从 200ms 直接放宽到 250ms 来迁就模型，是最省事的正解
拒或改：SLO 是硬红线，要么从别处省回 50ms，要么压缩模型，否则不上
options_en: Ship it: NDCG is the north-star, ranking quality wins, and a little latency overage is fine.
Ship it: sub-200ms is just advisory, and prod will not really reject a model over latency.
Just loosen the SLO from 200ms to 250ms to accommodate the model — the easiest right answer.
Reject or revise: the SLO is hard — reclaim the 50ms elsewhere or compress the model, else no ship.
optionExplanations: NDCG 高但顶破 SLO，用户等更久、体验崩，生产评审不会为一点排序质量放行。
sub-200ms 是硬 SLO 不是建议；真实评审会因为顶破延迟预算直接拒。
随手放宽 SLO 是把体验红线让给模型，除非有产品依据，否则不能这么迁就。
对；先想办法把 50ms 从召回/渲染省回来或压缩模型，省不回来就不上，延迟是硬约束。
optionExplanations_en: High NDCG that breaches the SLO makes users wait longer and wrecks UX; prod review will not pass it for a little ranking gain.
sub-200ms is a hard SLO, not advice; a real review rejects a model that breaches the latency budget.
Casually loosening the SLO hands the UX line to the model; without product justification you cannot accommodate it this way.
Correct — first reclaim the 50ms from recall/rendering or compress the model; if you cannot, do not ship — latency is a hard constraint.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级目标：给定的性能红线（sub-200ms），超了就拒，不是可推导数字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLO (Service Level Objective) is a given performance line (sub-200ms) that rejects on breach, not a derivable number.

termDefinitions.meaning: 离线排序质量指标，0–1 分；再高也不能违反延迟 SLO。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is an offline 0-1 ranking metric; however high, it cannot violate the latency SLO.

scenario: 你重训了 query encoder，新查询向量落在和旧文档向量不同的语义区域——文档索引还是旧模型编码的。
scenario_en: You retrained the query encoder; new query vectors land in a different region than the doc vectors, which were indexed by the old model.
q: embedding drift 的完整机制和后果是什么？
q_en: What is the full mechanism and consequence of embedding drift?
why: 正常路径：查询和文档向量在同一空间比相似度→重训 query encoder→新查询向量落到不同区域→与旧文档向量语义不兼容→召回退化。恢复动作：re-embed 整个语料（用新模型重编所有文档），代价是网页级要几天+大量算力；retrieval-specific 模型能减轻但消不掉漂移。
why_en: Normally query and doc vectors compare in one space, but retraining the query encoder moves new query vectors to an incompatible region and recall degrades; the fix is re-embedding the whole corpus at a cost of days and heavy compute.
diagram:
flowchart LR E["重训 query encoder"] --> N["新查询向量
落到不同区域"] N --> M["与旧文档向量
语义不兼容"] M --> G["召回退化"] G --> R["re-embed 整个语料
代价:数天+大算力"]
options: 重训查询编码器→新查询向量落到不同区域→与旧文档向量不兼容→召回退化，需 re-embed 全库
重训只会让查询向量更准，文档向量会自动跟着一起更新，不存在不兼容
drift 只是让检索延迟变高，召回结果本身不受影响，加机器即可解决
drift 指索引磁盘碎片化，做一次 compaction 压缩就能恢复
options_en: Retrain query encoder -> new query vectors in a different region -> incompatible with old doc vectors -> recall degrades, needing full re-embed.
Retraining only makes query vectors more accurate, and doc vectors auto-update along with them, so no incompatibility arises.
Drift merely raises retrieval latency; the recall results themselves are unaffected, and adding machines fixes it.
Drift means index disk fragmentation, recoverable with a single compaction pass.
optionExplanations: 对；查询侧换了模型、文档侧没换，两端不在同一空间，召回退化，只能重编全库文档对齐。
文档向量不会自动更新——它们是旧模型编码后固化在索引里的，这正是不兼容的根源。
drift 砸的是召回质量不是延迟：向量对不齐，加机器也召回错的东西。
这不是磁盘碎片；是查询和文档向量语义空间错位，compaction 完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the query side changed models but the doc side did not, so they leave the shared space and recall degrades, fixable only by re-embedding the corpus.
Doc vectors do not auto-update — they are frozen in the index from the old model, which is the very source of incompatibility.
Drift hits recall quality, not latency: with vectors misaligned, more machines just recall the wrong things.
This is not disk fragmentation; it is a semantic-space mismatch between query and doc vectors, and compaction is irrelevant.

termDefinitions.meaning: 重训查询编码器后新旧向量落到不同区域、语义不兼容，召回退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift: after retraining the query encoder, new and old vectors land in different, incompatible regions and recall degrades.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询编码成向量的模型；换了它就与旧文档向量不在同一空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The query encoder maps a query to a vector; swapping it leaves it out of the old doc vectors' space.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新模型把整个语料的文档重新编码，让两端回到同一空间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-embedding re-encodes the entire corpus with the new model so query and doc share one space again.

termDefinitions.term: retrieval-specific model / 检索专用模型
termDefinitions.meaning: 专为检索稳定性训练的编码器，能减轻但不能消除漂移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retrieval-specific model is an encoder trained for retrieval stability, reducing but not eliminating drift.

scenario: query encoder 升级后出现 embedding drift，旧文档向量和新查询向量对不齐，召回在退化。
scenario_en: After a query-encoder upgrade, embedding drift misaligns old doc vectors with new query vectors and retrieval is degrading.
q: 最彻底的缓解手段是什么，代价是什么？
q_en: What is the most thorough mitigation, and at what cost?
why: 最彻底是 re-embed 整个语料——用新编码器把所有文档重编一遍，让两端回到同一空间；代价是网页级几天+巨额算力。用 retrieval-specific 模型（专为检索稳定训练）能减轻漂移，但不能消除，仍需定期重编。
why_en: The most thorough fix is re-embedding the whole corpus with the new encoder to realign both sides, at a cost of days and heavy compute at web scale, while retrieval-specific models reduce but do not eliminate drift.
tradeoff: 全量 re-embed（彻底对齐、几天+大算力）vs retrieval-specific 模型（减轻不消除、省算力）
whenOtherWins: 如果语料小、重编便宜，或漂移轻微、召回退化在容忍范围内，可以先靠 retrieval-specific 模型顶着、延后全量重编，省算力。
options: 回滚到旧的 query encoder，永远不升级模型，drift 就永远不会发生
只重编最近更新过的文档，其余旧向量放着不管也能对齐
re-embed 整个语料，用新编码器重编所有文档回到同空间，代价是几天+大算力
给 ANN 索引加更多副本，用横向扩容来抵消 drift 带来的召回退化
options_en: Roll back to the old query encoder and never upgrade, so drift never happens.
Re-embed only recently updated docs and leave the rest of the old vectors alone — still aligned.
Re-embed the whole corpus with the new encoder back into one space, at a cost of days and heavy compute.
Add more ANN replicas and use horizontal scaling to offset drift's recall degradation.
optionExplanations: 永不升级等于放弃模型改进，drift 是升级的副作用，不能靠冻结模型来假装解决。
只重编部分文档，剩下的旧向量仍和新查询不兼容，语义错位没修好。
对；全量重编让文档和查询回到同一空间，是最彻底的解，代价是网页级几天和大量算力。
加副本只提吞吐/可用性，向量对不齐加多少副本都召回错的，扩容治不了 drift。
optionExplanations_en: Never upgrading forsakes model improvement; drift is a side effect of upgrading, not solved by freezing the model.
Re-embedding only some docs leaves the rest's old vectors incompatible with new queries — the mismatch stays.
Correct — full re-embedding returns docs and queries to one space, the most thorough fix, at a cost of web-scale days and heavy compute.
Replicas only raise throughput/availability; with vectors misaligned, any number of replicas recalls the wrong things — scaling cannot cure drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新模型重编整个语料的文档，是消除漂移最彻底的手段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-embedding re-encodes the whole corpus with the new model, the most thorough way to eliminate drift.

termDefinitions.term: retrieval-specific model / 检索专用模型
termDefinitions.meaning: 为检索稳定性训练的编码器，减轻漂移但不能消除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retrieval-specific model is trained for retrieval stability, reducing but not eliminating drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编码器升级后新旧向量不在同一空间，召回退化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift is when an encoder upgrade leaves new and old vectors out of one space, degrading recall.

scenario: 搜索要扛数万 QPS 的在线流量，单个 ANN 实例扛不住。
scenario_en: Search must handle tens of thousands of QPS, more than one ANN instance can serve.
q: 数万 QPS 的吞吐要求逼出哪些系统设计？
q_en: What system designs does tens-of-thousands QPS force?
why: 数万 QPS（每秒查询数）单实例扛不住，要横向扩 ANN 副本（同一索引多副本分摊查询）、前面加负载均衡分流、并做 failover 保证单副本挂了不影响可用性。吞吐是给定量级，决定副本数和容错设计。
why_en: Tens of thousands of QPS overwhelm one instance, so you horizontally scale ANN replicas sharing the query load, put load balancing in front, and add failover so a dead replica does not break availability.
options: 把 ANN 索引压进单机内存，靠垂直扩容一台大机器扛住全部 QPS
横向扩 ANN 副本分摊查询，前置负载均衡分流，做 failover 保可用
给每个查询排队串行处理，用队列削峰就能扛住数万 QPS
提高单次查询的 top-k，让每次多返回结果来减少查询次数
options_en: Cram the ANN index into one machine's memory and vertically scale a single big box to serve all QPS.
Horizontally scale ANN replicas to share load, front them with load balancing, and add failover for availability.
Queue and serially process each query — peak-shaving with a queue handles tens of thousands of QPS.
Raise each query's top-k to return more results and thereby reduce the number of queries.
optionExplanations: 垂直扩一台机器有物理上限，数万 QPS 单机内存和 CPU 都顶不住，必须横向扩副本。
对；多副本分摊 QPS、负载均衡分流、failover 兜底，是高吞吐检索的标准三件套。
串行排队会把延迟拉爆，顶破 sub-200ms SLO；削峰不等于能扛住持续的高吞吐。
加大 top-k 不减少查询次数，反而让每次更重，和吞吐问题南辕北辙。
optionExplanations_en: Vertical scaling on one box hits a physical ceiling; tens of thousands of QPS exceed single-box memory and CPU, so replicate horizontally.
Correct — replicas sharing QPS, load balancing, and failover are the standard trio for high-throughput retrieval.
Serial queuing blows latency past the sub-200ms SLO; peak-shaving does not equal sustaining high throughput.
Raising top-k does not cut query count and makes each query heavier — the opposite of what throughput needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询数，衡量在线吞吐；数万 QPS 决定副本数和容错设计。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS (Queries Per Second) measures online throughput; tens of thousands of QPS set replica count and fault-tolerance design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加更多同构副本分摊负载，而非把单机做大（垂直扩容）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Horizontal scaling adds more identical replicas to share load, rather than enlarging one machine (vertical scaling).

termDefinitions.meaning: 某副本挂掉时把流量切到健康副本，保住可用性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Failover reroutes traffic to healthy replicas when one dies, preserving availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询在多副本间分流，避免单副本过载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load balancing spreads queries across replicas to avoid overloading any one.

scenario: L5 要讲清召回和精排为什么用不同的编码器结构。
scenario_en: At L5 you must explain why recall and re-ranking use different encoder structures.
q: dual-encoder 召回和 cross-encoder 精排差在哪一维？
q_en: On what dimension do a dual-encoder for recall and a cross-encoder for re-ranking differ?
why: dual-encoder（双塔）分别编码查询和文档，可离线预算文档向量、在线只算查询向量做 ANN，快但精度低；cross-encoder 把查询和文档拼在一起联合编码，能建模细粒度交互、精度高，但每对都要在线算、贵，只能用在召回后的少量候选上精排。
why_en: A dual-encoder encodes query and doc separately so doc vectors precompute offline and only the query is encoded online for ANN — fast but less precise — while a cross-encoder co-encodes the pair for fine-grained interaction, precise but expensive, so it only re-ranks a few candidates.
tradeoff: dual-encoder（快、可预算、精度低）vs cross-encoder（精度高、贵、只精排少量）
options: dual-encoder 分开编码、可离线预算、快，用于大规模召回；cross-encoder 联合编码、精度高但贵，只做精排
两者网络结构完全相同，唯一区别是 dual 跑在 GPU、cross 跑在 CPU 上
cross-encoder 因为更快所以拿来做大规模召回，dual-encoder 更准所以放在精排
两者都能把全部文档向量离线预算好，在线的计算开销其实完全一样
options_en: Dual-encoder encodes separately, precomputes offline, and is fast for large-scale recall; cross-encoder co-encodes, is precise but costly, and only re-ranks.
Their networks are identical; the only difference is dual runs on GPU and cross runs on CPU.
Cross-encoder is faster so it does large-scale recall, and dual-encoder is more accurate so it does re-ranking.
Both can precompute all doc vectors offline, and their online compute cost is actually identical.
optionExplanations: 对；双塔查询文档各编各的、文档向量可离线存好，在线快；cross 拼一起算交互更准但每对都算，只精排。
结构本质不同：dual 是两座独立塔、cross 是单塔联合编码，不是 GPU/CPU 的区别。
说反了：cross 慢而准用于精排，dual 快而糙用于召回，别记颠倒。
只有 dual 能离线预算文档向量；cross 必须查询到达后才能和文档联合编码，在线开销大得多。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — two towers encode query and doc separately with doc vectors stored offline for fast online recall; cross co-encodes for precision but scores every pair, so only re-ranking.
The architectures differ fundamentally: dual is two separate towers, cross is one joint encoder — not a GPU/CPU distinction.
Reversed: cross is slow-but-precise for re-ranking, dual is fast-but-coarse for recall — do not flip them.
Only dual can precompute doc vectors offline; cross must co-encode with the doc after the query arrives, far costlier online.

termDefinitions.meaning: 查询和文档分别编码成向量，文档向量可离线预算，用于大规模召回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual-encoder (two-tower) encodes query and doc into separate vectors, precomputing doc vectors offline for large-scale recall.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把查询和文档拼在一起联合编码，建模细粒度交互，精度高但只能精排少量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder co-encodes query and doc together for fine-grained interaction, precise but only for re-ranking a few candidates.

scenario: 同一道语义搜索题，L4、L5、Staff+ 候选人被期待答出的深度不同。
scenario_en: For the same semantic-search question, L4, L5, and Staff+ candidates are expected to answer at different depths.
q: 什么最能把 Staff+ 的答法和 L4/L5 区分开？
q_en: What most distinguishes a Staff+ answer from L4/L5?
why: L4 给出问题定义+基础管道（encoder→ANN→ranker）+核心指标；L5 会拆查询理解、讲 dual vs cross-encoder 取舍、把 drift 当运营风险；Staff+ 主动驱动 framing、分配延迟预算、点出长度不匹配和反馈回路、权衡全量重编 vs 增量更新。越高越主动、越讲 org 级取舍。
why_en: L4 defines the problem, basic pipeline, and core metrics; L5 decomposes query understanding, weighs dual vs cross-encoder, and treats drift as operational risk; Staff+ proactively drives framing, allocates the latency budget, raises length mismatch and feedback loops, and weighs full re-embed vs incremental.
tradeoff: L4（定义+基础管道+核心指标）vs Staff+（主动 framing+延迟预算+反馈回路+org 取舍）
whenOtherWins: 如果是 L4 面试，能清晰给出基础管道和核心指标就达标，不必主动扛延迟预算分配和 org 级取舍——那是 Staff+ 的加分项。
options: Staff+ 要背出更多模型名字和论文，比 L4 记得多就够了
Staff+ 只要把 ANN 底层图结构讲得比 L4 更细就算到位
Staff+ 主动驱动 framing、分配延迟预算、点出长度不匹配和反馈回路、权衡重编 vs 增量
Staff+ 和 L4 答法一样，只是 Staff+ 要多写一些伪代码
options_en: Staff+ just needs to recite more model names and papers than L4.
Staff+ only needs to explain ANN's graph internals in more detail than L4.
Staff+ proactively drives framing, allocates the latency budget, raises length mismatch and feedback loops, and weighs re-embed vs incremental.
Staff+ answers the same as L4, only writing a bit more pseudocode.
optionExplanations: 区分不在记多少模型名，而在能否主动 framing、扛下延迟预算和 org 级取舍。
讲细 ANN 图结构是实现深度，不是 Staff+ 信号；Staff+ 看的是系统级主动权。
对；主动驱动 framing、分延迟预算、点反馈回路和重编 vs 增量取舍，是 Staff+ 的判别特征。
写伪代码不是分级依据；层级差在系统思维的主动性和取舍深度。
optionExplanations_en: The distinction is not how many model names you recall but whether you drive framing and own latency-budget and org-level tradeoffs.
Detailing ANN graph internals is implementation depth, not a Staff+ signal; Staff+ is judged on system-level initiative.
Correct — proactively driving framing, allocating the latency budget, and weighing feedback loops and re-embed vs incremental is the Staff+ marker.
Pseudocode volume is not the leveling criterion; the gap is initiative and depth of tradeoff in systems thinking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工程职级：L4 定义问题+基础管道，L5 拆解取舍，Staff+ 主动驱动 framing 和 org 级取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: L4/L5/Staff+ are engineering levels: L4 defines problem and pipeline, L5 decomposes tradeoffs, Staff+ drives framing and org-level tradeoffs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 编码器升级后向量不兼容、召回退化，L5 起要当运营风险讨论。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift is post-upgrade vector incompatibility degrading recall, discussed as operational risk from L5 up.

q: 把一次语义搜索请求的四个处理阶段排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the four processing stages of one semantic-search request.
steps: 检索：ANN 在稠密向量上召回候选
查询理解：意图分类+实体识别+消歧
渲染：组装 SERP 结果页返回
排序：cross-encoder / 特征精排候选
why: 请求主线是查询理解→检索→排序→渲染，正好对应 sub-200ms 预算的四段。理解先把查询变成意图/实体，检索用 ANN 拉候选，排序精排，渲染组页返回；顺序错了下游就没有输入。
why_en: A request flows query understanding to retrieval to ranking to rendering, matching the four latency-budget stages, since each stage needs the previous one's output.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["查询理解
意图/实体/消歧"] --> R["检索
ANN 召回候选"] R --> K["排序
精排候选"] K --> D["渲染
组装 SERP"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻，检索阶段在稠密向量上召回候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) recalls candidates over dense vectors in the retrieval stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排序阶段把查询和候选联合编码做精排的模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder co-encodes query and candidate to re-rank in the ranking stage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 渲染阶段组装并返回给用户的结果页。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SERP (Search Engine Results Page) is the results page assembled and returned in the rendering stage.

scenario: 语料在持续更新，你要在「模型升级后全量重编」和「只对新增/变更文档增量更新索引」之间做 org 级取舍。
scenario_en: The corpus keeps changing; you must weigh full re-embedding after a model upgrade against incremental index updates for only new/changed docs.
q: 全量重编和增量更新该怎么权衡？
q_en: How do you weigh full re-embedding against incremental updates?
why: 全量 re-embed 保证所有文档和新查询在同一空间、召回最一致，但网页级要几天+巨额算力；增量更新只重编新增/变更文档，便宜快，但换了编码器后新旧向量混在一个索引里会不兼容。取舍轴是「一致性 vs 成本」，换编码器偏全量，仅内容变动偏增量。
why_en: Full re-embedding keeps all docs in one space with the most consistent recall but costs days and huge compute at web scale, while incremental updates only re-embed changed docs cheaply but mix incompatible old and new vectors after an encoder swap — the axis is consistency vs cost.
tradeoff: 全量重编（一致性最好、贵、慢）vs 增量更新（省、快、换编码器后新旧不兼容）
whenOtherWins: 如果只是新增/删除文档、编码器没换，增量更新就够且更省；只有编码器升级导致全库向量不兼容时，才值得付全量重编的代价。
options: 永远只做增量更新，全量重编太贵，任何情况下都不该做
永远做全量重编，一致性最重要，成本完全不用考虑
两者随便选，结果都一样，纯看当天算力有没有空
换编码器导致全库不兼容时全量重编，只是内容增删时增量更新，轴是一致性 vs 成本
options_en: Always do incremental only — full re-embedding is too costly and should never be done.
Always do full re-embedding — consistency is paramount and cost need not be considered.
Pick either freely; results are identical, purely depending on spare compute that day.
Full re-embed when an encoder swap makes the corpus incompatible, incremental for content add/remove — the axis is consistency vs cost.
optionExplanations: 只增量的话，编码器一升级新旧向量就混在一个索引里不兼容，召回退化拦不住。
每次都全量重编，网页级几天+巨额算力，内容只是小改时纯属浪费。
两者结果不一样：一致性和成本差很大，不能凭当天算力随意选。
对；编码器升级要全量对齐、内容增删走增量，取舍轴就是召回一致性 vs 重编成本。
optionExplanations_en: Incremental-only means an encoder upgrade mixes incompatible old and new vectors in one index, and recall degradation cannot be stopped.
Full re-embedding every time costs web-scale days and huge compute — pure waste when only content changed slightly.
The two are not equivalent: consistency and cost differ greatly, so you cannot pick by spare compute.
Correct — an encoder upgrade needs a full realign while content add/remove goes incremental; the axis is recall consistency vs re-embed cost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用新模型重编整个语料，一致性最好但代价是几天+大算力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Re-embedding re-encodes the whole corpus with the new model, most consistent but costing days and heavy compute.

termDefinitions.term: incremental index update / 增量索引更新
termDefinitions.meaning: 只对新增/变更文档更新向量，便宜快但换编码器后会新旧混用不兼容。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An incremental index update re-embeds only new/changed docs, cheap and fast but mixing incompatible old/new vectors after an encoder swap.

scenario: 用户点击哪些结果会回流成下一轮训练数据，训练出的模型又决定展示哪些结果。
scenario_en: Which results users click feeds back as next-round training data, and the trained model decides what to show next.
q: 点击→重训的反馈回路会带来什么风险？
q_en: What risk does the click-to-retraining feedback loop introduce?
why: 模型决定展示什么→用户只能点被展示的→这些点击回流成训练数据→强化「已被展示」的结果，形成自我强化回路。风险是流行度偏置和位置偏置被放大，长尾/新文档拿不到曝光就永远学不到，短期指标好看但多样性和召回覆盖在退化。Staff+ 要主动点出这条回路。
why_en: The model decides what shows, users can only click what is shown, those clicks feed training and reinforce already-shown results — a self-reinforcing loop that amplifies popularity and position bias, so long-tail and new docs never get exposure to be learned.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  M["模型决定展示什么"] --> S["用户只能点被展示的"]
  S --> D["点击回流成训练数据"]
  D --> M
options: 没有风险：点击是真实信号，回流训练只会让模型单调地变得更好
风险只是训练变慢，因为数据量会随着点击不断变大
自我强化回路放大流行/位置偏置，长尾文档拿不到曝光就学不到，覆盖退化
回路只影响渲染阶段的 UI 样式，和召回质量、训练数据都无关
options_en: No risk: clicks are real signal, so feeding them back only makes the model monotonically better.
The only risk is slower training, since data volume keeps growing with clicks.
The self-reinforcing loop amplifies popularity/position bias; long-tail docs get no exposure to be learned, and coverage degrades.
The loop only affects rendering-stage UI styling, unrelated to recall quality or training data.
optionExplanations: 点击不是无偏信号——用户只能点被展示的，回流训练会把展示偏置当成真相强化。
数据变大不是核心风险；核心是回路把偏置越滚越大，不是训练时长。
对；被展示的越被点、越被强化，长尾和新文档拿不到曝光就永远学不到，多样性和覆盖退化。
回路直接改训练数据分布和召回覆盖，不只是 UI；这正是它危险的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Clicks are not unbiased — users can only click what is shown, so feeding them back reinforces exposure bias as if it were truth.
Growing data is not the core risk; the core is the loop compounding bias, not training duration.
Correct — shown results get clicked and reinforced, so long-tail and new docs get no exposure to be learned, and diversity and coverage degrade.
The loop directly changes the training-data distribution and recall coverage, not just UI — which is exactly why it is dangerous.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型的展示决策塑造未来训练数据，自我强化，放大偏置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feedback loop is when the model's exposure decisions shape future training data, self-reinforcing and amplifying bias.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热门结果因常被展示常被点而不断被强化，挤压长尾。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Popularity bias is when popular results, shown and clicked often, keep getting reinforced, squeezing out the long tail.

termDefinitions.meaning: 排在前面的结果因更易被看到而更常被点，与真实相关性混淆。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is when higher-ranked results get more clicks simply for being seen, confounding true relevance.

scenario: 面试官给你一道语义搜索(semantic search)设计题,你有 45 分钟,正准备开场。
scenario_en: An interviewer gives you a semantic search design question with 45 minutes, and you are about to open.
q: 开场该先讲数据策略还是先画双塔架构图?为什么?
q_en: Should you open with data strategy or with a two-tower architecture diagram, and why?
why: 语义搜索的质量上限由训练数据决定,不是模型架构;所以先讲 relevance pair 怎么从用户信号构造,再谈模型。反过来先画架构,面试官会觉得你没意识到数据才是天花板。
why_en: The quality ceiling of semantic search is set by the training data, not the architecture, so lead with how relevance pairs are built from user signals before drawing any model.
tradeoff: 先数据策略(点住真正的天花板) vs 先画架构(容易被追问数据从哪来而卡壳)
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确聚焦模型结构(如「设计 cross-encoder 重排层」)或数据管线已给定,才可以直接从架构讲起。
diagram:
flowchart TD D["数据策略
质量天花板"] --> P1["relevance pair
用户信号构造"] D --> P2["query 预处理
拼写纠错 + 改写"] D --> P3["双塔训练数据
正例 + 负例分层"]
options: 先画双塔 / cross-encoder 架构图,模型选型才是质量上限,数据是次要细节
先选向量库和 ANN 索引,检索基础设施才是决定质量的瓶颈所在
先讲数据策略:relevance pair 怎么从用户信号造出来,数据质量才是天花板
先定 embedding 维度、batch size 等超参,调参决定了最终召回上限
options_en: Draw the two-tower / cross-encoder architecture first — model choice is the quality ceiling and data is a minor detail.
Pick the vector store and ANN index first — retrieval infrastructure is the bottleneck that decides quality.
Lead with data strategy: how relevance pairs are built from user signals, since data quality is the ceiling.
Fix embedding dimension, batch size, and other hyperparameters first — tuning decides the recall ceiling.
optionExplanations: 架构再漂亮,喂进去的训练样本本身有噪声,模型学到的就是噪声——数据质量在前,架构选型在后。
向量库和 ANN 是工程承载,不产生监督信号;它们解决「查得快」,不解决「学得准」。
对;先钉住数据从哪来、怎么去噪,后面架构选型才有意义,这是面试官想听的顺序。
超参是最后的边际优化,数据管线不对,调再多参也顶不破数据设定的天花板。
optionExplanations_en: A great architecture fed noisy training samples just learns the noise — data quality comes before architecture choice.
Vector store and ANN are engineering carriers producing no supervision; they make search fast, not accurate.
Correct — pin down where data comes from and how it is denoised first, then architecture choices matter, which is what interviewers want to hear.
Hyperparameters are the final marginal tuning; if the data pipeline is wrong, no tuning breaks the data-set ceiling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按语义相似度而非关键词精确匹配来检索文档的搜索系统。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Semantic search retrieves documents by meaning similarity rather than exact keyword match.

termDefinitions.meaning: (query, doc) 加上「相关/不相关」标签,是训练检索模型的监督样本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relevance pair is a (query, doc) with a relevant/not-relevant label, the supervision for training retrieval models.

termDefinitions.meaning: query 和 doc 各用一个编码器映射成向量,按向量相似度检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual-encoder (two-tower) model encodes query and doc separately into vectors and retrieves by vector similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索:在向量空间里快速找相似向量,牺牲一点精度换速度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) quickly finds similar vectors in embedding space, trading a little accuracy for speed.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 双塔模型从 (query, doc) relevance pair 学习,这些 pair 要从真实数据里造出来,而不是凭空标注。
scenario_en: A dual-encoder learns from (query, doc) relevance pairs that must be constructed from real data, not labeled from scratch.
q: 构造 query-doc relevance pair 的三大信号来源是什么?
q_en: What are the three signal sources for constructing query-doc relevance pairs?
why: 三来源:隐式点击日志(海量但噪声大)、隐式停留时长(区分满意/不满意点击)、显式人工打分(0-4,干净但稀缺)。前两者撑规模训练,后者做可信评估。
why_en: Three sources: implicit click logs (abundant, noisy), implicit dwell time (separates satisfied clicks), and explicit human labels (0-4, clean but scarce).
options: 点击日志(隐式)、停留时长(隐式)、人工相关性打分(显式),三种互补的信号
只有人工标注一种来源是可靠的,点击和停留噪声太大应全部弃用
随机采样 (query, doc) 对,靠模型自监督推断相关性,不需要任何用户信号
直接爬网页的 title-body 对当正例,不看用户在搜索里的真实行为
options_en: Click logs (implicit), dwell time (implicit), and human relevance labels (explicit) — three complementary signals.
Only human labels are reliable; clicks and dwell are too noisy and should be dropped entirely.
Randomly sample (query, doc) pairs and let the model self-supervise relevance, needing no user signal.
Scrape web title-body pairs as positives, ignoring real user behavior in search.
optionExplanations: 对;三者互补——点击给规模、停留去噪、人工分做可信基准,数据策略就是编排这三者。
只用人工标注量太少、覆盖不了长尾,放弃隐式信号等于放弃规模训练。
自监督没有真实相关性锚点,造出来的正例可能根本不相关,喂出噪声模型。
title-body 是文档内部结构,不反映用户搜什么、点什么,不是相关性信号。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the three are complementary: clicks give scale, dwell denoises, human labels give a trusted baseline; data strategy orchestrates all three.
Human labels alone are too few to cover the long tail; dropping implicit signals gives up scale training.
Self-supervision has no real relevance anchor, so its positives may be irrelevant and train a noisy model.
Title-body is document-internal structure, not what users search or click, so it is not a relevance signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录用户对每个 query 点了哪些结果的日志,是最海量的隐式相关性信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A click log records which results a user clicked for each query, the most abundant implicit relevance signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点开一个结果后停留阅读的时长,用来区分满意点击和误点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dwell time is how long a user stays on a clicked result, used to tell satisfied clicks from accidental ones.

termDefinitions.term: explicit relevance label / 显式相关性标注
termDefinitions.meaning: 人工评审员给 (query, doc) 打的分级相关性(如 0-4),干净但昂贵。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An explicit relevance label is a human rater's graded score (e.g. 0-4) for a (query, doc), clean but costly.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 点击日志里排在第 1 位的结果点击量远高于第 5 位,哪怕两者真实相关性其实差不多。
scenario_en: In click logs, the rank-1 result gets far more clicks than rank-5 even when their true relevance is similar.
q: 点击日志的 position bias 是什么,怎么纠正?
q_en: What is position bias in click logs, and how do you correct it?
why: 高位置纯因曝光靠前被多点,不代表更相关(position bias);用 inverse propensity weighting 反向加权,把虚高点击压回真实信号,代价是要估准各位置 propensity。
why_en: Top ranks get more clicks from exposure, not relevance (position bias); IPW down-weights each click by its position propensity to recover the true signal.
diagram:
flowchart LR C["原始点击"] --> B["position bias
高位虚高"] B --> W["IPW 反向加权
÷ 曝光倾向"] W --> S["去偏 relevance 信号"]
options: position bias 是模型在训练集上过拟合,加 dropout 和权重衰减即可消除
高位置点击多,是因为排在前面的结果本来就更相关,属于真信号不必纠正
直接删掉排名前三位的所有点击样本,只留低位点击来训练模型
高位曝光抬高点击(非真相关),用 inverse propensity weighting 反向加权
options_en: Position bias is overfitting on the training set, removable with dropout and weight decay.
Top ranks get more clicks because those results are genuinely more relevant, a true signal needing no correction.
Just delete all clicks from the top three ranks and train only on low-rank clicks.
High-rank exposure inflates clicks (not true relevance); down-weight via inverse propensity weighting (IPW).
optionExplanations: position bias 是数据采集偏差,不是模型过拟合;正则改的是模型,救不了有偏的标签。
因果说反了:排前面才被多点,不是被多点才排前面,这正是要纠正的混淆。
删掉高位点击把最有信息量的正例也扔了,而且低位点击更稀疏、噪声更大。
对;IPW 用各位置的曝光倾向(propensity)反向加权,把「因位置而虚高」的点击折算回真实相关度。
optionExplanations_en: Position bias is a data-collection bias, not model overfitting; regularization changes the model, not the biased labels.
The causality is reversed: ranking high causes more clicks, not the other way, which is exactly the confound to correct.
Deleting top-rank clicks throws away the most informative positives, and low-rank clicks are sparser and noisier.
Correct — IPW down-weights clicks by each position's exposure propensity, converting position-inflated clicks back to true relevance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 结果排得越靠前越易被点击,与真实相关性无关的系统性偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is the systematic tendency for higher-ranked results to get more clicks regardless of true relevance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 逆倾向加权:用样本被曝光/观测的概率的倒数加权,抵消采集偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IPW (Inverse Propensity Weighting) weights each sample by the inverse of its exposure probability to cancel collection bias.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个结果在某位置被用户看到的概率,IPW 用它做反向加权。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Propensity is the probability a result at a given position is seen by the user, used by IPW for down-weighting.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 点击本身分不清用户是否满意:点开 2 秒就跳走 vs 点开读了 60 秒,是完全不同的信号。
scenario_en: A click alone cannot tell satisfaction: a 2-second bounce versus a 60-second read are very different signals.
q: 停留时长常用多少秒做「满意 vs 不满意」的二值化阈值?
q_en: What dwell-time threshold is commonly used to binarize satisfied vs unsatisfied clicks?
why: 约 30 秒是经验阈值(来自内容型场景的行业实践),不是公式推导;它把连续的 dwell time 二值化成满意/不满意标签,下游用来过滤短停留的误点、只留高质量正例。阈值随内容类型可调:新闻文章约 30 秒、商品列表约 10 秒。
why_en: About 30 seconds is an empirical threshold, not a derived formula, that binarizes continuous dwell time into satisfied/unsatisfied labels to filter accidental clicks and keep high-quality positives.
options: 约 30 秒:超过算满意点击(相关),几秒就跳出算不满意,用来过滤误点
约 0.5 秒:只要页面加载完就算满意,不看用户是否真的读了内容
约 10 分钟:必须读满十分钟才算相关,否则一律判为负例样本
不设阈值:所有点击一律当满意正例,dwell time 完全不参与判定
options_en: About 30 seconds: above it is a satisfied (relevant) click, a few-second bounce is unsatisfied, filtering accidental clicks.
About 0.5 seconds: as soon as the page loads it counts as satisfied, regardless of actual reading.
About 10 minutes: only a full ten-minute read counts as relevant, else it is a negative.
No threshold: every click is a satisfied positive and dwell time plays no role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点开结果后停留的时长,约 30 秒常作满意/不满意的二值化阈值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dwell time is time spent on a clicked result; ~30s is a common satisfied/unsatisfied binarization threshold.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点开发现不对就立刻跳走的点击,dwell 过滤要剔除的噪声。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An accidental click is one where the user immediately bounces, the noise dwell filtering removes.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 你的搜索同时索引新闻文章和电商商品列表,现在用一个固定 30 秒 dwell 阈值判断满意点击。
scenario_en: Your search indexes both news articles and e-commerce listings, using one fixed 30-second dwell threshold for satisfied clicks.
q: 该给所有内容类型用同一个 dwell 阈值吗?
q_en: Should you use the same dwell threshold across all content types?
why: 消费一条内容所需时间随类型差别大——读新闻要几十秒,扫一眼商品几秒就够。固定阈值会把「快速满意」的商品点击误判成不满意,所以按内容类型分别定阈值。
why_en: Time to consume content varies by type — reading news takes tens of seconds, scanning a product takes a few — so a fixed threshold misjudges quick satisfied clicks and thresholds should be per content type.
tradeoff: 按类型分别调阈值(贴合真实满意,多一套配置) vs 统一阈值(简单,误判快消费内容)
whenOtherWins: 如果平台只有单一内容类型(如纯新闻站),用一个统一阈值就够,没必要按类型区分。
options: 用统一 30 秒阈值最省事,内容类型不影响判断满意所需的停留时间
按内容类型调:新闻文章约 30 秒、商品列表约 10 秒(有加购信号更短)
阈值越高越干净,统一设成 5 分钟保证只留下最相关的正例样本
干脆不看 dwell time,只要有点击就一律算作满意的正例来训练
options_en: A uniform 30-second threshold is simplest; content type does not affect the time needed to feel satisfied.
Tune per content type: news ~30s, product listings ~10s (shorter with add-to-cart signals).
The higher the better — set a uniform 5 minutes so only the most relevant positives remain.
Skip dwell time entirely and count every click as a satisfied positive for training.
optionExplanations: 统一阈值把「几秒扫完就满意」的商品点击误杀成不满意,系统性丢失电商正例。
对;不同内容的满意时长不同,分类型定阈值才能把快消费内容的满意点击正确保留。
5 分钟过严,连正常读完新闻的用户都被判不满意,正例几乎全被过滤光。
不看 dwell 就退回原始点击,误点和 position bias 全灌进正例,失去过滤意义。
optionExplanations_en: A uniform threshold kills quick-scan product clicks as unsatisfied, systematically losing e-commerce positives.
Correct — satisfaction time differs by content, so per-type thresholds correctly keep quick-consumption satisfied clicks.
Five minutes is too strict; even normal news readers are judged unsatisfied and nearly all positives are filtered out.
Skipping dwell reverts to raw clicks, pouring accidental clicks and position bias into positives and losing the filter's point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判定满意点击的停留时间界限,应按内容类型(新闻 vs 商品)分别设定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dwell threshold is the stay-time cutoff for a satisfied click, set per content type (news vs product).

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户把商品加入购物车的动作,是比停留更强的满意信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Add-to-cart is a user placing an item in the cart, a stronger satisfaction signal than dwell.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 电商/招聘/社交搜索里,除了点击还有加购(add-to-cart)、投递(apply)、连接(connect)等动作。
scenario_en: In e-commerce/jobs/social search, beyond clicks there are actions like add-to-cart, apply, and connect.
q: 为什么 add-to-cart / apply / connect 比单纯点击是更强的正例信号?
q_en: Why are add-to-cart / apply / connect stronger positive signals than a plain click?
why: 加购/投递/连接是用户主动投入成本的动作,意图强、噪声低——比一次可能是误点的 click 更能证明 query-doc 相关。代价:量比点击少(中等规模),而且是平台专属信号,不通用。
why_en: Add-to-cart, apply, and connect are actions where the user invests effort, so intent is strong and noise low, proving relevance better than a possibly accidental click.
options: 因为它们的数据量比点击更大,海量所以更可靠、更适合当训练主信号
因为它们能自动纠正 position bias,而普通点击做不到这一点
因为它们代表更强的用户意图、噪声低,比「点了但可能误点」更能证明相关
因为它们不需要 dwell 过滤,天生就是显式人工标注级别的信号
options_en: Because their data volume is larger than clicks, so being abundant they are more reliable as the primary signal.
Because they automatically correct position bias, which ordinary clicks cannot.
Because they represent stronger user intent with low noise, proving relevance better than a possibly accidental click.
Because they need no dwell filtering and are natively as clean as explicit human labels.
optionExplanations: 恰恰相反,这类动作量比点击少(中等规模),强在意图而非数量。
纠 position bias 是 IPW 的活,和动作信号是两回事,不能混为一谈。
对;用户愿意加购/投递说明真的相关,噪声远低于一次可能手滑的点击。
它们仍是隐式信号、不是人工标注,只是意图更强,不能免去质控。
optionExplanations_en: On the contrary, these actions are fewer than clicks (medium volume); their strength is intent, not quantity.
Correcting position bias is IPW's job, a separate matter from action signals.
Correct — a user bothering to add-to-cart or apply signals genuine relevance, far less noisy than a possibly slipped click.
They are still implicit signals, not human labels; stronger intent does not remove the need for QC.

termDefinitions.meaning: 加购、投递、连接等高投入动作,意图强、噪声低的平台专属正例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An action signal is a high-effort action (add-to-cart, apply, connect), a low-noise, platform-specific positive.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 除了隐式信号,还可以雇人工评审员给 (query, doc) 对打相关性分,如 0-4 五档。
scenario_en: Beyond implicit signals, human raters can grade (query, doc) pairs on a 0-4 scale.
q: 显式人工相关性标注(如 0-4 分)在数据策略里扮演什么角色?
q_en: What role do explicit human relevance labels (e.g. 0-4) play in the data strategy?
why: 人工 0-4 分噪声极低(gold standard)但很贵、量少,所以不当训练主力,而是拿来做离线评估、校准 NDCG 这类需要可信基准的指标。隐式信号负责规模训练,显式标注负责可信评估。
why_en: Human 0-4 labels are very low-noise (gold standard) but costly and scarce, so they serve offline evaluation and NDCG calibration rather than bulk training.
options: 是模型的主要训练信号,靠这批海量标注直接训练双塔编码器上线
用来在线上实时纠正 position bias 和曝光偏差,替代 IPW 加权
完全替代点击日志,有了人工分就不再需要任何隐式信号做训练
干净但稀缺的 gold standard,主要用于离线评估、校准 NDCG
options_en: The model's primary training signal — train the dual-encoder directly on this abundant labeled set.
Used to correct position bias and exposure bias live online, replacing IPW.
A full replacement for click logs — with human labels you no longer need any implicit signal for training.
A clean but scarce gold standard, used mainly for offline evaluation and NDCG calibration.
optionExplanations: 人工标注太贵太少,覆盖不了长尾 query,当训练主力规模根本不够。
纠 position bias 靠 IPW,不是靠人工分;而且人工标注是离线的,做不了实时纠偏。
隐式信号才有规模,显式标注替代不了训练量,两者是分工不是替代。
对;0-4 分最干净,拿来当可信基准做离线评估、校准 NDCG,而不是喂大规模训练。
optionExplanations_en: Human labels are too costly and few to cover long-tail queries, nowhere near enough scale to be the primary trainer.
Position bias is corrected by IPW, not human labels, which are offline and cannot correct live.
Implicit signals provide the scale; explicit labels cannot replace training volume — they divide labor, not substitute.
Correct — 0-4 labels are cleanest, used as a trusted baseline for offline evaluation and NDCG calibration, not bulk training.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被当作最可信参考的标注,这里指人工分级相关性,用于评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A gold standard is the most trusted reference labels, here human graded relevance used for evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累计增益:按位置折扣累计相关性收益、再归一化的排序质量指标,需要分级标注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) is a ranking metric that discounts relevance gain by rank and normalizes it, requiring graded labels.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 隐式信号(点击/停留)海量但噪声大;显式人工标注干净但稀缺又贵。你要给两者分工。
scenario_en: Implicit signals (clicks/dwell) are abundant but noisy; explicit labels are clean but scarce and costly. You must divide their roles.
q: 隐式信号和显式标注该各自用在哪里?
q_en: Where should implicit signals and explicit labels each be used?
why: 隐式信号量大够喂训练但含 position bias 等噪声;显式标注干净但太少,拿去训练覆盖不了长尾。所以规模训练用隐式、可信评估用显式,各取所长。
why_en: Implicit signals are big enough to train but carry noise like position bias; explicit labels are clean but too few to train the long tail, so train on implicit and evaluate on explicit.
tradeoff: 隐式训练 + 显式评估(规模与可信兼得) vs 单一来源(要么噪声大要么量不够)
whenOtherWins: 如果隐式点击严重不可信(冷启动、恶意刷量)而预算充足,可以更多依赖显式标注,甚至用它做小规模训练。
options: 全用显式标注,又干净又权威,隐式信号噪声大应该彻底弃用不再采集
隐式信号做大规模训练,显式标注做离线评估——用规模喂训练、用干净保评估
全用隐式信号,人工标注太贵一律不做,评估也用点击率代替就行
两者混在一起当同一批训练数据,不区分噪声和用途直接一起喂进去
options_en: Use only explicit labels — clean and authoritative — and drop noisy implicit signals entirely.
Implicit signals for large-scale training, explicit labels for offline evaluation — scale for training, cleanliness for evaluation.
Use only implicit signals — human labeling is too costly, so replace evaluation with click rate too.
Mix both into one training set without distinguishing noise or purpose, feeding them together.
optionExplanations: 只用显式标注量太小,训练覆盖不了长尾,规模上根本喂不动大模型。
对;隐式给规模、显式给可信基准,这正是「训练用隐式、评估用显式」的标准分工。
没有显式基准,评估就没有可信锚点,点击率本身受排名靠前影响、并非真值。
混着喂等于把高噪声隐式和干净显式搅在一起,既污染训练又浪费宝贵的干净标签。
optionExplanations_en: Only explicit labels are too few; training cannot cover the long tail and cannot feed a large model at scale.
Correct — implicit gives scale, explicit gives a trusted baseline, the standard split of train-on-implicit, evaluate-on-explicit.
Without an explicit baseline, evaluation has no trusted anchor, and click rate itself is inflated by rank and is not ground truth.
Mixing pours noisy implicit and clean explicit together, polluting training and wasting the scarce clean labels.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从用户行为(点击、停留)间接推出的相关性,海量但含噪声。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An implicit signal infers relevance indirectly from user behavior (clicks, dwell), abundant but noisy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 上线前用固定测试集和可信标注衡量模型质量,常用 NDCG、recall@K。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offline evaluation measures model quality before launch on a fixed test set with trusted labels, using metrics like NDCG and recall@K.

category: Semantic Search Data Strategy Feature Engineering

scenario: 语义搜索要在数百万文档里为一个 query 找到最相关结果，还要在几十毫秒内返回。
scenario_en: Semantic search must find the most relevant results for a query among millions of docs and return in tens of milliseconds.
q: 为什么工业级语义搜索几乎都用「两阶段」架构，两阶段各干什么？
q_en: Why do production semantic-search systems use a two-stage architecture, and what does each stage do?
why: 第一阶段用便宜检索器在百万库毫秒级捞候选（召回优先），第二阶段用昂贵但精准的 re-ranker 只精排 top-K。单靠精排跑全库延迟爆炸，单靠检索器精度不够，分工才能同时拿到速度和精度。
why_en: A cheap retriever pulls candidates from millions of docs in milliseconds, then an expensive re-ranker precisely scores only the top-K, so you get both speed and precision.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["query"] --> R["① 检索器
百万库毫秒召回"] R --> F["融合候选
100–1000 篇"] F --> K["② re-ranker
精排 top-K"] K --> O["最终结果"]
options: 用一个昂贵精排模型给全库每篇文档逐一打分，牺牲延迟换全库最高精度，靠加机器扛吞吐
两阶段跑同一个检索模型，第二阶段把 top-K 重跑几遍取平均来降低打分方差
先用便宜检索器毫秒级从百万文档捞候选，再用昂贵 re-ranker 只精排 top-K
第一阶段先精排全库、第二阶段再粗排收窄，精度层层放宽以省算力
options_en: Use one expensive re-ranker to score every doc in the corpus, trading latency for max precision and scaling with hardware.
Run the same retrieval model in both stages, re-running the top-K a few times and averaging to cut scoring variance.
First a cheap retriever pulls candidates from millions of docs in ms, then an expensive re-ranker precisely scores only the top-K.
Stage one precisely ranks the whole corpus, stage two coarsely narrows it, loosening precision layer by layer.
optionExplanations: 精排模型对每篇一次前向传播，全库百万篇跑一遍是秒级甚至分钟级，直接超时；加机器也补不回 O(N) 全库精排的成本。
重跑取平均降的是方差不是延迟，也没解决「全库打分太贵」这个根本矛盾，纯属浪费算力。
对；检索器负责召回（快、召回优先），re-ranker 负责精度（慢、只看 top-K），分工让系统同时拿到速度和精度。
顺序反了：全库精排正是两阶段架构要避免的昂贵操作，先精后粗把最贵的一步放在最费的位置。
optionExplanations_en: The re-ranker runs one forward pass per doc, so scoring millions takes seconds to minutes and times out; hardware cannot undo O(N) full-corpus scoring.
Re-running and averaging cuts variance not latency and never fixes the core problem that full-corpus scoring is too expensive.
Correct — the retriever handles recall (fast, recall-first) and the re-ranker handles precision (slow, top-K only), so the split gets both.
Backwards: full-corpus precise ranking is exactly what two-stage avoids, and precise-then-coarse puts the costliest step where it hurts most.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第一阶段从全库快速召回候选的模型，通常是 dual encoder 配 ANN 索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retriever is the first-stage model that quickly recalls candidates from the full corpus, usually a dual encoder over an ANN index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第二阶段对少量候选做精细相关性打分的模型，通常是 cross-encoder。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A re-ranker is the second-stage model that finely scores a small candidate set, usually a cross-encoder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第一阶段召回后送去精排的前 K 篇候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-K is the K best candidates from stage one that get passed to re-ranking.

q: 两阶段语义搜索里有哪三个核心架构决策？(多选)
q_en: What are the three core architectural decisions in two-stage semantic search? (multiple)
why: 这三个决策——dual encoder 选型、hybrid 融合、cross-encoder 精排——都被同一根轴（延迟 vs 精度）牵着走；前端渲染是产品层，不影响检索质量。
why_en: The three decisions — dual-encoder choice, hybrid fusion, and cross-encoder re-ranking — are all governed by the latency-versus-accuracy axis.
options: dual encoder 选型（DPR / E5 / BGE 等 dense 检索模型）
hybrid retrieval 融合（BM25 稀疏 + dense 稠密怎么合并候选）
cross-encoder re-ranking（top-K 精排模型与候选数 K）
用哪种前端框架渲染搜索结果页
options_en: Dual-encoder choice (dense retrieval models like DPR / E5 / BGE).
Hybrid retrieval fusion (how to merge BM25 sparse and dense candidates).
Cross-encoder re-ranking (the top-K re-ranker and the candidate count K).
Which front-end framework renders the results page.
optionExplanations: 对；dual encoder 决定第一阶段召回质量和索引成本，是 dense 检索的地基。
对；dense 会漏精确关键词，hybrid 把 BM25 和 dense 候选融合，决定召回的完整性。
对；cross-encoder 决定精度上限，K 决定你在延迟-精度曲线上的位置。
错；渲染是前端产品层，和检索模型的延迟-精度权衡无关。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — the dual encoder sets stage-one recall quality and index cost, the foundation of dense retrieval.
Correct — dense misses exact keywords, so hybrid fuses BM25 and dense candidates and governs recall completeness.
Correct — the cross-encoder sets the precision ceiling and K sets where you sit on the latency-precision curve.
Wrong — rendering is a front-end product layer, unrelated to the model's latency-accuracy tradeoff.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个独立 transformer 分别把 query 和 doc 编码成同维向量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dual encoder uses two separate transformers to encode query and doc into same-dimension vectors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 经典稀疏检索函数，按词频/逆文档频率给关键词匹配打分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 (Best Matching 25) is a classic sparse retrieval function scoring keyword matches by term frequency and inverse document frequency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 query 和 doc 拼成一条序列过一个 transformer，让 token 互相 attend。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cross-encoder concatenates query and doc into one sequence through a transformer so tokens attend to each other.

scenario: 你要设计 dense 检索第一阶段：怎么让「一个 query」和「百万篇 doc」都变成可比的向量。
scenario_en: You design the dense-retrieval first stage: how to turn one query and millions of docs into comparable vectors.
q: dual encoder（双塔）怎么做 dense 检索，相关性怎么算？
q_en: How does a dual encoder do dense retrieval, and how is relevance computed?
why: 两个独立 transformer 分别把 query、doc 编成同维向量，相关性用点积/余弦算。关键是 doc 向量离线预算好，query 来了只跑 query 编码器，再用 ANN 找最近邻，毫秒返回。
why_en: Two separate transformers encode query and doc into same-dim vectors scored by dot product or cosine, with doc vectors precomputed offline so only the query encoder runs at query time.
options: 一个 transformer 同时读入 query 和 doc 输出匹配分，每来一个 query 就把全库重编码一遍
两个独立 transformer 分别把 query、doc 编成同维向量，相关性用点积/余弦，doc 向量离线预算
把 query 和 doc 拼成一句话过 transformer，让每个 query token attend 每个 doc token
用倒排索引按关键词精确匹配，不需要向量，靠词频排序
options_en: One transformer reads query and doc together to output a match score, re-encoding the whole corpus for each query.
Two separate transformers encode query and doc into same-dim vectors scored by dot product/cosine, with doc vectors precomputed offline.
Concatenate query and doc into one sequence through a transformer so every query token attends every doc token.
Use an inverted index for exact keyword matching, no vectors, ranking by term frequency.
optionExplanations: 那是 cross-encoder 的做法，每个 query 都要重扫全库、O(N) 前向传播，第一阶段召回根本扛不住。
对；双塔的精髓是 query 塔和 doc 塔解耦，doc 向量离线算好进 ANN 索引，在线只算 query 一次。
拼接过一个 transformer 是 cross-encoder，精度高但太慢，只适合第二阶段精排少量候选。
倒排+词频是 BM25 稀疏检索，抓精确关键词但不懂语义，不是 dense dual encoder。
optionExplanations_en: That is the cross-encoder approach, re-scanning the whole corpus per query with O(N) forward passes — first-stage recall cannot bear it.
Correct — the dual encoder decouples the query and doc towers, precomputing doc vectors into an ANN index and encoding only the query online.
Concatenating through one transformer is a cross-encoder: accurate but too slow, fit only for re-ranking a few candidates in stage two.
Inverted index plus term frequency is BM25 sparse retrieval — great at exact keywords but blind to semantics, not a dense dual encoder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两向量的点积/余弦相似度，值越大越相关，是 dense 检索的相关性分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dot product / cosine similarity between two vectors — higher means more relevant — is the dense-retrieval relevance score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻搜索：在向量索引里快速找与 query 向量最近的一批 doc，不用扫全库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search quickly finds the doc vectors closest to a query vector without scanning the whole corpus.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用稠密向量表示 query 和 doc，靠向量相似度找相关文档。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dense retrieval represents query and doc as dense vectors and finds relevant docs by vector similarity.

scenario: 语料库几百万篇，语义搜索要 <50ms 返回，每天还有海量 query。
scenario_en: The corpus has millions of docs, search must return in under 50ms, and query volume is huge.
q: dual encoder 为什么能做到毫秒级召回？关键设计是什么？
q_en: Why can a dual encoder recall in milliseconds — what is the key design?
why: doc 向量离线预算好存进 ANN 索引，在线只跑 query 编码器一次，再用 ANN 近似最近邻毫秒取回候选。若在线还要现编码全库 doc，就退化成 O(N) 全库扫描，延迟爆炸。
why_en: Doc vectors are precomputed offline into an ANN index, so at query time only the query encoder runs once and ANN returns neighbors in milliseconds.
options: doc 向量离线预算进 ANN 索引，query 来时只编码 query 一次，ANN 毫秒取回最近邻
每来一个 query 就把全库 doc 实时重新编码一遍，再逐一算相似度取最高
把所有 doc 全文缓存在内存里，用字符串匹配代替向量运算加速
靠更大的 GPU 集群把全库精排的秒级延迟硬压到毫秒
options_en: Doc vectors are precomputed into an ANN index, only the query is encoded per request, and ANN returns neighbors in ms.
Re-encode the entire corpus in real time for each query, then compute similarity one by one and take the max.
Cache all doc full text in memory and replace vector math with string matching to go faster.
Use a bigger GPU cluster to force full-corpus re-ranking's second-level latency down to milliseconds.
optionExplanations: 对；离线预算 + 在线只算 query + ANN 近似最近邻，是把「百万库」变成「毫秒召回」的三件套。
在线重编码全库就是 O(N) 全量前向传播，正是双塔要绕开的成本，延迟直接秒级。
字符串匹配丢掉了语义相似性，也没利用向量索引，退回关键词检索的老路。
堆 GPU 改善不了全库精排的算法复杂度，成本线性膨胀，仍然追不上 SLA。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — offline precompute plus online query-only encoding plus ANN is the trio that turns millions of docs into millisecond recall.
Re-encoding the corpus online is O(N) full forward passes — exactly what the dual encoder avoids — pushing latency to seconds.
String matching drops semantic similarity and ignores the vector index, falling back to plain keyword retrieval.
More GPUs cannot change the algorithmic complexity of full-corpus re-ranking; cost grows linearly and still misses the SLA.

termDefinitions.term: ANN index / 近似最近邻索引
termDefinitions.meaning: 预存 doc 向量、支持毫秒级近邻查询的向量索引（如 HNSW/IVF）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ANN index stores doc vectors and supports millisecond nearest-neighbor queries (e.g. HNSW or IVF).

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务级别协议，这里指搜索延迟的承诺上限（如 p99 <100ms）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA (Service Level Agreement) is a committed limit, here on search latency such as p99 under 100ms.

scenario: 你在 DPR（768 维）和 E5/BGE（1024 维）之间选 dual encoder，语料几百万篇要进 ANN 索引。
scenario_en: You choose a dual encoder between DPR (768-dim) and E5/BGE (1024-dim), with millions of docs going into an ANN index.
q: embedding 维度（768–1024）这个数字影响什么、下游怎么用？
q_en: What does the embedding dimension (768–1024) affect, and how is it used downstream?
why: 维度是每篇 doc 向量的长度：768–1024 直接决定 ANN 索引内存（向量数×维度×4B）和每次相似度计算开销，进而影响 query 延迟。比如 500 万篇×1024×4B≈20GB 原始向量，是算索引内存和延迟预算的基数。
why_en: The dimension is each vector's length, directly setting ANN index memory (count × dim × 4 bytes) and per-query similarity cost, e.g. 5M × 1024 × 4B ≈ 20GB of raw vectors.
options: 维度只反映模型训练时长，与在线索引内存和 query 延迟这些服务侧成本无关
维度越高检索一定越准，应无脑选最大维度，因为它几乎不带来额外存储或计算成本
768–1024 指 SLA 规定的 query 延迟毫秒上限，而不是每篇文档向量的长度
是每篇 doc 向量的长度，决定 ANN 索引内存与相似度计算开销，是延迟/内存预算的基数
options_en: Dimension only reflects training time and is unrelated to serving-side costs like index memory and query latency.
Higher dimension always retrieves better, so pick the max blindly since it adds almost no storage or compute cost.
768–1024 is the SLA's millisecond latency ceiling for queries, not the length of each doc vector.
It is each doc vector's length, setting ANN index memory and similarity-compute cost — the base for latency/memory budgets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 query/doc 向量的分量个数，常见 768（BERT-base）或 1024。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The embedding dimension is the number of components in each query/doc vector, commonly 768 (BERT-base) or 1024.

termDefinitions.term: ANN index memory / 索引内存
termDefinitions.meaning: 存所有 doc 向量占的内存 ≈ 向量数 × 维度 × 4 字节（float32）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN index memory is roughly vector count times dimension times 4 bytes (float32).

optionExplanations: 误解：768–1024 不是训练时长指标，它是向量长度，直接乘进在线索引内存和每次相似度计算，跟服务成本关系很大。
误解：维度越高不等于必然更准，而且更高维度会让索引内存和计算量同步涨，不是零成本。
误解：768–1024 说的是向量的分量数，不是 SLA 延迟上限，别把维度和延迟指标搞混。
对；这串数字是每个向量的长度，直接决定索引占多少内存、算一次相似度要多少乘法，是定内存和延迟预算的起点。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: the number isn't a training-time signal — it's vector length, and it multiplies straight into online index memory and per-query compute.
Misconception: bigger dimension doesn't guarantee better accuracy, and it also grows index memory and compute — never free.
Misconception: 768–1024 is the vector's component count, not an SLA latency ceiling — don't conflate dimension with latency.
Correct — that number is each embedding's size, setting how much memory the index needs and how many multiplies one similarity score costs.

scenario: 你要选一个 dual encoder 做 dense 检索，候选是 DPR、E5、BGE 三个主流模型。
scenario_en: You pick a dual encoder for dense retrieval among three mainstream models: DPR, E5, BGE.
q: DPR、E5、BGE 在「零样本能力 vs 微调投入」上怎么排？
q_en: How do DPR, E5, and BGE rank on zero-shot ability versus fine-tuning effort?
why: DPR 是双 BERT-base、768 维、NQ 上对比学习，零样本中等但微调投入最低；E5/BGE 是统一编码器、1024 维、大规模弱监督/指令训练，零样本强到 SOTA 但微调更重。核心轴是「开箱强度 vs 需要多少标注去微调」。
why_en: DPR is dual BERT-base with moderate zero-shot but the lowest fine-tune effort, while E5/BGE are unified encoders with strong-to-SOTA zero-shot but heavier fine-tuning.
options: 三者零样本能力相同，只是向量维度不同，微调投入也一样
DPR 零样本最强、微调最省；E5、BGE 都更弱更费
DPR 零样本中等、微调最省；E5、BGE 零样本更强直到 SOTA，但微调投入更高
BGE 零样本最弱，DPR 最强，三者微调投入递增
options_en: All three have identical zero-shot ability, differing only in vector dimension and with equal fine-tune effort.
DPR has the strongest zero-shot and cheapest fine-tuning; E5 and BGE are both weaker and costlier.
DPR is moderate zero-shot and cheapest to fine-tune; E5/BGE are stronger up to SOTA but cost more to fine-tune.
BGE has the weakest zero-shot and DPR the strongest, with fine-tune effort rising across the three.
optionExplanations: 三者维度不同（768 vs 1024）也罢，零样本和微调投入其实差别很大，说「相同」直接错。
说反了：DPR 是零样本中等而非最强，它的优势是微调省，不是开箱强。
对；DPR 微调最省、开箱中等，E5/BGE 靠大规模预训练拿到强/SOTA 零样本，代价是微调更重。
BGE 恰恰是 MTEB 上的 SOTA、零样本最强，说它最弱与事实相反。
optionExplanations_en: Dimensions differ (768 vs 1024), but zero-shot and fine-tune effort vary a lot, so 'identical' is simply wrong.
Backwards: DPR is moderate not strongest at zero-shot; its edge is cheap fine-tuning, not out-of-box strength.
Correct — DPR is cheapest to fine-tune and moderate out-of-box, while E5/BGE buy strong/SOTA zero-shot at the cost of heavier fine-tuning.
BGE is actually the MTEB SOTA and strongest zero-shot, so calling it weakest is the opposite of reality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 稠密段落检索：用双 BERT-base 在 Natural Questions 上对比学习训练的双塔模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) is a dual-tower model of two BERT-base encoders trained contrastively on Natural Questions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大规模弱监督对比学习训练、query/passage 加前缀的统一编码器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5 is a unified encoder trained with large-scale weakly-supervised contrastive learning, using query/passage prefixes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 智源通用嵌入：用 RetroMAE + 指令微调训练，MTEB 榜单 SOTA。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BGE (BAAI General Embedding) is trained with RetroMAE plus instruction tuning and is SOTA on MTEB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大规模文本嵌入基准，综合评测嵌入模型的检索/聚类等能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark) broadly evaluates embedding models on retrieval, clustering, and more.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不做领域微调，直接开箱使用的检索效果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Zero-shot is retrieval quality out of the box without any domain fine-tuning.

scenario: 垂直领域搜索（如电商），你手里有大量领域内标注的 query-doc 相关性数据，想最省事地训到强效果。
scenario_en: For a vertical search (e.g. e-commerce) you have abundant in-domain labeled query-doc relevance data and want the cheapest path to strong results.
q: 有充足领域标注数据时，dual encoder 该选哪个？
q_en: With abundant in-domain labeled data, which dual encoder should you pick?
why: 有充足领域标注就选 DPR：它最简单、微调最快就能到强效果，标注正好补上它零样本中等的短板。E5/BGE 的价值是缺标注时的开箱强，此时用不上它们更重的预训练优势。
why_en: With plenty of labels, pick DPR: it is simplest and fastest to fine-tune to strong results, and the labels cover its moderate zero-shot.
tradeoff: DPR（充足标注下微调最省最快）vs E5/BGE（缺标注时零样本更强）
whenOtherWins: 若几乎没有领域标注、又要马上有可用效果，就选 E5 或 BGE——它们零样本就强/SOTA，不靠你补标注。
options: DPR：最简单、微调最快到强效果，充足标注正好喂满它
E5：零样本就 SOTA，有没有标注都无所谓，直接开箱
BGE：微调投入最低，标注多时训得最省
三者随便选，标注数据量不影响 encoder 选型
options_en: DPR: simplest and fastest to fine-tune to strong results, and abundant labels feed it fully.
E5: it is SOTA zero-shot, so labels don't matter — just use it out of the box.
BGE: it has the lowest fine-tune effort, so it trains cheapest when labels are plentiful.
Pick any of the three; the amount of labeled data does not affect encoder choice.
optionExplanations: 对；有充足领域标注时 DPR 微调最省最快到强效果，标注正好补上它零样本中等的短板。
E5 的强项是缺标注时的零样本，有大量标注时它更重的预训练优势用不上，属于杀鸡用牛刀。
记反了：BGE 微调投入其实最高（中高），不是最低，标注多也不是它最省。
encoder 选型恰恰主要由「标注多不多」驱动，说不影响等于放弃了本题核心判据。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — with abundant labels DPR is cheapest and fastest to fine-tune to strong results, and the labels cover its moderate zero-shot.
E5's strength is zero-shot when labels are scarce; with plenty of labels its heavier pretraining edge goes unused — overkill.
Backwards: BGE actually has the highest fine-tune effort (medium-high), not the lowest, and isn't cheapest with many labels.
Encoder choice is mainly driven by how much labeled data you have, so 'no effect' discards this card's core criterion.

termDefinitions.meaning: 双 BERT-base 双塔，微调投入低、零样本中等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DPR (Dense Passage Retrieval) is a dual BERT-base tower, low fine-tune effort and moderate zero-shot.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一编码器系列，零样本强到 SOTA，缺标注时更划算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: E5/BGE are unified-encoder models with strong-to-SOTA zero-shot, best when labels are scarce.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为达到强检索效果需要的标注量与训练成本。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine-tune effort is the labeling volume and training cost needed to reach strong retrieval quality.

scenario: 训练 dual encoder 做对比学习时，要给每个正样本配「难负样本」——看着像相关、其实不相关的文档。
scenario_en: Training a dual encoder contrastively needs hard negatives for each positive — docs that look relevant but are not.
q: DPR/E5/BGE 分别怎么挖 hard negatives，为什么要用难负样本？
q_en: How do DPR/E5/BGE mine hard negatives, and why use hard negatives at all?
why: 难负样本逼模型区分「表面相似但不相关」，比随机负样本训练信号强得多。DPR 用 BM25 挖（关键词像但语义不对），E5 用 in-batch + 挖掘，BGE 进一步用 cross-encoder 挖更难的负例。
why_en: Hard negatives force the model to separate look-alike-but-irrelevant docs, giving far stronger signal than random negatives.
options: 三者都只用随机负样本，hard negatives 对检索训练没有帮助
DPR 用 BM25 挖、E5 用 in-batch+挖掘、BGE 用 cross-encoder 挖，难负样本训练信号更强
hard negatives 指正样本，用来直接当标签让模型背下来
难负样本只在推理时用，训练阶段一律用简单负样本
options_en: All three use only random negatives; hard negatives don't help retrieval training.
DPR mines with BM25, E5 uses in-batch plus mining, BGE mines with a cross-encoder — hard negatives give stronger training signal.
Hard negatives are the positives, used directly as labels for the model to memorize.
Hard negatives are used only at inference; training always uses easy negatives.
optionExplanations: 随机负样本太好区分、梯度信号弱；正因如此三家都专门挖 hard negatives，说「没帮助」与做法相反。
对；BM25 挖出关键词像但不相关的、cross-encoder 挖出更刁钻的负例，越难越逼模型学细粒度语义。
弄反了：hard negatives 是难的负样本不是正样本，作用是提供强对比信号而非背答案。
难负样本是训练期的对比信号，推理时无所谓正负，说反了阶段。
optionExplanations_en: Random negatives are too easy and give weak gradients; that's exactly why all three mine hard negatives, so 'no help' contradicts their design.
Correct — BM25 surfaces keyword-similar-but-irrelevant docs and a cross-encoder mines trickier ones; harder negatives force finer semantics.
Backwards: hard negatives are hard negative examples, not positives, providing strong contrast rather than answers to memorize.
Hard negatives are a training-time contrast signal; at inference positive/negative is moot, so the stage is reversed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 与 query 表面相似但实际不相关的文档，用作对比学习里最有信息量的负例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard negatives are docs that look similar to the query but are actually irrelevant, the most informative negatives in contrastive learning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把同一 batch 里其他样本的 doc 当作当前 query 的负样本，省去额外挖掘。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-batch negatives reuse other samples' docs in the same batch as negatives, avoiding extra mining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 拉近正样本对、推远负样本对的训练方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Contrastive learning pulls positive pairs together and pushes negative pairs apart.

scenario: 你的 dense 检索在语义相近 query 上表现好，但用户搜稀有 SKU 编号、错误码、生僻专名时经常搜不到。
scenario_en: Your dense retrieval works on semantically similar queries but often fails on rare SKUs, error codes, and uncommon proper nouns.
q: dense 检索为什么会漏掉精确关键词匹配，怎么补？
q_en: Why does dense retrieval miss exact keyword matches, and how do you fix it?
why: dense 向量擅长语义相似，但会把稀有 token（SKU、错误码、生僻专名）压进模糊语义空间，精确匹配反而丢了；BM25 这类稀疏检索对精确词命中天然强。所以并行跑 BM25 + dual encoder，融合两路取长补短。
why_en: Dense vectors blur rare tokens into fuzzy semantic space and lose exact matches, while BM25 nails exact terms, so you run both in parallel and fuse.
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["query"] --> D["dense 稠密
语义相似"] Q --> B["BM25 稀疏
精确关键词"] D --> F["融合候选"] B --> F F --> R["re-ranker"]
options: dense 检索本来就覆盖精确关键词，搜不到只是索引没建好
应该彻底换成 BM25，语义检索没有价值，dense 可以删掉
dense 擅长语义但漏精确词，并行加 BM25（稀疏检索）抓关键词，融合两路候选
把 embedding 维度调高就能解决所有精确关键词漏召回
options_en: Dense retrieval already covers exact keywords; failures just mean the index was built wrong.
Switch entirely to BM25 — semantic retrieval has no value, so drop dense.
Dense is great at semantics but misses exact terms, so add BM25 (sparse) in parallel and fuse the two candidate lists.
Just raise the embedding dimension and all exact-keyword misses disappear.
optionExplanations: 不是索引问题：稀有 token 被稠密向量抹成模糊语义，本质上就召不回精确匹配，重建索引也没用。
全换 BM25 会丢掉语义泛化（同义、改写查询），两者是互补不是替代。
对；dense 管语义、BM25 管精确词，hybrid 并行融合让稀有 SKU/错误码也能命中。
加维度提升的是语义容量，补不了「精确 token 匹配」这个稀疏检索才擅长的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Not an index bug: rare tokens get blurred into fuzzy semantics, so exact matches truly can't be recalled — rebuilding won't help.
Going all-BM25 loses semantic generalization (synonyms, paraphrases); the two are complementary, not substitutes.
Correct — dense handles semantics, BM25 handles exact terms, and hybrid fusion lets rare SKUs/error codes hit.
More dimensions add semantic capacity but can't supply exact-token matching, which is sparse retrieval's job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关键词词频匹配打分，对精确 token（SKU、错误码、专名）命中很强。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BM25 (Best Matching 25) sparse retrieval scores keyword frequency and excels at exact tokens like SKUs and error codes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 库存单位编号，电商里每个具体商品的唯一编码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) is the unique code identifying a specific product in commerce.

termDefinitions.meaning: 并行跑稀疏（BM25）+ 稠密（dual encoder）两路，融合候选再精排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid retrieval runs sparse (BM25) and dense (dual encoder) in parallel and fuses candidates before re-ranking.

scenario: 你想把 BM25 分和 dense 余弦分直接相加融合候选。BM25 从 0 到任意大（跟词频走），dense 余弦在 [−1,1]。
scenario_en: You try to fuse by directly adding BM25 and dense cosine scores. BM25 ranges 0 to arbitrarily large (term frequency); dense cosine is in [−1,1].
q: 为什么 BM25 分和 dense 分「直接相加」融合会失败？
q_en: Why does directly adding BM25 and dense scores fail as a fusion method?
why: 两个分布尺度根本不同——BM25 无上界（词频越高越大），dense 余弦夹在 [−1,1]。直接相加让数值天生更大的 BM25 主导融合分，dense 信号被淹没，等于没融合。要么按 rank 融合（RRF），要么先归一化再加权。
why_en: The two score distributions have different scales — BM25 is unbounded, dense cosine sits in [−1,1] — so adding them lets BM25's larger raw numbers dominate.
options: 直接相加没问题，两个分数本来就在同一尺度，结果可靠
失败是因为 dense 分太大，会盖过 BM25，应给 dense 乘小系数
因为 BM25 和 dense 测的是同一件事，相加等于重复计分
两个分布尺度不同、不可直接比较：BM25 无上界会主导，dense 的 [−1,1] 被淹没
options_en: Adding directly is fine — the two scores are already on the same scale and the result is reliable.
It fails because dense scores are too large and swamp BM25, so multiply dense by a small factor.
Because BM25 and dense measure the same thing, so adding double-counts.
The two distributions have different, non-comparable scales: unbounded BM25 dominates while dense's [−1,1] is drowned out.
optionExplanations: 恰恰不在同一尺度：一个无上界、一个夹在 [−1,1]，直接相加不可靠，这正是本题要否定的。
大小说反了：是 BM25 无上界会盖过 dense，不是 dense 盖过 BM25。
两者测的不是同一件事（精确词 vs 语义），问题在尺度不可比，不是重复计分。
对；尺度不可比让原始数值大的 BM25 主导，dense 信号被淹没，必须靠 RRF 或归一化加权解决。
optionExplanations_en: They are precisely not on the same scale — one unbounded, one in [−1,1] — so adding is unreliable, which is what this card rejects.
The magnitudes are reversed: unbounded BM25 swamps dense, not the other way around.
They measure different things (exact terms vs semantics); the problem is incomparable scale, not double-counting.
Correct — incomparable scales let the larger raw BM25 dominate and drown dense, which RRF or normalized weighting must fix.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把不同尺度的分数映射到可比区间（如 per-query min-max）再融合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization maps differently-scaled scores into a comparable range (e.g. per-query min-max) before fusing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两向量夹角余弦，取值 [−1,1]，是 dense 检索的相关性分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cosine similarity is the cosine of the angle between two vectors, in [−1,1], the dense-retrieval relevance score.

scenario: 你要融合 BM25 和 dense 两路候选，又不想处理两个分数尺度不同的归一化麻烦。
scenario_en: You want to fuse BM25 and dense candidates without dealing with the normalization headache of two different score scales.
q: RRF（Reciprocal Rank Fusion）是怎么融合两路候选的？
q_en: How does RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuse two candidate lists?
why: RRF 只看 rank 不看原始分：每篇 doc 在每一路的得分是 1/(k+rank)，k≈60，把两路相加。因为用排名而非分数，天然绕开尺度不可比问题，无需归一化、无学习参数，是 Elasticsearch/Vespa 的强基线。
why_en: RRF scores each doc 1/(k+rank) per list with k≈60 and sums both, using ranks not raw scores so it sidesteps scale mismatch with no normalization or learned params.
options: 每篇 doc 在每路按 1/(k+rank) 打分（k≈60），两路相加；只看 rank 不看原始分
把 BM25 和 dense 的原始分直接相加，谁大听谁的
用点击数据学一个权重 α，按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合
只取 dense 一路的 top 结果，BM25 只在 dense 为空时兜底
options_en: Score each doc 1/(k+rank) per list (k≈60) and sum both lists, using ranks not raw scores.
Add BM25 and dense raw scores directly and let the larger one win.
Learn a weight α from click data and fuse as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse.
Take only the dense list's top results, using BM25 only as a fallback when dense is empty.
optionExplanations: 对；1/(k+rank) 让排名靠前的 doc 得分高，k≈60 压平头部差距；只用 rank 就绕开了尺度不可比，零参数、零归一化。
直接相加原始分正是 RRF 要避免的尺度陷阱，BM25 无上界会主导。
那是 learned weighted fusion（学权重），需要点击数据和维护，不是无参数的 RRF。
dense 兜底式串联不是融合，会漏掉 BM25 独有的精确匹配候选。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — 1/(k+rank) rewards top-ranked docs, k≈60 flattens head gaps, and using only ranks sidesteps scale mismatch with zero params and no normalization.
Adding raw scores is exactly the scale trap RRF avoids; unbounded BM25 would dominate.
That is learned weighted fusion, which needs click data and maintenance — not parameter-free RRF.
Chaining dense with a BM25 fallback isn't fusion and misses BM25's unique exact-match candidates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 倒数排名融合：按 1/(k+rank) 用排名而非分数融合多路候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses multiple candidate lists by rank via 1/(k+rank), not by raw score.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一篇 doc 在某一路结果里的名次（第 1、第 2…）。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rank is a doc's position within one list (1st, 2nd, ...).

termDefinitions.meaning: 平滑常数，常取 60，越大越压平头部名次之间的得分差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The RRF constant k, typically 60, is a smoothing term; larger k flattens score gaps between top ranks.

scenario: 你希望融合能「看 query 意图」：关键词型 query 多信 BM25，语义型 query 多信 dense。
scenario_en: You want fusion to read query intent: trust BM25 more on keyword queries, dense more on semantic ones.
q: learned weighted fusion 怎么做，比 RRF 多了什么能力和代价？
q_en: How does learned weighted fusion work, and what ability and cost does it add over RRF?
why: 先把每路分数归一化（如 per-query min-max），再按 α·dense + (1−α)·sparse 加权，α 从点击数据学或在留出集上按 NDCG 调。它能按 query 意图调权（RRF 做不到），代价是要数据、要调、要长期维护。
why_en: Normalize each list then weight α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from clicks or tuned on held-out NDCG, adapting to intent at the cost of data and maintenance.
options: 和 RRF 完全一样，只是换了个名字，没有额外能力或代价
归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 加权，α 从点击/NDCG 学；能按意图调权，代价是要数据和维护
直接相加原始分，不归一化也不学权重，最省事
用 cross-encoder 重编码两路候选后取平均，不需要权重
options_en: Exactly the same as RRF, just renamed, with no extra ability or cost.
Normalize then weight α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from clicks/NDCG; adapts to intent, at the cost of data and maintenance.
Add raw scores directly, no normalization and no learned weights — the least effort.
Re-encode both lists with a cross-encoder and average, needing no weights.
optionExplanations: 关键差别在于 learned fusion 有可学的权重 α、能适配 query 意图，RRF 没有，说「一样」抹掉了这道题核心。
对；归一化解决尺度、α 让它按 query 意图在 BM25 和 dense 间调配，代价是要点击数据 + 调参 + 维护。
直接相加不归一化正是尺度陷阱；learned fusion 恰恰先归一化再加权。
cross-encoder 重编码是第二阶段精排的活，不是第一阶段两路融合的做法。
optionExplanations_en: The key difference is learned fusion's tunable α that adapts to intent, which RRF lacks, so 'the same' erases this card's point.
Correct — normalization fixes scale and α reallocates between BM25 and dense by intent, costing click data, tuning, and maintenance.
Adding raw scores unnormalized is the scale trap; learned fusion instead normalizes first, then weights.
Cross-encoder re-encoding is a second-stage re-ranking job, not first-stage two-list fusion.

termDefinitions.term: learned weighted fusion / 学习加权融合
termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合，α 由数据学出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned weighted fusion normalizes then fuses as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse, with α learned from data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化折损累积增益，衡量排序质量，越靠前的相关结果贡献越大。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NDCG (Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain) measures ranking quality, weighting relevant results higher when ranked earlier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户点了哪些结果的日志，用来学融合权重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Click-through data logs which results users clicked, used to learn fusion weights.

scenario: 你要在 RRF 和 learned weighted fusion 之间给 hybrid 检索选融合策略。
scenario_en: You must pick a fusion strategy for hybrid retrieval between RRF and learned weighted fusion.
q: RRF 和 learned weighted fusion 差在哪一维？
q_en: On what dimension do RRF and learned weighted fusion differ?
why: 核心轴是「鲁棒零参数 vs 能适配 query 意图」。RRF 无参数、只按 rank、开箱稳，但不会因 query 是关键词型还是语义型而调权；learned fusion 能按意图上调 BM25 或 dense，但需要点击数据、调参和长期维护。
why_en: The axis is robust-and-parameter-free versus intent-adaptive: RRF is fixed by rank and can't adapt, while learned fusion adapts to intent but needs data and upkeep.
tradeoff: RRF（零参数、鲁棒、不适配意图）vs learned fusion（适配 query 意图，但要数据+维护）
options: 两者都需要点击数据训练，区别只是公式写法不同
RRF 能按 query 意图调权，learned fusion 不能，正好相反
RRF 无参数按 rank、开箱稳但不适配意图；learned fusion 能按意图调权但要数据和维护
learned fusion 一定更好，RRF 已被淘汰没有使用场景
options_en: Both need click data to train, differing only in formula notation.
RRF adapts weights to query intent while learned fusion cannot — the reverse.
RRF is parameter-free by rank and robust but intent-blind; learned fusion adapts to intent but needs data and maintenance.
Learned fusion is always better and RRF is obsolete with no use case.
optionExplanations: RRF 恰恰不需要训练数据（纯按 rank），说两者都要数据是错的。
说反了：能按意图调权的是 learned fusion，RRF 是固定的无参数规则。
对；这就是取舍轴——RRF 拿鲁棒零维护换掉适配能力，learned fusion 拿维护成本换意图适配。
RRF 是 Elasticsearch/Vespa 的强基线、零维护，缺数据或求稳时反而更合适，没被淘汰。
optionExplanations_en: RRF needs no training data (pure rank), so claiming both need data is wrong.
Reversed: learned fusion is the intent-adaptive one; RRF is a fixed parameter-free rule.
Correct — that's the tradeoff axis: RRF trades adaptivity for robust zero-maintenance, learned fusion trades maintenance for intent adaptivity.
RRF is a strong zero-maintenance baseline in Elasticsearch/Vespa, better when data is scarce or robustness matters — not obsolete.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 1/(k+rank) 用排名融合，无参数、无需归一化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses by rank via 1/(k+rank), parameter-free and needing no normalization.

termDefinitions.term: learned weighted fusion / 学习加权融合
termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合，α 从数据学，能适配意图。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned weighted fusion fuses as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from data, adapting to intent.

termDefinitions.meaning: query 偏关键词型还是语义型，决定该多信 BM25 还是 dense。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Query intent is whether a query is keyword-heavy or semantic, deciding whether to trust BM25 or dense more.

scenario: 你在搭新搜索系统的 hybrid 融合，暂时没有点击日志，团队也没人力长期调权重，但要马上上线一个稳版本。
scenario_en: You're building hybrid fusion for a new search system with no click logs yet and no staffing to tune weights long-term, but need a stable version live now.
q: 没有点击数据、要快速上线一个稳基线，该选哪种融合？
q_en: With no click data and a need to ship a stable baseline fast, which fusion do you pick?
why: 选 RRF：无参数、只按 rank、不用归一化和标注，开箱就是强基线，正好匹配「没数据没人力维护」。等积累了点击数据、也有资源维护，再升级到 learned fusion 按意图调权。
why_en: Pick RRF: parameter-free, rank-based, no normalization or labels, a strong baseline out of the box that fits 'no data, no maintenance staff.'
tradeoff: RRF（零数据零维护、稳）vs learned fusion（要数据要维护、能适配意图）
whenOtherWins: 当你已有充足点击数据、且 query 意图差异大（关键词型 vs 语义型混杂），learned weighted fusion 能按意图调权，效果超过固定的 RRF。
options: learned weighted fusion：先花两周收点击数据训 α，再上线
RRF：无参数、按 rank、不用归一化，开箱即是强稳基线
直接相加 BM25 和 dense 原始分，最省事
只用 dense 一路，等有数据再考虑融合
options_en: Learned weighted fusion: spend two weeks collecting click data to train α, then ship.
RRF: parameter-free, rank-based, no normalization — a strong stable baseline out of the box.
Just add BM25 and dense raw scores directly — the least effort.
Use only the dense list and consider fusion once you have data.
optionExplanations: 没数据、没维护人力时先训 α 是本末倒置，上线被拖两周还没人长期调。
对；RRF 零参数零维护、开箱稳，正好配「没数据没人力还要快上线」的约束。
直接相加会踩 BM25 无上界主导的尺度陷阱，不是「稳基线」。
只用 dense 会漏精确关键词（SKU/错误码），放弃了 hybrid 的核心收益。
optionExplanations_en: Training α first with no data or maintenance staff is backwards — it delays launch two weeks with nobody to tune it long-term.
Correct — RRF is zero-parameter, zero-maintenance, and stable out of the box, matching 'no data, no staff, ship fast.'
Adding raw scores hits the scale trap where unbounded BM25 dominates — not a stable baseline.
Dense-only misses exact keywords (SKUs/error codes), throwing away hybrid's core benefit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 1/(k+rank) 用排名融合，无参数、开箱稳。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) fuses by rank via 1/(k+rank), parameter-free and stable out of the box.

termDefinitions.term: learned weighted fusion / 学习加权融合
termDefinitions.meaning: 归一化后按 α·dense+(1−α)·sparse 融合，α 从点击数据学，能适配意图但要维护。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Learned weighted fusion fuses as α·dense + (1−α)·sparse with α learned from clicks, adapting to intent but needing maintenance.

scenario: hybrid 融合后的候选集要交给 cross-encoder 精排；融合候选通常在 100–1000 篇量级。
scenario_en: The fused candidate set goes to the cross-encoder for re-ranking; fused candidates are typically 100–1000 docs.
q: 「融合候选 100–1000 篇」这个量级下游决定了什么？
q_en: What does the '100–1000 fused candidates' magnitude determine downstream?
why: 100–1000 是第一阶段召回后、进精排前的候选规模，它是算第二阶段成本的输入：cross-encoder 每篇一次前向传播，1000 篇≈2s（超 SLA），所以还要从这里再砍到 20–50 篇才精排。这个数字是连接召回和精排的桥。
why_en: It is the post-recall pre-rerank candidate size and the input to second-stage cost: at ~2ms/doc, 1000 docs ≈ 2s, so you further cut to 20–50 for re-ranking.
options: 是最终展示给用户的结果条数，页面上直接一次渲染这么多条
是 ANN 索引里 doc 向量的总量，决定整个索引占多大内存
是召回后进精排前的候选规模，决定 cross-encoder 精排成本和还要砍到多少篇
是系统每秒处理的 query 数（QPS），主要用于服务容量规划
options_en: The number of results shown to the user, all rendered on the page at once.
