optionExplanations: 误解：放进父类是继承层面的强绑定，跟两段代码要不要共享格式化逻辑是两码事。
误解：Singleton 管的是全局唯一实例，跟这两段格式化代码该不该合并无关。
对，文本相似不等于概念相同，收据展示和审计日志的变化规则不同，强行抽出来反而容易互相牵连。
误解：DRY 反对的是知识重复，不是禁止任何看起来相似的代码。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: putting it in a parent class is a heavy inheritance commitment, a different question from whether to share formatting logic.
Misconception: Singleton is about a single global instance, unrelated to whether these two formatting snippets should merge.
Correct — similar text isn't the same concept; the receipt and audit log change for different reasons, so forcing a merge risks entangling them later.
Misconception: DRY objects to duplicated knowledge, not to any code that merely looks similar.

q: 把应用设计原则的健康顺序排好：
q_en: Put the healthy order of applying design principles in sequence:
steps: 选择最小能解决当前问题的结构
从需求和变化点识别真实压力
如果出现重复、耦合或变化困难，再引入抽象或拆分
用原则名称解释取舍但不让名称驱动设计
why: 原则是判断工具，不是预制答案。先看问题，再决定简单结构是否已经不够。
why_en: Healthy principle use starts from real requirements and variation points, then adds only the abstraction needed.
tradeoff: 先看真实需求再决定结构 vs 先套用原则名称再找问题
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["read real requirement"] --> B["choose minimal structure"]
B --> C{"repetition, coupling, or change pain?"}
C -- no --> D["keep design simple"]
C -- yes --> E["introduce focused abstraction"]
E --> F["explain tradeoff with principle name"]

q: 补全通用原则速记：
q_en: Fill in the general-principles cheat sheet:
text: {{KISS}}：先简单；{{DRY}}：减少概念重复；{{YAGNI}}：不要实现未要求的未来。
why: 这三条能覆盖大部分 LLD 过度设计和维护性讨论。
why_en: KISS means start simple, DRY means avoid duplicated knowledge, and YAGNI means do not build speculative futures.

termDefinitions.meaning: KISS（Keep It Simple, Stupid）：优先选能工作的最简单方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: KISS stands for Keep It Simple, Stupid, meaning prefer the simplest design that works.

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: YAGNI（You Aren't Gonna Need It）：只实现当前需求真正要求的功能。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for You Aren't Gonna Need It, meaning only build what current requirements actually need.

q: 补全 SOLID 速记：
q_en: Fill in the SOLID cheat sheet:
text: {{SRP}} 让类职责聚焦，{{OCP}} 让新增行为少改旧代码，{{LSP}} 保证子类不破坏父类承诺，{{ISP}} 拆小接口，{{DIP}} 依赖抽象。
why: 这不是背诵终点，而是面试中解释设计取舍的语言。
why_en: SRP focuses responsibilities, OCP extends behavior safely, LSP preserves contracts, ISP keeps interfaces small, and DIP depends on abstractions.

termDefinitions.meaning: SRP（Single Responsibility Principle）：一个类应该只有一个改变的理由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SRP stands for Single Responsibility Principle, meaning a class should have only one reason to change.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

termDefinitions.meaning: LSP（Liskov Substitution Principle）：子类必须能替换父类而不破坏承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LSP stands for Liskov Substitution Principle, meaning subtypes must be usable wherever the base type is expected.

termDefinitions.meaning: ISP（Interface Segregation Principle）：接口应该小而专注。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ISP stands for Interface Segregation Principle, meaning interfaces should be small and focused.

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

scenario: OrderService 的方法里直接创建 StripeAPI 实例，导致单元测试必须连上真实的支付服务。
scenario_en: OrderService methods create a StripeAPI instance directly, so unit tests end up hitting the real payment service.
q: 哪项原则和技术最能改善这里的测试性？
q_en: Which principle and technique would most improve testability here?
options: 把所有字段都设成 public 属性
让 StripeAPI 反过来继承 OrderService
直接把相关单元测试删掉
用 DIP 依赖注入 PaymentGateway 接口
options_en: Make every field public.
Have StripeAPI inherit from OrderService instead.
Just delete the relevant unit tests.
Apply DIP and inject a PaymentGateway interface.
why: 依赖抽象之后，测试可以注入 fake 或 mock；业务逻辑不再绑死某个具体的外部服务。
why_en: Once the dependency points at an abstraction, tests can inject a fake or mock and the business logic is no longer tied to one concrete external service.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是一次性脚本，直接调用具体 API 也可能够用；面试里的服务设计通常应优先保留可测边界。
tradeoff: 直接依赖具体 API 的简单性 vs 依赖抽象带来的可测试性

termDefinitions.meaning: DIP（Dependency Inversion Principle）：高层业务应依赖抽象而不是具体实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DIP stands for Dependency Inversion Principle, meaning high-level logic should depend on abstractions rather than concrete implementations.

optionExplanations: 把字段全设成 public 只是放弃封装，测试照样得连真实的 StripeAPI。
让 StripeAPI 反过来继承 OrderService，关系完全颠倒，也没解决测试要连真实服务的问题。
删掉测试等于放弃验证，不是解决测试性问题的办法。
对，用 DIP 依赖 PaymentGateway 接口再注入，测试就能换成 fake，不用碰真实支付服务。
optionExplanations_en: Making every field public just abandons encapsulation; tests still have to hit the real StripeAPI.
Having StripeAPI inherit from OrderService inverts the relationship entirely and still doesn't stop tests from touching a real service.
Deleting the tests means giving up verification, not fixing the testability problem.
Correct — apply DIP by depending on a PaymentGateway interface and injecting it, so tests swap in a fake instead of the real service.

q: 每加一种支付方式都要改 PaymentProcessor，最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of editing PaymentProcessor every time a payment method is added?
options: 反复改核心逻辑，增加回归 bug 风险
新增的实现类数量变得太少
接口的数量会变得太多太杂
自动化测试变得完全不需要
options_en: Repeatedly editing core logic raises regression-bug risk.
You end up creating too few new implementation classes.
You end up with too many, too scattered interfaces.
Automated testing becomes completely unnecessary.
why: OCP 想避免的正是稳定代码被反复打开修改；把变化放进新的实现类能缩小回归范围。
why_en: OCP exists precisely to avoid reopening stable code again and again, and pushing change into new implementation classes shrinks the regression surface.

termDefinitions.meaning: OCP（Open/Closed Principle）：对扩展开放、对修改关闭。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OCP stands for Open/Closed Principle, meaning code should be open for extension but closed for modification.

optionExplanations: 对，反复打开这段核心逻辑改，每次都可能牵连出新的回归 bug。
误解：问题不是实现类太少，恰恰是没有用新实现类去承接变化。
误解：这里根本没引入接口，也就谈不上接口数量太多太杂。
误解：反而应该加测试防回归，自动化测试不会因此变得不需要。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — reopening this core logic every time risks pulling in a new regression bug each round.
Misconception: the problem isn't too few implementation classes, it's that new classes aren't being used to absorb the change at all.
Misconception: no interface was introduced here, so there's no interface-sprawl problem to speak of.
Misconception: if anything you need more regression tests here — automation doesn't become unnecessary.

scenario: CoffeeMachine 类同时管理库存、收款、冲泡配方和屏幕渲染，后续每个新需求都要改它。
scenario_en: CoffeeMachine manages inventory, payment, brew recipes, and screen rendering all at once, so every new requirement means editing it.
q: 你会如何解释重构方向？
q_en: How would you explain the refactoring direction here?
options: 把所有方法都统一改成 static 方法
按变化原因拆成四个协作类分开管理
只在原有方法里继续叠加 if 分支判断
只把类的名字换一个就足够
options_en: Turn every method into a static method.
Split into four collaborating classes by reason to change.
Keep stacking if-branches inside the original method.
Just rename the class and call it done.
why: SRP 不是为了类的数量多，而是让库存、支付、配方、显示的变化互不牵连。
why_en: SRP isn't about having more classes — it's about keeping inventory, payment, recipe, and display changes from tangling with each other.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目只要求最小冲泡流程、不涉及支付和显示，先留一个简单 orchestrator 也可以。
tradeoff: 单类快速起步 vs 拆分后每个变化互不影响
diagram:
flowchart LR
CM["CoffeeMachine orchestrator"] --> I["Inventory"]
CM --> P["Payment"]
CM --> R["Recipe/Brewer"]
CM --> D["Display"]
I --> IR["stock changes"]
P --> PR["payment changes"]
R --> RR["brew rules"]
D --> DR["UI text"]
optionExplanations: 把方法都改成 static 只是换个调用方式，库存、支付、配方、显示还是缠在一起变化。
对，按变化原因拆成库存、支付、配方、显示四个协作类，各自改动互不牵连。
继续叠 if 分支只会让这一个类越来越臃肿，职责混杂的问题完全没解决。
只改名字不改结构，库存、支付、配方、显示还是绑在同一个类里一起变化。
optionExplanations_en: Turning every method static just changes how it's called; inventory, payment, recipe, and display still change together.
Correct — split by reason to change into inventory, payment, recipe, and display classes so each change stays isolated.
Stacking more if-branches only bloats this one class further, leaving the tangled responsibilities untouched.
Renaming the class without restructuring it still leaves inventory, payment, recipe, and display bound together.

q: 为什么「接口越多越好」不是正确理解 SOLID？
q_en: Why is "more interfaces is always better" a wrong reading of SOLID?
options: 接口这种语法只能用在 Java 语言里
接口在任何场景下都完全没有成本
接口也有认知成本，只有真实变化点才值得加
接口会自动帮你生成对应的实现代码
options_en: Interfaces only exist as a Java-only syntax feature.
Interfaces never carry any cost in any scenario.
Interfaces have cognitive cost too, so they're worth adding only at a real variation point.
Interfaces automatically generate their implementations for you.
why: 抽象能隔离变化，但也会增加间接层；面试里要展示你知道何时加、何时不加。
why_en: Abstraction isolates change but also adds a layer of indirection, so the interview signal is knowing when to add it and when not to.
tradeoff: 接口带来的扩展安全 vs 额外的间接层认知成本

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

optionExplanations: 误解：接口是通用的面向对象概念，不是 Java 独有的语法。
误解：接口不是零成本的，多一层间接就多一层要理解和维护的东西。
对，接口也有认知成本，只有真的存在变化点时才值得为它多加一层间接。
误解：接口不会自动生成实现，该写的实现类一个都少不了。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: interfaces are a general OO concept, not Java-only syntax.
Misconception: interfaces aren't free — every extra layer of indirection is one more thing to understand and maintain.
Correct — interfaces carry cognitive cost too, worth the extra indirection only when a real variation point exists.
Misconception: interfaces don't auto-generate implementations; you still have to write every implementing class.

q: 关于如何在面试里使用这些设计原则，哪些说法是合理的？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about using these design principles in an interview are reasonable? (multi-select)
options: 不需要不断点名原则
用原则指导决策并解释取舍
原则是思考工具，不是打勾清单
必须在每句话里都提一次 SOLID
options_en: You don't need to keep naming principles out loud.
Use principles to guide decisions and explain tradeoffs.
Principles are thinking tools, not a checklist to tick off.
You must mention SOLID in every single sentence.
why: 好的设计会自然体现原则；刻意报术语不如清楚说明为什么这样拆类或抽象。
why_en: Good design shows the principles naturally, so explaining why you split a class or added an abstraction beats reciting the term names.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: SOLID：五项面向对象设计原则的合称。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is the acronym for five object-oriented design principles.

optionExplanations: 对，好设计会自然体现原则，不需要嘴上反复点名字。
对，原则该用来支撑你的决策并解释取舍，这才是面试官想听的。
对，原则是帮你判断的思考工具，不是拿来打勾交差的清单。
误选：刻意在每句话里塞 SOLID 只会显得在背书，不会加分。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — good design shows the principles naturally, no need to keep naming them out loud.
Correct — principles should back up your decisions and explain the tradeoff, that's what interviewers want to hear.
Correct — principles are thinking tools for judgment calls, not a checklist to tick off.
Wrong pick: forcing SOLID into every sentence just reads as reciting, it earns no extra credit.

scenario: 面试官问：“为什么不现在就抽象出一个 Validator 服务？”
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: "Why not abstract out a Validator service right now?"
q: 哪个回答最成熟？
q_en: Which answer sounds the most mature?
options: 因为 DRY 原则从来都不重要
我会立刻抽象出所有校验逻辑
Validator 必须做成 Singleton 模式
现在只有 User 一处用，先放 User 里；多处重复再提取
options_en: Because the DRY principle never matters.
I would abstract all validation logic immediately.
Validator must be built as a Singleton.
Only User uses this today, so keep it there for now and extract once the rule repeats in multiple places.
why: 这个回答同时体现了 KISS、DRY 和 YAGNI 的平衡；没有拒绝抽象，只是把它推迟到有证据时再做。
why_en: This answer balances KISS, DRY, and YAGNI at once — it doesn't reject abstraction, it just defers it until there's real evidence for it.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求已经写明多个实体共享同一验证规则，提前抽出 Validator 就合理。
tradeoff: 现在保持简单 vs 提前抽象共享校验逻辑

termDefinitions.meaning: DRY（Don't Repeat Yourself）：概念上相同的逻辑只维护一处。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DRY stands for Don't Repeat Yourself, meaning conceptually identical logic should live in one place.

termDefinitions.meaning: Singleton（单例模式）：保证一个类全局只有一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Singleton pattern ensures a class has only one instance globally.

optionExplanations: 误解：这否定了 DRY 的价值，实际上答案本身也在用 DRY 的判断，只是不着急动手。
立刻抽象所有校验逻辑是在没有证据前先下重注，只有多个实体已经共享规则时才该这样做。
误解：Validator 该不该做成 Singleton 是另一个问题，跟现在要不要抽象没关系。
对，现在只有 User 用，先放着；等重复出现在多处再提取，同时兼顾了 KISS、DRY、YAGNI。
optionExplanations_en: Misconception: this dismisses DRY entirely, but the right answer is still using DRY's judgment call, just not rushing it.
Abstracting all validation immediately bets early without evidence — that only makes sense once multiple entities already share the rule.
Misconception: whether Validator should be a Singleton is a separate question, unrelated to whether to abstract it now.
Correct — only User uses it today, so keep it there and extract once the rule repeats elsewhere, balancing KISS, DRY, and YAGNI.

q: 低层设计（LLD）面试主要考什么？
q_en: What do low-level design interviews mainly test?
options: 大规模分布式架构与跨机房容量估算方案
把自包含问题拆成清晰的类和交互关系
只写 SQL 查询语句的性能优化技巧
只背诵各种经典设计模式的名称清单
options_en: Large-scale distributed architecture and cross-datacenter capacity estimation.
Organizing a self-contained problem into classes, interfaces, and clean interactions.
Writing SQL query performance optimizations and nothing else.
Memorizing the names of classic design patterns and nothing else.
why: LLD 的核心是代码结构：对象是什么、谁拥有状态、方法如何协作、后续需求能否自然加入。它不是在白板上画服务拓扑。
why_en: Low-level design interviews test whether you can turn a scoped problem into clean classes, interfaces, state, and interactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层设计：面试中考察类、接口、方法和对象交互的设计能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD, or Low-Level Design, is an interview format that tests how you design classes, interfaces, and object interactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用于查询和操作关系型数据库的语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL, or Structured Query Language, is the language used to query and manipulate relational databases.

optionExplanations: 很多人把 LLD 和系统设计弄混，但真正考的不是跨机房容量和分布式拓扑，而是单个问题内部的对象设计。
这正是 LLD 的核心：把一个范围明确的问题拆成职责清楚的类、接口和交互，代码能不能维护是评分重点。
SQL 调优只是实现细节的一个角落，面试官更想看你怎么划分对象和状态，而不是查询语句本身。
背出模式名字说明不了设计能力，面试官要看你能不能在真实变化点上用对模式，而不是罗列词汇。
optionExplanations_en: It's tempting to confuse LLD with system design, but the interview isn't about cross-datacenter capacity or distributed topology.
This is the core of LLD: turning a scoped problem into classes, interfaces, and interactions with clear ownership and clean structure.
SQL tuning is just one implementation detail; the interviewer cares far more about how you split objects and state.
Reciting pattern names says nothing about design skill—what matters is applying a pattern at a real variation point.

scenario: 题目是“设计停车场系统”，面试官要求你做低层设计而不是系统设计。
scenario_en: The prompt is "design a parking lot," and the interviewer wants low-level design rather than system design.
q: 你的第一层关注点应该是什么？
q_en: What should you focus on first?
options: 先规划覆盖美国欧洲亚洲三地的完整跨区域部署方案
ParkingLot、Spot、Vehicle 类与方法
先估算 Kafka 分区数量和每秒消息吞吐量指标
先设计 CDN 边缘节点的静态内容分发缓存策略
options_en: Planning a full deployment spanning the US, Europe, and Asia across regions.
Modeling ParkingLot, Spot, and Vehicle classes and their methods.
Estimating Kafka partition count and per-second message throughput metrics.
Designing a CDN edge-node caching strategy for static content distribution.
why: LLD 关注单个功能或服务内部的代码蓝图。先建模类、状态和操作，再讨论边界和扩展。
why_en: For LLD, start with the domain objects, state, methods, and relationships inside the feature rather than distributed infrastructure.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求系统设计停车场平台或网约车后端，才切到服务、存储、流量和扩展架构。
tradeoff: 对象建模的代码蓝图 vs 分布式基础设施的架构取舍

termDefinitions.meaning: 停车场系统里代表整个场地、管理车位分配的核心类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ParkingLot is the core class that represents the whole facility and manages spot assignment.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种分布式消息队列，常用于系统设计里的异步事件流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue commonly used for asynchronous event streaming in system design.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN, or Content Delivery Network, caches static content on edge servers close to users.

optionExplanations: 多区域部署规划属于系统设计范畴，只有题目明确要跨地域运营停车场平台时才该先谈这个。
题目限定 LLD，就该先建模 ParkingLot、Spot、Vehicle 这些核心实体和它们之间的方法交互。
Kafka 分区和吞吐量估算是异步消息管线的系统设计话题，单场地停车逻辑用不上。
CDN 边缘缓存解决的是静态内容分发问题，跟车位分配这种强状态逻辑没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-region deployment planning belongs to system design—only start there if the prompt explicitly asks for a cross-region platform.
Since the prompt is scoped as LLD, start by modeling ParkingLot, Spot, and Vehicle and how their methods interact.
Kafka partition and throughput sizing is a system-design topic for async pipelines, not a single-facility parking problem.
CDN edge caching solves static-content delivery, which has nothing to do with stateful spot-assignment logic.

scenario: 你在准备一道“设计电梯调度系统”的 LLD 题，脑子里冒出要不要把 Factory、Observer、Visitor 等模式全部用上、并按经典 UML 继承层级建模。
scenario_en: You are preparing an elevator scheduling LLD and wondering whether to force Factory, Observer, Visitor, and a classic UML inheritance tree into it.
q: 更贴近现代生产代码的取向是什么？
q_en: What approach is closer to modern production code?
options: 把每个模式目录里的模式都尝试套进设计
先背熟 GoF 模式定义，再决定要不要用
优先组合和简单状态，只在真正需要变化点时才引入模式
用最深的继承层级覆盖所有电梯类型
options_en: Try to force every pattern from the catalog into the design.
Memorize GoF pattern definitions first, then decide whether to use them.
Default to composition and simple state, and only reach for a pattern at a real variation point.
Use the deepest inheritance hierarchy to cover every elevator type.
why: 现代生产代码更看重组合、简单状态和务实取舍；模式只在真正遇到变化点时才引入，不是提前铺好目录。
why_en: Modern production code favors composition and simple state, reaching for a design pattern only at an actual variation point instead of pre-loading the whole catalog.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确追问某个模式名称（常见于部分印度/亚洲公司），可以在合适场景点名模式，但仍以解决变化点为主。
tradeoff: 组合+按需引入模式 vs 教材式套用继承层级和模式目录

termDefinitions.meaning: 工厂模式：把对象创建逻辑集中封装，调用方不用关心具体子类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern centralizes object creation so callers don't need to know the concrete subclass.

termDefinitions.meaning: 观察者模式：状态变化时自动通知一组订阅者。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Observer pattern notifies a set of subscribers automatically when state changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 访问者模式：把对一组对象的操作抽出来，不用修改这些对象本身的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Visitor pattern pulls an operation on a group of objects out of those objects' own classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指经典《设计模式》一书作者合称，书中列出 23 种经典模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GoF, or Gang of Four, refers to the authors of the classic Design Patterns book and its 23 catalog patterns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

optionExplanations: 提前把目录里的模式全部塞进去，只会让代码变复杂，和真实变化点无关的模式就是过度设计。
先背定义没错，但只背不用于判断反而本末倒置——现代实践更看重能不能识别变化点。
现代生产代码优先用组合和简单状态表达行为，只有真正出现变化点时才引入某个具体模式。
继承层级越深，子类之间耦合越紧，后续加新电梯类型时改动会牵连整棵树，维护成本高。
optionExplanations_en: Forcing every catalog pattern in just adds complexity—patterns unrelated to a real variation point are over-engineering.
Memorizing definitions isn't wrong, but treating it as the deciding step gets the priority backwards for modern practice.
Modern production code defaults to composition and simple state, reaching for a specific pattern only at a real variation point.
A deep inheritance tree tightly couples subclasses, so adding a new elevator type forces changes across the whole hierarchy.

q: LLD 和系统设计最根本的区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between LLD and system design?
options: 两者都要求提交可编译完整项目
LLD 只画网络拓扑图，不谈状态
LLD 和系统设计都不需要解释取舍
LLD 管类和状态；系统设计管服务和流量
options_en: Both require a full compilable project submission.
LLD only draws network topology diagrams and ignores state.
Neither LLD nor system design requires explaining tradeoffs.
LLD is about classes and state; system design is about services and traffic.
why: 系统设计画的是大系统地图，LLD 写的是某个组件或功能内部的代码蓝图。二者问题、尺度和评价点都不同。
why_en: System design focuses on large-scale architecture, while LLD focuses on object models, APIs, state, and code-level behavior.
tradeoff: 组件内部代码蓝图 vs 分布式服务架构取舍

termDefinitions.meaning: 组件对外暴露的方法调用接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API, or Application Programming Interface, is the set of methods a component exposes to callers.

optionExplanations: 两边都不要求交出可编译完整项目，LLD 常用伪代码，系统设计更是几乎不写完整代码。
这个说法正好反了——LLD 恰恰围绕状态展开，网络拓扑图才是系统设计的产出。
两种面试都要求解释取舍，只是取舍的对象不同：一个是对象职责，一个是服务边界。
这正是两者的分界线：LLD 管的是类和状态所有权，系统设计管的是服务拆分和流量走向。
optionExplanations_en: Neither round requires a fully compilable project—LLD usually accepts pseudocode, and system design rarely writes complete code at all.
This has it backwards—LLD is centered on state, while network topology diagrams are what system design produces.
Both rounds expect you to explain tradeoffs, just about different things: object responsibilities versus service boundaries.
This is exactly the dividing line: LLD owns classes and state, system design owns service decomposition and traffic.

scenario: 同样是网约车题，面试官说这是低层设计面试。
scenario_en: The same rideshare prompt is explicitly framed as a low-level design interview.
q: 哪种产出更符合 LLD？
q_en: Which output better matches an LLD interview?
options: 画 matching service、pricing service、queue、datastore 的服务图
设计 Trip、TripState、PricingCalculator 以及状态转换方法
估算全球司机位置写入 QPS
讨论多区域强一致性
options_en: Draw a service diagram with a matching service, pricing service, queue, and datastore.
Design Trip, TripState, and PricingCalculator along with their state-transition methods.
Estimate global QPS for driver location writes.
Discuss multi-region strong consistency.
why: LLD 需要把某个功能的对象和行为讲清楚，例如 Trip 如何分配司机、开始、完成、取消。服务拓扑属于系统设计。
why_en: For rideshare LLD, model classes like Trip and PricingCalculator and their state transitions rather than distributed services.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目明确是“设计 Uber 后端架构”，服务图和扩展性讨论才是主线。
tradeoff: 对象/状态建模 vs 分布式服务拓扑与容量规划

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，衡量系统吞吐量的常用指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS, or Queries Per Second, measures how many requests a system handles each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 表示 Trip 生命周期状态的枚举，例如已请求、已分配司机、进行中、已完成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TripState is an enum representing the trip's lifecycle, such as requested, assigned, in progress, or completed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责根据行程数据计算车费的组件接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PricingCalculator is the component interface responsible for computing the fare from trip data.

optionExplanations: 画 matching/pricing service 拓扑图是系统设计该做的事，LLD 场景下这一步跳过了对象建模。
题目明确是 LLD，就该设计 Trip、TripState、PricingCalculator 这些实体和它们的状态转换方法。
全球司机位置写入 QPS 属于容量规划，是系统设计要算的数，不是 LLD 该展开的内容。
多区域强一致性讨论的是分布式存储取舍，只有在被要求做 Uber 后端架构时才该谈。
optionExplanations_en: Drawing a matching/pricing service diagram is a system-design move; it skips the object modeling this LLD round wants.
Since this is explicitly LLD, design Trip, TripState, and PricingCalculator along with their state-transition methods.
Global QPS for driver-location writes is a capacity-planning number that belongs to system design, not this LLD round.
Multi-region strong consistency is a distributed-storage tradeoff—only relevant if asked to design the Uber backend.

scenario: 你在设计 Trip 类，Trip 只能在 DRIVER_ASSIGNED 后 start，只能在 IN_PROGRESS 后 complete。
scenario_en: You are designing a Trip class: it can start only after DRIVER_ASSIGNED and complete only after IN_PROGRESS.
q: 这段代码展示了哪种 LLD 能力？
q_en: What LLD skill does this code demonstrate?
options: 只展示系统容量估算
把所有规则推给 UI
把业务状态转换封装在拥有状态的对象里
把 Trip 做成全局单例
options_en: Only show system capacity estimation.
Push all the validation rules into the UI layer.
Encapsulate business state transitions inside the object that owns the state.
Make Trip a global singleton.
why: LLD 看重对象是否能维护自己的不变量。Trip 拥有 state，就应该在相关方法里拒绝非法转换。
why_en: The code shows LLD state ownership by keeping transition rules inside the Trip object that owns the state.
whenOtherWins: 如果状态流非常复杂且行为随状态大幅变化，可以进一步引入状态机结构。
tradeoff: 对象自我校验状态转换 vs 把校验规则丢给外部调用方/UI
diagram:
stateDiagram-v2
[*] --> REQUESTED
REQUESTED --> DRIVER_ASSIGNED : assign driver
DRIVER_ASSIGNED --> IN_PROGRESS : start_trip
IN_PROGRESS --> COMPLETED : complete_trip
REQUESTED --> CANCELED : cancel
DRIVER_ASSIGNED --> CANCELED : cancel

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象在任何时刻都必须保持成立的规则，例如状态只能按合法顺序转换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a rule that must always hold for an object, such as only allowing legal state transitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单例模式：整个程序里某个类只允许存在一个实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A singleton is a pattern that allows only one instance of a class to exist in the whole program.

optionExplanations: 这段代码里完全没有容量或吞吐相关的内容，它展示的是状态转换逻辑，不是估算能力。
代码恰恰没有把校验丢给外部——start_trip 和 complete_trip 自己检查状态再决定能不能转换。
Trip 拥有 state 字段，也在自己的方法里拒绝非法转换，这正是对象自我维护不变量的写法。
代码里没有任何单例迹象，Trip 应该是每次行程各自独立的实例，做成单例反而会互相污染状态。
optionExplanations_en: There's nothing about capacity or throughput in this snippet at all—it's demonstrating state-transition logic, not estimation.
The code does the opposite of pushing validation to the UI—start_trip and complete_trip check state themselves before transitioning.
Trip owns the state field and its own methods reject illegal transitions—that's an object protecting its own invariant.
There's no singleton pattern here; each trip needs its own instance, or concurrent trips would corrupt each other's state.

q: 不同地区 LLD 面试格式的一个常见差异是？
q_en: What is one common regional difference in LLD interview format?
options: 所有地区都完全禁止使用伪代码
美国只问 UML，亚洲只问 CDN 架构
所有地区都要求提交可编译项目
美国偏真实语言代码，亚洲偏结构化伪代码
options_en: Every region completely forbids pseudocode.
US interviews only ask about UML, and Asian interviews only ask about CDN architecture.
Every region requires a fully compilable project submission.
US Big Tech leans toward real-language code, while some Asian interviews lean toward structured pseudocode.
why: 文章强调格式会变，但核心能力不变：类、关系、行为和解释。你应提前问清目标公司的期望。
why_en: Some interviews expect partial real-language code while others accept structured pseudocode, but the design skills are the same.
tradeoff: 真实语言部分代码 vs 结构化伪代码

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用接近自然语言的结构描述逻辑，不追求语法可编译。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pseudocode describes logic in near-natural-language structure without requiring compilable syntax.

optionExplanations: 说法太绝对——很多亚洲和部分美国公司的面试都接受结构化伪代码，不是完全禁止。
这把两地面试内容简化到荒谬——UML 和 CDN 架构都不是任何一个地区的唯一考点。
这也太绝对，两边面试通常都不要求交出可编译完整项目，重点在设计思路而非语法完整性。
这是文章总结的真实趋势：美国大厂偏真实语言部分代码，一些亚洲公司偏结构化伪代码，但核心能力一样。
optionExplanations_en: That's too absolute—many Asian and some US interviews accept structured pseudocode; it isn't universally forbidden.
This oversimplifies to absurdity—UML and CDN architecture are not the sole focus of either region's interviews.
Also too absolute: neither region typically requires a fully compilable submission; the focus is design reasoning, not syntax.
This matches the guide's real pattern: US Big Tech leans toward real-language code, some Asian interviews lean toward pseudocode, same underlying skill.

scenario: 你在面试中发现面试官明确追问 Factory、Strategy 等模式名称。
scenario_en: During the interview, the interviewer explicitly asks about pattern names such as Factory and Strategy.
q: 更合适的应对是什么？
q_en: What is the better way to respond?
options: 完全拒绝讨论任何设计模式的话题
在自然适用时点名模式并解释变化点
强行把模式套进每一个类里面
只背模式定义却不讲具体设计
options_en: Completely refuse to ever discuss design patterns.
Name a pattern when it naturally fits and explain the variation point.
Force a pattern onto every single class in the design.
Recite pattern definitions instead of discussing the design.
why: 有些地区或公司更直接考模式。你不需要强塞，但要能识别合适场景并说明取舍。
why_en: When pattern vocabulary is expected, name the pattern only where it naturally solves a concrete variation point.
whenOtherWins: 在更偏美国大厂的面试里，模式名称通常不如设计理由重要，但自然点名也没问题。
tradeoff: 按需点名模式并解释变化点 vs 完全回避或强行套用模式

termDefinitions.meaning: 策略模式：把可互换的算法封装成独立类，运行时切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms as separate classes that can be swapped at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 工厂模式：把对象创建逻辑集中封装，调用方不用关心具体子类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Factory pattern centralizes object creation so callers don't need to know the concrete subclass.

optionExplanations: 完全拒绝讨论模式会显得没准备，即便面试官更看重设计理由，聊模式本身也不该被回避。
在自然适用的地方点名模式并说清它解决的变化点，既满足喜欢模式名的面试官，也不牺牲设计质量。
强行在每个类上都套模式会制造不必要的抽象层，反而让代码更难读、更难维护。
只背定义不谈设计等于把面试变成默写，面试官想看的是你能不能把定义用在这道题上。
optionExplanations_en: Flatly refusing to discuss patterns looks unprepared—even when reasoning matters more, naming patterns shouldn't be off the table.
Naming a pattern only where it naturally applies and explaining the variation point satisfies pattern-focused interviewers without sacrificing design quality.
Forcing a pattern onto every class adds unnecessary abstraction layers, making the code harder to read and maintain.
Reciting definitions without applying them turns the interview into rote memorization instead of design judgment.

scenario: 题目只给一句“设计咖啡机”，没有说明饮品类型、支付、补料、错误处理或 UI 范围。
scenario_en: The prompt only says "design a coffee machine" and does not specify drinks, payment, refills, errors, or UI scope.
q: 你应该先做什么？
q_en: What should you do first?
options: 直接写完整代码
问少量澄清问题并确认范围
默认所有功能都要做
只讨论缓存
options_en: Immediately start writing complete code.
Ask a few clarifying questions and confirm scope.
Assume every possible feature is in scope.
Only discuss caching.
why: LLD prompt 常常故意模糊。先把核心能力、规则、错误和边界问清楚，才能避免设计跑偏。
why_en: Start ambiguous LLD prompts by asking focused clarifying questions and confirming scope before designing classes.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官已经给出完整需求并催促设计，就快速复述确认后进入实体和类设计。
tradeoff: 先澄清范围 vs 直接开始编码
optionExplanations: 题目连饮品类型和支付方式都没说，直接写完整代码大概率会做错方向，白白浪费时间。
先问几个关键澄清问题、确认范围，是应对模糊 LLD prompt 的标准开局，能避免设计跑偏。
默认所有功能都要做会让范围失控，你会把精力浪费在面试官根本不关心的边角功能上。
只讨论缓存跳过了核心的饮品制作、支付和错误处理逻辑，缓存不是这道题的重点。
optionExplanations_en: With drink types, payment, and refills all unspecified, writing complete code immediately risks solving the wrong problem.
Asking a few focused clarifying questions and confirming scope is the standard opener for an ambiguous LLD prompt—it prevents drift.
Assuming every possible feature is in scope lets the design run away and wastes time on edge cases the interviewer never asked for.
Jumping straight to caching skips the core brewing, payment, and error-handling logic that this prompt is actually about.

q: LLD 面试常见评估维度有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which dimensions are commonly assessed in LLD interviews? (Select all that apply.)
options: 问题分析
类设计
代码质量
可扩展性和沟通
options_en: Problem analysis
Class design
Code quality
Extensibility and communication
why: 不同公司 rubric 细节不同，但通常都在看你是否能理解问题、拆类、写出可维护结构，并清楚说明取舍。
why_en: LLD interviews commonly assess problem analysis, class design, code quality, extensibility, and communication.
optionExplanations: 问题分析体现在你能不能提取关键实体、问出恰当的澄清问题，把模糊需求变成可设计的范围。
类设计体现在职责划分是否清楚、状态该由谁持有、方法签名是否合理。
代码质量体现在封装、状态管理和关注点分离，而不只是语法能不能跑。
可扩展性和沟通体现在新需求能不能被现有边界吸收，以及你能不能把推理过程讲清楚。
optionExplanations_en: Problem analysis shows up in whether you extract the right entities and ask clarifying questions that turn a vague prompt into a scoped design.
Class design shows up in whether responsibilities are clear, who owns which state, and whether method signatures make sense.
Code quality shows up in encapsulation and separation of concerns, not just whether the syntax happens to run.
Extensibility and communication show up in whether new requirements fit existing boundaries and whether you can explain your reasoning.

q: 问题分析阶段强候选人的表现是什么？
q_en: What does a strong candidate do during problem analysis?
options: 提前实现所有可能出现的未来功能
完全不听需求描述就直接写代码
只背诵 SOLID 五个原则的定义
提取关键实体和职责，问澄清问题先框定范围
options_en: Try to implement every possible future feature upfront.
Start writing code without listening to the requirements at all.
Just recite the five SOLID principle definitions.
Extract entities and responsibilities, then scope with clarifying questions.
why: 面试官不希望你在没理解需求时开写。好的开局是把题目变成可设计的清晰范围。
why_en: Strong problem analysis extracts entities and responsibilities, asks clarifying questions, and scopes the problem before coding.

termDefinitions.fullName: Single Responsibility, Open-Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface Segregation, Dependency Inversion
termDefinitions.meaning: 五个面向对象设计原则的首字母缩写：单一职责、开闭、里氏替换、接口隔离、依赖倒置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOLID is an acronym for five object-oriented design principles: single responsibility, open-closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, and dependency inversion.

optionExplanations: 把所有可能的未来功能都实现是过度设计的信号，强候选人反而会先框定当前范围。
不听需求直接写代码是最常见的负信号，说明你跳过了理解问题这一步。
背 SOLID 定义不等于会用，面试官想看的是你怎么把原则落到这道具体题上。
提取关键实体、问几个澄清问题、先框定范围，正是强候选人开局该做的事。
optionExplanations_en: Trying to implement every possible future feature is a sign of over-engineering; strong candidates scope the current problem first.
Writing code without listening to requirements is the most common negative signal—it means you skipped understanding the problem.
Reciting SOLID definitions isn't the same as applying them; the interviewer wants to see the principles used on this actual problem.
Extracting key entities, asking a few clarifying questions, and scoping the problem is exactly how a strong candidate opens.

q: 类设计阶段面试官主要看什么？
q_en: What does the interviewer mainly look for during class design?
options: 是否精确估算了机房带宽和容量
是否画出了最复杂的 UML 符号图
是否用上了最多种类的设计模式
类的职责、状态所有权和依赖方向是否清楚
options_en: Whether you precisely estimated data-center bandwidth and capacity.
Whether you drew the most elaborate UML notation diagram.
Whether you used the greatest possible number of design patterns.
Whether responsibilities, state ownership, and dependencies are clear.
why: 好的类设计会让后续实现自然流动。职责和边界不清会让代码质量、扩展和解释都变难。
why_en: Class design is judged by clear responsibilities, state ownership, APIs, and dependency direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

optionExplanations: 机房带宽估算属于系统设计的容量规划，跟单个功能内部的类怎么划分没关系。
UML 符号画得多复杂不重要，图只是辅助沟通，核心还是类本身的设计质量。
用了多少设计模式不是评分标准，强行堆模式反而是负信号而不是加分项。
面试官真正看的是职责、状态所有权、方法签名和依赖方向是否清楚，这决定了代码能不能维护。
optionExplanations_en: Data-center bandwidth estimation is a system-design capacity concern, unrelated to how you split classes within one feature.
How elaborate the UML notation looks doesn't matter—diagrams are just communication support, not the actual design quality.
The number of patterns used isn't the metric; forcing in extra patterns is a negative signal, not a bonus.
What the interviewer actually checks is whether responsibilities, state ownership, method signatures, and dependencies are clear and maintainable.

q: LLD 面试里的代码质量不只是语法，它还包括什么？
q_en: Beyond syntax, what does code quality mean in an LLD interview?
options: 写了注释就算合格
能跑就行，不用管代码结构
封装、状态管理和关注点分离
只用运行时间复杂度打分
options_en: Having a comment is good enough.
As long as it runs, the structure doesn't matter.
Encapsulation, state management, and separation of concerns.
Only grade it by runtime complexity.
why: 即使用伪代码，面试官也在看你的代码是否像真实团队愿意维护的结构。
why_en: Code quality in LLD includes encapsulation, state management, separation of concerns, naming, and disciplined structure even in pseudocode.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装：把对象内部状态隐藏起来，只通过方法暴露受控的操作接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides an object's internal state and exposes only controlled operations through its methods.

optionExplanations: 写了注释不等于结构清楚，面试官在乎的是代码有没有把状态和职责组织好。
能跑但结构混乱一样会被扣分，LLD 看重的是团队愿不愿意接手维护这段代码。
封装、状态管理和关注点分离才是代码质量的核心，即使用伪代码也能体现出来。
只看运行时间复杂度是算法题的评分逻辑，LLD 更关心结构而不是性能数字。
optionExplanations_en: Having a comment doesn't mean the structure is clean; the interviewer cares whether state and responsibilities are organized well.
Code that runs but is poorly structured still loses points—LLD cares whether a team would actually want to maintain it.
Encapsulation, state management, and separation of concerns are the real core of code quality, visible even in pseudocode.
Grading only by runtime complexity is an algorithm-round metric; LLD cares about structure, not a performance number.

scenario: 你完成了核心设计，面试官追问“如果要支持新车辆类型/新支付方式怎么办？”
scenario_en: After your core design, the interviewer asks how it would support a new vehicle type or payment method.
q: 这个追问主要在考什么？
q_en: What is this follow-up mainly testing?
options: 你是否背出所有 GoF 模式
你能否估算全球流量
设计能否扩展而不重写主体结构
你能否写前端样式
options_en: Whether you can recite every GoF pattern.
Whether you can estimate global traffic.
Whether the design can absorb new functionality without rewriting the core structure.
Whether you can write frontend styling.
why: 跟进需求通常测试边界是否干净。好设计能通过新增类或小范围修改吸收变化。
why_en: Follow-up requirements test whether your design can evolve cleanly without rewriting the core structure.
whenOtherWins: 如果初始需求很小，不要提前实现所有未来扩展；只要能解释如何扩展即可。
tradeoff: 干净边界支撑扩展 vs 大范围重写主体结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 指经典《设计模式》一书作者合称，书中列出 23 种经典模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GoF, or Gang of Four, refers to the authors of the classic Design Patterns book and its 23 catalog patterns.

optionExplanations: 背出所有 GoF 模式名跟这个追问没关系，面试官不是在考模式词典。
全球流量估算是系统设计的容量话题，这个追问问的是代码结构能不能扩展。
这个追问在测试设计边界是否干净——能不能只加类或小改就吸收新车辆类型或支付方式。
前端样式跟后端类设计的扩展性完全无关，这不是这个追问想考察的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Reciting every GoF pattern name has nothing to do with this follow-up—it isn't testing a pattern glossary.
Estimating global traffic is a system-design capacity topic; this follow-up is asking about the code structure's flexibility.
This follow-up tests whether the design's boundaries are clean enough to absorb a new vehicle type or payment method with minimal changes.
Frontend styling has nothing to do with backend class extensibility—that's not what this follow-up is probing.

q: 为什么沟通本身是 LLD 评分项？
q_en: Why is communication itself part of LLD scoring?
options: 面试官要跟上推理路径并能一起调整设计
沟通可以完全替代设计能力
说得越多就越不用写代码
LLD 面试本质是销售话术面试
options_en: The interviewer needs to follow your reasoning and adjust the design together when probing.
Communication can fully substitute for design ability.
The more you talk, the less code you need to write.
An LLD interview is essentially a sales pitch.
why: LLD 是协作式设计。清楚讲出范围、取舍和修改点，比沉默写完一坨代码更能展示工程判断。
why_en: Communication matters because the interviewer needs to follow your reasoning and see how you adapt under probing.
optionExplanations: 面试官要跟着你的推理走，才能在中途提问和调整设计，这就是为什么沟通本身要打分。
沟通说得再好也替代不了设计本身，面试官最终还是要看结构和逻辑站不站得住。
说得多不代表可以少写代码，LLD 仍然需要具体的类、方法和状态转换。
这不是销售话术面试，清楚的推理是为了让面试官能跟上并一起调整设计，不是为了说服。
optionExplanations_en: The interviewer needs to follow your reasoning to probe and adjust the design together—that's why communication itself is scored.
No amount of talking substitutes for the design itself; the interviewer still has to see structure and logic that hold up.
Talking more doesn't mean writing less code—LLD still needs concrete classes, methods, and state transitions.
This isn't a sales pitch; clear reasoning exists so the interviewer can follow and adjust the design with you, not to persuade.

q: 把一场 LLD 面试从题目到实现的自然顺序排好：
q_en: Put an LLD interview flow in the natural order from prompt to implementation:
steps: 定义核心类、状态和方法
澄清需求并确认范围
提取实体和关系
实现关键方法并走查场景
why: 先把问题框清楚，再建模对象，最后写关键逻辑。跳过前两步直接写代码通常会丢分。
why_en: A good LLD flow clarifies scope, extracts entities, defines classes, and then implements and verifies core methods.
diagram:
flowchart TD
A["clarify scope"] --> B["extract entities"]
B --> C["define classes, state, APIs"]
C --> D["implement key method"]
D --> E["walk through scenario"]

q: 补全文章里的类比：
q_en: Complete the analogy for system design versus low-level design:
text: 系统设计像{{地图}}，低层设计像地图上一栋建筑的{{蓝图}}。
text_en: System design is like a {{map}}, while low-level design is like the {{blueprint}} for one building on that map.
why: 类比强调两者尺度不同：系统设计关注宏观组件，LLD 关注具体代码结构和对象协作。
why_en: The analogy is that system design is the map and low-level design is the blueprint for one building on that map.

scenario: 你不确定目标公司要求伪代码、真实语言、UML 还是模式名称。
scenario_en: You are not sure whether the target company expects pseudocode, real-language code, UML, or pattern names.
q: 最务实的做法是什么？
q_en: What is the most practical move?
options: 等面试结束后再去问清楚
默认所有公司要求完全相同
只准备一种固定表达方式
面试前先问清期望格式
options_en: Wait until after the interview to ask.
Assume every company expects exactly the same format.
Prepare only a single fixed way of presenting.
Ask the recruiter ahead of time what format is expected.
why: 文章明确说差异存在但不应主导准备。提前问清格式能减少不必要的不确定性。
why_en: Ask the recruiter or interviewer what format they expect so you can adapt without changing the core preparation.
whenOtherWins: 如果无法提前问到，就准备能在伪代码和常用语言之间切换的表达方式。
tradeoff: 面试前主动确认格式 vs 面试中默认单一固定表达

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调面试流程、可以提前说明面试期望格式的人。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A recruiter coordinates the interview process and can tell you the expected format ahead of time.

optionExplanations: 等面试结束再问已经来不及调整表达方式，提前问才能在准备阶段就校准。
默认所有公司要求一样会让你在遇到不同格式时措手不及，实际差异确实存在。
只准备一种固定表达方式碰到要求不同的公司会显得生硬，灵活切换更保险。
面试前主动问清楚是否要伪代码、真实语言、UML 或模式名，能减少不必要的不确定性。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting until after the interview to ask is too late to adjust how you present—asking ahead lets you calibrate during prep.
Assuming every company expects the same format leaves you unprepared when the actual format differs, and differences do exist.
Preparing only one fixed presentation style feels rigid when a company expects something different—flexibility is safer.
Asking ahead whether they want pseudocode, real-language code, UML, or pattern names removes unnecessary uncertainty.

q: 文章对现代 LLD 取向的描述包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which statements match the guide's modern LLD approach? (Select all that apply.)
options: 组合通常比深继承更实用
简单状态优先于过度层级
务实取舍优先于模式崇拜
所有问题都必须先设计抽象工厂
options_en: Composition is usually more practical than deep inheritance.
Simple state is preferred over excessive hierarchy.
Pragmatic tradeoffs come before pattern worship.
Every problem must start with an Abstract Factory design.
why: 现代生产代码更看重可读、可维护和适度抽象。强行套模式通常是负信号。
why_en: The guide favors composition, simple state, and pragmatic tradeoffs over deep inheritance and pattern worship.

termDefinitions.meaning: 抽象工厂模式：提供一族相关对象的创建接口，不暴露具体实现类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Abstract Factory pattern provides an interface for creating families of related objects without exposing concrete classes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 子类自动获得父类的属性和方法的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Inheritance is the mechanism where a subclass automatically gets the properties and methods of a parent class.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通过持有其他对象的引用来复用行为，而不是继承它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition reuses behavior by holding a reference to another object instead of inheriting from it.

optionExplanations: 组合让对象在运行时灵活拼装行为，不用像继承那样在编译期锁死层级关系。
简单状态优先意味着能用一个枚举或几个字段说清楚的状态，就不要提前搭复杂的状态机框架。
务实取舍优先于模式崇拜，指的是先看这道题真正的变化点，再决定要不要上某个模式。
这是个误解——不是所有问题都要先设计抽象工厂，绝大多数 LLD 题根本用不上它。
optionExplanations_en: Composition lets you assemble behavior flexibly at runtime, instead of locking a hierarchy in at compile time like inheritance does.
Preferring simple state means if an enum or a few fields describe it fine, don't pre-build an elaborate state-machine framework.
Pragmatic tradeoffs before pattern worship means look at this problem's real variation points first, then decide if a pattern helps.
This is a misconception—not every problem needs an Abstract Factory upfront; most LLD prompts never need it at all.

q: 只看材料但不练习，文章认为最大的风险是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest risk of reading the material without practicing?
options: 真正面试时无法把概念应用到具体题目
会忘记所有网络协议
一定无法写任何语法
会把 LLD 变成系统设计
options_en: You won't be able to apply the concepts to an actual problem under real interview conditions.
You will forget every network protocol.
You definitely won't be able to write any syntax at all.
LLD will turn into system design.
why: LLD 是应用型面试。知道原则不等于能在 35 分钟内澄清需求、拆类、写方法和应对追问。
why_en: The main risk of only reading is failing to apply the ideas under interview time pressure.
optionExplanations: 只读材料不练习，最大的风险是真到面试现场时无法在 35 分钟内把原则用到具体题目上。
网络协议跟这门课几乎没关系，忘不忘协议不是只看材料不练习的风险点。
说完全写不出语法太绝对，多数人能写点代码，问题在于结构和应用能力不熟练。
只是不练习不会让 LLD 自动变成系统设计，这两者的边界不会因为准备方式而改变。
optionExplanations_en: The biggest risk of only reading without practicing is being unable to apply the ideas to an actual problem under real time pressure.
Networking protocols have almost nothing to do with this material—forgetting them isn't the risk of skipping practice here.
Claiming you definitely can't write any syntax is too absolute; most people can write something—the gap is structure and application.
Skipping practice doesn't turn LLD into system design—the boundary between the two doesn't shift based on how you prepared.

scenario: 题目是“设计 Tic Tac Toe”，你开始讨论全球多人在线同步和匹配服务。
scenario_en: The prompt is "design Tic Tac Toe," but you start discussing global multiplayer synchronization and matchmaking services.
q: 这暴露了什么问题？
q_en: What problem does this reveal?
options: 棋盘逻辑缺少数据库索引优化
类的职责设计得过于简单
范围失控，把本地题扩成系统设计
这道题里状态机一定不能用
options_en: The board logic is missing a database index optimization.
The class responsibilities are designed too simplistically.
Scope has run away, turning a local prompt into system design.
A state machine absolutely cannot be used in this problem.
why: LLD prompt 常常只要求本地核心逻辑。把 UI、网络、AI 对手等都拉进来会浪费时间并模糊主线。
why_en: Expanding a local game prompt into global online infrastructure is scope creep from LLD into system design.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求网络多人游戏后端，那才讨论服务和同步架构。
tradeoff: 本地核心逻辑 vs 全球多人同步基础设施

termDefinitions.meaning: 一种用有限状态和转换规则描述对象行为的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A state machine models an object's behavior using a finite set of states and transition rules.

optionExplanations: 缺数据库索引跟这个场景完全无关，Tic Tac Toe 是本地逻辑题，不涉及数据库查询。
问题不是类设计太简单，而是你压根没有在做类设计，而是在讨论基础设施。
这暴露的正是范围失控：把一个本地棋盘逻辑题硬生生扩成了多人同步和匹配服务的系统设计。
状态机完全可以用来管理棋盘和回合状态，这个说法本身就是错的，跟场景无关。
optionExplanations_en: A missing database index is unrelated here—Tic Tac Toe is a local-logic problem with no database queries involved.
The issue isn't that the class design is too simple—you haven't even gotten to class design, you're discussing infrastructure instead.
This exposes scope creep: a local board-logic prompt has been stretched into a multiplayer sync and matchmaking system-design problem.
A state machine is perfectly usable for managing the board and turn state—this claim is just wrong regardless of the scenario.

scenario: 面试官希望看到你如何让一个小系统工作并能扩展。
scenario_en: The interviewer wants to see how you make a small system work and leave it extensible.
q: 最能打动面试官的产出通常是什么？
q_en: What output usually impresses the interviewer most?
options: 少量清楚的类加方法伪代码和场景走查
大量空接口和从没用上的设计模式
只画一张服务拓扑图却完全不落地
只罗列实体名词却不写具体行为
options_en: A small set of clear classes, method pseudocode, and a walkthrough.
A pile of empty interfaces and design patterns that never got used.
Just one service-topology diagram that never gets implemented.
Just a list of entity nouns with no actual behavior written.
why: LLD 不是名词收集。你要展示状态放在哪里、方法如何改变状态、边界如何保持清楚。
why_en: A strong LLD output is a small set of clear classes, core method pseudocode, and a walkthrough that proves the behavior.
whenOtherWins: 如果是非常早期需求澄清阶段，先列实体和范围再进入代码。
tradeoff: 少量类+方法走查证明行为 vs 只堆名词或服务拓扑图
diagram:
flowchart LR
A["clear classes"] --> B["core method pseudocode"]
B --> C["scenario walkthrough"]
C --> D["confident follow-up discussion"]
A --> D
optionExplanations: 少量清楚的类、关键方法的伪代码，再走查一遍场景，能直接证明状态和行为都站得住。
堆一堆没用上的空接口和模式只会让代码显得复杂，却证明不了任何实际行为。
只画服务拓扑图完全没有落地到代码层面，跟这个小系统该展示的东西不是一回事。
只列名词不写行为，面试官看不出状态怎么变、方法之间怎么协作，等于没有设计。
optionExplanations_en: A small set of clear classes, pseudocode for the key methods, and a walkthrough proves the state and behavior actually hold up.
Piling on empty interfaces and unused patterns just adds noise without proving any actual behavior.
Just a service-topology diagram never gets down to code, which isn't what this small system is supposed to demonstrate.
Listing nouns without behavior leaves the interviewer unable to see how state changes or methods interact—that's not a design.

q: 补全 LLD 评分主线：
q_en: Complete the main scoring thread for LLD interviews:
text: 面试官想看你能否把小而明确的问题拆成{{可维护的代码结构}}，并通过清晰沟通解释{{职责、状态和扩展点}}。
text_en: The interviewer wants to see whether you can turn a small, clear problem into a {{maintainable code structure}} and explain {{responsibilities, state, and extension points}} clearly.
why: 这比背出术语更重要。术语只是帮助表达，最终评分落在设计质量和推理过程。
why_en: The core evaluation is whether you can create maintainable code structure and explain responsibilities, state, and extension points.

q: 系统设计白板和 LLD 白板内容通常有什么不同？
q_en: How do system design and LLD whiteboards usually differ?
options: 系统设计画服务和数据流；LLD 画类和状态转换
系统设计只写代码，LLD 只写容量公式
系统设计和 LLD 都禁止画任何图
LLD 白板必须画完整 UML 图
options_en: System design draws services and data flow; LLD draws classes and state transitions.
System design only writes code, and LLD only writes capacity formulas.
Both system design and LLD forbid drawing any diagram.
An LLD whiteboard must contain a complete UML diagram.
why: LLD 可以画简单关系，但主要是为了支持代码结构讨论。系统设计图则表达分布式组件和数据流。
why_en: System design whiteboards show services and data flow, while LLD whiteboards show classes, methods, relationships, and state transitions.
tradeoff: 服务与数据流示意图 vs 类/方法/状态转换示意图

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一建模语言，用图表表示类、关系和继承结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UML, or Unified Modeling Language, is a diagram notation for classes, relationships, and inheritance.

optionExplanations: 这正是分界线：系统设计白板画服务和数据怎么流动，LLD 白板画类、方法和状态怎么转换。
说反了——容量公式才是系统设计常出现的东西，LLD 白板更少写纯数学公式。
两边都会画图，只是画的内容不同，说完全禁止画图跟实际面试情况不符。
LLD 白板不需要完整 UML，简单的关系示意图足够支撑代码结构讨论。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the dividing line: system-design whiteboards show services and data flow, LLD whiteboards show classes and state transitions.
That's backwards—capacity formulas show up more in system design; LLD whiteboards rarely involve pure math formulas.
Both rounds involve diagrams, just different content—claiming diagrams are forbidden entirely doesn't match real interviews.
An LLD whiteboard doesn't need a complete UML diagram; a simple relationship sketch is enough to support the code discussion.

scenario: 面试官在你设计后提出一个小扩展，例如添加新支付方式或撤销操作。
scenario_en: After your design, the interviewer adds a small extension, such as a new payment method or undo operation.
q: 回答时最好强调什么？
q_en: What should you emphasize in your answer?
options: 直接拒绝这个追问的新需求
马上把所有代码全部推倒重写
指出现有边界如何吸收变化需要改哪些类
只回一句用设计模式带过去
options_en: Flatly refuse this follow-up's new requirement outright.
Immediately tear down and rewrite all of the code.
Point out which boundary absorbs the change and which classes shift.
Just wave it off with "use a design pattern" and move on.
why: 扩展追问是在看初始设计是否有干净边界。具体说改哪里、为什么不会波及全局，比喊模式名更有说服力。
why_en: For follow-ups, explain which existing boundary absorbs the change and what minimal classes or methods need to change.
whenOtherWins: 如果扩展彻底改变需求，先承认原设计假设变化，再提出新的结构。
tradeoff: 指出边界吸收变化 vs 推倒重写或拒绝需求
optionExplanations: 直接拒绝新需求不会给面试官留下好印象，追问本来就是设计的一部分。
马上推倒重写说明原设计边界不干净，强候选人应该先看能不能局部吸收变化。
指出现有边界怎么吸收新支付方式或撤销操作、具体要改哪些类，最能体现设计的干净程度。
只回一句用设计模式没有说清具体改哪里、为什么，等于没有真正回答追问。
optionExplanations_en: Flatly refusing the new requirement doesn't reflect well—follow-up extensions are part of the design conversation.
Immediately rewriting everything suggests the original boundaries weren't clean; a strong candidate checks for a local fix first.
Pointing out which existing boundary absorbs the new payment method or undo, and which specific classes change, shows the design is clean.
Just saying "use a design pattern" doesn't explain what actually changes or why—that's not really answering the follow-up.

q: 哪些是 LLD 面试中的常见负信号？（多选）
q_en: Which are common negative signals in an LLD interview? (Select all that apply.)
options: 没澄清需求就直接写代码
为了炫技强行加很多模式
把问题范围扩到不相关系统设计
用简洁类和方法解释状态变化
options_en: Writing code immediately without clarifying requirements.
Forcing in lots of patterns just to show off.
Expanding the scope into unrelated system design.
Explaining state changes with clean classes and methods.
why: 负信号都指向同一个问题：没有按题目需要做取舍。简洁清楚的类和方法反而是正信号。
why_en: Common negative signals are skipping requirements, forcing patterns, and expanding beyond the requested LLD scope.
optionExplanations: 没澄清需求直接写代码是常见负信号，说明候选人跳过了理解问题这一步。
为了炫技硬塞很多模式也是负信号，暴露出候选人在意展示词汇而不是解决变化点。
把范围扩到不相关的系统设计同样是负信号，说明候选人没能控制住这道题该有的边界。
这其实是正信号而不是负信号——用简洁类和方法解释状态变化正是强候选人的表现。
optionExplanations_en: Writing code without clarifying requirements is a common negative signal—it means the candidate skipped understanding the problem.
Forcing in lots of patterns to show off is also a negative signal, revealing a focus on vocabulary instead of real variation points.
Expanding into unrelated system design is likewise a negative signal—it shows the candidate couldn't hold the intended scope.
This is actually a positive signal, not negative—explaining state changes with clean classes and methods is what strong candidates do.

q: 把这份指南建议的学习路径排好：
q_en: Put the guide's suggested study path in order:
steps: 用常见题目拆解和练习把方法应用出来
先学习交付框架管理面试时间
复习设计原则、OOP 概念和常见模式
根据目标公司确认格式差异
why: 先掌握流程，再补充工具箱，最后通过题目练习形成肌肉记忆。公司差异是准备中的校准项。
why_en: The preparation path is delivery framework, design fundamentals, practiced problem breakdowns, and then company-specific format calibration.

q: LLD 面试和纯算法面试的关注点有什么不同？
q_en: How does an LLD interview differ from a pure algorithm interview?
options: LLD 看对象结构和状态；算法看计算步骤和复杂度
LLD 面试只看 Big-O 一个指标
算法面试只看你画没画类图
两者面试都不需要解释思路
options_en: LLD looks at object structure and state; algorithm interviews look at computational steps and complexity.
An LLD interview only looks at Big-O.
An algorithm interview only checks whether you drew a class diagram.
Neither interview requires explaining your reasoning.
why: LLD 当然也要写正确逻辑，但评分重点是代码组织和变化承受能力。算法题则主要围绕数据结构、复杂度和正确性证明。
why_en: LLD emphasizes object structure, state, and maintainable interactions, while algorithm interviews emphasize computational steps and complexity.
tradeoff: 对象结构与可维护交互 vs 计算步骤与复杂度证明

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来描述算法运行时间或空间随输入规模增长趋势的记号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Big-O notation describes how an algorithm's runtime or space grows as the input size increases.

optionExplanations: 这正是两者的分界：LLD 评的是对象结构和状态管理，算法题评的是计算步骤和复杂度证明。
说反了——Big-O 是算法题的核心指标，LLD 几乎不会只靠时间复杂度打分。
算法面试不会去看你画没画类图，它关心的是数据结构选择和解法正确性。
两种面试都需要你讲清楚思路，只是解释的对象不同：一个讲设计取舍，一个讲复杂度分析。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the dividing line: LLD grades object structure and state management, algorithm rounds grade computational steps and complexity.
That's backwards—Big-O is the core metric for algorithm rounds; LLD is almost never scored on time complexity alone.
An algorithm interview doesn't check whether you drew a class diagram; it cares about data-structure choice and solution correctness.
Both rounds require explaining your reasoning, just about different things: design tradeoffs versus complexity analysis.

scenario: 面试白板/共享编辑器上写 OOD 的类和 API。
scenario_en: Writing OOD classes and APIs on the whiteboard / shared editor in an interview.
q: 为什么要在意命名和大小写的约定？
q_en: Why care about naming and casing conventions?
options: 一致、地道的命名一眼传达工程成熟度，也降低阅读认知负担
约定纯属个人审美，选哪种、混着用都完全没有影响，面试官根本不看这些细节
只有编译器强制的规则才重要，其余风格随意
命名越花哨越显得有创意
options_en: Consistent, idiomatic naming signals maturity at a glance and lowers reading load
Conventions are pure personal taste; mixing them has zero impact and interviewers never look at such details
Only compiler-enforced rules matter; everything else is free-form
The fancier the names, the more creative you look
optionExplanations: 对：地道命名是低成本的高信号——第一眼就传达「这人写过生产代码」，还让读者省力。
错：面试官恰恰会从命名一致性判断工程成熟度。
错：可读性约定虽不被编译器强制，却直接影响评价。
错：花哨≠专业，清晰表意才是。
optionExplanations_en: Right: idiomatic naming is a low-cost, high-signal cue — it says "this person has shipped code" and eases reading.
Wrong: interviewers do judge engineering maturity from naming consistency.
Wrong: readability conventions are not compiler-enforced but directly shape evaluation.
Wrong: fancy is not professional; clear intent is.
why: 命名约定低成本高信号:一致、地道的命名让面试官一眼觉得你写过生产代码,也降低阅读负担。它不被编译器强制,却实打实影响「工程成熟度」评价——别混用,跟语言惯例走。
why_en: Naming conventions are low-cost, high-signal: consistent, idiomatic names make an interviewer feel you have shipped real code and lower reading load. They are not compiler-enforced yet materially shape the "engineering maturity" impression — so do not mix styles; follow the language's idiom.

scenario: 先认全常见的几种大小写风格。
scenario_en: First, recognize the common casing styles.
q: `getUserProfile` 属于哪种大小写风格？
q_en: Which casing style is `getUserProfile`?
options: camelCase(小驼峰)
PascalCase(大驼峰)
snake_case(下划线)
kebab-case(连字符)
options_en: camelCase (lower camel)
PascalCase (upper camel)
snake_case
kebab-case
optionExplanations: 对：首字母小写、后续单词首字母大写 = camelCase。
错：PascalCase 是首字母也大写(GetUserProfile)。
错：snake_case 是全小写加下划线(get_user_profile)。
错：kebab-case 是全小写加连字符(get-user-profile)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: first letter lower, subsequent words capitalized = camelCase.
Wrong: PascalCase also capitalizes the first letter (GetUserProfile).
Wrong: snake_case is all-lower with underscores (get_user_profile).
Wrong: kebab-case is all-lower with hyphens (get-user-profile).
why: 五种大小写:camelCase、PascalCase、snake_case、SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE、kebab-case,分别用于 方法/类/Python方法/常量/URL。认清它们是后面所有约定的基础。
why_en: Five styles: camelCase (getUser), PascalCase (GetUser/ClassName), snake_case (get_user), SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (MAX_SIZE), kebab-case (get-user). Recognizing them underpins every convention that follows.

rows: 几乎所有语言的类/类型名

scenario: 给停车场 OOD 里的类命名。
scenario_en: Naming classes in a parking-lot OOD.
q: 类 / 类型名该用哪种大小写？
q_en: What casing do class/type names use?
options: PascalCase：ParkingLot、PaymentMethod
camelCase：parkingLot、paymentMethod
snake_case：parking_lot、payment_method
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE：PARKING_LOT
options_en: PascalCase: ParkingLot, PaymentMethod
camelCase: parkingLot, paymentMethod
snake_case: parking_lot, payment_method
SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: PARKING_LOT
optionExplanations: 对：类/类型名用 PascalCase 是 Java/JS/TS/Python/C#/C++/Go/Swift 的共同约定,几乎无例外。
错：camelCase 是给方法/变量的,不是类。
错：snake_case 类名在主流语言里都不地道。
错：全大写是常量,不是类。
optionExplanations_en: Right: PascalCase for class/type names is shared by Java/JS/TS/Python/C#/C++/Go/Swift with almost no exceptions.
Wrong: camelCase is for methods/variables, not classes.
Wrong: a snake_case class name is non-idiomatic in every mainstream language.
Wrong: all-caps is for constants, not classes.
why: 类/类型/枚举类型名用 PascalCase(首字母大写驼峰):ParkingLot、PaymentMethod、VehicleType。几乎跨所有主流语言通用,是最不会错的一条,先刻进肌肉。
why_en: Class/type/enum-type names use PascalCase (upper camel): ParkingLot, PaymentMethod, VehicleType. This is near-universal across mainstream languages and the safest rule — make it muscle memory.

scenario: 给方法和变量命名——这一步最容易露怯。
scenario_en: Naming methods and variables — where amateurism shows most.
q: 方法 / 变量该用 camelCase 还是 snake_case？
q_en: camelCase or snake_case for methods/variables?
options: 看语言：Java/JS 用 camelCase，Python 用 snake_case
不分语言，所有语言的方法和变量都统一用 camelCase，这样最省事、跨语言也最一致
所有语言都统一用 snake_case
方法用 PascalCase 才显得正式
options_en: Depends on language: camelCase in Java/JS, snake_case in Python
Ignore the language; uniformly use camelCase for methods and variables everywhere — simplest and most consistent across languages
All languages uniformly use snake_case
Methods should be PascalCase to look formal
optionExplanations: 对：方法/变量大小写是语言相关的——用错(如 Java 里写 snake_case)一眼就露外行。
错：Python/Ruby/Rust 的方法是 snake_case,不是 camelCase。
错：Java/JS/C# 的方法是 camelCase,不是 snake_case。
错：PascalCase 是类名;方法用它在多数语言里都不对(Go 的导出规则例外)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: method/variable casing is language-dependent — using the wrong one (e.g. snake_case in Java) instantly reads as amateur.
Wrong: Python/Ruby/Rust methods are snake_case, not camelCase.
Wrong: Java/JS/C# methods are camelCase, not snake_case.
Wrong: PascalCase is for classes; using it for methods is wrong in most languages (Go's export rule aside).
why: 方法/变量大小写跟语言走:camelCase 阵营(Java/JS/C#…)vs snake_case 阵营(Python/Ruby/Rust)。类名恒 PascalCase;方法搞混(Java 写 get_user)一眼外行。
why_en: This is the biggest professionalism tell: method/variable casing follows the language — the camelCase camp (Java/JS/TS/C#/Kotlin/Swift) vs the snake_case camp (Python/Ruby/Rust). Class names are PascalCase everywhere, but do not mix methods: get_user in Java or getUser in Python instantly looks amateur.
tradeoff: camelCase 阵营(Java/JS/C#/Kotlin/Swift) vs snake_case 阵营(Python/Ruby/Rust)——方法/变量随语言,类名恒 PascalCase

scenario: 定义一个「最大重试次数」的常量。
scenario_en: Defining a "max retries" constant.
q: 常量通常怎么命名？
q_en: How are constants typically named?
options: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE：MAX_RETRIES
camelCase：maxRetries
PascalCase：MaxRetries（在多数语言里看起来像个类名）
随便，常量命名没约定
options_en: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE: MAX_RETRIES
camelCase: maxRetries
PascalCase: MaxRetries (looks like a class name in most languages)
Anything; constants have no convention
optionExplanations: 对：Java/JS/Python/C++ 里常量惯用全大写下划线,一眼可辨「这是不可变的配置值」。
错：camelCase 是普通变量,读者分不出它是常量。
错：PascalCase 在多数语言里像类名(C# 是例外)。
错：常量有明确约定,不能随便。
optionExplanations_en: Right: Java/JS/Python/C++ conventionally use all-caps-underscore for constants, instantly signaling "immutable config value".
Wrong: camelCase reads as an ordinary variable; readers cannot tell it is constant.
Wrong: PascalCase looks like a class name in most languages (C# is the exception).
Wrong: constants do have a clear convention.
why: 常量用 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE(全大写+下划线):MAX_RETRIES。通行于 Java/JS/Python/C++,一眼传达「不可变配置值」。(Go/C# 例外,用 PascalCase。)
why_en: Constants use SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (all-caps + underscores): MAX_RETRIES, DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS. Common in Java/JS/Python/C++; it signals "immutable config value" at a glance. (Go/C# are exceptions, using PascalCase.)

scenario: 给类和方法起名时的语义规则。
scenario_en: The semantic rule when naming classes and methods.
q: 类名和方法名在词性上应该是？
q_en: What part of speech should class vs method names be?
options: 类=名词，方法=动词短语
类名用动词、方法名用名词
类名和方法名都统一用名词就行，不用区分词性
词性无所谓，能跑就行
options_en: class = noun, method = verb phrase
Class names are verbs; method names are nouns
Both class and method names can just be nouns, no need to distinguish
Part of speech does not matter as long as it runs
optionExplanations: 对：类=事物(名词)、方法=动作(动词),读代码像读句子,意图自明。
错：反过来会让 API 读起来别扭(order.paymentProcessor() ？)。
错：方法用名词(order.payment())读者不知道它「做」什么。
错：词性直接决定可读性,不是能跑就行。
optionExplanations_en: Right: class = thing (noun), method = action (verb); code reads like sentences and intent is self-evident.
Wrong: reversing makes APIs awkward (order.paymentProcessor()?).
Wrong: a noun method (order.payment()) hides what it does.
Wrong: part of speech drives readability; "it runs" is not enough.
why: 类名用名词(是什么:Order、PaymentProcessor),方法名用动词短语(做什么:createOrder、chargeCard、isExpired)。这样 order.charge(card) 读起来就是一句话,意图自明。
why_en: Class names are nouns (what it is: Order, PaymentProcessor); method names are verb phrases (what it does: createOrder, chargeCard, isExpired). Then `order.charge(card)` reads like a sentence with self-evident intent. Query methods often start with get/is/has.

scenario: 给一个表示「账号是否激活」的布尔字段/方法命名。
scenario_en: Naming a boolean field/method for "is the account active".
q: 布尔值怎么命名最专业？
q_en: How to name a boolean most professionally?
options: 用 is/has/can 前缀：isActive、hasPermission
用名词：active、permission、dispense，读到时再自己判断
用 flag1、flag2 这类通用名
用动词命令式：activate、dispense
options_en: is/has/can prefix: isActive, hasPermission
Nouns: active, permission, dispense — judge for yourself when reading
Use generic names like flag1, flag2
Use imperative verbs: activate, dispense
optionExplanations: 对：is/has/can 前缀让 `if (user.isActive)` 读起来就是个真假判断,一眼知道是布尔。
错：裸名词读者分不清是布尔还是对象。
错：flag1/flag2 毫无表意。
错：activate 像个会改状态的动作方法,不是布尔查询。
optionExplanations_en: Right: an is/has/can prefix makes `if (user.isActive)` read as a truth test — obviously boolean.
Wrong: a bare noun leaves readers unsure if it is a boolean or an object.
Wrong: flag1/flag2 conveys nothing.
Wrong: activate looks like a state-changing action, not a boolean query.
why: 布尔用 is/has/can 前缀,让它读起来像个是非判断:isActive、canDispense。if(order.isPaid) 一眼可读;裸名词 if(order.paid) 就含糊,分不清布尔还是对象。
why_en: Booleans take an is/has/can/should prefix so they read as a yes/no test: isActive, hasPermission, canDispense, isExpired. `if (order.isPaid)` reads clearly; a bare noun `if (order.paid)` is ambiguous about whether it is a boolean or an object.

scenario: 给「校验规则」的接口/抽象基类命名。
scenario_en: Naming the interface/abstract base for a "validation rule".
q: 接口该怎么命名？
q_en: How should you name an interface?
options: PascalCase 名词或 -able：ValidationRule、Comparable
统一加匈牙利前缀 I：IValidationRule、IPaymentMethod（多数语言不推荐）
用小写 snake_case：validation_rule
在名字里带上具体实现：CreditCardValidationRuleImpl
options_en: PascalCase noun or -able: ValidationRule, Comparable
Prefix everything with Hungarian I: IValidationRule, IPaymentMethod (discouraged in most languages)
Lowercase snake_case: validation_rule
Bake the concrete impl into the name: CreditCardValidationRuleImpl
optionExplanations: 对：接口是 PascalCase 名词或能力形容词(-able);它描述「能力/角色」,不该暴露实现。
错：I 前缀是 C#/旧 COM 习惯,Java/Python/Go/Swift 里不地道。
错：接口不用 snake_case,类型名恒 PascalCase。
错：接口名不该带 Impl/具体实现,那是给实现类留的。
optionExplanations_en: Right: an interface is a PascalCase noun or capability adjective (-able); it names a capability/role and should not leak the implementation.
Wrong: the I prefix is a C#/legacy-COM habit, non-idiomatic in Java/Python/Go/Swift.
Wrong: interfaces are not snake_case; type names are always PascalCase.
Wrong: an interface name should not contain Impl/a concrete implementation — that is for the impl class.
why: 接口/抽象类用 PascalCase,取名反映能力或角色:名词(ValidationRule)或 -able(Comparable)。别用匈牙利 IFoo(除 C#),也别把具体实现塞进接口名。
why_en: Interfaces/abstract classes are PascalCase, named for a capability or role: a noun (ValidationRule, PaymentMethod) or an -able adjective (Comparable, Iterable). Avoid Hungarian IFoo (outside the C# ecosystem) and do not bake a concrete implementation into the interface name. The impl class carries specificity: CreditCardPayment implements PaymentMethod.
tradeoff: 名词/-able 接口名(表能力·跨语言地道) vs I 前缀(C# 习惯·他处不地道)

termDefinitions.meaning: 在标识符前加类型/用途前缀的老习惯(如接口 IFoo、成员 m_x、字符串 strName)。现代多数语言(Java/Python/Go/Swift)不推荐,认为它冗余且易过时;C# 生态仍保留接口 I 前缀。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hungarian notation prefixes identifiers with their type/role (e.g. interface IFoo, member m_x, string strName). Most modern languages (Java/Python/Go/Swift) discourage it as redundant and stale-prone; the C# ecosystem still keeps the interface I prefix.

scenario: 给变量和方法起名时要不要缩写。
scenario_en: Whether to abbreviate when naming variables and methods.
q: 关于缩写和表意，哪种做法更专业？
q_en: On abbreviations and intent, which is more professional?
options: 名字表意、不含糊缩写：elapsedMs、userCount
尽量缩短，能省字母就省：usr、cnt、calc
用 data、info、manager、handler 这类万能空词就够
变量都叫 a、b、c，反正自己看得懂
options_en: Intent-revealing, no cryptic abbreviations: elapsedMs, userCount
Shorten aggressively, drop letters where you can: usr, cnt, calc
Generic empty words like data, info, manager, handler are enough
Name variables a, b, c — you understand them yourself
optionExplanations: 对：表意命名让读者无需猜;循环里的 i 等公认短名可以,但业务变量要说人话。
错：省字母省不了多少,却大幅增加理解成本。
错：data/info/manager 太泛,等于没说。
错：a/b/c 只有你当下懂,面试官和未来的你都要重新猜。
optionExplanations_en: Right: intent-revealing names spare the reader guessing; well-known short names like loop i are fine, but business variables should read plainly.
Wrong: dropping letters saves little but greatly raises comprehension cost.
Wrong: data/info/manager are too vague — they say nothing.
Wrong: a/b/c only you understand right now; the interviewer and future-you must re-guess.
why: 名字要表达意图,别含糊缩写:elapsedMs 胜过 e、userCount 胜过 cnt。例外是公认惯例(循环 i/j、坐标 x/y)。也避开 data/info/manager 这类万能空词。清晰 > 简短。
why_en: Names should reveal intent, not use cryptic abbreviations: elapsedMs beats e, userCount beats cnt, retryAttempt beats r. Exceptions are well-known idioms (loop i/j, coordinates x/y). Also avoid catch-all empty words like data/info/manager. Clear > short — an interviewer understanding it at first glance is what reads as professional.

scenario: 设计取某个用户的 REST 端点。
scenario_en: Designing the REST endpoint to fetch a user.
q: 资源路径该怎么写？
q_en: How should you write the resource path?
options: 复数名词、无动词：GET /users/123、GET /users/123/orders
路径里带动词：GET /getUser?id=123
单数名词：GET /user/123、POST /user
每个操作一个独立路径：/createUser、/deleteUser、/updateUser
options_en: Plural nouns, no verbs: GET /users/123, GET /users/123/orders
Verbs in the path: GET /getUser?id=123
Singular nouns: GET /user/123, POST /user
One path per operation: /createUser, /deleteUser, /updateUser
optionExplanations: 对：资源用复数名词,同一 /users 既表集合也表其下的 /users/123,动作交给 HTTP 方法。
错：路径带动词是 RPC 风格,不是 REST;/getUser 里 GET 已表意。
错：单复数混用不一致;主流约定是集合用复数。
错：为每个动作建路径正是 REST 要避免的,动作应由方法承载。
optionExplanations_en: Right: resources are plural nouns; the same /users covers the collection and /users/123 under it, with actions handled by HTTP methods.
Wrong: verbs in the path are RPC-style, not REST; GET already conveys the action in /getUser.
Wrong: mixing singular/plural is inconsistent; the mainstream convention is plural for collections.
Wrong: a path per action is exactly what REST avoids; actions belong to methods.
why: REST 资源路径用复数名词、不带动词:GET /users/123、POST /users、GET /users/123/orders。同一个 /users 既是集合又派生单个资源,一致可预测。动词交给 HTTP 方法,不写进 URL。
why_en: REST resource paths use plural nouns and no verbs: GET /users/123, POST /users, GET /users/123/orders. The same /users is both the collection and the base for a single resource — consistent and predictable. Verbs (create/delete) go to HTTP methods, not the URL.

scenario: 路径里出现多词资源，比如「用户档案」。
scenario_en: A multi-word resource in the path, e.g. "user profiles".
q: URL 路径段的大小写该怎么写？
q_en: What casing do URL path segments use?
options: 全小写 + kebab-case：/user-profiles
camelCase：/userProfiles
snake_case：/user_profiles（下划线，更像数据库风格）
PascalCase：/UserProfiles
options_en: All-lowercase + kebab-case: /user-profiles
camelCase: /userProfiles
snake_case: /user_profiles (underscores, more of a database style)
PascalCase: /UserProfiles
optionExplanations: 对：URL 惯例是全小写 + 连字符,清晰且避开大小写敏感带来的坑。
错：camelCase 在 URL 里别扭,还可能因大小写敏感出问题。
错：下划线更像数据库/JSON 约定,URL 里少见,还容易被下划线装饰遮住。
错：URL 里用 PascalCase 极不常见。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the URL convention is all-lowercase + hyphens — clear and avoids case-sensitivity pitfalls.
Wrong: camelCase looks awkward in URLs and can break on case sensitivity.
Wrong: underscores are more of a database/JSON convention, rare in URLs, and can hide under link underlines.
Wrong: PascalCase in URLs is highly unusual.
why: URL 路径段用全小写 + kebab-case(连字符):/user-profiles。web 标准约定,比 camelCase(大小写敏感)、snake_case(更像 DB/JSON)都清晰。注意跟 JSON 字段约定不同,别混。
why_en: URL path segments use all-lowercase + kebab-case (hyphens): /user-profiles, /shipping-addresses. This is the web-standard convention — clearer than camelCase (case-sensitivity risk) or snake_case (more DB/JSON). Note this differs from the JSON-field convention; do not mix them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 全小写、单词间用连字符 - 连接(user-profiles)。因为形似串在扦子上的烤串(kebab)得名。是 URL 路径段的通行约定:清晰、无大小写敏感问题;但不能用于多数编程语言的标识符(- 会被当成减号)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: kebab-case is all-lowercase with words joined by hyphens (user-profiles), named for looking like items on a skewer (kebab). It is the standard for URL path segments — clear and case-insensitive-safe — but cannot be used for identifiers in most languages (the hyphen parses as minus).

scenario: 要「创建一个订单」和「取消一个订单」。
scenario_en: You need to "create an order" and "cancel an order".
q: 「动作」应该体现在哪里？
q_en: Where should the "action" live?
options: 动作放 HTTP 方法：POST /orders、DELETE /orders/9
体现在 URL 上：POST /createOrder、POST /cancelOrder
全用 GET，动作放在查询参数里：GET /orders?action=create
每个动作用不同端口区分
options_en: Action in the HTTP method: POST /orders, DELETE /orders/9
In the URL: POST /createOrder, POST /cancelOrder
All GET, action in a query param: GET /orders?action=create
Distinguish each action by a different port
optionExplanations: 对：REST 用 HTTP 方法表达动作(POST 建、GET 读、PUT/PATCH 改、DELETE 删),URL 只指资源。
错：把动词塞进 URL 是 RPC 风格,丢掉了 HTTP 方法的语义。
错：全 GET 违反语义(GET 应无副作用),还会被缓存/预取误伤。
错：用端口区分动作是奇技淫巧,毫无必要。
optionExplanations_en: Right: REST expresses the action via the HTTP method (POST create, GET read, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE delete); the URL only points at the resource.
Wrong: putting verbs in the URL is RPC-style and discards HTTP-method semantics.
Wrong: all-GET violates semantics (GET must be side-effect-free) and gets hit by caching/prefetch.
Wrong: distinguishing actions by port is a hack with no benefit.
why: REST 里动作由 HTTP 方法承载,不写进 URL:POST 建、GET 读、PATCH 改、DELETE 删。URL 始终只描述资源。所以路径里几乎不该出现 create/get/update/delete 这类动词。
why_en: In REST the action is carried by the HTTP method, not the URL: POST /orders to create, GET /orders/9 to read, PATCH /orders/9 to update, DELETE /orders/9 to delete. The URL always names the resource only. So you should almost never see verbs like create/get/update/delete in a path.
tradeoff: 动作放 HTTP 方法(REST·URL 只指资源) vs 动词写进 URL(RPC 风格·丢方法语义)

scenario: 设计 API 返回的 JSON body 字段名。
scenario_en: Designing the field names in an API JSON body.
q: JSON 字段大小写怎么定最专业？
q_en: How to decide JSON field casing professionally?
options: camelCase 或 snake_case 选一种，全程一致
每个端点随手用不同风格，反正字段名能对上就行
JSON 字段必须和 URL 保持一样，统一都用 kebab-case
JSON 字段必须用 PascalCase
options_en: Pick camelCase or snake_case, stay consistent throughout
Use a different style per endpoint at will, as long as field names match up
JSON fields must match URLs and all use kebab-case
JSON fields must use PascalCase
optionExplanations: 对：camelCase(常见于 JS/Node 系)和 snake_case(Stripe/Twitter 等)都可,关键是全程一致。
错：风格不一致会让客户端解析混乱、显得业余。
错：kebab-case 的连字符在多数语言里不能直接做字段名(obj.user-name 报错)。
错：PascalCase 不是 JSON 字段的通行约定(.NET 老风格除外)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: both camelCase (common in JS/Node) and snake_case (Stripe/Twitter) are fine; what matters is consistency throughout.
Wrong: inconsistent styles confuse client parsing and read as amateur.
Wrong: kebab-case hyphens cannot be field names directly in most languages (obj.user-name errors).
Wrong: PascalCase is not the common JSON-field convention (legacy .NET aside).
why: JSON 字段 camelCase 或 snake_case 都行,关键是选一种、全 API 一致。别用 kebab-case(连字符不能当字段名)。注意 URL 用 kebab、JSON 用 camel/snake,两层不同别混。
why_en: JSON body fields can be camelCase or snake_case (camelCase is common in JS/Node; snake_case appears in Stripe, Twitter, etc.) — the key is picking one and staying consistent across the whole API. Do not use kebab-case (hyphens cannot be field names in most languages). Note: URLs use kebab-case while JSON fields use camel/snake — two different layers, do not mix.

scenario: 要「取第 2 页、状态为 active、按创建时间倒序」的用户。
scenario_en: Fetch users on page 2, status active, sorted by creation time descending.
q: 过滤 / 排序 / 分页这些参数放哪？
q_en: Where do filter/sort/pagination params go?
options: 查询参数：?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at
编进路径：GET /users/active/page/2/sort/created-desc
放进请求体，即使是 GET
放 HTTP 头里传
options_en: Query params: ?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at
Encoded into the path: GET /users/active/page/2/sort/created-desc
In the request body, even for GET
Passed in HTTP headers
optionExplanations: 对：过滤/排序/分页是对同一集合的「修饰」,用查询参数最贴切、可组合、可省略。
错：把这些编进路径会让路径爆炸,且语义上它们不是资源层级。
错：GET 一般不带 body,很多客户端/代理会忽略它。
错：这类业务参数放 header 不合常规,难发现难调试。
optionExplanations_en: Right: filter/sort/pagination modify the same collection, so query params fit best — composable and optional.
Wrong: encoding them into the path explodes the path and misrepresents them as resource hierarchy.
Wrong: GET usually carries no body; many clients/proxies ignore it.
Wrong: putting business params in headers is unconventional, hard to discover and debug.
why: 过滤、排序、分页用查询参数,不进路径:GET /users?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at。它们是对集合的「修饰」,可组合可省略。路径表达资源层级,query 表达对集合的筛选与视图。
why_en: Filtering, sorting, and pagination go in the query string, not the path: GET /users?status=active&page=2&sort=-created-at. They modify the same collection resource — composable and optional. The path expresses resource hierarchy (/users/123/orders); the query expresses filtering and views over a collection.

scenario: 复盘让 OOD/API 代码显得业余的命名失误。
scenario_en: Review naming mistakes that make OOD/API code look amateur.
q: 下面哪些会让你的代码一眼显得业余？（多选）
q_en: Which make your code look amateur at a glance? (multi-select)
options: 在 Java 里给方法用 snake_case、或在 Python 里给方法用 camelCase
REST 路径写成动词：POST /createUser、GET /getOrder
同一个 API 里 JSON 字段一会儿 camelCase 一会儿 snake_case
类名用 PascalCase、方法名跟随语言惯例、常量用 SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
options_en: snake_case methods in Java, or camelCase methods in Python
REST paths written as verbs: POST /createUser, GET /getOrder
JSON fields flip-flopping between camelCase and snake_case within one API
PascalCase classes, methods following the language idiom, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants
optionExplanations: 错误:方法大小写用错语言的惯例,是最刺眼的外行信号。
错误:动词进 URL 是 RPC 风格,丢掉 HTTP 方法语义。
错误:同一 API 内 JSON 风格不一致,客户端解析混乱、显得随意。
这是对的:类 PascalCase + 方法随语言 + 常量全大写,正是专业基线。
optionExplanations_en: Mistake: wrong-language method casing is the most glaring amateur signal.
Mistake: verbs in the URL are RPC-style and discard HTTP-method semantics.
Mistake: inconsistent JSON style within one API confuses clients and reads as careless.
This is correct: PascalCase classes + language-idiomatic methods + all-caps constants is the professional baseline.
why: 三个高频失分:①方法大小写用错语言惯例(Java 写 snake_case)②REST 路径带动词(/createUser)③同一 API 内 JSON 字段风格不一致。正解见前面各卡的组合。
why_en: Four common losses: (1) wrong-language method casing (snake_case in Java); (2) verbs in REST paths (/createUser); (3) inconsistent JSON field style within one API; (4) (the fix) PascalCase classes + language-idiomatic methods + SCREAMING_SNAKE constants + kebab-case URLs. Consistent + idiomatic = professional.

q: OOP 概念页与设计原则页的关系是什么？
q_en: How do the OOP concepts page and the design principles page relate to each other?
options: 两者是互不相关的两套独立知识
OOP 概念只在系统设计面试里出现，LLD 不会考
设计原则决定取舍方向，OOP 概念是实现这些取舍的语言机制
设计原则的内容只适用于前端框架代码
options_en: The two pages are unrelated, independent topics.
OOP concepts only appear in system-design interviews, not LLD.
Design principles decide the direction of a tradeoff, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that implement it.
Design principles only apply to frontend framework code.
why: 设计原则回答“该怎么取舍”，封装、抽象、多态、继承回答“怎么把取舍写进类和接口里”。两者是同一决策链的上下游。
why_en: Design principles decide what tradeoff to make, and OOP concepts are the language mechanisms that turn that tradeoff into classes and interfaces.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向对象编程（OOP）：用类和对象组织代码、通过封装/抽象/多态/继承表达设计决策的编程范式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OOP stands for Object-Oriented Programming, a paradigm that organizes code into classes and objects using encapsulation, abstraction, polymorphism, and inheritance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 低层次设计（LLD）：面试中要求把需求落到具体类、接口和方法的设计环节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLD stands for Low-Level Design, the interview stage that asks you to turn requirements into concrete classes, interfaces, and methods.

optionExplanations: 把两者当成孤立知识会让你在面试里各说各话；实际上原则给方向，OOP 概念给落地方式。
OOP 概念在 LLD 白板题里天天用到，把它当成系统设计专属考点是常见误解。
对：原则先定取舍方向，接口、封装、继承再把这个方向落成具体代码结构。
设计原则同样适用于后端类设计，把它限定在前端框架是范围搞错了。
optionExplanations_en: Treating them as unrelated leaves you unable to connect tradeoffs to code in an interview — principles set direction, OOP concepts implement it.
OOP concepts show up constantly in LLD whiteboard rounds too, not just system-design interviews.
Correct: principles set the tradeoff direction first, then encapsulation, interfaces, and inheritance turn that into class structure.
