optionExplanations: 前提就错了：Board 从不存玩家名字，它只知道格子里放的是什么颜色。
「玩家想撤销」是动机不是设计依据，Player 本身没有能力恢复 state/currentPlayer 这些字段。
DiscColor 只是一个颜色枚举，没有任何字段或方法能承载撤销逻辑。
撤销要把棋盘、轮次，连同 state、winner 一起复原，这些全归 Game 编排，只有它能把整条链路走一遍。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong premise — Board never stores player names, it only knows what color sits in each cell.
'The player wants to undo' is a motivation, not a design reason; Player itself has no ability to restore state or currentPlayer.
DiscColor is just a color enum with no fields or methods that could carry undo logic.
Undo has to roll back the board, the turn, plus state and winner all together — that's Game's orchestration job, and only it can walk the whole chain back.

q: 支持 undo 通常需要哪些变化？（多选）
q_en: What changes are usually needed to support undo? (Select all that apply.)
options: Game 增加 moveHistory 栈
每次成功移动记录 player、row、col
Board 增加 clearCell(row,col)
重置或重算 state/winner
options_en: Game gains a moveHistory stack.
Every successful move records the player, row, and column.
Board gains a clearCell(row, col) method.
Reset or recompute state and winner.
why: 撤销是对最后一次成功移动的逆操作。记录 row 和 col 可直接清除对应格子，不用重新推断落点。
why_en: Undo needs a move history, a board clear operation, and lifecycle state restoration.

termDefinitions.meaning: moveHistory 是 Game 里记录历史成功移动的栈，用于支持撤销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: moveHistory is a stack Game keeps of past successful moves, used to support undo.

termDefinitions.meaning: clearCell(row, col) 是 Board 提供给 undo 用的方法，把某个格子重新置空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: clearCell(row, col) is the method Board exposes for undo, resetting one cell back to empty.

termDefinitions.meaning: Board 是拥有 7x6 网格状态、负责落子和胜负几何检查的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the class that owns the 7x6 grid state and handles disc placement and win-geometry checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 是编排整局流程的类，管理轮次、生命周期状态和 winner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Game is the orchestrator class that manages turns, lifecycle state, and the winner.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

termDefinitions.meaning: Move 是 undo 用的值对象，记录一次成功移动的 player、row、col。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Move is the value object used for undo, recording the player, row, and column of one successful move.

optionExplanations: moveHistory 栈让 Game 知道「上一步到底是谁走的、走在哪」。
记录 player/row/col 三个字段，撤销时才能精确清空那一格而不用重新推断落点。
Board 得新增一个专门清空格子的方法，因为 placeDisc 只会往里放，不会往外拿。
撤销可能把已经 WON 或 DRAW 的对局拉回 IN_PROGRESS，所以 state 和 winner 必须一起复原。
optionExplanations_en: A moveHistory stack is what lets Game know exactly who moved last and where.
Recording player/row/col per move means undo can clear that exact cell instead of re-deriving where the disc landed.
Board needs a dedicated cell-clearing method, since placeDisc only ever writes, never removes.
Undo can pull an already-WON or DRAW match back to IN_PROGRESS, so state and winner both need to be restored together.

q: 撤销最后一步的正确高层顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct high-level order for undoing the last move?
steps: 从 moveHistory 弹出最后 Move。
如果历史为空，返回 false。
调用 board.clearCell(last.row,last.col)。
currentPlayer 恢复为 last.player。
将 state/winner 恢复到可继续状态或重算。
why: 撤销应先确认有可撤销动作，再回滚棋盘和轮次。获胜后的撤销尤其需要恢复生命周期状态。
tradeoff: 先弹出历史记录确认可撤销 vs 直接回滚棋盘（可能没有历史）
why_en: Undo pops the last recorded move, clears the board cell, restores turn, and fixes game state.

termDefinitions.meaning: moveHistory 是 Game 里记录历史成功移动的栈，用于支持撤销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: moveHistory is a stack Game keeps of past successful moves, used to support undo.

termDefinitions.meaning: clearCell(row, col) 是 Board 提供给 undo 用的方法，把某个格子重新置空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: clearCell(row, col) is the method Board exposes for undo, resetting one cell back to empty.

termDefinitions.meaning: currentPlayer 是 Game 保存的字段，标记当前该谁落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the field Game keeps to track whose turn it is.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

scenario: 后续要添加电脑对手，但游戏规则不变。
scenario_en: You need to add a computer opponent later, but the game rules stay the same.
q: 最干净的扩展方式是什么？
q_en: What is the cleanest extension approach?
options: 新增 BotEngine 选列，照常调用 makeMove
让 Board 自动替 AI 下子
把 Player 改成庞大继承层级作为默认方案
复制一份 Game 给 AI
options_en: Add a BotEngine that picks a column and still calls makeMove.
Let Board automatically move for the AI.
Turn Player into a large inheritance hierarchy by default.
Duplicate a whole separate Game just for the AI.
why: AI 只是选择列的决策层，规则仍由 Game 和 Board 执行。不要为了人类玩家也没有行为的场景强行接口化 Player。
tradeoff: 新增 BotEngine 决策层 vs 把 Player 做成继承层级
whenOtherWins: 如果系统要支持多种主动玩家实现并统一驱动，Player 接口或 Actor 抽象才可能有价值。
why_en: A bot can be a decision component that chooses a column while Game still enforces the rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: BotEngine 是扩展设计里新增的组件，负责替电脑玩家选一列，不改动 Game/Board 规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BotEngine is the extension component that picks a column for the computer player without changing Game or Board rules.

termDefinitions.meaning: makeMove(player, column) 是 Game 唯一会修改游戏状态的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: makeMove(player, column) is the only method on Game that mutates game state.

termDefinitions.meaning: currentPlayer 是 Game 保存的字段，标记当前该谁落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the field Game keeps to track whose turn it is.

termDefinitions.meaning: Player 是只存身份和棋子颜色的轻量数据类，不含规则逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Player is a lightweight data class holding only identity and disc color, with no rule logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: Board 是拥有 7x6 网格状态、负责落子和胜负几何检查的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the class that owns the 7x6 grid state and handles disc placement and win-geometry checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 是编排整局流程的类，管理轮次、生命周期状态和 winner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Game is the orchestrator class that manages turns, lifecycle state, and the winner.

optionExplanations: BotEngine 只负责挑一列，规则校验和状态转移照旧走 makeMove，等于给现有流程加了个新调用方。
Board 只懂网格几何，让它替 AI 做决策会把选列策略和落子规则强行焊在一起。
人类玩家没有任何行为要实现，为了 AI 就把 Player 变成继承层级是过度设计。
复制一份 Game 意味着两套规则代码要同步维护，任何规则改动都要改两遍。
optionExplanations_en: BotEngine only picks a column; rule validation and state transitions still flow through the same makeMove call, just from a new caller.
Board only understands grid geometry — making it decide for the AI would weld move-picking strategy onto placement rules.
Human players have no behavior to implement, so turning Player into an inheritance hierarchy just for the AI is over-engineering.
Duplicating Game means two copies of the rules to keep in sync, so every rule change has to be made twice.

q: 为什么“WinChecker interface + 四个方向实现”被视为 pattern abuse？
q_en: Why is “WinChecker interface plus four direction implementations” pattern abuse?
options: 接口在任何设计中都不该使用
需求固定，四个实现只差 dr/dc 参数
它无法检测 diagonal
它会改变棋盘尺寸
options_en: Interfaces should never be used in any design.
The requirement is fixed; the four implementations differ only by dr/dc.
It cannot detect diagonal wins.
It would change the board size.
why: Strategy 适合真实可替换算法。这里是固定几何规则，用参数化函数更直接。
tradeoff: 参数化数据（方向向量） vs Strategy 模式换出可替换算法
why_en: The WinChecker hierarchy adds polymorphism where simple direction data is enough.

termDefinitions.meaning: WinChecker 是文中反例：为每个方向单独建一个类去检查连四，属于过度抽象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WinChecker is the article's anti-pattern example: a separate class per direction to check four-in-a-row, which is over-abstraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 策略模式是一种设计模式，用来在运行时切换可互换的算法实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern is a design pattern for swapping interchangeable algorithm implementations at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方向向量 (dr,dc) 是一对整数偏移，描述沿哪个方向逐格移动，例如水平是 (0,1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A direction vector (dr, dc) is a pair of integer offsets describing which way to step through the grid, such as (0, 1) for horizontal.

optionExplanations: 这话太绝对了，接口本身没有错，错的是在不需要多态的地方硬套接口。
四个方向只是同一个计数算法换了 dr/dc 偏移，做成四个类纯属重复劳动。
WinChecker 完全可以写出检测 diagonal 的实现，问题不在于能不能检测，而在于要不要拆成四个类。
WinChecker 类层级和棋盘有多少行多少列毫无关系，它只处理胜负判断。
optionExplanations_en: Too absolute — interfaces aren't inherently wrong; the issue is forcing one where no real polymorphism is needed.
All four directions are the same counting algorithm with a different dr/dc offset, so splitting them into classes is pure duplication.
A WinChecker class could absolutely detect diagonals fine; the issue isn't detection capability, it's whether splitting into four classes is worth it.
The WinChecker hierarchy has nothing to do with how many rows or columns the board has — it only handles win detection.

q: 基础题明确不需要哪些功能？（多选）
q_en: Which features are explicitly out of scope for the base problem? (Select all that apply.)
options: UI 渲染
多局并发
移动历史和撤销
可配置棋盘尺寸
options_en: UI rendering.
Multiple concurrent games.
Move history and undo.
Configurable board size.
why: 这些都可以作为扩展讨论，但不应污染基础模型。基础目标是一局游戏规则正确。
why_en: UI, concurrent games, undo, history, and configurable board size are scoped out of the base problem.

termDefinitions.meaning: UI（用户界面）是渲染棋盘、展示对局给用户看的层，被排除在本设计范围外。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UI (User Interface) is the layer that renders the board for the user, and it is explicitly out of scope for this design.

optionExplanations: 渲染棋盘属于表现层，基础版只做后端规则模拟，完全不涉及画面。
多局并发要考虑隔离和调度，这些复杂度会淹没单局规则本身，先放到扩展阶段。
撤销和历史记录需要额外的状态和数据结构，基础版先把一局走对再说。
尺寸写死成 7x6，可配置尺寸留到面试官追问扩展性时再参数化。
optionExplanations_en: Rendering the board is a presentation concern; the base design only models backend rules, no visuals at all.
Concurrent games add isolation and scheduling complexity that would drown out the single-match rules, so it's deferred.
Undo and history need extra state and data structures; the base version focuses on getting one match right first.
Size is hardcoded to 7x6; configurable size is left for when the interviewer explicitly asks about extensibility.

scenario: 虽然 UI out of scope，但外部代码可能需要展示棋盘。
scenario_en: Even though UI is out of scope, external code may need to display the board.
q: Board 提供哪个只读方法最自然？
q_en: Which read-only Board method is the most natural?
options: setWinner(player)
sendPixelsToCanvas()
getCell(row,column)
makeMoveWithoutGame()
options_en: setWinner(player).
sendPixelsToCanvas().
getCell(row, column).
makeMoveWithoutGame().
why: getCell 让 UI 或测试读取棋盘状态，而不泄露 grid 可变引用。渲染本身仍不属于 Board。
tradeoff: 只读 getCell 暴露状态 vs 让 Board 直接做渲染/越权写入
whenOtherWins: 如果需要一次性渲染全部棋盘，可返回不可变 board snapshot。
why_en: getCell exposes board state for rendering or tests without making Board a UI component.

termDefinitions.meaning: getCell(row, column) 是 Board 提供的只读方法，返回该格子的棋子颜色或空。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: getCell(row, column) is Board's read-only method that returns the disc color at that cell, or empty.

termDefinitions.meaning: Board 是拥有 7x6 网格状态、负责落子和胜负几何检查的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the class that owns the 7x6 grid state and handles disc placement and win-geometry checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: UI（用户界面）是渲染棋盘、展示对局给用户看的层，被排除在本设计范围外。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UI (User Interface) is the layer that renders the board for the user, and it is explicitly out of scope for this design.

optionExplanations: setWinner 是写操作而且改的是 winner 字段，跟「读棋盘给外部展示」完全是两回事。
把画布绘制塞进 Board 会让它直接依赖渲染库，彻底违背 Board 只管规则的边界。
getCell 只读一个格子的颜色，外部代码可以据此逐格渲染，又不会拿到内部数组的可变引用。
绕开 Game 直接落子会让轮次和状态校验全部失效，这不是渲染需要的东西。
optionExplanations_en: setWinner is a write, and it mutates the wrong field entirely — this has nothing to do with reading the board for display.
Putting canvas drawing inside Board would make it depend directly on a rendering library, breaking its whole rules-only boundary.
getCell just reads one cell's color, letting external code render cell by cell without ever getting a mutable reference to the grid.
Bypassing Game to place a disc directly would skip turn and state validation entirely — nothing to do with what rendering needs.

q: 补全 Game 构造初始状态：
q_en: Fill in Game's initial construction state:
text: Game 构造时创建空 Board，保存两个 Player，设置 {{currentPlayer=player1}}，{{state=IN_PROGRESS}}，{{winner=null}}。
why: 明确初始状态让 makeMove 逻辑简单。winner 为 null 表示尚无胜者或最终平局。
why_en: A new game starts with player one, an empty board, IN_PROGRESS state, and no winner.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

termDefinitions.meaning: currentPlayer 是 Game 保存的字段，标记当前该谁落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the field Game keeps to track whose turn it is.

scenario: 列顶端已经被占满，玩家继续选择该列。
scenario_en: The top cell of a column is already occupied, and a player chooses that column again.
q: 应该发生什么？
q_en: What should happen?
options: 覆盖棋盘顶端已经落好的棋子
自动帮玩家换成相邻的空列
直接切换到下一回合，但棋子并未真正落下
placeDisc 返回 -1，状态保持不变
options_en: Overwrite the disc that's already sitting on top of the stack.
Automatically switch the player to an adjacent empty column instead.
Switch straight to the next turn, but the disc never actually gets placed.
placeDisc returns -1 and state stays unchanged.
why: 满列是非法移动，不能改变棋盘或回合。让 Board 拒绝并让 Game 不切换玩家。
tradeoff: 满列直接拒绝、状态不变 vs 允许覆盖/自动改列
whenOtherWins: 如果 API 使用异常，可抛 ColumnFullException，但仍不能改变状态。
why_en: A full-column move should fail without changing the board or current turn.

termDefinitions.meaning: placeDisc(column, color) 是 Board 的方法，把棋子放到该列重力允许的最低空格并返回行号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: placeDisc(column, color) is Board's method that drops a disc into the lowest open cell of a column and returns the landed row.

termDefinitions.meaning: makeMove(player, column) 是 Game 唯一会修改游戏状态的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: makeMove(player, column) is the only method on Game that mutates game state.

optionExplanations: 覆盖已有棋子会凭空抹掉一次历史落子，破坏棋盘的真实记录。
自动换列悄悄替玩家做了选择，玩家实际选中的列信息就丢失了。
切换回合却没有真正落子，会让「谁走了这一步」变得对不上。
满列时 placeDisc 直接返回 -1，Game 看到失败信号就不改状态、不切换玩家。
optionExplanations_en: Overwriting the existing disc silently erases a past move, corrupting the board's true history.
Auto-switching columns quietly makes the choice for the player, losing which column they actually picked.
Switching turns without actually placing a disc leaves no record of who really made this move.
On a full column, placeDisc simply returns -1, and Game sees the failure signal and leaves state and turn untouched.

scenario: 已经 state=WON，另一个玩家继续调用 makeMove。
scenario_en: The game is already state=WON, and the other player calls makeMove.
q: 正确处理是什么？
q_en: What is the correct handling?
options: 立即返回 false，不落子
允许落子但不检查胜负
重置游戏
把 winner 改成新玩家
options_en: Return false immediately without placing a disc.
Allow the move but skip the win check.
Reset the game.
Change winner to the new player.
why: 游戏结束后任何移动都非法。先检查 state 可以避免结束后状态被破坏。
tradeoff: 结束后立即拒绝新落子 vs 允许继续修改已结束对局
whenOtherWins: 如果产品支持 rematch，应创建新 Game，而不是继续修改已结束对象。
why_en: Moves after a win or draw should be rejected before touching the board.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

termDefinitions.meaning: makeMove(player, column) 是 Game 唯一会修改游戏状态的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: makeMove(player, column) is the only method on Game that mutates game state.

optionExplanations: state 已经是 WON，makeMove 第一步检查就该拦下来，直接返回失败，棋盘和 winner 都不动。
跳过胜负检查却仍然落子，等于在已经结束的对局上继续改棋盘，制造出没有意义的额外状态。
重置整局是另一个功能（比如 rematch），不该被一次多余的落子请求顺带触发。
winner 应该只在真正获胜的那一刻被设置一次，之后的调用不该覆盖它。
optionExplanations_en: state is already WON, so the very first check in makeMove should catch it and return failure without touching the board or winner.
Skipping the win check but still placing a disc keeps mutating a match that's already over, producing meaningless extra state.
Resetting the whole match is a different feature, like rematch, and shouldn't be triggered as a side effect of a stray move request.
winner should be set exactly once, at the moment someone actually wins — later calls shouldn't be allowed to overwrite it.

q: 文章验证流程覆盖了哪些行为？（多选）
q_en: Which behaviors does the verification trace cover? (Select all that apply.)
options: 棋子落到正确行
纵向连四检测
获胜后 state 和 winner 更新
获胜后后续移动被拒绝
options_en: The disc lands in the correct row.
Vertical four-in-a-row detection.
state and winner update after a win.
Moves after a win are rejected.
why: 验证不是形式主义，它确认落子、胜负检测、状态转移和非法后续移动都连贯。
why_en: The verification trace checks placement, win detection, state transition, and rejection after game over.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

termDefinitions.meaning: checkWin(row, column, color) 是 Board 的方法，判断以该格为起点是否形成连四。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: checkWin(row, column, color) is Board's method that checks whether a four-in-a-row forms starting from that cell.

optionExplanations: 先确认棋子真的落到了重力该到的那一格，这是最基本的正确性。
纵向连四是四个方向之一，专门验证它能确认 checkWin 不只对某个方向有效。
赢了之后 state 和 winner 有没有正确写入，是整条流程最终要交付的结果。
赢了以后再落子应该被拒绝，这条验证确认游戏真的会「停下来」。
optionExplanations_en: First confirming the disc actually lands in the row gravity dictates is the most basic correctness check.
Vertical four-in-a-row is one of four directions, and testing it specifically confirms checkWin isn't only correct in one orientation.
Whether state and winner get written correctly after a win is the actual deliverable of the whole flow.
Moves after a win should be rejected, and this check confirms the match genuinely stops instead of silently continuing.

scenario: 你要单元测试 Board.checkWin，不想构造玩家和 Game。
scenario_en: You want to unit test Board.checkWin without constructing players or a Game.
q: 哪个设计选择最有帮助？
q_en: Which design choice helps the most?
options: Game 类负责所有的扫描工作
grid 存 DiscColor 而不是 Player
Player 对象里持有一个 Board 引用
所有测试统一共用一个全局 currentPlayer
options_en: Game itself is made responsible for all the scanning work.
The grid stores DiscColor instead of Player.
Player objects hold a reference to a Board instance.
All tests share one single global currentPlayer variable.
why: 用简单颜色类型填充 grid，测试可直接设置棋盘并验证几何逻辑。Board 不依赖 Game 或 Player。
tradeoff: grid 存轻量 DiscColor 独立测试 vs 存 Player 引入额外依赖
whenOtherWins: 如果语言里 Player 是轻量值对象，存 Player 也可行，但测试依赖更多。
why_en: Storing DiscColor makes Board tests independent of Game and Player objects.

termDefinitions.meaning: DiscColor 是棋子颜色枚举，只有 RED 和 YELLOW 两个取值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DiscColor is an enum for the disc color, holding only RED or YELLOW.

termDefinitions.meaning: Player 是只存身份和棋子颜色的轻量数据类，不含规则逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Player is a lightweight data class holding only identity and disc color, with no rule logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: Board 是拥有 7x6 网格状态、负责落子和胜负几何检查的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the class that owns the 7x6 grid state and handles disc placement and win-geometry checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 是编排整局流程的类，管理轮次、生命周期状态和 winner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Game is the orchestrator class that manages turns, lifecycle state, and the winner.

termDefinitions.meaning: currentPlayer 是 Game 保存的字段，标记当前该谁落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the field Game keeps to track whose turn it is.

optionExplanations: 把扫描逻辑挪到 Game 里，反而让测试 checkWin 时必须先搭出一个 Game 实例。
grid 只存颜色，测试时几行代码摆好颜色就能验证胜负几何，不用碰 Game 或 Player。
Player 持有 Board 会造出循环依赖，单独实例化 Player 都绕不开 Board。
全局 currentPlayer 会让不同测试之间互相污染状态，跟「独立测试」这个目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Moving the scan logic into Game would force any checkWin test to first stand up a whole Game instance.
Storing plain colors in the grid means a test can set up a board in a few lines and check win geometry without touching Game or Player.
Player holding a Board reference creates a circular dependency — you can't even instantiate Player without Board.
A global currentPlayer would let different tests bleed state into each other, which is the opposite of independent testing.

q: 方向向量方案体现了哪种设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does the direction-vector approach show?
options: 每个方向都必须是独立行为
所有循环都应该消除
把变化的数据 dr/dc 和稳定的计数逻辑分开
Board 不应有私有 helper
options_en: Every direction must be an independent behavior.
All loops should be eliminated.
It separates the variable data (dr/dc) from the stable counting logic.
Board should not have private helpers.
why: 四个方向的差别只是移动增量，不是四种独立业务规则。把方向作为数据能减少重复和 bug。
tradeoff: 数据参数化(方向向量) vs 每方向单独一份行为代码
why_en: Direction vectors separate variable data from the shared counting algorithm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方向向量 (dr,dc) 是一对整数偏移，描述沿哪个方向逐格移动，例如水平是 (0,1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A direction vector (dr, dc) is a pair of integer offsets describing which way to step through the grid, such as (0, 1) for horizontal.

termDefinitions.meaning: countInDirection 是从起点沿一个方向数连续同色棋子数量的辅助函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: countInDirection is a helper that counts consecutive same-color discs starting from a cell along one direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: Board 是拥有 7x6 网格状态、负责落子和胜负几何检查的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the class that owns the 7x6 grid state and handles disc placement and win-geometry checks.

optionExplanations: 恰恰相反，方向向量方案说明四个方向根本不需要各自独立的行为，一份逻辑就够。
countInDirection 内部照样有循环，方案要消除的是重复代码，不是循环本身。
dr/dc 是会变的输入数据，遍历计数的算法是稳定不变的，把两者拆开就是这个方案的核心判断。
这个计数函数正是一个私有 helper，方案完全依赖它才成立。
optionExplanations_en: The opposite is true — the vector approach shows the four directions specifically don't need separate behaviors; one routine is enough.
countInDirection still has a loop inside it; what the approach eliminates is duplicated code, not loops themselves.
dr/dc is the variable input, while the counting algorithm that walks it stays fixed — separating the two is exactly the judgment this approach makes.
That counting helper is itself a private routine, and the whole approach depends on it existing.

q: 按顺序排列 Connect Four 的主设计链路：
q_en: Put the main Connect Four design chain in order:
steps: 用 GameState enum 表示生命周期，避免多个 boolean。
Board 使用 grid<DiscColor?>，封装落子和 win check。
先澄清固定 7x6、单局、无 UI/undo。
Game 作为入口，验证轮次并调用 Board。
checkWin 用四个方向向量而非四个类。
why: 这条链路从范围、状态建模、职责边界到核心算法。按此表达能展示设计不是随意拆类。
tradeoff: 先定范围/状态建模，再定编排和算法 vs 没有分层直接写代码
why_en: The design chain moves from scope to state modeling, orchestration, board responsibility, and vector-based win checking.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

termDefinitions.meaning: Board 是拥有 7x6 网格状态、负责落子和胜负几何检查的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the class that owns the 7x6 grid state and handles disc placement and win-geometry checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 是编排整局流程的类，管理轮次、生命周期状态和 winner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Game is the orchestrator class that manages turns, lifecycle state, and the winner.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方向向量 (dr,dc) 是一对整数偏移，描述沿哪个方向逐格移动，例如水平是 (0,1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A direction vector (dr, dc) is a pair of integer offsets describing which way to step through the grid, such as (0, 1) for horizontal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 枚举（enum）是只能取一组预先定义常量之一的类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An enum is a type that can only hold one of a fixed set of predefined constant values.

q: Senior 级答案应主动说明哪些设计点？（多选）
q_en: Which design points should a senior-level answer call out? (Select all that apply.)
options: Player 是数据对象而非规则引擎
GameState enum 优于多个 boolean
win checking 属于 Board
方向向量优于过度 WinChecker 类层级
options_en: Player is a data object, not a rules engine.
A GameState enum beats multiple booleans.
Win checking belongs to Board.
Direction vectors beat an over-engineered WinChecker class hierarchy.
why: 高级答案不仅能写代码，还能解释为什么这些边界稳定。尤其要能识别何时不使用模式。
why_en: Senior answers justify simple boundaries and avoid unnecessary design patterns.

termDefinitions.meaning: Player 是只存身份和棋子颜色的轻量数据类，不含规则逻辑。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Player is a lightweight data class holding only identity and disc color, with no rule logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

termDefinitions.meaning: Board 是拥有 7x6 网格状态、负责落子和胜负几何检查的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Board is the class that owns the 7x6 grid state and handles disc placement and win-geometry checks.

termDefinitions.meaning: WinChecker 是文中反例：为每个方向单独建一个类去检查连四，属于过度抽象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WinChecker is the article's anti-pattern example: a separate class per direction to check four-in-a-row, which is over-abstraction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方向向量 (dr,dc) 是一对整数偏移，描述沿哪个方向逐格移动，例如水平是 (0,1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A direction vector (dr, dc) is a pair of integer offsets describing which way to step through the grid, such as (0, 1) for horizontal.

optionExplanations: 点明 Player 只是数据对象，说明候选人分得清身份数据和规则引擎的边界。
解释 enum 优于多个 boolean，说明候选人在意非法状态能不能被类型系统排除。
指出胜负检查归 Board，说明候选人清楚谁最懂网格就该谁负责几何判断。
能说出方向向量优于四个 WinChecker 类，说明候选人懂得识别何时不该用设计模式。
optionExplanations_en: Calling out that Player is just a data object shows the candidate separates identity data from a rules engine.
Explaining why an enum beats multiple booleans shows the candidate cares whether illegal states are excluded by the type system.
Pointing out that win checking belongs on Board shows understanding that whoever owns the grid should own the geometry.
Being able to say direction vectors beat four WinChecker classes shows the candidate recognizes when NOT to reach for a pattern.

scenario: 你要总结 makeMove 的关键不变量。
scenario_en: You need to summarize the key invariant of makeMove.
q: 哪个不变量最准确？
q_en: Which invariant is most accurate?
options: 任何玩家都能在任何状态落子
Board 负责切换玩家
每次移动都必须产生 winner
成功移动只改一格，且只能当前玩家执行
options_en: Any player can move in any state.
Board is responsible for switching players.
Every move must produce a winner.
A successful move changes one cell and only the current player can make it.
why: 成功移动是唯一改变棋盘的路径，且受 state 和 turn 保护。这个不变量让游戏流程可推理。
tradeoff: 不变量保护单格变更+仅当前玩家 vs 不加约束允许任意状态落子
whenOtherWins: 如果加入并发网络对战，还需要同步 makeMove 以保护同一局状态。
why_en: A successful move changes one cell and is only allowed for the current player while the game is in progress.

termDefinitions.meaning: currentPlayer 是 Game 保存的字段，标记当前该谁落子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: currentPlayer is the field Game keeps to track whose turn it is.

termDefinitions.meaning: GameState 是表示对局生命周期的枚举，只能是 IN_PROGRESS、WON 或 DRAW 之一。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GameState is an enum that represents the match lifecycle as exactly one of IN_PROGRESS, WON, or DRAW.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不变量（invariant）是系统在任何合法操作后都必须保持成立的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a rule that must remain true after every legal operation on the system.

optionExplanations: 这恰好是要被拒绝的情况：state 和轮次校验存在就是为了不让任何人任何时候都能落子。
切换玩家是 Game 的职责，Board 从头到尾不知道谁是当前玩家。
大多数移动只是普通落子，并不会产生 winner，平局和继续对局都是合法结果。
每次成功落子只写入一个格子，并且只有轮到的玩家才能触发，这条约束贯穿整个 makeMove。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly what should be rejected — the state and turn checks exist specifically so not just anyone can move at any time.
Switching players is Game's job; Board never knows who the current player is at all.
Most moves are ordinary placements that produce no winner — continuing play or a draw are both valid outcomes.
Every successful move writes exactly one cell, and only the player whose turn it is can trigger it — that constraint holds throughout makeMove.

q: 中级和高级答案在 win-checking 上的分水岭是什么？
q_en: What separates mid-level and senior answers on win checking?
options: 方向向量配合 countInDirection
只实现横向检查
把所有逻辑放进一个巨大 Game 类
让 UI 判断胜负
options_en: Cover all four directions with direction vectors and countInDirection, and explain why not to split into four classes.
Only implement horizontal checking.
Cram all the logic into one giant Game class.
Let the UI decide who won.
why: 方向向量方案体现模式识别和克制抽象。它比四份重复代码或类层级都更适合固定规则游戏。
tradeoff: 方向向量+countInDirection 通用算法 vs 只做部分方向或塞进 Game/UI
why_en: The vector-based countInDirection approach is the clean expected solution for all four win directions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 方向向量 (dr,dc) 是一对整数偏移，描述沿哪个方向逐格移动，例如水平是 (0,1)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A direction vector (dr, dc) is a pair of integer offsets describing which way to step through the grid, such as (0, 1) for horizontal.

termDefinitions.meaning: countInDirection 是从起点沿一个方向数连续同色棋子数量的辅助函数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: countInDirection is a helper that counts consecutive same-color discs starting from a cell along one direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: Game 是编排整局流程的类，管理轮次、生命周期状态和 winner。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Game is the orchestrator class that manages turns, lifecycle state, and the winner.

termDefinitions.meaning: UI（用户界面）是渲染棋盘、展示对局给用户看的层，被排除在本设计范围外。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UI (User Interface) is the layer that renders the board for the user, and it is explicitly out of scope for this design.

optionExplanations: 覆盖全部四个方向、复用同一份 countInDirection，还能讲清楚为什么不拆四个类，这才是完整答案。
只做横向检查会直接漏掉纵向和两条对角线的胜利，是明显的功能缺失。
把胜负几何塞进 Game，会让 Game 同时懂编排又懂网格坐标，职责边界就消失了。
UI 本就不在设计范围内，让它判断胜负等于把规则逻辑泄漏到表现层。
optionExplanations_en: Covering all four directions with one shared countInDirection, and being able to explain why it's not split into four classes, is the complete answer.
Only implementing horizontal checking flat-out misses vertical and both diagonal wins — a clear functional gap.
Cramming win geometry into Game would make it understand both orchestration and grid coordinates at once, erasing the responsibility boundary.
UI is out of scope by design; letting it decide the winner would leak rules logic into the presentation layer.

q: Elevator 基础需求包含哪些约束？（多选）
q_en: Which constraints are part of the base Elevator problem? (Select all that apply)
options: 需要实现载重、门控和紧急停止
用户可发 hall call，进入后可选目的楼层
仿真通过 step/tick 离散推进
3 部电梯服务 0-9 共 10 层
why: 基础题聚焦调度和移动模拟。载重、门、紧急停止、动态配置和 UI 都被排除。
why_en: The base elevator design focuses on three elevators, ten floors, hall and destination requests, and discrete simulation ticks.
options_en: The system must implement weight limits, door control, and emergency stop.
Users can send a hall call, and once inside pick a destination floor.
The simulation advances through discrete step/tick calls.
Three elevators serve ten floors, numbered 0 through 9.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推进仿真一个离散时间单位的方法调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: step() advances the discrete-time simulation by one tick.

optionExplanations: 载重、门控、紧急停止是真实电梯的硬件安全层，这道题只做调度仿真，不建这些部件。
hall call 加轿厢内选楼层，是整个仿真唯一的请求入口，没它就没有 pickup/destination 可调度。
把时间切成离散 tick，每次 step 只推进一步，仿真行为可预测、可复现。
3 部电梯、10 层楼把规模钉死，楼层合法性和电梯数量从一开始就有明确边界。
optionExplanations_en: Weight limits, door control, and emergency stop are hardware-safety concerns for a real elevator, but this scoped design only simulates scheduling and movement.
A hall call plus an in-cab floor pick is the only request entry point driving the simulation — without it there's nothing to schedule.
Slicing time into discrete ticks means each step advances exactly one unit, keeping the simulation predictable and reproducible.
Fixing three elevators and ten floors pins the scale, so valid-floor and elevator-count boundaries are clear from the start.

q: Elevator 题的核心实体是什么？
q_en: What are the core entities in the Elevator design?
options: ElevatorController、Elevator、Request
Floor、Door、Sensor
Passenger、Payment、Ticket
Building、Lobby、Renderer
why: Controller 负责任务分配和 step 推进，Elevator 管自身位置、方向和请求集合，Request 捕获楼层和类型。Floor 只是整数。
why_en: The core model is a controller coordinating elevators, each elevator owning movement state, and requests carrying floor and type.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class ElevatorController
  class Elevator
  class Request
  ElevatorController --> Elevator
  ElevatorController --> Request
  Elevator --> Request
options_en: ElevatorController, Elevator, and Request.
Floor, Door, and Sensor.
Passenger, Payment, and Ticket.
Building, Lobby, and Renderer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

optionExplanations: 这三类刚好覆盖调度协调、单梯运动状态和请求身份三件事，是这道题真正要建的模型。
楼层、门和传感器属于硬件控制层，这道题范围内没有门控和传感器，不需要为它们建类。
乘客、计费、票据是电商或购票系统的实体，跟电梯调度和移动无关。
楼宇外壳和渲染层是 UI/物理呈现，这道题只考调度逻辑，不建这些展示层对象。
optionExplanations_en: These three classes are exactly enough to cover fleet coordination, one elevator's motion state, and request identity.
Floor, door, and sensor are hardware-control concerns, and this problem's scope has no door control or sensors to model.
Passenger, payment, and ticket are entities from a booking or billing system, unrelated to elevator scheduling.
Building shell and renderer are UI or physical-presentation concerns; this problem only covers scheduling logic.

scenario: 需求中楼层只表示位置，没有状态、规则或生命周期。
scenario_en: In scope, a floor is only a position; it has no state, rules, or lifecycle.
q: Floor 应该如何建模？
q_en: How should Floor be modeled?
options: 包含乘客队列和门状态的类
int 楼层号
Elevator 的子类
RequestType 枚举值
why: 当前范围里 floor 不维护任何状态，只是坐标。把它建成类会增加无用间接层。
why_en: Floor remains an integer because it has no state or behavior in the scoped problem.
whenOtherWins: 如果后续要建模楼层按钮、显示屏、门厅传感器或无障碍区域，Floor 才可能成为实体。
options_en: A class holding a passenger queue and door state.
A plain int floor number.
A subclass of Elevator.
A RequestType enum value.
tradeoff: int 原语 vs 独立 Floor 类

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

optionExplanations: 楼层要真的管乘客队列和门状态时才值得建类，本题范围没有门控，这个类会是空壳。
本题里楼层只是坐标，没有状态或行为，用 int 就够，也让 Request 和 Elevator 直接持有它。
楼层不是电梯的特化版本，继承关系在语义上就错了。
RequestType 表达的是请求种类，把位置塞进枚举会把楼层和请求类型混成一件事。
optionExplanations_en: A Floor class earns its keep only once it owns a passenger queue or door state; in this scope it would stay an empty shell.
Floor is nothing but a coordinate here, so a plain int is enough and lets Request or Elevator hold it directly.
A floor isn't a specialized elevator, so an inheritance relationship is semantically wrong.
RequestType encodes the kind of request, not a location — folding floor into it conflates two different things.

q: RequestType 需要区分哪些类型？（多选）
q_en: Which request types does RequestType need to distinguish? (Select all that apply)
options: PICKUP_UP
IDLE
DESTINATION
PICKUP_DOWN
why: hall call 有方向，destination 是轿厢内按钮，不带方向。IDLE 属于 Elevator 的 Direction，不是请求类型。
why_en: RequestType distinguishes up pickups, down pickups, and destination stops, while IDLE belongs to elevator direction.
options_en: PICKUP_UP for an up hall call.
IDLE for no active request.
DESTINATION for an in-cab floor button.
PICKUP_DOWN for a down hall call.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

optionExplanations: 楼层外呼叫必须带方向，PICKUP_UP 让向上电梯才去接这个人。
IDLE 描述的是电梯自己有没有请求、要不要动，属于 Direction 而不是请求种类。
轿厢内按下的目的楼层不带方向，到达即服务，所以单独算一种类型。
同理，PICKUP_DOWN 让下行电梯去接，不会被上行电梯错误接走。
optionExplanations_en: A hall call needs a direction, and PICKUP_UP makes sure only an up-moving elevator answers it.
IDLE describes whether the elevator itself has work to do, so it belongs to Direction, not to request type.
An in-cab destination has no direction — the elevator just serves it on arrival, so it gets its own type.
Symmetrically, PICKUP_DOWN routes the pickup to a down-moving elevator instead of an upward one.

scenario: 电梯在 5 楼向上，已有 7、8 楼请求；7 楼有人按 DOWN。
scenario_en: The elevator is on floor 5 moving up with requests at floors 7 and 8; someone on floor 7 presses DOWN.
q: 为什么只用 Set<Integer> 存楼层不够？
q_en: Why is Set<Integer> not enough for pending floors?
options: 楼层号不能比较大小
Set<Integer> 不能去重
无法区分 7 楼向上停靠和 7 楼向下接人
目的楼层不能用整数表示
why: 同一楼层不同请求类型语义不同。向上的电梯不应为了 PICKUP_DOWN 在 7 楼停下接错方向乘客。
why_en: A floor-only request loses whether a hall call is for up or down pickup.
whenOtherWins: 初级或极简模拟可以只存楼层，只要承认会有方向体验问题。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  F["floor 7"] --> U["PICKUP_UP"]
  F --> D["PICKUP_DOWN"]
  U --> A["up elevator may stop"]
  D --> B["down elevator may stop"]
options_en: Floor numbers cannot be compared for ordering.
Set<Integer> cannot deduplicate entries.
It cannot distinguish an up-bound stop at floor 7 from a down pickup at floor 7.
A destination floor cannot be represented as an integer.
tradeoff: Set<Integer> vs Set<Request>

termDefinitions.meaning: 只存楼层号的集合，无法区分同楼层不同方向的请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Integer> stores only floor numbers and cannot distinguish same-floor requests of different direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储 Request 对象的集合，用楼层加类型共同判重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Request> stores Request objects and de-duplicates using floor plus type together.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

optionExplanations: 整数天然可比较大小，排序和距离计算都没问题，这不是失败点。
Set 恰恰会去重——问题在于它把 7 楼两个不同方向的请求错误合并成一个。
同一楼层的上行停靠和下行接人是两件事，只存楼层号会把它们混成一条记录。
目的楼层照样能用整数表示，这不是本题真正的限制。
optionExplanations_en: Integers compare fine for ordering and distance, so that isn't the actual failure.
A Set does deduplicate — the real issue is it wrongly merges two different-direction requests at floor 7 into one.
An up-bound stop and a down pickup at the same floor 7 are two different things a floor-only entry can't tell apart.
A destination floor is still perfectly representable as an integer, so that isn't the real limitation.

q: 补全 Request 的身份字段：
q_en: Fill in the identity fields for Request:
text: Request 应包含 {{floor}} 和 {{RequestType}}；相等和 hash 应基于这两个字段，因此 Request(7,PICKUP_UP) 与 Request(7,PICKUP_DOWN) {{不相等}}。
why: 同楼层不同方向不能被 Set 合并成一个请求。目的楼层则可在任何方向停靠。
why_en: Request equality should include both floor and request type so opposite-direction hall calls remain distinct.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了下行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_DOWN is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the down button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定两个对象在集合中是否视为相等、以及哈希桶位置的两个方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: equals() and hashCode() determine object equality and hash-bucket placement inside a collection.

scenario: 电梯没有任何请求时，不应该继续向上或向下漂移。
scenario_en: When an elevator has no pending requests, it should not keep drifting up or down.
q: Direction enum 为什么需要 IDLE？
q_en: Why does the Direction enum need IDLE?
options: 表示电梯故障
表示 hall call 的向上按钮
表示目的楼层
表示无请求不移动的状态
why: UP/DOWN 只能表示运动方向，不能表达静止。IDLE 让 step 在无请求时自然停住。
why_en: IDLE represents an elevator with no active movement, preventing it from drifting forever.
whenOtherWins: 如果用 nullable direction 或状态机对象，也能表达 idle，但 enum 更简单。
options_en: It represents an elevator malfunction.
It represents the up button of a hall call.
It represents a destination floor.
It represents the no-requests, not-moving state.
tradeoff: IDLE 枚举值 vs nullable direction

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: 故障应该用单独的错误状态或字段表达，混进 Direction 会让正常和异常判断纠缠。
上行按钮的方向属于 hall call 的 RequestType，不该塞进电梯自身的运动方向。
目的楼层是 Request 里的一个字段，不是电梯的运动方向。
UP/DOWN 只能表达在动，电梯没请求时需要一个显式的静止值，否则 step 无法收敛。
optionExplanations_en: A malfunction deserves its own error state or field — folding it into Direction blurs normal and abnormal cases.
The up-button direction belongs to the hall call's RequestType, not to the elevator's own movement state.
A destination floor is a field on Request, not a direction the elevator moves in.
UP/DOWN can only describe motion, so an elevator with no requests needs an explicit still value or step never settles.

q: Elevator 需要保存哪些状态？（多选）
q_en: Which state should an Elevator store? (Select all that apply)
options: currentFloor
direction
其他电梯的位置
requests: Set<Request>
why: 单部电梯只管理自身运动。其他电梯由 ElevatorController 观察和调度。
why_en: An Elevator owns its current floor, direction, and pending requests, not the whole fleet.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class Elevator
  class ElevatorController
  class Request
  ElevatorController --> Elevator
  Elevator --> Request
  Request : floor
  Request : type
options_en: currentFloor, its own position.
direction, its own movement state.
The positions of other elevators.
requests: Set<Request>, its own pending stops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存储 Request 对象的集合，用楼层加类型共同判重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Set<Request> stores Request objects and de-duplicates using floor plus type together.

optionExplanations: 每次移动和边界检查都要知道自己在哪层，这是最基本的状态。
UP/DOWN/IDLE 决定该不该反向、该不该停，缺了它 step 无法判断下一步。
全局视图属于 Controller 的职责，单部电梯知道别的电梯位置会打破封装边界。
自己的待服务请求集合决定它下一步往哪走、在哪停，是这台电梯的核心待办清单。
optionExplanations_en: Every movement and boundary check needs to know which floor it's on right now — the most basic piece of state.
UP/DOWN/IDLE decides whether to reverse or stop, so step can't make its next move without it.
Fleet-wide visibility is the controller's job; letting one elevator know others' positions breaks encapsulation.
Its own pending-request set is what decides where it heads next and where it stops — this elevator's to-do list.

scenario: 用户在 5 楼按上行按钮，系统需要决定哪部电梯响应。
scenario_en: A user on floor 5 presses the up button, and the system must decide which elevator responds.
q: 这个决策应该放在哪里？
q_en: Where should this dispatch decision live?
options: ElevatorController
单个 Elevator 内部逻辑
Request 的构造函数中
Floor 这个类里
why: 调度需要看多部电梯的全局状态，因此属于 Controller。单个 Elevator 不应该知道其他电梯。
why_en: Dispatch belongs in ElevatorController because it requires fleet-level information.
whenOtherWins: 单电梯系统可以直接给该 Elevator.addRequest，省掉 Controller 调度逻辑。
options_en: ElevatorController.
Inside a single Elevator's own logic.
Inside the Request constructor.
Inside the Floor class.
tradeoff: 全局调度决策 vs 单电梯本地状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

optionExplanations: 派发要比较所有电梯的状态才能选出最合适的一部，只有 Controller 拿得到这个全局视角。
单部电梯只认识自己的楼层和请求，让它比较别的电梯会破坏封装边界。
构造函数应该只负责校验和初始化字段，不该在创建对象时顺带做调度决策。
本题没有 Floor 实体，也不该让一个坐标类承担派发这种协调职责。
optionExplanations_en: Dispatch has to compare every elevator's state to pick the best one, and only the controller has that fleet-wide view.
A single elevator only knows its own floor and requests — asking it to compare others breaks the encapsulation boundary.
A constructor should just validate and initialize fields, not sneak in a fleet-wide dispatch decision.
This problem doesn't even model Floor as an entity, and a coordinate class shouldn't own dispatch responsibility.

scenario: requestElevator 是 hall call API，只接受上行或下行呼叫。
scenario_en: requestElevator is the hall-call API, and it accepts only up or down hall calls.
q: 为什么参数用 RequestType 而不是 Direction？
q_en: Why should the API parameter use RequestType instead of Direction?
options: Direction 不能表示上行方向
RequestType 排除 IDLE 值
RequestType 会自动选择电梯
Direction 类型无法做相等比较
why: hall call 不可能是 IDLE。使用更窄的类型减少运行时校验和非法状态。
why_en: Using RequestType for hall calls avoids accepting IDLE as a valid request direction.
whenOtherWins: 内部电梯运动状态仍应使用 Direction，因为它确实需要 IDLE。
options_en: Direction cannot represent the up direction.
RequestType excludes IDLE at the type level.
RequestType automatically selects an elevator.
Direction values cannot be compared for equality.
tradeoff: RequestType 参数 vs Direction 参数

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: Direction 里明明有 UP，这不是问题所在。
hall call 永远带方向，用 RequestType 能在类型层面就排除 IDLE 这个非法输入，不用运行时再校验。
参数类型只负责表达合法输入，真正选哪部电梯仍由 Controller 的调度逻辑决定。
枚举之间的相等比较没有问题，这不是选类型的理由。
optionExplanations_en: Direction clearly includes UP, so that isn't the actual problem.
A hall call is never IDLE, so typing the parameter as RequestType rules out that illegal value at compile time instead of a runtime check.
The parameter type only shapes valid input — which elevator gets picked is still the controller's dispatch logic.
Enum equality comparisons work fine here; that's not the reason to pick one type over the other.

scenario: 你需要先实现一个简单正确的 dispatch 策略，在小楼轻流量下可接受。
scenario_en: You need a simple, correct dispatch strategy that is acceptable for a small building with light traffic.
q: 最简单策略是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest dispatch strategy?
options: 随机选择任意电梯
总是选择 0 号电梯
选择当前楼层距离请求楼层最近的电梯
只选择当前向下的电梯
why: nearest elevator 容易实现且能工作，但不考虑方向会产生等待体验问题。面试中可先实现再说明局限。
why_en: Nearest-elevator dispatch is simple and acceptable as a first implementation, though it ignores direction.
whenOtherWins: 当体验要求更高时，应考虑方向、当前请求队列是否会经过该楼层、或更完整的调度策略。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["new hall call"] --> B["check elevators"]
  B --> C["score distance and direction"]
  C --> D["choose best elevator"]
  D --> E["add request"]
options_en: Pick any elevator at random.
Always pick elevator number 0.
Pick whichever elevator's current floor is closest to the requested floor.
Only pick an elevator that is currently going down.
tradeoff: 实现简单 vs 等待体验

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调度函数，按某种策略从多部电梯中选出最合适的一部。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: selectBestElevator is the dispatch function that picks the best elevator under a chosen strategy.

optionExplanations: 完全不看位置的随机派发，只有在压力测试制造混乱负载时才有价值，正常场景下等待时间不可预期。
永远指定同一部电梯会让其余电梯闲置、这部电梯超载，只有单电梯系统才等价于它。
只比较各电梯 currentFloor 到请求楼层的距离，实现最简单，在小楼轻流量下是个能跑的起点。
只服务向下电梯会让所有上行请求永远等不到车，是个方向性的错误规则。
optionExplanations_en: Random dispatch ignoring position only makes sense for stress-testing chaotic load — normal traffic gets unpredictable waits.
Always picking the same elevator leaves the rest idle while overloading one, which only makes sense in a single-elevator system.
Comparing each elevator's currentFloor to the request floor is the simplest thing to implement and a workable start for a small, light-traffic building.
Restricting to down-moving elevators would starve every up request forever — that's a directionally broken rule.

q: 按顺序排列 nearest 策略的问题场景：
q_en: Order the failure scenario for the nearest-elevator strategy:
steps: 6 楼电梯最近，但正在向下去 1 楼。
5 楼用户按 UP。
nearest 策略派 6 楼电梯。
该电梯向下路过 5 楼不会接 UP 用户，用户等待更久。
why: 最近不等于最合适。电梯当前方向和请求类型必须一起考虑。
why_en: The nearest elevator can be a poor choice when it is moving away or serving the opposite direction.

scenario: 要改进 nearest 策略，使正在正确方向移动且会经过请求楼层的电梯优先。
scenario_en: Improve nearest dispatch so elevators already moving the right way and passing the request floor are preferred.
q: 更好的优先级是什么？
q_en: What is the better dispatch priority?
options: 只按电梯编号顺序挑选
先找最远、不管方向的电梯
只考虑 idle 电梯，忽略在途电梯
先同向顺路电梯，再最近 idle，最后任意最近
why: 这个分层策略能减少让乘客看着电梯朝反方向经过的情况。它仍然保持实现可解释。
why_en: A direction-aware dispatch first uses elevators moving toward the request, then idle ones, then the nearest fallback.
whenOtherWins: 如果已有请求不会带电梯到达或越过该楼层，还需要进一步检查 hasRequestsAtOrBeyond。
options_en: Elevators picked purely by their index order.
The farthest elevator regardless of direction.
Only idle elevators, ignoring elevators already en route.
Same-direction elevators already heading toward the floor first, then nearest idle, then any nearest.
tradeoff: 方向感知优先级 vs 纯最近距离

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调度函数，按某种策略从多部电梯中选出最合适的一部。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: selectBestElevator is the dispatch function that picks the best elevator under a chosen strategy.

optionExplanations: 按编号挑选完全忽略了位置和方向，跟乘客实际等待体验无关。
故意选最远的电梯只会让等待距离变长，没有任何场景值得这么做。
忽略在途电梯会浪费本来顺路就能捎带服务的机会。
先用同向顺路电梯接，再退到最近 idle，最后才任意兜底，这个分层能减少乘客看着电梯反向经过的尴尬。
optionExplanations_en: Picking by index order ignores position and direction entirely — it has nothing to do with actual wait experience.
Deliberately choosing the farthest elevator only lengthens the wait, with no scenario where that helps.
Ignoring en-route elevators wastes chances to pick up a rider who's already on the way.
Preferring a same-direction elevator already heading that way, then nearest idle, then any nearest as a fallback, cuts down on passengers watching an elevator go the wrong way first.

scenario: 电梯在 3 楼向上，只剩 4 楼请求；7 楼用户按 UP。
scenario_en: An elevator is on floor 3 moving up, but only has a remaining request at floor 4; a user on floor 7 presses UP.
q: 仅检查“方向向上且当前楼层低于 7”有什么问题？
q_en: What is wrong with only checking "moving up and below floor 7"?
options: 电梯到 4 楼后可能反向，根本不会继续到 7 楼
电梯无法到 4 楼
7 楼请求不需要处理
UP 请求必须由向下电梯处理
why: 方向只是当前状态，还要看队列是否会把电梯带到请求楼层或更远。否则会错误派发即将反向的电梯。
why_en: Current direction is not enough; the queued requests must extend to or past the requested floor.
whenOtherWins: 简单面试实现可先用方向感知策略，并主动说明这个限制。
options_en: The elevator may reverse after floor 4 and never actually continue to floor 7.
The elevator cannot reach floor 4 at all.
The floor 7 request does not need to be handled.
UP requests must be served by a downward-moving elevator.
tradeoff: 只看当前方向 vs 检查请求队列是否顺路

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检查请求队列是否会把电梯带到或超过某楼层，用于判断电梯是否真正顺路。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: hasRequestsAtOrBeyond checks whether the queue actually commits the elevator to reach or pass a given floor.

optionExplanations: 方向只是这一刻的状态，电梯服务完 4 楼请求后完全可能反向，根本不会经过 7 楼。
4 楼正是电梯已有的请求楼层，它显然到得了。
7 楼的 hall call 仍然合法，需要被某部电梯服务。
这把方向规则完全说反了，UP 请求应该交给正在或即将上行的电梯。
optionExplanations_en: Direction only describes the current instant — after serving floor 4 the elevator can easily reverse and never reach floor 7.
Floor 4 is exactly where the elevator already has a pending request, so it obviously can reach it.
The floor 7 hall call is still a valid request that some elevator needs to serve.
That gets the direction rule backwards — an UP request should go to an elevator moving or about to move up.

scenario: 实现 request-aware dispatch 时，需要判断某电梯是否会继续经过请求楼层。
scenario_en: For request-aware dispatch, you need to know whether an elevator will continue to or past the request floor.
q: 这段 helper 的作用是什么？
q_en: What does this helper check?
codeSample:
hasRequestsAtOrBeyond(floor, dir)
    for request in requests
        if dir == UP && request.floor >= floor
            if request.type == PICKUP_UP || request.type == DESTINATION
                return true
        if dir == DOWN && request.floor <= floor
            if request.type == PICKUP_DOWN || request.type == DESTINATION
                return true
    return false
options: 立即删除所有请求
确认队列会把电梯带到或越过请求楼层
判断当前楼层是否越界
替代 step 的移动逻辑
why: 它避免派发即将反向的电梯。只把匹配方向的 pickup 和 destination 当作可延伸路径。
why_en: The helper checks whether existing requests commit the elevator to travel to or beyond the requested floor.
whenOtherWins: 如果只实现 nearest 或 direction-aware 初版，可以不写该 helper，但要说明等待体验的局限。
options_en: It immediately deletes every pending request.
It confirms the queue actually commits the elevator to reach or pass the requested floor.
It checks whether the current floor is out of bounds.
It replaces step's movement logic entirely.
tradeoff: 顺路检查（hasRequestsAtOrBeyond） vs 只看方向

q: FIFO 移动策略的主要问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main problem with FIFO movement?
options: 它总是最省距离
它无法移动到任何楼层
按请求到达顺序会频繁折返，体验和效率差
它不需要请求队列

why_en: FIFO movement can thrash between floors because it ignores direction and batching.
options_en: It always travels the shortest possible distance.
It cannot move to any floor at all.
Serving requests strictly in arrival order thrashes back and forth, hurting experience and efficiency.
It does not need a request queue.
tradeoff: FIFO 简单 vs 频繁折返体验差

termDefinitions.meaning: 先进先出：按请求到达的先后顺序处理，不考虑方向或距离。

optionExplanations: FIFO 完全不管距离，8 楼、3 楼、7 楼这种顺序反而会拉长总路程。
FIFO 照样能移动到任意楼层，问题不在于能不能到，而在于路径难看。
严格按到达顺序服务会让电梯像 8→3→7 这样来回折返，乘客感觉被无视。
FIFO 恰恰依赖一个按到达顺序保存的队列，不用队列它连顺序都记不住。
optionExplanations_en: FIFO ignores distance entirely — an order like floor 8, then 3, then 7 actually lengthens the total trip.
FIFO can still reach any floor; the problem isn't reachability, it's how ugly the resulting path looks.
Serving strictly in arrival order can make the elevator zigzag like floor 8 then 3 then 7, so riders feel ignored.
FIFO depends entirely on a queue that preserves arrival order — without one it couldn't even remember the sequence.

q: Nearest-first 移动虽然可能减少距离，为什么仍不理想？

它总距离一定比 SCAN 更长

为最近请求反复变向，乘客看到电梯先离开再回来
why: 电梯调度不仅是总距离，还要可预测和减少折返。SCAN 更符合真实电梯的扫掠行为。

options_en: It needs an extra Set data structure just to run.
It always travels a longer total distance than SCAN.
It never skips a request going the opposite direction.
It still reverses direction for the nearest request, so passengers watch the elevator leave then come back.
tradeoff: Nearest-first 距离可能更短 vs 仍会反复反向

termDefinitions.meaning: 移动策略：每次都去当前最近的请求楼层，不管方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Nearest-first always moves toward whichever pending request is currently closest, regardless of direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: SCAN 是沿当前方向持续服务请求、直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法，借用了磁盘调度的思想。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in the current direction serving requests, and only reverses once nothing remains ahead — the same idea used in disk-arm scheduling.

optionExplanations: 数据结构选型跟这个问题无关，任何策略都可以用 Set 存请求。
总距离不一定比 SCAN 长，真正的问题是可预测性和体验，不是纯距离。
nearest-first 恰恰会被最近的反方向请求拽走，不是不跳过，而是会频繁被拉偏。
只看谁最近会让电梯为一个新请求反复掉头，乘客看着电梯先离开又折返，行为不可预期。
optionExplanations_en: Data-structure choice is unrelated here — any strategy can store requests in a Set.
Total distance isn't necessarily longer than SCAN's; the real problem is predictability and experience, not raw distance.
Nearest-first is exactly what gets pulled off course by the closest opposite-direction request, not something that skips them.
Chasing whichever request is closest makes the elevator reverse repeatedly, so riders watch it leave and then double back unpredictably.

scenario: 电梯当前向上，前方还有请求，后方也有请求。

q: SCAN 算法的基本选择是什么？
q_en: What is the basic choice made by SCAN?
options: 继续当前方向，沿途服务，直到前方没有请求再反向
立刻去最近请求
按请求到达顺序处理
每 tick 随机决定方向

why_en: SCAN keeps moving in one direction, serves stops along the way, and reverses only when no requests remain ahead.
whenOtherWins: 极简模拟可以用 FIFO 或 nearest-first，只要说明用户体验和效率较差。
diagram:

  B --> C{more ahead?}
  C -->|yes| A
  C -->|no| D[reverse]
  D --> E[serve down ahead]

Go straight to the nearest request immediately.
Process requests strictly in arrival order.
Pick a random direction every tick.

optionExplanations: SCAN 沿当前方向一路服务，直到前方没有请求才反向，行为可预期，最多反一次向。

q: Elevator.step 的高层顺序是什么？

steps: 如果当前楼层应停靠，移除匹配请求，必要时设 IDLE，并且本 tick 不移动。

如果 direction=IDLE，根据最近请求选择初始方向。

pickupRequest = Request(currentFloor, pickupType)

It does not count, so the elevator should just stay idle.
It should make the elevator stop immediately at floor 6.
It counts as a request ahead, so the elevator keeps going up but does not stop at floor 6.

The elevator can physically travel past floor 9.
