This is a legal input, not an error case, so returning false would be a false alarm.
Forcing the direction has nothing to do with this request and would corrupt the elevator's existing motion state.

q: requestElevator / addRequest 应拒绝哪些输入？（多选）
q_en: Which inputs should requestElevator / addRequest reject? (Select all that apply)
options: 楼层小于 0 或大于 9
hall call 使用 DESTINATION 类型
空请求对象
当前楼层 no-op
why: 无效楼层和错误请求类型应拒绝。当前楼层按需求是已服务，不算错误。
why_en: Invalid floors, invalid hall-call types, and null requests should be rejected, while current-floor requests are no-ops.
options_en: A floor number below 0 or above 9.
A hall call that uses the DESTINATION type.
A null request object.
A request for the current floor treated as a no-op.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: 超出 0-9 范围的楼层会让电梯试图停在不存在的地方，必须拒绝。
hall call 只能是 PICKUP_UP/PICKUP_DOWN，用 DESTINATION 冒充楼层外呼叫会破坏方向语义。
没有 floor/type 字段的空对象一旦进入状态机，后续访问就会崩溃，必须提前挡掉。
当前楼层请求按需求视为已服务的 no-op，是合法输入，不该被拒绝。
optionExplanations_en: A floor outside 0–9 would make the elevator try to stop somewhere that doesn't exist, so it must be rejected.
A hall call must be PICKUP_UP or PICKUP_DOWN — letting DESTINATION masquerade as one breaks the direction semantics.
A null object with no floor or type would crash later code that reads those fields, so it needs to be caught early.
A current-floor request is a legitimate no-op that's treated as already served, not something to reject.

scenario: 有人因为 Controller.requestElevator 和 Elevator.addRequest 都“接收请求”而想抽共同接口 IRequestHandler。
scenario_en: Someone wants a shared IRequestHandler interface because Controller.requestElevator and Elevator.addRequest both receive requests.
q: 为什么这是不必要抽象？
q_en: Why is this an unnecessary abstraction?
options: addRequest 其实不能返回 boolean 值
共享接口会导致代码编译失败
语义不同：Controller 协调选择，Elevator 只改队列
requestElevator 根本不需要楼层参数
why: 相同参数形状不代表同一行为。接口应服务可替换多态，而不是为了名字相似。
why_en: Similar method shapes do not justify an interface when the responsibilities are different.
options_en: addRequest cannot actually return a boolean.
A shared interface would fail to compile.
Their semantics differ: the controller coordinates a choice, the elevator only mutates its own queue.
requestElevator does not actually need a floor parameter.
tradeoff: 按行为语义分离接口 vs 按参数形状合并接口

termDefinitions.meaning: 本题中假设的一个公共接口名，用来说明为相似方法签名强行抽公共接口的反例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IRequestHandler is a hypothetical shared interface used here as a counter-example of forcing an interface onto unrelated methods.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

whenOtherWins: 如果未来真的出现多种可互相替换的请求处理器实现，需要在运行时切换，那时抽接口才有实际价值。
optionExplanations: addRequest 完全可以返回 boolean，这不是问题所在。
共享接口在语法上完全能编译通过，编译与否不是判断依据。
选哪部电梯这件事要看多部电梯的状态，addRequest 只是改自己的队列，两者职责不同，硬凑成一个接口没有意义。
这个方法要知道去哪层接人，楼层参数显然是必需的，不能省略。
optionExplanations_en: addRequest can perfectly well return a boolean — that isn't the issue.
A shared interface would compile just fine syntactically, so compilability isn't the deciding factor.
Choosing an elevator has to look across the whole fleet, while addRequest just mutates its own queue — different jobs that don't need forcing into one interface.
requestElevator obviously needs the floor parameter to know which floor to go pick someone up from.

q: 文章中电梯从 3 楼向上服务 5 楼 pickup 和 7 楼 destination 的关键 tick 顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the key tick order from floor 3 to pickup at 5 and destination at 7?
steps: 到 5 楼，移除 PICKUP_UP，并本 tick 不移动。
从 3 楼向上移动到 4 楼。
继续移动到 7 楼。
到 7 楼，移除 DESTINATION，请求清空后 IDLE。
why: 验证展示了停靠消耗 tick、destination 可被服务、请求清空后进入 IDLE。
why_en: The trace validates upward movement, stop ticks, destination handling, and transition to idle.
diagram:
stateDiagram
  [*] --> Floor3Up
  Floor3Up --> Floor4
  Floor4 --> Floor5Stop
  Floor5Stop --> Floor6
  Floor6 --> Floor7Stop

termDefinitions.meaning: hall call 请求类型，表示乘客在某楼层按了上行按钮。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PICKUP_UP is a hall-call request type for someone pressing the up button on a floor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 轿厢内乘客按下的目的楼层请求，不带方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DESTINATION is an in-cab floor request that carries no direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

scenario: 后续加入 express elevator，只停 0、5、9 层。
scenario_en: A later requirement adds express elevators that stop only at floors 0, 5, and 9.
q: 更好的基础扩展是什么？
q_en: What is the better basic extension?
options: 在 RequestType 里新增 EXPRESS_UP 类型
把所有电梯的请求队列换成 priority queue
直接删掉所有普通（非快速）电梯
给 Elevator 加 isExpress，addRequest 校验楼层
why: express 主要是电梯能力约束和 Controller 的派发偏好，不必改变 Request 结构。
why_en: Express support can be modeled as elevator capability validation plus dispatch preference.
whenOtherWins: 如果有 VIP 或紧急请求，Request 可能需要 priority 字段，但这会影响移动算法。
options_en: Add a new EXPRESS_UP value to RequestType.
Replace every elevator's request queue with a priority queue.
Delete all regular, non-express elevators.
Add isExpress to Elevator and validate allowed floors inside addRequest.
tradeoff: 电梯能力约束 vs 修改 Request 结构

termDefinitions.meaning: 扩展字段，标记某电梯是否为只停靠指定楼层的快速梯。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: isExpress is an extension flag marking an elevator that only serves a restricted set of floors.

termDefinitions.meaning: 快速电梯允许停靠的楼层集合，如 {0, 5, 9}。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: expressFloors is the set of floors an express elevator is allowed to serve, such as {0, 5, 9}.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按优先级取出元素的队列，不保证到达顺序或位置顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A priority queue pops elements by priority rather than arrival or positional order.

optionExplanations: 把电梯能力塞进请求类型会让 Request 结构越来越臃肿，跟请求本身语义无关。
换成 priority queue 是给移动排序引入新维度，跟这部电梯只停哪些楼层没关系，还可能打乱 SCAN。
题目要求两种电梯共存，删掉普通电梯会让非快速楼层没人服务。
express 本质是电梯自己的能力限制，加一个标志位并在 addRequest 里校验楼层最贴近这个约束，不用碰 Request。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming elevator capability into the request type would keep bloating Request with concerns unrelated to what a request actually means.
Swapping in a priority queue changes how movement gets ordered, which has nothing to do with which floors one elevator serves, and could disrupt SCAN.
The requirement is for both kinds of elevators to coexist — deleting regular ones leaves non-express floors unserved.
Express is really a capability limit on one elevator, so a flag plus a floor check inside addRequest matches that constraint without touching Request.

scenario: 想支持 priority floors 或 VIP，但仍希望保持平滑扫掠。
scenario_en: You want to support priority floors or VIP riders while keeping smooth SCAN-style movement.
q: 为什么直接用 priority queue 替代 SCAN 有风险？
q_en: Why is replacing SCAN with a priority queue risky?
options: 会打破沿方向扫掠，导致电梯跳来跳去
priority queue 不能存楼层
SCAN 不能处理优先级
VIP 一定不需要电梯
why: 优先级可能让电梯频繁改变方向，损害效率和体验。更稳的是让 dispatch 偏好特定电梯或在局部策略中权衡。
why_en: A priority queue can undermine the smooth sweep behavior that makes SCAN predictable.
options_en: It breaks the one-direction sweep, making the elevator jump around.
A priority queue cannot store floor numbers.
SCAN is fundamentally unable to handle priorities.
VIP passengers would never need an elevator at all.
tradeoff: priority queue 灵活抢占 vs SCAN 平滑扫掠的可预测性

termDefinitions.meaning: 按优先级取出元素的队列，不保证到达顺序或位置顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A priority queue pops elements by priority rather than arrival or positional order.

termDefinitions.fullName: Scan（电梯/磁盘扫描调度算法）
termDefinitions.meaning: SCAN 是沿当前方向持续服务请求、直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法，借用了磁盘调度的思想。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in the current direction serving requests, and only reverses once nothing remains ahead — the same idea used in disk-arm scheduling.

whenOtherWins: 如果需求是紧急呼叫必须抢占普通请求，可以用 priority queue，但要接受折返和饥饿风险。
optionExplanations: 一旦按优先级取请求，电梯可能为了高优先级楼层反复掉头，破坏 SCAN 原本的单向扫掠。
priority queue 存楼层号或 Request 对象都没有技术障碍。
SCAN 本身不排斥优先级，真正的风险在于它会打断扫掠顺序，不是完全不能兼容。
VIP 请求仍然需要坐电梯，只是希望被优先服务，这跟不需要电梯是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Once requests come out by priority, the elevator can reverse repeatedly chasing high-priority floors, breaking SCAN's one-direction sweep.
A priority queue has no trouble storing a floor number or a Request object at all.
SCAN itself isn't incompatible with priority — the real risk is that priority can interrupt the sweep order, not a hard technical block.
VIP riders still need the elevator; they just want to be served sooner, which is a different claim than not needing one at all.

scenario: 用户误按一个目的楼层按钮，想撤销。
scenario_en: A rider accidentally presses a destination floor button and wants to cancel it.
q: 最小扩展是什么？
q_en: What is the minimal extension?
options: 整个 ElevatorController 都要重建
加 removeRequest(request)，从 set 删除
把该电梯全部请求都清空
直接把 direction 强制设成 IDLE
why: 请求集合是电梯状态的事实来源，removeRequest 是 addRequest 的逆操作。step 算法无需大改。
why_en: Canceling a floor request can be the inverse of addRequest by removing it from the request set.
whenOtherWins: 真实电梯通常不允许撤销，因为按钮亮灯给其他乘客承诺了停靠；产品要求决定是否支持。
options_en: Rebuild the entire ElevatorController.
Add removeRequest(request), which deletes it from the set.
Clear every pending request on that elevator.
Force the elevator's direction to IDLE.
tradeoff: removeRequest 逆操作 vs 重建 Controller

termDefinitions.meaning: addRequest 的逆操作，把某个请求从集合中删除。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: removeRequest is the inverse of addRequest — it deletes a request from the set.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

optionExplanations: 撤销一个按钮跟重建整个协调者的职责没有关系，改动范围过大。
requests 集合就是电梯状态的事实来源，加一个对称的 removeRequest 删除对应请求就是最小改动。
清空该电梯全部请求会连累其他乘客已经排队的目的地。
强制回到 IDLE 会让电梯忘掉自己还有其它没撤销的请求。
optionExplanations_en: Undoing one button press has nothing to do with rebuilding the whole coordinator — that's far too broad a change.
The requests set is the source of truth for elevator state, so a symmetric removeRequest that deletes just that entry is the minimal fix.
Clearing every request on that elevator would also wipe out other riders' destinations still waiting in the queue.
Forcing the elevator back to IDLE would make it forget any other requests it still legitimately has.

scenario: 多个 hall call 同时进入，且 step 正在遍历 requests。
scenario_en: Multiple hall calls can arrive while step is iterating through the requests set.
q: 最简单正确的并发方案是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest correct concurrency approach?
options: 只给 getCurrentFloor 这个读方法加锁
允许两个线程同时修改同一个 HashSet
同一把锁包住 requestElevator 和 step
只要把 Request 设计成不可变类就够
why: select+add 和 step 遍历/删除都接触共享状态，必须互斥。简单全局锁正确但并发度低。
why_en: A shared lock around request assignment and stepping prevents concurrent modification and selection races.
whenOtherWins: 更高并发可用线程安全队列收集请求，在每个 tick 开始时由 step drain 到 active set。
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A["requestElevator"] --> L["controller lock"]
  B["step"] --> L
  L --> C["assign or mutate requests"]
  C --> D["consistent elevator state"]
options_en: Only put a lock around the read-only getCurrentFloor.
Let two threads mutate the same HashSet concurrently.
Wrap requestElevator and step with the same lock.
Just make Request an immutable class and stop there.
tradeoff: 全局锁简单正确 vs 并发度低

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥锁，保证同一时刻只有一个线程能进入被保护的代码段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock (mutex) ensures only one thread can enter the protected section at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于哈希表实现的集合，元素遍历顺序不保证稳定。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A HashSet is a hash-table-backed set whose iteration order is not guaranteed to be stable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

codeSample:
requestElevator(floor, type)
    lock.acquire()
    ... select + add ...
    lock.release()

step()
    lock.acquire()
    ... move + remove ...
    lock.release()
optionExplanations: 只给读方法上锁，挡不住选电梯和挪动电梯这些真正的写操作。
两个线程直接改同一个 HashSet 会触发数据竞争或遍历时抛异常。
选电梯这一步和电梯移动这一步都会读写同一份 requests 数据，只要用一把锁把两处调用都包起来，就不会互相踩踏。
让 Request 本身不可变确实有帮助，但 requests 这个集合仍会被并发增删，光靠不可变对象保护不了集合操作。
optionExplanations_en: Locking only a read-only method doesn't protect the actual writes happening in select+add or step.
Letting two threads mutate the same HashSet directly invites data races or iteration exceptions.
Picking an elevator and moving one both end up reading and writing the same requests data, so wrapping both call sites in one lock keeps them from stepping on each other.
Making Request immutable helps, but the requests collection itself is still concurrently added to and removed from, so immutability alone doesn't protect the collection operations.

scenario: 你想避免 hall call 在 step 执行时长时间阻塞。
scenario_en: You want to avoid blocking hall-call threads for the full duration of step.
q: 替代锁的更优雅方案是什么？
q_en: What is the cleaner alternative to locking?
options: 让 Controller 干脆忽略并发请求
每来一个请求就新建一个 Elevator
直接把 requests 这个 set 删掉不用
写入线程安全队列，step 时 drain 到 active set
why: 生产者只碰队列，step 只处理 active set，读写分离减少锁竞争。这个模式适合离散 tick 模拟。
why_en: A thread-safe pending queue lets producers enqueue while the step loop drains into active requests at tick boundaries.
whenOtherWins: 如果实现时间有限或并发很低，单锁方案更容易证明正确。
options_en: Have the controller simply ignore concurrent requests.
Spin up a brand-new Elevator for every incoming request.
Just delete the requests set entirely.
Write into a thread-safe queue and drain it into the active set at the start of each step.
tradeoff: 并发队列读写分离 vs 全局锁实现更简单

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持多线程并发读写且不产生数据竞争的队列，如 Java 的 BlockingQueue。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A thread-safe queue supports concurrent reads and writes without data races, such as Java's BlockingQueue.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥锁，保证同一时刻只有一个线程能进入被保护的代码段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lock (mutex) ensures only one thread can enter the protected section at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

optionExplanations: 忽略并发请求会直接丢单，用户的 hall call 会消失。
每个请求都新建电梯会让电梯数量无限膨胀，跟固定 3 部电梯的题设矛盾。
删掉 requests 集合，step 就没有事实来源可读，整个状态机会失效。
生产者只写入线程安全队列，step 开始时统一 drain 到 active set 处理，读写分离让锁竞争降到最低。
optionExplanations_en: Ignoring concurrent requests just drops them silently — a rider's hall call would vanish.
Spinning up a new elevator per request makes the fleet grow without bound, contradicting the fixed-three-elevator setup.
Deleting the requests set leaves step with no source of truth to read, and the whole state machine stops working.
Producers just write into a thread-safe queue, and step drains it into the active set once at the start of each tick, separating reads from writes to minimize contention.

q: Elevator.step 必须处理哪些细节？（多选）
q_en: Which details must Elevator.step handle? (Select all that apply)
options: 无请求则 IDLE
IDLE 有请求时确定初始方向
停靠后本 tick 不移动
前方无请求时反向
why: 这些 edge cases 决定模拟是否稳定。漏掉任一项都可能导致漂移、不可复现或跳过停靠。
why_en: The step method must handle idle, initial direction, stop ticks, and reversal explicitly.
options_en: Go IDLE when there are no requests.
Pick an initial direction when IDLE but requests exist.
Do not move on the same tick it stops.
Reverse when nothing remains ahead in the current direction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

optionExplanations: 漏了这一步，电梯没请求时会继续沿旧方向漂移，永远不停。
静止但有新请求时不显式选方向，第一步该往哪走就没有依据。
不显式 return 会让电梯在停靠的同一 tick 又移动一层，行为不自然。
前方清空却不反向，电梯会卡死在一端，永远接不到反方向的请求。
optionExplanations_en: Skip this and an elevator with no requests keeps drifting in its old direction forever.
Without explicitly picking a direction when idle but requests exist, there's no basis for which way the first move should go.
Without an explicit return, the elevator would move one more floor on the same tick it just stopped — an unnatural double action.
Failing to reverse once nothing remains ahead strands the elevator at one end, never able to serve the opposite direction.

q: 补全 Elevator 构造初始状态：
q_en: Fill in the initial state constructed for each Elevator:
text: 每部电梯初始在 {{0}} 楼，direction 为 {{IDLE}}，requests 是 {{空集合}}。
why: 题目给出固定 3 部电梯服务 0-9 层，构造时统一从 ground floor 开始。
why_en: Each elevator starts at floor zero, idle, with no pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

q: Controller 立即派发 hall call 而不是维护 pending 队列的取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the tradeoff of dispatching hall calls immediately instead of keeping a pending queue?
options: 更简单，但忙时不如队列灵活重派
一定比排队模型更公平地服务乘客
根本无法同时处理多个请求
必须依赖数据库才能实现
why: 立即派发让 Controller 状态少，只存 elevators。队列模型可在电梯空闲时重新选择，但实现更复杂。
why_en: Immediate dispatch keeps the controller simple, while a controller queue enables more flexible scheduling.
options_en: Simpler to build, but less flexible than a queue for re-dispatching when elevators are busy.
It is always fairer to passengers than a queuing model.
It cannot handle more than one request at a time.
It requires a database to work at all.
tradeoff: 立即派发实现简单 vs 忙时无法重新调度

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

optionExplanations: 把 hall call 直接分给一部电梯，Controller 只用记着 elevators 这一份状态，代价是电梯都忙时没法回头重新分配。
公平与否取决于调度策略本身，不是立即派发这个动作天然带来的，不能一概而论。
多个 hall call 依然可以逐个立即派发到不同电梯的队列，并不受限于同时只能处理一个。
这套设计完全可以用内存里的 elevators 列表实现，不需要数据库参与。
optionExplanations_en: Dispatching immediately means the controller only tracks the elevator list, simple to build, but it can't reconsider a bad pick once every elevator is already busy.
Fairness depends on the actual dispatch policy, not something that automatically comes from dispatching immediately — it's not a given.
Multiple hall calls can still be dispatched immediately, one after another, into different elevators' own queues, not limited to handling one at a time.
This whole design runs fine off an in-memory elevator list — a database isn't required at all.

scenario: 公司要把同一套电梯软件部署到不同建筑，有的重视等待时间，有的重视能耗。
scenario_en: The same elevator software will run in different buildings; some optimize wait time, others optimize energy.
q: 调度算法应如何扩展？
q_en: How should the dispatch algorithm be extended?
options: 给每栋建筑各复制一份 Controller 代码
抽出 SchedulingStrategy 接口供 Controller 组合
让 Elevator 自己猜测所在建筑类型
把 RequestType 直接改成字符串类型
why: 当选择电梯的策略确实要替换时，Strategy 才有价值。基础题不用先抽象。
why_en: Scheduling strategy becomes useful when different buildings genuinely need swappable dispatch policies.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有一种简单调度规则，直接写在 Controller 中更清楚。
options_en: Duplicate a whole copy of the Controller for every building.
Extract a SchedulingStrategy interface that the controller composes.
Have each Elevator guess what kind of building it's in.
Change RequestType into a plain string.
tradeoff: Strategy 接口可替换 vs 基础题直接写死

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可替换的算法各自封装成同一接口的实现，运行时可切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern wraps interchangeable algorithms behind one common interface that can be swapped at runtime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 调度函数，按某种策略从多部电梯中选出最合适的一部。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: selectBestElevator is the dispatch function that picks the best elevator under a chosen strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

optionExplanations: 复制代码会让维护成本随建筑数量线性增长，每次改一处逻辑都要同步改所有副本。
把调度算法抽成 SchedulingStrategy 接口，让 Controller 组合持有，能在运行时换算法而不改 Controller 本身。
单部电梯拿不到、也不该拿到所在建筑类型这种全局信息，这是 Controller 层的事。
把枚举改成字符串会丢掉编译期类型安全，跟策略可替换性完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Duplicating the code makes maintenance cost grow with every building — one logic change now has to be repeated in every copy.
Extracting a SchedulingStrategy interface that the controller composes lets the algorithm be swapped at runtime without touching the controller itself.
A single elevator has no business knowing, or needing to know, which kind of building it's in — that's controller-level information.
Turning the enum into a plain string throws away compile-time type safety and has nothing to do with making the strategy swappable.

scenario: 电梯反向后当前楼层正好有反方向 pickup。
scenario_en: After an elevator reverses, the current floor may now have a pickup matching the new direction.
q: 为什么反向时 return，下一 tick 再检查停靠？
q_en: Why return after reversing and check stopping on the next tick?
options: 因为反向会让 requests 自动清空
因为反向这一步必须顺带移动一层
让新方向 shouldStopHere 能正确匹配
因为反向后 currentFloor 变得不可信
why: 反向改变了 pickupType。下一 tick 重新执行停靠检查，能服务当前楼层的反方向请求。
why_en: Returning after reversal lets the next tick evaluate stops at the same floor under the new direction.
options_en: Because reversing automatically empties the requests set.
Because reversing must also move the elevator one floor.
So the newly reversed direction's stop check can correctly match requests at the same floor.
Because currentFloor becomes untrustworthy after reversing.
tradeoff: 反向后 return 等下一 tick vs 同 tick 立即检查停靠

termDefinitions.meaning: 判断电梯是否该在当前楼层停靠的检查，只认同方向 pickup 或 destination。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: shouldStopHere decides whether to stop at the current floor, honoring only same-direction pickups or destinations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

whenOtherWins: 如果把停靠检查和反向检查合并成一次 tick 内的多步状态机，也能得到同样结果，但实现和调试都更复杂。
optionExplanations: 反向只是改变 direction 字段，requests 集合完全不受影响。
代码里反向后直接 return，明确不在同一 tick 里移动。
反向之后 pickupType 的含义也跟着变了，下一 tick 用新方向重新跑一次停靠检查，才能接住当前楼层刚好符合新方向的乘客。
currentFloor 是独立字段，反向不会让它变得不可靠。
optionExplanations_en: Reversing only flips the direction field — the requests set is completely unaffected.
The code returns right after reversing, deliberately not moving on that same tick.
Reversing flips what pickupType means, so the very next tick has to redo the stop check with the fresh direction — that's how it catches a rider at this floor who now matches.
currentFloor is an independent field; reversing direction doesn't make it any less trustworthy.

scenario: 仿真调用 controller.step()。
scenario_en: The simulation advances by calling controller.step().
q: Controller.step 应该做什么？
q_en: What should Controller.step do?
options: 重新构造所有电梯
自己移动所有电梯楼层并删除请求
只调度新请求不推进时间
遍历每部电梯调用 e.step()
why: Controller 推进整体时间，但运动细节由每个 Elevator 封装。这样 Controller 不需要知道 SCAN 的内部状态。
why_en: Controller.step advances time by asking each elevator to step itself.
options_en: Reconstruct every elevator from scratch.
Move every elevator's floor and remove requests itself.
Only dispatch new requests without advancing time.
Loop through every elevator and call e.step().
tradeoff: Controller 只推进时间 vs 直接操控电梯内部状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 推进仿真一个离散时间单位的方法调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: step() advances the discrete-time simulation by one tick.

whenOtherWins: 如果需要跨电梯的全局约束（比如统一限速或动画帧同步），Controller 可以在遍历时附加逻辑，但单部电梯的移动算法仍应留在 Elevator.step 内部。
optionExplanations: 每 tick 重建电梯会丢掉它们当前的楼层、方向和请求这些运行状态。
让 Controller 亲自改楼层和删请求，会把本该封装在 Elevator 内部的移动细节泄漏出来。
只调度不推进时间，仿真的时钟就永远不会往前走。
Controller 只负责推进整体时间，具体怎么走、停、反向都交给每部电梯自己的 step 处理。
optionExplanations_en: Rebuilding every elevator each tick would throw away their live floor, direction, and request state.
Having the controller directly change floors and remove requests leaks movement details that should stay encapsulated inside Elevator.
Dispatching without advancing time would leave the simulation clock stuck forever.
The controller's job is just to advance overall time, leaving how each elevator moves, stops, or reverses to its own step method.

q: 按顺序排列 Elevator 设计主链路：
q_en: Order the main design path for the Elevator problem:
steps: Request 保存 floor 和 PICKUP_UP/PICKUP_DOWN/DESTINATION。
澄清固定 3 部电梯、10 层、离散 tick、无门控。
Elevator 用 SCAN 在当前方向扫掠请求。
Controller 负责接收 hall call 并选择电梯。
step 区分 travel-any-request 和 stop-matching-direction。
why: 这题先定仿真边界，再区分协调者和单电梯，再用 Request 类型支撑正确移动。
why_en: The design chain moves from simulation scope to controller dispatch, typed requests, SCAN movement, and direction-aware stopping.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["scope requirements"] --> B["model Request"]
  B --> C["assign via Controller"]
  C --> D["Elevator.step"]
  D --> E["SCAN movement"]
  E --> F["validate invariants"]
tradeoff: 先框需求范围 vs 先写调度算法

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装一次停靠请求的类，包含楼层号和请求类型两个字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Request object bundles a floor number together with a request type.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求类型枚举，取值为 PICKUP_UP、PICKUP_DOWN 或 DESTINATION。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RequestType is an enum whose values are PICKUP_UP, PICKUP_DOWN, or DESTINATION.

termDefinitions.fullName: Scan（电梯/磁盘扫描调度算法）
termDefinitions.meaning: SCAN 是沿当前方向持续服务请求、直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法，借用了磁盘调度的思想。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in the current direction serving requests, and only reverses once nothing remains ahead — the same idea used in disk-arm scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

q: Senior 级回答应该主动说明哪些点？（多选）
q_en: Which points should a senior-level answer call out? (Select all that apply)
options: floor-only requests 的方向问题
nearest dispatch 的局限和 request-aware 改进
SCAN step 的停靠/反向 edge cases
并发 hall calls 的锁或队列方案
why: 高级答案要能覆盖状态建模、调度权衡、移动算法和并发风险。只写基本类不够。
why_en: Senior answers discuss request typing, dispatch limits, SCAN edge cases, and concurrent hall-call handling.
options_en: The direction problem with floor-only requests.
The limits of nearest dispatch and the request-aware improvement.
SCAN step's stop/reverse edge cases.
Lock or queue solutions for concurrent hall calls.

termDefinitions.fullName: Scan（电梯/磁盘扫描调度算法）
termDefinitions.meaning: SCAN 是沿当前方向持续服务请求、直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法，借用了磁盘调度的思想。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in the current direction serving requests, and only reverses once nothing remains ahead — the same idea used in disk-arm scheduling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 楼层外呼叫按钮发出的请求，必须带上行或下行方向。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hall call is a request from a floor button, and it always carries an up or down direction.

optionExplanations: 说明白只存楼层号会丢掉方向，证明候选人理解请求身份建模。
主动指出 nearest 会派错方向的电梯，并给出 request-aware 的改进，展示从能跑到正确的推进过程。
讲清停靠占一个 tick、反向后要重新判断停靠，说明状态机边界考虑周全。
主动提出锁或队列方案，说明候选人想到了真实系统里请求会并发到达。
optionExplanations_en: Calling out that storing bare floor numbers loses direction shows the candidate understands request-identity modeling.
Proactively flagging nearest dispatch's failure mode and proposing the request-aware fix shows the progression from working to correct.
Explaining that a stop consumes a tick and a reversal needs a fresh stop check next tick shows careful state-machine boundary thinking.
Raising a lock or queue solution on their own shows the candidate anticipated concurrent requests in a real system.

scenario: 你要总结 Elevator.step 的核心不变量。
scenario_en: You need to summarize the core invariant of Elevator.step.
q: 哪个不变量最准确？
q_en: Which invariant is the most accurate?
options: 每 tick 最多一种动作：停靠/反向/移动/idle
每个 tick 都必须移动整整一层
每个请求进来都必须立刻被服务
电梯的方向永远保持不变
why: 离散模拟的清晰性来自每 tick 单动作。停靠和反向都不应再同 tick 移动。
why_en: A clear tick model lets an elevator do at most one action per step: stop, reverse, move one floor, or idle.
whenOtherWins: 如果仿真粒度更细，可把开门、关门、移动拆成更多状态。
options_en: Each tick performs at most one action: stop, reverse, move one floor, or idle.
Every tick must move the elevator exactly one floor.
Every incoming request must be served immediately.
The elevator's direction never changes.
tradeoff: 每 tick 单动作的清晰性 vs 一 tick 内多动作的复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯当前没有任何请求、原地静止的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IDLE means the elevator has no pending requests and stays still.

optionExplanations: 每个 tick 只做停靠、反向、移动或 idle 里的一件事，这个约束让整套模拟行为清晰、可推理。
停靠或反向的那个 tick 就不移动，每 tick 必须移动一层的说法跟代码实际行为矛盾。
请求进来后先排队等待电梯经过，不是立刻被服务，这不符合调度模型。
方向恰恰会随请求变化而反向，说它永远不变是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Each tick does exactly one of stop, reverse, move-one-floor, or idle — that single-action constraint is what keeps the whole simulation reasoning clear.
A tick spent stopping or reversing doesn't move at all, so claiming every tick must advance a floor contradicts the actual code.
An incoming request waits in the queue until an elevator passes it, not served the instant it arrives — that doesn't match the dispatch model.
Direction is exactly what flips as requests change; claiming it never changes is simply false.

q: 中级候选人在本题最应稳定实现哪部分？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate implement reliably in this problem?
options: 完整真实电梯硬件控制
继续当前方向直到前方无请求再反向的状态机
分布式调度协议
乘客重量传感器
why: 中级重点是正确的 UP/DOWN/IDLE 转换、停靠不移动、请求清空转 idle。硬件细节不在范围内。
why_en: The expected mid-level core is a correct directional state machine for elevator movement.
options_en: Full real elevator hardware control.
A state machine that keeps its direction until nothing remains ahead, then reverses.
A distributed dispatch protocol.
Passenger weight sensors.
tradeoff: 中级：方向状态机 vs 高级功能（硬件/分布式）

termDefinitions.meaning: 电梯运动方向枚举，取值为 UP、DOWN 或 IDLE。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Direction is an enum whose values are UP, DOWN, or IDLE.

termDefinitions.fullName: Scan（电梯/磁盘扫描调度算法）
termDefinitions.meaning: SCAN 是沿当前方向持续服务请求、直到前方没有请求才反向的调度算法，借用了磁盘调度的思想。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SCAN keeps moving in the current direction serving requests, and only reverses once nothing remains ahead — the same idea used in disk-arm scheduling.

optionExplanations: 真实硬件控制超出了这道软件模拟题的范围，不是候选人要证明的能力。
候选人要把方向在 UP、DOWN 和 IDLE 之间怎么切换、什么时候不该移动、请求清空后怎么归位这套逻辑做对，这是这道题最基本也最该稳的部分。
这是单机 LLD 题，分布式调度协议属于更高阶的系统设计范畴。
载重和传感器属于硬件安全层，题目明确排除，不该在这里实现。
optionExplanations_en: Full real hardware control is outside this software-simulation problem's scope — it's not what the candidate needs to prove.
Getting the UP/DOWN/IDLE transitions right, not moving on a stop tick, and going idle once requests clear is the most basic thing this problem asks a candidate to nail.
This is a single-machine LLD problem — a distributed dispatch protocol belongs to a higher-level system-design question.
Weight sensors sit in the hardware-safety layer that this problem explicitly excludes; they shouldn't show up here.

scenario: 有人想让 Controller 直接读写每部电梯的 requests set 来实现移动。
scenario_en: Someone wants Controller to read and mutate each elevator requests set directly to implement movement.
q: 为什么不推荐？
q_en: Why is this design not recommended?
options: requests 不能删除
Controller 没有 elevators 列表
移动规则是单部电梯内部行为，应封装在 Elevator.step
Elevator 不应保存 currentFloor
why: Controller 的职责是协调和推进，不应知道电梯如何停靠、反向和移动。封装让移动算法可单独测试和替换。
why_en: Elevator.step should encapsulate movement rules so the controller stays a coordinator.
options_en: Requests inside the set cannot be removed.
The controller doesn't actually have a list of elevators.
Movement rules are a single elevator's internal behavior and belong inside Elevator.step.
Elevator should not store currentFloor at all.
tradeoff: 移动逻辑封装在 Elevator vs Controller 直接读写电梯状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表单部电梯的类，维护自己的楼层、方向和请求集合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An Elevator instance tracks its own current floor, direction, and set of pending requests.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负责协调多部电梯、接收 hall call 并派发电梯的中枢类，不了解电梯内部移动细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The ElevatorController is the coordinator that receives hall calls and decides which elevator to dispatch, without knowing each elevator's internal movement logic.

whenOtherWins: 如果未来要支持跨进程的分布式电梯集群，可能需要一个中间协调层读写共享状态，但单机设计里移动逻辑仍应封装在 Elevator。
optionExplanations: Set 里的元素完全可以删除，停靠动作本身就是一次 remove。
Controller 通常持有整个 fleet 列表，这不是它缺少的信息。
怎么停靠、反向、移动是单部电梯的内部行为，应该封装在 Elevator.step 里，让移动算法能单独测试和替换。
currentFloor 恰恰是 Elevator 最核心的一块状态，不存它电梯就不知道自己在哪。
optionExplanations_en: Elements in the set can absolutely be removed — a stop is literally a remove operation.
The controller typically holds the whole fleet list already, so that isn't information it's missing.
How to stop, reverse, and move is a single elevator's internal behavior that belongs inside Elevator.step, so the movement algorithm can be tested and swapped independently.
currentFloor is exactly the core piece of state an elevator needs — without it, it wouldn't know where it is.

scenario: 面试官说：设计一个支持创建文件/目录、路径导航和基本文件操作的内存文件系统，只保留单根目录树。
q: 这个内存文件系统的基础能力包含哪些？（多选）
options: 单根目录的层级树
文件存储字符串内容
创建、删除、列出、重命名、移动文件或文件夹
支持相对路径、权限、持久化和符号链接
why: 范围是内存中的单根绝对路径树：创建、删除、列出、重命名、移动加内容存储。相对路径、权限、持久化、符号链接都被面试官明确排除。
why_en: The base file system is an in-memory, single-root, absolute-path tree with string content plus five core mutation operations.
options_en: A hierarchical tree under a single root.
Files store string content.
Create, delete, list, rename, and move files or folders.
Support relative paths, permissions, persistence, and symlinks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从根目录 / 开始书写的完整路径，如 /home/user/notes.txt。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An absolute path is a full path written from the root, such as /home/user/notes.txt.

q_en: Which base capabilities does this in-memory file system support? (multi-select)
scenario_en: The interviewer says: design an in-memory file system that supports creating files/folders, path navigation, and basic file operations, keeping just a single-root tree.
optionExplanations: 单根树是这套内存文件系统的骨架，后续所有路径都从这一个 root 出发解析。
文件不区分类型，统一按字符串存内容，省去序列化和类型系统的复杂度。
这五个操作对应最终需求清单，是这版实现必须跑通的最小操作集。
这四项每个都单独被面试官划出范围，实现里不用为它们预留接口。
optionExplanations_en: The single root gives this in-memory tree one entry point that every path resolves from.
Files skip type distinctions and just hold string content, avoiding serialization overhead.
These five operations are the minimum command set this version has to support end to end.
Each of these four was explicitly carved out by the interviewer, so there's no need to design for them here.

scenario: 需求中反复出现 /home/user/docs 这类路径。
q: Path 应该如何建模？
options: 作为独立实体，自己保存全局状态和子节点列表
定义成 Folder 的子类类型
字符串输入，由 FileSystem 解析
定义成 File 的父类类型
why: 路径是定位输入，不拥有生命周期或可变状态；把解析逻辑集中在 FileSystem helper 里就够。
why_en: Path is just an input string to resolve, not a domain entity with its own state.
tradeoff: Path 作为无状态输入字符串 vs 独立 Path/Resolver 实体
whenOtherWins: 如果支持相对路径、规范化、符号链接、挂载点和权限检查，Path/Resolver 可能值得独立建模。
options_en: A standalone entity that holds its own global state and list of children.
Defined as a subclass of Folder.
A string input that FileSystem resolves.
Defined as a superclass of File.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标识树中某个位置的字符串，例如 /home/user/docs。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A path is a string that identifies a location in the tree, such as /home/user/docs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 持有 root 并对外提供路径 API 的入口类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FileSystem is the entry-point class that owns the root and exposes the path-based API.

q_en: How should Path be modeled?
scenario_en: The requirements repeatedly reference paths like /home/user/docs.
optionExplanations: 把 Path 做成有状态的实体会引入生命周期管理，但这里连规范化都不需要，纯属过度设计。
路径和文件夹是两种不同的概念，硬塞进 Folder 继承体系会让类型语义变乱。
路径只是定位输入，交给 FileSystem 统一解析成 parent+name，不用为它单独建模。
File 不该从一个字符串概念派生，这个继承方向在语义上说不通。

A path and a folder are different concepts, so wedging Path under Folder's hierarchy corrupts the type semantics.

为了完全替代 Folder 和 File 这两个类

why_en: FileSystem acts as a facade over root navigation, centralizing path parsing behind one public API.

whenOtherWins: 如果 API 只面向已持有 Folder 引用的内部代码，直接操作 Folder 也可以；但用户级路径 API 需要 facade。

Because FileSystem stores every file's content.
To fully replace both Folder and File as classes.

q_en: Why do we need a FileSystem class?
scenario_en: A caller wants to call createFile('/home/user/notes.txt','hi') without manually navigating from root.
optionExplanations: Folder 本来就能通过 addChild 装 File，这从来不是引入 FileSystem 的原因。
内容其实存在 File.content 上，FileSystem 并不代管每个文件的字节。
Folder 和 File 仍然各司其职，FileSystem 只是在它们之上加一层编排，不是替代品。
FileSystem 拥有 root，把路径拆分和逐级导航都收在一个入口，调用方只用记一个 API。
optionExplanations_en: Folder can already hold File via addChild, so that was never the reason FileSystem exists.
Content actually lives on File.content — FileSystem doesn't stash every file's bytes itself.
Folder and File still keep their own jobs; FileSystem just orchestrates on top, it doesn't replace them.
FileSystem owns root and folds path-splitting and step-by-step navigation into one entry point, so callers only need one API.

optionExplanations: FileSystem 是持有 root 并对外暴露公共 API 的入口类，属于最终类型清单。

q: FileSystemEntry 抽象解决了什么问题？
options: 它让 File 也能像 Folder 一样包含并管理子节点
File/Folder 共享字段与方法，children 需统一类型
它替代了 FileSystem 里的路径解析器，不再需要 resolvePath
它负责对每个文件的内容做全文关键词搜索和索引

tradeoff: 共享基类统一身份 vs 各自独立类型省去继承耦合
options_en: It lets File contain and manage children like Folder does.
File/Folder share fields and methods, and children need one shared type.
It replaces FileSystem's path resolver, so resolvePath is no longer needed.
It handles full-text keyword search and indexing over every file's content.

termDefinitions.meaning: File 和 Folder 共同的抽象基类，封装 name/parent/getPath。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FileSystemEntry is the shared abstract base class holding name, parent, and getPath for both files and folders.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来区分一个 entry 是文件夹还是文件的方法。

q_en: What problem does the FileSystemEntry abstraction solve?
scenario_en: File and Folder each implement almost identical name, parent, getPath, and isDirectory, and the duplication is obvious.
optionExplanations: File 依然是叶子节点，这个抽象并不会给它加上管理子节点的能力。
File 和 Folder 共享 name/parent/getPath 等字段方法，抽出基类还能让 children 用统一类型存两种节点。
路径解析仍是 FileSystem.resolvePath 的职责，这个抽象跟它无关。
全文搜索是完全独立的功能扩展，跟节点身份抽象没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: File stays a leaf — this abstraction doesn't give it any child-managing power.
File and Folder share fields like name/parent/getPath, and the shared base also lets children hold one uniform type covering both.
Path resolution still belongs to FileSystem.resolvePath — this abstraction has nothing to do with it.
Full-text search is a completely separate extension, unrelated to node identity.

scenario: File 和 Folder 都稳定共享 name、parent、getPath 行为。
q: 为什么 abstract class 比只有 interface 更合适？
options: 能共享字段和 getPath 实现，interface 只有契约
interface 类型本身不能被任何具体类实现
abstract class 具备自动持久化到磁盘的能力
Folder 作为容器不需要任何多态行为
why: 这里共享的不只是方法名，还有稳定实现；继承在真实 is-a 关系且共享行为稳定时是合理选择。
why_en: An abstract class is justified because File and Folder share stable state and behavior, not just a method contract.
tradeoff: 共享实现的 abstract class vs 只共享契约的 interface
whenOtherWins: 如果语言偏组合，或两者只共享很少契约，interface 加工具函数也可以。
options_en: It can share fields and the getPath implementation, while an interface only has a contract.
An interface type itself cannot be implemented by any concrete class.
An abstract class can automatically persist data to disk.
Folder as a container needs no polymorphic behavior at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以包含共享字段和默认实现、但不能直接实例化的类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract class can hold shared fields and default implementations but cannot be instantiated directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只定义方法契约、不提供共享实现的类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface defines a method contract without providing shared implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用统一类型引用不同子类对象，并调用各自实现的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polymorphism lets code refer to different subclass objects through one shared type and call their own implementations.

q_en: Why is an abstract class a better fit here than a plain interface?
scenario_en: File and Folder both stably share name, parent, and getPath behavior.
optionExplanations: File 和 Folder 能直接继承 getPath 等方法实现，不用各自重写一遍，这正是选 abstract class 的理由。
interface 本来就是设计给具体类实现的，这个说法本身就站不住。
抽象类和磁盘持久化毫无关系，这版设计连磁盘都不涉及。
children: Map<string, FileSystemEntry> 正靠多态把 File/Folder 当同一类型处理。
optionExplanations_en: File and Folder can inherit getPath's real implementation instead of each rewriting it — that's the actual case for an abstract class.
An interface exists precisely to be implemented by concrete classes, so this claim doesn't hold up.
An abstract class has nothing to do with disk persistence — this design doesn't even touch disk.
children: Map<string, FileSystemEntry> relies on polymorphism to treat File and Folder as one type.

scenario: 需要从任意 File 或 Folder 引用得到完整路径，并支持 rename/move。
q: 为什么优先存 parent 指针而不是每个 entry 存 full path 字符串？
options: getPath 无论树多深都必须保持 O(1) 常数时间
parent 指针除了定位还能自动搜索文件内容
rename/move 只改 name/parent，路径按需计算
full path 字符串无法正确显示中文文件名
why: 存 full path 会让重命名大目录时必须更新所有后代路径；parent 指针把 rename/move 降为局部更新，getPath 付出 O(depth)。
why_en: Parent pointers avoid cascading path updates on rename or move, trading O(1) getPath for O(depth).
tradeoff: parent 指针的局部更新 vs full path 字符串的级联更新
whenOtherWins: 如果几乎只读路径且很少 move/rename，可缓存路径字符串，但要有失效策略。
options_en: getPath must stay O(1) no matter how deep the tree is.
Parent pointers can also automatically search file content.
Rename/move only changes name/parent; the path is computed on demand.
Full path strings cannot correctly display Chinese file names.

termDefinitions.meaning: 子节点保存的指向父节点的引用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A parent pointer is the reference a child node keeps back to its parent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时随树的深度增长，而不是随节点总数增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(depth) means the operation's cost grows with the tree's depth, not with the total number of nodes.

q_en: Why store a parent pointer instead of a full path string on every entry?
scenario_en: You need to compute the full path from any File or Folder reference, and support rename/move.
optionExplanations: getPath 用 parent 指针其实是 O(depth) 而非 O(1)，这不是这里权衡的目标。
parent 指针只负责定位和导航，不做任何内容层面的搜索。
重命名或移动时只需要改这一个 entry 的 name/parent，getPath 再按需要往上拼一次。
路径字符串本身跟字符集无关，这不是工程上真实存在的限制。
optionExplanations_en: getPath over parent pointers is actually O(depth), not O(1) — that's not the tradeoff being made here.
Parent pointers only handle locating and navigating, never any content-level search.
Rename or move only touches that one entry's name/parent, and getPath just walks up on demand afterward.
A path string's encoding has nothing to do with the character set — that's not a real engineering constraint.

q: 按顺序排列存 full path 字符串导致的问题：
steps: 如果 /home 被重命名为 /house，所有后代路径前缀都变了。
每个 entry 持有自己的 path 字符串。
必须遍历整个子树更新每个 path。
一次 rename/move 从局部操作变成 O(descendants)。
why: 这就是 parent 指针方案胜出的主要理由：深层目录下路径字符串冗余会让简单操作变复杂。
why_en: Storing full paths on every entry turns a folder rename or move into a cascading update across all descendants.
tradeoff: 存 full path 读取简单 vs parent 指针写入简单但读取要递归

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 entry 自己保存的完整路径字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A full path is the complete path string stored directly on each entry.

termDefinitions.meaning: 某个节点子树下所有更深层的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A descendant is any node deeper in the subtree rooted at a given node.

q: Folder.children 为什么用 Map<string, FileSystemEntry> 而不是 List？
options: List<FileSystemEntry> 完全不能保存任何多态对象
Map 在按名查找时会自动递归搜索整个子树
List 结构本身无法列出文件夹里的内容
Map 用 O(1) 按名查找子节点，并天然保证同目录唯一名
why: 路径解析每一级都要按名称查子节点；Map 同时提升查询效率，并把'同一文件夹内名称唯一'变成数据结构约束。
why_en: A map keyed by child name gives O(1) path-resolution lookups and enforces unique names within a folder.
tradeoff: Map 的 O(1) 查找+天然唯一名 vs List 的顺序但 O(n) 扫描
options_en: List<FileSystemEntry> cannot hold any polymorphic objects at all.
A map automatically recurses into the whole subtree when looking up by name.
A list structure itself cannot list a folder's contents.
A map gives O(1) lookup by name and naturally enforces unique names per folder.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以子节点名称为 key、entry 为 value 的哈希表。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Map<string, FileSystemEntry> is a hash table keyed by child name with the entry as the value.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时不随数据规模增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(1) means the operation's time does not grow as the data size grows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时随元素数量 n 线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(n) means the operation's time grows linearly with the number n of elements.

q_en: Why does Folder.children use Map<string, FileSystemEntry> instead of a List?
scenario_en: Folder needs to quickly locate a child by name while guaranteeing no duplicate names within one folder.
optionExplanations: List 完全能装任意类型的对象，这个限制本身就是编造的。
Map 只做单层 key 查找，并不会自动往子树里递归。
List 本身完全能枚举出文件夹内容，这不是选 Map 的理由。
Map 按名字 O(1) 查子节点，还顺带让重名冲突变成插入时就能检测到的结构约束。
optionExplanations_en: A list can hold any object type just fine — this restriction is simply made up.
A map only does one-level key lookup; it never auto-recurses into a subtree.
A list can enumerate a folder's contents perfectly well, so that's not the reason to pick a map.
A map gives O(1) lookup by name and turns duplicate names into something caught at insert time.

scenario: FileSystem 是唯一入口，所有操作都通过它的公共方法完成。
q: FileSystem 的公共 API 通常包括哪些？（多选）

createFolder(path)
delete(path)

get(path)
rename(path,newName)

why_en: The FileSystem public API maps directly to create, delete, list, get, rename, and move — permissions stay out of scope.
options_en: createFile(path, content)
createFolder(path)
delete(path)
list(path)
get(path)

q_en: What does FileSystem's public API typically include? (multi-select)
scenario_en: FileSystem is the single entry point; every operation goes through its public methods.
optionExplanations: 对应'创建文件并写入初始内容'这个需求，是最基础的写操作。
对应'创建空目录'需求，内部走一次 resolvePath+addChild。
对应删除需求，默认让整个子树跟着消失。
对应列出目录需求，只对文件夹有意义。
对应按路径直接取到某个 entry 的需求，不管是文件还是文件夹。
对应改名需求，要同步维护 parent map 里的 key。

权限管理被面试官明确划出这版范围，公共 API 不用留这个方法。
optionExplanations_en: Covers the 'create a file with initial content' requirement — the most basic write op.
Covers 'create an empty folder,' internally doing one resolvePath plus addChild.
Covers delete, and by default the whole subtree disappears with it.
Covers listing a directory's contents — only meaningful for folders.
Covers fetching an entry directly by path, whether it's a file or a folder.
Covers renaming, which has to keep the key in the parent map in sync.
Covers move, which updates both the source and destination parent together.
Permission management was explicitly scoped out by the interviewer, so the public API skips this method.

scenario: 调用 createFile('/home/user/notes.txt','hello')。
q: 正确高层步骤是什么？
options: 把整条完整路径当 key 直接存进 root.children
解析 parent 和 name，查重名后创建并挂载
自动帮用户先创建所有缺失的中间目录
把文件内容错误地写到 Folder.content 字段
why: createFile 不自动创建中间目录，也不能覆盖同名 entry；parent.addChild 负责维护 parent 指针。
why_en: createFile resolves the parent, checks for a name collision, creates a File, and adds it to the parent folder.
tradeoff: createFile 要求父目录已存在 vs mkdir -p 式自动建目录
whenOtherWins: 如果需求是 mkdir -p 或 createFile 自动建父目录，需要显式扩展 API 语义。
options_en: Use the entire full path directly as the key in root.children.
Resolve the parent and name, check for a collision, then create and attach it.
Automatically create every missing intermediate directory first.
Mistakenly write the file's content onto Folder.content.

termDefinitions.meaning: Folder 用来加入子节点并同步设置 parent 指针的方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: addChild is the Folder method that inserts a child and sets its parent pointer.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一文件夹下已经存在同名 entry 的冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A name collision means an entry with the same name already exists in that folder.

q_en: What are the correct high-level steps?
scenario_en: Calling createFile('/home/user/notes.txt','hello').
optionExplanations: 这样会把树结构压扁成一层，getChild 逐级查找立刻失效。
先解析出父目录和文件名，查有没有重名，再创建 File 挂到 parent 上。
createFile 默认不做 mkdir -p，中间目录缺失应该直接抛错，不是自动补全。
Folder 没有 content 字段，内容只属于 File。
optionExplanations_en: That flattens the tree into one layer, and getChild's step-by-step lookup breaks immediately.
Resolve the parent folder and name, check for a name collision, then create the File and attach it to the parent.
createFile doesn't do mkdir -p by default — a missing intermediate directory should throw, not get auto-created.
Folder has no content field at all; content only belongs to File.

scenario: 调用 createFile('/') 或 createFolder('/')。
q: 应该如何处理？
options: 拒绝；根目录已存在且不能被创建成文件
把 root 替换成新文件
创建名为空字符串的 child
忽略并返回 null
why: 根是唯一入口，不能作为新文件创建，也不应被覆盖；createFolder('/') 可视为 AlreadyExists。
why_en: The root path is a special existing folder and cannot be created as a file or recreated.
tradeoff: 对根目录抛出明确异常 vs 静默忽略或覆盖根节点
whenOtherWins: 如果需求允许 touch / 式幂等创建（已存在就直接返回而不报错），可以把这里的异常改成静默成功。
options_en: Reject; the root already exists and cannot be created as a file.
Replace root with the new file.
Create a child with an empty-string name.
Ignore the call and return null.

termDefinitions.meaning: 表示目标位置已经存在同名 entry 的异常类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AlreadyExistsException signals that an entry already exists at the target location.

q_en: How should this be handled?
scenario_en: Calling createFile('/') or createFolder('/').
optionExplanations: 根已经存在且是唯一入口，抛 AlreadyExistsException 比其他处理都清楚。
替换 root 会让所有已解析出的路径瞬间全部失效，风险太大。
空字符串不是一个合法的路径组件，不该被当成正常子节点名。
静默返回 null 会让调用方分不清是失败还是真的创建了空东西。
optionExplanations_en: Root already exists as the one entry point, so throwing an AlreadyExistsException is the clearest response.
Replacing root would instantly invalidate every path anyone has already resolved — way too risky.

    if path == null || !path.startsWith('/') throw InvalidPath
    if path == '/' return root
    parts = path.substring(1).split('/')
    current = root
    for part in parts

        if !current.isDirectory() throw NotADirectory
        current = current.getChild(part)

why: Folder 需要控制自己的不变量；暴露内部 map 会让外部代码直接修改 children 而不维护 parent。
why_en: Returning a copy of the children protects Folder's invariants from uncontrolled external mutation.
tradeoff: 返回副本保护不变量 vs 直接暴露内部结构换取零拷贝
whenOtherWins: 如果 Folder 只在受信任的内部代码里被使用，直接暴露引用也可以接受，但会失去这层保护。
options_en: Returning a copy is purely to make lookups faster.
Folder's internal map cannot be iterated at all.
It stops callers from bypassing addChild/removeChild and breaking internal invariants.
A FileSystemEntry can never be stored inside any List.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内部状态隐藏起来，只通过受控方法修改的设计原则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation hides internal state and only allows changes through controlled methods.

q_en: Why does getChildren() return a copy of the values instead of the internal map?
scenario_en: Calling getChildren() to list a directory's contents.
optionExplanations: 返回副本这件事本身跟查找速度无关，这不是暴露内部 map 的真正风险点。
Map 本来就可以用 values() 遍历，这个断言站不住。
暴露内部 map 会让外部代码绕开 addChild/removeChild 直接改结构，破坏 parent 一致性。
List 完全能存放包括 FileSystemEntry 在内的任意对象。
optionExplanations_en: Returning a copy has nothing to do with lookup speed — that's not the real risk of exposing the internal map.
A map can already be iterated via values(); that claim doesn't hold up.
Exposing the internal map lets outside code bypass addChild/removeChild and mutate structure directly, breaking parent consistency.
A list can hold any object, FileSystemEntry included, without any restriction.

scenario: 文件内容是普通字符串，当前不支持文件类型专属行为。
q: File 应承担哪些职责？
options: 像 Folder 一样独立管理自己的 children map
脱离 FileSystem，独立负责整个系统的所有路径解析
额外计算目录大小和访问权限信息
有共享字段，加 content，isDirectory=false
why: File 是 leaf，唯一额外状态是字符串内容；目录容器逻辑属于 Folder，路径编排属于 FileSystem。
why_en: File is a leaf entry whose only extra responsibility beyond the shared fields is storing string content.
tradeoff: File 只管内容的单一职责 vs 把容器/路径逻辑也塞进 File
whenOtherWins: 如果后续要支持文件类型专属行为（如图片生成缩略图），才需要给 File 拆分子类型。
options_en: Independently manage its own children map just like Folder does.
Break away from FileSystem and resolve every path in the system itself.
Additionally compute folder size and access permissions.
Has the shared fields, adds content, and sets isDirectory=false.

termDefinitions.meaning: 树里不能再包含子节点的末端节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A leaf is a tree node that cannot contain further children.

q_en: What responsibilities should File carry?
scenario_en: File content is a plain string, and file-type-specific behavior is not supported yet.
optionExplanations: children map 是 Folder 的职责，File 是叶子节点，没有子节点可管。
路径解析集中在 FileSystem 的 helper 里，File 不该自己接管整个系统的解析。
权限和目录大小这两项都被面试官明确排除在这版范围之外。
File 只在共享字段基础上多加一个内容字段，isDirectory 固定为 false，这就是它的全部职责。
optionExplanations_en: The children map is Folder's job — File is a leaf with no children to manage.
Path resolution stays centralized in FileSystem's helper; File shouldn't take over parsing for the whole system.
Both permissions and folder-size aggregation were explicitly scoped out by the interviewer.
File just adds one content field on top of the shared fields, with isDirectory fixed to false — that's its entire job.

scenario: resolvePath 是所有路径操作共用的核心 helper，需要统一识别哪些输入算作非法路径。
q: resolvePath 应识别哪些错误？（多选）
options: path 为空或不是绝对路径
路径中有连续斜杠导致空组件
中间组件不是目录
某一级 child 不存在
文件名包含非 ASCII 字符
why: 这些错误都属于路径解析层；统一 helper 能让 public 方法保持简洁，字符集不是 resolvePath 的校验范围。
why_en: resolvePath should centralize absolute-path, empty-component, not-a-directory, and not-found errors.
options_en: path is empty or not absolute.
Consecutive slashes create an empty path component.
A middle component is not a directory.
A child does not exist at some level.
The file name contains non-ASCII characters.

termDefinitions.meaning: 表示路径字符串本身格式非法的异常类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: InvalidPathException signals that the path string itself is malformed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 表示路径指向的 entry 不存在的异常类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NotFoundException signals that the entry the path points to does not exist.

q_en: Which errors should resolvePath recognize? (multi-select)
scenario_en: resolvePath is the core helper shared by every path operation, so it needs one consistent notion of which inputs are illegal.
optionExplanations: 路径为空或不是以 / 开头，都应该在最开始就被 resolvePath 拦下。
连续斜杠会产生空的路径组件，说明这段路径格式本身有问题。
路径中途遇到一个 File 却还要继续往下找 child，说明这一段其实不是目录。
某一级按名字找不到对应 child，说明路径指向了不存在的位置。
resolvePath 只管路径结构是否合法，从不检查文件名用了什么字符集。
optionExplanations_en: An empty path or one that doesn't start with / should get caught right at the top by resolvePath.
Consecutive slashes produce an empty path component, which means the path's format itself is broken.
Hitting a File partway through and still trying to descend into a child means that segment isn't actually a directory.
Not finding a matching child by name at some level means the path points somewhere that doesn't exist.
resolvePath only checks whether the path's structure is valid — it never inspects what character set a name uses.

scenario: 两个线程同时 createFile('/home/notes.txt', ...)；都先看到 hasChild=false。
q: 这是哪类并发 bug？
options: dead code elimination
check-then-act race
cache miss
path normalization
why: 检查重名和 addChild 之间没有原子性，两个线程都可能通过检查；需要锁住完整检查+写入。
why_en: Concurrent create has a check-then-act race between the hasChild check and the addChild write.
tradeoff: 把检查和写入锁在一起保证原子性 vs 各自独立执行更快但可能重复创建
whenOtherWins: 单线程内存题可以先不实现并发，但高级讨论应指出这个风险。
options_en: Dead code elimination.
A check-then-act race.
A cache miss.
Path normalization.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先检查条件、再执行动作，中间可能被其他线程插入的并发缺陷模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Check-then-act is a concurrency bug pattern where checking a condition and acting on it are not atomic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多个线程同时读写共享状态、结果依赖执行时序的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is a bug where the outcome depends on the timing of concurrent threads touching shared state.

q_en: What kind of concurrency bug is this?
scenario_en: Two threads call createFile('/home/notes.txt', ...) at the same time, and both first see hasChild=false.
optionExplanations: 这是编译器优化的术语，跟运行时的线程时序完全无关。
两个线程都先看到 hasChild 为 false 再各自 addChild，检查和动作之间没有原子性保护。
整个场景里根本没有缓存层，跟命中不命中没关系。
两个线程用的是同一个合法路径，这跟路径格式化没关系。
optionExplanations_en: That's a compiler-optimization term, completely unrelated to runtime thread timing.
Both threads see hasChild as false and then each call addChild — there's no atomicity between the check and the action.
There's no caching layer anywhere in this scenario, so hit or miss doesn't apply.
Both threads are using the exact same valid path — this isn't about path formatting.

scenario: 面试要求快速给出线程安全方案，吞吐不是重点。
q: 最简单正确方案是什么？
options: 给 FileSystem public 方法加粗粒度锁
每个 File 都加独立锁但不锁 Folder
只同步 getPath
完全依赖 HashMap
why: 粗粒度锁让所有路径解析和修改串行化，容易证明正确；代价是不同目录的无关操作也会互相阻塞。
why_en: Coarse-grained locking around FileSystem's public methods is the simplest provably-correct thread-safety strategy.
tradeoff: 粗粒度锁简单正确 vs 不同目录操作也被迫串行
whenOtherWins: 高并发且不同目录操作很多时，可改为每个 Folder 的细粒度锁。
codeSample:
createFile(path, content)
    synchronized(this)
        parent = resolveParent(path)
        if parent.hasChild(name) throw AlreadyExists
        parent.addChild(File(name, content))
// this 锁住整个 FileSystem
// 同一时刻只有一个线程能执行任意公共方法
options_en: Wrap FileSystem's public methods in one coarse-grained lock.
Give every File its own lock but never lock Folder.
Only synchronize getPath.
Rely entirely on a HashMap for safety.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一把大锁保护整个对象所有操作的并发策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coarse-grained locking protects all of an object's operations with a single lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 进入代码块前必须先获得指定锁的并发关键字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: synchronized is the keyword requiring a thread to acquire a given lock before entering a code block.

q_en: What is the simplest correct approach?
scenario_en: The interview wants a thread-safety approach quickly; throughput is not the focus.
optionExplanations: 一把锁包住所有公共方法，所有操作天然串行，最容易论证正确性。
真正的竞争发生在 Folder.children 这个容器上，只锁 File 起不到保护作用。
createFile/delete 这些写路径完全没被保护，getPath 不是竞争发生的地方。
标准 HashMap 从来不保证并发安全，不能替代显式加锁。
optionExplanations_en: One lock around every public method serializes all operations, which is the easiest way to prove correctness.
The real contention is on the Folder.children container — locking only File doesn't protect anything.
Write paths like createFile and delete stay completely unprotected; getPath was never where the race happens.
A plain HashMap never guarantees concurrency safety on its own — it can't substitute for explicit locking.

scenario: 希望不同目录下的 createFile 并行执行。
q: 可采用哪种更细粒度方案？
options: 只锁 root
每个路径字符串一个锁但不管理顺序
锁住被修改的 parent Folder
不锁 hasChild
why: 创建只修改目标父目录的 children map，锁 parent 即可让不同父目录并发；move 更复杂，因为会触碰两个父目录。
why_en: Per-folder locking lets operations on different folders proceed concurrently while still protecting shared state.
tradeoff: 细粒度锁并发更好 vs 复杂度和死锁风险上升
whenOtherWins: 如果实现复杂度或死锁风险不可接受，粗粒度 FileSystem 锁更稳。
codeSample:
createFile(path, content)
    parent = resolveParent(path)
    synchronized(parent)
        if parent.hasChild(name) throw AlreadyExists
        parent.addChild(File(name, content))
// 只锁目标父目录，不同父目录的调用可并行
options_en: Only lock root.
One lock per path string, without managing lock order.
Lock the parent Folder being modified.
Skip locking hasChild.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给每个子资源单独加锁、只锁被修改部分的并发策略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine-grained locking gives each sub-resource its own lock so only the touched part is locked.

q_en: Which finer-grained approach can be used?
scenario_en: You want createFile calls in different directories to run in parallel.
optionExplanations: 只锁 root 等于退回粗粒度锁，不同目录的操作依然会互相等待。
没有固定顺序地给每个路径分别加锁，很容易埋下死锁隐患。
锁住被修改的那个父目录，不同父目录下的创建操作就能真正并行。
跳过 hasChild 的锁保护会让检查和写入之间重新出现竞争窗口。
optionExplanations_en: Locking only root collapses back into coarse-grained locking — operations on different folders still wait on each other.
Handing out one lock per path with no fixed order is a straightforward way to introduce deadlocks later.
Locking just the parent folder being modified lets creates under different parents run truly in parallel.
Skipping the lock around hasChild reopens a race window between the check and the write.

q: 按顺序排列 move 中细粒度锁的死锁场景：
steps: 线程 A 持有 /alice，等待 /bob。
线程 B 持有 /bob，等待 /alice。
A 执行 move('/alice/file','/bob/file')。
B 执行 move('/bob/other','/alice/other')。
两个线程形成循环等待。
why: move 需要同时锁源父和目标父；不同线程按相反顺序加锁就会死锁。
why_en: Moving between two folders can deadlock if different threads acquire the two folder locks in opposite orders.
tradeoff: 按固定全局顺序加锁避免死锁 vs 按 src/dest 角色加锁埋下循环等待
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant T1
  participant A as Folder A
  participant B as Folder B
  participant T2
  T1->>A: lock
  T2->>B: lock
  T1-->>B: waits
  T2-->>A: waits

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个或多个线程互相等待对方持有的锁，永远无法继续执行。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A deadlock happens when threads wait on locks held by each other and none can proceed.

q_en: Order the deadlock scenario for fine-grained locking in move:

scenario: 细粒度 move 需要同时锁 srcParent 和 destParent。
q: 如何防止死锁？
options: 先锁源再锁目标，所有调用都这样但路径可能反向
每次都尝试用随机顺序重新获取锁
只锁两个文件夹中较新创建的那个
按固定顺序加锁，如按 getPath() 字典序
why: 稳定全局顺序消除循环等待；src/dest 角色会随操作方向变化，不能作为锁顺序。
why_en: A consistent global lock order, not the src/dest role, is what prevents circular wait during move.
tradeoff: 全局稳定顺序锁定两把锁 vs 按调用角色顺序锁定（会反转导致死锁）
whenOtherWins: 粗粒度 FileSystem 锁不需要双锁排序，但牺牲并发。
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["need two folder locks"] --> B["sort by stable id or path"]
  B --> C["lock first"]
  C --> D["lock second"]
  D --> E["move safely"]
codeSample:
move(srcPath, destPath)
    a = resolveParent(srcPath)
    b = resolveParent(destPath)
    first  = a.getPath() < b.getPath() ? a : b
    second = a.getPath() < b.getPath() ? b : a
    synchronized(first)
        synchronized(second)
            // 安全地修改两个 folder
// 无论谁是 src/dest，都按路径字典序先锁 first
options_en: Always lock the source before the destination, even though the roles can reverse across calls.
Retry every time with a freshly randomized lock order.
Only lock whichever of the two folders was created more recently.
Acquire locks in a fixed order, such as alphabetically by getPath().

termDefinitions.meaning: 约定所有线程按同一固定顺序获取多把锁，避免循环等待。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Lock ordering means every thread acquires multiple locks in the same fixed order to avoid circular waits.

q_en: How do you prevent deadlock?
scenario_en: Fine-grained move needs to lock both srcParent and destParent at the same time.
optionExplanations: src/dest 的角色会随调用方向反转，两个线程互为镜像时依然会循环等待。
随机顺序只是降低概率，并不能从根本上排除循环等待。
'较新创建'不是一个全局稳定的排序标准，无法保证一致的加锁顺序。
两个线程都先锁 getPath() 字典序更小的那个文件夹，就永远不会形成循环等待。
optionExplanations_en: The src/dest roles flip depending on call direction, so two mirrored threads can still deadlock on each other.
A random order only lowers the odds — it doesn't eliminate circular wait as a structural guarantee.
'Created more recently' isn't a globally stable ordering key, so it can't guarantee a consistent lock order.
If both threads always lock whichever folder sorts first by getPath(), circular wait becomes impossible.

scenario: 系统读多写少，很多线程同时 get/list，不常 create/delete/move。
q: 什么锁策略能提升吞吐？
options: 所有读和写操作都共用同一把互斥锁保护
读写锁，读操作共享锁、写操作互斥锁
每一次读取都要先复制一整棵树再返回
读方法完全不加任何锁保护，直接裸读
why: 读写锁允许多个读者并行，同时保证写者独占；适合读多写少的文件系统。
why_en: A read-write lock lets concurrent readers run in parallel while still giving writers exclusive access.
tradeoff: 读写锁提升读并发 vs 实现和维护成本更高
whenOtherWins: 如果实现时间有限或写很多，普通互斥锁更简单，可能也足够。
options_en: Protect every read and write with one shared mutex, no distinction.
A read-write lock: reads take a shared lock, writes take an exclusive lock.
Copy the entire tree from scratch and return it on every single read.
Give the read methods no lock protection at all, reading raw.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许多个读者并行、但写者独占的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-write lock lets multiple readers run in parallel while giving a writer exclusive access.

q_en: What locking strategy improves throughput?
scenario_en: The system is read-heavy: many threads call get/list concurrently, and create/delete/move are rare.
optionExplanations: 读者之间本来可以并行，共用一把互斥锁会让他们不必要地互相等待。
多个 read lock 可以同时持有，只有 write lock 才会独占，正好匹配读多写少。
数万 entry 的树每次读都整份复制，开销远大于收益。
完全不加锁会让读者读到写操作写到一半的不一致状态。
optionExplanations_en: Readers could run in parallel, but sharing one mutex forces them to wait on each other for no reason.
Multiple read locks can be held at once, and only a write lock is exclusive — a perfect match for read-heavy traffic.
Copying the whole tree of tens of thousands of entries on every read costs far more than it saves.
Skipping locking entirely lets readers see a half-written, inconsistent state mid-write.

scenario: 用户要按文件名查找 config.json，但不知道在哪个目录。
q: 最简单搜索实现是什么？
options: 从 root 递归遍历整棵树找名字匹配
只查 root 的直接子节点，不深入子树
要求用户必须给完整路径
扫描每个文件的完整内容
why: 递归遍历正确且容易实现，但每次搜索是 O(n)；如果搜索频繁，再维护索引。
why_en: Recursive traversal from root is the simplest correct name search, at O(n) cost per query.
tradeoff: 递归遍历零额外状态 vs 维护索引换取更快查询
whenOtherWins: 频繁按名搜索时，维护 name -> entries 的索引能把查询降到接近 O(1)。
options_en: Recursively traverse the whole tree from root, collecting name matches.
Only search root's direct children, without going deeper into the subtree.
Require callers to always give the full path.
Scan every file's full content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 操作耗时随树中 entry 总数 n 线性增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: O(n) means the search cost grows linearly with the total number n of entries in the tree.

q_en: What is the simplest search implementation?
scenario_en: A user wants to find config.json by name but doesn't know which folder it's in.
optionExplanations: 从 root 开始递归下探，名字对上就收进结果，正确且最容易实现，只是每次都是 O(n)。
只看 root 底下第一层，深层目录里的文件根本找不到。
用户本来就是因为不知道文件在哪个目录才要搜索，要求给完整路径违背了这个前提。
这是按内容搜索，跟'按文件名找文件'是完全不同的功能。
optionExplanations_en: Recurse down from root and collect every name match — correct and the easiest to implement, just O(n) per query.
That only looks at root's immediate children, so files buried deeper in the tree never get found.
The whole reason to search is that the user doesn't know which directory the file is in — demanding a full path defeats that.
That's searching by content, a completely different feature from finding a file by name.

scenario: 按名称搜索非常频繁，文件树有数万 entry。
q: 应该如何优化？
options: 每次搜索仍然要遍历整棵文件树
把所有文件内容拼接成一个大字符串
维护 name→entries 索引，写时同步更新
搜索功能只能覆盖 root 下的直接子节点
why: 名称索引用额外空间和写路径复杂度换查询速度；rename/delete 尤其要同步更新索引。
why_en: A name index speeds up frequent search, but create, delete, and rename must all keep it in sync.
tradeoff: 维护 nameIndex 加快查询 vs 每次写操作都要多做一步索引维护
whenOtherWins: 如果搜索很少，递归遍历更简单且不需要维护派生状态。
options_en: Keep doing a full-tree traversal on every single search.
Concatenate all file content into one giant string.
Maintain a name-to-entries index, kept in sync on every write.
Only let search cover the direct children of root.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从文件名映射到对应 entry 列表的辅助索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: nameIndex is an auxiliary map from a file name to the list of entries with that name.

q_en: How should this be optimized?
scenario_en: Name-based search is very frequent, and the file tree has tens of thousands of entries.
optionExplanations: 数万 entry 规模下还坚持每次全树遍历，完全没针对'频繁'这个新约束做优化。
把内容拼成一个大字符串既定位不了路径，又白白浪费内存。
search(name) 直接查表变成近似 O(1)，代价是 create/delete/rename 都要多维护一步索引。
人为把搜索范围限制在 root 直接子节点，违背了要覆盖全树的需求。
optionExplanations_en: Still doing a full-tree walk on every search at tens of thousands of entries does nothing about the new 'frequent' constraint.
Concatenating all content into one string can't locate a path and just wastes memory.
search(name) becomes a near-O(1) lookup, at the cost of create, delete, and rename each having one more index to maintain.
Artificially limiting search to root's direct children breaks the requirement to cover the whole tree.

q: 补全搜索索引的维护代价：
text: nameIndex 让 search(name) 更快，但 create/delete/rename/move 必须维护索引；尤其 rename 要从{{旧名字列表}}删除，再加入{{新名字列表}}。
why: 索引是派生数据；任何写操作都可能让它与树结构不一致，rename 要同时改旧名和新名两处列表。
why_en: A name index is derived state that must be updated on every relevant mutation, especially rename.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从主数据结构计算或复制出来、需要手动保持同步的辅助数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Derived state is auxiliary data computed from the main structure that must be kept in sync manually.

q_en: Fill in the maintenance cost of the search index:

scenario: 后续要支持前缀搜索，例如 config*。
q: 支持前缀搜索最合适的数据结构是什么？
options: Stack
Queue
单个 boolean
Trie
why: Trie 可以按字符前缀定位节点，再收集所有后代匹配项；它比普通 map 更适合前缀查询。
why_en: A trie supports efficient prefix search by walking the prefix and then collecting descendant matches.
tradeoff: Trie 支持前缀匹配 vs nameIndex 只支持精确匹配
whenOtherWins: 只做精确文件名搜索时，nameIndex map 更简单。
options_en: Stack.
Queue.
A single boolean.
Trie.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按字符逐层组织字符串的树形结构，适合前缀匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A trie is a tree that indexes strings character by character, which makes prefix search efficient.

q_en: What data structure best supports prefix search?
scenario_en: You need to support prefix search later, such as config*.
optionExplanations: Stack 是后进先出的线性结构，完全不索引字符串的前缀关系。
Queue 同样是线性结构，也定位不了共享前缀的一组条目。
单个 boolean 连'有哪些匹配项'这种集合语义都表达不了。
Trie 按字符逐层组织，先走到 'config' 节点，再收集它下面所有匹配的后代。
optionExplanations_en: A stack is a last-in-first-out linear structure with no notion of shared string prefixes.
A queue is likewise linear and can't locate a group of entries sharing a prefix either.
A single boolean can't even express set semantics like 'which entries matched.'
A trie organizes characters level by level — walk to the 'config' node, then collect every matching descendant beneath it.

scenario: 后续要按文件内容中的词搜索。
q: 应该考虑什么索引？
options: 只按文件扩展名做分类的 map
倒排索引：从词映射到包含它的文件
沿用 Folder.children 这套树形索引
只靠 parent 指针逐级定位
why: 内容搜索本质上是小型搜索引擎问题；倒排索引能从词快速找到包含它的文件。
why_en: Content search calls for an inverted index that maps each word to the files containing it.
tradeoff: 倒排索引支持任意词查询 vs nameIndex 只支持按文件名查询
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要按文件名找文件，不需要按内容里的词搜索，nameIndex 已经够用，不必上倒排索引。
options_en: A map that only classifies files by extension.
An inverted index: word maps to the files containing it.
Reuse the same Folder.children tree-shaped index.
Locate files only by walking parent pointers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从词映射到包含该词的文档/文件集合的索引结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each word to the set of files or documents that contain it.

q_en: What kind of index should be considered?
scenario_en: You need to support searching by words inside file content later.
optionExplanations: 按扩展名分类只能筛类型，回答不了'哪些文件包含这个词'。
倒排索引把词映射到包含它的文件集合，直接支持按内容里的词查询。
children map 是路径导航结构，从来不索引文件内部的文字。
parent 指针只用来算路径，同样不涉及文件内容。
optionExplanations_en: Classifying by extension only filters by type — it can't answer 'which files contain this word.'
An inverted index maps each word to the set of files containing it, directly supporting search by content.
The children map is a navigation structure — it never indexes the text inside a file.
Parent pointers are only for computing paths; they don't touch file content either.

scenario: 面试官明确把相对路径、符号链接、权限和持久化都划出范围，只保留内存里的单根绝对路径树。
q: 这些范围排除分别为 resolvePath 和树结构带来了什么简化？（多选）
options: resolvePath 不需要处理 ../ 或 ./ 这类相对跳转
环检测只需要覆盖 move，不用再处理符号链接造成的环
不需要在每次操作前做权限校验
不需要设计任何持久化或崩溃恢复逻辑
仍然需要支持 Windows 风格的多盘符路径
why: 范围排除不是要背的清单，而是直接简化了实现：resolvePath 只走绝对路径、环检测只管 move、没有权限校验和持久化逻辑。
why_en: Scoping out relative paths, symlinks, permissions, and persistence directly simplifies resolvePath and cycle detection, not just the requirement list.
options_en: resolvePath does not need to handle relative jumps like ../ or ./.
Cycle detection only needs to cover move, not cycles caused by symlinks.
No permission check is needed before every operation.
No persistence or crash-recovery logic needs to be designed.
It still needs to support Windows-style multi-drive paths.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以 ../ 或 ./ 开头、相对当前位置解析的路径，与绝对路径相对。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A relative path starts with ../ or ./ and resolves relative to the current location, unlike an absolute path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 指向另一个路径的特殊引用节点，可能造成解析环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A symlink is a special node that points to another path and can introduce resolution cycles.

q_en: What simplifications do these scope exclusions bring to resolvePath and the tree structure? (multi-select)
scenario_en: The interviewer explicitly scoped out relative paths, symlinks, permissions, and persistence, leaving only an in-memory single-root absolute-path tree.
optionExplanations: 相对路径被划出范围后，resolvePath 从头到尾只需要处理以 / 开头的绝对路径。
没有符号链接，树里唯一可能造成环的操作就只剩 move，环检测不用管别的入口。
权限被排除后，每个公共方法都不用在操作前插一段权限校验代码。
一切都在内存里，不用为崩溃恢复或落盘设计任何持久化逻辑。
面试官确认的是 Unix 风格单根树，从没提过要支持多盘符路径。
optionExplanations_en: With relative paths out of scope, resolvePath only ever has to handle absolute paths starting with /.
Without symlinks, move is the only operation that can create a cycle, so cycle detection doesn't need to watch anywhere else.
With permissions scoped out, no public method needs a permission check inserted before it runs.
Everything lives in memory, so there's no crash-recovery or on-disk persistence logic to design at all.
The interviewer confirmed a Unix-style single root — multi-drive paths were never part of this.

q: 创建 /home/user/notes.txt 的正确状态变化顺序是什么？
steps: resolveParent('/home/user/notes.txt') 返回 user Folder。
extractName 得到 notes.txt。
检查 user.hasChild('notes.txt') 为 false。
创建 File('notes.txt','...')。
user.addChild(file) 并设置 file.parent=user。
why: 创建操作只修改目标父目录，并通过 addChild 维护双向关系；中间目录不存在则应在 resolveParent 失败。
why_en: Create resolves the parent, checks for a collision, creates the entry, and attaches it while setting the parent pointer.
tradeoff: createFile 要求父目录已存在 vs 自动创建缺失的中间目录

termDefinitions.meaning: 解析出路径最后一级组件所在父 Folder 的 helper。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: resolveParent resolves the parent Folder that contains the path's final component.

q_en: What is the correct order of state changes when creating /home/user/notes.txt?

q: 移动 /home/user/notes.txt 到 /home/notes.txt 的正确顺序是什么？
steps: srcParent.removeChild('notes.txt')，清除旧 parent。
解析 srcParent=user、entry=notes.txt。
解析 destParent=home、destName=notes.txt。
检查目标无重名并跳过文件 cycle 检查。
entry.setName('notes.txt') 后 destParent.addChild(entry)。
why: move 应在验证完成后再修改源和目标；addChild 重新设置 parent，使 getPath 反映新位置。
why_en: Move validates both the source and destination first, then detaches from the source and attaches to the destination.
tradeoff: 先验证两侧再修改 vs 边验证边修改可能留下不一致的中间状态

termDefinitions.meaning: move 操作里目标位置所在的父 Folder。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: destParent is the destination parent Folder in a move operation.

q_en: What is the correct order for moving /home/user/notes.txt to /home/notes.txt?

scenario: 面试官在候选人讲完基础设计后问'还有什么值得深入'，用来判断候选人的资历层级。
q: Senior 级文件系统回答应主动覆盖哪些点？（多选）
options: parent pointer vs stored path tradeoff
children 用 Map 保证路径解析效率和唯一名
move 的 cycle detection
线程安全中的锁粒度和 lock ordering
搜索索引的空间/写复杂度权衡
总是应该一开始就实现分布式多节点文件系统
why: 高级答案要能主动处理树不变量、性能和并发；但过度设计超出题目范围的方案不是资深信号，反而是警号。
why_en: Senior answers proactively cover path storage, locking, and search tradeoffs, but over-engineering beyond scope is a red flag, not a signal of seniority.
options_en: The parent-pointer vs stored-path tradeoff.
Using a Map for child lookup and enforcing unique names.
Cycle detection in move.
Lock granularity and lock ordering for thread safety.
The space/write tradeoff of a search index.
Always building a distributed multi-node file system from the start.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在需求没有要求的情况下引入远超范围的复杂方案。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Over-engineering means introducing a far more complex solution than the requirements actually call for.

q_en: Which points should a senior-level file system answer proactively cover? (multi-select)
scenario_en: After the candidate finishes the base design, the interviewer asks 'anything else worth going deeper on' to gauge seniority.
optionExplanations: 主动提出 parent 指针换局部更新、还是存 full path 换 O(1) 读，是资深候选人会讨论的权衡。
点出用 Map 保证按名 O(1) 查找、同时天然拦住重名，体现对数据结构约束的理解。
主动提 move 的环检测，说明候选人在主动维护树的不变量而不是等面试官提醒。
讲清锁粒度和固定加锁顺序，体现对并发正确性和死锁风险的把控。
点出索引加速查询但要付出写路径维护成本，是空间换时间的权衡意识。
题目从没要求分布式，主动往这个方向堆功能是过度工程，不是加分项。
optionExplanations_en: Proactively raising parent pointers for local updates versus storing full paths for O(1) reads is the tradeoff a senior candidate would bring up.
Pointing out that a map gives O(1) lookup by name and blocks duplicates for free shows real grasp of the data-structure constraint.
Bringing up cycle detection in move on your own shows you're actively guarding the tree's invariant, not waiting to be prompted.
Explaining lock granularity and a fixed lock order shows control over concurrency correctness and deadlock risk.
Naming the index's write-path maintenance cost alongside its query speedup shows awareness of the space-for-time tradeoff.
The problem never asked for distributed at all — piling that on unprompted is over-engineering, not a bonus signal.

q: 按顺序排列文件系统主设计链路：
steps: 用 FileSystemEntry 抽取 File/Folder 的 name、parent、getPath。
先收敛为内存绝对路径树，排除权限/持久化/symlink。
FileSystem 作为 facade 持有 root 并解析路径。
Folder.children 使用 Map<string,FileSystemEntry>。
move/rename 通过 parent 指针和 map 更新维护树不变量。
why: 这个顺序从范围到入口、节点抽象、数据结构和复杂操作；它展示设计不是为了套模式而套模式。
why_en: The design chain moves from scope to facade, shared entry abstraction, child maps, and invariant-preserving mutations.
tradeoff: 先定范围再逐步引入抽象 vs 一开始就套用设计模式

termDefinitions.meaning: File 和 Folder 共同的抽象基类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FileSystemEntry is the shared abstract base class for File and Folder.

q_en: Order the main design chain of the file system:

scenario: 面试最后要你总结最重要的不变量。
q: 哪一个最准确？
options: 树必须无环，child 与 parent 的引用要双向一致
每个文件夹最多只能包含一个文件
每个 entry 都必须保存完整 path 字符串
所有文件系统里的名字必须全局唯一
why: 树结构正确性依赖 parent/children 双向一致且无环；名称唯一只要求同一文件夹内唯一，不是全局唯一。
why_en: The core invariant is an acyclic tree with consistent parent-child links and only per-folder unique names.
tradeoff: 无环+双向一致的最小不变量 vs 额外强加全局唯一名等不必要约束
whenOtherWins: 如果加入 hard link 或 symlink，结构不再是纯树，需要重新定义路径解析和循环规则。
options_en: The tree must stay acyclic, with child and parent references pointing back to each other consistently.
Each folder can hold at most a single file.
Every entry must store its full path string.
Every file name across the whole system must be globally unique.

termDefinitions.meaning: 从任意节点沿引用往下走都不会回到自己祖先的树结构性质。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Acyclic means that following references from any node never loops back to one of its ancestors.

q_en: Which one is the most accurate?
scenario_en: At the end of the interview you're asked to summarize the single most important invariant.
optionExplanations: getPath、move、遍历全都要靠无环、且父子引用互相对得上，这是根本条件。
Folder.children 本来就能装任意多个文件，从没有过这种数量限制。
这版设计选择的是 parent 指针方案，本来就不存 full path 字符串。
唯一性只在同一个文件夹内要求，不同文件夹完全可以出现同名文件。
optionExplanations_en: getPath, move, and traversal all depend on the tree staying acyclic with parent-child references matching up — that's the root condition.
Folder.children could always hold any number of files — there was never a limit like that.
This design chose the parent-pointer approach, which by design never stores a full path string.
Uniqueness is only required within one folder — different folders can absolutely share the same file name.

q: Inventory Management 基础需求包含哪些能力？（多选）
q_en: Which capabilities belong in the base inventory management design?
options: 跨多个仓库跟踪产品库存
按仓库 add/remove stock
查询哪些仓库可满足某产品数量
仓库间 transfer stock
低库存告警和线程安全
