It makes spot search, claim, and ticket save one atomic operation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要么完整执行，要么完全不执行，不会被其他线程看到中间状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An atomic operation either completes fully or not at all, with no other thread able to observe a partial result.

termDefinitions.meaning: 互斥锁，同一时刻只允许一个线程进入被保护的代码块。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A mutex lock allows only one thread at a time to enter the protected section of code.

optionExplanations: 这段代码里没有出现计费逻辑，锁包住的是找位、占位和建票，不是 fee 计算。
加锁的目的正相反，是要阻止两个入口拿到同一个 spot，不是制造这个问题。
generateId() 本来就在锁里被调用，锁不是用来替代它，只是保证它和其他步骤一起原子执行。
锁把找空位、标记占用、创建保存票据这三步合成一个不可分割的操作，别的线程看不到中间状态。
optionExplanations_en: There's no fee-calculation logic in this snippet at all — the lock wraps the search, claim, and ticket steps, not a fee computation.
The whole point of the lock is the opposite — preventing two entrances from claiming the same spot, not causing it.
generateId() is already called inside the lock; the lock isn't replacing it, it's just making it atomic alongside the other steps.
The lock fuses finding a spot, marking it occupied, and creating/storing the ticket into one indivisible operation no other thread can observe mid-way.

scenario: 想让多个入口并发搜索空位，只在真正占用车位时短暂互斥。
scenario_en: We want multiple entrances to search for free spots concurrently and only take a short exclusive lock when claiming a spot.
q: 支持并发搜索、只在占用时短暂独占的更细粒度方案是什么？
q_en: What finer-grained approach supports concurrent search and short exclusive claiming?
options: 读锁搜索，写锁内 double-check 后占用，冲突则重试
完全不加任何锁，读写都自由进行
只锁 activeTickets，不锁 occupiedSpotIds
给每个 ticket 单独分配一把锁
why: 读写锁允许多个搜索并行，但 read 和 write 之间可能被别的线程抢先，所以写锁内要二次检查后再占用。
why_en: A read-write approach searches concurrently, then double-checks and claims the spot under the write lock, retrying on conflict.
whenOtherWins: 对 3-5 个入口的普通停车场，方法级互斥更简单，性能也已经足够。
tradeoff: 读写锁提高并发但要 double-check vs 单一互斥锁简单但完全串行
options_en: Search under a read lock, then double-check and claim under a write lock, retrying on conflict.
Use no locking at all for reads or writes.
Lock only activeTickets and leave occupiedSpotIds unlocked.
Give every ticket its own separate lock.

termDefinitions.meaning: 允许多个读操作并发进行，但写操作需要独占访问的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A read-write lock lets multiple readers run concurrently but gives a writer exclusive access.

optionExplanations: 读多写少的场景下，多个搜索可以并发跑，真正占用车位那一刻才切到写锁并二次确认，兼顾并发度和正确性。
不加锁能获得最大并发，但代价是彻底放弃正确性，check-then-act 的窗口会天天暴露。
占用状态实际记在 occupiedSpotIds 里，只锁 activeTickets 完全保护不到真正会冲突的数据。
冲突发生在多个线程抢同一个 spot，而不是抢同一张 ticket，按 ticket 分锁根本锁不住这场竞争。
optionExplanations_en: When reads dominate, multiple searches can run concurrently and only the moment of claiming switches to a write lock with a re-check, balancing concurrency against correctness.
No locking at all buys maximum concurrency, but at the cost of correctness entirely — the check-then-act window gets exposed every time.
Occupancy actually lives in occupiedSpotIds; locking only activeTickets doesn't protect the data that can actually conflict.
The conflict is multiple threads racing for the same spot, not the same ticket, so a per-ticket lock doesn't guard against that race at all.

q: 按顺序排列多入口 race 的发生过程：
q_en: Put the multi-entrance race in order:
steps: 入口 A 和 B 同时调用 findAvailableSpot。
二者都看到 spot B 不在 occupiedSpotIds 里。
A 创建 ticket 指向 spot B。
B 也创建 ticket 指向 spot B。
两辆车拿到了同一个车位。
why: 问题窗口在『检查空闲』和『写入占用』之间；必须把两步合并成同一个临界区才能消除这个 race。
why_en: The race occurs because two entrances observe the same free spot before either one claims it, so the check and the claim must become one critical section.
tradeoff: 分离的检查与占用步骤 vs 合并成一个原子临界区
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Gate A
  participant S as spot B
  participant B as Gate B
  A->>S: sees free
  B->>S: sees free
  A->>S: claim
  B->>S: claim

termDefinitions.meaning: 多线程同时读写共享状态导致结果依赖执行顺序的错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition happens when concurrent threads read and write shared state and the outcome depends on timing.

scenario: 停车场有 3-5 个入口，单次 enter 处理约 100 毫秒；200 个车位平均每 2 小时周转一次。
scenario_en: The lot has 3 to 5 entrances, one enter call takes about 100 ms, and 200 spots turn over about once every 2 hours on average.
q: 为什么同步整个 enter() 方法在现实停车场规模下通常足够？
q_en: Why is synchronizing the whole enter() method usually enough at real parking-lot scale?
options: 因为加锁本身会让车位的物理数量凭空增加
因为这类题目里假设停车场永远只有一个车位
因为 ticket map 的按 ID 查找本身非常慢
入场频率远低于锁可处理的吞吐，车通过闸机/支付耗时远大于内存操作
why: 工程取舍要看数量级：停车场的真实入场频率很低，简单正确的方案应该优先于过早优化。
why_en: A coarse enter lock is usually fine because parking-lot arrival rates are tiny compared with in-memory critical-section throughput.
tradeoff: 按数量级判断是否需要优化 vs 不看数量级就上复杂并发方案
options_en: Because locking itself somehow makes the physical spot count grow.
Because this kind of problem always assumes only one spot exists.
Because ticket-map lookup by ID is itself extremely slow.
Arrival frequency is far below what the lock can handle, since gate and payment time dwarf in-memory work.

termDefinitions.meaning: 单位时间内系统能处理的请求数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Throughput is the number of requests a system can process per unit of time.

optionExplanations: 加锁只是控制并发访问顺序，不会改变车位这类物理资源的数量，这个因果关系不成立。
题目场景是 200 个车位、3-5 个入口，不是只有一个车位的极端情况。
map 查找是微秒级操作，慢的从来不是查找本身。
锁能处理的吞吐是微秒到毫秒级，而真实入场受限于闸机和支付这些慢得多的物理环节，锁根本不是瓶颈。
optionExplanations_en: Locking only controls the order of concurrent access; it can't change how many physical spots exist — that causal link doesn't hold.
The scenario is 200 spots and 3-5 entrances, not the degenerate case of a single spot.
Map lookup runs in microseconds — lookup speed was never the slow part here.
The lock can handle throughput on the order of microseconds to milliseconds, while real entries are bottlenecked by gates and payment, which are far slower — the lock is never the constraint.

scenario: 有人说 Node.js 单线程就完全不会有 race condition。
scenario_en: Someone claims Node.js is single-threaded, so race conditions cannot happen at all.
q: 面对这个说法应该如何回应？
q_en: How should you respond to that claim?
options: 单线程模型下永远不会出现逻辑上的 race
异步 await 之间仍可能交错，持久化时要靠数据库事务或分布式锁保证原子性
Node.js 这门编程语言本身就完全不适合拿来实现这样的停车场系统
只要用 Set 存状态就自动获得事务保证
why: 单线程事件循环避免了同一时刻执行两段 JS，但异步 I/O 会在 await 点把请求流程切开，数据库层仍要保证 check-and-claim 原子。
why_en: Single-threaded event loops can still interleave async workflows at await points, so persistence still needs transactional protection.
whenOtherWins: 如果所有状态更新都在同一个不跨越 await 的同步代码块里，才真的不需要额外加锁。
tradeoff: 单线程避免同一时刻双执行 vs 异步交错仍需事务或分布式锁
options_en: A single-threaded model can never have a logical race.
Async await points can still interleave, so persistence needs database transactions or a distributed lock.
Node.js as a programming language is simply never suited at all for building a system like this parking lot.
Storing state in a Set automatically gives you transaction guarantees.

termDefinitions.meaning: Node.js 单线程调度模型，在 I/O 等待点切换执行其他任务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The event loop is Node.js's single-threaded scheduler that switches to other work while one task waits on I/O.

termDefinitions.meaning: 跨多个进程或服务器协调、只允许一个持有者继续执行的锁。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A distributed lock coordinates across multiple processes or servers so only one holder can proceed at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库锁定被查询的行，防止其他事务并发修改它们。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SELECT FOR UPDATE locks the selected database rows so no other transaction can modify them concurrently.

optionExplanations: 单线程只保证同一时刻只有一段 JS 在跑，但 await 会把一次操作拆成好几段，中间照样能被别的请求插进来。
两个 await 之间事件循环会去处理别的任务，状态要落库时还是得靠数据库事务或分布式锁保证检查和占用是一体的。
语言的并发模型只影响要不要额外加锁，跟这门语言适不适合实现某个系统是两件事。
Set 只是一种数据结构，本身不提供任何跨请求的原子性或回滚能力。
optionExplanations_en: Single-threaded only guarantees one piece of JS runs at a time — await splits one operation into several steps, and another request can still slip in between them.
Between two await points the event loop can go handle other work, so if state is persisted, it still needs a database transaction or distributed lock to keep check-and-claim atomic.
The language's concurrency model only affects whether extra locking is needed — that's a separate question from whether it's suited to building the system at all.
A Set is just a data structure; it provides no cross-request atomicity or rollback on its own.

scenario: ticketId 从未存在过，或者已经出场使用过一次。
scenario_en: The ticketId either never existed or was already used once at exit.
q: 基础 exit 应该对这两种情况返回什么语义？
q_en: What semantic result should base exit return for these two cases?
options: 必须区分成两个不同的复杂错误码
自动为用户重新发一张新 ticket
两种情况统一视为 invalid ticket
照常释放一个任意车位再报错
why: activeTickets 只表示当前有效票据集合，不存在和已使用对出场流程都是不可用，没必要区分。
why_en: A ticket not present in activeTickets is invalid whether it never existed or was already used, so exit treats them the same.
whenOtherWins: 如果客服或审计需要区分这两种情况，可以额外保存历史 used tickets 和状态。
tradeoff: 统一 invalid 语义换实现简单 vs 区分两种错误换更精确反馈
options_en: The two cases must be distinguished with two different complex error codes.
Automatically issue the user a brand-new ticket.
Treat both cases uniformly as an invalid ticket.
Free some arbitrary spot anyway before reporting an error.
optionExplanations: 两种情况对出场流程的结果都一样——都不能继续，区分成两个错误码是给基础流程增加不必要的分支。
无效票据不该被系统当成新会话来处理，自动补发一张票会掩盖真正的问题。
系统只用『当前有效』这一个状态描述票据，不在这个集合里的票据不管原因是什么，对出场来说都是同一种结果。
错误的票据本来就没有对应的正确车位，随便释放一个反而会破坏别的会话的占用状态。
optionExplanations_en: Both cases lead to the same outcome for exit — neither can proceed — so splitting them into two error codes adds branching the base flow doesn't need.
An invalid ticket shouldn't be treated as the start of a new session; auto-issuing a replacement would paper over the real problem.
The system expresses only one state, currently valid; anything missing from that set produces the same result for exit, regardless of why.
An invalid ticket has no spot it actually corresponds to, so releasing some arbitrary one would corrupt another session's occupancy instead.

scenario: 后续要支持车位维修或临时封闭。
scenario_en: A later requirement adds spot maintenance or temporary closure.
q: 在当前占用建模（occupiedSpotIds Set）下，新增维修状态最自然放在哪里？
q_en: With the current occupiedSpotIds Set model, where should maintenance state go?
options: ParkingSpot 加 status 字段，或 ParkingLot 加 disabledSpotIds 过滤
在 Ticket 记录上增加一个记录维修人员姓名和联系方式的字段
往 VehicleType 这个车辆分类 enum 类型里硬是新增一个 BROKEN 取值来表示这个新状态
把这个车位的 hourlyRate 计费字段直接改成 0 表示不可用
why: 维修是车位自身或可用性约束，不是 ticket 会话的一部分；基础设计没有实现，但可以沿分配过滤自然扩展。
why_en: Maintenance can be modeled as spot status or a disabled-spot-ID set that allocation simply skips.
whenOtherWins: 如果车位物理状态很多，ParkingSpot.status enum 更适合；只是临时屏蔽少数车位，用 disabled set 更轻量。
tradeoff: 维护性状态放进车位可用性过滤 vs 混进车辆分类或计价字段
options_en: Add a status field to ParkingSpot, or a disabledSpotIds filter on ParkingLot.
Add a field on the Ticket record storing the maintenance worker's name and contact info.
Hard-add a brand-new BROKEN value into the VehicleType vehicle-classification enum type just to represent this new state.
Change that spot's hourlyRate billing field directly to zero to mark it unusable.
optionExplanations: 维修状态描述的是车位本身能不能用，跟 ParkingSpot 的固有属性天然是一类，扩展起来最顺。
Ticket 描述的是一次停车会话，跟车位要不要维修是完全不相关的两条线。
VehicleType 分类的是车辆而不是车位，BROKEN 描述的是车位状态，塞进这个 enum 混淆了两个维度。
费率是计价字段，把它改成 0 只是掩盖了『不可用』这件事，还会让计费逻辑读到假价格。
optionExplanations_en: Maintenance status describes whether the spot itself can be used, which naturally belongs alongside ParkingSpot's own properties — the easiest place to extend.
Ticket describes one parking session; whether a spot needs maintenance is an entirely unrelated concern.
VehicleType classifies vehicles, not spots — BROKEN describes spot state, so cramming it into that enum conflates two different dimensions.
Rate is a pricing field; zeroing it out only hides the 'unavailable' fact and leaves fee logic reading a fake price.

scenario: 监控或前端目前都没有提出『查询实时车位状态』的需求。
scenario_en: Neither monitoring nor the frontend currently requires querying real-time spot status.
q: 为什么基础 API 不主动加 getAvailableSpots 或 getParkingStatus？
q_en: Why should the base API not proactively add getAvailableSpots or getParkingStatus?
options: 这两个方法在技术上根本无法实现
需求没有要求，暴露内部状态会扩大 API；监控需求来了再加
加了这两个方法会破坏 ticketId 的唯一性
使用者必须提前知道全部车位信息
why: 接口应该围绕核心工作流最小化；过早暴露内部集合会增加耦合，等真正的监控需求出现再加不迟。
why_en: The base API stays focused on entry and exit until status queries are explicitly required, to avoid premature coupling.
tradeoff: 接口按需最小化 vs 提前暴露内部状态换『可能有用』
options_en: These two methods are technically impossible to implement.
There is no requirement for them, and exposing internal state widens the API; add them when monitoring is actually needed.
Adding them would break the uniqueness of ticketId.
Callers must already know the full spot inventory in advance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只暴露必要的公开接口，隐藏内部实现细节。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Encapsulation means exposing only the necessary public interface while hiding internal implementation details.

optionExplanations: 查询车位状态在技术上没有任何障碍，说做不到是站不住脚的。
没有监控或前端提出这个需求，先加上等于提前把内部索引暴露成公开接口，真需要时再加不迟。
这两个方法是只读查询，跟 ticketId 怎么生成、是否唯一完全没有关系。
现在的入场出场流程不要求调用方提前知道任何车位库存信息。
optionExplanations_en: There's no technical obstacle to querying spot status; claiming it's impossible doesn't hold up.
Neither monitoring nor the frontend has asked for this yet, so adding it now means turning an internal index into a public API early — it can be added the moment it's actually needed.
These are read-only queries and have nothing to do with how ticketId is generated or whether it stays unique.
The current entry/exit flow doesn't require a caller to know anything about spot inventory ahead of time.

q: 出场计费的正确执行顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order for exit fee calculation?
steps: 从 activeTickets 取出 ticket。
计算 exitTime - entryTime。
按小时向上取整。
乘以 hourlyRateCents。
释放 spot 并删除 ticket。
why: 必须先有 ticket 才能知道 entryTime 和 spotId；删除 ticket 前要先取够计费和释放所需的数据。
why_en: Exit fee calculation uses the active ticket's entry time, rounds duration up, multiplies by the rate, and only then clears state.
tradeoff: 先读后清理保证数据完整 vs 先清理导致计费数据丢失

scenario: 所有 car spotId 都已经在 occupiedSpotIds 中，此时来了一辆车，车辆类型为 CAR。
scenario_en: All car spot IDs are already in occupiedSpotIds, and now a CAR arrives.
q: enter(CAR) 应该如何处理？
q_en: How should enter(CAR) behave?
options: 发一张 ticket，但 spotId 留空
拒绝入场，且不创建 ticket
临时占用一个 motorcycle spot
把最早入场的旧 ticket 强制删除
why: 没有兼容空位时不能创建停车会话；创建一张没有 spot 的 ticket 会破坏 exit 释放逻辑的不变量。
why_en: Entry must fail without creating a ticket when no compatible spot is available.
whenOtherWins: 如果支持候补排队，可以创建一个 WaitingRequest，但那不是基础 ticket 流程。
tradeoff: 无空位时拒绝并保持状态不变 vs 创建残缺 ticket 破坏不变量
options_en: Issue a ticket but leave spotId empty.
Reject entry and create no ticket at all.
Temporarily occupy a motorcycle spot instead.
Force-remove the oldest active ticket to make room.
optionExplanations: spotId 留空的票据后面没法出场释放车位，等于制造了一条无法闭环的记录。
没有兼容空位时最直接的做法就是不创建任何状态、直接拒绝，保持系统状态一致。
car 不兼容 motorcycle spot，临时借用会破坏『按车型精确匹配』这条基础规则。
强制清退别人正在使用的合法车位，本质上是抢别人的车位来解决自己的容量问题。
optionExplanations_en: A ticket with an empty spotId has no spot to release at exit later — it creates a record that can never close cleanly.
With no compatible spot available, the most direct move is to create no state at all and simply reject, keeping the system consistent.
A car isn't compatible with a motorcycle spot; borrowing one anyway breaks the exact-type-match rule the base design relies on.
Force-evicting someone else's legitimate, still-active session is really just stealing their spot to solve your own capacity problem.

scenario: 多层停车楼希望根据不同目标（靠近出口/均衡/靠近目的地）选择不同分配策略。
scenario_en: A multi-floor garage wants to switch allocation policies based on goals such as nearest exit, load balancing, or destination proximity.
q: 何时应该引入 AllocationStrategy？
q_en: When should AllocationStrategy be introduced?
options: 单层 exact-match 场景一开始就必须引入
当 Ticket 没有 entryTime 字段时
当金额改用 cents 存储时
当分配规则会在低楼层优先、均衡、目的地接近等策略间切换时
why: Strategy 模式适合真实存在、可能被替换的算法；基础单一规则下直接实现更简洁。
why_en: AllocationStrategy earns its complexity when spot-selection policy genuinely varies and needs to be swapped.
whenOtherWins: 如果只有单层、单一规则，不必引入 Strategy，直接 inline 实现更清楚。
tradeoff: 真实可替换算法才上 Strategy vs 单一规则直接内联实现
options_en: The single-floor exact-match case must introduce it right away.
When the Ticket has no entryTime field.
When money switches to storing cents.
When allocation policy genuinely switches among lowest-floor-first, balanced, and destination-proximity strategies.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["one simple allocation rule"] --> B["inline method"]
  C["multiple changing policies"] --> D["AllocationStrategy"]
  D --> E["nearest, cheapest, level aware"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可替换的算法封装成独立类，运行时可以互换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms as separate classes that can be swapped at runtime.

optionExplanations: 只有一条精确匹配规则时还没有『多种算法互换』这个需求，一开始就上 Strategy 是提前抽象。
entryTime 缺不缺跟怎么选车位是两回事，这个条件跟分配策略没有因果关系。
金额存储方式是计费问题，跟车位该怎么分配是完全不相关的两条逻辑。
当低楼层优先、均衡、目的地接近这些规则会互相替换或组合时，『可插拔算法』的需求才真正出现，Strategy 才值回复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: With only one exact-match rule, there's no 'swap between algorithms' need yet — introducing Strategy at the start is abstracting too early.
Whether entryTime exists is unrelated to how a spot gets chosen; that condition has no causal link to allocation policy.
How money is stored is a billing concern, entirely separate from the logic of choosing a spot.
Once rules like lowest-floor-first, balanced, and destination-proximity actually need to swap or combine, a genuine 'pluggable algorithm' need shows up — that's when Strategy earns its complexity.

q: 补全三类对象的职责：
q_en: Fill in the responsibilities of the three object types:
text: ParkingLot 管 {{分配、activeTickets、occupiedSpotIds、计费}}；ParkingSpot 管 {{id 和 spotType}}；Ticket 管 {{ticketId、spotId、vehicleType、entryTime}}。
why: 职责边界清晰后，入场和出场流程都变成 orchestrator 对简单记录和物理资源的协调。
why_en: ParkingLot owns workflows and indexes, ParkingSpot owns intrinsic spot properties, and Ticket records a session.

q: Senior 级 Parking Lot 回答应主动覆盖哪些技术要点？（多选）
q_en: Which technical points should a senior-level Parking Lot answer cover proactively? (Select all that apply.)
options: Vehicle 不建实体的理由
occupied flag / derived / Set 三种方案的权衡
Ticket 用 map 按 ID 查找的理由
金额用整数 cents 存储
多入口并发 race 的成因和加锁方案
why: 高级答案要能主动解释状态归属、数据结构选择和并发正确性，而不仅仅是列出类图。
why_en: Senior answers explain entity pruning, occupancy tradeoffs, ticket lookup, integer money, and multi-entrance races without being prompted.
options_en: Why Vehicle is not modeled as an entity.
The tradeoffs among flag, derived, and Set approaches to occupancy.
Why Ticket lookup uses a map keyed by ID.
Storing money as integer cents.
The cause of multi-entrance races and how to lock against them.
optionExplanations: 能主动说清车辆为什么只是分类标签而不是实体，说明理解状态归属这条主线。
能对比三种占用方案的查找成本和加锁边界，说明不是死记答案，而是懂权衡。
能说出用 map 而不是 list 的原因，展示的是对数据结构选择背后意图的理解。
主动提到用整数分存钱，说明对精度这类容易被单独追问的细节有防备。
能主动指出多入口下的 race 窗口并给出加锁方案，是这道题体现并发意识的关键得分点。
optionExplanations_en: Being able to explain unprompted why Vehicle stays a label instead of an entity shows the candidate follows the state-modeling thread.
Comparing lookup cost and locking boundaries across the three occupancy approaches shows real tradeoff understanding, not a memorized answer.
Explaining why a map beats a list demonstrates understanding of the intent behind a data-structure choice, not just the choice itself.
Volunteering integer-cent storage shows the candidate is ahead of a precision question the interviewer might otherwise probe separately.
Proactively naming the multi-entrance race window and its fix is the key signal of concurrency awareness in this problem.

q: 按顺序排列 Parking Lot 的主设计链路：
q_en: Put the main Parking Lot design argument in order:
steps: ParkingLot 作为入口，持有 spots、occupiedSpotIds、activeTickets、hourlyRateCents。
澄清三类车、自动兼容分配、ticket、出场计费和释放。
Vehicle 降级为 enum，Ticket 建成不可变会话记录。
占用建模为 ParkingLot 维护的关系索引 Set。
enter/exit 分别原子维护 ticket 和 occupied spot 状态。
why: 从范围澄清到实体裁剪，再到状态归属和流程不变量，是这道题的主要论证路径。
why_en: The design chain moves from scoped requirements to entity pruning, orchestrator state, occupancy indexing, and lifecycle updates.
tradeoff: 范围裁剪先行再定状态归属 vs 一上来就画类图

scenario: 系统需要同时用 occupiedSpotIds 和 activeTickets 两个索引描述同一次停车会话，两者必须保持同步。
scenario_en: The system uses both occupiedSpotIds and activeTickets to describe the same parking session, and the two indexes must stay in sync.
q: 面试收尾时，哪一句最准确地总结这个不变量？
q_en: Which closing sentence best summarizes this invariant in an interview?
options: 系统里每一辆曾经进出过的车辆，不管现在是否已经离开车场了，都必须始终对应一个持久化保存完整状态的 Vehicle 实体类
active ticket 指向的 spotId 必须在 occupiedSpotIds 中；成功 exit 后二者都要被删除
所有车位的编号命名必须在整个停车场范围内按楼层严格连续排序
所有发出的 ticket 只要生成成功就永久有效，理论上永远不会失效或过期
why: ParkingLot 用两个索引表达同一会话；入场同时创建两者，出场同时清理两者，才能避免重复出场或重复分配。
why_en: The key invariant is that active tickets and occupied spot IDs stay in sync for every parking session.
whenOtherWins: 如果从 activeTickets 推导 occupancy，就不需要维护 Set，但分配时要保护对 tickets 的读取和修改。
tradeoff: 双索引同步的不变量 vs 单一来源但需要每次重新推导
options_en: Every single vehicle that has ever entered, whether or not it has already left the lot by now, must always have a persisted, fully stateful Vehicle entity class.
The spotId an active ticket points to must be in occupiedSpotIds, and a successful exit removes both.
Spot numbers must be strictly and continuously sorted by floor across the entire lot.
Every issued ticket stays valid forever once created, theoretically never expiring or timing out.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统在任何时刻都必须保持成立的约束。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An invariant is a condition the system must always keep true.

optionExplanations: 车辆从头到尾都只是分类标签，这句总结把它错误地升级成了需要持久化的实体。
两个索引描述同一件事，出场那一刻必须同时清理，这才是真正撑住系统的不变量。
车位编号怎么命名是展示细节，不是这道题真正要保护的正确性约束。
如果票据永远有效，重复出场和重复释放的风险就无法被排除，这跟不变量的方向正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: A vehicle was only ever a classification label; this statement wrongly promotes it to something requiring persisted entity state.
Both indexes describe the same fact and must always agree, with exit clearing both at the same moment — that's what actually holds the system together.
How spot numbers are labeled is a display detail, not the correctness constraint this problem is protecting.
If a ticket stayed valid forever, double-exit and double-release risk could never be ruled out — the opposite of what the invariant guarantees.

scenario: 面试官按中级候选人的标准评估这道 Parking Lot 设计。
scenario_en: The interviewer evaluates this Parking Lot design at the mid-level candidate bar.
q: 中级候选人在本题应能稳定说明什么？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate be able to explain reliably in this problem?
options: 必须一次性实现多层楼分配策略并处理跨楼层并发锁
无论如何都必须使用数据库事务加上 SELECT FOR UPDATE 语句来保证强一致性
必须把 Vehicle 建成完整类并存车主、车牌信息
ParkingLot 编排、ParkingSpot 存属性、Ticket 是记录，能处理三类边界情况
why: 中级重点是职责清晰和关键边界情况；多层策略和并发多入口是高级候选人再深入的部分。
why_en: A mid-level answer should clearly separate ParkingLot, ParkingSpot, and Ticket and handle the key entry and exit edge cases.
tradeoff: 中级看职责分离与边界情况 vs 高级才要求的并发/多层深挖
options_en: Implement multi-floor allocation and cross-floor concurrency locking in one pass.
Database transactions plus a SELECT FOR UPDATE statement must always be used no matter what, to guarantee strong consistency.
Build Vehicle as a full class storing owner and license-plate information.
ParkingLot orchestrates, ParkingSpot stores properties, Ticket is a record, and it handles the three key edge cases.
optionExplanations: 多层分配和跨楼层并发是这道题深挖之后才出现的加分项，不是中级候选人一次要做完的基线。
题目场景是内存态设计，数据库事务是持久化层的加分项，不是中级候选人的硬性门槛。
把 Vehicle 建成完整类恰好是这道题要避免的过度设计，中级候选人应反过来说明为什么不这么做。
分清谁编排、谁存属性、谁是记录，再处理满位、无效票据、重复出场三类边界情况，是中级候选人真正的及格线。
optionExplanations_en: Multi-floor allocation and cross-floor concurrency only show up once the problem gets pushed deeper — they aren't the mid-level baseline for a single pass.
This scenario is an in-memory design; database transactions are a persistence-layer bonus, not a hard bar for a mid-level candidate.
Building Vehicle as a full class is exactly the over-engineering this problem wants avoided — a mid-level candidate should explain why not, if anything.
Separating who orchestrates, who stores properties, and who is a record, plus handling the full-lot, invalid-ticket, and double-exit edge cases, is the actual mid-level bar here.

scenario: entryTime 和 exitTime 相同，车辆几乎立刻出场。
scenario_en: entryTime and exitTime are the same because the vehicle exits almost immediately.
q: 按『hourly rounded up』规则，durationMillis 为 0 时应如何思考？
q_en: Under an hourly-rounded-up rule, how should you reason about durationMillis = 0?
options: 永远都应该直接收取 0，完全不追问产品是否需要设定最低消费门槛
永远收 24 小时，把这种情况当成整天处理
是否收 0 或 1 小时要先向产品澄清；非零但不足一小时仍向上收 1 小时
认为这种边界情况在数学上根本无法算出费用
why: 计费规则强调部分小时向上取整，但 0 分钟是否有最低收费属于产品语义，面试中应该主动澄清或明确定义，而不是自己假设。
why_en: Partial hours clearly round up, but the exact zero-duration minimum charge is a product rule that should be clarified rather than assumed.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务明确规定最低一小时收费，那么 duration 为 0 时也直接返回一小时的费用。
tradeoff: 边界语义需要产品澄清 vs 默认套用向上取整规则
options_en: It should always just charge exactly 0 outright every time, without ever asking product whether a minimum charge applies.
Always charge 24 hours, treating this edge case as a full day.
Clarify with product whether 0 or 1 hour applies; any nonzero partial hour still rounds up to 1.
Claim this edge case is mathematically impossible to bill at all.

termDefinitions.meaning: 无论实际使用多短，至少收取的费用下限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A minimum charge is the smallest fee charged regardless of how briefly the resource was used.

optionExplanations: 直接收 0 是自己替产品做了『不设最低消费』的决定，边界语义没有被真正澄清。
把瞬间出场当成整天收费缺乏依据，跟计费规则里『向上取整到小时』的粒度完全对不上。
取整规则本身很清楚，但零时长要不要收最低一小时是产品语义，主动提出澄清比自己瞎猜更稳妥。
取模加乘法就能算出 0，这个边界情况在数学上没有任何障碍。
optionExplanations_en: Charging 0 outright silently decides on the product's behalf that there's no minimum charge — the edge case was never actually clarified.
Billing a full day for an instant exit has no basis; it doesn't match the hourly rounding granularity the rule actually describes.
The rounding rule itself is clear, but whether zero duration still hits a one-hour minimum is a product decision — raising it beats guessing.
Modulo plus multiplication computes 0 without issue; there's no mathematical obstacle in this edge case at all.

q: 限流器基础设计的需求范围，哪些正确？
options: 配置只在系统启动时加载一次
请求只携带 clientId 和 endpoint 两个字符串
每个 endpoint 可以指定不同算法和参数
结果包含 allowed、remaining、retryAfterMs 三个字段
支持运行时动态更新已加载的配置
options_en: Configuration is loaded exactly once at startup.
A request carries only two strings: clientId and endpoint.
Each endpoint can specify its own algorithm and parameters.
The result has three fields: allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs.
The system supports hot-reloading configuration at runtime.
why: 基础设计把配置加载、请求输入、endpoint 策略和结构化结果先固定下来；运行时热更新会引入原子替换或保状态更新，不在这版范围内。
why_en: The base design fixes startup config, simple request keys, per-endpoint policies, and structured results; hot reload is out of scope.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识发起请求客户端的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: clientId is the string that uniquely identifies the caller making a request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被限流的 API 路径标识，用作查配置的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: endpoint is the API path used as the lookup key for its rate-limit config.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求被拒绝时，建议客户端等待多少毫秒后重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: retryAfterMs tells a denied caller how many milliseconds to wait before retrying.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务不重启的情况下加载并应用新配置。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hot reload applies new configuration without restarting the service.

q_en: Which requirements are in scope for the base rate limiter design? (Select all that apply.)
optionExplanations: 启动时读一次配置就够，构造阶段可以直接创建好所有 limiter，不用为运行中 reload 铺路。
clientId 和 endpoint 这两个字符串就是查表和限流 key 的全部输入，不需要更复杂的请求对象。
algorithm 字段按 endpoint 区分，Factory 才能给不同 endpoint 建不同的 Limiter 实现。
allowed/remaining/retryAfterMs 一起返回，调用方才能设置响应头、显示剩余额度和重试提示。
热更新配置属于后续扩展题——基础版本里配置只在启动时加载，改这条会牵出原子替换或保状态更新的复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: Startup-only config load means the constructor can create every limiter once, with no live-reload path to build for.
clientId and endpoint are the only two strings needed to look up a policy and key a limiter — nothing more elaborate.
The algorithm field varies per endpoint, so the factory builds a different Limiter for each one.
allowed, remaining, and retryAfterMs travel together so callers can set headers, show quota, or hint a retry.
Hot-reloading config is a later extension — the base design loads config once at startup, and adding this pulls in atomic swap or state-preserving update complexity.

scenario: 请求只以 clientId 和 endpoint 两个字符串进入系统，处理后立即用于查 limiter 和 key。
scenario_en: Requests enter only as clientId and endpoint strings, then immediately route to a limiter and key.
q: Request/Client/Endpoint 应如何建模？
q_en: How should Request, Client, and Endpoint be modeled?
options: 都保持为输入字符串或 key，不建实体
三者都建成复杂类
Endpoint 继承 Limiter
Client 保存所有算法状态
options_en: Keep all three as plain input strings or lookup keys — no entity classes.
Turn all three into full-blown classes.
Make Endpoint inherit from Limiter.
Let Client hold all algorithm state.
why: 这些对象在系统内没有生命周期或行为。真正有状态的是具体 Limiter 的 per-key 记录。
why_en: Request, client, and endpoint are input keys, while limiter implementations own the rate-limit state.
whenOtherWins: 如果要管理客户端套餐、endpoint 元数据或请求上下文，才可能新增实体。
tradeoff: 建实体便于未来扩展 vs YAGNI 精简（无行为就不建类）

termDefinitions.meaning: “你不会需要它”，即不要为不存在的需求预先构建功能的设计原则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: YAGNI stands for "you aren't gonna need it," meaning don't build for requirements that don't exist yet.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个 key 独立维护的状态数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key state is state tracked independently for each key.

optionExplanations: clientId/endpoint 没有行为也没有生命周期，直接当 map key 用就够，不用为它们建实体类。
假设每个名词都得有类，会造出三个没有行为的空壳类，违反 YAGNI。
把纯标签误当成算法子类型——Endpoint 和 Limiter 语义完全不同，继承在这里是误用。
把 per-key 算法状态错放进 Client，会让 Client 要感知每种算法的字段，职责被搞乱。
optionExplanations_en: clientId and endpoint have no behavior or lifecycle, so they stay plain lookup keys instead of becoming entity classes.
This assumes every noun needs a class, producing three empty shells that violate YAGNI.
This treats a plain label as an algorithm subtype — Endpoint and Limiter mean completely different things, so inheritance misuses it here.
This puts per-key algorithm state in Client, forcing it to know every algorithm's fields and blurring ownership.

q: 最终设计中的核心类型有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core types are in the final design? (Select all that apply.)
options: RateLimiter
Limiter interface
LimiterFactory
RateLimitResult
TokenBucketLimiter / SlidingWindowLogLimiter
Client 类持有该用户的完整请求历史
options_en: RateLimiter.
Limiter interface.
LimiterFactory.
RateLimitResult.
TokenBucketLimiter / SlidingWindowLogLimiter.
A Client class holds the user's full request history.
why: 五个类型对应编排、算法契约、创建、结果封装和具体算法；Client 不是实体，请求历史归属具体 Limiter 的 per-key state。
why_en: The five real types cover orchestration, the algorithm contract, creation, the result object, and concrete algorithms, while Client is deliberately not modeled as an entity.
diagram:
classDiagram
  class RateLimiter
  class Limiter {
    +allow(key)
  }
  class LimiterFactory
  class RateLimitResult
  RateLimiter --> Limiter
  RateLimiter --> LimiterFactory
  Limiter <|.. TokenBucket
  Limiter <|.. SlidingWindowLog

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统入口/编排类，负责按 endpoint 路由到具体 Limiter。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RateLimiter is the entry-point class that routes each request to the right Limiter implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 统一的限流算法接口，只有 allow(key) 一个方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Limiter is the common interface every rate-limiting algorithm implements, with a single allow(key) method.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据配置中的 algorithm 字段创建具体 Limiter 实例的工厂类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LimiterFactory reads the algorithm field in config and instantiates the matching Limiter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 封装 allowed/remaining/retryAfterMs 的不可变结果对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RateLimitResult is an immutable value object packaging the allowed flag, remaining quota, and retry time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个 key 独立维护的状态数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key state is state tracked independently for each key.

optionExplanations: RateLimiter 是请求进来的编排入口，按 endpoint 路由到具体 Limiter。
Limiter 只暴露 allow(key) 一个方法，是所有算法共用的契约。
LimiterFactory 把配置解析和具体类创建集中到一处，新增算法不用碰其他类。
RateLimitResult 是不可变值对象，封装 allowed/remaining/retryAfterMs。
TokenBucketLimiter 和 SlidingWindowLogLimiter 是两个具体算法实现，各自管理自己的 per-key state。
把请求历史放进 Client 放错了所有者——它不该管理任何算法状态，那是各 Limiter 实现自己的事。
optionExplanations_en: RateLimiter is the entry point that routes each incoming request to the right Limiter.
Limiter exposes just one method, allow(key) — the single contract every algorithm implements.
LimiterFactory centralizes config parsing and object creation, so adding an algorithm never touches other classes.
RateLimitResult is an immutable value object packaging allowed, remaining, and retryAfterMs.
TokenBucketLimiter and SlidingWindowLogLimiter are the two concrete algorithms, each owning its own per-key state.
This puts request history in Client, the wrong owner — algorithm state belongs to each Limiter implementation, not Client.

q: 为什么 Limiter 用 interface 而不是抽象基类共享状态？
q_en: Why use a Limiter interface instead of an abstract base class with shared state?
options: 不同算法的 per-key 状态完全不同，抽象基类不会有共享字段
假设 Java 语法完全不支持抽象类这种机制
误以为 interface 能自动帮你解析配置字段
误以为所有算法都必须共用同一个 timestamp 队列
options_en: Different algorithms need completely different per-key state, so an abstract base class would have no shared fields.
This assumes Java's language syntax does not support abstract classes at all.
This mistakenly assumes an interface can auto-parse config fields.
This mistakenly assumes every algorithm must share one timestamp queue.
why: Token Bucket 需要 tokens/lastRefillTime，Sliding Window Log 需要 timestamp queue，没有共同字段可提取，基类只会是空壳。
why_en: Limiter is an interface because algorithms have different per-key state and only share the allow contract, so a base class would carry no shared fields.
tradeoff: interface：零共享但形状统一 vs 抽象基类：可共享字段但常是空壳

termDefinitions.meaning: 只声明方法契约、不含状态实现的类型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An interface declares a method contract without holding shared state or implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 可以包含共享字段和默认实现、且不能直接实例化的父类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An abstract base class can hold shared fields and default logic and cannot be instantiated directly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个 key 独立维护的状态数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key state is state tracked independently for each key.

optionExplanations: TokenBucket 要 tokens/lastRefillTime，SlidingWindowLog 要 timestamp queue，两者没有可提取的公共字段。
把设计选择误判成语言限制——Java 完全支持抽象类，只是这里没必要用。
把配置解析的职责错放到接口上——那其实是 Factory 该干的事。
把一种算法的队列状态硬套给所有算法，TokenBucket 会被迫持有它用不到的队列。
optionExplanations_en: TokenBucket needs tokens/lastRefillTime while SlidingWindowLog needs a timestamp queue — the two share no extractable field.
This mistakes a design choice for a language limit — Java fully supports abstract classes, it's just unnecessary here.
This puts config-parsing duty on the interface, when that job actually belongs to the factory.
This forces one algorithm's queue state onto every algorithm, so TokenBucket would carry a queue it never uses.

scenario: 配置 JSON 中 algorithm 字段可能是 TokenBucket 或 SlidingWindowLog，参数结构不同。
scenario_en: The config JSON has an algorithm field, either TokenBucket or SlidingWindowLog, and each algorithm has different parameters.
q: 创建具体 Limiter 的逻辑应放在哪里？
q_en: Where should the logic for creating concrete Limiters live?
options: LimiterFactory.create(configData)
RateLimitResult 构造函数
每次 allow() 的调用点里 switch
clientId 字符串方法
options_en: LimiterFactory.create(configData).
Inside the RateLimitResult constructor.
A switch statement at every allow() call site.
A method on the clientId string.
why: Factory 集中处理异构配置和算法类型选择。RateLimiter 构造时只调用 factory，不散落 switch。

q: 为什么 retryAfterMs 不用 0 表示“无需等待”？

options: null 表示'不适用'，避免和'0ms 立即可重试'混淆

This mistakenly assumes JSON cannot represent the number zero.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求被拒绝时，建议客户端等待多少毫秒后重试。

This confuses unit clarity with data type — the Ms suffix already states the unit, no string needed.

create(config)
    algorithm = config['algorithm']
    algo = config['algoConfig']
    switch algorithm
        case 'TokenBucket':
            return TokenBucketLimiter(algo['capacity'], algo['refillRatePerSecond'])
        case 'SlidingWindowLog':
            return SlidingWindowLogLimiter(algo['maxRequests'], algo['windowMs'])

            throw UnknownAlgorithm
options: Factory 根据配置 discriminator 创建具体 Limiter 策略

scenario: 系统启动时配置了几十个 endpoint。
scenario_en: At startup, the system has a few dozen configured endpoints.
q: 为什么构造时 eager 创建所有 limiters 合理？
q_en: Why is eager creation of all limiters reasonable in the constructor?
options: 端点数通常不大，eager 创建比懒创建的同步复杂度更简单
误以为每个请求都必须重新创建 limiter
误以为 eager 创建会自动清理内存
误以为 lazy 创建在技术上无法实现
options_en: Endpoint counts are usually small, and eager creation avoids the sync complexity of lazy creation.
This mistakenly assumes a limiter must be recreated on every request.
This mistakenly assumes eager creation automatically frees memory.
This mistakenly assumes lazy creation is technically impossible.
why: 启动配置固定，几十到几百个小对象内存成本低，eager 初始化不需要处理并发首次创建，更容易推理。

whenOtherWins: 如果有数千 endpoint 且大多数没有流量，lazy creation 才可能值得。
tradeoff: 启动时一次性创建、无需加锁 vs 首次请求才创建、需处理并发初始化

termDefinitions.meaning: 启动时就把所有对象提前创建好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eager creation builds every object up front at startup instead of on demand.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有第一次用到时才创建对象。

optionExplanations: 几十到几百个 endpoint 内存成本可忽略，启动时一次建好还省掉了首次并发创建的加锁逻辑。

把创建时机和内存回收机制搞混——eager 创建不负责清理，回收要靠 TTL/LRU。
lazy creation 完全可以实现，只是要多处理一步首次并发的场景。
optionExplanations_en: Endpoint counts are usually a few dozen, so building every limiter once at startup skips the sync complexity of lazy first-use creation.
This treats limiters as disposable per request — rebuilding would lose per-key state and break limiting.
This confuses creation timing with memory cleanup — eager creation reclaims nothing; that's TTL or LRU's job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 key 一个令牌桶，按固定速率补充令牌，允许短时突发。

q: Token Bucket 的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff of Token Bucket?
options: 允许突发到 capacity，按平均速率补充
精确保存窗口内每次请求的时间戳，代价是内存更高
窗口边界实现简单，但边缘可能放过突刺流量
完全不需要维护任何 per-key 状态信息
options_en: It allows bursts up to capacity while refilling at the average rate.
It precisely stores every request's timestamp, at the cost of more memory.
The fixed window is simple to build but can leak bursts at its edge.
It needs to maintain no per-key state information at all.

why_en: Token bucket allows bursts up to capacity while enforcing an average refill rate, unlike exact-timestamp or fixed-window approaches.
tradeoff: 允许短时突发（token 桶） vs 严格恒定速率（无缓冲）

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 key 一个令牌桶，按固定速率补充令牌，允许短时突发。

That's actually sliding window log's tradeoff, not token bucket's.
That's actually fixed window counter's own boundary error, unrelated to token bucket.

q: TokenBucket.tokens 为什么可以用 double？

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理完当前请求后，调用方还剩多少可用额度。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A boundary burst happens when requests cluster around two adjacent window edges and nearly double the short-term allowance.

这其实是 Sliding Window Log 的成本——Fixed Window 只存 count 和 windowStart。
把结果字段能力说错了——remaining 完全可以用 limit 减 count 算出。
把 key 维度和窗口算法混为一谈——只要用 clientId 当 key 建 counter，照样能按 client 限流。
optionExplanations_en: Two adjacent window edges can each allow a full quota, so short-term traffic can approach double the limit.
That's actually sliding window log's cost — fixed window only stores count and windowStart.
This misstates what the result can report — remaining is just limit minus count.
This confuses key choice with the window algorithm — keying the counter by clientId still gives per-client limiting.

scenario: 两个线程同时对同一个 client 的 TokenBucket 调用 allow，bucket.tokens=1。
scenario_en: Two threads call allow for the same client's TokenBucket at the same time, with bucket.tokens=1.
q: 如果没有同步会怎样？
q_en: What happens without synchronization?
options: 两个线程都可能看到 1 并都允许，超过限制
误以为运行时会让一个线程自动等待
误以为并发 bug 会让 tokens 变成无限大
误以为 Java 会禁止多线程读取 double
options_en: Both threads can see tokens=1, both allow, and the limit is exceeded.
This mistakenly assumes the runtime makes one thread wait automatically.
This mistakenly assumes the race would make tokens grow unbounded.
This mistakenly assumes Java blocks concurrent reads of a double.
why: 同一 key 的额度判断和扣减必须在一个临界区里完成；否则并发请求会绕过“一份额度只放行一次”的约束。
why_en: Without synchronization, two threads can both read the same token count and both consume the same single token.
whenOtherWins: 如果限流器保证单线程调用（比如单个 event loop），确实不需要额外加锁。
tradeoff: 不加锁的高吞吐 vs check-then-act 竞态导致超发

termDefinitions.meaning: 多线程同时读写共享状态、结果依赖执行顺序的并发错误。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A race condition is a bug where concurrent threads read and write shared state and the outcome depends on timing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先读旧值、再基于旧值计算、最后写回的三步操作，若不原子化就会产生竞态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Read-modify-write is the read-then-update-then-write sequence that must be atomic or it produces a race condition.

optionExplanations: 这是经典的 check-then-act 竞态——两个线程各自扣减，实际放行了 2 个请求却只有 1 个额度。
误以为运行时会自动帮你排队——没有 synchronized/锁，线程根本不会等待。
误以为竞态会让数值往错误方向暴涨——实际后果通常是丢更新、超发，不是数值爆炸。
误以为 double 类型自带并发保护——Java 允许任何线程自由读写基本类型。
optionExplanations_en: This is the classic check-then-act race — each thread deducts independently, so two requests pass on one credit.
This wrongly assumes the runtime auto-queues threads — without synchronized or a lock, nothing makes them wait.
This wrongly assumes the race pushes values toward infinity — the real outcome is lost updates and over-admission.
This wrongly assumes a double has built-in concurrency protection — Java lets any thread freely read or write it.

scenario: 需要支持不同 client 并发检查限流，只有同一 client 互相阻塞。
scenario_en: Different clients should be checked concurrently, while only the same client blocks itself.
q: 标准方案是什么？
q_en: What is the standard solution?
options: ConcurrentHashMap 原子建 bucket，再锁 bucket 本身
误以为必须给整个 RateLimiter 系统加一把粗粒度全局锁
误以为只要 tokens 字段用 double 类型就不需要任何锁
误以为每个请求都该重新创建一个全新的 bucket 对象
options_en: Atomically get-or-create the bucket via ConcurrentHashMap, then synchronize on the bucket itself.
This mistakenly assumes the whole RateLimiter system needs one coarse global lock.
This mistakenly assumes storing tokens as a double removes the need for any lock.
This mistakenly assumes a brand-new bucket object must be created per request.
why: per-key locking 让 client A 和 B 并行，同一 key 的状态更新串行；全局锁会让所有请求排队，过度阻塞。
why_en: Per-key locking synchronizes only requests for the same client while allowing different clients to proceed concurrently.
whenOtherWins: 极低吞吐或快速面试实现可用全局锁，但不是高并发场景下的默认选择。
tradeoff: per-key 锁只挡同一 client vs 全局锁挡住所有 client
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[client A] --> LA[lock A]
  B[client B] --> LB[lock B]
  LA --> SA[state A]
  LB --> SB[state B]
  C[client A again] -.waits.-> LA

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持多线程安全并发读写的哈希表实现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ConcurrentHashMap is a hash map implementation safe for concurrent multi-threaded reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只对同一个 key 的并发请求加锁，不同 key 互不阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key locking only serializes concurrent requests for the same key, so different keys never block each other.

optionExplanations: 锁的粒度精确到单个 key——client A、B 互不阻塞，只有同一 client 的请求会串行。
锁的粒度粗到整个系统——所有 client 的请求都要排队，吞吐会大跌。
误以为数据类型能替代同步机制——double 的读写在多线程下依然会竞态。
误以为可以绕开状态共享问题——每请求新建 bucket 会丢失该 client 已有的限流历史。
optionExplanations_en: The lock granularity is exactly one key — clients A and B never block each other, only same-client requests serialize.
This makes the lock granularity the whole system — every client's requests queue up and throughput drops sharply.
This wrongly assumes a data type can replace synchronization — reading and writing a double still races.
This wrongly assumes shared state can be sidestepped — a fresh bucket per request would lose that client's history.

scenario: 给 TokenBucketLimiter 加线程安全。
scenario_en: Make TokenBucketLimiter thread-safe.
q: 这段伪代码的并发边界是什么？
q_en: What is the concurrency boundary in this pseudocode?
codeSample:
bucket = buckets.computeIfAbsent(key, k -> TokenBucket(capacity, now()))
synchronized(bucket)
    now = currentTimeMillis()
    refill(bucket, now)
    if bucket.tokens >= 1
        bucket.tokens -= 1
        allowed = true
    else
        allowed = false
return Result(...)
options: bucket 创建是原子的，同一 key 的读改写都在 bucket 锁内完成
误以为这段代码会把所有 key 全局串行化
误以为 synchronized 只保护 Result 对象的构造
误以为 computeIfAbsent 顺带完成了扣减 token
options_en: Bucket creation is atomic, and the same key's read-modify-write happens inside the bucket lock.
This mistakenly assumes this code globally serializes every key.
This mistakenly assumes synchronized only protects building the Result.
This mistakenly assumes computeIfAbsent also deducts a token.
why: bucket 对象是该 key 的稳定同步点；Result 可以在锁外创建，只要锁内已经捕获了结果字段。
why_en: Atomic bucket creation plus a bucket-level lock protects each client's mutable limiter state.
whenOtherWins: 在没有 computeIfAbsent 的语言中，可用 buckets map 锁保护创建，再用 bucket 自身锁保护状态。
tradeoff: 锁只包住必要的读改写 vs 把无关工作也锁进去拖慢吞吐

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在 key 不存在时原子创建并插入值的 Map 方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: computeIfAbsent atomically creates and inserts a value only when the key is not already present.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让同一时刻只有一个线程能进入某段代码块的关键字。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: synchronized ensures only one thread can execute a code block at a time.

optionExplanations: computeIfAbsent 原子建桶，synchronized(bucket) 把 tokens/lastRefillTime 的读改写圈在同一个临界区里。
把 per-key 锁误当成全局锁——不同 client 本可以并行，被误判成要排队。
把锁的对象搞错了——真正需要保护的是 bucket 内可变字段，Result 构造完全可以在锁外做。
把两个独立操作合并成一个——computeIfAbsent 只负责创建，扣减仍在 synchronized 块里发生。
optionExplanations_en: computeIfAbsent atomically creates the bucket, and synchronized(bucket) wraps the same key's tokens/lastRefillTime read-modify-write.
This mistakes a per-key lock for a global one — different clients could run in parallel but get wrongly serialized.
This misidentifies what's protected — the mutable bucket fields need the lock, not building the Result.
This merges two separate steps — computeIfAbsent only creates the bucket; deduction still happens inside the synchronized block.

scenario: 运行时要更新配置，且可以接受清空已有限流状态。
scenario_en: Runtime config updates are needed, and clearing existing limiter state is acceptable.
q: 最简单方案是什么？
q_en: What is the simplest approach?
options: reloadConfig 重建所有 limiter 并整体原子替换
误以为可以不加任何锁就直接改旧 limiter 的字段值
误以为收到新配置后可以安全地直接忽略它
误以为应该让每次请求都重新读一次配置文件
options_en: reloadConfig rebuilds every limiter and swaps them all atomically.
This mistakenly assumes fields on old limiters can be edited with no lock at all.
This mistakenly assumes a pushed new config can just be safely ignored.
This mistakenly assumes every request should re-read the config file.
why: 重建再原子替换逻辑简单，能处理新增、删除、换算法各种变化；代价是 per-key 状态全部重置。
why_en: Rebuilding limiters and atomically swapping them is the simplest dynamic-config approach, but it loses all per-key state.
whenOtherWins: 如果反滥用或计费要求状态连续，就不能随便重置，需要 updateConfig 保状态方案。
tradeoff: 重建+原子替换的简单性 vs 丢失所有 per-key 历史状态

termDefinitions.meaning: 未配置 endpoint 时使用的兜底 Limiter 实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: defaultLimiter is the fallback Limiter instance used when an endpoint has no specific config.

optionExplanations: 复用启动时的 Factory 创建逻辑重建整份 limiter map，再整体原子替换，能接受状态清空的前提下最简单。
在无保护情况下改运行中的共享对象——并发请求可能读到修改到一半的字段。
假装配置更新没发生——配置服务推送的新规则会永远不生效。
把配置加载和请求处理路径混在一起——每请求读文件的 IO 开销和已知需求矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: It reuses the same startup factory logic to rebuild every limiter, then swaps the whole map in atomically — simplest when a state reset is acceptable.
This edits a running shared object with zero protection — concurrent requests could read a half-updated field.
This pretends the config push never happened — the new rules would never take effect.
This conflates config loading with the request path — per-request file IO is expensive and contradicts the requirements.

q: reloadConfig 全量替换的最大缺点是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest drawback of full reloadConfig replacement?
options: 所有 client 的 token/窗口历史被清空，滥用者也跟着重置
误以为 reloadConfig 没办法切换到别的算法
误以为 reloadConfig 无法新增一个 endpoint
误以为重建 limiter 会让 Result 变成空值
options_en: Every client's token/window history is wiped, giving abusive clients a fresh start too.
This mistakenly assumes reloadConfig cannot switch to a different algorithm.
This mistakenly assumes reloadConfig cannot add a new endpoint.
This mistakenly assumes rebuilding limiters makes Result null.
why: 状态丢失有时可接受，但降低限额或防滥用时，让滥用者拿到 fresh start 会破坏更新的目的。
why_en: Full reload loses per-key limiter history, which is acceptable sometimes but defeats the purpose when tightening limits against abuse.
tradeoff: 重建简单直接 vs per-key 状态连续性被牺牲

termDefinitions.meaning: 重建全部 limiter 并原子替换的配置更新方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: reloadConfig is the update method that rebuilds every limiter and atomically swaps them in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个 key 独立维护的状态数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key state is state tracked independently for each key.

optionExplanations: 全量重建连带清空每个 key 的历史，刚被限制的滥用者也会拿到一份全新配额。
误以为重建不能换实现类——Factory 正好能按新算法字段创建新对象。
误以为重建不能增加路由项——新 endpoint 完全可以随新 map 一起上线。
把 limiter 生命周期和结果对象混淆——Result 是请求返回值，不会因 limiter 重建而变空。
optionExplanations_en: Full rebuild wipes every key's history too, so a client just throttled gets a completely fresh quota again.
This wrongly assumes rebuild can't switch implementation class — the factory handles that from the new algorithm field.
This wrongly assumes rebuild can't add a route — a new endpoint ships fine alongside the new map.
This confuses limiter lifecycle with the result object — Result is a per-request value, unaffected by rebuild.

scenario: 需要在更新 capacity/refillRate 时保留 client 历史。
scenario_en: Client history must be preserved while updating capacity/refillRate.
q: 更复杂但保状态的方案是什么？
q_en: What is the more complex state-preserving approach?
options: 给 Limiter 加 updateConfig，各算法自己调参保留旧 state
误以为还是应该继续用重建全部 limiter 的老办法
误以为配置更新的解析逻辑该写进 RateLimitResult 里
误以为想保留状态就该先删光所有 bucket 再重建
options_en: Add updateConfig to Limiter so each algorithm adjusts its own parameters while keeping existing state.
This mistakenly assumes the old rebuild-every-limiter approach is still the answer.
This mistakenly assumes update-parsing logic belongs inside RateLimitResult.
This mistakenly assumes preserving state means deleting every bucket first.
why: TokenBucket 可更新 capacity/refillRate，并把已有 tokens clamp 到新 capacity；不同算法需要各自不同的更新逻辑。
why_en: State-preserving dynamic config requires each limiter implementation to update its own parameters and existing state.
whenOtherWins: 如果算法类型本身也要改变（比如 TokenBucket 换 SlidingWindowLog），状态不兼容时仍可能需要替换 limiter。
tradeoff: 保留 per-key 历史 vs 每种算法都要写自己的更新逻辑

termDefinitions.meaning: 让每种算法自己调整参数、同时保留已有 per-key 状态的接口方法。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: updateConfig is the interface method letting each algorithm adjust its own parameters while keeping existing per-key state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数值限制在某个上限或下限之内。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: clamp restricts a value so it never exceeds a given upper or lower bound.

optionExplanations: 接口新增一个方法交给各实现自己处理——TokenBucket 降 capacity 时只需 clamp 已有 tokens，不丢历史。
又绕回会清空状态的简单方案——这正是要避免的、把滥用者重置成新用户的结果。
把配置更新的职责放错类——Result 是每次请求的返回值，不该持有配置逻辑。
把“保留状态”做反成了“清空状态”——删光 bucket 后下次请求会被当成全新 client。
optionExplanations_en: Adding updateConfig lets each algorithm handle its own parameters — TokenBucket just clamps existing tokens to the new capacity, no history lost.
This falls back to the state-wiping rebuild approach, exactly the abuser-resetting outcome we're trying to avoid.
This puts update-parsing duty on the wrong class — Result is a per-request return value, not a config holder.
This inverts 'preserve state' into 'wipe state' — deleting every bucket first makes the next request look brand new.

q: 按顺序排列 TokenBucket.updateConfig 的合理行为：
q_en: Put the reasonable TokenBucket.updateConfig behavior in order:
steps: 读取 newCapacity 和 newRefillRatePerSecond。
更新 limiter 参数。
遍历已有 buckets。
如果 bucket.tokens > newCapacity，则截断到 newCapacity。
why: 降低 capacity 时不能让旧 bucket 保留超过新容量的 token；参数更新和遍历 clamp 应放在同一临界区，避免请求线程看到半更新状态。
why_en: Token bucket config updates should adjust parameters and clamp existing buckets to the new capacity inside the same critical section so request threads never observe partial updates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一时刻只允许一个线程执行的代码区域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A critical section is a code region only one thread may execute at a time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数值限制在某个上限或下限之内。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: clamp restricts a value so it never exceeds a given upper or lower bound.

tradeoff: 保状态更新参数 vs 全量重建会清空 client 历史

scenario: 系统服务数百万 clientId，buckets/logs map 不断增长。
scenario_en: The service handles millions of clientIds, so the buckets/logs map keeps growing.
q: 需要什么机制？
q_en: What mechanism is needed?
options: 基于 lastAccess 做 TTL 清理，或用 LRU 做 eviction
误以为可以永远不清理任何 per-key 状态
误以为该用重启整个服务来释放内存
误以为把 clientId 写进日志级别能解决问题
options_en: Clean up by lastAccess-based TTL, or evict with LRU.
This mistakenly assumes per-key state never needs cleanup.
This mistakenly assumes restarting the whole service frees memory.
This mistakenly assumes writing clientId into log level solves it.
why: on-demand 创建的 per-key state 如果不清理会内存泄漏；活跃 client 会持续更新 lastAccess，不活跃状态才会被淘汰。
why_en: Per-key limiter state needs TTL or LRU eviction to prevent unbounded memory growth from millions of clients.
whenOtherWins: 分布式 Redis 实现可以直接用 key TTL 自动过期，省去手写清理逻辑。
tradeoff: 主动淘汰控制内存 vs 无限增长直到 OOM
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A["client bucket map grows"] --> B{"over capacity?"}
  B -- no --> C["keep bucket"]
  B -- yes --> D["evict old idle bucket"]
  D --> E["next request creates fresh bucket"]

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动删除长期不活跃的 per-key 状态以控制内存增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction actively removes long-idle per-key state to keep memory bounded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略，优先删除最久没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU evicts the entry that has gone the longest without being accessed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 给缓存或状态条目设置的过期时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the expiration time set on a cached or tracked entry.

optionExplanations: 按 lastAccess 设 TTL 或用 LRU 淘汰，能让不活跃 client 的状态被回收，活跃的不受影响。
假设内存可以无限增长——数百万 clientId 会让 map 一路涨到 OOM。
把内存管理和服务可用性搞混——重启会丢失所有 client 状态，也不是长期方案。
把日志级别误当成状态清理机制——LogLevel 只影响输出，不会删除任何 per-key state。
optionExplanations_en: TTL by lastAccess or LRU eviction reclaims idle clients' state while leaving active ones untouched.
This assumes memory can grow forever — millions of clientIds would push the map straight to OOM.
This confuses memory management with availability — a restart loses every client's state and isn't a long-term fix.
This mistakes log level for a cleanup mechanism — it only affects output, never deletes per-key state.

q: 淘汰某 client 的 bucket 后，下次请求会怎样？
q_en: What happens on the next request after a client's bucket is evicted?
options: 像首次请求一样新建 state，通常拿到完整 burst capacity
误以为被淘汰的 client 之后会被永久拒绝
误以为淘汰 bucket 会连累 endpoint 路由失效
误以为新建 state 后 remaining 会变成负数
options_en: It creates fresh state like a first-time request, typically with full burst capacity.
This mistakenly assumes the evicted client is denied forever afterward.
This mistakenly assumes evicting a bucket breaks endpoint routing too.
This mistakenly assumes remaining goes negative after fresh state is created.
why: 这对长期不活跃 client 通常可接受；活跃 client 不会被淘汰，因为它们的 lastAccess 会持续刷新。
why_en: After eviction, the next request creates fresh state, typically granting a new initial quota.
tradeoff: 淘汰后 fresh start（简单） vs 完全丢失该 client 的限流历史

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动删除长期不活跃的 per-key 状态以控制内存增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction actively removes long-idle per-key state to keep memory bounded.

optionExplanations: 淘汰只删旧状态，不删规则——下次请求重新建 bucket，通常从 full capacity 开始。
把一次清理误解为永久封禁——eviction 只是回收内存，不是拉黑。
把 per-key 状态和 endpoint 路由混为一谈——RateLimiter 的路由 map 不受淘汰影响。
误以为新对象会产生非法剩余额度——新建 state 的 remaining 从合法初始值算起。
optionExplanations_en: Eviction only removes old state, not the rule — the next request rebuilds a bucket, usually at full capacity.
This mistakes one cleanup pass for a permanent ban — eviction just reclaims memory, it's not a blacklist.
This confuses per-key state with endpoint routing — the routing map is untouched by eviction.
This wrongly assumes a fresh object yields an invalid remaining value — it's computed from a valid initial quota.

q: 基础题明确 out of scope 的内容有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which items are explicitly out of scope for the basic problem? (Select all that apply.)
options: 分布式 Redis 限流
动态配置更新
指标和监控
复杂配置校验
每个请求都以 clientId 和 endpoint 作为输入
options_en: Distributed rate limiting with Redis.
Dynamic configuration updates.
Metrics and monitoring.
Deep configuration validation.
Every request carries clientId and endpoint as input.
why: 这四项都明确列为 out of scope；clientId+endpoint 输入恰恰是 in-scope 的基础需求，不是被排除的部分。
why_en: These four items are explicitly listed as out of scope, while clientId-plus-endpoint input is an in-scope base requirement, not something excluded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 唯一标识发起请求客户端的字符串。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: clientId is the string that uniquely identifies the caller making a request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被限流的 API 路径标识，用作查配置的 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: endpoint is the API path used as the lookup key for its rate-limit config.

optionExplanations: 跨实例共享限流状态的分布式方案明确排除在基础版本外。
运行时热更新配置也排在 out of scope——基础版本配置只在启动时加载一次。
限流命中率、拒绝率这类指标监控同样不在这版要求里。
配置字段的复杂合法性校验也被排除，基础版本假设配置是可信的。
这其实是 in-scope 的基础输入要求，不是被排除的部分——clientId+endpoint 正是请求必须携带的两个字段。
optionExplanations_en: Sharing limiter state across instances via a distributed backend is explicitly excluded from the base design.
Runtime config hot-reload is also out of scope — the base design only loads config once at startup.
Metrics like hit rate or deny rate are likewise not part of this version's requirements.
Deep validation of config fields is excluded too — the base design trusts the config as given.
This is actually an in-scope base requirement, not something excluded — clientId and endpoint are exactly what every request must carry.

scenario: 要新增 FixedWindowCounterLimiter。
scenario_en: You need to add FixedWindowCounterLimiter.
q: 需要改哪些地方？
q_en: What needs to change?
options: 实现 Limiter 接口，再给 Factory 加一个 case 解析参数
误以为要重写 RateLimiter.allow 这个入口方法
误以为要改动 RateLimitResult 的字段结构
误以为加新算法要先删掉已有的 TokenBucket
options_en: Implement the Limiter interface, then add one case to the factory to parse its parameters.
This mistakenly assumes RateLimiter.allow, the entry point, must be rewritten.
This mistakenly assumes RateLimitResult's fields must change.
This mistakenly assumes adding an algorithm requires deleting TokenBucket first.
why: 这就是 Strategy + Factory 的价值：RateLimiter 只依赖 Limiter 接口，不关心具体算法，新增互不影响已有代码。
why_en: Adding an algorithm means implementing Limiter and teaching the factory to construct it, without touching existing code.
whenOtherWins: 算法插件很多时，factory 里的 switch 可换成 registry，减少每次新增对核心 factory 的修改。
tradeoff: 开闭原则：只加代码不改现有类 vs 每加一个算法都要碰核心类

termDefinitions.meaning: 把可互换的算法封装成同一接口的不同实现的设计模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The strategy pattern encapsulates interchangeable algorithms behind one common interface.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把'根据类型创建哪个具体实现'集中到一个类里的创建型模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The factory pattern centralizes the logic for creating the right concrete implementation from input data.

optionExplanations: 只加一个新实现和一个 Factory case，RateLimiter 和已有算法完全不用碰——这就是 Strategy+Factory 的价值。
把改动范围错误地扩大到入口方法——allow 只做路由委派，不关心具体算法。
把改动范围错误地扩大到结果对象——Result 的字段是通用的，不因算法而变。
把新增和删除混为一谈——TokenBucket 仍在正常工作，不需要移除。
optionExplanations_en: Just add one implementation and one factory case — RateLimiter and existing algorithms stay untouched, exactly what Strategy plus Factory buys you.
This wrongly widens the change to the entry point — allow only routes and delegates, it doesn't know about algorithms.
This wrongly widens the change to the result object — Result's fields are generic and algorithm-independent.
This conflates adding a new algorithm with removing an old one — TokenBucket keeps working fine.

q: remaining 字段表示什么？
q_en: What does the remaining field mean?
options: 当前请求处理之后剩余的可用额度
误以为是请求处理之前的额度
误以为是总配置上限
误以为是 retryAfterMs 的秒数
options_en: The quota still available after the current request is processed.
This mistakenly assumes it is the quota before the request.
This mistakenly assumes it is the configured total limit.
This mistakenly assumes it is retryAfterMs expressed in seconds.
why: 例如 Token Bucket 允许后先扣 1，再 floor(tokens) 返回；remaining 描述调用方后续还能做多少请求，而不是配置上限。
why_en: Remaining represents quota left after processing the current request, not the quota before it or the configured limit.
tradeoff: remaining 反映处理后的状态 vs 若返回处理前的值会多报 1

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理完当前请求后，调用方还剩多少可用额度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: remaining is how much quota the caller has left after this request is processed.

optionExplanations: 允许后先扣 1 再 floor(tokens) 返回，remaining 描述的是这次请求之后还能做多少次。
把返回时点放到了扣减之前——按处理前的值返回会比真实剩余多报 1。
把动态剩余额度当成静态配置——总上限不会反映这个 client 已经用掉多少。
把两个不同的结果字段混在一起——等待时间有自己独立的 retryAfterMs 字段。
optionExplanations_en: After deducting one token, remaining reports floor(tokens) — how many more calls this client can make right now.
This measures before deduction — reporting the pre-request value overstates remaining by one.
This treats a dynamic remaining quota as a static config value, ignoring what this client already spent.
This mixes up two separate fields — wait time has its own retryAfterMs field.

scenario: 请求 endpoint='/unknown'，配置里没有该 endpoint。
scenario_en: A request comes in for endpoint='/unknown', and that endpoint is missing from config.
q: 基础设计如何处理？
q_en: How should the base design handle this?
options: 调用 defaultLimiter.allow 走默认限流
误以为未知 endpoint 应该直接放行所有请求
误以为未知 endpoint 应该直接拒绝所有请求
误以为应该临时创建一个无上限的 limiter
options_en: Call defaultLimiter.allow to apply the default rate limit.
This mistakenly assumes unknown endpoints should be allowed unconditionally.
This mistakenly assumes unknown endpoints should be denied outright.
This mistakenly assumes an unlimited limiter should be created on the fly.
why: 需求明确未配置 endpoint 要使用默认限制，确保所有请求至少有基础保护，而不是被放行或直接拒绝。
why_en: Unknown endpoints fall back to the default limiter instead of bypassing rate limiting or being denied outright.
whenOtherWins: 如果希望未知 endpoint 独立计数，可用 defaultConfig 懒创建各自的 endpoint-specific limiter。
tradeoff: 统一走 default 兜底 vs 未知 endpoint 完全不设限或直接拒绝

termDefinitions.meaning: 未配置 endpoint 时使用的兜底 Limiter 实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: defaultLimiter is the fallback Limiter instance used when an endpoint has no specific config.

optionExplanations: 统一走 default 兜底，任何没配置 endpoint 的请求也至少有一层保护。
把“没有专门配置”误解为“不需要限流”——这会给攻击者一个绕过限流的漏洞。
把还没配置的 endpoint 误判成“应该拒绝”——会误伤所有正常的新 endpoint。
误以为没配置就该无限放行——无上限等于没有限流，风险跟不设限一样。
optionExplanations_en: Falling back to defaultLimiter.allow(clientId) means even an unconfigured endpoint still gets baseline protection.
This misreads 'no specific config' as 'no limiting needed,' handing attackers a way to bypass limiting entirely.
This misjudges an unconfigured endpoint as one that 'should be denied,' wrongly blocking legitimate new endpoints.
This wrongly assumes missing config means unlimited — no cap is functionally the same as no rate limiting.

q: 按顺序排列 TokenBucket 的验证例子：
q_en: Put the TokenBucket verification example in order:
steps: t=0 首次请求创建 tokens=10 的 bucket。
允许请求后 tokens=9，remaining=9。
t=500ms，按 1 token/s 补 0.5，tokens=9.5。
再允许后 tokens=8.5，remaining=floor(8.5)=8。
桶空附近请求被拒绝，并返回补足 1 token 的 retryAfterMs。
why: 验证覆盖首次创建、连续补充、小数 token、扣减和拒绝重试计算，逐步复现真实运行时序。
why_en: The token bucket trace validates first-use capacity, fractional refill, consumption, remaining, and retry timing in order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个 key 一个令牌桶，按固定速率补充令牌，允许短时突发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Token bucket gives each key a bucket that refills at a fixed rate and allows short bursts up to its capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 令牌桶能容纳的最大令牌数，即最大突发量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: capacity is the maximum number of tokens a bucket can hold, i.e. the largest burst it allows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理完当前请求后，调用方还剩多少可用额度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: remaining is how much quota the caller has left after this request is processed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求被拒绝时，建议客户端等待多少毫秒后重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: retryAfterMs tells a denied caller how many milliseconds to wait before retrying.

tradeoff: 用时序例子验证边界 vs 只看静态字段定义容易漏掉扣减时点

q: Senior 级 Rate Limiter 回答应主动覆盖哪些点？（多选）
q_en: What should a senior Rate Limiter answer proactively cover? (Select all that apply.)
options: Factory/Strategy 的边界
on-demand refill vs background refill
per-key locking 而非全局锁
动态配置重建 vs 保状态更新
per-key state eviction
必须提前实现分布式 Redis 限流才算 senior
options_en: The boundary between Factory and Strategy.
On-demand refill versus background refill.
Per-key locking rather than a global lock.
Rebuild-on-reload versus state-preserving config updates.
Per-key state eviction.
You must implement distributed Redis rate limiting to count as senior.
why: 高级答案要覆盖对象边界、补充模型、并发、配置演进和内存上界；分布式 Redis 是扩展话题，不是这道单机 LLD 的门槛。
why_en: A senior answer covers boundaries, refill, per-key concurrency, config evolution, and eviction without requiring distributed Redis.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只对同一个 key 的并发请求加锁，不同 key 互不阻塞。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key locking only serializes concurrent requests for the same key, so different keys never block each other.

termDefinitions.meaning: 主动删除长期不活跃的 per-key 状态以控制内存增长。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction actively removes long-idle per-key state to keep memory bounded.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只在请求到来时按经过时间计算补充量，不用后台线程扫描。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: On-demand refill computes the refill amount from elapsed time only when a request arrives, with no background scanning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存数据存储，可用来做分布式共享限流状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory data store often used to share rate-limit state across processes.

optionExplanations: 说清 Factory 只管创建、Strategy(Limiter)只管算法，两者边界不混。
解释按需补充为什么够用，不用后台线程扫描所有 bucket。
讲清并发正确性靠的是 per-key 锁，不是把所有请求串成一条队。
对比重建全量替换（简单但清状态）和保状态 updateConfig（复杂但保历史）。
说明长期运行下 per-key 状态需要 TTL/LRU，内存不会无限涨。
把本题从单机 LLD 硬拔高成分布式系统实现——分布式 Redis 是扩展话题，不是这道题的门槛。
optionExplanations_en: Explain that the factory only creates while Strategy (Limiter) only runs the algorithm — the boundary stays clean.
Explain why on-demand refill is enough, with no background thread scanning every bucket.
Explain that concurrency correctness comes from per-key locks, not serializing every request behind one lock.
Contrast rebuild-and-swap (simple but wipes state) against state-preserving updateConfig (more work, keeps history).
Explain that per-key state needs TTL or LRU over time, or memory grows without bound.
This inflates a single-node LLD into distributed infrastructure — Redis is the extension topic, not this problem's bar.

q: 按顺序排列 Rate Limiter 主设计链路：
q_en: Put the main Rate Limiter design chain in order:
steps: RateLimiter 持有 endpoint->Limiter 和 defaultLimiter。
澄清启动配置、clientId/endpoint 输入、结构化结果和默认限制。
Limiter interface 让不同算法成为策略。
LimiterFactory 从 algorithm/algoConfig 创建具体 limiter。
具体 limiter 管理自己的 per-key state，并处理线程安全和内存清理扩展。
why: 这个链路从范围和入口到策略、工厂和算法状态，说明 RateLimiter 不应管理所有算法内部字段。
why_en: The design chain moves from scope to routing state, the strategy interface, factory creation, and algorithm-owned per-key state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统入口/编排类，负责按 endpoint 路由到具体 Limiter。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RateLimiter is the entry-point class that routes each request to the right Limiter implementation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据配置中的 algorithm 字段创建具体 Limiter 实例的工厂类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LimiterFactory reads the algorithm field in config and instantiates the matching Limiter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 未配置 endpoint 时使用的兜底 Limiter 实例。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: defaultLimiter is the fallback Limiter instance used when an endpoint has no specific config.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个 key 独立维护的状态数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key state is state tracked independently for each key.

tradeoff: 编排层保持薄 vs 把算法状态塞进 RateLimiter

scenario: 系统改成多线程环境，多个请求可能同时命中同一个 clientId。
scenario_en: The system now runs multi-threaded, so multiple requests may hit the same clientId at once.
q: 哪条不变量最能保证限流仍然正确？
q_en: Which invariant best keeps rate limiting correct?
options: 同一 key 的 state 更新必须原子化，不能让两个请求抢同一份配额
误以为所有 endpoint 必须共用同一种算法
误以为 retryAfterMs 永远只能是 null
误以为每个请求都必须新建一个 limiter
options_en: The same key's state update must be atomic, so no two requests can spend the same quota.
This mistakenly assumes every endpoint must share one algorithm.
This mistakenly assumes retryAfterMs can only ever be null.
This mistakenly assumes a limiter must be created fresh per request.
why: 限流正确性取决于 per-key 状态的一致更新，无论算法是 bucket 还是 sliding log，同一 key 的检查+写入都必须原子。
why_en: The core invariant is atomic per-key state update so concurrent requests cannot spend the same quota twice.
whenOtherWins: 单线程同步调用中不需要锁，但一旦多线程或异步交错，就需要同步或事务保护。
tradeoff: per-key 原子更新的正确性 vs 加锁带来的并发开销

termDefinitions.meaning: 按每个 key 独立维护的状态数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-key state is state tracked independently for each key.

optionExplanations: 拿锁的边界要卡在 per-key 状态本身——检查剩余额度和真正扣减必须发生在同一个原子操作里，才不会被并发请求撞车。
把算法选择自由度误当成必须统一——不同 endpoint 本可以各配各的算法，互不影响。
忽略了拒绝路径会返回真实等待时间——retryAfterMs 只有放行时才是 null。
把一次性创建误当成每请求都要重建——重建会丢失该 client 已积累的限流状态。
optionExplanations_en: The lock must wrap the per-key state itself — checking remaining quota and deducting it need to happen as one atomic step, or concurrent requests collide.
This wrongly turns algorithm freedom into forced uniformity — different endpoints can use different algorithms independently.
This ignores that the deny path returns a real wait — retryAfterMs is null only when the request is allowed.
This confuses one-time creation with per-request rebuilding — rebuilding would discard that client's accumulated state.

q: 中级候选人在本题最应稳定说明什么？
q_en: What should a mid-level candidate explain reliably in this problem?
options: 说清 RateLimiter 编排、Factory 创建、Limiter 管理状态
误以为面试必须背下所有限流算法的名字
误以为中级候选人必须现场写出分布式 Redis 脚本
误以为应该强行把 Client 建成一个实体类
options_en: Explain that RateLimiter orchestrates, the factory creates, and Limiter manages state.
This mistakenly assumes you must memorize every algorithm's name for the interview.
This mistakenly assumes mid-level candidates must write a distributed Redis script live.
This mistakenly assumes Client should be forced into its own entity class.
why: 中级答案要能划清 RateLimiter、Factory、Limiter、Result 的对象边界和状态归属；死背算法名或提前写分布式 Redis 都偏离主线。
why_en: A mid-level answer should separate orchestration, creation, limiter state, and result semantics, not jump to Redis or trivia.
tradeoff: 划清类边界和状态归属 vs 死记算法名称或提前实现分布式方案

termDefinitions.meaning: 根据配置中的 algorithm 字段创建具体 Limiter 实例的工厂类。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LimiterFactory reads the algorithm field in config and instantiates the matching Limiter.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存数据存储，可用来做分布式共享限流状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory data store often used to share rate-limit state across processes.

optionExplanations: 划清 RateLimiter 编排、Factory 创建、Limiter 管理状态这几个对象边界，面试官就能看到清晰的委派路径。
把目标误判成算法名词背诵——算法名只有在解释具体取舍时才有用。
把单机对象设计升级成分布式脚本题——Redis 脚本是扩展话题，不是基础答案核心。
把无行为输入硬建成实体——Client 只有在聚合套餐、身份和状态时才值得建类。
optionExplanations_en: Separating RateLimiter's orchestration, the factory's creation, and each Limiter's state gives the interviewer a clear delegation path.
This mistakes the goal for reciting algorithm names — names only matter when explaining a concrete tradeoff.
This turns a single-node object design into a distributed scripting task — Redis scripts belong to the extension, not the base answer.
This forces a behavior-free input into an entity — Client only deserves one when it owns plan, identity, or state.

scenario: 面试：设计一个「句子校验器」——按一组规则(首字母大写、以标点结尾、无连续空格…)判断一句话是否合法。
scenario_en: Interview: design a sentence validator that checks a sentence against a set of rules (capital start, ends with punctuation, no double spaces...).
q: 动手写类之前，最该先澄清哪组问题？
q_en: What should you clarify before writing classes?
options: 有哪些规则、遇到第一条不过就停还是收集全部错误、以后要不要方便加新规则
用什么字体渲染错误提示给用户看
数据库用 MySQL 还是 Postgres 存句子
直接开始写一个大 if-else 判断所有情况
options_en: Which rules, fail-fast vs collect all errors, and whether new rules must be easy to add later
What font to render the error message in
Whether to store sentences in MySQL or Postgres
Just start writing one big if-else covering every case
optionExplanations: 对：规则集、fail-fast vs 收集全部、可扩展性——这三点直接决定类怎么设计。
错：渲染是 UI 细节，跟 OOD 类设计无关。
错：存储不是这道 OOD 题的核心。
错：一上来大 if-else 正是要避免的反模式(违反 OCP/SRP)。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the rule set, fail-fast vs collect-all, and extensibility directly shape the class design.
Wrong: rendering is a UI detail, unrelated to the OOD.
Wrong: storage is not the core of this OOD.
Wrong: a big if-else up front is the anti-pattern to avoid (breaks OCP/SRP).
why: OOD 先问清「有哪些规则、是遇错即停还是收集全部错误、以后加规则要不要免改老代码」——这三点决定你把规则抽成什么、校验器怎么聚合结果。
why_en: Clarify the rules, fail-fast vs collect-all, and whether adding rules must avoid touching old code — these shape how you abstract rules and aggregate results.

scenario: 你有很多条校验规则，还要能随时加新规则。
scenario_en: You have many validation rules and must be able to add new ones anytime.
q: 规则该怎么抽象？
q_en: How should you abstract a rule?
options: 定义一个 ValidationRule 接口(check(sentence)→错误或空)，每条规则一个实现类
把所有规则写成 SentenceValidator 里的一个大 validate() 方法
每条规则用一个全局布尔变量表示
把规则硬编码进 if-else，改需求就改这个方法
options_en: Define a ValidationRule interface (check(sentence) → error or none); one class per rule
Put all rules in one big validate() method inside SentenceValidator
Represent each rule with a global boolean flag
Hard-code rules into an if-else and edit that method when requirements change
optionExplanations: 对：一个公共接口 + 每规则一类，就能统一调用、独立测试、随意增删。
错：塞进一个大方法 → 加规则就改它，违反开闭原则、也难测。
错：全局布尔表达不了「怎么校验」的逻辑。
错：硬编码 if-else 正是要抽象掉的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a common interface + one class per rule gives uniform calling, isolated testing, and easy add/remove.
Wrong: one big method means editing it to add a rule — breaks OCP and is hard to test.
Wrong: a global boolean cannot express the checking logic.
Wrong: a hard-coded if-else is exactly what abstraction removes.
why: 核心抽象=一个 ValidationRule 接口(每条规则实现 check(sentence)，返回错误或空)，每条规则是一个独立的类。这样校验器能统一调用、每条规则能单独测、增删规则互不影响。
why_en: The core abstraction is a ValidationRule interface (each rule implements check(sentence) → error or none), one class per rule. The validator calls them uniformly, each rule is tested in isolation, and adding/removing rules is independent.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「一族可互换的算法/规则」各封装成一个类、实现同一个接口，调用方持有接口、运行时可换。这里每条校验规则就是一个策略
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Strategy pattern: encapsulate a family of interchangeable algorithms/rules as classes behind one interface; the caller holds the interface and can swap them. Each validation rule is a strategy.

termDefinitions.meaning: Python 没有 Java 那种 interface 关键字。表达「规则契约」的两种地道写法:①abc.ABC + @abstractmethod(强制子类实现 check);②typing.Protocol(结构化子类型,谁有 check 方法谁就算)。甚至靠 duck typing——任何有 check(sentence) 方法的对象都能用
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Python has no interface keyword. Two idiomatic ways to express the rule contract: abc.ABC + @abstractmethod (forces subclasses to implement check), or typing.Protocol (structural typing). With duck typing, any object having check(sentence) works.

scenario: SentenceValidator 要把一堆规则跑一遍并给出结果。
scenario_en: SentenceValidator must run a set of rules and produce a result.
q: SentenceValidator 的核心结构应该是？
q_en: What is the core structure of SentenceValidator?
options: 持有一个 List<ValidationRule>，遍历每条 check、收集错误，返回 ValidationResult
为每条规则写一个专门的 if 分支
继承每一条规则类
把规则逻辑复制进 validate 方法里
options_en: Hold a List<ValidationRule>, iterate each check, collect errors, return a ValidationResult
Write a dedicated if-branch per rule
Inherit from every rule class
Copy each rule's logic into the validate method
optionExplanations: 对：校验器只持有规则列表、统一遍历聚合——加规则只往列表里加，校验器代码不变。
错：每规则一个 if 又回到硬编码。
错：校验器不该继承规则，是「组合」它们。
错：复制逻辑违反 DRY、且不可扩展。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the validator just holds a list of rules and iterates/aggregates — adding a rule only appends to the list, the validator is unchanged.
Wrong: an if per rule is hard-coding again.
Wrong: the validator composes rules, it does not inherit them.
Wrong: copying logic breaks DRY and is not extensible.
why: SentenceValidator 用「组合」：持有一个 List<ValidationRule>，validate() 遍历每条 check、把错误收集进 ValidationResult。加规则=往列表里注册一个新规则对象，校验器本身一行不改。
why_en: SentenceValidator uses composition: it holds a List<ValidationRule> and validate() iterates each check, collecting errors into a ValidationResult. Adding a rule just registers a new rule object; the validator itself never changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一个类「持有」别的对象(这里 validator 持有一列规则)来复用能力,而不是靠继承。更灵活:运行时能换、能增删,不被继承层级绑死
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Composition over inheritance: a class holds other objects (the validator holds a list of rules) instead of inheriting. More flexible — swap/add/remove at runtime, not locked into a hierarchy.

scenario: 产品要加一条新规则:句子不能以连续两个空格出现。
scenario_en: Product adds a new rule: a sentence must not contain a double space.
q: 在这个设计里加这条规则要动什么？
q_en: What do you change to add this rule?
options: 只新增一个 NoDoubleSpaceRule 类并注册进规则列表，SentenceValidator 和其他规则都不用改
在 SentenceValidator.validate 里加一个新的 if 分支
改每一条已有规则的代码
重写整个校验器
options_en: Add one NoDoubleSpaceRule class and register it in the list; SentenceValidator and other rules are untouched
Add a new if-branch inside SentenceValidator.validate
Edit every existing rule
Rewrite the whole validator
optionExplanations: 对：加规则=加一个实现 ValidationRule 的新类并注册——对扩展开放、对修改关闭(OCP)。
错：往 validate 里加 if 就是「改老代码」，违反 OCP。
错：新规则跟老规则无关，不该动它们。
错：整体重写完全没必要。
optionExplanations_en: Right: adding a rule = a new class implementing ValidationRule + register it — open for extension, closed for modification (OCP).
Wrong: adding an if inside validate edits old code, breaking OCP.
Wrong: the new rule is unrelated to old ones; do not touch them.
Wrong: a full rewrite is unnecessary.
why: 这就是开闭原则(OCP)的价值:加需求=加一个新类(对扩展开放),不改 SentenceValidator 和已有规则(对修改关闭)。反面(大 if-else)每次加规则都要改那个方法,越改越脆、越难测。
why_en: This is the payoff of the Open/Closed Principle: a new requirement = a new class (open for extension) without touching SentenceValidator or existing rules (closed for modification). The opposite (a big if-else) edits that method every time — fragile and hard to test.
tradeoff: 每规则一类(易扩展·类多一点) vs 大 if-else(集中·每次改老代码)

termDefinitions.meaning: 对扩展开放、对修改关闭:加新行为靠「加新代码(新类/新实现)」,而不是「改已有代码」。规则即插件是它的典型体现
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Open/Closed Principle: open for extension, closed for modification — add behavior by adding new code (new classes), not editing existing code. Pluggable rules are the classic example.

scenario: 前端想知道「哪几条规则没过、分别为什么」，不只是「合不合法」。
scenario_en: The client wants to know which rules failed and why, not just pass/fail.
q: validate 该返回什么？
q_en: What should validate return?
options: 一个 ValidationResult：是否通过 + 所有失败规则的错误列表
只返回一个 boolean
遇到第一条失败就抛异常，什么也不返回
返回一个拼好的字符串给前端直接显示
options_en: A ValidationResult: overall pass/fail + a list of all failed-rule errors
Just a boolean
Throw an exception on the first failure and return nothing
Return a pre-formatted string for the frontend to display
optionExplanations: 对：返回结构化 ValidationResult(通过与否 + 错误列表),调用方能拿到每条错误自己决定怎么用。
错：只回 boolean 丢失了「为什么、哪几条」的信息。
错：用异常表达「校验不过」是滥用异常;而且只暴露第一条。
错：返回拼好的字符串把展示格式写死进了业务层。
optionExplanations_en: Right: return a structured ValidationResult (pass/fail + error list) so the caller has each error and decides how to use it.
Wrong: a bare boolean loses which rules failed and why.
Wrong: using exceptions for validation failure is abuse, and only surfaces the first.
Wrong: returning a formatted string bakes display format into the business layer.
why: 返回结构化 ValidationResult(isValid + List<ValidationError>),而不是裸 boolean 或异常:调用方能拿到「哪几条、为什么」,展示格式留给上层。异常留给「真正的意外」,不用来表达业务校验结果。
why_en: Return a structured ValidationResult (isValid + List<ValidationError>) rather than a bare boolean or an exception: the caller gets which rules failed and why, and formatting stays in the upper layer. Reserve exceptions for real faults, not for expressing validation outcomes.
