optionExplanations_en: Writes only land in the current shard's own index, keeping the path shortest; a brand query then has to fan out to every shard and wait for the slowest one — since writes come first here, that read-side cost is acceptable.
A global term index makes reads faster, but every write must also update whatever index shard owns that term, lengthening the write path — conflicting with 'writes must stay fast'.
Deleting the index removes any accelerated path for brand queries, leaving nothing but a full scan.
A DNS TXT record is a text field for domain verification or mail policy — not where a database secondary index belongs.

scenario: 数据库已经分片，客户端或路由层必须知道 `userId=42` 当前在哪个 shard；分片迁移时映射会变化。
scenario_en: The database is sharded, and the client or routing tier must know which shard currently owns `userId=42`; mappings change during shard moves.
q: 如何维护分片路由信息？
q_en: How should shard-routing information be maintained?
options: 用协调服务维护 partition 到 node 的映射并通知路由方
把映射直接硬编码进每一个移动端 App，并且永远不更新
让每一个请求都先做全表扫描，遍历所有 shard 才能定位
把 shard 映射信息塞进浏览器端的 CSS 样式文件里
options_en: Use a coordination service to store partition-to-node mappings and notify routers.
Hard-code the mapping directly into every single mobile app, and never update it again.
Make every single request do a full scan across all shards before it can locate the data.
Stuff the shard mapping information into a browser-side CSS stylesheet file.
why: 分片拓扑会变化，路由层需要可更新的权威映射；ZooKeeper 这类协调服务可以保存映射并通知客户端或路由器。代价是协调服务本身要高可用。
why_en: A coordination service keeps shard maps current and notifies routers or clients when topology changes.
whenOtherWins: 如果分片很少且拓扑长期不变，静态配置能先用；如果客户端很厚，也可以缓存映射但要有刷新机制。
tradeoff: 路由信息实时更新 vs 协调服务运维成本
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Client["Client"] --> Router["Routing tier"]
  Router --> ZK["Coordination service"]
  ZK --> Map["partition -> node map"]
  Router --> S1["Shard A"]
  Router --> S2["Shard B"]

termDefinitions.meaning: ZooKeeper：常用协调服务，可保存集群元数据、监听变化并通知客户端。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZooKeeper is a coordination service that stores cluster metadata and notifies clients about changes.

optionExplanations: 分片拓扑会变，用协调服务保存 partition 到 node 的映射并主动通知路由方，正好应对迁移时的变化。
把映射硬编码进每个 App 且永不更新，一旦分片迁移，客户端手里的映射立刻过期失效。
让每个请求先扫描所有 shard 才能定位数据，等于放弃了分片带来的定位优势。
CSS 文件是给浏览器做样式渲染用的，不是存储路由映射这种运行时状态的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Shard topology changes, so a coordination service that stores the partition-to-node map and actively notifies routers is exactly what handles shard moves.
Hard-coding the mapping into every app and never updating it means the mapping goes stale the instant a shard migration happens.
Making every request scan all shards to find the data throws away the whole benefit of sharding in the first place.
A CSS file is for browser styling, not a place to store runtime routing state like a shard map.

scenario: 一个产品早期数据量小、强一致要求高；后期全球用户增长，单节点容量和延迟都成了瓶颈。
scenario_en: An early product has small data and strong consistency needs; later, global growth makes one-node capacity and latency bottlenecks.
q: 集中式和分布式数据库的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core tradeoff between centralized and distributed databases?
options: 集中式简单且强一致更容易；分布式扩展和就近访问更强但协调更复杂
集中式只能用来保存 DNS 记录；分布式只能用来做浏览器动画效果
集中式天然就没有任何单点故障；分布式天然就没有任何同步成本
集中式数据库一定永远更快；分布式数据库一定完全不能查询
options_en: Centralized databases are simpler and easier to keep strongly consistent; distributed databases scale and serve nearby users better but need more coordination.
Centralized databases can only store DNS records; distributed databases can only do browser animation effects.
Centralized systems are naturally free of any single point of failure; distributed systems are naturally free of any synchronization cost.
A centralized database is always faster no matter what; a distributed database can never support queries at all.
why: 集中式适合数据能装进单节点且一致性优先的阶段；分布式用更多节点换容量、可用性和地理低延迟。代价是跨节点 join、同步和一致性处理更难。
why_en: Centralized databases are simpler for small strongly consistent workloads, while distributed databases buy scale and locality with coordination cost.
tradeoff: 简单强一致 vs 扩展性和地理可用性
optionExplanations: 数据能装进单节点、一致性优先时，集中式更简单；用户全球增长后，分布式用更多节点换容量和就近访问，但要多处理跨节点协调。
DNS 存储和浏览器动画都不是数据库该做的事，这个说法跟集中式/分布式的区别毫无关系。
集中式恰恰是单点，故障时整体不可用；分布式的多节点同步恰恰是要付出协调成本的，两个说法都反了。
集中式在小规模下确实可能更快，但它照样能查询；分布式数据库同样支持查询，只是协调更复杂。
optionExplanations_en: When data fits on one node and consistency comes first, centralized is simpler; once users grow globally, distributed trades more coordination for capacity and locality with more nodes.
Storing DNS records and animating browsers aren't database jobs at all — this has nothing to do with the centralized/distributed distinction.
A centralized database is actually the single point that goes down entirely on failure, and a distributed database's multi-node sync is exactly what costs coordination — both claims are backwards.
Centralized can be faster at small scale, but it still supports queries; distributed databases support queries too, just with more coordination overhead.

scenario: 分布式查询要在站点 A 和 B join 三张表。`Product` 在 B 有 100,000 行，每行 200 bit；网络 50 Mbps，访问延迟 0.1s。若先在 B 用 `Brand='Wolf'` 过滤到 10 行再发到 A，传输量会大幅下降。
scenario_en: A distributed query joins tables across sites A and B. `Product` at B has 100,000 rows, each 200 bits; the link is 50 Mbps with 0.1s access delay. Filtering `Brand='Wolf'` at B leaves 10 rows before sending to A.
q: 这个例子训练的设计结论是什么？
q_en: What design lesson does this example teach?
options: 尽量在数据源头过滤，少跨站点搬无关行
总是把最大表完整搬到另一个站点
跨站点 join 时网络传输量可以忽略
过滤必须等所有表都搬到同一台机器后再做
options_en: Filter at the data source whenever possible to avoid moving irrelevant rows across sites.
Always move the largest table completely to the other site.
Network transfer volume is negligible for cross-site joins.
Filtering must wait until all tables are moved to one machine.
why: 公式是 T = a + v/b；100,000 行要传约 20,000,000 bit，50 Mbps 下约 0.5s，而过滤到 10 行后传输接近 0.1s 的访问延迟。这个数字告诉我们：分布式查询先做选择和投影，少搬数据。
why_en: The formula T = a + v/b shows that filtering at the source cuts transferred bits, so distributed queries should push selection down.

termDefinitions.meaning: Megabits per second（Mbps）：每秒传输多少百万 bit 的带宽单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mbps means megabits per second, a bandwidth unit for millions of bits transferred each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: JOIN：按关联条件把多张表的行组合起来的关系型查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JOIN combines rows from multiple tables according to a relationship condition.

optionExplanations: 在 B 先用 `Brand='Wolf'` 过滤到 10 行再传，比整表 100,000 行搬过去省下的传输量是数量级的差距，这正是先选择再传输的价值。
不管数据用不用得上，整表搬过去会把大量无关行也传一遍，传输量和延迟都白白变大。
T = a + v/b 里的 v 就是要传的数据量，忽略它等于假装跨站点传输不花时间，不成立。
过滤本该在源头就地执行，等所有表都搬到一台机器后再过滤，反而先付了搬运无关行的代价。
optionExplanations_en: Filtering to 10 rows at B with `Brand='Wolf'` before sending, versus shipping all 100,000 rows, is an order-of-magnitude difference in transfer — that's the whole value of selecting before transmitting.
Moving the whole table regardless of what's actually needed drags along a lot of irrelevant rows, inflating both transfer volume and latency for nothing.
v in T = a + v/b is exactly the data volume being transferred; ignoring it pretends cross-site transfer takes no time, which isn't true.
Filtering should happen right at the source; waiting until every table is moved to one machine first means you've already paid the cost of moving the irrelevant rows.

scenario: 面试官让你设计一个全球文件分享服务，用户会上传、下载、同步文件；题目还没给规模、延迟和一致性要求。
scenario_en: You are asked to design a global file-sharing service for upload, download, and sync, but scale, latency, and consistency are still unstated.
q: 第一步该把什么问清楚？
q_en: What should you clarify first?
options: 先选对象存储、数据库和 CDN
先问功能需求、规模、延迟、一致性和故障容忍
先画微服务拆分图
先估算每台服务器的 CPU 型号
options_en: Pick object storage, databases, and a CDN first.
Clarify functional needs, scale, latency, consistency, and failure tolerance first.
Draw the microservice decomposition first.
Estimate the CPU model for each server first.
why: 我会先把约束问清楚，因为这些约束会决定存储、缓存、复制和同步协议。直接选组件容易把题目做成背模板。
why_en: Clarify the constraints first because they determine storage, caching, replication, and sync choices.
whenOtherWins: 如果题目已经给出完整约束，才进入组件选择和容量估算。
tradeoff: 需求澄清 vs 过早定架构

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络，把静态或可缓存内容放到离用户更近的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content at edge locations closer to users.

optionExplanations: 选组件感觉进展快，但没约束时很容易选错存储和一致性模型，白白浪费白板时间。
先问清规模、延迟、一致性和故障容忍，才能让后面每个选择都有依据，不会白讲。
拆微服务图看起来结构完整，但如果连读写规模都没问，边界很可能划错。
纠结 CPU 型号是容量采购阶段的事，题目连基本约束都还没定，做这个太早。
optionExplanations_en: Jumping straight to storage or a CDN feels fast, but without constraints you can easily pick the wrong consistency model and waste the whiteboard.
Clarifying scale, latency, consistency, and failure tolerance first gives every later choice something to point back to.
A service diagram looks thorough, but drawing boundaries before you know read/write scale usually draws them wrong.
Debating a CPU model belongs to the procurement stage, and this prompt hasn't even fixed its basic constraints yet.

scenario: 你在白板上解释一个电商系统，已经有成熟的负载均衡器、缓存、队列和对象存储可选；时间只有 40 分钟。
scenario_en: You are explaining an e-commerce system on a whiteboard with mature load balancers, caches, queues, and object stores available, and only 40 minutes.
q: 为什么用 building blocks 组织设计？
q_en: Why organize the design around building blocks?
options: 能把每个成熟组件当作有接口和代价的模块讨论
能保证所有组件都不用再解释故障模式
能让系统自动满足所有非功能需求
能避免做任何容量估算
options_en: They let you discuss each mature component as a module with interfaces and costs.
They guarantee every component's failure mode no longer needs explanation.
They make the system automatically satisfy every non-functional requirement.
They remove the need for capacity estimation.
why: building block 的价值是复用稳定抽象，同时仍然说明接口、压力点和代价。它不是魔法盒，缓存、队列、数据库在高压和故障下都要讲行为。
why_en: Building blocks save time by reusing known modules, but you still need to explain their interfaces, pressure points, and trade-offs.
whenOtherWins: 如果组件行为本身就是题目重点，例如设计队列或缓存，就要展开内部机制。
tradeoff: 复用抽象 vs 展开机制
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client"] --> LB["Load balancer"]
    LB --> App["App servers"]
    App --> Cache["Cache"]
    App --> Queue["Queue"]
    App --> Store["Object store"]
optionExplanations: 把负载均衡、缓存这些成熟组件当模块讨论，还是要说清接口、压力点和代价，才站得住面试追问。
组件成熟不代表故障消失，面试官一问异常流量、连接爆满，这类说法立刻站不住。
可用性、延迟、安全都不是引用组件名字就自动达标的，还是要设计副本、限流和加密。
省掉容量估算只在玩具演示里成立，真实设计仍要算吞吐、存储和机器数。
optionExplanations_en: Calling a load balancer or cache a building block still leaves you naming its API surface, where it starts to strain, and what running it costs — reuse isn't a free pass.
Maturity doesn't erase failure modes; one question about traffic spikes or connection floods breaks this claim immediately.
Availability, latency, and security don't appear just because you named a component — you still design replicas, limits, and encryption.
Skipping capacity math only works for toy demos; a real design still needs throughput, storage, and machine-count numbers.

q: 为什么初版架构后还要留时间迭代？
q_en: Why should you leave time to iterate after the first architecture?
text: 系统设计里，初版方案先覆盖主路径；测出瓶颈后再迭代，因为真实压力常暴露 {{热点}}, {{容量上限}}, 或 {{故障模式}}。
text_en: In system design, the first version covers the main path; iteration follows measurement because real load exposes {{hotspots}}, {{capacity limits}}, or {{failure modes}}.
why: 我会把初版当假设而不是终点。测量后再优化，才能知道该扩容、加缓存、分片还是改协议。
why_en: Treat the first design as a hypothesis, then measure before deciding whether to scale, cache, shard, or change protocols.

scenario: 你要为消息服务选择存储和处理路径，功能已经确定，但数据特征还没问清楚。
scenario_en: You need to choose storage and processing paths for a messaging service; features are clear, but data characteristics are not.
q: 哪些问题会直接影响组件选择？
q_en: Which questions directly affect component choices?
options: 数据是读多还是写多
是否必须读到最新写入
数据保存多久、能丢多少
团队最喜欢哪种架构图配色
options_en: Whether the workload is read-heavy or write-heavy.
Whether reads must see the latest write.
How long data is retained and how much loss is acceptable.
Which architecture-diagram color palette the team likes.
why: 读写比例决定缓存、索引和分片压力；一致性和耐久性决定复制、事务和确认路径。配色不改变系统行为。
why_en: Read/write mix, consistency, and durability shape storage and replication choices; diagram colors do not.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据被确认后，在故障后仍能保留下来的能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Durability means acknowledged data survives failures.

optionExplanations: 读多写少决定要不要加缓存和只读副本，读写各半则要多想写路径的分片和锁。
要不要读到最新写决定复制策略是同步还是异步，选错会让用户看到过期数据或白等延迟。
保留多久、能丢多少决定归档、压缩和确认路径，直接影响存储成本和故障恢复策略。
配色只影响评审时好不好看，不会改变分片、复制或索引的任何一行代码。
optionExplanations_en: A read-heavy or write-heavy split decides whether you add caches and read replicas, or design around write-path sharding and locks.
Whether reads must see the latest write decides sync versus async replication — get it wrong and users see stale data or pay needless latency.
Retention and acceptable loss decide archival, compaction, and acknowledgment paths, which drive storage cost and recovery design.
A color palette only affects how the diagram looks in review; it changes no sharding, replication, or indexing decision.

scenario: 题目是“设计 WhatsApp”，但只有 40 分钟；产品有聊天、群聊、状态、支付、备份、搜索等很多功能。
scenario_en: The prompt is "Design WhatsApp," but you only have 40 minutes; the product includes chat, groups, status, payments, backups, search, and more.
q: 怎样控制设计范围最合理？
q_en: How should you control the design scope?
options: 声明只覆盖核心消息收发和在线状态，并确认哪些功能不做
尝试把聊天、群聊、状态、支付这些真实产品功能都画进同一张图里
跳过所有需求澄清，直接动手设计一套 Kafka 消息集群
只讲客户端 UI 页面样式，完全不涉及任何后端投递路径
options_en: State that you will cover core messaging and presence, and confirm what is out of scope.
Try to squeeze chat, groups, status, and payments all into the same one diagram.
Skip every requirements question and jump straight into designing a Kafka cluster.
Discuss only client-side UI screen styling and skip any backend delivery path.
why: 我会先保住核心不变量：消息能送达、顺序可解释、失败可恢复。范围收窄后，架构深度才够。
why_en: Narrow the scope to the core invariants so you can reason deeply about delivery, ordering, and recovery.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试官明确要求搜索或备份，再把该功能加入主路径或扩展路径。
tradeoff: 核心路径深度 vs 全产品覆盖

termDefinitions.meaning: Kafka 是分布式事件流平台，常用于日志、消息和异步数据管道。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed event streaming platform used for logs, messaging, and async data pipelines.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户界面，指用户直接交互的页面和控件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: User Interface means the screens and controls that users interact with.

optionExplanations: 先声明只做核心收发和在线状态、明确哪些功能不做，40 分钟才够把消息投递和故障恢复讲深。
想把聊天、群聊、支付、备份都画进去，只会让每块都停在名字层面，深度反而不够。
还没定范围就跳去选 Kafka，等于把组件选择建在没验证过的假设上。
只讲界面看不出消息怎么送达、怎么排序、怎么在离线后补投，后端问题一个都没答。
optionExplanations_en: Stating up front that you'll cover only core messaging and presence, with explicit out-of-scope items, leaves room to go deep on delivery and recovery.
Trying to fit chat, groups, payments, and backups into one diagram keeps every piece shallow instead of letting any path go deep.
Jumping to a Kafka cluster before scope is set builds the component choice on an unverified guess.
Talking only about screens skips over how a message actually gets sent, put in order, and re-sent once someone comes back online — none of that gets answered.

scenario: 一个服务启动后流量突然翻倍，你说“加更多服务器”但没有定位瓶颈；当前 DB CPU 很低，应用 CPU 已接近 90%。
scenario_en: Traffic doubles after launch; you say "add more servers" without locating the bottleneck; DB CPU is low, while app CPU is near 90%.
q: 这个跟进问题暴露了什么风险？
q_en: What risk does this follow-up expose?
options: 应该先分库分表，因为所有扩容都从 DB 开始
需要先诊断瓶颈；这次更像应用计算层扩容
应该把所有请求都改成强一致事务
应该删掉监控，避免被数字干扰
options_en: Shard the database first because all scaling starts at the DB.
Diagnose the bottleneck first; this case looks like app-compute scaling.
Turn every request into a strongly consistent transaction.
Remove monitoring so the numbers do not distract you.
why: 扩容动作要对准瓶颈；DB 没忙时先分片只会增加复杂度。这里应用 CPU 接近饱和，先横向扩应用或优化计算路径更合理。
why_en: Scaling should target the bottleneck; with app CPU saturated and DB idle, app-tier scaling is the first move.
whenOtherWins: 如果监控显示 DB 写入、锁等待或存储 I/O 才是瓶颈，数据库分片或索引优化会反超。
tradeoff: 诊断式扩容 vs 组件名扩容

termDefinitions.meaning: 执行程序指令的处理器；CPU 饱和常意味着计算路径排队。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The CPU executes instructions, and saturation often means compute requests are queuing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统读写磁盘、网络或外设的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O is work spent reading or writing disks, networks, or devices.

optionExplanations: DB CPU 还很低就先分库分表，只是照搬“扩容=分库”的模板，没对准这次真正吃紧的地方。
先看指标：DB 闲着、应用 CPU 逼近 90%，说明这次该扩的是应用计算层，不是数据库。
把所有请求改成强一致事务只会加更多协调开销，对 CPU 瓶颈没有帮助。
删监控是把体温计砸了，看不见指标之后连诊断的依据都没了。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding while the DB is barely busy just repeats the "scaling means sharding" template without matching where the pressure actually is.
The metrics say it plainly: DB is idle, app CPU is near 90%, so this round of scaling belongs to the application tier.
Turning every request into a strongly consistent transaction only adds coordination overhead — it does nothing for a CPU bottleneck.
Removing monitoring is breaking the thermometer; without the numbers there's no evidence left to diagnose anything.

scenario: 支付服务依赖风控接口；风控接口开始 2 秒超时，调用方把失败请求无限重试，整体延迟和错误率继续上升。
scenario_en: A payment service depends on a risk-check API; that API starts timing out after 2 seconds, and callers retry failed requests indefinitely.
q: 最该先加哪类保护？
q_en: What protection should you add first?
options: 无限增加重试次数
断路器、超时上限和降级路径
把数据库改成最终一致
关闭所有告警
options_en: Increase retries without a limit.
Use circuit breakers, timeout budgets, and a degraded path.
Make the database eventually consistent.
Turn off all alerts.
why: 依赖已经慢了，更多重试会放大排队和下游压力。我会设置超时和断路器，必要时走缓存结果、人工审核或拒绝高风险请求。
why_en: When a dependency is already slow, bounded timeouts and circuit breakers prevent retries from amplifying the outage.
whenOtherWins: 如果失败是瞬时丢包且下游容量充足，少量带退避的重试才有价值。
tradeoff: 可用性保护 vs 完整实时校验

termDefinitions.meaning: 断路器在依赖连续失败时短期开路，避免调用方继续压垮下游。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A circuit breaker temporarily stops calls to a failing dependency to prevent overload.

optionExplanations: 依赖已经在超时了，无限重试只会把请求堆得更多，进一步拖垮本就吃紧的下游。
设超时上限、加断路器、准备降级路径，能在依赖变慢时把爆炸半径挡住。
把数据库改最终一致解决的是复制延迟问题，跟风控接口超时没有关系。
关掉告警只是让你看不到问题在恶化，错误率不会因此下降。
optionExplanations_en: A risk-check call that's already stalling doesn't recover just because you call it again; retrying without a cap only adds more load onto a struggling downstream.
Capping how long you wait, tripping the breaker once failures cluster, and falling back to a degraded path keep one slow risk check from dragging payments down with it.
Switching the database to eventual consistency addresses replication lag, not a risk-check API that's timing out.
Turning off alerts only hides the problem getting worse — it does nothing to lower the error rate.

q: 为什么“NoSQL box”不是一个完整设计？
q_en: Why is a "NoSQL box" not a complete design?
text: 存储设计要说明 {{访问模式}}, {{主键/排序键}}, {{分页}}, {{版本或幂等键}}；只写一个数据库名字无法判断读写路径。
text_en: A storage design should state {{access patterns}}, {{primary/sort keys}}, {{pagination}}, and {{versioning or idempotency keys}}; a database name alone does not define the read/write path.
why: 数据库类型只是起点，真正决定可扩展性的是查询怎么进来、数据怎么分布、重复请求怎么处理。
why_en: The database category is only a starting point; scalability depends on access patterns, keys, and duplicate-handling semantics.

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等键用于识别重复请求，让重试不会重复创建订单或扣款。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key identifies duplicate requests so retries do not create duplicate side effects.

scenario: 订单服务需要同时扣库存和创建订单；并发请求可能同时抢最后一件商品。
scenario_en: An order service must decrement inventory and create an order; concurrent requests may race for the last item.
q: 数据库事务这个抽象帮你隐藏什么？
q_en: What does the database transaction abstraction hide for you?
options: 提交/回滚接口背后的并发控制和一致状态切换
所有跨机器、跨数据中心的网络分区问题
所有业务层的幂等去重逻辑
所有读路径的缓存失效策略细节
options_en: The concurrency control and consistent-state transition behind commit or rollback.
Every cross-machine, cross-datacenter network partition problem.
All application-level idempotent deduplication logic.
Every read-path cache invalidation policy detail.
why: 事务让业务代码用 commit/abort 表达原子变化，数据库负责隔离并发和保持约束。但它不自动解决跨服务网络失败或缓存一致性。
why_en: A transaction lets business code express an atomic commit or abort while the database handles concurrency and constraints.
whenOtherWins: 跨多个服务的长流程更适合 saga、消息或补偿动作，而不是把所有步骤塞进单库事务。
tradeoff: 本地一致状态 vs 跨服务可用性

termDefinitions.meaning: 事务把一组数据库操作包装成要么全部提交、要么全部回滚的单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction groups database operations so they either all commit or all roll back.

optionExplanations: 事务把并发控制和状态切换都收进 commit/rollback 边界里，业务代码只用管一个原子结果。
事务管的是单库内的一致状态，跨机网络分区还得靠 saga、消息或补偿流程处理。
重试造成的重复扣款要靠幂等键挡住，事务本身不会替业务逻辑去重。
缓存什么时候失效是应用层自己要定的策略，数据库事务不会替你管缓存。
optionExplanations_en: Commit or rollback is the only outcome business code has to reason about; locking and state transitions stay hidden behind that boundary.
One database staying internally consistent is a different problem from a multi-service workflow surviving a network partition — that calls for sagas, messages, or compensation instead.
Duplicate charges from a retry need an idempotency key — the transaction itself doesn't deduplicate business logic.
Cache invalidation is a policy the application layer owns; a database transaction never manages the cache for you.

scenario: 两个后端服务要频繁互调，团队希望接口像本地函数一样强类型、低开销，并自动处理序列化。
scenario_en: Two backend services call each other frequently; the team wants low-overhead, strongly typed APIs that feel like local functions and handle serialization.
q: 哪种通信抽象最贴合？
q_en: Which communication abstraction fits best?
options: RPC/gRPC
手写原始 TCP 字节流
浏览器 localStorage
只靠离线批处理文件
options_en: RPC or gRPC.
Hand-written raw TCP byte streams.
Browser localStorage.
Offline batch files only.
why: RPC 把远程调用包装成函数接口，stub/runtime 处理序列化、传输和响应。代价是调用看起来像本地，但仍会遇到超时、重试和部分失败。
why_en: RPC fits frequent backend calls because it gives a typed function-like interface while still requiring timeout and retry design.
whenOtherWins: 如果调用是公开 Web API 或需要浏览器直接消费，REST/HTTP 可能更合适；如果是流式事件，消息队列或 pub-sub 更自然。
tradeoff: 函数式接口便利 vs 分布式失败显式处理

termDefinitions.meaning: 远程过程调用，让程序像调用本地函数一样调用另一台机器上的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Remote Procedure Call lets a program invoke a procedure on another machine like a local function.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常见高性能 RPC 框架，通常用接口定义生成客户端和服务端代码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is a high-performance RPC framework that generates client and server code from interface definitions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输控制协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Transmission Control Protocol provides reliable, ordered byte-stream transport.

optionExplanations: RPC/gRPC 把远程调用包成强类型函数接口，序列化和传输都由 stub/runtime 接管。
手写原始 TCP 字节流能做，但团队要自己重造序列化、重试和协议兼容，成本太高。
localStorage 是浏览器本地键值存储，两个后端服务之间根本连不上它。
离线批处理文件只适合非实时数据交换，两个服务频繁互调等不起一天一次的批次。
optionExplanations_en: RPC or gRPC wraps a remote call in a strongly typed function interface, with stubs and the runtime handling serialization and transport.
Hand-rolled raw TCP is possible, but the team ends up rebuilding serialization, retries, and protocol compatibility from scratch.
localStorage is a browser-local key-value store; two backend services have no way to reach it at all.
Offline batch files fit non-real-time exchange; two services calling each other frequently can't wait for a once-a-day batch.

q: 同步 RPC 的调用链正确顺序是什么？
q_en: What is the correct order of a synchronous RPC call?
steps: 服务端 stub 解包参数并调用目标函数
客户端 stub 把参数序列化成网络消息
客户端 runtime 把消息发到服务端并等待响应
服务端函数执行后把结果交回服务端 stub
客户端 stub 解包响应，调用线程继续执行
why: RPC 的关键链条是 stub 做打包/解包，runtime 做传输，服务端执行真实函数。同步调用期间客户端线程会阻塞到响应或超时。
why_en: In synchronous RPC, stubs marshal and unmarshal data while runtimes transmit messages, and the caller blocks until a response or timeout.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Client
    participant CS as Client stub
    participant R as RPC runtime
    participant SS as Server stub
    participant S as Server
    C->>CS: call method(args)
    CS->>R: marshal request
    R->>SS: transmit message
    SS->>S: invoke function
    S-->>SS: result
    SS-->>R: marshal response
    R-->>CS: response
    CS-->>C: return value

termDefinitions.meaning: stub 是本地代理代码，负责把函数参数和返回值转换成可传输消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stub is local proxy code that turns function arguments and return values into transportable messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: marshaling 是把内存中的参数编码成标准消息格式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Marshaling encodes in-memory arguments into a standard message format.

scenario: 订单服务通过 RPC 调支付服务；客户端超时了，但网络中断前支付服务可能已经扣款。
scenario_en: An order service calls a payment service over RPC; the client times out, but the payment service may already have charged the card before the network failed.
q: 为什么超时不能被 RPC 完全隐藏？
q_en: Why can't RPC fully hide timeouts?
options: 因为调用方无法仅凭超时判断远端是否执行成功
因为 RPC 一定不会序列化参数
因为所有远程调用都必须改成 UDP
因为本地函数也会产生网络分区
options_en: Because the caller cannot know from a timeout alone whether the remote side completed.
Because RPC never serializes arguments.
Because every remote call must use UDP.
Because local functions also create network partitions.
why: 超时只说明调用方没及时拿到响应，不说明远端没做副作用。我会加幂等键、查询状态或补偿流程，避免重试造成重复扣款。
why_en: A timeout only means the caller lacks a response, so idempotency keys or status checks are needed before retrying side effects.
whenOtherWins: 如果操作是纯读且无副作用，简单重试的风险低很多。
tradeoff: 调用抽象简洁 vs 副作用可判定性

termDefinitions.meaning: 幂等键把多次相同请求识别成一次业务动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An idempotency key lets repeated requests map to one business action.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户数据报协议，提供无连接、不保证送达或顺序的数据报传输。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: User Datagram Protocol sends connectionless datagrams without delivery or ordering guarantees.

optionExplanations: 超时只说明调用方没等到响应，扣款到底有没有发生，调用方其实并不知道。
RPC 从来都要序列化参数才能传输，这个选项直接说反了它的工作方式。
把超时归咎于该用 UDP，是把可靠性问题误诊成传输协议选择，换了协议问题照样在。
本地函数调用不跨机器，也就不存在网络分区，这个说法把本地和远程搞混了。
optionExplanations_en: Not hearing back in time tells the caller nothing about whether the charge actually landed on the payment service's side.
RPC always has to serialize arguments before they go over the wire; this option gets the mechanism backwards.
Blaming the timeout on needing UDP misdiagnoses a reliability problem as a transport choice — the same risk survives the swap.
A local function call never leaves one machine, so there's no network partition to speak of; this conflates local and remote calls.

scenario: 你要设计 DNS 记录传播；更新后短时间内有些地区读到旧值可以接受，但最终所有缓存要收敛。
scenario_en: You are designing DNS record propagation; some regions may temporarily read old values after an update, but all caches must eventually converge.
q: 应选择哪种一致性模型？
q_en: Which consistency model should you choose?
options: 线性一致性
顺序一致性
因果一致性
最终一致性
options_en: Linearizability.
Sequential consistency.
Causal consistency.
Eventual consistency.
why: DNS 更看重高可用和全球传播，短暂旧值通常可接受。最终一致性承诺停止写入后副本收敛，代价是读到旧记录。
why_en: DNS fits eventual consistency because temporary stale reads are acceptable as long as replicas converge after updates stop.
whenOtherWins: 如果是改密码或撤销权限，确认后所有读都必须看到新值，线性一致性更合适。
tradeoff: 高可用低协调 vs 读最新写

termDefinitions.meaning: 域名系统，把域名解析成可连接的网络地址。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The Domain Name System maps domain names to network addresses.

optionExplanations: 线性一致性要求实时看到最新值，DNS 传播这种场景用不上，也换不来对应的高可用。
顺序一致性保的是同一进程看到的操作顺序，跟 DNS 允许短暂读旧值的场景对不上号。
因果一致性适合“回复不能早于原文”这类依赖关系，DNS 记录之间并没有这种依赖。
DNS 更看重全球高可用，短暂读到旧记录能接受，只要停止更新后所有副本最终收敛。
optionExplanations_en: Linearizability demands seeing the latest value in real time, which DNS propagation doesn't need and doesn't buy back any availability for.
Sequential ordering only promises a process sees its own operations in the order it issued them — a narrower promise than what DNS propagation actually needs.
Reply-after-parent ordering is what a causal guarantee protects; plain DNS records carry no such dependency between separate updates.
Global reach matters more than instant freshness here, so a client reading an old record briefly is fine as long as every replica catches up once writes stop.

scenario: 评论系统允许用户回复评论；读者可以稍晚看到新评论，但回复不能出现在被回复的原评论之前。
scenario_en: A comment system supports replies; readers may see new comments slightly late, but a reply must not appear before its parent comment.
q: 哪种一致性约束最贴合？
q_en: Which consistency guarantee fits best?
options: 完全不保证顺序的最终一致性
因果一致性
所有操作都线性一致
只保证磁盘耐久性
options_en: Eventual consistency with no ordering guarantee.
Causal consistency.
Linearize every operation.
Only guarantee disk durability.
why: 回复依赖原评论，所以依赖关系必须保序；不同独立评论可以晚点或换序显示。因果一致性比最终一致性多保这条关系，又比全局线性一致便宜。
why_en: Causal consistency preserves reply-after-parent ordering without forcing every independent comment into one global real-time order.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求所有用户看到完全相同的实时评论顺序，才需要更强的一致性或中心化排序。
tradeoff: 依赖关系正确 vs 全局实时排序成本
optionExplanations: 完全不保序的最终一致性可能让回复在原评论之前冒出来，破坏了这条依赖关系。
因果一致性专门保住“回复跟着原评论”这条依赖，同时允许其他独立评论晚点或换序显示。
把所有操作都线性一致能保住顺序，但要为一个只需要局部依赖的场景付全局协调的代价。
只保磁盘耐久性只管数据不丢，完全不管评论之间谁先谁后显示的顺序问题。
optionExplanations_en: With zero ordering guarantee, a reply could render before the comment it's answering, which breaks the one dependency this feature actually needs.
Keeping a reply pinned after its parent is exactly the guarantee this model gives, and it still leaves unrelated comments free to arrive late or out of order.
Linearizing every operation does preserve order, but it pays global coordination cost for a case that only needs one local dependency.
Guaranteeing only disk durability keeps data from being lost, but says nothing about which comment should display before which.

scenario: 用户刚修改密码并收到成功响应；安全要求是旧密码立即失效，之后任何登录读都不能再接受旧密码。
scenario_en: A user has just changed their password and received success; the old password must become invalid immediately for all later login reads.
q: 这个字段需要什么一致性？
q_en: What consistency does this field need?
options: 最终一致性即可
只要本地缓存命中即可
线性一致性/强一致读写
只要异步日志最终写入即可
options_en: Eventual consistency is enough.
A local cache hit is enough.
Linearizable or strongly consistent reads and writes.
Eventually writing an async log is enough.
why: 密码变更确认后，后续登录必须读到新状态。线性一致性通常要同步复制或共识，代价是延迟和分区时可用性下降。
why_en: Password changes need linearizable behavior because once the write is acknowledged, every later login must see the new state.
whenOtherWins: 如果是点赞数、浏览量或推荐缓存，短暂旧值可接受，最终一致性通常更划算。
tradeoff: 安全正确性 vs 低延迟高可用

termDefinitions.meaning: 线性一致性要求操作看起来按真实时间顺序一个个生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Linearizability makes operations appear to take effect one at a time in real-time order.

optionExplanations: 最终一致性允许短暂读到旧密码，登录窗口里旧密码可能还能通过，这正是安全要求不允许的。
本地缓存命中根本不保证读到最新写入，旧密码换新密码后缓存完全可能还没更新。
密码一改完就必须立刻失效，任何一次后续登录都不能再读到旧值，这正是线性一致性承诺的读写行为。
异步日志只保证数据最终落盘，不保证登录校验那一刻读到的就是最新密码。
optionExplanations_en: Eventual consistency allows a brief window where the old password still reads as valid, which is exactly what the security requirement forbids.
A local cache hit gives no guarantee of reading the latest write; the cache can easily still hold the old password after the change.
The security requirement is that the old password stops working the instant the change is confirmed — that behavior is what linearizable reads and writes guarantee.
An async log only guarantees the write eventually lands on disk, not that a login check at that instant reads the newest password.

scenario: 你在解释“consistency”一词：一个场景是数据库约束不被破坏，另一个场景是副本在分区时是否暴露不同值。
scenario_en: You are explaining the word "consistency": one case is about database invariants, the other about whether replicas expose different values during partitions.
q: ACID consistency 和 CAP consistency 差在哪？
q_en: How do ACID consistency and CAP consistency differ?
options: ACID 管约束状态，CAP 管分布式副本视图
ACID 只用于缓存，CAP 只用于单机数据库
两者都只表示低延迟
两者都表示数据永不丢失
options_en: ACID is about valid database states, while CAP is about replica views in distributed systems.
ACID is only for caches, and CAP is only for single-node databases.
Both only mean low latency.
Both mean data is never lost.
why: ACID 的一致性是事务前后满足约束；CAP 的一致性是分布式读写看到同一个逻辑值。混用这两个词会把数据库约束和副本可见性讲乱。
why_en: ACID consistency protects database invariants, while CAP consistency is about what values distributed replicas expose.
tradeoff: 本地数据约束 vs 分布式副本可见性

termDefinitions.meaning: ACID 是事务数据库常见的四类保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ACID is the set of transaction guarantees: atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability.

termDefinitions.meaning: CAP 描述分布式系统在网络分区下对一致性和可用性的取舍。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CAP describes the consistency and availability trade-off under network partitions.

optionExplanations: ACID 的一致性管的是事务前后约束不被破坏，CAP 的一致性管的是分布式副本是否看到同一个值，两者根本是不同维度。
ACID 和 CAP 都不是绑定某种存储形态的专属词，单机数据库一样要满足 ACID，缓存也能谈 CAP。
低延迟是性能指标，跟 ACID 保约束、CAP 保副本视图这两件事都不是一回事。
耐久性只是 ACID 四个字母之一，CAP 的一致性完全不承诺数据不丢，说“两者都不丢”混淆了概念。
optionExplanations_en: One term guards the rules a transaction must leave intact inside a single database, and the other describes whether scattered copies show the same value — they live on entirely different axes.
Neither ACID nor CAP is tied to one storage shape; a single-node database still needs ACID, and caches can still be discussed under CAP.
Low latency is a performance metric, not what either ACID's invariants or CAP's replica-view guarantee is actually about.
Durability is just one letter in ACID, and the C in CAP promises nothing about data survival at all — folding both into "never lost" mixes up two separate guarantees.

scenario: 集群里一个节点不再响应；监控可能明确知道它永久停机，也可能只是看不到心跳。
scenario_en: A node in a cluster stops responding; monitoring may know it halted permanently, or it may only miss heartbeats.
q: fail-stop 和 crash failure 的关键差异是什么？
q_en: What is the key difference between fail-stop and crash failure?
options: fail-stop 可可靠检测停止，crash 可能静默停掉
crash 一定是恶意节点篡改消息并继续响应
fail-stop 只表示消息延迟，不涉及节点停止
两者都表示节点返回随机错误值而不是停机
options_en: Fail-stop is reliably detectable, while a crash may be silent.
A crash always means a malicious node keeps changing messages.
Fail-stop only means delayed messages and not a stopped node.
Both mean random wrong values rather than a halted node.
why: 可检测性决定恢复动作：fail-stop 可以更快摘除节点，静默 crash 需要心跳超时、重试和误判处理。两者都不是任意作恶。
why_en: The key difference is detectability, which changes how quickly the system can remove or replace the failed node.
tradeoff: 可靠检测恢复 vs 心跳超时误判
optionExplanations: fail-stop 停机能被系统可靠检测到，crash 则可能悄悄停响应，监控只看到心跳消失，判断不出到底停没停。
crash failure 只是意外停止响应，不等于恶意篡改消息，那属于 Byzantine 的范畴。
fail-stop 说的是节点彻底停止且能被可靠检测，不是消息延迟这种时序问题。
两者都是节点停止响应的模型，不涉及返回随机错误值，那种行为要归到 Byzantine failure。
optionExplanations_en: One mode halts in a way monitoring can trust immediately; the other can go quiet with nothing but a missed heartbeat, leaving real uncertainty about whether the node actually stopped.
A crash is simply an unexpected halt, not a node maliciously altering messages — that behavior belongs to Byzantine failure.
Fail-stop describes a node halting completely and being reliably detected, not a timing issue like a delayed message.
Both models describe a node that stops responding, not one that returns random wrong values — that behavior is Byzantine failure.

scenario: 竞价系统要求 50 ms 内返回出价；某节点计算结果正确，但 500 ms 后才返回。
scenario_en: An ad-bidding system requires bids within 50 ms; one node computes the correct result but returns after 500 ms.
q: 这更像哪类失败？
q_en: Which failure model does this resemble?
options: temporal failure
fail-stop failure
Byzantine failure
receive omission only
options_en: Temporal failure.
Fail-stop failure.
Byzantine failure.
Receive omission only.
why: 结果正确但超过业务截止时间，对系统来说仍然不可用。不能把它简单当 crash，因为它可能稍后回来并造成重复或乱序副作用。
why_en: A correct answer that arrives after the deadline is a temporal failure, not simply a crash.
whenOtherWins: 如果节点完全停止且可被可靠检测，fail-stop 才更贴切；如果返回任意假结果，才接近 Byzantine。
tradeoff: 正确结果 vs 截止时间可用性

termDefinitions.meaning: 拜占庭失败指节点可能任意、矛盾或恶意地响应。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Byzantine failure means a node can behave arbitrarily, inconsistently, or maliciously.

optionExplanations: 结果算对了但 500ms 才回来，业务截止时间是 50ms，这属于超过时限的 temporal failure。
fail-stop 要求节点彻底停止且能被可靠检测，这个节点还是回应了，只是晚了。
节点返回的是正确结果，不是任意或矛盾的错误值，套不上 Byzantine failure。
receive omission 说的是没收到请求，这里请求收到了、也算对了，问题只出在时限上。
optionExplanations_en: Getting the right number back at ten times the allowed wait still misses the bidding window — that's a deadline violation, not a node going down.
Fail-stop requires the node to halt completely and be reliably detected; this node still responded, just late.
The node returned a correct result, not an arbitrary or contradictory one, so Byzantine failure doesn't fit.
Receive omission means the request never arrived; here it arrived and was computed correctly — the only problem is timing.

scenario: 你在给消息系统做故障注入，需要区分发送端没发、接收端没收、节点任意作恶和响应过晚。
scenario_en: You are injecting failures into a messaging system and need to distinguish send omissions, receive omissions, arbitrary behavior, and late responses.
q: 哪些映射是正确的？
q_en: Which mappings are correct?
options: send omission：节点没有发出应答
receive omission：节点没有收到请求也无法确认
Byzantine：节点可能返回随机或恶意结果
temporal：节点永久停机且可被可靠检测
options_en: Send omission: the node fails to send a response.
Receive omission: the node fails to receive the request and cannot acknowledge it.
Byzantine: the node may return random or malicious results.
Temporal: the node halts permanently and is reliably detected.
why: omission 关注消息收发丢失，Byzantine 关注任意错误行为。temporal 是返回太晚，不是可靠检测的永久停机。
why_en: Omission failures are about missing sends or receives, Byzantine failures are arbitrary behavior, and temporal failures are late responses.
optionExplanations: send omission 是节点算完了却没能把应答发出去，接收方永远等不到回复。
receive omission 是节点根本没收到请求，自然也没法确认，跟发送端没关系。
Byzantine 覆盖节点可能返回随机甚至恶意结果，这跟单纯丢消息是不同的风险类别。
这里把 temporal 描述成“永久停机且可靠检测”，其实那是 fail-stop 的定义，temporal 说的是回应太晚。
optionExplanations_en: Send omission is a node that computed a response but never got it out, so the receiver waits forever for a reply.
Receive omission means the node never got the request in the first place, so it can't acknowledge — nothing to do with the sender.
Byzantine covers a node returning random or even malicious results, a different risk category from simply losing a message.
This describes it as "halts permanently and is reliably detected," but that's actually the definition of fail-stop — the node here just answered too late.

scenario: 一个服务承诺 99.999% 年可用性；一年按 365 天估算，总时间约 525,600 分钟。
scenario_en: A service promises 99.999% annual availability; using 365 days, the year has about 525,600 minutes.
q: five nines 会迫使哪条设计路径？
q_en: What design path does five nines force?
options: 自动故障检测、快速 failover 和谨慎发布
只靠人工 24 小时值班，事故后再慢慢排查恢复
把计划维护窗口都统一放进业务高峰期执行
不需要任何监控，因为停机预算看起来足够宽松
options_en: Automated detection, fast failover, and careful releases.
Rely only on round-the-clock human staffing and recover slowly after incidents.
Schedule every planned maintenance window during peak business hours.
Skip monitoring entirely because the downtime budget looks generous.
why: 公式是 downtime = 525,600 分钟 × (1 - 0.99999) ≈ 5.26 分钟。这个数字会约束故障检测、自动 failover、发布和维护窗口。
why_en: Five nines allows about 5.26 minutes of yearly downtime, which forces fast detection, failover, and careful releases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标，定义服务要达到的可用性、延迟或错误率目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Objective is a target for availability, latency, or error rate.

optionExplanations: 525,600 分钟乘以 0.00001，一年的停机预算只剩 5 分钟出头，这点余量逼着你上自动检测、快速切换和谨慎发布这条路。
全年停机预算才 5 分钟出头，靠人工值班再慢慢排查，光响应时间就能把预算烧光。
维护本身就是计划内停机，安排进业务高峰只会让本来就紧的停机预算更快见底。
预算只有 5 分钟多，恰恰说明这套系统最不能没有监控，不然故障发生都不知道。
optionExplanations_en: 525,600 minutes times 0.00001 leaves roughly five minutes of slack for the whole year, and that tight a margin is what pushes teams toward automated detection, a quick handoff to a healthy node, and cautious rollouts.
With barely five clock-minutes of slack across the whole year, a team that waits for a human to notice and triage can burn the entire budget on response time alone.
Maintenance is itself planned downtime; scheduling it during peak hours only drains an already thin downtime budget faster.
A budget of five-and-a-bit minutes is exactly why this system can least afford to skip monitoring — you wouldn't even know a failure happened.

scenario: 供应商声称 99.99% 可用，但合同排除了计划维护、部分区域故障和某些攻击导致的停机。
scenario_en: A provider claims 99.99% availability, but the contract excludes planned maintenance, partial regional outages, and some attack-related downtime.
q: 评估这个 SLA 时最该注意什么？
q_en: What should you watch when evaluating this SLA?
options: 只看 nines 数字即可
确认停机口径、统计起点和排除项
把 SLA 当作性能延迟承诺
默认所有用户受影响才算停机
options_en: Only look at the number of nines.
Check downtime definitions, measurement start, and exclusions.
Treat the SLA as a latency guarantee.
Assume downtime only counts if every user is affected.
why: availability 的分母和停机定义会改变真实风险。部分故障、维护和安全事件若被排除，你自己的冗余和监控仍要覆盖。
why_en: Availability claims are only meaningful after you inspect what downtime counts and what the provider excludes.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是内部容量草算，先用 nines 做粗估可以，但合同评审不能停在那里。
tradeoff: 宣传指标 vs 可执行故障预算

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议，是供应商和客户之间可执行的服务承诺。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Service Level Agreement is an enforceable service commitment between provider and customer.

optionExplanations: 只看 nines 数字会漏掉排除条款，同样是 99.99%，被排除的场景越多，真实风险越大。
评估合同要看停机口径、统计起点和排除项，这些才是真正决定风险敞口的细节。
SLA 是可用性承诺，不是延迟指标，把它当延迟保证会让你漏看真正该盯的东西。
很多真实事故只影响部分区域或部分用户，默认全员受影响才算停机会低估实际风险。
optionExplanations_en: Looking only at the nines count misses the exclusion clauses; the same 99.99% can hide very different real risk depending on what's excluded.
Evaluating the contract means checking downtime definitions, measurement start, and exclusions — those details actually set the risk exposure.
An SLA is an availability commitment, not a latency metric; treating it as one means watching the wrong number.
Many real incidents only affect part of a region or user base; requiring every user to be affected before it counts underestimates real risk.

scenario: 服务一个月只故障一次，但修复花了 12 小时；另一个服务每周都有小故障，但 1 分钟自动恢复。
scenario_en: One service fails only once a month but takes 12 hours to repair; another has weekly small failures but recovers automatically in one minute.
q: 这说明可靠性和可用性怎么区分？
q_en: What does this show about reliability versus availability?
options: 可靠性看故障频率和持续正确运行，可用性还强烈受修复时间影响
可靠性和可用性完全相同，都只看服务名字
只要 MTBF 高，可用性一定高，不受恢复时间影响
MTTR 只影响代码可读性，不影响用户可访问时间
options_en: Reliability is about failure frequency and continued correct operation, while availability is strongly affected by repair time.
Reliability and availability are identical and only depend on the service name.
High MTBF always means high availability, regardless of recovery time.
MTTR affects only code readability, not user-visible access time.
why: 罕见但长时间故障会拖低可用性；频繁但秒级恢复也可能保持较高可用性。设计上要同时提高 MTBF、降低 MTTR。
why_en: Rare long outages can hurt availability more than frequent short ones, so design for both high MTBF and low MTTR.
tradeoff: 少故障 vs 快恢复

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均故障间隔，表示可修复系统两次故障之间的平均运行时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mean Time Between Failures is the average operating time between failures.

termDefinitions.meaning: 平均修复时间，表示从故障到恢复的平均耗时。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Mean Time To Repair is the average time needed to restore service after a failure.

optionExplanations: 可靠性看多久出一次故障、能不能持续正确运行，可用性还要叠加修复要花多久，这正是本题两个服务的差别。
可靠性和可用性是两个不同指标，不是同一个东西换了个名字。
MTBF 高只说明故障少，如果每次故障修 12 小时，可用性照样会被拖低。
MTTR 是恢复服务要花的真实时间，直接决定用户能不能访问，跟代码可读性无关。
optionExplanations_en: Reliability is about how often failures happen and continued correct operation; availability layers repair time on top — exactly the gap between the two services here.
Reliability and availability are two distinct metrics, not the same thing under a different label.
High MTBF only means failures are rare; if each one takes 12 hours to fix, availability still drops.
MTTR is the real time spent restoring service, which directly decides user access — it has nothing to do with code readability.

q: 可维护性常拆成哪三类能力？
q_en: What three abilities commonly make up maintainability?
text: 可维护性不只是代码好看；它包括 {{operability}}, {{lucidity}}, 和 {{modifiability}}。
text_en: Maintainability is not just pretty code; it includes {{operability}}, {{lucidity}}, and {{modifiability}}.
why: operability 让系统容易运行和恢复，lucidity 让代码容易理解，modifiability 让新需求更容易接入。三者共同降低 MTTR。
why_en: Operability, lucidity, and modifiability all reduce the time needed to operate, understand, and change a system.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统容易运行、监控、排障和恢复的程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Operability is how easy a system is to run, monitor, debug, and recover.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统接入变更和新功能的难易程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Modifiability is how easily a system accepts changes and new features.

scenario: 内部工具流量稳定，单台数据库 CPU 持续 70%，内存不足；目标是快速缓解压力，不想马上改分片和复制拓扑。
scenario_en: An internal tool has stable traffic; one database sits around 70% CPU and lacks memory, and the goal is quick relief without changing sharding or replication.
q: 优先考虑哪种扩容？
q_en: Which scaling approach should you consider first?
options: 垂直扩容
立刻做全球多活
把所有请求异步化
删除所有索引
options_en: Vertical scaling.
Build global active-active immediately.
Make every request asynchronous.
Delete every index.
why: 稳定负载下，加 CPU/RAM 能快速提高单机上限，接口和数据模型变化小。代价是有硬件天花板，升级也可能需要维护窗口。
why_en: Vertical scaling is a quick fit for stable load because it raises one machine's ceiling with minimal architecture change.
whenOtherWins: 如果流量快速波动或单机已经到物理上限，水平扩容和分片更合适。
tradeoff: 实施简单快速 vs 单机上限
optionExplanations: 负载稳定、只是 CPU/内存吃紧，垂直扩容改动最小，能快速把单机上限提高。
内部工具流量稳定又不大，直接上全球多活是在给一个不需要的问题上双份工程量。
全部异步化能缓解排队感，但不解决 CPU 和内存本身不够用的问题。
删索引换来的是写更快、读更慢，跟眼下 CPU/内存瓶颈完全不是一回事。
optionExplanations_en: With load steady and just CPU and memory running short, adding more of both lifts the current box's ceiling without touching the rest of the architecture.
Traffic on an internal tool is stable and modest; going straight to global active-active pays double the engineering for a problem that isn't there.
Making everything async can ease the feeling of queuing, but it does nothing about CPU and memory actually running short.
Dropping indexes trades faster writes for slower reads — it has nothing to do with the CPU and memory shortage at hand.

scenario: 短视频服务用户增长很快，流量有明显峰谷；单机升级越来越贵，还需要某台机器挂了其他机器继续服务。
scenario_en: A short-video service is growing quickly with traffic peaks and valleys; bigger single machines are expensive, and other machines must continue if one fails.
q: 哪种扩容更适合作为长期主线？
q_en: Which scaling approach is the better long-term path?
options: 永远只买更大更贵的单台机器
水平扩容，加机器并配合负载均衡/分片/复制
把所有用户的请求数量直接降到零
把全部数据放进用户浏览器本地缓存里
options_en: Always buy one bigger, more expensive machine.
Scale horizontally with more machines plus load balancing, sharding, and replication.
Drive every user's request count straight down to zero.
Put all of the data into each user's local browser cache.
why: 水平扩容能把请求和数据分摊到多台机器，也能让单点故障影响变小。代价是分区、复制、协调和跨节点延迟更复杂。
why_en: Horizontal scaling is the long-term path for rapid growth because it spreads load and reduces single-node failure impact.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统很小、负载可预测、团队运维能力有限，先垂直扩容更省事。
tradeoff: 横向容量与容错 vs 分布式复杂度
optionExplanations: 只买更大机器迟早撞上单机硬顶，也没法解决“一台挂了别的还要能接管”这条要求。
水平扩容把请求和数据摊到多台机器，单点故障影响变小，跟长期高增长、要求容错这两条约束都对得上。
把用户请求数压到零不是扩容方案，是把产品需求本身砍掉了。
浏览器缓存只属于单个用户自己，既扛不住全体用户的负载，也和容错完全不相关。
optionExplanations_en: Always buying a bigger machine eventually hits a hardware ceiling and still doesn't satisfy "other machines keep serving if one dies."
Adding machines behind a load balancer, sharded and replicated, spreads both traffic and data so one box going down doesn't take the whole service with it.
Driving every user's request count to zero isn't a scaling plan — it's deleting the product requirement itself.
Browser cache belongs to one user's own device; it can't absorb the whole user base's load and has nothing to do with fault tolerance.

scenario: 电商服务白天和大促时流量暴涨，夜间很低；团队希望按 CPU、网络流量或队列长度自动增减实例。
scenario_en: An e-commerce service spikes during the day and promotions but is quiet at night; the team wants instance count to follow CPU, network traffic, or queue length.
q: 应该引入什么能力？
q_en: What capability should you introduce?
options: autoscaling
只做手工扩容
固定最大实例数不变
把监控延迟到事故后再看
options_en: Autoscaling.
Manual scaling only.
Keep the maximum instance count fixed forever.
Look at monitoring only after incidents.
why: autoscaling 按指标加减容量，能在峰值保可用、低谷降成本。代价是需要合适阈值、冷启动预算和防抖，避免来回抖动。
why_en: Autoscaling follows demand, but it needs good metrics, startup budgets, and damping to avoid oscillation.
whenOtherWins: 如果负载长期稳定且变更窗口严格，手工容量规划可能更可控。
tradeoff: 弹性成本效率 vs 自动化复杂度
optionExplanations: 流量白天大促猛涨、夜里很低，autoscaling 能按 CPU、流量或队列长度自动增减实例，跟着需求走。
只靠手工扩容跟不上大促瞬间的流量曲线，等人工发现再加机器时峰值可能已经过去了。
固定最大实例数在大促时会先撞到上限限流，夜间又白白占着资源，两头都不划算。
等出事故才看监控，容量调整永远慢半拍，等于把 autoscaling 该做的事留给人工事后补锅。
optionExplanations_en: Instance count tracking CPU, traffic, or queue depth means the fleet grows for the promotion and shrinks again overnight, instead of being sized for one extreme or the other.
Manual scaling alone can't keep up with a promotion's sudden traffic curve — by the time a human notices, the peak may already be over.
A fixed max instance count hits its ceiling during a promotion and still wastes resources overnight — losing on both ends.
Only checking monitoring after an incident means capacity adjustment is always a step behind, leaving humans to clean up what autoscaling should have done.

scenario: 聊天产品要求双方在线时消息低延迟双向传输，服务器也要主动推送新消息。
scenario_en: A chat product needs low-latency bidirectional message transfer while both sides are online, and the server must push new messages.
q: 哪种协议方向更合适？
q_en: Which protocol direction fits better?
options: WebSocket 长连接
每分钟一次 HTTP 轮询
每天离线批处理文件
只靠 CDN 缓存聊天消息
options_en: A WebSocket long-lived connection.
HTTP polling once per minute.
Daily offline batch files.
Only CDN-cache chat messages.
why: 双向实时消息需要服务器主动推送，WebSocket 避免每次都重新建请求。代价是连接数、心跳和断线重连要纳入容量设计。
why_en: WebSocket fits bidirectional low-latency messaging, but connection count, heartbeats, and reconnects become capacity concerns.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是偶尔刷新状态，短轮询或长轮询的运维成本可能更低。
tradeoff: 低延迟双向推送 vs 长连接运维成本

termDefinitions.meaning: WebSocket 是在单个长连接上进行双向通信的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for bidirectional communication over one long-lived connection.

optionExplanations: 既要双向低延迟，又要服务端能主动推消息，这两条 WebSocket 靠一条长连接就能同时满足。
每分钟轮询一次意味着新消息最多要等接近一分钟才能到，对聊天来说延迟感会很明显。
离线批处理文件按天处理，聊天消息等一天才送达，跟“低延迟”的要求完全相反。
CDN 缓存的是相对静态的内容，聊天消息是每个用户独有的实时数据，缓存不适用也不安全。
optionExplanations_en: Both sides need low-latency bidirectional transfer plus server-initiated push, and a WebSocket's long-lived connection matches both requirements.
Polling once a minute means a new message can take nearly a minute to arrive — that latency is very noticeable in a chat product.
Daily offline batch files process once a day, so a chat message could wait a full day to be delivered, the opposite of low latency.
CDN caching suits relatively static content; chat messages are per-user real-time data, which caching neither fits nor safely handles.

scenario: 社交平台里明星发帖会触达上千万粉丝；所有粉丝都在写入时 fan-out 会压垮写路径，但活跃用户打开首页要很快。
scenario_en: On a social platform, a celebrity post may reach tens of millions of followers; fanning out to everyone on write overloads writes, but active users need fast home feeds.
q: 更合理的 feed 策略是什么？
q_en: What feed strategy is more reasonable?
options: 所有粉丝都写入时立刻预计算
活跃 feed cache，非活跃读时生成
所有用户每次都全表扫描关注关系
禁止明星发布内容
options_en: Precompute for every follower immediately on write.
Use feed cache for active users and generate inactive feeds on read.
Full-scan follow relationships for every user on every read.
Ban celebrities from posting.
why: 关键是把高价值的低延迟读和巨大的写放大拆开。活跃用户吃预计算缓存，非活跃用户把成本推迟到读时。
why_en: Splitting active and inactive users reduces write amplification while keeping active-user reads fast.
whenOtherWins: 如果粉丝量小且读远多于写，全量写时 fan-out 会更简单。
tradeoff: 写放大 vs 首页读取延迟
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Post["Celebrity post"] --> Active["Active followers: feed cache"]
    Post --> Inactive["Inactive followers: generate on read"]
    Active --> FastRead["Fast home feed"]
    Inactive --> LazyRead["Deferred cost"]
optionExplanations: 明星发帖时给上千万粉丝立刻预计算，写路径瞬间被放大到千万级，这正是要避免的写风暴。
活跃用户吃预计算的 feed cache 保证首页快，非活跃用户的成本推迟到他们真正打开时再算，写路径不会被放大。
每次读都全表扫描关注关系，活跃用户打开首页的延迟会直接崩掉。
禁止明星发帖是把产品功能砍掉去回避架构问题，不是一个扩展方案。
optionExplanations_en: Precomputing for tens of millions of followers the instant a celebrity posts blows up the write path exactly the way the design needs to avoid.
Active followers get a cache that's ready before they open the app, while everyone else's feed only gets built the moment they actually look — the fan-out never has to hit millions at once.
Full-scanning follow relationships on every read would blow past any acceptable home-feed latency for active users.
Banning celebrities from posting removes the product feature to dodge the architecture problem — that's not a scaling plan.

scenario: 打车系统每 4 秒收到一次司机位置更新；附近司机查询要快，但空间索引更新也会占 CPU 和锁资源。
scenario_en: A ride-hailing system receives driver location updates every 4 seconds; nearby-driver queries must be fast, but spatial-index updates consume CPU and locking resources.
q: 为什么不能只说“用 Quadtree”就结束？
q_en: Why can't you just say "use a Quadtree" and stop?
options: 因为频繁移动会让索引维护成本成为瓶颈
因为 Quadtree 不能表达二维空间
因为附近查询不需要任何索引
因为所有司机位置必须放在 CDN
options_en: Because frequent movement can make index maintenance the bottleneck.
Because a Quadtree cannot represent two-dimensional space.
Because nearby queries never need an index.
Because all driver locations must be stored in a CDN.
why: Quadtree 让附近查询快，但每 4 秒批量更新会产生重平衡、锁和写放大。面试里要说明更新频率、查询频率和可能的混合方案。
why_en: A Quadtree can speed nearby queries, but high-frequency updates may shift the bottleneck to index maintenance.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象移动少、读查询远多于写更新，Quadtree 这类空间索引更直接。
tradeoff: 查询速度 vs 索引更新成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 四叉树把二维空间递归切成四块，用于空间查找和附近查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Quadtree recursively divides two-dimensional space into four regions for spatial lookup.

optionExplanations: 司机每 4 秒就更新一次位置，高频移动会让 Quadtree 频繁重平衡、抢锁，索引维护本身可能变成新瓶颈。
Quadtree 本来就是为二维空间查找设计的结构，这个说法直接说反了它的用途。
附近查询要在大量司机里快速筛出近处的，没有空间索引就只能全量扫描，延迟根本扛不住。
CDN 缓存的是相对静态的内容，司机位置每几秒就变一次，放 CDN 既没意义也没帮助。
optionExplanations_en: Drivers report in every four seconds, and that much churn means the tree spends real CPU and lock time rebalancing itself — the lookup speed you wanted can get eaten by upkeep.
A Quadtree exists specifically to organize two-dimensional space for lookup; this option gets its purpose backwards.
A nearby-driver query needs to narrow down a large moving set quickly; without a spatial index it degenerates into a full scan that can't meet latency.
CDNs cache relatively static content; driver locations change every few seconds, so putting them in a CDN neither fits nor helps.

scenario: 地图服务的道路图太大，单机放不下；用户从不同地区请求路线，目标是降低延迟并避免单点故障。
scenario_en: A map service's road graph is too large for one machine; users from many regions request routes, and the goal is lower latency without a single point of failure.
q: Google Maps 类路线服务该怎么拆？
q_en: How should a Google-Maps-like routing service be split?
options: 道路图分 segment，并复制 segment servers
只保留一台全球唯一的主服务器独自承接所有路线请求
把系统里所有可能出现的路线组合都预先写成静态 HTML 文件
每次请求都下载完整道路图到客户端本地计算
options_en: Split the road graph into segments and replicate segment servers.
Keep just one single global primary server handling every routing request all alone.
Prewrite every possible route combination the system could ever produce as static HTML files.
Download the entire road graph to the client and compute locally each time.
why: segment 拆分让数据和计算分摊到多台机器，复制后还能在节点故障时继续服务。代价是跨 segment 路由要协调边界和缓存。
why_en: Segmenting the road graph spreads storage and routing work, while replication avoids one server becoming the failure point.
whenOtherWins: 如果地图很小且只服务一个地区，单机或少量分区可能更简单。
tradeoff: 数据/计算分摊 vs 跨分区路由复杂度
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Route request"] --> LB["Load balancer"]
    LB --> S1["Segment server A"]
    LB --> S2["Segment server B"]
    S1 <--> S2
    S1 --> R1["Replica"]
    S2 --> R2["Replica"]
optionExplanations: 道路图太大单机放不下，按 segment 拆开再复制，既能分摊数据和计算，也能在某台挂掉时让副本接手。
全球只留一台主服务器处理所有路线，既放不下完整道路图，也是明显的单点故障。
路线是海量组合，预先写成静态文件既存不下也覆盖不了实时路况变化。
把完整道路图下载到客户端计算，图本身太大传不动，客户端算力也扛不住。
optionExplanations_en: No single box can hold the whole graph, so cutting it into segments spreads the data and the route computation across machines, and a replica behind each one means a crash doesn't stall requests.
Keeping one global primary server for every request can't hold the full graph and is an obvious single point of failure.
Routes are a combinatorial explosion; prewriting them as static files can't fit in storage or reflect real-time road conditions.
Downloading the full road graph to the client fails on both counts — the graph is too large to transfer and the client can't compute routes at that scale.

scenario: 你要解释 YouTube 类服务如何同时降低响应时间和提高可靠性。
scenario_en: You need to explain how a YouTube-like service lowers response time while improving reliability.
q: 哪些组件和目标匹配？
q_en: Which components match the goals?
options: CDN/ISP 缓存：把视频和缩略图放近用户，减少回源
blob storage：存放视频这类大对象
heartbeat：发现并移除异常服务器
单机内存数组：长期保存全部原始视频
options_en: CDN or ISP caches: place videos and thumbnails near users and reduce origin traffic.
Blob storage: store large video objects.
Heartbeats: detect and remove unhealthy servers.
One in-memory array: persist all raw videos forever.
why: 媒体服务的主成本是大对象存储、跨地域传输和故障摘除。缓存和 blob store 降低读路径压力，heartbeat 缩短故障影响时间。
why_en: A video service needs edge caching, blob storage, and heartbeats because media cost is dominated by large objects, distance, and failure detection.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对象/Blob 存储用于保存视频、图片、备份等非结构化大对象。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage stores large unstructured objects such as videos, images, and backups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 心跳是服务定期发送的健康信号，用来检测节点是否仍可用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a periodic health signal used to detect whether a node is still alive.

optionExplanations: 视频和缩略图放到离用户更近的 CDN/ISP 缓存，回源次数变少，响应时间跟着降下来。
视频是大对象，blob storage 专门为这类非结构化大文件设计，比塞进关系表更合适。
heartbeat 定期探活，一旦某台服务器不响应就能及时摘除，缩短故障对可靠性的影响时间。
单机内存数组既存不下海量视频，也扛不住重启就丢数据，跟“提高可靠性”的目标正相反。
optionExplanations_en: Placing videos and thumbnails in CDN or ISP caches closer to users cuts origin round-trips and lowers response time.
Video is a large object, and blob storage is purpose-built for unstructured large files instead of cramming them into relational tables.
Heartbeats probe health regularly, so an unresponsive server gets pulled out quickly, shortening how long a failure hurts reliability.
A single in-memory array can't hold that much video and loses everything on restart — the opposite of improving reliability.

scenario: 系统要在部分组件失败时继续输出正确结果；你可以修正错误状态，也可以用冗余把错误挡住。
scenario_en: A system must keep producing correct results when some components fail; you can either correct the bad state or mask the fault with redundancy.
q: fault-removal 和 fault-masking 怎么区分？
q_en: How do fault-removal and fault-masking differ?
options: removal 修错状态，masking 用冗余挡故障
removal 只用于 UI，masking 只用于日志系统
两者都要求关闭备份节点后再恢复服务
两者都表示不处理故障并等待用户重试
options_en: Removal corrects bad state, while masking uses redundancy to hide faults.
Removal is only for UI, and masking is only for logging systems.
Both require turning off backup nodes before restoring service.
Both mean ignoring failures and waiting for user retries.
why: fault-removal 的思路是把系统带回正确状态；fault-masking 的思路是让冗余副本接住输出。前者偏恢复动作，后者偏持续服务。
why_en: Fault-removal corrects state, while fault-masking uses redundant components so users do not see the fault.
tradeoff: 恢复修正 vs 冗余掩盖
optionExplanations: 一个是把系统修正回该有的状态，另一个是让多余的副本顶上继续对外服务，两条路径解决问题的方式完全不同。
这两个概念都不限定用在 UI 或日志系统，任何需要容错的组件都可能用到其中一种或两者结合。
关掉备份节点正好是 masking 依赖的冗余被移除了，跟这两种容错方式的思路都相反。
什么都不做只等用户重试既不是修复状态，也没有冗余接管，用户会直接看到故障。
optionExplanations_en: One path fixes the broken state directly; the other lets a spare component take over so nothing broken is ever visible to the caller — different mechanics entirely.
Neither concept is scoped to UI or logging specifically; any component that needs fault tolerance can use one or a mix of both.
Turning off backup nodes removes exactly the redundancy that masking depends on — it works against both approaches.
Doing nothing and waiting for user retries neither restores state nor hands off to redundancy — users see the failure directly.

scenario: 支付主库故障时，业务希望几乎零停机；预算允许长期运行一套已同步的备用库。
scenario_en: When the primary payment database fails, the business wants near-zero downtime and can afford a continuously running synchronized standby.
q: 哪种 failover 更贴合？
q_en: Which failover style fits better?
options: hot failover
cold failover
手工从备份磁带恢复
等用户重试到成功
options_en: Hot failover.
Cold failover.
Manual restore from backup tape.
Wait for users to retry until it works.
why: hot failover 让备用实例已经运行并接近可接管状态，所以切换延迟最小。代价是资源常驻和同步复杂度更高。
why_en: Hot failover minimizes downtime because the standby is already running, at the cost of extra resources and synchronization.
whenOtherWins: 如果系统不关键、允许分钟级恢复，warm/cold failover 能省成本。
tradeoff: 低停机 vs 常驻冗余成本
optionExplanations: 预算撑得起一套长期同步运行的备库，切到它几乎不用等待，这正好对上“几乎零停机”的要求。
cold failover 的备用实例平时不跑，故障后要先启动再追数据，恢复时间比这里要求的“几乎零停机”长得多。
手工从磁带恢复要人工介入加装载时间，动辄几十分钟起步，跟零停机的要求差距太大。
让用户自己重试到成功，其实是把恢复责任甩给用户体验，故障期间该完成的支付照样没完成。
optionExplanations_en: A budget for a continuously synced standby means it's already warm and ready to take over the moment the primary dies, keeping the cutover gap about as small as it gets.
A cold-failover standby isn't running day to day, so recovery means starting it up and catching up data first — far slower than the near-zero downtime asked for.
Manually restoring from tape needs a human plus load time, typically tens of minutes at minimum, nowhere close to zero downtime.
Waiting for users to retry until it works just shifts the recovery burden onto their experience — the payment still doesn't complete during the outage.

scenario: 购物车服务要在多副本间复制写入；产品可以选择写入确认前等所有关键副本，或先确认再异步传播。
scenario_en: A cart service replicates writes across replicas; the product can wait for key replicas before acknowledgment, or acknowledge first and propagate asynchronously.
q: 同步复制和异步复制的核心取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the core trade-off between synchronous and asynchronous replication?
options: 同步保新鲜读但慢，异步快但可能读旧
同步复制一定更便宜，也不增加写入等待
异步复制一定不需要冲突处理或回放
两者都不影响读到的数据或分区行为
options_en: Sync keeps reads fresher but slower; async is faster but may read stale data.
Synchronous replication is always cheaper and adds no write wait.
Asynchronous replication never needs conflict handling or replay.
Neither affects what reads observe or how partitions behave.
why: 同步路径把副本确认放进用户延迟和分区风险里；异步路径先保响应，但副本落后时会读到旧状态。选哪种要看业务能否容忍 stale read。
why_en: Synchronous replication buys fresher reads with coordination cost, while asynchronous replication buys availability with possible stale reads.
tradeoff: 强一致/新鲜读 vs 可用性/低延迟
optionExplanations: 同步复制等确认后再返回，读到的是最新值但延迟更高；异步先确认再传播，响应快但副本可能落后，读到旧值。
同步复制恰恰是要等关键副本确认才返回，写入延迟只会更高，不会更便宜也不会不等待。
异步复制副本之间仍可能出现冲突或需要重放消息，不会因为异步就自动免掉这些处理。
同步还是异步直接决定了读到的数据新不新、分区时能不能继续写入，说“都不影响”正好说反了。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting on acknowledgment before returning keeps reads current but adds latency; acknowledging up front and propagating after keeps responses snappy at the risk of a replica lagging behind.
Waiting for key replicas to confirm before returning is what this mode actually does — that adds write latency, it doesn't remove it or come free.
Async replicas can still diverge and need conflict handling or replay; going async doesn't remove that work automatically.
Sync versus async directly decides how fresh reads are and whether writes can proceed during a partition — claiming neither matters gets it backwards.

scenario: 三个进程在保存 checkpoint 时仍互发消息；恢复后，进程 i 的快照记录“收到 m1”，但进程 j 的快照没有记录“发送 m1”。
scenario_en: Three processes keep exchanging messages during checkpointing; after recovery, process i's snapshot says it received m1, but process j's snapshot lacks the send of m1.
q: 这个 checkpoint 有什么问题？
q_en: What is wrong with this checkpoint?
options: 全局状态不一致，恢复后会出现无来源消息
它一定比同步复制更强一致
它说明所有消息都已安全提交
它只是 UI 显示问题
options_en: The global state is inconsistent and can restore a message with no recorded source.
It is always stronger than synchronous replication.
It proves every message has been safely committed.
It is only a UI display problem.
why: 一致 checkpoint 要么同时包含发送和接收，要么都不包含。只记录接收不记录发送，会让恢复后的状态违反消息历史。
why_en: A consistent checkpoint must not contain a received message without the corresponding recorded send.
whenOtherWins: 如果 checkpoint 协议能冻结或记录 in-flight 消息，恢复状态就能保持一致。
tradeoff: 独立快照简单 vs 全局状态一致
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant J as Process j
    participant I as Process i
    J-->>I: m1
    Note over I: checkpoint records receive
    Note over J: checkpoint misses send
    I->>I: restore sees orphan message
optionExplanations: 进程 i 的快照记了“收到 m1”，j 的快照却没记“发出 m1”，恢复后就会凭空冒出一条没有来源的消息，全局状态不一致。
这种不一致的快照跟“比同步复制更强一致”完全无关，它反而是快照本身出了错。
记录不一致恰恰说明消息状态没对齐，不能拿它证明消息已经被安全提交。
这是分布式系统恢复后状态违反消息历史的正确性问题，不是界面显示层面的小事。
optionExplanations_en: Process i's snapshot records receiving m1, but j's snapshot never records sending it — recovery then produces a message with no recorded source, an inconsistent global state.
This kind of inconsistent snapshot has nothing to do with being "stronger than synchronous replication" — it's simply a broken checkpoint.
A mismatched record is exactly evidence that message state isn't aligned, not proof that every message was safely committed.
This is a correctness problem where the recovered state violates message history, not a cosmetic display issue.

scenario: 银行系统支持查余额、转账、缴费和对账单；用户愿意等几百毫秒，但不能接受错账或凭证泄露。
scenario_en: A banking system supports balances, transfers, bill pay, and statements; users can tolerate a few hundred milliseconds, but not incorrect balances or credential leaks.
q: NFR 优先级应该怎么排？
q_en: How should you prioritize the NFRs?
options: 安全和一致性优先，低延迟不能牺牲账务正确性
低延迟永远第一，余额可以稍后修
只优化界面动画
只追求最终一致，不做审计
options_en: Security and consistency first; latency must not sacrifice financial correctness.
Latency is always first, and balances can be fixed later.
Optimize only UI animations.
Use eventual consistency only and skip auditing.
why: 金融场景的核心风险是错账和泄露，所以认证、审计、事务和强一致路径优先。延迟仍重要，但不能换掉账务正确性。
why_en: For banking, security and consistency outrank raw latency because incorrect balances and leaks are product failures.
whenOtherWins: 如果是点赞数或推荐流，低延迟和可用性通常可以压过强一致。
tradeoff: 账务正确性/安全 vs 极低延迟
optionExplanations: 银行场景的真正风险是错账和凭证泄露，所以安全和一致性要排在前面，低延迟不能拿账务正确性去换。
把低延迟放第一、余额稍后修，等于允许用户先看到错的余额，这对银行是不可接受的。
只优化界面动画完全没碰到错账和泄露这两个真正的风险点。
只追最终一致又不做审计，转账对不上账的时候连排查依据都没有。
optionExplanations_en: A wrong balance or a leaked credential is the failure that actually costs a bank its customers, so auth, auditing, and strong consistency win over shaving off milliseconds.
Putting latency first and fixing balances later means letting users see a wrong balance in the meantime — unacceptable for a bank.
Polishing UI animations never touches the two things that can actually sink a banking product: money showing the wrong number and credentials getting out.
Eventual consistency with no auditing leaves nothing to investigate when a transfer doesn't reconcile.

scenario: 航天器和地面通信中断，同时硬件模块故障；系统必须在人工干预前保持关键控制能力。
scenario_en: A spacecraft loses communication with Earth while a hardware module fails; it must preserve critical control before humans can intervene.
q: 最重要的 NFR 是什么？
q_en: What is the most important NFR?
options: fault tolerance
社交内容分享与转发能力
广告点击率与转化率数据
界面主题颜色可自由配置
options_en: Fault tolerance.
Social content sharing and reposting.
Ad click-through and conversion rates.
Freely configurable UI theme colors.
why: 通信断开时不能依赖外部恢复，系统要靠冗余、隔离和本地恢复继续运行。这里可用性和安全都建立在容错能力上。
why_en: Fault tolerance dominates because the spacecraft must keep critical control locally when communication and hardware fail.
whenOtherWins: 如果是普通内容网站，成本和快速迭代可能比极端容错更优先。
tradeoff: 自主生存能力 vs 成本/复杂度
optionExplanations: 通信中断又赶上硬件故障，航天器要靠自己的冗余和本地恢复撑住关键控制，容错能力是唯一能兜底的。
地面通信都断了，社交分享这种功能根本无从谈起，也帮不了关键控制。
广告点击率是消费互联网产品的指标，跟航天器的生存和控制毫无关系。
界面主题能不能配置属于体验细节，通信中断时航天器根本没有人在看界面。
optionExplanations_en: With the ground link down and a module already failing, the craft has nothing to lean on but its own redundancy and local recovery to hold onto flight control.
There's no ground link to share anything over in the first place, and a sharing feature does nothing to keep the craft flying itself.
Ad click-through rate is a consumer-internet metric with nothing to do with a spacecraft's survival or control.
Nobody is choosing a color theme while the craft is out of contact and fighting a hardware fault on its own.

scenario: 你在比较一个请求是 CPU-bound、memory-bound 还是 IO-bound；只需要数量级，不需要精确 benchmark。
scenario_en: You are comparing whether a request is CPU-bound, memory-bound, or IO-bound; you only need order of magnitude, not an exact benchmark.
q: 哪个经验锚点最适合白板估算？
q_en: Which rule of thumb fits a whiteboard estimate?
options: CPU 任务为 X，内存约 10X，IO 约 100X
CPU、内存、磁盘总是同样快
磁盘 seek 通常比 CPU cache 访问更快
网络跨洲 RTT 可以忽略不计
options_en: If a CPU task is X, memory is roughly 10X and IO roughly 100X.
CPU, memory, and disk are always equally fast.
Disk seeks are usually faster than CPU cache access.
Cross-continent RTT can be ignored.
why: 这是数量级锚点：CPU 缓存/计算最快，内存慢一档，磁盘和网络 I/O 再慢很多。它会影响你是优化算法、缓存数据，还是减少远程/磁盘访问。
why_en: The CPU-memory-IO gap tells you whether to optimize computation, cache data, or remove disk and network hops.

termDefinitions.meaning: 往返时延，表示请求到达对端并收到响应的时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Round-Trip Time is the time for a request to reach the peer and for the response to return.

optionExplanations: CPU 计算最快，内存慢一档，磁盘/网络 I/O 再慢上百倍，这个量级差决定该优化算法还是该减少远程调用。
CPU、内存、磁盘的访问速度差着好几个数量级，说它们一样快会让你完全找错优化方向。
磁盘 seek 是机械或介质级延迟，比 CPU 片上缓存慢得多，这个说法把两者顺序反了。
跨洲光纤传播本身就有几十毫秒的物理下限，忽略它会让延迟预算算得完全不靠谱。
optionExplanations_en: CPU compute is fastest, memory is roughly one order slower, and disk or network I/O is roughly two orders slower still — that gap decides whether you optimize an algorithm or cut a remote call.
CPU, memory, and disk access speeds differ by orders of magnitude; treating them as equal points optimization effort in the wrong place entirely.
A disk seek is a mechanical or media-level delay, far slower than an on-chip CPU cache — this option has the ordering backwards.
Cross-continent fiber has a physical propagation floor of tens of milliseconds; ignoring it makes any latency budget unreliable.

scenario: 估算单台 64 核服务器处理简单 CPU 请求：假设每请求 350 万条指令、CPI=1、主频 3.5 GHz。
scenario_en: Estimate a 64-core server handling simple CPU requests: assume 3.5 million instructions per request, CPI=1, and a 3.5 GHz clock.
q: 64K RPS 粗估在设计里怎么用？
q_en: How should the 64K RPS estimate be used in design?
options: 作为服务器数量估算的分母，再用真实压测修正
当作所有请求类型永远成立的 SLA
替代峰值流量、缓存命中率和数据库瓶颈分析
证明单机一定能承接所有生产流量
options_en: Use it as the denominator for server-count estimates, then correct it with load tests.
Treat it as an SLA that holds for every request type forever.
Use it instead of analyzing peaks, cache hit rate, and database bottlenecks.
Use it to prove one machine can handle all production traffic.
why: CPU time = 3.5M × 1 / 3.5GHz = 0.001 秒，所以每核约 1,000 RPS，64 核约 64,000 RPS。这个数是后续估服务器数量的分母。
why_en: At 1 ms per request, one core handles about 1,000 RPS, so 64 cores give roughly 64,000 RPS for capacity estimates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒请求数，用来衡量服务吞吐。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Requests Per Second measures how many requests a service handles each second.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条指令平均消耗的 CPU 时钟周期数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cycles Per Instruction is the average CPU cycles spent per instruction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 十亿赫兹，常用于表示 CPU 每秒时钟周期数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gigahertz means billions of clock cycles per second.

optionExplanations: 64K RPS 只是粗算出的分母，真实压测会因为缓存命中率、请求差异等因素修正它，不能直接当最终结论。
这个数字来自简化假设（固定指令数、CPI=1），把它当成对所有请求类型永远成立的 SLA 会高估实际能力。
粗估不能替代峰值分析、缓存命中率和数据库瓶颈，这些仍然要单独建模。
64K RPS 只是单机理论上限的估算，不能证明一台机器就能扛住生产环境的全部真实流量。
optionExplanations_en: 64K RPS is just a rough denominator; real load tests correct it for cache hit rate, request variance, and other factors — it isn't the final number.
This figure comes from simplified assumptions (fixed instruction count, CPI=1); treating it as an SLA for every request type forever overstates real capacity.
A rough estimate can't replace peak analysis, cache hit rate, or database bottleneck modeling — those still need separate work.
64K RPS is a theoretical single-machine ceiling, not proof that one machine can absorb all of production's real traffic.

scenario: Twitter-like 服务有 500M DAU，每人每天 20 次请求；假设请求均匀分布，单机 64,000 RPS。
scenario_en: A Twitter-like service has 500M DAU and 20 requests per user per day; assume even distribution and 64,000 RPS per server.
q: 平均负载下服务器数估算给出什么警告？
q_en: What warning does the average-load server estimate give?
options: 把 2 台当下限，再建峰值模型
把 2 台当最终答案，不再看峰值和余量
DAU 不能用于任何估算，也不能转成 RPS
只要平均值够低，就不需要监控和压测
options_en: Treat two servers as a lower bound, then model peaks.
Treat two servers as final and ignore peaks and buffer.
DAU can never be converted into RPS for estimates.
If the average is low, monitoring and load tests are unnecessary.
why: 公式是 500M × 20 / 86,400 ≈ 115K RPS；115K / 64K ≈ 2 台。这个结果太乐观，说明平均值必须接峰值模型、监控和余量。
why_en: The average estimate gives about two servers, which is a sanity-check failure because real traffic is not evenly spread.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日活跃用户数，表示一天内使用产品的独立用户数量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Daily Active Users is the number of unique users active in one day.

optionExplanations: 平均负载算出来的 2 台只是下限，真实流量有峰谷，还要按峰值模型和余量往上加。
把 2 台当最终答案，等同于假设流量永远均匀分布，一到高峰立刻扛不住。
DAU 乘人均请求数正是这类估算的标准起点，完全可以转成 RPS，只是不能当唯一依据。
平均值低不代表峰值低，该有的监控和压测一样不能少，否则峰值来了才发现容量不够。
optionExplanations_en: Two servers from the average-load estimate is only a lower bound; real traffic has peaks and valleys, so a peak model and buffer still need to be added.
Treating two servers as final assumes traffic is always evenly spread — the first real peak overwhelms it.
DAU times requests-per-user is exactly the standard starting point for this kind of estimate and converts to RPS fine — it just can't be the only input.
A low average doesn't mean a low peak; monitoring and load tests are still needed, or the capacity gap only shows up once the peak hits.

scenario: 同一个 Twitter-like 服务每天 10B 请求；若用 80/20 假设：80% 流量集中在一天 20% 的时间，即 4.8 小时；单机 64,000 RPS。
scenario_en: The same Twitter-like service has 10B requests/day; with an 80/20 assumption, 80% of traffic lands in 20% of the day, or 4.8 hours; each server handles 64,000 RPS.
q: 80/20 峰值模型改变了什么判断？
q_en: What judgment does the 80/20 peak model change?
options: 把平均容量改成更接近峰值窗口的容量
证明平均流量模型已经足够，不用看峰值
证明所有日请求都会挤在同一秒发生
说明服务器数量和流量分布没有关系
options_en: It turns the average-capacity estimate into a peak-window estimate.
It proves the average traffic model is enough and peaks can be ignored.
It proves every daily request arrives in the same second.
It says server count is unrelated to traffic distribution.
why: 公式是 0.8 × 10B / (4.8 × 3600) ≈ 463K RPS；463K / 64K ≈ 7.2，向上取约 8 台。它用于把平均负载改成更像真实的峰值容量。
why_en: The 80/20 peak model gives about 8 servers and is a better capacity input than a flat daily average.
optionExplanations: 把 80% 流量压进一天 20% 的时间窗口重算，服务器数从平均模型的 2 台变成约 8 台，这才是更贴近真实峰值的容量。
正是因为平均模型算出的 2 台太乐观，才需要用 80/20 峰值窗口去修正它，不能说平均模型已经够用。
80/20 假设的是流量集中在一天 20% 的时间窗口（4.8 小时），不是全部挤进同一秒。
流量分布直接决定了峰值窗口有多短、需要多少台服务器，两者是强相关，不是无关。
optionExplanations_en: Recomputing with 80% of traffic packed into 20% of the day changes the server count from the average model's 2 to about 8 — a much closer match to real peak capacity.
It's precisely because the average model's 2-server estimate was too optimistic that the 80/20 peak window is needed to correct it — the average model wasn't enough.
The 80/20 assumption packs traffic into 20% of the day (4.8 hours), not into a single second.
Traffic distribution directly decides how short the peak window is and how many servers are needed — the two are tightly linked, not unrelated.

scenario: Twitter-like 服务：500M DAU，每人每天 3 条 tweet；每条 250B 元数据，10% 带 200KB 图片，5% 带 3MB 视频。
scenario_en: A Twitter-like service has 500M DAU, 3 tweets per user per day, 250B metadata per tweet, 10% with a 200KB image, and 5% with a 3MB video.
q: 每日存储量为什么由媒体主导？
q_en: Why is daily storage dominated by media?
options: 按文本、图片、视频分别相乘，视频项主导容量
文本一定比视频大，因为每条 tweet 都有文字
图片和视频比例不影响存储，只看用户数
只需要算 tweet 条数，不需要对象大小
options_en: Multiply text, image, and video terms separately, and the video term dominates.
Text is always larger than video because every tweet has text.
Image and video ratios do not affect storage; only user count matters.
Only tweet count matters, and object size is irrelevant.
why: 公式是 1.5B tweets/day 分别乘以对象大小和媒体比例；视频对象虽然只占 5%，但 3MB 远大于文本。这个数会决定 blob storage、保留期和带宽预算。
why_en: Media dominates because object size overwhelms count, driving blob storage, retention, and bandwidth planning.

termDefinitions.meaning: 太字节，约等于 10^12 字节，常用于存储估算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A terabyte is about 10^12 bytes and is commonly used in storage estimates.

optionExplanations: 文本、图片、视频分别按各自比例和大小相乘，视频虽然只占 5%，但单条 3MB 远超文本的 250B，加总后视频项主导总容量。
每条 tweet 都带 250B 文本没错，但一条 3MB 的视频比它大上万倍，视频显然更占空间。
图片、视频各占的比例直接乘进总容量公式，改变这两个比例会明显改变结果。
只算 tweet 条数会漏掉媒体附件的大小差异，250B 的文本和 3MB 的视频完全不是一个数量级。
optionExplanations_en: Text, image, and video are each multiplied by their own ratio and size; video is only 5% of tweets, but at 3MB each versus 250B of text, the video term dominates the total.
Every tweet does carry 250B of text, but a single 3MB video is tens of thousands of times larger — video clearly takes more space.
Image and video ratios plug directly into the storage formula; changing either ratio visibly changes the result.
Counting only tweet volume misses the size gap in media attachments — 250B of text and 3MB of video aren't remotely the same order of magnitude.

scenario: 服务每天写入约 255TB 媒体和文本数据；要估算平均入站带宽，按一天 86,400 秒，字节转 bit 乘 8。
scenario_en: A service ingests about 255TB of media and text per day; estimate average inbound bandwidth using 86,400 seconds per day and multiply bytes by 8 for bits.
q: 24 Gbps 入站估算约束哪条路径？
q_en: Which path does the 24 Gbps ingress estimate constrain?
options: 上传入口、网络链路和对象存储写入能力
只约束前端按钮颜色和页面布局
只约束离线推荐模型训练指标
说明出站视频播放带宽一定为零
options_en: Upload ingress, network links, and object-store write capacity.
Only frontend button colors and page layout.
Only offline recommendation-training metrics.
It means outbound video playback bandwidth is zero.
why: 公式是 255 × 10^12 bytes / 86,400 × 8 ≈ 24 × 10^9 bit/s。这个数是网络、入口代理和对象存储写入能力的起点。
why_en: Dividing daily bytes by seconds and multiplying by 8 gives about 24 Gbps, the starting point for ingress and storage capacity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒十亿比特，常用于网络带宽估算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Gigabits per second measures network bandwidth in billions of bits per second.

optionExplanations: 24 Gbps 是入站数据流经的路径：上传入口要能吃下这个速率，网络链路和对象存储的写入能力都要按它来配。
带宽估算跟前端按钮颜色或页面布局完全是两个层面的事，不会互相约束。
这个数字算的是入站写入带宽，跟离线训练用什么指标衡量模型没有关系。
24 Gbps 算的是入站上传，完全没涉及出站播放流量，不能反推出站带宽为零。
optionExplanations_en: 24 Gbps is the path the inbound data actually flows through: upload ingress has to absorb that rate, and network links plus object-store writes size to it.
Bandwidth sizing and frontend button colors or layout live on completely different layers and don't constrain each other.
This number measures inbound write bandwidth, which has nothing to do with what metrics offline training uses.
24 Gbps is calculated from inbound uploads only; it says nothing about outbound playback traffic, so it can't imply outbound bandwidth is zero.

scenario: 你在做容量草算，需要把机器角色和主要资源压力对应起来，而不是把所有服务器都当同一种盒子。
scenario_en: You are doing a capacity estimate and need to map server roles to their dominant resource pressure instead of treating every server as the same box.
q: 哪些角色映射合理？
q_en: Which role mappings are reasonable?
options: Web server：接负载均衡后的 API 入口，CPU 和网络更关键
Application server：跑业务逻辑和动态内容，CPU/内存压力更大
Storage server：优先提供大容量持久存储
Storage server：一定比所有缓存服务器低延迟
options_en: Web server: API entry point after load balancing, with CPU and network pressure.
Application server: runs business logic and dynamic content, often heavier on CPU and memory.
Storage server: prioritizes large persistent capacity.
Storage server: always lower latency than every cache server.
why: 不同角色的瓶颈不同：入口看连接和 CPU，业务层看逻辑计算，存储层看容量、I/O 和耐久性。混成一种机器会让估算失真。
why_en: Server roles have different bottlenecks, so capacity estimates should separate entry, business logic, and storage pressure.
optionExplanations: web server 是负载均衡后的入口，扛的是连接数和请求分发，CPU 和网络是它的主要压力点。
