q_en: Which are core functional requirements for a blob store?
options: 创建 container 并上传 blob
通过生成路径读取 blob
按保留期删除 blob 或 container
为每个 blob 执行跨表 SQL JOIN
options_en: Create containers and upload blobs
Read blobs through generated paths
Delete blobs or containers with retention behavior
Run cross-table SQL joins for every blob
why: Blob store 的 API 围绕 container、blob、路径和删除生命周期；JOIN 不是对象存储接口的主职责。
why_en: Blob-store APIs center on containers, blobs, paths, and lifecycle deletion, not relational joins.
optionExplanations: 创建 container 并上传 blob 是写路径的起点，account 下先建好容器才谈得上放对象。
通过生成的路径读取 blob 让读操作只认一个稳定标识，不用关心底层数据分布在哪。
按保留期删除 blob 或 container 让清理逻辑跟着生命周期走，而不是靠人工临时清盘。
对每个 blob 跑跨表 SQL JOIN 需要关系模型和查询优化器，不是对象存储接口该承担的职责。
optionExplanations_en: Creating a container and uploading a blob is where the write path starts — you need a container under the account before anything else.
Reading a blob through its generated path lets a read only care about one stable identifier, not where the data physically lives.
Deleting blobs or containers under a retention rule ties cleanup to the object lifecycle instead of ad hoc manual purges.
Running cross-table SQL joins per blob needs a relational model and query optimizer, which isn't what an object-storage API is for.

scenario: 估算一个 I/O 密集 blob 服务：峰值按 5M RPS 粗算，每台服务器保守按 500 RPS。
scenario_en: Estimate an I/O-heavy blob service with a rough 5M peak RPS and 500 RPS per server.
q: 服务器数量估算如何得到？
q_en: How do you estimate the server count?
text: 服务器数 = peak RPS / per-server RPS = 5,000,000 / 500 ≈ {{10,000 servers}}。
text_en: Server count = peak RPS / per-server RPS = 5,000,000 / 500 ≈ {{10,000 servers}}.
why: RPS = Requests Per Second，每秒请求数；这个数不是背答案，而是后续负载均衡、机房容量和监控阈值的输入。
why_en: RPS means requests per second, and this estimate feeds load balancing, capacity planning, and monitoring thresholds.

termDefinitions.meaning: RPS：每秒请求数，用来估算服务吞吐需求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPS means requests per second and measures service throughput demand.

scenario: 每天 250,000 个上传，每个视频约 50 MB，缩略图约 20 KB，先按单副本、单清晰度估算。
scenario_en: There are 250,000 uploads per day; each video is about 50 MB with a 20 KB thumbnail, estimated as one copy and one resolution.
q: 每日新增存储量的粗估公式是什么？
q_en: What is the rough daily storage formula?
text: 每日存储 ≈ uploads/day × (video + thumbnail) = 250,000 × (50 MB + 20 KB) ≈ {{12.5 TB/day}}。
text_en: Daily storage ≈ uploads/day × (video + thumbnail) = 250,000 × (50 MB + 20 KB) ≈ {{12.5 TB/day}}.
why: 这个值只是单副本基线；复制、多分辨率和保留策略会把真实容量继续放大。
why_en: This is only the single-copy baseline; replicas, multiple resolutions, and retention increase the real footprint.

scenario: 同一 blob 服务每天新增约 12.5 TB，读路径按 5M DAU、每人 20 次、每次 50 MB 粗算。
scenario_en: The service adds about 12.5 TB per day; reads are estimated from 5M DAU, 20 reads per user, and 50 MB per read.
q: 为什么 outgoing bandwidth 会远高于 incoming bandwidth？
q_en: Why is outgoing bandwidth much higher than incoming bandwidth?
text: 写入带宽约 daily bytes / 86,400；读取带宽约 DAU × reads/user × object size / 86,400，因此读侧可到 {{hundreds of Gb/s}}。
text_en: Ingress is daily bytes / 86,400; egress is DAU × reads per user × object size / 86,400, so reads can reach {{hundreds of Gb/s}}.
why: DAU = Daily Active Users；读多写少会把 CDN、并行下载和缓存放到设计重点。
why_en: DAU means daily active users, and read-heavy bandwidth pushes the design toward CDN, caching, and parallel download.

termDefinitions.meaning: DAU：每日活跃用户数，常用来估算读请求和带宽。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DAU means daily active users and is often used to estimate read traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN：把公开内容缓存到离用户更近的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches public content at edge locations closer to users.

q: Blob store 的基础组件通常包括哪些？
q_en: Which building blocks commonly appear in a blob store?
options: Rate limiter 控制调用速率
Load balancer 分配请求
Metadata database 存对象元数据
Monitoring 跟踪磁盘和节点健康
options_en: A rate limiter controls request rates
A load balancer distributes requests
A metadata database stores object metadata
Monitoring tracks disk and node health
why: 这些组件分别保护入口、分摊流量、定位数据和触发扩容或修复。
why_en: These components protect the edge, spread traffic, locate data, and trigger scaling or repair.
optionExplanations: Rate limiter 挡在入口控制调用速率，防止突发流量或滥用直接压垮后端节点。
Load balancer 把请求分摊到多台 frontend 或 data node 上，避免单点扛下全部流量。
Metadata database 记录 blob 在哪些 chunk、哪些节点，是定位真实数据的入口。
Monitoring 持续跟踪磁盘和节点健康，故障发生时能触发扩容或修复流程。
optionExplanations_en: A rate limiter sits at the edge controlling call rate, stopping a burst or abuse from overwhelming backend nodes directly.
A load balancer spreads requests across multiple frontends or data nodes so no single one takes all the traffic.
A metadata database records which chunks and nodes hold a blob, acting as the lookup that locates the real data.
Monitoring continuously tracks disk and node health so a failure can trigger scaling or repair automatically.

q: Blob store API 为什么围绕 containerPath 和 blobPath？
q_en: Why do blob-store APIs revolve around containerPath and blobPath?
text: containerPath 通常包含 accountID + containerID；blobPath 再包含唯一 blob ID，让系统能 {{定位账户、容器和对象}}。
text_en: containerPath usually includes accountID plus containerID, and blobPath adds a unique blob ID so the system can {{locate account, container, and object}}.
why: 路径是 API 层的稳定名字，内部可以用 metadata 把它映射到 chunk 和 data node。
why_en: The path is the stable API name, while metadata maps it to chunks and data nodes internally.

scenario: 一个账号下可以有多个 container，container 不能嵌套，名字在同一账号内必须唯一。
scenario_en: An account can own multiple containers; containers are not nested, and names must be unique within the account.
q: 创建 container 时应检查什么不变量？
q_en: What invariant should createContainer enforce?
options: 同一 account 下 containerName 唯一
全世界所有账号不能用同一个 containerName
container 必须嵌套在另一个 container 里
每个账号只能有一个 blob
options_en: containerName is unique within the account
No two accounts globally can reuse a containerName
A container must be nested inside another container
Each account can have only one blob
why: 名字作用域在 storage account 内，过度做成全局唯一会增加协调成本且不符合 API 模型。
why_en: The name scope is the storage account, so global uniqueness would add unnecessary coordination.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品明确把 containerName 做成公开全局域名，才需要全局唯一。
tradeoff: 局部命名空间 vs 全局协调成本
optionExplanations: container 名字的作用域是账号内部，同一账号下不能重名就够了，不需要跨账号协调。
全世界所有账号都不能重名意味着每次创建都要跨账号做全局协调，成本远超实际需要。
题目已经说明 container 不能嵌套，要求它嵌套在另一个 container 里违反了这条约束。
一个账号能有多个 container，每个 container 也能装多个 blob，只能有一个 blob 与此矛盾。
optionExplanations_en: The container name only needs to be unique within its own account, no cross-account coordination required.
Requiring the name to be globally unique across every account means coordinating globally on every create, far more cost than needed.
The scenario already states containers cannot be nested, so requiring nesting directly contradicts that constraint.
One account can hold several containers, and each container can hold several blobs, contradicting a one-blob-per-account limit.

scenario: 同一 container 中用户再次上传同名 blob，系统假设 blob 不原地修改。
scenario_en: A user uploads a blob with the same name in the same container, and blobs are assumed not to be modified in place.
q: 系统应如何处理同名上传？
q_en: How should the system handle the duplicate-name upload?
options: 创建新版本或新唯一 ID
直接覆盖旧 chunk 且不记录版本
拒绝所有同名文件直到人工处理
把 container 删除后重建
options_en: Create a new version or unique ID
Overwrite old chunks without recording a version
Reject every duplicate name until manual handling
Delete and recreate the container
why: 版本化保留了不可变对象语义，也让并发同名写不会互相覆盖。
why_en: Versioning preserves immutable-object semantics and avoids overwriting concurrent uploads.
optionExplanations: 同名再次上传就生成新版本或新 ID，既保住不可变对象的语义，也让并发写不会互相覆盖。
直接覆盖旧 chunk 且不记录版本会破坏不可变假设，还可能让并发上传的两个版本互相踩掉。
拒绝所有同名文件直到人工处理会阻塞正常的重复上传场景，成本远高于自动生成新版本。
把 container 删除重建是极端操作，会连带清掉其它 blob，跟单个同名上传的场景不成比例。
optionExplanations_en: A same-name upload gets a new version or a new ID, preserving immutable-object semantics and keeping concurrent writes from clobbering each other.
Overwriting the old chunks without recording a version breaks the immutability assumption and lets two concurrent uploads stomp on each other.
Rejecting every duplicate name until manual handling blocks a perfectly normal re-upload scenario, far costlier than just versioning it.
Deleting and recreating the container is a drastic move that wipes out every other blob too, wildly disproportionate to one duplicate name.

scenario: 用户删除一个大视频，视频有多个 chunk 和副本；删除 API 需要低延迟返回。
scenario_en: A user deletes a large video with many chunks and replicas, and the delete API should return quickly.
q: 为什么先标记 DELETED 再异步 GC？
q_en: Why mark DELETED first and run garbage collection later?
options: 让用户立即不可见，同时避免同步删除所有副本的高延迟
确保删除请求永远不会成功
让旧数据继续可公开访问
把 metadata 和 data node 永久分离
options_en: Make it invisible immediately while avoiding synchronous deletion of every replica
Ensure delete requests never succeed
Keep old data publicly accessible
Permanently separate metadata from data nodes
why: 元数据标记先切断可见性，后台 GC 再慢慢回收 chunk；代价是空间回收会滞后。
why_en: A metadata tombstone hides the blob immediately, while background GC reclaims chunks later.

termDefinitions.meaning: GC：后台清理不再可达或已删除数据的过程。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Garbage collection is the background process that removes no-longer-reachable data.

optionExplanations: 先把 metadata 标记为 DELETED 让用户立刻看不到它，真正回收多个 chunk 副本的工作留给后台 GC 慢慢做，避免同步删除拖慢延迟。
标记删除后 API 立刻返回成功，删除请求本身是成功的，只是底层字节的回收还没完成。
标记为 DELETED 后前端查询就该把它当不存在处理，不应该让旧数据继续对外可见。
GC 只是清理已删除数据的后台流程，跟 metadata 和 data node 是否永久分离没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: Marking metadata DELETED first makes it invisible right away, while background GC slowly reclaims the many chunk replicas, avoiding a slow synchronous delete.
The delete API returns success right after the tombstone is set, so the request does succeed — only the byte reclamation is still pending.
Once marked DELETED, front-end lookups should treat it as gone; it shouldn't stay visible to the public afterward.
GC is just the background process reclaiming deleted data; it has nothing to do with whether metadata and data nodes are permanently separate systems.

q: Blob store 的高层架构链路是什么？
q_en: What is the high-level architecture flow of a blob store?
steps: Load balancer 把请求分发到 frontend servers
Client 发起上传、下载或删除 API
Frontend 与 manager 协调 metadata 和授权
Data nodes 存储或读取实际 chunks
Monitoring 观察节点和磁盘健康
why: 前端服务器处理 API，manager 负责位置和权限，data node 负责真实字节。
why_en: Frontend servers handle APIs, the manager handles placement and permissions, and data nodes store the bytes.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C[Client] --> LB[Load balancer]
  LB --> FE[Frontend]
  FE --> M[Manager]
  M --> MD[(Metadata DB)]
  FE --> DN[Data nodes]
  MON[Monitoring] --> M
  MON --> DN

q: Blob 上传写路径应如何排序？
q_en: What is the correct order of the blob upload path?
steps: Manager 生成 blob ID 并选择 chunk 放置位置
Frontend 接收 uploadBlob 请求
Frontend 把 chunks 写到 data nodes
Manager 记录 blob metadata 和副本信息
客户端拿到 fully qualified blob path
why: 写路径先确定身份和放置，再写真实数据，最后把可寻址路径和元数据发布给客户端。
why_en: The write path chooses placement, writes chunks, records metadata, and then returns the stable blob path.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant F as Frontend
  participant M as Manager
  participant D as DataNodes
  C->>F: uploadBlob
  F->>M: ask placement
  M-->>F: blob id + chunk map
  F->>D: write chunks
  M->>M: record metadata
  F-->>C: blob path

q: Blob 下载读路径应如何排序？
q_en: What is the correct order of the blob download path?
steps: Manager 检查 public/private 权限
Frontend 用 blobPath 请求 metadata
Manager 返回 chunk 到 data node 的映射
Client 或 frontend 从 data nodes 读取 chunks
客户端缓存 chunk metadata 以便后续读
why: 读路径先拿 metadata 和授权，再按 chunk map 读数据；缓存 metadata 能减轻 manager 压力。
why_en: Reads fetch metadata and authorization first, then use the chunk map to read data and cache future lookups.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant F as Frontend
  participant M as Manager
  participant D as DataNodes
  C->>F: downloadBlob(path)
  F->>M: metadata + auth
  M-->>F: chunk map
  C->>D: read chunks
  C->>C: cache metadata

scenario: 下载 2 GB 视频时，metadata 只有 chunk 位置和权限信息，真实字节在 data nodes 上。
scenario_en: When downloading a 2 GB video, metadata contains chunk locations and access information, while bytes live on data nodes.
q: 为什么要分离 metadata path 和 blob data path？
q_en: Why separate the metadata path from the blob data path?
options: metadata 管位置，data node 传字节
所有视频字节都要经过 manager 转发
metadata 可以在读路径里直接丢弃
data nodes 只用来存账号名单
options_en: metadata handles location, data nodes carry the bytes
All video bytes must be relayed through the manager
metadata can be discarded directly on the read path
Data nodes only store the list of accounts
why: manager 擅长做位置和权限决策，不适合承载大文件传输带宽；字节流分散到 data nodes 才能横向扩展。
why_en: The manager should decide placement and authorization, while data nodes carry the scalable byte-transfer load.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象很小且吞吐低，让 frontend 代理数据会更简单。
tradeoff: 集中控制 metadata vs 分散传输带宽
optionExplanations: 下载 2GB 视频时，manager 只做位置和权限这类轻量决策，真正的大字节流走 data nodes，控制面和数据面分开才能横向扩展。
如果所有视频字节都经过 manager，2GB 这种大文件会直接把它的带宽和连接压垮，manager 撑不住这种流量。
metadata 记着 chunk 位置和权限，丢掉它读路径就定位不到数据在哪些 data node 上。
账号列表只是 metadata 里的一小部分，data nodes 存的是真实字节而不是账号信息。
optionExplanations_en: Downloading a 2 GB video means the manager only makes light location/permission decisions while the actual bytes flow through data nodes, so control and data planes can each scale on their own.
Routing every video byte through the manager would let a 2 GB file overwhelm its bandwidth and connections — it just isn't built for that traffic.
Metadata holds chunk locations and permissions; drop it and the read path has no way to find which data nodes hold the bytes.
Account lists are only a small slice of metadata; data nodes hold the real bytes, not account information.

scenario: Blob store 的 manager 维护数据节点、路径、权限和 chunk 映射；如果它挂掉，新请求会受影响。
scenario_en: The manager tracks data nodes, paths, permissions, and chunk mappings; if it fails, new requests are affected.
q: 如何降低 manager 单点故障风险？
q_en: How can you reduce the manager single-point-of-failure risk?
options: 定期 snapshot，standby 随时接管
metadata 只放在内存里不落盘
把权限检查这一步整个删掉
让客户端随机去猜 chunk 位置
options_en: Snapshot regularly so standby can take over anytime
Keep metadata only in memory, never persisted
Remove the authorization check step entirely
Let the client randomly guess the chunk location
why: snapshot 给 standby 一个可恢复的状态基线，故障后能从保存状态继续服务。
why_en: Persisted snapshots give a standby manager a recoverable state to take over after failure.
optionExplanations: 定期给 manager 状态打快照，standby 节点能从这份快照恢复并接管，故障后不用从零重建。
metadata 只放内存意味着 manager 一重启或崩溃，节点、路径、权限这些状态就全丢了。
删除权限检查解决不了单点故障，反而把访问控制这道保护也一起去掉了。
客户端随机猜 chunk 位置既没有恢复能力，也拿不到正确数据，不是可靠性方案。
optionExplanations_en: Periodically snapshotting the manager's state gives a standby a recoverable baseline, so it can take over after a failure without rebuilding from scratch.
Keeping metadata only in memory means one manager restart or crash wipes out every node, path, and permission record it held.
Removing authorization checks does nothing for single-point-of-failure risk and just strips away access control on top of it.
Having clients randomly guess chunk locations has no recovery story and won't even fetch the right data — it isn't a reliability plan.

q: Blob store 的 metadata 层级如何组织？
q_en: How is blob-store metadata organized?
text: 常见层级是 account → container → blob；blob metadata 再记录 {{chunk IDs, data node IDs, replica IDs}}。
text_en: A common hierarchy is account to container to blob; blob metadata records {{chunk IDs, data node IDs, and replica IDs}}.
why: 这个布局让 list containers、list blobs 和按 blob 定位 chunks 分别落在清晰的 metadata 层。
why_en: This layout separates listing accounts and containers from locating the chunks of one blob.

scenario: 用户上传 128 MB 文件，单个数据节点不一定连续持有整块空间，系统还要并行读取和复制。
scenario_en: A user uploads a 128 MB file; one data node may not have contiguous space, and the system wants parallel reads and replication.
q: 为什么把 blob 切成固定大小 chunks？
q_en: Why split blobs into fixed-size chunks?
options: 让大对象分布存储、复制和并行读取
让 metadata 完全消失
保证所有 chunk 永远在同一磁盘
让删除必须同步扫全盘
options_en: To distribute, replicate, and read large objects in parallel
To eliminate metadata entirely
To keep all chunks on the same disk forever
To force deletion to scan every disk synchronously
why: 固定 chunk 让 manager 可以计算 byte range，并把 chunk 映射到多个 data nodes 和副本。
why_en: Fixed chunks let the manager compute byte ranges and map pieces to data nodes and replicas.
whenOtherWins: 如果对象都很小，整对象存储能减少 metadata 和寻址开销。
tradeoff: 并行和容量弹性 vs metadata 数量
optionExplanations: 128MB 文件切成固定大小 chunk 后，各个 chunk 能分布到不同 data node、各自复制、并行读取，不必挤在一个节点上。
切成 chunk 反而需要 metadata 记录每个 chunk 落在哪个 data node，不是让 metadata 消失。
分布式存储的意义就是把 chunk 散到多个磁盘和节点，永远在同一磁盘违背了这个目的。
chunk 化让删除可以按 chunk 逐个异步回收，不需要同步扫描全盘去找数据。
optionExplanations_en: Splitting a 128 MB file into fixed-size chunks lets each chunk sit on a different data node, replicate independently, and be read in parallel instead of jamming onto one node.
Chunking actually needs metadata to record which data node each chunk landed on — it doesn't make metadata disappear.
The whole point of distributed storage is scattering chunks across many disks and nodes, so keeping them all on one disk defeats that purpose.
Chunking lets deletion reclaim chunks one at a time asynchronously, with no need to synchronously scan the whole disk.

scenario: 你在选择 blob chunk size：小 chunk 让调度更细，大 chunk 让 metadata 更少。
scenario_en: You are choosing blob chunk size: small chunks give finer placement, while large chunks reduce metadata.
q: chunk size 的主要取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the main chunk-size tradeoff?
options: 小增 metadata，大伤 I/O
小 chunk 不需要 metadata
大 chunk 提供强一致
chunk size 改用户名
options_en: Small adds metadata; large can hurt I/O
Small chunks need no metadata
Large chunks provide strong consistency
Chunk size changes usernames
why: chunk size 是 metadata 数量和数据面效率的折中，不能只追求越小或越大。
why_en: Chunk size balances metadata overhead against data-path efficiency, so neither extreme is automatically best.
whenOtherWins: 如果底层硬件和对象大小高度固定，按硬件块或对象分布定一个经验值即可。
tradeoff: metadata 开销 vs I/O 效率
optionExplanations: chunk 切得越小，需要记录的 chunk 数和 metadata 条目就越多；切得越大，单次 I/O 和迁移的代价就越重，两头都有成本。
不管 chunk 切多小，manager 都得记录它在哪个 data node 上，metadata 只会更多不会消失。
chunk 大小改变的是存储和 I/O 效率，跟一致性模型是不是强一致完全是两个维度。
chunk size 是存储层的参数，跟账户系统里的用户名毫无关系，这个说法文不对题。
optionExplanations_en: Smaller chunks mean more chunk entries and more metadata to track; larger chunks make each I/O and rebalance heavier — both directions carry a cost.
No matter how small a chunk gets, the manager still has to record which data node holds it — metadata only grows, it never disappears.
Chunk size affects storage and I/O efficiency; it has nothing to do with whether the consistency model is strong or not.
Chunk size is a storage-layer parameter and has no connection to usernames in the account system — this option is a non sequitur.

scenario: 用户经常 list 某个 container 下的 blobs；如果只按随机 blobID 分区，同一用户的数据会散在很多 partition。
scenario_en: Users often list blobs in one container; random blobID partitioning scatters one user's data across many partitions.
q: metadata partition key 更适合怎么选？
q_en: What metadata partition key is a better fit?
options: full path 范围分区
随机 blobID 打散
只按文件大小分区
只按上传 IP 分区
options_en: Range-partition by full path
Scatter by random blobID
Partition only by file size
Partition only by uploader IP
why: full path 让同账号同容器的数据更容易共置，list blobs 不用扫太多分区。
why_en: Full-path partitioning keeps related container metadata near each other, making list operations cheaper.
whenOtherWins: 如果唯一目标是均匀写入且几乎不 list，随机 blobID 分布会更简单。
tradeoff: 列表局部性 vs 写入均匀性
optionExplanations: 用户常常 list 一个 container 下的 blobs，按 full path 范围分区能把同账号同容器的数据放在相邻分区，list 不用跨太多分区扫描。
按随机 blobID 打散能让写入很均匀，但同一用户的数据会散落在很多分区，list 操作要扇出查询一大堆分区。
按文件大小分区解决的是冷热或容量分层问题，跟经常按 container 列出 blob 这个访问模式没关系。
按上传 IP 分区会让同一用户换了网络就换了分区，跟他实际访问的 container 结构完全对不上。
optionExplanations_en: Since users often list blobs in one container, range-partitioning by full path co-locates one account's container data, so a list scans few partitions.
Scattering by random blobID gives very even writes, but one user's data ends up spread across many partitions, forcing list to fan out widely.
Partitioning by file size addresses hot/cold tiering, not the access pattern of frequently listing blobs within a container.
Partitioning by uploader IP moves a user to a different partition the moment they switch networks, unrelated to their actual container structure.

scenario: 用户想按 upload date、media type 和 container name 搜索对象，并支持排序和分页。
scenario_en: Users want to search objects by upload date, media type, and container name, with sorting and pagination.
q: 应增加哪类能力？
q_en: What capability should be added?
options: tags + indexing engine
扫描所有 data node 字节
禁止用户 metadata
视频转成 SQL 行
options_en: Tags plus an indexing engine
Scan bytes on every data node
Forbid user metadata
Convert videos into SQL rows
why: 标签索引把搜索条件放在 metadata 层解决，避免每次查询扫描大对象字节。
why_en: Tag indexing answers searches in the metadata layer instead of scanning large object bytes.
whenOtherWins: 如果只按完整 blobPath 点查，不建二级索引也可以。
tradeoff: 搜索能力 vs 索引维护成本
optionExplanations: 按 upload date、media type、container name 搜索并排序分页，靠给 metadata 打 tag 加一个索引引擎在这一层就能查完，不用碰对象字节。
扫描所有 data node 上的字节意味着每次搜索都要读遍存储的大文件，代价高到不现实。
禁止用户 metadata 恰恰抹掉了这些字段可搜索的能力，比如上传时间、媒体类型这些查询条件根本没地方存。
把视频内容转成 SQL 行既做不到，也偏离了问题——要索引的是元数据字段，不是视频本身。
optionExplanations_en: Searching and paging by upload date, media type, and container name can be answered entirely at the metadata layer by tagging and indexing it, no need to touch object bytes.
Scanning bytes on every data node means reading through large stored files for every search — an unrealistically expensive approach.
Forbidding user metadata removes exactly the searchable fields like upload date and media type that the query needs, breaking search entirely.
Turning video content into SQL rows isn't feasible and misses the point — it's the metadata fields that need indexing, not the video itself.

q: List blobs 为什么使用 continuation token？
q_en: Why does listBlobs use a continuation token?
text: 当 prefix 匹配太多 blob 时，响应返回一页结果和 {{continuation token}}；客户端带 token 请求下一页。
text_en: When a prefix matches too many blobs, the response returns one page plus a {{continuation token}}, which the client sends for the next page.
why: token 让服务端保持稳定扫描位置，避免一次返回过大 payload 或用脆弱的页码偏移。
why_en: The token preserves scan position so the service avoids huge responses and fragile offset paging.

scenario: Blob store 要同时容忍磁盘/机架故障、同区域机房故障和整个区域故障。
scenario_en: The blob store must tolerate disk or rack failures, same-region data-center failures, and regional failures.
q: 副本应如何跨 failure domains 放置？
q_en: How should replicas be placed across failure domains?
options: 本地、同区域不同 DC、异区域分别放置副本
所有副本放在同一块盘上
只在客户端浏览器缓存一份
只保留 metadata，不复制 chunk
options_en: Place replicas locally, in another same-region DC, and in another region
Put every replica on the same disk
Keep the only replica in the browser cache
Replicate metadata only, not chunks
why: 副本要跨独立故障域才有意义；同盘副本不能抵御磁盘或机房故障。
why_en: Replicas must span independent failure domains; copies on the same disk do not protect against disk or site failure.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是临时缓存对象且可重算，同区域单副本也许能省成本。
tradeoff: 灾难恢复能力 vs 存储和复制成本
optionExplanations: 要同时扛住磁盘/机架、同区域机房和整个区域的故障，副本就得分别放本地、同区域另一个 DC、以及异区域，跨独立故障域才真正有用。
所有副本放在同一块盘上，磁盘一坏所有副本一起没了，连最基本的磁盘故障都扛不住。
只在客户端浏览器缓存一份既不是服务端可控的副本，用户清了缓存数据就彻底没了。
只复制 metadata 不复制 chunk，字节本身没有冗余，data node 一挂就真的丢数据了。
optionExplanations_en: To survive disk/rack, same-region DC, and full-region failures at once, replicas need to sit locally, in another DC in the region, and in another region — spanning independent failure domains is what actually protects you.
Putting every replica on the same disk means one disk failure wipes out all copies at once — it can't survive even the simplest failure.
Keeping the only copy in a browser cache isn't a server-controlled replica at all, and the data is gone the moment the user clears it.
Replicating only metadata and not the chunks leaves the actual bytes with no redundancy, so one data-node failure means real data loss.

scenario: 系统要求本集群内强一致和故障容忍，同时还要把数据复制到远端区域提高区域级可用性。
scenario_en: The system needs strong consistency and fault tolerance within the primary cluster, while also copying data to remote regions for regional availability.
q: 同步复制和异步远端复制应如何搭配？
q_en: How should synchronous and asynchronous replication be combined?
options: 集群内同步复制，远端 DC 异步复制
所有远端区域都同步阻塞写入
只异步复制 metadata 不复制数据
不做复制，只靠监控告警
options_en: Synchronously replicate within the cluster, and asynchronously replicate to remote DCs
Synchronously block writes on every remote region
Only replicate metadata asynchronously, not data
Do no replication and rely on alerts
why: 本地同步给写后读和故障容忍，远端异步避免跨区域 RTT 把上传路径拖慢。
why_en: Local synchronous replication protects strong reads and failures, while remote async replication avoids cross-region latency on uploads.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务要求跨区域 RPO=0，远端同步或共识复制才值得讨论。
tradeoff: 强一致写路径 vs 跨区域延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: DC：数据中心，包含机房内的计算、网络和存储资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A DC is a data center containing compute, network, and storage resources.

termDefinitions.meaning: RTT：请求到达对端再返回的往返时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the round-trip time for a request to reach the peer and return.

termDefinitions.meaning: RPO：灾难发生时最多允许丢失的数据时间窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPO is the maximum acceptable data-loss window after a disaster.

optionExplanations: 本集群内要强一致和容错，就同步复制拿到写后读保证；远端 DC 只求区域级可用性，就异步复制，不让跨区域 RTT 拖慢上传。
所有远端区域都同步阻塞写入意味着每次上传都要等最慢那个区域的 RTT 返回，延迟会被拉到很高。
只异步复制 metadata 不复制数据字节，等于目录还在但内容没备份，区域故障时数据本身仍然丢失。
完全不做复制、只靠监控告警，出问题时告警只能通知你数据已经丢了，挽救不回任何东西。
optionExplanations_en: Needing strong consistency and fault tolerance in the local cluster calls for synchronous replication there, while remote DCs only need regional availability, so async is fine and cross-region RTT never blocks the upload.
Synchronously blocking writes on every remote region means each upload has to wait for the slowest region's round trip, pushing latency way up.
Replicating only metadata asynchronously and not the data leaves the directory intact but the content unbacked up — a regional failure still loses the actual bytes.
Doing no replication and relying only on alerts means the alert can only tell you the data is already gone, with nothing left to recover.

scenario: Data node 磁盘故障后，该节点上的 chunk 副本不可读，系统需要恢复副本数。
scenario_en: A data-node disk fails, making chunk replicas on that node unreadable; the system must restore replica count.
q: heartbeat 和 re-replication 的闭环是什么？
q_en: What is the heartbeat and re-replication loop?
options: heartbeat 查坏节点，补齐缺失副本
客户端随机去读那块坏盘
只发告警，不更新路由 mapping
直接删掉 metadata 避免被读到
options_en: Heartbeat finds the bad node, missing replicas get copied back
The client randomly reads from that bad disk
Only alert, without updating the routing mapping
Delete the metadata outright to avoid it being read
why: 正常路径是心跳上报健康；故障后 manager 标记节点不可用、路由到健康副本，并复制新副本补回冗余。
why_en: Heartbeats detect unhealthy nodes, then the manager routes around them and re-replicates chunks to restore redundancy.

termDefinitions.meaning: heartbeat：节点周期性发送的健康信号，管理节点用它判断节点是否存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a periodic health signal used to detect whether a node is alive.

optionExplanations: 节点定期发心跳，manager 靠心跳中断发现坏节点，把请求路由到健康副本，同时把缺失的副本复制回其它节点补齐冗余。
manager 发现坏节点后会把路由指向健康副本，不会让客户端继续去读已经确认故障的磁盘。
只告警不更新 chunk 到节点的映射，读请求还是会被指向那块坏盘，问题并没有被真正处理。
删掉 metadata 只会让这个 blob 彻底找不到，跟恢复副本数的目标背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Nodes send periodic heartbeats; when one stops, the manager marks the node down, routes to a healthy replica, and copies missing replicas elsewhere to restore redundancy.
Once the manager detects a bad node, it routes to a healthy replica instead — clients don't keep reading a disk already confirmed as failed.
Alerting without updating the chunk-to-node mapping still leaves reads pointed at the failed disk, so nothing actually gets fixed.
Deleting the metadata makes the blob unfindable entirely, the opposite of the goal of restoring its replica count.

q: Blob store 里哪些缓存层能分别减轻什么压力？
q_en: Which caching layers reduce which pressures in a blob store?
options: Client cache chunk metadata，减少重复问 manager
Frontend cache partition map，加快路由
Manager cache hot chunks，减少磁盘 I/O
CDN cache public blobs，减少 origin 读取
options_en: Client caches chunk metadata to reduce repeated manager lookups
Frontend caches partition maps for faster routing
Manager caches hot chunks to reduce disk I/O
CDN caches public blobs to reduce origin reads
why: 缓存不是一个点：metadata、routing、hot data 和公网分发各自挡住不同瓶颈。
why_en: Caching appears at several layers because metadata lookup, routing, hot data, and public delivery have different bottlenecks.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN：把公开内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches public content at edge nodes close to users.

termDefinitions.meaning: I/O：系统读写磁盘、网络或设备的数据操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: I/O means input/output operations such as reading or writing disk or network data.

optionExplanations: Client 缓存 chunk metadata 后，同一批 chunk 不用每次都重新问 manager 要位置信息。
Frontend 缓存 partition map 能就近算出该转发到哪个分区，少一次跨节点查询再路由。
Manager 缓存热点 chunk 能直接命中内存，减少反复打磁盘 I/O 带来的延迟。
CDN 缓存公开 blob 让大部分读请求在边缘就返回，不用每次都回源打 origin。
optionExplanations_en: Once the client caches chunk metadata, it doesn't have to ask the manager for location again for chunks it already knows about.
The frontend caching the partition map lets it compute the target partition locally, skipping an extra cross-node lookup before routing.
The manager caching hot chunks serves them straight from memory, cutting the disk I/O it would otherwise repeat on every request.
The CDN caching public blobs answers most reads right at the edge, so origin doesn't take the hit on every single request.

scenario: 公开图片经 CDN 分发，origin 设置 Cache-Control TTL。
scenario_en: Public images are delivered through a CDN, and the origin sets a Cache-Control TTL.
q: TTL 对 CDN 行为意味着什么？
q_en: What does TTL mean for CDN behavior?
options: TTL 内走缓存，过期回源
TTL 删除 origin blob
TTL 自动公开私有对象
TTL 禁止浏览器缓存
options_en: Serve cache within TTL, then refresh from origin
TTL deletes the origin blob
TTL makes private objects public
TTL forbids browser caching
why: TTL 控制边缘缓存的新鲜度窗口，能减少 origin 压力，但也带来缓存旧内容的时间上限。
why_en: TTL defines how long edge caches may serve content before refreshing, reducing origin load with bounded staleness.

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL：缓存项在需要刷新或过期前的有效时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached item remains valid before it must refresh or expire.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN：把内容缓存在靠近用户的边缘网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content in an edge network closer to users.

optionExplanations: 在 TTL 有效期内，边缘节点直接用缓存副本响应，一过期就回源刷新，用一个时间窗口换掉大部分 origin 压力。
TTL 只控制边缘副本何时刷新，不会触发对 origin 上那份 blob 本身的删除。
TTL 管的是缓存新鲜度，跟对象的访问权限是公开还是私有完全是两回事。
TTL 是给缓存设的有效期，浏览器照样可以按自己的缓存策略继续缓存这份内容。
optionExplanations_en: Within the TTL window, the edge just serves the cached copy directly and only goes back to origin once it lapses, trading a bounded staleness window for most of the origin load.
TTL only governs when the edge copy refreshes; it never triggers deleting the actual blob sitting at origin.
TTL controls cache freshness, which is a completely separate concern from whether an object's access is public or private.
TTL sets an expiry window for the cache, but the browser can still cache the content under its own separate caching policy.

q: Blob streaming 如何分段读取大文件？
q_en: How does blob streaming read a large file in pieces?
text: Streaming 按顺序请求 byte ranges：0..X-1、X..2X-1，以 {{range reads}} 方式逐段读取。
text_en: Streaming requests byte ranges in order, such as 0..X-1 and X..2X-1, using {{range reads}}.
why: 分段读取让客户端不用等完整对象下载完才开始处理，也能对失败片段重试。
why_en: Range reads let clients start processing before the whole object is downloaded and retry failed pieces.

scenario: 上传成功返回后，同一集群内所有读者都应看到同一个 blob 视图；远端区域复制可以稍后完成。
scenario_en: After upload succeeds, all readers in the same cluster should see the same blob view, while remote-region replication may finish later.
q: 一致性设计应优先保证哪条路径？
q_en: Which path should the consistency design prioritize?
options: 本集群同步复制并提交 metadata 才返回
先返回成功，再慢慢决定 blob ID 是谁
只复制远端区域，本地反而不复制
读请求可以永远绕开 metadata 查
options_en: The local cluster replicates synchronously and commits metadata before returning
Return success first, then decide the blob ID later
Only replicate to remote regions, not locally
Reads can always bypass metadata entirely
why: 强一致读依赖写路径先完成本地副本和 metadata 提交；远端异步只影响跨区域新鲜度。
why_en: Strong local reads require the write path to commit local replicas and metadata before success is returned.
whenOtherWins: 如果只是可重建的媒体缓存，写后读一致性可以放松来换上传延迟。
tradeoff: 写后读一致性 vs 上传延迟
optionExplanations: 要让本集群内所有读者立刻看到同一个视图，写入就必须先在本地同步复制并提交 metadata，成功返回后这份状态才算数。
先返回成功再慢慢定 blob ID，等于客户端已经拿到确认，但系统这时其实还没决定好这个对象到底是谁。
只复制远端区域不复制本地，本集群内的读者反而看不到刚写入的数据，这跟同集群立即一致正好相反。
读请求要靠 metadata 才能定位 chunk 在哪些 data node 上，绕开它就找不到数据本身。
optionExplanations_en: For every reader in the same cluster to see one consistent view immediately, the write must synchronously replicate locally and commit metadata before returning success.
Returning success and deciding the blob ID later means the client already has a confirmation for an object the system hasn't actually finalized yet.
Replicating only to remote regions and not locally means readers in the same cluster can't see the just-written data — the opposite of same-cluster consistency.
A read needs metadata to know which data nodes hold the chunks; bypass it and there's no way to locate the bytes at all.

scenario: 一个大 blob 被拆成多个 chunks，chunks 分散在多个 data nodes 上，并且每个 chunk 有副本。
scenario_en: A large blob is split into chunks distributed across data nodes, with replicas for each chunk.
q: 这种布局如何提高下载吞吐？
q_en: How does this layout improve download throughput?
options: 客户端可并行从多个 data nodes 拉取不同 chunks
所有 chunks 必须从 manager 串行读取
副本越多 metadata 越少到零
并行读取会自动取消权限检查
options_en: The client can fetch different chunks from multiple data nodes in parallel
All chunks must be read serially from the manager
More replicas reduce metadata to zero
Parallel reads automatically remove authorization
why: 吞吐来自把大对象拆成多条数据流；权限和 chunk map 仍由 metadata 路径控制。
why_en: Throughput improves by splitting the object into parallel data streams while metadata still controls access and locations.
optionExplanations: chunk 分散在不同 data node 上，客户端能同时从多个节点并行拉取不同 chunk，吞吐随并行度往上叠。
manager 只负责给出 chunk map，真正的字节传输走 data nodes，不需要每个 chunk 都串行经过 manager。
副本数量跟 metadata 条目多少是两件事，副本再多，chunk 位置信息该记还是要记。
权限检查在 metadata path 上完成，并行读取只是数据面并发拉取，不会绕开授权判断。
optionExplanations_en: With chunks spread across data nodes, the client can pull different chunks from several nodes at once, so throughput scales with parallelism.
The manager only hands back the chunk map; the actual byte transfer runs through data nodes, with no need to serialize each chunk through the manager.
Replica count and metadata volume are separate things — more replicas doesn't erase the need to still track where each chunk lives.
Authorization is checked on the metadata path; reading chunks in parallel is just concurrent data-plane fetching, it doesn't skip that check.

scenario: 单个 manager 大约只能处理 10,000 QPS 的协调请求，业务继续增长到远超这个量级。
scenario_en: A single manager can handle about 10,000 QPS of coordination requests, and the business grows far beyond that scale.
q: 下一步扩展 manager 的方向是什么？
q_en: What is the next scaling direction for the manager?
options: 分片或联邦 manager
所有请求固定到一个 manager
删除 metadata 服务
客户端直写任意磁盘
options_en: Shard or federate managers
Pin all requests to one manager
Delete the metadata service
Clients write arbitrary disks
why: 单 manager 是协调瓶颈，按命名空间拆分能把 metadata 和放置决策横向扩展。
why_en: Once one manager is the coordination bottleneck, sharding or federation spreads metadata and placement decisions horizontally.
whenOtherWins: 如果 QPS 远低于瓶颈，先用 standby 和 snapshot 提高可用性更划算。
tradeoff: 协调简单性 vs 横向扩展
optionExplanations: 单个 manager 撑到 10,000 QPS 就到顶了，按命名空间分片或联邦多个 manager 能把协调请求横向摊开继续扩容。
所有请求固定到一个 manager 正是当前瓶颈的成因，继续这么做只会让协调请求排队更久。
删掉 metadata 服务等于放弃位置和权限管理，读写都定位不到数据，不是扩展方案。
客户端直接写任意磁盘绕开了 manager 的放置和副本决策，数据一致性和可发现性都没法保证。
optionExplanations_en: One manager tops out around 10,000 QPS, so sharding or federating managers by namespace spreads coordination requests horizontally to keep scaling.
Pinning every request to one manager is exactly what created the bottleneck in the first place; keeping that just queues coordination requests longer.
Deleting the metadata service throws away placement and permission tracking, so nothing can locate data anymore — not a scaling plan.
Having clients write to arbitrary disks skips the manager's placement and replication decisions, so consistency and discoverability both break.

q: 设计 scalable blob store 的一条合理决策链是什么？
q_en: What is a reasonable decision chain for designing a scalable blob store?
steps: 用 chunking 和 replica placement 处理大对象与容灾
先定义 container、blobPath、upload/download/delete/list API
把 metadata path 与 blob data path 分离
用 full path partitioning 和 continuation token 支持 listing
用 heartbeat、GC、caching 和 manager standby 补可靠性
why: 我会先定对象模型和 API，再拆控制面/数据面，最后补扩展、列表和故障恢复细节。
why_en: Start with the object API, split control and data paths, then add scaling, listing, and recovery mechanisms.
diagram:
flowchart TD
  A[API model] --> B[Metadata vs data path]
  B --> C[Chunking + replicas]
  C --> D[Partition + pagination]
  D --> E[Heartbeat + GC + cache + standby]

q: 「核心概念」与具体技术（Redis、Kafka）的区别是？
q_en: What is the difference between core concepts and specific technologies like Redis or Kafka?
options: 核心概念就是记住产品名（Redis、Kafka 叫什么）
核心概念是技术无关的通用构件，面试处处会用到
核心概念只在学校课堂里出现，工作中用不到
核心概念和具体技术没有区别，学会一个就等于学会另一个
options_en: Core concepts are just the product names, like Redis or Kafka.

Core concepts are technology-agnostic building blocks — caching, sharding, consistency — that show up in almost every design problem; interviewers assume you know them and will probe once you propose a specific technology.
Core concepts only show up in academic courses, not real work.
There is no difference; learning one technology means you already know the concepts.
why: 核心概念是系统设计的「词汇与语法」：缓存是什么、何时分片、网络如何工作——先有这些才谈得上设计 Instagram。
why_en: Core concepts are technology-agnostic building blocks that interviewers assume you know and will probe when you propose using them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存/数据存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式消息队列/流处理平台。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed streaming and message-queue platform.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    API["APIs"] --> Data["Data model"]
    Data --> Scale["Scaling"]
    Scale --> Consistency["Consistency"]
    Consistency --> Numbers["Numbers"]
optionExplanations: 只背产品名撑不住追问：换成 Kafka 照样答不出该不该分片、要不要缓存。
对，缓存、分片、一致性这些构件跟具体产品无关，换哪家都用得上。
线上系统和面试天天在考这些构件，不是学校才用得到的东西。
会用 Redis 不代表懂缓存原理，换个产品名思路照样断掉。
optionExplanations_en: Memorizing product names alone breaks down under follow-ups — swap in Kafka and you still cannot answer whether to shard or cache.
Right — caching, sharding, and consistency are product-agnostic, so they carry over no matter which vendor you name.
These ideas get probed daily in production and interviews alike, not just in a classroom.
Knowing Redis's API is not the same as understanding caching; rename the product and the reasoning falls apart.

scenario: 常规的客户端-服务通信，没有实时推送需求，也没有极端的内部性能要求，要选通信协议。
scenario_en: Routine client-to-service communication has no real-time push need and no extreme internal performance requirement, so you need to choose a protocol.
q: 默认应该选什么？
q_en: For routine client-server communication, what should you choose by default?
options: 自研 UDP 协议
WebSocket
HTTP over TCP
FTP
options_en: A custom protocol built on UDP.
WebSocket.
HTTP over TCP, which is universal, mature, and covers ninety percent of use cases.
FTP.
why: 没有特殊理由就默认 HTTP over TCP：人人都懂、到处能跑；面试官也默认你会这么选。
why_en: Default to HTTP over TCP, which is well understood, works everywhere, and covers ninety percent of use cases.
whenOtherWins: 需要实时推送时才引入 SSE/WebSocket；内部服务间性能关键时用 gRPC。

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，不保证送达和顺序，换来更低开销。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: UDP is a transport-layer protocol that skips delivery and ordering guarantees for lower overhead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 早期用于文件传输的协议，现代系统间通信很少用它。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FTP is an older protocol for transferring files, rarely used for modern service communication.

tradeoff: 通用协议覆盖 90% 场景 vs 为特定需求换专用协议的额外收益
optionExplanations: 只有极端延迟场景、且能自己扛丢包和乱序时，自研 UDP 才划算，普通 API 不值得。
客户端和服务端都要频繁主动发消息（聊天、协作）时才上 WebSocket，常规请求响应用不着。
常规客户端-服务通信没有特殊要求时，HTTP over TCP 工具链和团队都现成，默认选它。
FTP 只服务纯文件传输场景，业务 API 不会选它。
optionExplanations_en: Custom UDP only pays off for extreme-latency cases where you're willing to handle loss and reordering yourself — not worth it for a normal API.
WebSocket earns its keep when both sides need to push messages often, like chat or collaboration, not routine calls.
With no special latency or push requirement, HTTP over TCP is the default because tooling and teams already support it everywhere.
FTP is built for file transfer, not the kind of request/response API this scenario needs.

scenario: 系统要给客户端做服务器推送（server push），在 SSE 和 WebSocket 之间选通信方式。
scenario_en: The system needs server push to clients, and you are choosing between SSE and WebSocket.
q: SSE 与 WebSocket 的关键区别是？
q_en: What is the key difference between SSE and WebSocket?
options: SSE 单向推送，WebSocket 双向
SSE 更快
WebSocket 是无状态的
两者完全等价
options_en: SSE is one-way: after the client opens the HTTP connection, only the server pushes down it; WebSocket is truly bidirectional and both sides can send freely.
SSE is faster.
WebSocket is stateless.
The two are completely equivalent.
why: SSE 里客户端无法在同一连接上继续发数据，适合比分/通知这类下行推送；聊天、实时协作这类双向场景要 WebSocket。
why_en: Server-sent events are unidirectional with the server pushing down one HTTP connection, while WebSockets are truly bidirectional.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 客户端
    participant S as 服务器
    Note over C,S: SSE：单向
    C->>S: HTTP 请求（打开连接）
    S-->>C: 持续推送事件
    Note over C,S: WebSocket：双向
    C->>S: 消息
    S-->>C: 消息
tradeoff: 单向推送的简单性 vs 双向实时通信能力
optionExplanations: 对，SSE 只能服务器往下推；WebSocket 两边都能随时发消息。
速度不是分界线，方向才是——先问谁能发消息，不是谁更快。
正相反，WebSocket 是有状态长连接，要占住服务器资源。
两者一个单向一个双向，能不能双发就区分开了，不是等价协议。
optionExplanations_en: Right — SSE only lets the server push down, while WebSocket lets both sides send anytime.
Speed is not the deciding factor here; direction of communication is.
The opposite is true — WebSocket holds stateful connection resources on the server.
One is one-way and the other two-way, so they cannot be interchangeable.

scenario: 做直播比分 / 站内通知：服务器持续往客户端推数据，客户端不需要频繁往回发。
scenario_en: You are building live scores or in-app notifications: the server keeps pushing updates, and clients rarely send messages back.
q: 更合适的实时方案是？
q_en: For one-way live updates, which real-time approach fits better?
options: WebSocket
SSE，实现更简单
定时整页刷新
gRPC 流
options_en: WebSocket.
Server-sent events, which are simpler to implement and work better with standard HTTP infrastructure.
Full-page polling on a timer.
A gRPC stream.
why: 单向下行推送用 SSE 就够：更简单、能复用标准 HTTP 设施，别为「实时」两个字直接上 WebSocket。
why_en: For one-way server push like live scores or notifications, server-sent events are simpler and fit standard HTTP infrastructure better.
whenOtherWins: 客户端需要频繁上行发数据（聊天、协作编辑）时，才需要 WebSocket 的双向通道。

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化，常用于内部服务间调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an RPC framework built on HTTP/2 with binary serialization, commonly used for internal service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

tradeoff: 实现简单 + 复用标准 HTTP 设施 vs 双向实时通信能力
optionExplanations: 只有客户端也要频繁上行（聊天、协作编辑）时才值得上 WebSocket 的双向通道。
服务器只需往下推分数或通知时，SSE 用更少的协议复杂度就够，还能复用标准 HTTP 设施。
低频后台数据可以轮询，但直播级更新会浪费延迟和带宽。
gRPC 流适合内部服务间的二进制通信，浏览器通知不走这条路。
optionExplanations_en: WebSocket's two-way channel is only worth it when the client also sends frequently, like chat or collaborative editing.
For server-only pushes like live scores, SSE solves it with less protocol complexity and rides on plain HTTP infrastructure.
Polling can work for infrequent updates, but live-level refresh wastes latency and bandwidth.
gRPC streams fit internal binary service calls, not browser-facing notifications.

scenario: SSE/WebSocket 连接要接入生产环境的负载均衡与容量规划。
scenario_en: SSE and WebSocket connections need to run in production behind load balancing and capacity planning.
q: SSE 和 WebSocket 都是有状态连接，这带来的设计后果是？
q_en: What design consequence follows because SSE and WebSocket are stateful connections?
options: 没有影响，照常部署
只能单机部署
必须换成 UDP
不能直接放负载均衡器后面
options_en: No impact, deploy as usual.
It can only run on a single machine.
You must switch to UDP.
You cannot just drop it behind a standard load balancer — you must plan for connection persistence and for a server dying with thousands of active connections.
why: 有状态连接绑定在具体服务器上：LB 策略、连接迁移、宕机时成千上万条连接的重连风暴都要提前设计。
why_en: Both are stateful connections, so you must plan for connection persistence and for a server dying with thousands of active connections.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

optionExplanations: 有状态长连接绑定在具体服务器上，LB 策略、宕机重连都得提前规划，不是照常部署。
多机部署可以做，只是要靠一致性哈希或 sticky session 把连接钉在固定实例上。
换协议不解决连接状态问题，UDP 本身也不管连接归属。
对，得规划连接保持策略，还要预案宕机时成千上万条连接同时重连的风暴。
optionExplanations_en: Stateful long connections tie to one server, so LB routing and reconnect storms need advance planning — it is not business as usual.
Multi-server deployment still works, it just needs sticky routing or consistent hashing to pin each connection to one instance.
Switching transport does not decide which server holds a connection; UDP itself says nothing about that either.
Right — you need a connection-persistence plan and a playbook for a reconnect storm when a server holding thousands of connections dies.

scenario: 内部服务与服务之间的调用，性能关键，接口不对浏览器/外部用户暴露。
scenario_en: Internal service-to-service calls are performance-critical and are not exposed to browsers or external users.
q: 值得提出的通信方案是？
q_en: For performance-critical internal service calls, what communication option is worth mentioning?
options: gRPC——二进制更快
对外 REST 原样复用
SOAP
服务间直接共享同一个数据库读写，跳过 API 调用
options_en: gRPC, with binary serialization over HTTP/2, much faster than JSON over HTTP.
Reuse the public REST API as-is.
SOAP.
Have the services share one database directly and skip the API call.
why: 性能关键的内部通信用 gRPC；常见模式是「对外 REST + 对内 gRPC」。
why_en: Use gRPC for internal service-to-service communication when performance is critical, since binary serialization over HTTP/2 beats JSON over HTTP.
whenOtherWins: 对外公开 API 仍用 REST——浏览器不原生支持 gRPC（gRPC-Web 需要代理且功能不全）。

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 提出的 RPC 框架，基于 HTTP/2 和二进制序列化，常用于内部服务间调用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: gRPC is an RPC framework built on HTTP/2 with binary serialization, commonly used for internal service-to-service calls.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 协议的第二代主要版本，支持多路复用等特性，是 gRPC 的传输基础。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP/2 is the second major HTTP version with multiplexing support and is the transport gRPC runs on.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把资源映射到 URL、用 HTTP 方法操作它们的 API 设计风格。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that maps resources to URLs and manipulates them with HTTP methods.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 XML 信封的老式远程调用协议，企业遗留系统里常见。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SOAP is an older XML-envelope RPC protocol common in legacy enterprise systems.

tradeoff: 二进制 + HTTP/2 的性能 vs 浏览器原生兼容性
optionExplanations: 内部高 QPS、强类型接口、同团队掌控两端时，gRPC 的二进制序列化比 JSON 更省开销。
对外公开的 REST/JSON 接口是给浏览器和第三方设计的，内部调用没必要照搬这套开销。
SOAP 多见于老系统集成，新建的内部服务基本不会主动选它。
共享数据库会让服务边界消失，一方改表结构另一方就崩，规模一大就很危险。
optionExplanations_en: For high-QPS, strongly typed internal calls under one team's control, gRPC's binary serialization beats JSON's overhead.
The public REST/JSON API is shaped for browsers and third parties; internal calls don't need to carry that overhead.
SOAP mostly shows up in legacy integrations; new internal services rarely pick it on purpose.
Sharing one database erases the service boundary — one team's schema change breaks the other, which gets dangerous at scale.

q: L7 与 L4 负载均衡器的区别是？
q_en: How do L7 and L4 load balancers differ?
options: L4 更智能，L7 更快
L7 懂内容能路由；L4 更快但不看内容
两者完全一样
L4 能读取 HTTP 路径来决定路由到哪个服务
options_en: Layer four is smarter and layer seven is faster.

Layer seven works at the application layer and can route by HTTP content, like sending API calls to one service and pages to another; layer four works at the TCP level, faster but content-blind, just distributing connections.
The two are exactly the same.
Layer four can read the HTTP path to decide which service to route to.
why: L7 看得懂请求内容所以能做内容路由；L4 只管 TCP 连接分发所以更快。WebSocket 这类持久 TCP 连接通常配 L4。
why_en: Layer seven balancers route based on HTTP content while layer four balancers work at the TCP level, faster but content-blind, which suits WebSockets.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层负载均衡，能读懂 HTTP 内容按路径/头部路由。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-seven load balancer reads application content like HTTP paths and headers to route traffic.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层负载均衡，只按 TCP 连接分发，不看内容，速度更快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A layer-four load balancer distributes TCP connections without inspecting content, which makes it faster.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用层协议，浏览器和服务器之间传输请求/响应的通用标准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP is the application-layer protocol browsers and servers use to exchange requests and responses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 传输层协议，提供可靠、有序的字节流连接。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TCP is a transport-layer protocol that provides a reliable, ordered byte stream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

tradeoff: 内容感知路由能力 vs 传输层转发速度
optionExplanations: 能力和速度说反了：是 L7 更懂内容，L4 转发更快。
对，L7 能读 HTTP 内容按路径路由；L4 只看连接和端口，所以更快。
两者看到的信息层级不同：一个懂 HTTP，一个只懂 TCP 包。
读 HTTP 路径是 L7 的能力，L4 只转发 TCP 连接，看不到应用层内容。
optionExplanations_en: The capabilities are swapped — L7 is the content-aware one, L4 is the faster one.
Right — L7 reads HTTP content to route by path, while L4 only sees connections and ports, which makes it faster.
They operate at different layers: one understands HTTP, the other only sees TCP packets.
Reading the HTTP path is an L7 capability; L4 just forwards TCP connections without seeing application content.

q: 题目一提「real-time」就上 WebSocket，为什么是常见错误？
q_en: Why is it a common mistake to jump to WebSocket whenever a prompt says real-time?
options: WebSocket 协议已经过时，工程实践里不会再用它
把 real-time 目标当成技术上不可能做到的事
长轮询/SSE 够用时，WebSocket 只是多余复杂度
WebSocket 协议本身不支持任何形式的加密传输
options_en: WebSocket the protocol is obsolete and no longer used in practice.
Treat the real-time target as something technically impossible to achieve.
When long polling or server-sent events would do, WebSocket only adds needless complexity.
WebSocket the protocol has no support for encrypted transport of any kind.
why: WebSocket 的代价是规模化的有状态连接管理；不是「实时」都要它，先问是否真需要客户端频繁上行。
why_en: Proposing WebSockets when long polling or server-sent events would do adds needless stateful-connection complexity at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在单个 TCP 连接上做全双工通信的协议，客户端和服务器都能随时发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket is a protocol for full-duplex communication over one TCP connection, letting either side send messages anytime.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务器通过一个 HTTP 连接持续单向推送数据给客户端的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE lets a server push data to the client continuously over one HTTP connection, one-way only.

optionExplanations: WebSocket 没过时，聊天、协作、多人游戏这些双向场景还是靠它。
real-time 只是延迟目标，不等于必须上双向长连接。
对，只需要下行推送时上 WebSocket，等于白背有状态连接管理和扩容成本。
加密走 TLS/WSS 就能解决，不是弃用 WebSocket 的理由。
optionExplanations_en: WebSocket is not obsolete — chat, collaboration, and multiplayer games still rely on it.
Real-time is just a latency target; it does not mean you must have a bidirectional long connection.
Right — reaching for WebSocket when you only need downstream push means carrying stateful-connection and scaling costs for nothing.
Encryption is handled by TLS or WSS; that's not a reason to avoid WebSocket.

scenario: 设计面向全球用户的低延迟系统，服务器在纽约，部分用户在伦敦访问。
scenario_en: You are designing a low-latency global system; servers are in New York, and some users access it from London.
q: 纽约到伦敦的请求，仅光纤中的光速就决定了最低延迟约是？
q_en: For a New York to London request, what latency floor does fiber propagation alone create?
options: ~1ms
RTT 约 70-90ms
options_en: About one millisecond.
A practical round trip of about seventy to ninety milliseconds, with a pure physical floor around sixty.
About two seconds.
About one hundredth of a millisecond.
why: 纽约到伦敦纯物理 RTT 下限约 55-60ms，实践中常在 70-90ms；还没开始处理就有这个级别的跨洋成本，所以全球低延迟必须区域化部署、按地理复制或分区数据。
why_en: A New York to London round trip has a physical lower bound around 55-60ms and practical network latency often around 70-90ms, which is why regional deployments and CDNs exist.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个请求从发出到收到响应的往返时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the round-trip time from sending a request to receiving its response.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把静态内容缓存到靠近用户的边缘节点的网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches static content on edge servers close to users.

q: 面试官对 API 设计环节的真实期待是？
q_en: What does an interviewer usually expect from the API-design section?
options: 完美的 API 规范文档
每个字段都定义好类型
跳过 API 直接画架构
端点合理即可，快速推进
options_en: A perfect API specification document.
Every field with its type fully defined.
Skip the API and go straight to the architecture.
Reasonable endpoints so you can move quickly to the harder architecture problems — though sloppy API design signals inexperience.
why: 多数考官不纠结完美 API，他们想看你给出合理端点后把时间留给难点；基本功还是要在，否则显得生疏。
why_en: Most interviewers just want reasonable endpoints so you can move on to harder problems, though sloppy API design signals inexperience.

termDefinitions.meaning: 程序之间约定好的调用接口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the agreed-upon interface programs use to call each other.

optionExplanations: 正式 OpenAPI 文档是给生产系统写的，面试时间根本不够磨这个。
字段能说清主流程就行，边界字段不用逐个抠。
跳过 API 会让考官看不到你定义的核心对象和主路径。
对，给出合理端点就该往下走，把时间留给存储、扩展、一致性这些难点。
optionExplanations_en: A full OpenAPI spec belongs in production docs — interview time simply does not allow for that polish.
Fields just need to convey the main flow; edge-case fields don't need individual scrutiny.
Skipping the API hides the core objects and main flow the interviewer wants to see.
Right — sketch reasonable endpoints and move on, saving time for storage, scaling, and consistency.

scenario: 面试进行到 API 设计环节，时间有限，要决定投入多少精力。
scenario_en: In the API-design part of an interview, time is limited and you need to decide how deep to go.
q: API 设计环节的合理节奏是？
q_en: What is a reasonable pace for the API-design section?
options: 开场就花 10 分钟反复打磨每一个端点的细节
用 20 分钟把每个端点的全部字段都写清楚
几分钟内画出 4-5 个关键端点然后继续推进
整个 API 设计环节完全跳过，什么都不画
options_en: Spend ten minutes right away polishing every single endpoint's details.
Spend twenty minutes writing out every field for every endpoint.
Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes, then move on.
Skip the whole API-design section entirely and draw nothing.
why: 两三分钟给出 4-5 个关键端点即可；开场 10 分钟还在磨 API 细节说明陷得太深了。
why_en: Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes and move on; ten minutes on API details is going too deep.
diagram:
flowchart LR
    Client["Client"] --> Page["GET page?cursor"]
    Page --> DB["Query next N"]
    DB --> Token["Return next cursor"]
optionExplanations: 开场就花 10 分钟反复打磨每一个端点的细节。
用 20 分钟把每个端点的全部字段都写清楚。
几分钟内画出 4-5 个关键端点就继续推进。
整个 API 设计环节完全跳过，什么都不画。
optionExplanations_en: Spend ten minutes right away polishing every single endpoint's details.
Spend twenty minutes writing out every field for every endpoint.
Sketch four or five key endpoints in a couple of minutes, then move on.
Skip the whole API-design section entirely and draw nothing.

q: 分页方式的选择：cursor-based vs offset-based，正确的判断是？
q_en: How should you choose between cursor-based and offset-based pagination?
options: cursor 适合实时插入；offset 够用
offset 永远更好
cursor 无法用 SQL 实现
两者不能混用于同一系统
options_en: Cursor-based pagination works better for real-time data where items are added frequently, while offset-based is fine for most cases.
Offset is always better.
Cursor-based pagination cannot be implemented in SQL.
The two cannot coexist in the same system.
why: 返回大结果集需要分页：数据实时增长时 offset 会漂移，cursor 更稳；一般场景 offset 简单够用。
why_en: Cursor-based pagination works better for real-time data where items are added frequently, while offset-based is fine for most cases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用上一页最后一条记录的位置作为下一页起点的分页方式，不受新插入影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor-based pagination uses the last item's position as the start of the next page, so new inserts don't shift it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用「跳过前 N 条」定位页码的分页方式，实现简单但新增数据会导致漂移/重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Offset-based pagination skips the first N rows to find a page; it's simple but drifts when new rows are inserted.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

codeSample:
-- cursor-based, stable under inserts
SELECT * FROM posts
WHERE id < :last_id
ORDER BY id DESC
LIMIT 20;
tradeoff: 插入场景下的稳定性 vs 实现的简单程度
optionExplanations: 对，高频插入的列表用 cursor 防漂移；稳定后台表格 offset 简单够用。
offset 在小而稳定的列表能用，高速插入的列表会重复或漏读。
cursor 完全能用 SQL 写：WHERE id < last_id 就是一个稳定范围查询。
同一系统按端点混用没问题，不必把一种分页方式全局化。
optionExplanations_en: Right — use cursors where inserts are frequent to avoid drift, and plain offset where the list is small and stable.
Offset works on small, stable lists, but fast-changing ones can repeat or skip rows under it.
Cursor pagination is plain SQL — `WHERE id < last_id` is a perfectly stable range query.
Mixing pagination styles per endpoint in one system is fine; you don't need to force one style everywhere.

scenario: 系统既有用户登录会话，又有内部服务之间的调用，要给两者选认证方式。
scenario_en: The system has both user login sessions and internal service-to-service calls, so you need auth for each path.
q: 标准搭配是？
q_en: What is the standard auth pairing for user sessions and service-to-service calls?
options: 都用明文密码
都用 IP 白名单
用户会话用 API key、服务间用 JWT
用户会话 JWT，服务间 API key
options_en: Use plaintext passwords for both.
Use IP allowlists for both.
Use an API key for user sessions and a JWT for service-to-service calls.
Use a JWT token for user sessions and an API key for service-to-service calls.
why: 面试口径：JWT 管用户会话、API key 管 service-to-service；点到为止，除非被追问不必展开。
why_en: Use JWT tokens for user sessions and API keys for service-to-service calls.
whenOtherWins: 若有第三方开发者生态，才需要展开 OAuth 之类的授权协议——一般面试不用主动深入。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把用户信息编码进一段签名令牌、服务端验签即可信任内容的认证方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JWT is a signed token that encodes user info so any service can verify it without a database lookup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 颁发给调用方（通常是服务或第三方）的长期凭证字符串，用于识别调用者身份。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API key is a long-lived credential string issued to a caller, usually a service, to identify who is calling.

termDefinitions.meaning: 授权协议，让第三方应用在用户同意下访问资源而不拿到密码。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: OAuth is an authorization protocol that lets a third-party app access resources with user consent, without seeing the password.

tradeoff: 用户会话免查库验签 vs 服务间凭证的可轮换/可吊销
optionExplanations: 明文密码只在本地临时调试能忍，线上认证绝不能这样做。
固定 IP 白名单能当额外防线，但替代不了身份凭证。
把两者用途对调了：JWT 更适合带身份和过期时间的用户会话，不是服务间调用。
对，用户会话要能免查库验签就用 JWT，服务间调用更常用可轮换的 API key 或 mTLS。
optionExplanations_en: Plaintext passwords might survive a local debug session, but production auth can never work that way.
A fixed IP allowlist can be an extra layer, but it never replaces an actual credential.
This swaps the two use cases — JWT fits identity-plus-timeout user sessions, not service-to-service calls.
Right — JWT lets any service verify a user session without a database hit, while API keys give service calls a rotatable credential.

scenario: 你的系统可能被机器人刷接口或恶意滥用打爆。
scenario_en: Your system may be abused by bots or malicious callers that can flood the API.
q: API 层面应该主动提的一句是？
q_en: What API-layer point should you proactively mention for an abuse-prone system?
options: 把 API 下线
提到限流，点到为止
换一种编程语言
禁止所有匿名访问
options_en: Take the API offline.
Mention rate limiting, but don't go deep unless the interviewer asks.
Switch to a different programming language.
Block all anonymous access.
why: 可能被滥用的系统值得提一句限流；分页/认证/限流这些点都是「提到即可」，深挖等考官发起。
why_en: If the system could get hammered by bots or abuse, mention rate limiting but do not go deep unless asked.
whenOtherWins: 纯内部、流量完全可信的系统就不必主动展开限流，把时间留给核心架构。

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制单位时间内允许的请求数量，防止接口被刷爆或滥用的机制。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Rate limiting caps how many requests are allowed in a time window to prevent abuse or overload.

tradeoff: 展现生产意识的成本 vs 深挖占用有限的面试时间
optionExplanations: 下线只适合真的无法服务，不是面试里的常规架构答案。
对，接口可能被刷时提一句限流，说明你想到了滥用和下游保护，别深挖占时间。
换语言不改变请求量、配额或滥用风险，这不是相关手段。
全面禁止匿名会砍掉合法的公开读路径，用限流比强制登录更精细。
optionExplanations_en: Taking the service offline only fits an inability to serve at all, not a normal interview architecture answer.
Right — mention rate limiting when abuse is plausible to show you considered it, then move on without a deep dive.
Changing languages doesn't touch request volume, quotas, or abuse risk, so it's unrelated.
Blocking every anonymous request kills legitimate public reads too; rate limiting is the more precise tool.

scenario: 数据是结构化的、关系清晰（用户账户→订单→商品），需要强一致、事务和复杂查询。
scenario_en: The data is structured with clear relationships, such as users to orders to products, and needs transactions and strong consistency.
q: 最合适的存储是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits structured relational data with transactions?
options: MongoDB，文档型数据库，schema 灵活
DynamoDB，键值/宽列数据库，按 key 强项
关系型数据库（如 Postgres），支持事务和复杂查询
S3 对象存储，适合存大文件
options_en: MongoDB, a document store with a flexible schema.
DynamoDB, a key-value/wide-column store strong at key access.
A relational database like Postgres, with transactions and complex queries.
S3 object storage, built for large files.
why: 结构化 + 清晰关系 + 强一致，正是关系型的主场：SQL 表达复杂查询、事务保一致、外键约束护关系。
why_en: Relational databases like Postgres excel with structured data, clear relationships, strong consistency, transactions, and complex SQL queries.
whenOtherWins: schema 频繁变化、或需要不依赖复杂 join 的水平扩展时，NoSQL（DynamoDB/MongoDB）更合适。

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档型 NoSQL 数据库，schema 灵活，常用 JSON 风格文档存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database with a flexible schema, storing JSON-like documents.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 的对象存储服务，用来存文件/二进制大对象，不是给结构化查询用的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: S3 is AWS's object storage service for files and blobs, not built for structured queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库强制「这个引用必须指向一条真实存在的记录」的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key constraint forces a reference to point to a row that actually exists.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组操作要么全部成功要么全部回滚的执行单元，保证数据一致。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction is a unit of operations that either all succeed or all roll back, keeping data consistent.

tradeoff: 结构化强一致 + 复杂查询 vs 灵活扩展能力
optionExplanations: 文档库适合半结构化数据，但强 join 和事务主路径不是它的强项。
键值/宽列库按 key 高吞吐访问很强，但不擅长跨实体的复杂关系查询。
对，结构清楚、关系多、要强一致时，SQL、事务和外键正是关系型的主场。
对象存储适合大文件二进制数据，不是给订单这类关系查询设计的。
optionExplanations_en: Document stores fit semi-structured data, but heavy joins and transaction-critical paths are not their strength.
Key-value or wide-column stores excel at fast key access, not queries that span relationships across entities.
Right — clear structure, many relationships, and strong consistency are exactly where SQL, transactions, and foreign keys shine.
Object storage is built for large binary files, not for relational queries across orders and users.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流
shard key 选错导致 scatter query

scenario: 数据结构频繁变化（schema 灵活），并且要跨多台服务器水平扩展，不依赖复杂 join。
scenario_en: The data shape changes often, must scale horizontally across machines, and does not rely on complex joins.
q: 更匹配的存储是？
q_en: Which storage choice fits flexible schema and horizontal scaling without complex joins?
options: NoSQL（DynamoDB / MongoDB）
单机 Postgres，不做任何扩展准备
强一致的分布式 SQL（如 Spanner），join 成本依旧高
关系型 + 只读副本，schema 变化仍要迁移脚本
options_en: NoSQL, such as DynamoDB or MongoDB.
A single Postgres instance with no scaling plan.
A strongly consistent distributed SQL database like Spanner, where joins still cost the same.
Relational plus read replicas, still needing migration scripts for schema changes.
why: 灵活 schema 与横向扩展是 NoSQL 的两大主场；代价是放弃复杂 join 和部分关系型保证。
why_en: NoSQL databases shine when you need flexible schemas or horizontal scaling across many servers without complex joins.
whenOtherWins: 需要强一致、事务与复杂关系查询时回到关系型——别为扩展性提前放弃这些保证。

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档型 NoSQL 数据库，schema 灵活，常用 JSON 风格文档存储。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database with a flexible schema, storing JSON-like documents.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流行的开源关系型数据库，支持事务、外键约束和复杂 SQL 查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database supporting transactions, foreign keys, and complex SQL.

tradeoff: 灵活 schema + 水平扩展 vs 复杂 join / 强一致保证
optionExplanations: 对，schema 常变又要横向扩展、不依赖复杂 join 时，文档或宽列 NoSQL 正合适。
单机不做扩展准备撑不住并发和数据增长，这不是应对扩容需求的方案。
分布式 SQL 保的是强关系和事务，不是为了甩掉 schema 设计成本。
只读副本能扩读不扩写，schema 变化照样要跑迁移脚本。
optionExplanations_en: Right — when schema shifts often and you need horizontal scale without heavy joins, document or wide-column NoSQL fits.
A single instance with no scaling plan can't absorb rising concurrency or data growth; it doesn't answer the scaling need.
Distributed SQL preserves strong relationships and transactions; it's not meant to shed schema-design cost.
Read replicas scale reads, not writes, and schema changes still need migration scripts either way.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流
shard key 选错导致 scatter query

q: 「规范化（normalization）」的含义与代价是？
q_en: What does normalization mean, and what does it cost?
options: 把所有数据塞进一张宽表，不做任何拆分
拆表避免重复，读取需要 join
给每个字段单独建一张表来省空间
把重复字段做压缩存储，但仍然保留每处的拷贝
options_en: Put all data into one wide table with no splitting.

Split data across tables to avoid duplication, so orders reference a user ID instead of copying user data: updating once updates everywhere, but reading full data needs joins, which get expensive at scale.
Give every single field its own table to save space.
Compress duplicate fields but still keep a copy in every place.
why: 规范化保一致性（改一次商品名全站生效），代价是读取要 join；表巨大或跨多表 join 时开销显著。
why_en: Normalization splits data across tables to avoid duplication, keeping it consistent but requiring joins that get expensive at scale.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的数据拼在一起返回的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库强制「这个引用必须指向一条真实存在的记录」的规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A foreign key constraint forces a reference to point to a row that actually exists.

optionExplanations: 全塞一张表是反规范化的极端，会让重复数据和更新不一致更严重。
对，拆实体表用引用代替拷贝，更新更一致，但读取常常要 join。
每个字段单独成表是过度拆分，查询要 join 太多张表，成本很高。
压缩只省字节，不解决实体关系或重复的事实数据。
optionExplanations_en: Cramming everything into one wide table is the extreme opposite of normalization, and it makes duplication and inconsistent updates worse.
Right — splitting entities and using references instead of copies keeps updates consistent, though reads often need joins.
A table per field is over-splitting; queries end up joining far too many tables and get expensive.
Compression just saves bytes; it doesn't resolve entity relationships or duplicate facts.

q: 反规范化（denormalization）与规范化在「读写」上的取舍是？
q_en: What is the read/write tradeoff between denormalization and normalization?
options: 反规范化会让读和写两条路径都变得更慢
规范化因为省去冗余，读取反而更快
两者在读性能和写性能上其实完全一样
反规范化省 join 换读快，但写要改多处更贵
options_en: Denormalization makes both the read path and the write path slower.
Normalization skips redundancy, so reads end up faster.
The two are actually identical on both read and write performance.
Denormalization skips joins for faster reads, but every write must now update multiple copies.
why: 把 username 直接冗余进订单，展示订单不用再 join users 表；读重、数据少变的系统这笔账通常划算。
why_en: Denormalization duplicates data to avoid joins and speed up reads, at the cost of updating every copy when the source changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据冗余拷贝进多处以省去 join、换取更快读取的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization duplicates data in multiple places to skip joins and speed up reads.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按关联字段把多张表的数据拼在一起返回的查询操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A join combines rows from multiple tables based on a related column.

tradeoff: 读性能（免 join） vs 写一致性维护成本（改多处）
optionExplanations: 反规范化通常是为了少 join、读更快，不是让两条路径都变慢。
规范化读取常常要 join 多张表，反而不是读得更快的那一边。
读路径要不要 join、更新要改几处，两者的成本形状完全不同。
对，把字段冗余进多处能省 join、读更快，但源数据一变就要改所有拷贝。
optionExplanations_en: Denormalization is usually meant to cut joins and speed reads, not slow down both paths.
Normalized reads often require joining several tables, so it's not actually the faster side for reads.
Whether reads need a join and how many places a write must update — their cost shapes are quite different.
Right — duplicating a field in multiple places skips joins and speeds reads, but every source change must now update every copy.

scenario: 面试中要给数据建模起手式，还没发现任何具体的性能问题。
scenario_en: You are starting data modeling in an interview and have not found a specific performance bottleneck yet.
q: 安全的默认策略是？
q_en: What is the safer default when you start data modeling in an interview?
options: 一上来就全面反规范化
全部数据放进一张宽表
先规范化，按需反规范化热路径
先反规范化冲刺上线，等出现数据不一致问题再回头改规范化
options_en: Denormalize everything from the start.
Put all data into one wide table.
Start with a normalized relational model and denormalize specific hot paths only after identifying read performance issues.
Denormalize first to ship faster, then fix it back to normalized once inconsistency shows up.
why: 别无缘无故上来就反规范化；考官要看的是你懂取舍，而不是盲套技巧。
why_en: Start with a normalized relational model and denormalize specific hot paths only after identifying read performance issues.
whenOtherWins: 如果有明确理由（读极重、数据几乎不变的展示路径），可以更早论证反规范化——关键是给出理由。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据拆到多张表、用引用代替拷贝以避免重复的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Normalization splits data across tables and uses references instead of copies to avoid duplication.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据冗余拷贝进多处以省去 join、换取更快读取的建模方式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Denormalization duplicates data in multiple places to skip joins and speed up reads.

tradeoff: 先保正确性再优化热路径 vs 一步到位追求读性能
optionExplanations: 还没量出读瓶颈就全面反规范化，等于提前替不存在的问题背复杂度。
完全不拆表会让重复和不一致从第一天就存在，不是起步该选的建模方式。
对，先保证正确性和一致更新，再对被证实的热路径做小范围冗余。
先冗余后补救等于先制造一致性问题，再花更大代价往回修。
optionExplanations_en: Going all-in on denormalization before measuring a read bottleneck means paying complexity for a problem you don't have yet.
Skipping table splits entirely bakes in duplication and inconsistency from day one — not a sound starting model.
Right — normalize first for correctness and consistent updates, then denormalize narrowly once a hot path is proven.
Denormalizing first just creates the consistency problem sooner, then costs more to walk back later.

q: 社交 App 用 user_id 做 DynamoDB 分区键（匹配「取用户 X 的全部帖子」），那「查提到 hashtag Y 的帖子」会怎样？
q_en: If DynamoDB is partitioned by user_id for fetching a user posts, what happens when you query posts by hashtag?
options: 要扫描整张表——因为没为这个访问模式设计
自动走索引，很快
DynamoDB 会拒绝该查询语法
和分区键查询一样快
options_en: It scans the entire table, because you did not design for this access pattern.
It automatically uses an index and stays fast.
DynamoDB rejects that query syntax outright.
It's just as fast as a partition-key query.
why: NoSQL 必须预先知道查询、围绕访问模式设计 partition/sort key：匹配的查询是单分区秒查，没设计过的查询就是全表扫描。
why_en: With user id as the partition key, a hashtag query scans the whole table because you did not design for that access pattern.

termDefinitions.meaning: DynamoDB 用来决定数据落在哪个分区的主键字段，决定了哪些查询是单分区秒查。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key decides which partition an item lands in, which in turn decides which queries are fast single-partition lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 托管的 key-value/宽列 NoSQL 数据库，靠 partition/sort key 设计访问模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is AWS's managed key-value/wide-column NoSQL database, designed around partition and sort keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

diagram:
flowchart LR
    Query1["by user_id"] --> Hit["single partition"]
    Query2["by hashtag"] --> Scan["table scan unless indexed"]
optionExplanations: 对，partition key 只加速按它查询的路径；hashtag 查询没被设计进去，只能全表扫。
DynamoDB 不会自动为你没设计的访问模式建索引，得手动加 GSI 才行。
语法本身是合法的，只是没有索引支撑，代价是扫描整张表而不是报错。
分区键查询是单分区秒查，hashtag 查询没有这个优势，速度差距很大。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the partition key only accelerates lookups by that key; a hashtag query wasn't designed for, so it's a full table scan.
DynamoDB doesn't auto-index access patterns you never designed for; you'd need to add a GSI yourself.
The query syntax itself is valid — it's just unindexed, so the cost is a full scan, not a rejection.
A partition-key query is a fast single-partition lookup; a hashtag query has none of that advantage, so the gap is large.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 补全关系型 vs NoSQL 的取向：
q_en: Fill in the relational versus NoSQL design bias.
text: 关系型长于{{强一致}}与复杂查询（SQL、事务、外键约束）；NoSQL 长于{{灵活 schema}} 与不依赖复杂 join 的{{水平扩展}}。
why: 这是数据建模的第一层选型直觉，之后再用具体的访问模式和一致性需求收敛。
why_en: Relational databases favor strong consistency and rich queries, while NoSQL favors flexible schemas and horizontal scaling without joins.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库使用的结构化查询语言，用于表达复杂查询和事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SQL is the structured query language relational databases use for complex queries and transactions.

termDefinitions.meaning: 非关系型数据库的统称，通常牺牲复杂 join 换取灵活 schema 和水平扩展。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NoSQL is an umbrella term for non-relational databases that usually trade complex joins for flexible schemas and horizontal scaling.

tradeoff: 强一致 + 复杂查询 vs 灵活扩展 + 水平扩容

q: users 表 1000 万行，没有索引时按 email 找一个用户意味着？
q_en: On a 10-million-row users table, what does an email lookup mean without an index?
options: 数据库自动建索引
毫秒级返回
全表扫描；建索引后毫秒直达
查询直接报错
options_en: The database automatically creates an index.
It returns in milliseconds.
It scans all ten million rows; once you add an index on email, the database can jump straight to the row in milliseconds.
The query fails outright.
why: 索引的意义就是把「全表扫描」变成「直达」；查询模式里高频出现的字段就是建索引的候选。
why_en: Without an index, finding a user by email scans all ten million rows, while an index lets the database jump straight to the row in milliseconds.
optionExplanations: 数据库不会替你猜访问模式自动建索引，索引要显式声明。
没有索引时反而要扫完全部行，不可能是毫秒级返回。
对，没索引就得扫一千万行；给 email 建了索引后直接跳到目标行，落到毫秒级。
缺索引只是慢，不是语法或权限错误，查询照样能跑完只是很久。
optionExplanations_en: Databases don't guess your access pattern and auto-build an index; you have to declare one explicitly.
Without an index it has to scan every row, so millisecond response is not realistic here.
Right — no index means scanning ten million rows; an index on email lets it jump straight to the row in milliseconds.
Missing an index just makes it slow, not invalid — the query still runs, it just takes a long time.

q: 最常见的索引结构是什么，强在哪？
q_en: What is the most common index structure, and why is it useful?
options: B-tree，数据有序，支持范围查询
布隆过滤器，判断元素可能存在
位图索引，标记低基数字段
全文索引，给关键词搜索分词
options_en: B-tree, keeping data sorted for range queries.
Bloom filter, testing whether an item might exist.
Bitmap index, flagging low-cardinality columns.
Full-text index, tokenizing text for keyword search.
why: B-tree 用有序树同时覆盖「找 email 为 X 的用户」和「查日期 A 到 B 的订单」两类查询，所以成为默认。
why_en: The B-tree keeps data sorted so it supports both exact lookups and range queries, which is why relational databases default to it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据有序存放的树形索引结构，同时支持精确查找和范围查询，是关系库默认索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree keeps data sorted in a tree structure, supporting both exact lookups and range queries; it's the default relational index.

termDefinitions.meaning: 概率型数据结构，能快速判断「一定不存在」或「可能存在」，不能精确定位记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter is a probabilistic structure that quickly says an item definitely doesn't exist or might exist, without locating the row.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用二进制位标记每行是否满足某个值的索引，适合低基数字段。
