termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cache miss means the data is absent from cache and must be fetched from the database.

optionExplanations: 对，热门短码被反复点击，内存缓存能直接命中返回，miss 才回源查库，把大部分读挡在数据库前。
队列适合削峰写入或异步任务，重定向是同步读请求，加个只处理写的队列帮不上这条读路径。
重定向不需要知道用户是谁，登录系统解决的是身份问题，跟查找延迟没关系。
短码到长链是固定映射，请求时重新生成会跟数据库里存的值对不上，直接破坏已发出去的链接。
optionExplanations_en: Right — popular codes get clicked repeatedly, so an in-memory cache answers hits directly and only falls back on a miss.
A queue is for smoothing write bursts or async work; a redirect is a synchronous read, so a write-only queue does not help.
A redirect doesn't need to know who the user is; login solves an identity problem, unrelated to lookup latency.
The code-to-URL mapping is fixed; regenerating it per request would no longer match the stored value, breaking every link out there.

q: 按正确顺序排列一次缓存 miss 的重定向流程：
q_en: Put the redirect flow for a cache miss in the correct order.
steps: 把查到的 short_code -> long_url 映射写回缓存
请求到达 Read Service，先查 Redis/Memcached
缓存未命中，Read Service 查询数据库索引
返回 302 Redirect 到 long_url
why: cache-aside 路径是先查缓存，miss 再查库，随后回填缓存并完成重定向。这样热门短码后续请求会直接命中缓存。
why_en: The cache-aside flow checks cache first, reads the database on a miss, fills the cache, and then redirects.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant R as Read Service
  participant Cache as Cache
  participant DB as DB
  C->>R: GET /{code}
  R->>Cache: get(code)
  Cache-->>R: miss
  R->>DB: lookup(code)
  DB-->>R: long_url
  R->>Cache: set(code, long_url)
  R-->>C: 302 Location
tradeoff: 先查缓存省数据库负载 vs 缓存未命中时多一跳查库延迟

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先查缓存，未命中时再查数据库并回填缓存的模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside means the app checks the cache first and, on a miss, reads the database and fills the cache.

q: 这个量级差距最支持哪条缓存设计判断？
q_en: Which cache design decision is best supported by this order-of-magnitude latency gap?
options: SSD 已经够快，不需要再引入内存缓存
HDD 和内存之间的访问延迟差距完全可以忽略不计
把热点映射放进内存缓存，能带来数量级的读延迟收益
只要把存储全部换成 SSD 就能达到内存缓存的效果
why: 内存比 SSD 快约 1000 倍、比 HDD 快约 10 万倍，这个量级差距正是给热点重定向加内存缓存的理由。
why_en: Memory is roughly 1,000 times faster than SSD and 100,000 times faster than HDD, and that gap is exactly why hot redirects deserve an in-memory cache.
scenario: 内存访问约 100 纳秒，SSD 约 0.1 毫秒，HDD 约 10 毫秒，量级依次拉开。
scenario_en: Memory access is about 100 nanoseconds, SSD is about 0.1 milliseconds, and HDD is about 10 milliseconds.
options_en: SSD is already fast enough, so there's no need to add an in-memory cache.
The latency gap between HDD and memory can be safely treated as negligible.
Putting hot mappings in an in-memory cache buys an order-of-magnitude latency win.
Switching all storage to SSD alone matches what an in-memory cache gives you.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒输入输出操作数，衡量存储设备吞吐能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IOPS is input/output operations per second, a measure of storage throughput.

optionExplanations: SSD 比内存慢了大约 1000 倍，「已经够快」只是相对机械硬盘而言，热点读还是能感受到差距。
内存比 HDD 快了大约 10 万倍，这是数量级差距，说可以忽略不计是完全说反了。
对，内存读取比磁盘存储快了好几个数量级，把高频访问的短码放进内存缓存，延迟收益立竿见影。
SSD 依然比内存慢约 1000 倍，全换 SSD 只是缩小了差距，达不到内存缓存那个量级的收益。
optionExplanations_en: SSD is roughly 1,000 times slower than memory; 'fast enough' only holds relative to a spinning disk — hot reads still feel the gap.
Memory beats HDD by roughly five orders of magnitude; calling that gap negligible has it exactly backwards.
Right — memory is about 1,000x faster than SSD and 100,000x faster than HDD, so caching hot codes buys an order-of-magnitude win.
SSD is still roughly 1,000x slower than memory; switching everything to SSD narrows the gap but never reaches the cache’s order of magnitude.

q: 引入内存缓存后要主动处理哪些问题？（多选）
q_en: Which issues must you actively handle after adding an in-memory cache?
options: 缓存预热，冷启动时 miss 仍会打到数据库
缓存失效，尤其是 URL 过期或删除后不能返回旧 long_url
容量和淘汰策略，如 LRU
所有写入都必须停止
why: 缓存提升读性能，但带来预热、失效、容量和淘汰策略。短链较少更新，失效难度比通用可变数据低，但过期时间必须和 TTL 对齐。
why_en: Caching adds warmup, invalidation, capacity, and eviction concerns even in a mostly read-heavy URL shortener.
options_en: Cache warmup: on a cold start, misses still hit the database.
Invalidation: an expired or deleted URL must not keep returning the old long_url.
Capacity and eviction policy, such as LRU.
All writes must stop.
optionExplanations: 冷启动或节点重启时缓存是空的，这段时间的 miss 会集中打到数据库，得规划预热或容忍这段压力。
URL 一旦过期或被删除，缓存里的旧映射如果不失效，用户会被继续带到一个本该已经失效的地址。
内存有限装不下所有映射，得靠 LRU 这类策略决定谁被淘汰，不然热数据会被冷数据挤出去。
缓存只是加速读路径，写入依然正常落库，跟暂停写入完全是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Cache is empty on a cold start or restart, so misses pile onto the database during that window — plan warmup or absorb the load.
Once a URL lapses or gets deleted, a stale mapping left in cache keeps sending users to an address that should already be dead.
Memory cannot hold every mapping, so a policy like LRU decides who gets evicted, or cold data crowds out the data you need.
Caching only speeds up reads; writes still land in the database normally — nothing like pausing all writes.

scenario: 短链支持 expiration_date，某个 short_code 已经过期，但缓存里还有旧映射。
scenario_en: Short links support expiration_date, and one short_code has already expired while the cache still holds the old mapping.
q: 缓存 TTL 应该如何设置？
q_en: How should the cache TTL be set?
options: 永不过期，大幅减少数据库访问次数
TTL 应等于或短于剩余过期时间
统一设置成一个固定的 10 年
只依赖客户端浏览器本地缓存
why: 缓存项不能活得比 URL 本身更久，否则过期短链仍可能被重定向。TTL 对齐 expiration_date 是最直接的防 stale 策略。
why_en: Cache TTL must not outlive the URL expiration time or expired links can keep redirecting.
whenOtherWins: 如果业务不支持过期或删除，长 TTL 更可接受；如果要求立即撤销，还需要主动失效或版本化。
options_en: Never expire the entry, to drastically cut database access.
TTL should equal or be shorter than the URL's remaining validity window.
Set every TTL to a flat, fixed 10 years.
Only rely on the client's local browser cache.
tradeoff: TTL 越短越新鲜 vs TTL 越长数据库压力越小

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cache entry lives before it must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 缓存活得比 URL 本身还久，过期后仍会命中缓存返回旧映射，白白省了数据库访问却放出了错误结果。
对，TTL 卡在剩余有效期之内，缓存条目最晚跟 URL 同时到期，不会比 URL 本身活得更久。
10 年在实践中等同于永不过期，只是把「放出旧映射」的窗口拉得非常长，问题本质没变。
浏览器缓存只能减少这一个用户的重复请求，服务端缓存里的旧映射照样存在，问题根本没解决。
optionExplanations_en: A cache that outlives the URL keeps serving the stale mapping after it should be gone — saving hits at the cost of wrong answers.
Right — capping TTL at the remaining validity window means the cache entry lapses no later than the URL itself.
10 years is effectively never expiring in practice — it just stretches the 'stale mapping' window very long, same problem.
Browser caching only cuts repeat requests from that one user; the stale server-side cache entry is still there, untouched.

scenario: 用户分布全球，热门短码希望尽量靠近用户完成重定向，减少跨区域往返。
scenario_en: Users are global, and popular short codes should redirect as close to the user as possible to reduce cross-region round trips.
q: 可以引入哪一层优化？
q_en: Which optimization layer can be introduced?
options: CDN 边缘节点直接执行重定向逻辑
只是把数据库磁盘容量调大
让用户手动复制粘贴 long_url
把所有请求都固定发到单一区域主库
why: CDN PoP 可以缓存热门 short_code 映射，edge function 甚至能直接返回 redirect，避免请求回源到 Primary Server。
why_en: A CDN and edge function can serve popular redirects near users without reaching the origin service.
whenOtherWins: 如果用户集中在单区域、延迟目标宽松或成本敏感，应用层缓存可能已经足够，不必先上边缘计算。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    User["Global user"] --> Edge["CDN PoP / Edge function"]
    Edge -->|hit| Redirect["302 near user"]
    Edge -->|miss| Origin["Origin Read Service"]
    Origin --> Store[("origin cache / DB")]
    Origin --> Edge
options_en: A CDN with edge nodes running the redirect logic directly.
Just increase the database's disk capacity.
Have users manually copy and paste the long_url.
Route every request to a single-region primary database.
tradeoff: 边缘就近响应换低延迟 vs 边缘失效/运维复杂度和成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行在 CDN 边缘节点上的代码，能在离用户最近的地方处理请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge function is code that runs on CDN edge nodes, handling requests close to the user.

termDefinitions.meaning: CDN 在某个地理位置部署的边缘接入点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A PoP (point of presence) is a CDN's edge location in a given geographic area.

optionExplanations: 对，把热门映射放到离用户最近的边缘节点，跳转逻辑就地执行完，不用每次都跑一趟回源，省下跨洲往返。
磁盘容量解决的是存不存得下的问题，跟请求要跑多远、跨几个大洲完全是两个维度。
人工复制粘贴牺牲了产品最核心的一键跳转体验，只能算临时补救，不是常规方案。
单一区域主库反而会让所有跨洲用户都得先绕远路打到那一个区域，加剧延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a popular mapping can live at the CDN edge nearest the user, and the edge function redirects before reaching the origin.
Disk capacity is about whether the data fits, an entirely different axis from how far a request travels across continents.
Manual copy-paste throws away the product's core one-click experience — a stopgap, not a real solution.
A single-region primary actually forces every cross-continent user to travel further to reach that one region.

q: CDN/edge redirect 的代价包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: What costs come with CDN or edge redirects?
options: 全局缓存失效和一致性更复杂
边缘函数有执行时间、内存和依赖限制
调试和监控比中心化服务更难
它会让所有短码立刻变长
why: 边缘层用成本和复杂度换延迟：失效、资源限制、观测性和费用都要讨论。它不会改变短码本身长度。
why_en: Edge redirects trade latency for more complex invalidation, runtime limits, monitoring, and cost.
options_en: Global cache invalidation and consistency become more complex.
Edge functions have execution time, memory, and dependency limits.
Debugging and monitoring are harder than with a centralized service.
It makes every short code instantly longer.
optionExplanations: 映射改了或失效了，得让分布在全球的每个边缘节点都同步更新，协调成本比单一数据库高得多。
边缘运行时通常有严格的执行时长、内存上限和可用依赖清单，复杂逻辑塞不进去。
请求分散到几十上百个边缘节点，出问题时定位是哪个节点、哪次部署出的错要费更多工夫。
边缘部署改变的是重定向发生的位置，短码本身的生成方式和长度完全不受影响。
optionExplanations_en: Once a mapping changes or lapses, every edge node scattered worldwide needs that update — far more coordination than one database.
Edge runtimes typically cap execution time, memory, and allowed dependencies, so complex logic just does not fit.
With requests spread across dozens of edge nodes, pinpointing which node and deployment caused an issue takes more digging.
Edge deployment changes where the redirect happens, not how codes are generated or how long they are.

q: 这个存储量级对数据库架构选择意味着什么？
q_en: What does this storage size imply for the database architecture choice?
options: 500GB 已经远远超过单机容量，必须从第一天就做分片
500GB 单实例数据库能轻松容纳，不必一开始就分片
这个量级下必须放弃关系型数据库，全面改用列式存储
存储量级这么大，建索引已经没有意义
why: 500GB 对现代 SSD 和单个数据库实例都不是问题；除非真的碰到硬件瓶颈，否则不必一开始就分片。
why_en: 500 GB is not a problem for a modern SSD or a single database instance, so sharding isn't necessary until a real hardware limit shows up.
scenario: 按每行约 500 bytes 估算，10 亿条短链映射总共约需 500GB 主数据存储。
scenario_en: At about 500 bytes per row, one billion short-link mappings require roughly 500 GB of primary data storage.
options_en: At 500 GB we already exceed single-machine capacity, so sharding is required from day one.
500 GB fits comfortably on a single database instance, so sharding is not needed on day one.
At this scale we must abandon relational databases entirely for columnar storage.
At this scale, indexing no longer makes sense.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据切分到多台机器存储，用来突破单机容量上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across multiple machines to get past a single machine's capacity limit.

optionExplanations: 500GB 对现代硬盘来说只是零头，远远够不上「超过单机容量」，分片在这个阶段是过度设计。
对，500GB 一个数据库实例就能轻松扛住，除非真的碰到实测的硬件瓶颈，不必现在就分片。
500GB 加上事务和索引需求，关系型数据库处理得游刃有余，换列式存储解决的是分析型大宽表场景。
存储量级大反而更需要索引——没有它，十亿行规模下的每次查找都要付出线性扫描的代价。
optionExplanations_en: A 500 GB is a rounding error for a modern disk, nowhere near exceeding single-machine capacity — sharding here is over-engineering.
Right — 500 GB fits comfortably on one database instance; sharding is not needed until you hit an actual hardware limit.
At 500 GB with transactional and indexing needs, a relational database handles this easily; columnar stores solve a different problem.
A larger dataset makes indexing more necessary, not less — without it every lookup across a billion rows pays for a linear scan.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

scenario: 短链系统读流量已由缓存承担，创建新短链每天约 100k，写入吞吐很低。
scenario_en: Reads are handled by cache, and the system creates about 100k new short links per day, so write throughput is low.
q: 数据库选择上最务实的答案是什么？
q_en: What is the most pragmatic database choice here?
options: 只能选 Cassandra，别的数据库都写不了
只能选图数据库来存这份映射
大多数成熟数据库都可以，Postgres 是合理默认
这个场景根本不需要持久化数据库
why: 写入量约 1 row/s，读峰值被缓存分担，Postgres/MySQL/DynamoDB 等都能做。面试里选自己熟悉且能解释 HA/索引/备份的数据库更重要。
why_en: Once reads are cached and writes are low, many databases work, with Postgres being a reasonable default.
whenOtherWins: 如果需求变成极高写入、多区域本地写或弱一致可接受，DynamoDB/Cassandra 这类方案可能更有优势。
options_en: Only Cassandra can handle the writes here.
Only a graph database can store this mapping.
Most mature databases can do this; Postgres is a reasonable default.
This scenario doesn't need a persistent database at all.
tradeoff: 选熟悉的数据库换开发效率 vs 为未来极端写入预留专用数据库

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的开源关系型数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Postgres is a popular open-source relational database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 面向海量写入和多区域场景的宽列存储数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cassandra is a wide-column database built for very high write throughput and multi-region deployments.

optionExplanations: 写入量约 1 row/s 这种低负载下，Cassandra 的高写吞吐能力根本用不上，选它是资源浪费。
图数据库擅长的是多跳关系遍历，这里只是 code 到 URL 的一次性直接查找，用不上图结构。
对，这个负载水平下，几款主流数据库都能扛住，挑一个自己吃得透、能讲清高可用和索引设计的更实际。
映射必须能在重启和故障后还在，缓存只是加速层，不能替代持久化存储。
optionExplanations_en: At roughly 1 row/s of write load, Cassandra's high-write-throughput strength never gets exercised — picking it is overkill.
Graph databases shine at multi-hop relationship traversal; this is a single direct code-to-URL lookup, no graph needed.
Right — with low writes and cached reads, Postgres, MySQL, or DynamoDB all work; pick whichever you can defend HA and backups on.
The mapping has to survive restarts and failures; a cache only speeds things up, it cannot replace durable storage.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重
AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

scenario: 读请求远多于写请求，读路径是 GET /{short_code}，写路径是 POST /urls。
scenario_en: Read requests far outnumber writes: the read path is GET /{short_code}, and the write path is POST /urls.
q: 服务层如何拆分更利于独立扩展？
q_en: How should the service layer be split to scale independently?
options: 把 Read/Write Service 拆开，各自独立扩容
所有请求固定打到同一个实例
只留 Write Service，重定向交给客户端处理
把数据库拆成多张没有索引的表
why: 读写负载差异巨大时，拆分服务可让 redirect path 大规模横向扩展，而写路径保持较小规模并专注短码生成。
why_en: Separating read and write services lets the high-volume redirect path scale independently from the low-volume creation path.
whenOtherWins: 在早期低流量系统里，一个服务更简单；等读写负载和团队运维能力需要时再拆。
options_en: Split Read Service and Write Service apart so each scales independently.
Pin every request to the same single instance.
Keep only the Write Service and let the client handle redirects.
Split the database into multiple tables with no indexes.
tradeoff: 读写分离换独立扩容能力 vs 多一层服务拆分和路由复杂度
optionExplanations: 对，读写负载差几个数量级时，拆开服务能让重定向那条高流量路径单独横向扩容，不必带着写路径一起扩。
单实例扛不住重定向那种高并发读流量，早晚会在某个 QPS 阈值上被打垮。
重定向要查数据库才知道目标地址，客户端手里没有这份映射，做不了这件事。
拆表不解决查找效率问题，没有索引的表无论拆成几张，逐行扫描的代价还在。
optionExplanations_en: Right — with read and write load orders of magnitude apart, splitting the services lets redirects scale on their own.
A single instance cannot absorb redirect-level concurrent reads; it will get overwhelmed past some QPS threshold.
A redirect needs the database to know the target address; the client never holds that mapping, so it cannot do this.
Splitting tables does not fix lookup efficiency — however many pieces, an unindexed table still pays for a row scan.

q: 按正确顺序排列 counter 方案下创建短链的写入流程：
q_en: Put the write flow for creating a short link with the counter approach in the correct order.
steps: Write Service 把 counter 值编码成 Base62 短码
用户提交 long_url 到 POST /urls
Write Service 向 Redis INCR 获取全局唯一 counter
把 short_code、long_url、expiration_date 写入数据库并返回 short_url
why: 写路径先接收请求，再拿全局唯一 ID，编码为短码，最后持久化映射并返回给用户。
why_en: The write path receives the URL, gets a unique counter, encodes it, stores the mapping, and returns the short URL.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant W as Write Service
  participant R as Redis
  participant DB as DB
  C->>W: POST /urls
  W->>R: INCR counter
  R-->>W: next id
  W->>W: base62(id)
  W->>DB: insert mapping
  W-->>C: short_url
tradeoff: 预先批量取号段省网络调用 vs 单次 INCR 实现简单

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is Redis's atomic increment command.

q: 更高级别答案里，counter 方案还应补充哪些生产化细节？（多选）
q_en: Which production-readiness details should a stronger counter-based design include?
options: counter batching：每个 Write Service 申请一批号段，减少 Redis 网络调用
Redis Sentinel/Cluster：避免 counter 服务成为无保护单点
多区域 disjoint counter ranges：各区域本地写，避免跨区域协调
要求所有区域都从 counter=0 开始，方便调试
why: 号段批量、Redis 故障转移、多区域互斥范围是 counter 方案走向生产时的关键补强。所有区域从 0 开始会直接制造重复短码。
why_en: Production counter designs add batching, Redis failover, and disjoint regional ranges to reduce calls and preserve uniqueness.
options_en: Counter batching: each Write Service instance requests a batch of values, cutting Redis network calls.
Redis Sentinel/Cluster: avoids the counter service becoming an unprotected single point of failure.
Disjoint counter ranges per region: each region writes locally, avoiding cross-region coordination.
Require every region to start its counter at 0, for easier debugging.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的高可用方案，主节点故障时自动切换。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis Sentinel and Cluster provide automatic failover when the primary Redis node fails.

optionExplanations: 每次创建都单独找 Redis 要一个号，网络往返成本会随写入量线性增加，批量取一段号省下大部分调用。
counter 全靠单个 Redis 实例发号，它一挂全局创建流程就跟着停摆，加故障转移能补上这个单点。
跨区域每次都回中心节点抢号会拖慢延迟，给各区域分配互不重叠的号段就能各自本地写不用协调。
所有区域从 0 开始等于让不同区域各自独立生成一样的号码，最先落库的映射会互相覆盖或冲突。
optionExplanations_en: Asking Redis for one number per creation makes round trips scale linearly with writes; a batch of values cuts most of that.
If a single Redis instance is the only number source, it going down halts creation entirely; failover closes that single point.
Racing back to one central node for every number adds latency; a non-overlapping range per region lets it write locally.
Starting every region at zero means they would independently generate the same numbers, so mappings collide or overwrite.

scenario: 邮箱有几十万封邮件，搜索匹配到数千封，要把它们批量移动到 newsletter 文件夹。
scenario_en: A mailbox has hundreds of thousands of emails; a search matches several thousand, which must be bulk-moved to the newsletter folder.
q: 这个批量移动 API 该做成同步还是异步？
q_en: Should this bulk-move API be synchronous or asynchronous?
options: 异步：立刻返回 job_id + queued，后台慢慢移动
同步：请求里一次性把几千封邮件都移完再返回
让前端一封一封地串行调用移动接口
不用后端，直接在浏览器里改所有邮件
options_en: Asynchronous: return a job_id + queued immediately and move in the background
Synchronous: move all several-thousand emails within the request before returning
Have the frontend call a move endpoint one email at a time, serially
Skip the backend and change all emails in the browser
optionExplanations: 对：几千封的活儿放后台，API 秒回 job_id，用户不被阻塞、也不会请求超时。
错：同步移几千封会长时间阻塞、极易超时，是坏设计。
错：前端串行调几千次又慢又脆，一断就残缺。
错：移动是服务端数据操作，浏览器改不了、也不安全。
optionExplanations_en: Right: push the several-thousand moves to the background and return a job_id instantly, so the user is not blocked and the request cannot time out.
Wrong: moving thousands synchronously blocks for a long time and easily times out — a bad design.
Wrong: thousands of serial frontend calls are slow and fragile; one drop leaves it half-done.
Wrong: moving is a server-side data operation; the browser cannot and should not do it.
why: 数千封批量移动要异步：POST 只入队并返回 job_id + queued，真正移动交给后台 worker。同步会占住请求线程，几千封一慢就超时。
why_en: Make a several-thousand-email move async: POST returns job_id + queued, and workers do the real moves in the background.
tradeoff: 同步阻塞请求 vs 异步作业可查进度
whenOtherWins: 只有数量很小、能在一次请求超时预算内完成且失败影响可接受时，同步才值得考虑。

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求只负责「登记任务 + 立刻返回 job_id」，实际耗时工作交给后台 worker 慢慢做，客户端事后查进度
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An async job means the request just records the task and returns a job_id immediately; the heavy work runs in background workers and the client polls progress later.

scenario: 为批量移动设计一组 REST 接口：发起、查进度、拉明细。
scenario_en: Design a REST API set for bulk move: kick off, check progress, list details.
q: 这组批量移动接口的合理形态是？
q_en: What is a reasonable shape for this bulk-move API?
options: POST 发起(带 search token+目标文件夹)→{job_id,queued}；GET 查 job 进度；GET job/items 分页拉明细
只用一个同步 POST，一次返回全部移动结果
用 GET 发起移动、把邮件 ID 全塞进 URL 查询串
每封邮件一个独立 endpoint，前端自己拼
options_en: POST to start (search token + destination folder) → {job_id, queued}; GET job progress; GET job/items paginated details
A single synchronous POST that returns all move results at once
Use GET to start the move and stuff all email ids into the query string
One endpoint per email, assembled by the frontend
optionExplanations: 对：一个 POST 发起(返回 job_id)、一个 GET 查进度、一个 GET 分页拉明细——异步三件套。
错：同步返回全部结果就退回阻塞式设计了。
错：GET 不该有副作用，URL 也塞不下几千个 ID。
错：一封一个 endpoint 违背批量的初衷。
optionExplanations_en: Right: one POST to start (returns job_id), one GET for progress, one GET for paginated details — the async trio.
Wrong: returning all results synchronously falls back to the blocking design.
Wrong: GET should be side-effect-free, and a URL cannot hold thousands of ids.
Wrong: one endpoint per email defeats the point of a bulk op.
why: 异步 API 三件套：POST 发起并回 job_id+queued，GET job 查进度，GET job/items 分页拉每封结果。发起有副作用用 POST，查询只读用 GET。
why_en: Use the async trio: POST starts and returns job_id, GET reads progress, and GET job/items pages through per-message results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代表「那批搜索结果」的引用/句柄（不是加密串）：请求只带这个短 token，服务端拿它去查出对应的几千个 message id（从结果表/缓存/重跑查询）。作用是「少传一堆 id + 引用服务端的集合」，不是保密；服务端是「查找」不是「解密」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A reference/handle to the search result set (not an encrypted blob): the request carries this short token and the server looks up the thousands of message ids it points to (from a store/cache/re-run). It is about indirection (avoid sending many ids), not secrecy; the server dereferences it, not decrypts it.

termDefinitions.meaning: HTTP 状态码：请求已受理但还没处理完——异步作业发起后的标准返回
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HTTP 202 Accepted: the request was accepted but not yet completed — the standard return for kicking off an async job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两码事：「谁在操作」由请求头里的鉴权 token(session/JWT)决定、不放 body(放 body 客户端能伪造)；search_result_token 只回答「移哪些邮件」(那批搜索结果)。别拿 user id 当 body token
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two separate things: WHO is acting comes from the auth token in the header (session/JWT), never the body (spoofable); search_result_token only says WHICH emails to move. Do not put a user id as a body token.

termDefinitions.meaning: processed_count=已处理(试过)的条数 = success + fail；success_count=其中成功的；fail_count=失败的。processed 看「进度」(和 total 比判完成)，success/fail 看「结果」
termDefinitions.meaningEn: processed_count = tasks attempted (= success + fail); success_count = those that succeeded; fail_count = those that failed. processed tracks progress (vs total for completion); success/fail track the outcome.

scenario: 批量移动请求刚打到服务端，还没开始建作业。
scenario_en: The bulk-move request just hit the server, before any job is created.
q: 服务端收到请求后，第一件该做的事是什么？
q_en: What is the first thing the server should do on receiving the request?
options: 鉴权：确认这个用户有权移动这些邮件、访问目标文件夹
立刻把几千封邮件全部移动完
先给前端发一封确认邮件
先重建整个搜索索引
options_en: Authorize: verify this user may move these emails and access the destination folder
Immediately move all several-thousand emails
First send the frontend a confirmation email
First rebuild the entire search index
optionExplanations: 对：先鉴权(authn/authz)——用户是谁、有没有权限动这些邮件和目标文件夹，否则是越权漏洞。
错：还没鉴权就动数据，且移动本身要走异步作业。
错：确认邮件不是移动流程该做的事。
错：搜索已给定，不需要在移动前重建索引。
optionExplanations_en: Right: authorize first — who the user is and whether they may touch these emails and the destination folder; otherwise it is a privilege-escalation hole.
Wrong: touching data before authorizing, and the move itself must go async.
Wrong: a confirmation email is not part of the move flow.
Wrong: search is given; no need to rebuild the index before moving.
why: 第一步是鉴权(authentication + authorization)：确认用户是谁，并检查他能移动这些邮件、写入目标文件夹。跳过这步就是越权和数据泄漏。
why_en: Authorize first: confirm the user and verify they may move these emails into the destination folder.
tradeoff: 先鉴权再建作业 vs 未授权先动数据
whenOtherWins: 只有纯公开、无用户归属的数据才可能弱化授权；邮箱邮件是私有数据，不能这样做。

termDefinitions.meaning: 鉴权：确认「已登录的这个用户，有没有权限做这个操作/访问这些资源」；区别于 authn(确认你是谁)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Authorization checks whether the authenticated user is allowed to perform this action / access these resources — distinct from authentication (who you are).

scenario: 邮箱几十万封邮件，搜索匹配到数千封要批量移到某文件夹；画出支撑这个异步批量移动的服务端架构。
scenario_en: A mailbox has hundreds of thousands of emails; a search matches several thousand to bulk-move into a folder — sketch the server architecture for this async bulk move.
q: 哪条链路是这题的合理架构？
q_en: Which is a reasonable architecture for this problem?
options: API 网关→bulk-move 服务(建 job+入队)→队列→worker 池并行移动、逐条回写状态
API 网关→bulk-move 服务→在这一次请求里同步循环把几千封全部移完再返回
API 网关→服务→把几千封打包成一条巨型队列消息→交给单个 worker 全做完
客户端直连数据库、逐条发 SQL 修改→绕过网关和服务层、也不用队列
options_en: API gateway → bulk-move service (create job + enqueue) → queue → worker pool moving in parallel, writing status back
API gateway → bulk-move service → synchronously loop and move all several-thousand within this one request
API gateway → service → pack all several-thousand into one giant queue message handled by a single worker
The client issues SQL row-by-row directly to the DB, bypassing the gateway/service and using no queue
optionExplanations: 对:网关→服务(建 job+入队)→队列→worker 池并行、逐条回写——异步、可水平扩、失败可重试。
错:同步循环几千封会长时间阻塞、请求超时,退回阻塞设计。
错:巨型单消息+单 worker=单点、无并行、失败全丢。
错:客户端直连库、绕过服务层是安全与耦合灾难。
optionExplanations_en: Right: gateway → service (create job + enqueue) → queue → worker pool in parallel, writing status back — async, scalable, retryable.
Wrong: a synchronous loop over thousands blocks and times out — the blocking design again.
Wrong: one giant message + a single worker is a single point, no parallelism, all-or-nothing failure.
Wrong: a client connecting directly to the DB and bypassing the service is a security and coupling disaster.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["client"] --> G["API Gateway"] --> S["bulk-move 服务"]
  S -->|建作业| DB[("job DB\njobs / message / task")]
  S -->|每封一个任务入队| Q["队列"]
  Q --> W["worker 池"]
  W -->|移动 + 更新状态| DB
why: 标准异步批处理架构：client→API 网关→bulk-move 服务，服务把 job 写进库、并把每封邮件的移动任务丢进队列；下游 worker 池并行消费、逐条移动并回写状态。异步、可水平扩、失败可重试。
why_en: A standard async batch architecture: client → API gateway → bulk-move service, which writes the job to the DB and enqueues a move task per email; a downstream worker pool consumes in parallel, moves one by one, and writes back status. Async, horizontally scalable, retryable.

scenario: 批量移动要知道「移哪些邮件」。搜索已由别的服务给出。
scenario_en: Bulk move needs to know which emails to move; search is provided by another service.
q: 「移哪些」用存好的结果集，还是存查询重跑？
q_en: Should "which emails" come from a stored result set or from re-running a stored query?
options: 两种都行：存 search_result_token(结果集快照)，或存查询条件、发起时在服务端重跑
只能把几千个 message id 全部塞进请求体
必须让用户在前端把每封邮件都勾一遍再传上来
直接移动全邮箱，不用管搜索结果
options_en: Either works: store a search_result_token (a snapshot of the set), or store the query and re-run it server-side on kickoff
You must stuff all several-thousand message ids into the request body
The user must tick every email in the frontend and upload them
Just move the whole mailbox and ignore the search result
optionExplanations: 对：token=结果快照(稳定、不随邮箱变)；重跑查询=省存储但结果可能已变。看要不要「所见即所得」。
错：几千个 id 塞请求体又大又脆。
错：手动勾几千封不现实。
错：移全邮箱不是用户要的。
optionExplanations_en: Right: a token is a snapshot (stable, unaffected by mailbox changes); re-running the query saves storage but the set may have changed. Depends on whether you need what-you-saw-is-what-you-get.
Wrong: thousands of ids in the body are bulky and fragile.
Wrong: ticking thousands by hand is unrealistic.
Wrong: moving the whole mailbox is not what the user asked.
why: 两条路：①存 search_result_token——搜索结果的快照，稳定(移动时仍是当初看到的那批)、但要存；②只存查询条件，发起时在服务端重跑——省存储，但邮箱变了结果可能不同。取舍=一致性快照 vs 存储成本。
why_en: Two options: (1) store a search_result_token — a snapshot of the results, stable (you move exactly what you saw) but needs storage; (2) store the query and re-run it server-side on kickoff — cheaper, but the set may differ if the mailbox changed. Trade-off: consistent snapshot vs storage cost.
tradeoff: 存结果集快照(稳定·占存储) vs 存查询重跑(省存储·结果可能变)

scenario: message 表只存每封邮件「当前在哪个文件夹」。
scenario_en: The message table only stores each email's current folder.
q: 为什么还要一张 task 表（每次移动一条记录）？
q_en: Why also keep a task table (one row per move)?
options: 做审计/历史：message 表只有当前快照，task 表能重建「这封为什么到了这个文件夹」
因为 message 表存不下 message_id
为了让搜索更快
因为队列必须有一张同名表
options_en: For audit/history: the message table is only the current snapshot; the task table reconstructs why an email ended up in a folder
Because the message table cannot store message_id
To make search faster
Because the queue requires a same-named table
optionExplanations: 对：message 表=当前状态，看不出历史；task 表逐条记录每次移动(源→目标)，可回溯审计。
错：message 表当然存得下 message_id。
错：task 表跟搜索性能无关。
错：队列不要求这张表。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the message table is current state with no history; the task table records each move (source → destination) for auditability.
Wrong: the message table can of course store message_id.
Wrong: the task table is unrelated to search speed.
Wrong: the queue does not require this table.
why: message 表只回答「现在在哪」；task 表每次移动追加一行，记录源/目标、job、状态和时间，所以能审计和续跑。一次移动仍用事务同时改 message.folder 并标 task done。
why_en: The message table says where the email is now; the task table logs each move, so you can audit and resume safely.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只记录「发生过什么」的追加表；主表存当前状态，审计表存变更历史，用于回溯与合规
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An append-only table recording what happened; the main table holds current state while the audit table holds change history for traceability and compliance.

termDefinitions.term: job 表 vs task 表
termDefinitions.meaning: 两张表、两种粒度：job 表=1 行汇总(total/processed/success/fail + 总状态)；task 表=N 行、每封一条执行记录(状态、源/目标、job_id)。job 的计数是 task 状态的「汇总缓存」，查进度不用扫全 task 表。这跟 job scheduler 的 job / run(execution) 两表是同一套
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Two tables, two granularities: the job table is one summary row (total/processed/success/fail + overall status); the task table is N rows, one per-email execution (status, source/dest, job_id). The job counts are a denormalized cache of task statuses, so progress needs no full task scan — the same job/run(execution) split as a job scheduler.

termDefinitions.meaning: 移了 300/1000 中途停了 → 不新建 job、沿用原 job；task 表里每封的状态区分「已完成/未完成」，只重跑 status≠done 的 700 封。配合幂等 worker(已 done 就跳过)，重投也不会重复移动。这也是为什么必须有 task 表：没有每封状态就没法精确续跑
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Resume: if 300 of 1000 moved and it stopped, reuse the same job — the task table's per-email status separates done from not-done, so only the 700 not-done are re-run; idempotent workers skip already-done ones. This is why the task table is essential: without per-item status you cannot resume precisely.

termDefinitions.term: message 表 vs task 表
termDefinitions.meaning: message 表=邮件的「户口本」:一封邮件一行,存它「现在」在哪个文件夹(状态,移动时原地改)。task 表=移动的「流水账」:每移动一次记一行(从哪→到哪、状态、哪个 job),同一封邮件可能有多行(移过几次)。前者=当前状态,后者=操作历史
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The message table is the email ID card: one row per email holding its current folder (state, updated in place on a move). The task table is the move ledger: one row per move (source→dest, status, job), and one email can have many rows over time. State vs history of operations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 这道题里 message = 一封邮件(email)。邮件系统里 email 的标准叫法就是 message(RFC 822、IMAP)。实体含主题/正文/发件人/current_folder_id;「移动」=改 current_folder_id。注意别和 WhatsApp deck 的 Message(聊天消息)混——同词不同领域。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In this problem message = an email. "Message" is the standard term for an email (RFC 822, IMAP). The entity holds subject/body/sender/current_folder_id; a "move" changes current_folder_id. Do not confuse it with the WhatsApp deck's Message (a chat message) — same word, different domain.

termDefinitions.term: 快照实体 vs 操作记录
termDefinitions.meaning: message 是「快照实体」:只保存当前状态(在哪个文件夹)，改一次覆盖一次，答不出历史。task 是「操作记录/日志」:每次操作追加一行，保留历史，能回答「怎么变成现在这样」。二者是互补的两类表——一个记 what-is，一个记 what-happened，不能互相替代。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: message is a snapshot entity: it stores only current state (which folder), overwritten each change, unable to answer history. task is an operation log: append one row per operation, retaining history, able to answer "how did it become this". They are complementary tables — one records what-is, the other what-happened; neither replaces the other.

termDefinitions.meaning: job=整批操作(一次「移动全部」一行:查询条件、源/目标、total、processed/success/fail、status);task=批里的一个工作单元(一封邮件一条)。一个匹配 1 万封的 job 派生 1 万个 task。job 只存「聚合」(意图+计数+总状态),装不下 1 万个逐封状态;逐封的追踪/重试/续跑/审计全靠 task。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: job = the whole batch operation (one row per "move all": query, source/dest, total, processed/success/fail, status); task = one unit of work within it (one row per email). A job matching 10k emails spawns 10k tasks. The job holds only the aggregate (intent + counters + overall status) and cannot hold 10k per-email statuses; per-email tracking/retry/resume/audit all live on tasks.

termDefinitions.meaning: task(移一封)是原子:改 message.folder + 标 task.done 同事务,全成或全滚。job(整批)不原子、故意做成可续跑:由 N 个原子 task 增量拼成,永不「1 万封一个大事务」。每完成一个 task 就原子递增 job 的 processed/success/fail 计数(幂等守护防重投重复加),服务端在 processed==total 时标 job completed(见卡010)。所以是 task 往上汇总进 job。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The atomic unit is a task (moving one email): change message.folder + mark task.done in one transaction, all-or-nothing. The job (whole batch) is non-atomic and deliberately resumable: built incrementally from N atomic tasks, never "10k in one transaction". Each completed task atomically increments the job's processed/success/fail counter (idempotency-guarded against redelivery double-count), and the server marks the job completed when processed==total (see card 010). So tasks roll up into the job.

scenario: 面试官问：明天要支持批量删除、批量归档等其它批操作，task 表怎么改才通用？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: to also support bulk delete, archive, and other batch ops tomorrow, how should the task table generalize?
q: 怎么把 task 表从「只支持移动」泛化成「任意批操作」？
q_en: How do you generalize the task table from move-only to any batch op?
options: 加 task_type + task_payload：类型定义干什么，payload 放该操作的参数(如源/目标文件夹)
为每种操作各建一张全新的表
把操作类型硬编码进列名
删掉 task 表，改由前端记录操作
options_en: Add task_type + task_payload: the type says what to do, the payload holds that op's params (e.g. source/destination folder)
Create a brand-new table for every operation type
Hard-code the operation type into column names
Drop the task table and let the frontend record operations
optionExplanations: 对：把「移动专属」的源/目标字段收进通用的 task_payload，另加 task_type，一张表支持任意批操作。
错：每操作一张表会表爆炸、worker 也要各写一套。
错：把类型编进列名就是不可扩展的硬编码。
错：审计/执行状态必须在服务端，不能交前端。
optionExplanations_en: Right: fold the move-specific source/destination into a generic task_payload and add a task_type, so one table supports any batch op.
Wrong: a table per operation explodes tables and forces separate worker code.
Wrong: encoding the type into column names is unscalable hard-coding.
Wrong: audit/execution state must live server-side, not in the frontend.
why: task_type 说明 move/delete/archive/label，task_payload 放各自参数。一张 task 表、一套队列和 worker 可服务多种批操作；新增类型只注册 handler，不改老表。
why_en: Use task_type for the operation and task_payload for its arguments, so one task table and worker framework can support many batch actions.
tradeoff: 移动专属字段(简单·不通用) vs task_type+payload(通用·多一层解释)

termDefinitions.meaning: 通用任务建模：一列存「操作类型」，一列(JSON)存该类型的具体参数——一张表/一套 worker 支持多种操作，加新操作只加 type 不改表
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Generic task modeling: one column for the operation type and one (JSON) for that type's params — one table/worker set supports many ops; a new op just adds a type, no schema change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把「要做的操作」数据化:task_type 标明操作种类、payload 装该操作的参数。worker 用 type 查 handler 表分派、从 payload 取参执行——正是命令/策略模式(操作被封装成可入队、可重试、可撤销的对象)。好处:一套队列/worker/重试/续跑框架服务所有操作类型;加操作=注册新 handler,不改框架(OCP)。对比:为每种操作各建表/队列/worker = 重复造轮子。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Turn "the operation to perform" into data: task_type names the operation kind, payload carries its params. The worker looks up a handler by type and executes with the payload — the Command/Strategy pattern (an operation encapsulated as a queueable, retryable object). Benefit: one queue/worker/retry/resume framework serves all operation types; adding one = registering a handler, not editing the framework (OCP). Contrast: a table/queue/worker per operation = reinventing the wheel.

codeSample:
HANDLERS = {"move": move, "delete": delete,
            "archive": archive, "label": label}

def run(task):
    if task.status == "done": return
    handler = HANDLERS[task.task_type]
    with txn:
        handler(task.message, task.payload)
        task.status = "done"
# 新操作 = 新 task_type + handler

scenario: 一次匹配到 1 万封邮件要移动。
scenario_en: 10,000 emails match and must be moved in one job.
q: 队列 + worker 池怎么把这活干完？
q_en: How do the queue and worker pool get this done?
options: 每封邮件建一个任务入队；worker 池各自拉一条、执行移动、回写状态，天然并行+可重试
把 1 万封打包成一条巨型消息，一个 worker 一次做完
每个 worker 各扫全表找自己该做的邮件
不用队列，服务在请求里同步循环 1 万次
options_en: Enqueue one task per email; workers each pull one, do the move, write status back — naturally parallel and retryable
Pack all 10k into one giant message for a single worker to finish
Each worker scans the whole table to find its emails
No queue; the service loops 10k times synchronously in the request
optionExplanations: 对：一封一任务，worker 池并行消费，某条失败只重投那一条，不影响其余。
错：巨型单消息=单点、没并行、失败全丢。
错：各自扫全表既慢又会抢同一封。
错：同步循环 1 万次又回到阻塞设计。
optionExplanations_en: Right: one task per email, workers consume in parallel, and a failed one is redelivered alone without affecting the rest.
Wrong: one giant message is a single point, no parallelism, and one failure loses everything.
Wrong: scanning the whole table each is slow and workers fight over the same email.
Wrong: a synchronous 10k loop returns to the blocking design.
why: 生产者把 1 万封拆成 1 万个单封任务入队，worker 池各拉一条、移动、回写状态。粒度到单封才有并行度，失败也只重试那一封。
why_en: Enqueue one task per email, then let workers move and mark them independently; per-email granularity gives parallelism and isolated retries.
tradeoff: 单封任务可并行重试 vs 巨型任务简单但脆
whenOtherWins: 只有数量很小、单 worker 能很快完成且失败可整体重试时，才可能接受一条批任务。

termDefinitions.meaning: 生产者把任务丢进队列，消费者(worker 池)各自拉取处理；队列在中间削峰、解耦、支持重试
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A producer puts tasks on a queue and consumers (a worker pool) pull and process them; the queue in between smooths spikes, decouples, and enables retries.

scenario: worker 移动一封邮件：既要改它的所在文件夹，又要标这条任务已完成。
scenario_en: A worker moves one email: change its folder and mark the task done.
q: worker 该怎么保证这封邮件的移动不出现「半完成」？
q_en: How should the worker avoid a half-done move for one email?
options: 同一个事务里：改 message 的 current_folder_id + 把该 task 标为 finished，一起提交
先改文件夹，几秒后再单独去标任务，中间不管崩没崩
只标任务完成，别真去改文件夹
每封移动都锁全表，串行做
options_en: In one transaction: change the message current_folder_id AND mark the task finished, committed together
Change the folder, then separately mark the task seconds later, ignoring crashes in between
Only mark the task done without actually changing the folder
Lock the whole table for every move and do them serially
optionExplanations: 对：改文件夹和标任务放同一事务，要么都成、要么都回滚，不会出现「移了但没记」或反之。
错：两步分开，中间崩溃就状态不一致(半完成)。
错：不真移动就没意义。
错：锁全表串行毁掉并行、吞吐崩。
optionExplanations_en: Right: put the folder change and task mark in one transaction — both commit or both roll back, so you never get "moved but not recorded" or vice versa.
Wrong: two separate steps leave inconsistent (half-done) state if it crashes between them.
Wrong: not actually moving is pointless.
Wrong: locking the whole table serializes everything and kills throughput.
why: 单封移动的原子边界是：改 current_folder_id 和标 task finished 同事务提交，崩溃时一起回滚。整批 job 不做大事务，而是靠可信的单封 checkpoint 续跑；否则会重复移或漏掉邮件。
why_en: Make one email the atomic unit: update its folder and mark the task finished in the same transaction, then resume the batch from trusted per-email checkpoints.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一任务执行一次或多次结果相同；这里靠「先查任务状态、已 finished 就跳过」保证重投无害
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means running a task once or many times has the same effect; here, checking task status and skipping if already finished makes redelivery harmless.

termDefinitions.meaning: 要原子的是「一个工作单元」(移一封邮件),不是「整个作业」(移 1 万封)。作业级别故意不原子、而是可续跑:拆成一堆单元原子+幂等的小任务，每完成一单元就落一个可信 checkpoint(task.finished)，崩溃后从未完成处接着做。单元原子是续跑安全的地基，二者不冲突。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: What must be atomic is a work unit (move one email), not the whole job (move 10k). The job is intentionally non-atomic but resumable: split into many atomic+idempotent unit tasks, each committing a trustworthy checkpoint (task.finished), so a crash resumes from where it stopped. Per-unit atomicity is the foundation of safe resume — the two do not conflict.

termDefinitions.meaning: 长作业崩溃/重启后，不从头再来，而是「扫出还没完成的单元、接着做」。前提是每个单元的完成标记(finished)可信——由单元级原子提交保证。再加移动幂等，重投/重试同一单元不会重复生效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: After a crash/restart, a long job does not start over but scans for unfinished units and continues. It requires each unit's finished flag to be trustworthy — guaranteed by per-unit atomic commit. With an idempotent move, redelivering/retrying the same unit has no duplicate effect.

whenOtherWins: 别把整个作业(1 万封)包进一个大事务:会锁全表、长事务、第 1 万封失败就回滚前 9999 封成功、还无法增量前进。正确是「单封原子 + 作业可续跑」:一堆单元原子+幂等的小任务，每单元 checkpoint，从 checkpoint 续跑。
whenOtherWins_en: Do not wrap the whole job (10k emails) in one big transaction: it locks broadly, runs long, and one failure at #10,000 rolls back 9,999 successes with no incremental progress. The right shape is "per-email atomic + job resumable": many atomic+idempotent unit tasks, a checkpoint per unit, resume from the checkpoint.

scenario: 面试官追问：谁把 job 的 status 标成 completed？总不能等 UI 轮询来标。
scenario_en: The interviewer probes: who marks the job status completed? You cannot rely on the UI polling to flip it.
q: job 完成状态该怎么判定和推送？
q_en: How should job completion be detected and delivered?
options: 服务端在 processed==total 时自己标 completed，并用 SSE/WebSocket 推给 UI
等 UI 每次轮询时顺便帮忙把 job 标成 completed
让每个 worker 都直接去改 job 的最终状态
永远靠前端每秒轮询数据库来判断
options_en: The server marks completed when processed==total, and pushes to the UI via SSE/WebSocket
Let the UI flip the job to completed whenever it happens to poll
Have every worker directly set the job's final status
Rely forever on the frontend polling the DB every second
optionExplanations: 对：计数更新后由服务端判定完成，再把结果通知 UI。
错：UI 不轮询时 job 就永远不完成，状态机放错层。
错：多个 worker 抢改最终状态，容易竞态和重复收尾。
错：前端可以读状态，但不能自己判定并写完成。
optionExplanations_en: Right: after counters update, the server decides completion and notifies the UI.
Wrong: if the UI stops polling, the job would never complete; the state machine is in the wrong layer.
Wrong: many workers racing to set final status creates races and duplicate finalization.
Wrong: the frontend may read status, but it must not decide and write completion.
why: 完成判定必须在服务端：worker 每完成一条原子 processed++，processed==total 时标 completed。UI 只读这个状态；短命作业可轮询，低延迟单向通知用 SSE，需要双向再用 WebSocket。
why_en: Completion belongs on the server: workers increment processed atomically, and the server marks completed when processed equals total.
tradeoff: 服务端权威状态机 vs 前端猜测完成
whenOtherWins: 若量很小、无实时性要求，UI 用短轮询读取服务端状态即可；但完成判定仍不能交给前端。

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端经一条长连接单向推送给客户端；作业完成时推一条通知，比前端反复轮询省且实时
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Server-Sent Events push updates server→client over one long-lived connection; pushing a completion event beats repeated frontend polling.

termDefinitions.meaning: SSE(Server-Sent Events)=服务器→客户端的单向推送，走纯 HTTP、自带断线重连、轻。WebSocket=全双工双向、需 upgrade 握手、更重。进度/通知这种单向场景 SSE 更贴;只有还需要 client→server 走同一通道(如同连接取消 job)或高频双向时，WebSocket 才有价值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: SSE (Server-Sent Events) is one-way server→client push over plain HTTP with built-in auto-reconnect, lightweight. WebSocket is full-duplex bidirectional, needs an upgrade handshake, heavier. For one-way progress/notifications SSE fits better; WebSocket only pays off when you also need client→server on the same channel (e.g. cancel over the same connection) or high-frequency two-way.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对短命作业，轮询(GET /jobs/{id} 每 1-2s)常是更好默认:无持久连接、无状态、任意服务器都能答。而 push(SSE/WS)有隐藏成本——持连接的那台必须正好知道该 job 进度，否则要加 pub/sub 把完成事件路由过去(即多机路由问题)。轮询绕开这一切;缺点(空轮询浪费+一个间隔延迟)对盯进度条的人可忽略。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: For short-lived jobs, polling (GET /jobs/{id} every 1-2s) is often the better default: no persistent connection, stateless, any server can answer. Push (SSE/WS) has a hidden cost — the server holding the connection must know that job's progress, else you need pub/sub to route the completion event there (the multi-server routing problem). Polling avoids all of it; its downsides (empty polls, one-interval latency) are negligible for someone watching a progress bar.

scenario: 面试官问：UI 想要一份「哪些成功、哪些失败」的报告，量还很大，甚至要 CSV/PDF。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: the UI wants a report of which succeeded/failed — large, possibly as CSV/PDF.
q: 这份报告该怎么给？
q_en: How should this report be delivered?
options: 明细用分页 GET(cursor)从 task 表拉；CSV/PDF 走异步导出到 S3 给下载链接；且报告在 job 完成时生成一次
一次性把几万条明细全塞进一个响应返回
每次 UI 请求就重新现算一份 CSV
把报告塞进 job 状态接口的一个字段里返回
options_en: Paginate details with GET (cursor) from the task table; export CSV/PDF asynchronously to S3 with a download link; and generate the report once at job completion
Return all tens-of-thousands of rows in one response
Regenerate a fresh CSV on every UI request
Stuff the report into a field of the job-status endpoint
optionExplanations: 对：明细分页(cursor)拉、文件走异步导出到 S3 返回 URI、且在 job 完成时生成一次报告——UI 多次取也不重算。
错：几万条一次返回会撑爆响应。
错：每次请求现算=重复生成、浪费。
错：大报告塞进状态字段既臃肿又不该。
optionExplanations_en: Right: paginate details (cursor), export files asynchronously to S3 returning a URI, and generate the report once at job completion so repeated fetches do not recompute.
Wrong: returning tens of thousands of rows at once blows up the response.
Wrong: recomputing on every request wastes work.
Wrong: a big report does not belong in a status field.
why: 明细用 cursor 分页从 task 表拉；大 CSV/PDF 走后台导出到 S3 并返回下载链接。报告在 job 完成时生成一次，UI 之后只取现成文件，不每次重算。
why_en: Page details from the task table, export big CSV/PDF files asynchronously to S3, and generate the report once when the job completes.
tradeoff: 分页/异步导出可扩展 vs 一次性大响应或反复现算
whenOtherWins: 只有结果很小、只在当前页面展示时，状态接口里带少量摘要才合理；大明细和文件仍要分页或导出。

termDefinitions.meaning: 用「上一页末尾的位置(cursor)」取下一页，适合大列表稳定翻页；比 offset 在数据变动时更稳
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor pagination fetches the next page from the last item's position — stable for large, changing lists, unlike offset.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大文件(CSV/PDF)不在请求里现生成，而是后台作业生成后存对象存储(S3)、返回下载链接
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Async export generates a large file (CSV/PDF) in a background job, stores it in object storage (S3), and returns a download link.

scenario: worker 从队列拿到一个「把 msg 移到目标文件夹」的任务。
scenario_en: A worker pulls a "move msg to destination folder" task from the queue.
q: 哪段代码正确地完成一次移动？
q_en: Which snippet correctly performs one move?
options: BEGIN; UPDATE message SET folder=? WHERE id=?; UPDATE task SET status=done WHERE id=?; COMMIT;
UPDATE message SET folder=? WHERE id=?;  然后另一个连接里 UPDATE task SET status=done;
UPDATE task SET status=done WHERE id=?;  -- 只标完成，不改文件夹
DELETE FROM message WHERE id=?;  -- 删掉而不是移动
options_en: BEGIN; UPDATE message SET folder=? WHERE id=?; UPDATE task SET status=done WHERE id=?; COMMIT;
UPDATE message SET folder=?; then in a separate connection UPDATE task SET status=done;
UPDATE task SET status=done WHERE id=?;  -- only mark done, do not change folder
DELETE FROM message WHERE id=?;  -- delete instead of move
optionExplanations: 对：改文件夹 + 标任务在同一事务，要么全成要么全回滚，不会半完成。
错：两次独立提交，崩在中间就状态不一致。
错：没真移动，只标了完成。
错：移动是改 folder，不是删除邮件。
optionExplanations_en: Right: folder change + task mark in one transaction — all or nothing, no half-done state.
Wrong: two independent commits leave inconsistency if it crashes between them.
Wrong: nothing is actually moved, only marked done.
Wrong: moving means changing the folder, not deleting the email.
why: 移动 = 改 message.folder + 标 task done，必须放在同一个数据库事务里。两步要么都提交、要么都回滚，才不会「移了没记」或「记了没移」。
why_en: Change the folder and mark the task done in one transaction, so both writes commit or both roll back.
tradeoff: 单事务一致性 vs 分开提交留下半完成
whenOtherWins: 如果只是最终一致的统计或日志，可以异步补写；但这里 task.done 会驱动续跑，不能和移动分开提交。

termDefinitions.meaning: BEGIN…COMMIT 包起来的一组写，具备原子性：全部成功或全部回滚，中间崩溃不留半成品
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A transaction (BEGIN…COMMIT) groups writes atomically: all succeed or all roll back, so a crash leaves no half-done state.

scenario: 队列是 at-least-once：同一个移动任务可能被重投两次。
scenario_en: The queue is at-least-once: the same move task may be redelivered twice.
q: 哪段 worker 逻辑对「重复投递」是安全的？
q_en: Which worker logic is safe against duplicate delivery?
options:
if task.status==done: return   # 幂等：已做过就跳过
  with txn: move(msg); mark_done(task)
move(msg); mark_done(task)     # 不查状态，来一次做一次
for _ in range(3): move(msg)   # 保险起见移三遍
mark_done(task)                # 直接标完成，不移动
options_en:
if task.status==done: return   # idempotent: skip if already done
  with txn: move(msg); mark_done(task)
move(msg); mark_done(task)     # no status check, act on every delivery
for _ in range(3): move(msg)   # move three times to be safe
mark_done(task)                # just mark done, no move
optionExplanations: 对：先查状态、已完成就跳过，重投也无害（幂等）；否则在事务里移动+标完成。
错：不查状态，重投会把同一封重复处理。
错：故意移三遍更糟，纯属重复。
错：不移动只标完成，等于没干活。
optionExplanations_en: Right: check status first and skip if done (idempotent), so redelivery is harmless; otherwise move + mark done in a transaction.
Wrong: no check means redelivery reprocesses the same email.
Wrong: moving three times is deliberately worse.
Wrong: marking done without moving does no real work.
why: at-least-once 队列可能重投同一 task，所以 worker 先查状态：done 就返回，否则事务里移动并标 done。这样重复投递只会变成 no-op。
why_en: With at-least-once delivery, check task status first; done tasks return, and unfinished tasks move and mark done in one transaction.
tradeoff: 幂等消费可重投 vs 假设队列只投一次
whenOtherWins: 只有队列和存储都能严格 exactly-once 且成本可接受时，才可能少做幂等检查；常规队列不要赌这一点。

termDefinitions.meaning: 队列的投递语义：保证不丢，但可能重复投递，所以消费者必须幂等
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An at-least-once queue never drops a message but may redeliver it, so consumers must be idempotent.

scenario: 几十个 worker 并发地把 job 的 processed_count 各自 +1。
scenario_en: Dozens of workers concurrently each increment the job processed_count by 1.
q: 哪种计数更新不会漏计（无并发竞态）？
q_en: Which counter update avoids lost increments (no race)?
options: UPDATE jobs SET processed_count = processed_count + 1 WHERE job_id=?   -- 或 Redis INCR
c = SELECT processed_count; c = c + 1; UPDATE jobs SET processed_count = c   -- 读改写
每个 worker 存自己的局部计数，永不合并
让前端每次轮询时自己重新数一遍
options_en: UPDATE jobs SET processed_count = processed_count + 1 WHERE job_id=?   -- or Redis INCR
c = SELECT processed_count; c = c + 1; UPDATE jobs SET processed_count = c   -- read-modify-write
Each worker keeps its own local count, never merged
Let the frontend re-count on every poll
optionExplanations: 对：数据库自己执行 +1（或 Redis INCR），多个 worker 同时来也是原子写。
错：读改写窗口会让后提交覆盖先提交，少算一次。
错：局部计数永不合并，job 永远数不全。
错：前端重数是聚合压力，且不是权威计数。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the DB does the +1 (or Redis INCR), so concurrent workers still get atomic writes.
Wrong: read-modify-write lets a later commit overwrite an earlier one, losing one increment.
Wrong: local counts never merged means the job is never fully counted.
Wrong: re-counting in the frontend is aggregation load and not authoritative.
why: 并发自增要让存储层原子执行：`processed_count = processed_count + 1` 或 Redis `INCR` 都是一条写。读出来再加再写会让并发 worker 覆盖彼此，造成 lost update。
why_en: Concurrent counters need an atomic storage-side increment; read-modify-write can overwrite another worker and lose an update.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个并发的「读-改-写」都基于同一旧值，后写的覆盖前写的，导致一次更新丢失
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update: two concurrent read-modify-write ops start from the same old value and one overwrites the other, losing an update.

scenario: 复盘这题的 API/设计层。
scenario_en: Reviewing this problem at the API/design level.
q: 下面哪些是这题常见的「设计」错误？（多选）
q_en: Which are common design-level mistakes here? (multi-select)
options: 同步 API：在请求里把几千封移完再返回
靠前端轮询顺便把 job 标成 completed
每次 UI 要报告就现算一份，不缓存
提供一个 GET 接口查 job 进度
options_en: A synchronous API that moves all thousands within the request
Relying on frontend polling to flip the job to completed
Recomputing the report on every UI request, uncached
Providing a GET endpoint to check job progress
optionExplanations: 错误：同步移几千封会阻塞、超时——该异步作业。
错误：完成判定放在服务端(processed==total)，不能等 UI 轮询来标。
错误：报告应在 job 完成时生成一次，UI 反复取现成的。
这是对的：查进度就该有个 GET 接口，不是错误。
optionExplanations_en: Mistake: moving thousands synchronously blocks and times out — should be an async job.
Mistake: completion is decided server-side (processed==total), not flipped by UI polling.
Mistake: the report should be generated once at completion and re-served, not recomputed.
This is correct: a GET progress endpoint is right, not a mistake.
why: 设计层三个坑是同步阻塞、前端判完成、报告反复现算。正解是异步作业、服务端判定完成、报告完成时生成一次；GET 查进度本身没错。
why_en: The design fixes are async jobs, server-owned completion, and one-time report generation; a GET progress endpoint is fine.
tradeoff: 服务端异步流程 vs 前端/同步请求硬扛

scenario: 复盘这题的服务端架构层。
scenario_en: Reviewing this problem at the server-architecture level.
q: 下面哪些是这题常见的「架构」错误？（多选）
q_en: Which are common architecture-level mistakes here? (multi-select)
options: 不要队列，服务在请求里同步循环几千次
把几千封打包成一条巨型消息，一个 worker 做完
让客户端直连数据库、自己发 SQL 移动
用 worker 池并行消费队列、逐条移动
options_en: No queue; the service loops thousands of times synchronously in the request
Pack all thousands into one giant message for a single worker
Let the client connect directly to the DB and issue SQL
Use a worker pool to consume the queue in parallel, moving one by one
optionExplanations: 错误：没队列的同步循环就是阻塞设计。
错误：巨型单消息=单点、无并行、失败全丢。
错误：客户端直连库是安全与耦合灾难。
这是对的：队列+worker 池并行消费才是正解。
optionExplanations_en: Mistake: a synchronous loop with no queue is the blocking design.
Mistake: one giant message is a single point, no parallelism, all-or-nothing failure.
Mistake: a client connecting directly to the DB is a security and coupling disaster.
This is correct: a queue + worker pool consuming in parallel is the right answer.
why: 架构层三个坑是无队列同步循环、巨型单消息、客户端直连数据库。正解是网关→服务→队列→worker 池，单条消费、单条重试。
why_en: The architecture fix is gateway to service to queue to worker pool, with per-item processing and per-item retry.
tradeoff: 队列+worker 池可扩展 vs 同步/单点/直连库

scenario: 复盘这题的数据模型层。
scenario_en: Reviewing this problem at the data-model level.
q: 下面哪些是这题常见的「数据模型」错误？（多选）
q_en: Which are common data-model-level mistakes here? (multi-select)
options: 不建 task 表，只靠 message 表的当前状态
task 表死绑 source/destination 文件夹，无法泛化
job 表没有 total_count，无法判定何时完成
用 task_type + payload 让任务模型通用
options_en: No task table, relying only on the message table current state
A task table hard-bound to source/destination folder, not generalizable
A job table with no total_count, so completion cannot be detected
Using task_type + payload to make the task model generic
optionExplanations: 错误：没 task 表就没有历史，无法审计「为什么这封在这个文件夹」。
错误：死绑移动字段就没法扩到批删除/归档等操作。
错误：没 total_count 就无法判断 processed==total，判不了完成。
这是对的：task_type + payload 正是让它通用的正解。
optionExplanations_en: Mistake: no task table means no history and no audit of "why is this email here".
Mistake: hard-bound move fields cannot extend to bulk delete/archive, etc.
Mistake: no total_count means you cannot check processed==total to detect completion.
This is correct: task_type + payload is exactly what makes it generic.
why: 数据模型的核心是两层：task 记录逐封历史和执行状态，job 存 total_count 等聚合。task_type/payload 让同一套执行框架继续扩到删除、归档、打标签。
why_en: Model it in two layers: tasks keep per-message execution history, jobs keep aggregate counts, and task_type/payload generalizes the worker framework.
tradeoff: 可审计通用模型 vs 只存当前状态的短路设计

scenario: 面试里被追问「这个接口该返回什么状态码」，要答得准。
scenario_en: In an interview you are asked what status code an endpoint should return, and you need it right.
q: 关于 HTTP 状态码，下面哪个说法正确？
q_en: Which statement about HTTP status codes is correct?
options: 401=未认证、403=有身份但无权限、202=异步已受理、429=被限流
2xx 表示客户端出错，4xx 表示请求成功，正好这样对应
404 表示服务器内部错误，500 表示请求的资源不存在
301 表示请求成功，500 表示重定向到新地址
options_en: 401 = unauthenticated, 403 = authenticated but not allowed, 202 = accepted (async), 429 = rate limited
2xx means the client erred and 4xx means success — exactly that mapping
404 means an internal server error and 500 means the resource does not exist
301 means the request succeeded and 500 means redirect to a new address
optionExplanations: 对：401 是没认证/没登录，403 是登录了但无权限；202 是异步已受理；429 是限流。
错：反了——2xx 是成功，4xx 才是客户端错误。
错：反了——404 是找不到资源，500 才是服务器内部错误。
错：301 是永久重定向、500 是服务器错误，都不是成功。
optionExplanations_en: Right: 401 is unauthenticated, 403 is authenticated-but-forbidden; 202 is accepted async; 429 is rate limited.
Wrong: reversed — 2xx is success, 4xx is the client error.
Wrong: reversed — 404 is not found, 500 is the internal server error.
Wrong: 301 is a permanent redirect and 500 is a server error; neither is success.
why: 四大组记牢：2xx 成功、3xx 重定向、4xx 客户端错、5xx 服务端错。面试高频区分：401(未认证)vs 403(无权限)、202(异步已受理)、429(限流)、502/503/504(网关坏响应/不可用/超时)。
why_en: Memorize four families: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error. High-frequency distinctions: 401 (unauthenticated) vs 403 (forbidden), 202 (accepted async), 429 (rate limited), 502/503/504 (bad gateway / unavailable / timeout).

termDefinitions.meaning: 401 Unauthorized=没认证(你没登录/身份没验证)；403 Forbidden=认证过了但没权限。口诀：401 不知道你是谁，403 知道你是谁但不让
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 401 Unauthorized = not authenticated (not logged in); 403 Forbidden = authenticated but not allowed. Mnemonic: 401 = who are you, 403 = I know you but no.

termDefinitions.meaning: 4xx=客户端的错(请求有问题，重发同样的还会错)；5xx=服务端的错(请求没问题，是服务器崩了，可重试)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 4xx = the client's fault (the request is bad; retrying the same fails); 5xx = the server's fault (the request was fine; the server broke, retry may help).

termDefinitions.meaning: 301 永久移动(改域名、永久换 URL——浏览器/搜索引擎会缓存并更新链接)；302 临时(维护页、登录跳转、短链——短链用 302 是为了每次点都回服务端计数、且目标可改)；304 未改(条件请求 If-None-Match/If-Modified-Since，没变就用本地缓存、不回 body 省流量)
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 301 permanent (domain change / permanent URL move — browsers cache and update links); 302 temporary (maintenance, login redirect, URL shorteners — 302 so each click hits the server for counting and the target stays editable); 304 Not Modified (conditional GET; unchanged → use local cache, no body).

termDefinitions.meaning: 请求与资源当前状态冲突：①重复创建(注册一个已被占用的邮箱)②乐观并发版本不匹配(你要改，但别人先改了)③非法状态转换(取消一个已发货的订单)。请求本身合法，只是跟现状打架
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 409 Conflict: the request clashes with current state — duplicate create (registering a taken email), optimistic-concurrency version mismatch (someone updated it first), or an invalid state transition (cancelling an already-shipped order). The request is valid but conflicts with reality.

termDefinitions.meaning: 500=应用自己崩了(代码 bug/未捕获异常)；502=网关从上游拿到「坏响应」(上游崩了/返回垃圾)；503=服务暂时不可用(过载/维护，可 Retry-After)；504=网关等上游「超时」(上游太慢没回)。502 是上游答了但答坏了，504 是上游根本没按时答
termDefinitions.meaningEn: 500 = the app itself errored (bug/unhandled exception); 502 = a gateway got a bad response from upstream (upstream crashed/garbage); 503 = temporarily unavailable (overload/maintenance); 504 = a gateway timed out waiting for upstream. 502 = upstream answered badly; 504 = upstream did not answer in time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 状态码是给「客户端软件」按程序反应用的(5xx/429→退避重试、401→跳登录)、也给开发/运维 debug 定位哪层挂了；终端用户只看到 app 翻译后的友好提示(「稍后再试」)，不看原始码。500 vs 502 vs 504 的细分主要给运维排障
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Status codes are for client software to react programmatically (5xx/429 → back off & retry, 401 → re-auth) and for devs/ops to debug which layer failed; the end user sees a friendly translation. The fine 500/502/504 split is mainly for ops diagnosis.

q: CamelCamelCamel 这个系统的核心业务是什么？
q_en: What is CamelCamelCamel's core business?
options: 跨零售商比价搜索引擎
Amazon 官方价格 API
跟踪 Amazon 价格历史并做降价提醒
电商商品推荐系统
why: 它持续监控 Amazon 商品价格，用户设阈值后价格跌破即收到通知；100 万用户的 Chrome 插件还能直接在商品页显示历史价并一键订阅。
why_en: CamelCamelCamel tracks Amazon product prices over time and alerts users when a price drops below their chosen threshold, backed by a Chrome extension with a million users.
options_en: A price-comparison search engine across multiple retailers.
Amazon's own official price API.
A service that tracks Amazon price history and sends drop alerts.
A general e-commerce product recommendation engine.

termDefinitions.meaning: 运行在浏览器里的小程序，可以读取当前网页内容并上报数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Chrome extension is a small program that runs inside the browser and can read the current page and report data back.

optionExplanations: 这想的是跨站比价，CamelCamelCamel 只盯 Amazon 一家，不比价其他零售商。
Amazon 从没开放过官方价格接口，这个前提本身就不成立。
对，它记录 Amazon 商品的历史价格，跌破用户设的线就提醒。
推荐系统是猜你想买什么，这里要做的是记录某个商品自己的价格走势。
optionExplanations_en: That's cross-retailer price comparison — CamelCamelCamel only watches Amazon, not other stores.
Amazon has never offered an official price API, so this premise doesn't hold.
Right — it logs an Amazon product's price history and alerts once it drops below a user's threshold.
A recommendation engine suggests items to buy; this service instead tracks one product's own price over time.

q: 本题的两条核心功能需求是哪两条？（多选）
q_en: Which two are the core functional requirements for this problem? (multi-select)
options: 查看 Amazon 商品的价格历史
站内搜索和发现商品
订阅带价格阈值的降价通知
跨多家零售商做价格对比
why: 核心功能只有两条：看价格历史、订阅带阈值的降价提醒。站内搜索发现和跨零售商比价都被明确划到范围之外。
why_en: The two core functional requirements are viewing price history and subscribing to threshold-based price-drop alerts, while search and cross-retailer comparison are out of scope.
options_en: View price history for an Amazon product.
Search for and discover products on the site.
Subscribe to a price-drop alert with a threshold.
Compare prices across multiple retailers.
optionExplanations: 这是两条核心功能之一：用户要能拉出商品的历史价格走势。
站内搜索发现是这版明确排除的功能，不用为它设计。
这是另一条核心功能：价格跌破用户定的心理价位就触发提醒。
跨零售商比价同样被排除，这题的边界就是 Amazon 一家。
optionExplanations_en: This is one of the two core features: let users pull up a product's price history.
In-site search and discovery is explicitly out of scope for this version.
The other core feature: fire a drop alert once price crosses the line a user set.
Cross-retailer price comparison is also out of scope — this system only watches Amazon.

q: CamelCamelCamel 的核心非功能需求包括以下哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are CamelCamelCamel's core non-functional requirements? (multi-select)
options: 优先可用性，接受最终一致
价格历史查询延迟低于 500ms
价格数据必须强一致
亚分钟级的实时价格更新
why: 核心 NFR：可用性优先（最终一致）、支撑 5 亿商品、历史查询 <500ms、变价后 1 小时内通知。强一致和亚分钟实时更新被明确排除。
why_en: The core non-functional requirements are availability over strong consistency and sub-500-millisecond history queries, while strong consistency and sub-minute updates are explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Prioritize availability and accept eventual consistency.
Price history queries return in under 500 milliseconds.
Price data must be strongly consistent.
Prices update in near real time, under a minute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短暂看到旧数据是允许的，系统最终会收敛到最新值。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means a read may briefly return stale data after a write, but the system converges to the latest value over time.

optionExplanations: 对，系统接受短暂陈旧，换来可用性优先的设计空间。
对，图表查询要控制在 500 毫秒内，这条直接排除现场全量聚合。
强一致会逼着写路径上分布式事务，这题的 NFR 明确不要这个代价。
亚分钟级实时更新的成本很高，题面只要求变价后 1 小时内通知，用不着这么快。
optionExplanations_en: Right — the system accepts brief staleness in exchange for prioritizing availability.
Right — chart queries must stay under 500ms, which rules out scanning raw points live.
Strong consistency would force distributed transactions on the write path — this NFR explicitly avoids that cost.
Sub-minute real-time updates are expensive to guarantee; the requirement only asks for delivery within an hour.

scenario: 面试官告诉你 CamelCamelCamel 要覆盖 Amazon 全站约 5 亿个商品，而且这是持续运行的目标规模，不是一次性上限。
scenario_en: The interviewer tells you CamelCamelCamel must cover roughly 500 million products across all of Amazon, and this is an ongoing steady-state target, not a one-time cap.
q: 这个商品规模量级，对整体架构提出的最直接要求是什么？
q_en: What does this product-scale order of magnitude most directly require of the overall architecture?
options: 只要把数据库服务器换成更贵机型就够了
采集和存储都必须支持水平扩展与按优先级分层
数量级不影响架构设计，先做完功能再说
商品越多，越应该优先做前端渲染优化
why: 5 亿商品让单机爬虫和单库存储都撑不住，逼出后面的分层爬取和存储拆分设计；数字本身不必死记，它改变的架构选择才是重点。
why_en: Half a billion products rules out a single crawler or a single database, which is exactly why the design needs tiered crawling and split storage.
options_en: Just upgrading to a bigger database server is enough.
Both collection and storage must scale horizontally with tiered priority.
The scale does not change the architecture; ship features first.
More products just means the frontend rendering needs work.
optionExplanations: 换更贵的机器只是垂直扩容，撑不住 5 亿商品这种量级的持续增长。
对，采集和存储都得能水平扩展，还要按优先级分层，单机单库顶不住。
规模恰恰是这道题最重要的约束，它逼出后面分层爬取和存储拆分的每个决定。
前端渲染优化解决不了后端采集和存储撑不住 5 亿商品的问题。
optionExplanations_en: A bigger single machine is only vertical scaling — it can't absorb continuous growth at this scale.
Right — both crawling and storage need horizontal scale plus priority tiers; one machine or one database can't hold up.
Scale is exactly the constraint driving every later decision, from tiered crawling to storage splits.
Frontend rendering tweaks don't fix a backend that can't collect or store 500 million products.

scenario: 非功能需求写明：价格跌破阈值后，通知必须在 1 小时内送达用户。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirements state that once a price drops below a user's threshold, the notification must reach them within one hour.
q: 这条 1 小时 SLA，直接排除了下面哪种通知实现方式？
q_en: Which notification implementation does this one-hour SLA directly rule out?
options: 每 2 小时跑一次的批量轮询 cron
价格变化时发布事件的实时管道
秒级消费事件的 Kafka 订阅者
变价后几分钟内触发的 webhook
why: 1 小时是给定 SLA，不是估算结果；2 小时 cron 的最坏等待约 2 小时，已经超过通知窗口。所以纯批量轮询被排除，通知链路要在变价时触发事件。
why_en: The one-hour SLA is a fixed target, and a two-hour cron can wait about two hours before notifying, so the alert path needs event-triggered processing.
options_en: A batch cron job that scans for changes every two hours.
A real-time pipeline that publishes an event on every price change.
A Kafka consumer that processes events within seconds.
A webhook fired within a few minutes of a price change.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务承诺的量化指标，比如「1 小时内送达通知」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An SLA is a quantified service commitment, such as delivering a notification within one hour.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定时间表周期性触发任务的调度器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cron is a scheduler that triggers a job on a fixed recurring schedule.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定间隔扫描一批数据，找出期间发生的变化。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Batch polling scans a batch of records on a fixed interval to find changes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 状态变化发生时立即发布事件，让下游消费者异步处理。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Event-driven design publishes an event when state changes and lets downstream consumers react asynchronously.

termDefinitions.meaning: 事件发生时由服务端主动向指定地址发一次 HTTP 回调。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A webhook is an HTTP callback the server fires to a configured URL the moment an event happens.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个分布式消息队列，用来在服务之间可靠地传递事件流。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed message queue used to reliably stream events between services.

optionExplanations: 对，2 小时轮询的最坏延迟约 2 小时，已经超过 1 小时窗口，被直接排除。
变价即发事件的实时管道最坏延迟是秒级到分钟级，不会撞线。
Kafka 订阅者秒级消费事件，延迟远低于 1 小时，能满足 SLA。
webhook 几分钟内触发同样在窗口内，不是被排除的那个。
optionExplanations_en: Right — worst-case wait for a 2-hour cron is about 2 hours, already past the 1-hour window, so it's ruled out.
An event-driven pipeline fires on change, with worst-case latency in seconds to minutes — well inside the window.
A Kafka subscriber consumes events in seconds, far under the 1-hour SLA.
A webhook firing within minutes of a price change also stays inside the window, so it isn't the excluded option.

scenario: 非功能需求写明：价格历史图表查询延迟必须低于 500ms，即使商品已经积累了几年的价格点。
scenario_en: The non-functional requirements state that price-history chart queries must stay under 500 milliseconds, even for products with years of accumulated price points.
q: 这条 500ms 延迟要求，最直接排除了下面哪种查询方式？
q_en: Which query approach does this 500ms latency requirement most directly rule out?
options: 每次请求现场扫描全部原始价格点做聚合
查预先算好的日/周/月聚合表
用 TimescaleDB 的 time_bucket 实时聚合
命中 Redis 里缓存好的图表数据
why: 500ms 是给定查询 SLO，不是推导值；热门商品几年价格点可达数千级。请求时现场聚合会把 CPU/IO 压到读路径上，所以要预聚合或时序库。
why_en: The 500 ms target is a read SLO, so chart requests should hit precomputed or time-series aggregates instead of scanning years of raw points.
options_en: Scanning and aggregating every raw price point on each request.
Reading a precomputed daily, weekly, or monthly summary table.
Using TimescaleDB's time_bucket for real-time aggregation.
Serving a chart already cached in Redis.
optionExplanations: 对，热门商品几年能攒到数千个价格点，请求时现场聚合会把延迟推过 500 毫秒。
查预聚合表只是读几十行结果，属于满足 500 毫秒的方案，不是被排除的那个。
TimescaleDB 的 time_bucket 有分区压缩加持，同样能落在 500 毫秒内。
命中 Redis 缓存直接读现成结果，延迟通常在毫秒级，不会超时。
optionExplanations_en: Right — a popular product can accumulate thousands of price points over years, and aggregating them live pushes latency past 500ms.
Reading a pre-aggregated table just returns a few dozen rows, so it meets the SLO — not the excluded option.
TimescaleDB's time_bucket rides on partitioning and compression, so it also lands under 500ms.
Hitting a Redis cache returns a ready result in milliseconds, so it won't blow the budget.

scenario: 这四个数字来自 CamelCamelCamel 的非功能需求，贯穿了后续所有深挖话题。
scenario_en: These four numbers come from CamelCamelCamel's non-functional requirements and run through every deep dive that follows.
q: 补全本题的规模与性能锚点：
q_en: Fill in this problem's scale and performance anchors:
text: 规模锚点：跟踪 {{5 亿}} 个商品；价格历史查询 < {{500}}ms；降价通知在 {{1 小时}} 内送达；一致性上接受{{最终一致}}。
why: 这些是给定锚点，不是背数字比赛：5 亿决定水平采集/存储，500ms 约束读路径，1 小时约束通知链路，最终一致允许异步化。
why_en: These anchors drive the design: scale splits collection and storage, 500 ms shapes reads, one hour shapes alerts, and eventual consistency allows async pipelines.

q: 以下哪项被明确划为范围之外（below the line）？
q_en: Which of these is explicitly out of scope (below the line)?
options: 查看商品价格历史
通过 Chrome 插件一键订阅
跨多家零售商的价格对比
订阅降价通知
why: 跨零售商比价、站内商品搜索发现、评论评分集成都在范围外；聚焦两条核心功能才能把时间留给深挖。
why_en: Cross-retailer price comparison is explicitly out of scope, along with product search and review integration.
options_en: Viewing a product's price history.
One-click subscribing through the Chrome extension.
Comparing prices across multiple retailers.
Subscribing to a price-drop notification.
optionExplanations: 查看价格历史是两条核心功能之一，在范围内。
插件订阅是核心功能落地的入口，同样在范围内。
对，跨零售商比价被明确划出范围，题目只盯 Amazon 一家。
订阅降价通知是另一条核心功能，在范围内。
optionExplanations_en: Viewing price history is one of the two core features — it's in scope.
Subscribing via the extension is how the core feature gets used — also in scope.
Right — cross-retailer comparison is explicitly out of scope; this system only watches Amazon.
Subscribing to drop alerts is the other core feature — in scope.

q: 「优先可用性而非一致性」对这个系统的实际含义是？
q_en: What does "prioritize availability over consistency" actually mean for this system?
options: 每次读取都必须是最新价格
允许短暂陈旧，可用性优先于强一致
写入必须靠分布式事务保证
通知可以无限期延迟
why: 价格跟踪是历史趋势类产品，短暂陈旧无伤大雅；换来的是架构可以放心用异步管道、缓存和时序库，而不必为强一致付复杂度。
why_en: Prioritizing availability means price data may be briefly stale under eventual consistency, which frees the architecture to use asynchronous pipelines instead of distributed transactions.
options_en: Every read must return the absolute latest price.
Brief staleness is fine; availability wins over strong consistency.
Writes must be guaranteed by distributed transactions.
Notifications can be delayed indefinitely.
optionExplanations: 这其实是强一致的要求，跟「优先可用性」正相反。
对，允许短暂陈旧换可用性，架构才能放心用异步管道和缓存。
分布式事务是为强一致服务的，这里恰恰不需要这份复杂度。
无限期延迟已经违反 1 小时通知的 SLA，不是这条原则的意思。
optionExplanations_en: That's actually a strong-consistency requirement — the opposite of prioritizing availability.
Right — tolerating brief staleness in exchange for availability lets the design lean on async pipelines and caches.
Distributed transactions exist to guarantee strong consistency, which is exactly the complexity being avoided here.
Indefinite delay would violate the 1-hour notification SLA — that's not what this principle means.

q: CamelCamelCamel 的数据模型里，以下哪些是核心实体？（多选）
q_en: Which of these are core entities in CamelCamelCamel's data model? (multi-select)
options: Subscription：关联用户与商品并保存触发阈值
Price：按时间序列记录商品价格变化
Product：被跟踪的 Amazon 商品及其元数据
Retailer：跨平台的零售商主档
why: 核心实体是 Product、User、Subscription、Price 四个；Retailer 属于被排除的跨零售商比价场景。Price 单独建模成时间序列是后面存储拆分的伏笔。
why_en: The core entities are Product, User, Subscription, and time-series Price, while a retailer entity belongs to the out-of-scope comparison feature.
options_en: Subscription: links a user to a product and stores the trigger threshold.
Price: a time series of a product's price changes.
Product: the tracked Amazon item and its metadata.
Retailer: a master record of a retailer for cross-platform comparison.
optionExplanations: 对，Subscription 把用户和商品连起来，还存着触发阈值。
对，Price 单独建模成时间序列，是后面存储拆分的关键伏笔。
对，Product 是被跟踪的 Amazon 商品本体，核心实体之一。
Retailer 主档服务的是跨零售商比价，这题的范围里没有它。
optionExplanations_en: Right — Subscription links a user to a product and stores the trigger threshold.
Right — modeling Price as its own time series is the setup for the later storage split.
Right — Product is the Amazon item being tracked, one of the core entities.
A Retailer master record only matters for cross-retailer comparison, which isn't part of this system.

q: Subscription 实体在数据模型里承担什么角色？
q_en: What role does the Subscription entity play in the data model?
options: 存储商品的价格历史
记录用户的浏览行为
缓存爬虫的抓取结果
记录用户对商品的降价阈值
why: Subscription 是用户和商品之间的连接表，核心字段是 user_id、product_id 和 price_threshold；通知逻辑全靠它找到「谁关心这次降价」。
why_en: A subscription links a user to a product and stores the price threshold that triggers a notification.
options_en: Stores a product's price history.
Logs a user's browsing behavior.
Caches the crawler's fetch results.
Records the drop threshold a user set for a product.
optionExplanations: 存价格走势是 Price 实体的工作，不是 Subscription。
Subscription 不记录浏览行为，那更像是插件采集要处理的数据。
缓存爬虫结果也不是它的职责，那是采集管道内部的事。
对，它是用户和商品之间的关联表，核心字段决定了谁在等这次降价。
optionExplanations_en: Storing price history is Price's job, not Subscription's.
Subscription doesn't log browsing behavior — that would be data the extension's collector deals with.
Caching crawler output isn't its role either — that lives inside the collection pipeline.
Right — it's the join record between user and product, and its fields determine who's waiting on this drop.

q: Price 实体的正确建模方式是？
q_en: What is the correct way to model the Price entity?
options: 按时间序列记录每次价格变化
只在 Product 上存一个当前价格字段
存用户的历史订单价格
存通知发送日志
why: Price 是 append-only 的时间序列数据，每个商品随时间累积价格点；只有这样才能画出价格历史曲线，也因此它和 CRUD 表的存储需求完全不同。
why_en: Price is modeled as append-only time-series data capturing each change over time, which is what makes historical charts possible.
options_en: Record every price change as a time series.
Store only a single current-price field on Product.
Store a user's historical order prices.
Store a log of sent notifications.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只追加新记录、不修改旧记录的写入模式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Append-only means new records are added but existing rows are never updated or overwritten.

optionExplanations: 对，append-only 记录每次变化，才能画出完整的价格走势曲线。
只存一个当前价字段会把历史全部覆盖掉，图表根本画不出来。
用户订单价格是另一回事，跟商品自身的价格走势无关。
通知发送日志记录的是「谁被通知了」，不是价格本身的变化。
optionExplanations_en: Right — an append-only log of every change is the only way to draw a full price history curve.
A single current-price field overwrites history on every update, so there'd be nothing left to chart.
A user's order price is a different thing entirely, unrelated to the product's own price movement.
A notification log records who got alerted, not how the price itself changed.

scenario: 设计查询价格历史的 GET 接口时，要决定 product_id 放 URL 路径还是放请求体。
scenario_en: While designing the GET endpoint for price history, you must decide whether product_id belongs in the URL path or the request body.
q: 为什么选择把 product_id 放在 URL 路径中？
q_en: Why put product_id in the URL path?
options: 把参数放进路径就能天然加密，更安全
GET 请求的协议本身不允许携带查询参数
利于网关和 CDN 缓存，也符合 REST 资源语义
请求体在设计上根本无法传递字符串数据
why: 资源 ID 进 URL 让同一商品的历史请求有稳定的可缓存键，同时符合 REST 的资源定位习惯；period 和 granularity 这类修饰参数放查询串。
why_en: Putting the product ID in the URL path gives a stable cacheable key and follows REST resource semantics, with modifiers like period and granularity in the query string.
whenOtherWins: 如果是多条件组合的复杂筛选或批量查询，参数塞不进一条 URL 时，才考虑 POST + 请求体的搜索型接口。
tradeoff: 路径参数的可缓存性 vs 请求体参数的灵活性
options_en: Putting a value in the path adds encryption automatically, making it safer.
The GET protocol itself doesn't allow carrying any query parameters.
It's cache-friendly for gateways and CDNs, and matches REST resource semantics.
A request body is architecturally incapable of carrying string data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用资源和标准 HTTP 方法组织 API 的风格，例如用 GET 读一个资源。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: REST is an API style that models operations as resources accessed through standard HTTP methods like GET.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把内容缓存到离用户更近的边缘节点，加速静态或可缓存请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN caches content on edge servers closer to users to speed up static or cacheable requests.

optionExplanations: 路径参数不会自动带来加密，安全性跟放哪没关系。
GET 完全可以带查询参数，period、granularity 就是走这条路。
对，同一商品的请求有了稳定的可缓存键，也更符合 REST 的资源定位习惯。
请求体能传任意字符串，这个说法本身就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Putting a value in the path doesn't add encryption — security has nothing to do with where a param lives.
GET requests can absolutely carry query params — that's exactly where period and granularity go.
Right — the same product now has a stable, cacheable key, and it matches REST's resource-addressing convention.
A request body can carry any string just fine, so that claim doesn't hold.

q: 价格历史接口里 granularity 参数的作用是？
q_en: What does the granularity parameter do in the price-history endpoint?
options: 控制返回结果的压缩编码格式
控制数据粒度：长周期返回日级，近期返回小时级
控制结果分页的每页大小
决定服务端缓存条目的 TTL 时长
why: granularity 让同一个接口既能给 2 年图表返回日/月级均值，又能给近期图表返回小时级数据，避免把海量原始点全部推给客户端。
why_en: The granularity parameter lets the API return daily averages for long ranges and hourly points for recent windows instead of dumping raw data.
options_en: Controls the compression encoding format of the response.
Controls data granularity: long ranges return daily rollups, recent ranges return hourly.
Controls how many rows appear per page of results.
Determines the TTL on the server-side cache entry.
optionExplanations: 它跟返回体的压缩格式无关，压缩是传输层的事。
对，同一个接口靠它决定返回日级还是小时级，避免把海量原始点全推给客户端。
分页大小是另一个参数的事，granularity 管的是数据密度不是条数切分。
缓存 TTL 由服务端策略决定，跟这个参数没有关系。
optionExplanations_en: It has nothing to do with response compression — that's a transport-layer concern.
Right — the same endpoint uses it to decide daily vs hourly resolution, instead of shipping every raw point to the client.
Pagination size is a separate concern; granularity controls data density, not how results are chunked.
Cache TTL is set by server-side policy and isn't controlled by this parameter.

scenario: 用户想看某商品最近 30 天的日级价格走势图，客户端需要发一个请求拿到画图数据。
scenario_en: A user wants to see a product's daily price trend for the last 30 days, and the client needs one request to fetch the chart data.
q: 哪个请求设计是正确的？
q_en: Which request design is correct?
options: GET /products/{id}/price?period=30d&granularity=daily
POST /products/price，把 id 放进请求体
GET /price-history?product_id=...
GET /products/{id}/price?period=30d&granularity=monthly
why: 读操作用 GET、资源 ID 进路径、period=30d 配 daily 粒度正好返回约 30 个点；monthly 粒度在 30 天区间里只剩 1 个点，画不成趋势图。
why_en: A GET with the product ID in the path plus a thirty-day period at daily granularity returns about thirty points, exactly what the chart needs.
whenOtherWins: 会改变状态的操作才用 POST，比如创建订阅；纯读取保持 GET 才能被网关和 CDN 缓存。
tradeoff: 资源路径 + 恰当粒度 vs 请求体传参或错配粒度
codeSample:
# 查询 30 天日级价格历史
GET /products/{product_id}/price?period=30d&granularity=daily
-> 200 PriceHistory[]

# 订阅降价通知
POST /subscriptions
{ "product_id": "...", "price_threshold": 249.99, "notification_type": "email" }
-> 200
options_en: GET the product's price with a 30-day period at daily granularity.
POST to a shared price endpoint with the product id in the body.
GET a price-history endpoint with product id only in the query string.
GET the same 30-day period but at monthly granularity.
optionExplanations: 对，GET 配路径 ID，30 天窗口下选 daily 粒度，正好凑出能画趋势的点数。
纯读取用 POST 会丢掉网关和 CDN 缓存的能力，还破坏了 REST 语义。
