Cap how many times a single post can be read.
why: 只要缓存装得下大多数近期帖子，绝大部分读就不再落库；长 TTL 可行是因为帖子极少编辑，LRU 自动腾出冷帖空间。
why_en: As long as the cache holds most recent posts, most reads never hit the database, and a long TTL is safe because posts are rarely edited while LRU frees space for cold posts.
whenOtherWins: 若读负载本来均匀、量级不大，DynamoDB 直查就够，缓存只是多余的复杂度。
tradeoff: 缓存吸收热点读 vs 直查数据库的简单性

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 缓存服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store commonly used as a cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用淘汰策略，优先清掉最久没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU evicts the entry that has gone the longest without being accessed.

optionExplanations: 对：在数据库前插一层缓存，把重复的热点读挡在数据库之外，只有真正的 miss 才落库。
花十倍预算硬扛，不解决负载分布不均本身，成本还会持续线性上涨。
S3 是为大对象和静态分发设计的，不适合这种低延迟点查场景。
限制单条帖子的阅读次数会直接违背『帖子能被大量浏览』的产品目标。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: inserting a cache layer in front of the database intercepts repeated hot reads before they reach the database, only real misses fall through.
Paying for ten times the throughput brute-forces the symptom without fixing the underlying load imbalance, and the bill keeps climbing linearly.
S3 is built for large objects and static distribution, not this kind of low-latency point lookup.
Capping how many times a post can be read directly contradicts the product goal of letting posts be widely viewed.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: Post 缓存在什么时机做失效（invalidate）？
q_en: When should the Post cache be invalidated?
options: 每次有新帖创建时全量失效
编辑时按 postId 精确失效
每小时定时清空
永不失效，全靠 TTL
options_en: Flush the entire cache every time a new post is created.
Precisely invalidate by postId only when a post is edited; a new post needs no invalidation.
Clear the whole cache on a fixed hourly schedule.
Never invalidate at all, relying purely on TTL.
why: 新帖不存在缓存里，谈不上失效；只有编辑会让缓存变陈旧，只需在编辑时删掉对应 postId 的条目。
why_en: A new post was never cached, so there's nothing to invalidate, and only an edit makes the cache stale, so deleting that one postId is enough.
optionExplanations: 新帖当时根本还没进缓存，谈不上要为它做失效。
对：只有编辑会让缓存陈旧，只需在编辑那一刻删掉对应 postId 的条目就够了。
按小时定时清空和真正的编辑事件完全脱钩，清早了浪费、清晚了脏读。
完全放弃主动失效，编辑后的旧内容会一直留到 TTL 自然到期才消失。
optionExplanations_en: A brand-new post was never in the cache yet, so there's nothing to invalidate for it.
Correct: only an edit makes the cache stale, so deleting just that one postId at the moment of the edit is all that's needed.
A fixed hourly flush is completely decoupled from actual edit events — too early wastes work, too late serves stale reads.
Giving up active invalidation entirely leaves edited content stale until the TTL naturally times out.

scenario: 分布式帖子缓存由 N 台主机组成，每台主机有 M 内存。
scenario_en: The distributed post cache has N hosts, and each host has M memory.
q: 这个集群总容量怎么估算，说明了什么？
q_en: How do we estimate total cache-cluster capacity, and what does it imply?
options: 等于单台主机的内存 M
等于数据库的总大小
无法估算，只能靠压测
约 N×M，大多数读会命中缓存
options_en: Equal to a single host's memory M.
Equal to the database's total size.
Impossible to estimate, only load testing can tell.
Roughly N times M; as long as it holds most recent posts, most reads hit the cache.
why: 分片式缓存容量随节点数线性增长（N×M）；结合读集中在近期帖子的模式，不大的集群就能挡住大部分读流量。
why_en: A sharded cache's capacity scales linearly with node count, roughly N times M, and since reads concentrate on recent posts, even a modest cluster absorbs most read traffic.
optionExplanations: 只按单台主机算，忽略了分片式缓存靠多台机器拼出总容量这件事。
缓存容量不需要等于数据库总大小，能装下大部分近期热数据就够。
总容量其实能直接用节点数和单机内存算出来，不需要靠压测猜。
对：分片式缓存总容量约等于 N×M，随节点数线性增长，配合读集中在近期的模式就能挡住大部分流量。
optionExplanations_en: Counting only one host's memory ignores that a sharded cache pools capacity across many machines.
Cache capacity doesn't need to match the database's total size — holding most of the hot recent data is enough.
The total capacity can actually be computed directly from node count and per-node memory, no load test needed to guess it.
Correct: a sharded cache's total capacity is roughly N times M, scaling linearly with node count, enough to absorb most traffic given how reads concentrate on recent posts.

q: 按 postId 分片的帖子缓存，还残留什么问题？
q_en: What problem remains with a postId-sharded post cache?
options: 热 key 原样搬进缓存单点
缓存的成本高于数据库
TTL 无法与 LRU 共存
Redis 不支持按 key 分片
options_en: The hot-key problem gets copied straight into the cache: the shard holding a viral post gets crushed while other nodes sit underused.
The cache costs more than the database.
TTL and LRU can't coexist.
Redis doesn't support sharding by key.
why: 分片缓存里每个帖子只住一个节点，爆款的全部流量仍砸向单点，很多主机反而利用率低下。
why_en: In a sharded cache each post lives on exactly one node, so a viral post's entire traffic still slams a single node while the rest sit underused.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问的单个缓存 key，容易压垮承载它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key that receives disproportionately heavy traffic and can overload the node holding it.

optionExplanations: 对：分片路由把同一个 key 固定钉死在一个节点上，没有第二个节点能分担它的流量。
缓存的成本和这个问题无关，这里讨论的是热点分布，不是价格。
TTL 和 LRU 是两套独立机制，完全可以同时使用，互不冲突。
Redis 完全支持按 key 做一致性哈希分片，这个说法本身就不成立。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: shard routing pins a given key permanently to one node, and no second node exists to share that node's traffic.
Cache cost is unrelated to this problem — the issue here is hotspot distribution, not pricing.
TTL and LRU are two independent mechanisms that work together fine, with no conflict between them.
Redis fully supports consistent-hash sharding by key, so that claim just isn't true.

scenario: 单个爆款帖子的读流量超过任何一台缓存节点的能力上限，按 postId 分片没有出路。
scenario_en: A single viral post has more read traffic than any one cache node can serve, so postId-based sharding has no path forward.
q: 『great』级别的缓存架构是？
q_en: What is the 'great' cache architecture?
options: 在分片缓存前面再加一层缓存
复制式：任何实例都能服务任意帖子
给热分片换更大的机器
把爆款帖子内联进每个用户的 feed 条目
options_en: Add yet another cache layer in front of the sharded cache.
Switch to a replicated cache: every instance can serve any post, and the load balancer spreads requests across all N instances.
Upgrade the hot shard's node to a bigger machine.
Inline the viral post directly into every user's feed entry.
why: 从『每个帖子只住一个节点』改成『每个实例都可服务任何帖子』，热 key 吞吐直接乘 N，且无需任何协调。
why_en: Switching from 'each post lives on one node' to 'every instance can serve any post' multiplies hot-key throughput by N with zero coordination needed.
whenOtherWins: 没有极端热 key、但数据量大时，分片缓存能容纳多得多的不同帖子，总命中率更高。
tradeoff: 复制式的热 key 吞吐 vs 分片式的总容量

termDefinitions.meaning: 每个缓存实例都保存相同的完整数据副本，任何实例都能应答任意 key。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A replicated cache keeps a full copy on every instance so any instance can answer any key.

optionExplanations: 在分片缓存前再叠一层缓存，热 key 还是集中砸向同一个分片，没解决单点问题。
对：所有实例保有相同的数据副本，负载均衡器可以把请求随意撒给任意一台，不用管哪台『拥有』这个帖子。
垂直扩容单个热分片的机器还是有硬件上限，撑不住持续增长的热度。
把爆款帖子内联进每个用户的 feed 条目，存储会随粉丝数线性膨胀，方向反了。
optionExplanations_en: Stacking another cache layer in front still funnels a hot key at the same single shard, leaving the core problem unsolved.
Correct: every instance holds an identical copy of the data, so the load balancer can route a request to any of them without caring which one 'owns' the post.
Vertically scaling the hot shard's machine still hits a hardware ceiling that can't outrun continued growth in popularity.
Inlining a viral post into every user's feed entry makes storage balloon with follower count, the wrong direction entirely.

q: 复制式缓存的代价是什么？
q_en: What is the cost of a replicated cache?
options: 写扇出的整体写入量会变大
读取延迟会因此显著上升
初期 miss 变多，最多 N 次回源
缓存条目将无法再设置 TTL
options_en: Write fan-out volume goes up as a result.
Read latency rises significantly because of it.
More initial misses: the same viral post may be fetched from the origin once per instance, N times instead of once.
Cache entries can no longer have a TTL set on them.
why: 每个实例独立回源，冷启动时同一帖子最多 N 次 miss；拿 N 次回源换 N 倍热 key 吞吐是划算的交换。
why_en: Each instance fetches from the origin independently, so a cold start can cost up to N misses for the same post, a fair trade for N times the hot-key throughput.
optionExplanations: 复制式缓存改变的是读路径的服务方式，跟写扇出的机制没有关系。
复制式缓存反而是为了降低热 key 的读延迟，说延迟上升和目的相反。
对：多个实例第一次遇到同一个帖子时各自单独去数据库要一次，这些 miss 并行发生、彼此独立。
复制式缓存照样能设 TTL，跟分片式没有区别，这个说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: A replicated cache changes how reads are served, unrelated to the write-path fan-out mechanism.
A replicated cache exists specifically to cut hot-key read latency, so claiming latency rises is the opposite of the goal.
Correct: multiple instances each hit the database once on their own first encounter with the same post, and those misses happen independently in parallel.
A replicated cache can set a TTL just fine, no different from a sharded one, so that claim doesn't hold.

q: 分片缓存与复制缓存，在『单个热 key 的吞吐上限』维度上的区别是？
q_en: How do sharded and replicated caches differ on single-hot-key throughput?
options: 分片卡单点；复制乘 N 倍
两者的热 key 吞吐相同
复制式的热 key 吞吐更低
取决于 TTL 设多长
options_en: Sharded: hot-key throughput is roughly one node's limit; replicated: roughly N times one node's limit, with no coordination needed.
The two have identical hot-key throughput.
A replicated cache actually has lower hot-key throughput.
It depends entirely on how long the TTL is set.
why: 这是空间换吞吐：分片容量大但热 key 卡单点；复制容量小但热 key 吞吐乘 N。
why_en: This is capacity traded for throughput: sharding caps a hot key at one node, while replication multiplies hot-key throughput by N.
tradeoff: 热 key 吞吐 vs 总缓存容量
optionExplanations: 对：分片式里热 key 卡在单节点的上限；复制式里每个实例都能应答，吞吐乘 N 且不需要协调。
两者在热 key 这个维度上差得很远，说『相同』忽视了架构本质的不同。
把两者的能力关系说反了，复制式的热 key 吞吐其实更高，不是更低。
TTL 决定的是数据新鲜度，跟热 key 能被多少个节点同时服务是两个独立维度。
optionExplanations_en: Correct: sharded caps a hot key at one node's limit, while replicated lets every instance answer, multiplying throughput by N with no coordination.
The two differ a lot on this dimension; calling them 'identical' ignores their fundamentally different architectures.
This reverses the actual relationship — a replicated cache's hot-key throughput is higher, not lower.
TTL governs data freshness, a separate dimension from how many nodes can serve a hot key at once.

scenario: 用 Redis 缓存帖子：key 按 postId；帖子极少编辑所以 TTL 可以设 1 天；一旦编辑要立刻失效。
scenario_en: Use Redis to cache posts by postId. Posts are rarely edited, so TTL can be one day, but edits must invalidate immediately.
q: 哪组命令符合这套策略？
q_en: Which Redis command sequence matches this caching strategy?
options: SET post:p123 ... EX 60，一分钟就过期
SET post:p123 ...（不带 TTL），并在创建新帖时 DEL
SET post:p123 ... EX 86400，编辑帖子时 DEL 对应 key
只用 GET post:p123，miss 时完全不做任何回填
options_en: SET post:p123 ... EX 60, expiring after one minute.
SET post:p123 ... with no TTL, and DEL it whenever a new post is created.
SET post:p123 ... EX 86400, and DEL the matching key whenever the post is edited.
Only GET post:p123, doing absolutely no backfill at all on a miss.
codeSample:
# fill on miss, long TTL (1 day)
SET post:p123 '{"content":"..."}' EX 86400

# read path
GET post:p123

# post edited: precise invalidation
DEL post:p123
why: 长 TTL（EX 86400）匹配『帖子几乎不变』的事实，编辑时 DEL 精确失效；TTL 60 秒会造成大量无谓 miss。
why_en: A long TTL of EX 86400 matches how rarely posts change, while DEL on edit gives precise invalidation, unlike a 60-second TTL that would cause needless misses.
whenOtherWins: 若帖子频繁编辑且必须立刻可见，就该缩短 TTL 或改成写时同步更新缓存。
tradeoff: 长 TTL+精确失效 vs 短 TTL 的保守新鲜度

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的过期时间，过期后必须重新获取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is the expiration time after which a cached entry must be refreshed.

optionExplanations: 60 秒的时长远短于帖子几乎不变的真实变化频率，会制造大量不必要的 miss。
在创建时机做失效没有意义，而且完全没有兜底的自动清理。
对：一天的时长匹配帖子极少变化的事实，编辑发生时精确删掉对应 key。
只读不写意味着缓存永远不会被填充，等于没有缓存。
optionExplanations_en: A 60-second span is far shorter than how rarely a post actually changes, causing needless misses.
Invalidating at creation time doesn't make sense, and there's no automatic cleanup as a backstop either.
Correct: a one-day span matches how rarely posts actually change, with a precise delete on that key the moment an edit happens.
Read-only with no write path means the cache never gets populated at all — effectively no cache.

q: 把『爆款帖子读扇出』的决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the viral-post read fan-out decision chain in the right order.
steps: 代价：分片缓存自身也有热 key——爆款所在的分片照样被打爆
缓解：接受最多 N 次回源和更小的有效容量，DynamoDB 能吸收这点波动
需求：爆款帖子头几小时读量巨大，而 DynamoDB 只有负载均匀才能高吞吐
升级：换成复制式缓存+负载均衡，任何实例都能服务任何帖子
选型：在 Post 表前加分布式缓存，长 TTL + LRU
why: 链条完整走一遍：热读需求 → 加缓存 → 缓存自己也热 → 复制式缓存摊平 → 接受少量回源。
why_en: The chain runs from a hot-read requirement, to adding a cache, to the cache itself getting hot, to replication spreading the load.

termDefinitions.meaning: 被异常高频访问的单个缓存 key，容易压垮承载它的节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A hot key is a single key that receives disproportionately heavy traffic and can overload the node holding it.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 复制式缓存能装下的『不同帖子总数』比分片式少，为什么可以接受？
q_en: Why is it acceptable that a replicated cache holds fewer distinct posts than a sharded cache?
options: 因为帖子会自动压缩
因为可以无限加内存
因为旧帖子根本没人读，不缓存也没影响
DynamoDB 兜得住这点额外 miss
options_en: Because posts get automatically compressed.
Because memory can be added without limit.
Because nobody reads old posts anyway, so not caching them has no impact.
Because the DynamoDB backend can absorb some read-throughput variability, and the small extra misses fall well within that.
why: 复制牺牲了有效容量，换来热 key 吞吐；落库的 miss 变多一点没关系，DynamoDB 不是不能读，只是不能被单点打爆。
why_en: Replication trades away effective capacity for hot-key throughput, and the extra misses falling through to DynamoDB are easily absorbed.
optionExplanations: 帖子并不会自动压缩，这是编出来的机制。
内存可以加但成本会跟着线性上涨，不是『无限』就没代价。
『旧帖子根本没人读』说得太绝对，只是读得少，不是完全没有。
对：复制牺牲的是有效容量，多出来的 miss 落回 DynamoDB 完全兜得住，不是被单点打爆。
optionExplanations_en: Posts don't actually get auto-compressed — that's a fabricated mechanism.
Memory can be added, but cost keeps scaling linearly with it; 'unlimited' doesn't mean free.
'Nobody reads old posts' overstates it — they're read less often, not never.
Correct: replication trades away effective capacity, and the resulting extra misses falling through to DynamoDB are easily absorbed, not a single-point overload.

numberAnchors.risk: AWS 管扩展，但 hot key 仍会限流

q: 面试官禁止使用 Elasticsearch / Postgres 全文索引后，设计上你被迫要亲手做的核心工作是？
q_en: When Elasticsearch and Postgres full-text search are off limits, what core work must you build yourself?
options: 亲手设计数据布局与倒排索引
改用 NoSQL 自带的搜索功能
放弃关键词搜索改做前缀匹配
把过滤逻辑全放到客户端本地
why: 没有现成全文索引可依赖，你必须自己决定数据如何布局、如何构建倒排索引、如何扩展——这正是这类题要考的底层功。
why_en: With no off-the-shelf full-text index available, you must design the data layout, build the inverted index, and scale it yourself.
options_en: Hand-build the data layout and an inverted index yourself.
Rely on a NoSQL database's built-in search.
Drop keyword search and only do prefix matching.
Push all filtering to the client side.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开箱即用的分布式搜索引擎，内部本身就用倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an off-the-shelf search engine built on inverted indexes.

optionExplanations: 禁用现成引擎后，唯一出路就是这个：自己定布局、建索引、想扩展。
误以为 NoSQL 自带全文检索能绕过限制，但题目已经排除了这类现成搜索方案。
把关键词搜索偷换成前缀匹配，其实是在悄悄阉割功能需求，题目并未允许。
客户端拿不到全量帖子数据，把过滤全丢给它做不出真正的搜索匹配。
optionExplanations_en: With Elasticsearch and native full-text search off the table, you're the one deciding the data layout, the index shape, and how it scales.
NoSQL's built-in search is exactly the kind of off-the-shelf engine this problem rules out, so it doesn't get you out of building your own.
Swapping keyword search for prefix matching quietly drops a stated requirement instead of solving the indexing problem.
The client never sees the full post corpus, so pushing filtering there can't reproduce real keyword search.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: 为 FB 帖子搜索定义需求时，哪些属于核心功能需求？（多选）
q_en: When defining requirements for FB Post Search, which are core functional requirements?
options: 用户能创建和点赞帖子
用户能按关键词搜索帖子
搜索结果能按时间或点赞数排序
搜索结果按用户兴趣做个性化排序
why: 核心需求只有三条：创建/点赞、关键词搜索、按时间或赞数排序；个性化被明确划出范围，这个决定让后面的缓存设计大为简化。
why_en: The core requirements are creating and liking posts, keyword search, and sorting by recency or like count, while personalization is explicitly out of scope.
options_en: Users can create and like posts.
Users can search posts by keyword.
Results can be sorted by recency or like count.
Results are personalized to each user's interests.
optionExplanations: 创建和点赞是搜索得以运作的前提动作，属于核心功能需求。
关键词搜索是本题唯一被点名的核心检索方式，必须支持。
结果排序是明确列出的核心需求，为后面的双索引设计埋下伏笔。
个性化听起来像加分项，但被题目明确划出范围，不是核心需求。
optionExplanations_en: Creating and liking posts are the baseline actions the whole search feature depends on, so they're core requirements.
Keyword search is the one retrieval mode this problem names explicitly, so it has to be supported.
Sorting results is called out as a core requirement, which is what later motivates the dual-index design.
Personalization sounds like a nice add-on, but the problem explicitly puts it out of scope, not a core requirement.

q: FB 帖子搜索里，下列哪些被划为范围外（out of scope）？（多选）
q_en: In FB Post Search, which items are out of scope?
options: 模糊匹配（搜 bird 命中 ostrich）
隐私规则与过滤
新帖 1 分钟内可被搜索
搜索页对新帖做实时推送更新
why: 模糊匹配、个性化、隐私、复杂相关性排序、多媒体、实时更新都在范围外；「新帖 1 分钟内可搜」恰恰是核心非功能需求，不是范围外。
why_en: Fuzzy matching, privacy filters, and realtime result updates are out of scope, whereas making new posts searchable within a minute is a core requirement.
options_en: Fuzzy matching (searching bird also matches ostrich).
Privacy rules and filtering.
New posts searchable within one minute.
Realtime push updates to the search page.
optionExplanations: 模糊匹配要理解语义相近词，这类高级检索能力被划出了范围。
隐私规则涉及权限体系，这道题聚焦索引和检索，不含在内。
这条其实是核心非功能需求（新帖可搜的时限），不是范围外项目。
实时推送要额外的长连接和通知系统，本题只做拉取式搜索。
optionExplanations_en: Fuzzy matching needs semantic-similarity understanding, an advanced capability this problem puts out of scope.
Privacy rules are an authorization concern; this problem stays focused on indexing and retrieval, not access control.
This is actually a core non-functional requirement — the new-post visibility deadline — not an out-of-scope item.
Realtime push needs long-lived connections and a notification system; this design only does pull-based search.

scenario: 明确需求阶段，你在考虑是否把「搜索结果个性化」留在范围内，这个决定将影响后续架构的复杂度。
scenario_en: During requirements clarification, you are deciding whether personalized search results are in scope, which will drive downstream architecture complexity.
q: 把个性化划出范围，对系统设计最大的红利是什么？
q_en: What is the biggest system-design benefit of making personalization out of scope?
options: 数据库可以少建一个索引来省空间
读写请求都不再需要 API 网关拦截
相同查询人人同结果，查询级缓存极其有效
写入路径可以完全省掉
why: 没有个性化意味着搜索结果只取决于查询本身、人人相同，结果可以进缓存和 CDN 被海量复用；所以值得当面问「个性化是不是硬需求」。
why_en: Dropping personalization means identical queries return identical results for everyone, which makes query-level caching and CDN reuse dramatically more effective.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品硬性要求千人千面的搜索结果，查询级缓存基本失效，只能退到缓存更底层的索引数据、在线上做个性化重排。
options_en: The database needs one fewer index.
You no longer need an API gateway.
Identical queries return identical results, so query-level caching becomes extremely effective.
The write path can be dropped entirely.
tradeoff: 无个性化换来缓存高复用 vs 千人千面的相关性

termDefinitions.meaning: 读路径最前端的入口，负责鉴权、限流后转发给后端服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API gateway authenticates and rate-limits requests before forwarding them.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

optionExplanations: 少建索引只是锦上添花的小事，撑不起「舍弃个性化」这么大的取舍。
API 网关管的是鉴权限流，跟结果是否因人而异毫无关系。
无个性化时同一查询谁来查结果都一样，缓存可以被海量请求复用，这才是真正的红利。
发帖点赞的写入路径跟个性化无关，砍掉个性化也不会让写入消失。
optionExplanations_en: Trimming one database index is a footnote, not the payoff big enough to justify dropping personalization.
The API gateway just handles auth and rate limiting, unrelated to whether results differ per user.
Without personalization, identical queries return identical results for everyone, so a shared cache absorbs massive request volume — that's the real win.
The write path for posts and likes has nothing to do with personalization; dropping it doesn't remove writes.

scenario: FB Post Search 面试先给定两个目标：中位搜索延迟 <500ms，新帖 <1分钟可搜。这些是 SLO/SLA 目标，不是由帖子量公式算出的结果。
scenario_en: In the FB Post Search interview, median search latency under 500 ms and new posts searchable within one minute are given SLO/SLA targets, not capacity-derived numbers.
q: 这些 NFR 数字分别约束哪条设计路径？
q_en: Which design paths do these NFR numbers constrain?
text: 500ms 约束{{查询路径}}，推动内存索引、缓存和避免请求时全量排序；1分钟约束{{新帖可见性}}，反推索引流水线延迟和缓存 TTL 上限。
why: 这两个数不是算出来的容量结果，而是面试中先约定的用户体验目标。真正的计算发生在后面：用它们倒推索引、缓存、冷热分层和写入流水线。
why_en: The five-hundred-millisecond and one-minute numbers are service targets, not derived constants, and they constrain the query path and freshness path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 延迟、吞吐、可用性这类衡量系统「好不好」的指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-functional requirements cover latency, throughput, and availability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级目标：团队希望系统达到的内部目标，如中位搜索 <500ms。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level objective is an internal target for system behavior, such as median search latency under five hundred milliseconds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务等级协议：对外承诺的服务指标，如新帖 1 分钟内可搜。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A service level agreement is a promised service level, such as new posts being searchable within a minute.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存存活时间。超过 TTL 后缓存条目过期，系统必须重新取或重算。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Time to live is how long a cache entry may live before it expires and must be refreshed.

q: 「老帖、冷门帖也要可搜索，但允许更慢」这条需求在为哪个设计决策埋伏笔？
q_en: Which later design decision is hinted by the requirement that old and unpopular posts are searchable but slower?
options: 放弃高可用目标
冷热分层：热数据进内存、冷数据下沉廉价存储
换一台内存更大的单机数据库来扛全部数据
把所有索引都搬进 CDN
why: 大数据量系统天然有热/冷数据之分：热数据高频访问要内存级速度，冷数据低频访问可放磁盘、远端库甚至磁带；这条 NFR 正是后面「冷索引下沉 S3」的伏笔。
why_en: Allowing old or unpopular posts to be slower foreshadows a hot-cold split where hot data lives in memory and cold data moves to cheaper, slower storage.
options_en: Abandon the high-availability goal.
A hot-cold split: hot data in memory, cold data on cheaper storage.
Switch to a single bigger database machine.
Move all indexes into the CDN.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

optionExplanations: 允许冷帖慢一点跟放弃高可用是两码事，系统仍要保持可用。
这正是后面冷索引下沉 blob 存储的伏笔：热数据留内存，冷数据可以慢。
单机再大也扛不住海量冷热数据，纵向扩容不是长久之计。
CDN 缓存的是响应结果，不是拿来放整份可写索引的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Tolerating slower cold posts is not the same as giving up on availability; the system still has to stay up.
This is exactly what later motivates demoting cold indexes to blob storage: hot data stays in memory, cold data can be slower.
No single machine, however large, absorbs unbounded hot-and-cold data growth; vertical scaling doesn't hold up.
A CDN caches response payloads, not a place to host a live, writable index.

q: 补全写入侧的规模估算（10 亿用户，每天按约 10 万秒取整）：
q_en: Fill in the write-side scale estimate for 1B users and roughly 100K seconds per day.
text: 每人每天 1 帖 → 约 {{10k}} posts/秒；每人每天 10 个赞 → 约 {{100k}} likes/秒；点赞写入量是发帖的 {{10}} 倍。
why: 用 1B ÷ 100k 秒的快捷除法得出发帖 10k/s、点赞 100k/s；点赞比发帖多一个数量级，这个观察直接决定了后面必须重点优化点赞写入。
why_en: A billion users produce roughly ten thousand posts and one hundred thousand likes per second, so likes outnumber post creations ten to one.
scenario: 规模估算：10 亿用户，每天约 10 万秒，估算写入侧的量级。
scenario_en: Estimate write-side order of magnitude from 1B users and about 100K seconds per day.

q: 由这个读规模，读路径最该具备的能力是？
q_en: Given this read scale, what capability does the read path need most?
options: 读会突发到 10 倍，重复查询要能被缓存/CDN 吸收
读量极小，单台普通机器就足以稳稳承载全部流量
读远大于写，就该牺牲写路径来保读
读流量根本无法估算，直接跳过这步
why: 搜索读约 10k/s 但可能突发 10 倍；因为无个性化、查询重复度高，读路径靠结果缓存和 CDN 吸收峰值，而不是一味加索引机器。
why_en: Search reads run about ten thousand per second but can spike tenfold, so the read path leans on result caching and a CDN to absorb bursts.
scenario: 10 亿用户、每人每天约 1 次搜索，读流量还可能突发到平时的 10 倍以上。
scenario_en: With 1B users and about one search per user per day, read traffic can still spike over 10x.
options_en: Reads can spike 10x, so repeated queries must be absorbable by a cache/CDN.
Read volume is tiny; a single machine can carry all traffic.
Reads dominate writes, so sacrifice the write path to protect reads.
Read traffic can't be estimated, so skip this step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge HTTP caches that serve users from nearby locations.

optionExplanations: 10k/s 的常态读量还可能突发到 10 倍，读路径得靠缓存和 CDN 顶住峰值。
1 万/秒已经不是单机量级，读量并不小。
前面已经算出写才是大头，这里反而说读碾压写，判断反了。
估算恰恰是这一步的意义所在，「无法估算」是在回避该做的工作。
optionExplanations_en: A steady ten thousand reads a second can still burst tenfold, so the read path leans on cache and CDN to absorb spikes.
Ten thousand requests a second is well past what a single box handles; the volume isn't tiny.
The earlier estimate already showed writes dominate; claiming reads crush writes gets the comparison backwards.
Estimating scale is the whole point of this step; skipping it dodges the work instead of doing it.

q: 对比估算结果（写约 110k/s vs 搜索 10k/s），关于系统性质最重要的结论是？
q_en: Comparing about 110K writes/s with 10K searches/s, what is the key system takeaway?
options: 系统读多写少，应重点优化读路径
系统写多读少——别被「搜索」二字骗成读为主
读写均衡，无需特别优化
数据量不大，单机即可承载
why: 这题最容易犯的错是被「搜索系统」带偏、假设读是大头；估算揭示写入（尤其点赞）远超读，写路径才是主要瓶颈。
why_en: The estimates reveal a write-heavy system, overturning the common assumption that a search problem must be read-heavy.
options_en: The system is read-heavy; optimize the read path.
The system is write-heavy—don't let the word 'search' fool you into assuming reads dominate.
Reads and writes are balanced; no special optimization.
The data is small; one machine suffices.
optionExplanations: 这正是「搜索」二字带来的常见误判，估算结果其实相反。
110k/s 写 vs 10k/s 读，写才是十倍量级的大头。
两者相差一个数量级，说「均衡」低估了真实的写入压力。
十亿用户规模下的写入量早已远超单机承载能力。
optionExplanations_en: This is exactly the misread the word 'search' invites; the estimate actually points the other way.
At roughly 110K writes/s versus 10K reads/s, writes outweigh reads by a full order of magnitude.
The two differ by 10x, so calling it 'balanced' understates the real write pressure.
At a billion-user scale, write volume already far exceeds what one machine can carry.

q: 这个存储量级对搜索系统提出的设计要求是？
q_en: What does this storage scale force the search system to do?
options: 内存放不下 3.6PB，索引要设上限、冷数据下沉便宜存储
数据量不大，一台大内存机器即可
把全部帖子原文都整份塞进 Redis 内存加速
存储不是问题，无需特别处理
why: 3.6 万亿帖 × 1kb ≈ 3.6PB，全量放内存/单机不可行；这直接催生后面给索引设上限、把冷门关键词下沉 blob 存储的设计。
why_en: Ten years of a billion posts a day is about 3.6 petabytes, far too much to keep in memory, which forces index caps and cold blob storage.
scenario: FB 运营 10 年、每天约 10 亿帖、每帖元数据约 1kb，原始存储估算约 3.6 PB。
scenario_en: After 10 years at roughly 1B posts per day and 1 KB metadata per post, raw storage is about 3.6 PB.
options_en: 3.6 PB won't fit in memory, so indexes must be capped and cold data pushed to cheap storage.
The data is small; one big-memory machine is enough.
Stuff every post's full text into Redis for speed.
Storage isn't a concern; no special handling needed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

optionExplanations: 3.6PB 远超任何单机内存容量，索引必须设上限、冷数据另找便宜去处。
3.6PB 早已超出「一台大内存机器」能装下的范围。
把原文塞进内存型的 Redis，成本和容量都撑不住 PB 级数据。
3.6PB 正是逼出「索引设上限+冷数据下沉」设计的根源，不能忽视。
optionExplanations_en: 3.6 petabytes dwarfs any single machine's memory, so indexes need a cap and cold data needs a cheaper home.
3.6 petabytes is already far beyond what one big-memory box can hold.
Stuffing raw post text into memory-priced Redis can't afford petabyte-scale cost or capacity.
3.6 petabytes is precisely what forces the index-cap-plus-cold-storage design; it can't be waved away.

q: FB 帖子搜索的核心实体（User/Post/Like）里，哪些说法正确？（多选）
q_en: Which statements about the core User/Post/Like entities in FB Post Search are correct?
options: User——发帖的主体
Post——被搜索的对象，有内容、作者，隐含点赞数
Like——我们主要关心它的计数而非每条记录
Comment——搜索的主要目标
why: 实体刻意简单：User、Post、Like 三个，且对 Like 只关心 count；实体简单就不必恋战，快速推进到 API 和设计。
why_en: The entities are just User, Post, and Like, and for likes we mostly care about the count rather than individual records.
options_en: User — the author who creates posts.
Post — the searchable object with content, author, and an implicit like count.
Like — we mostly care about its count, not each record.
Comment — the primary search target.
optionExplanations: User 只是发帖的主体，本题不深挖用户模型本身。
Post 是搜索真正的目标对象，携带内容、作者和点赞数。
点赞我们只关心总数用于排序，单条点赞记录不重要。
评论从未出现在本题的核心实体里，搜索的目标始终是帖子。
optionExplanations_en: User is just the actor who creates posts; this problem doesn't dig into the user model itself.
Post is the actual object being searched, carrying content, author, and an implicit like count.
For likes we only care about the running total for sorting, not each individual like record.
Comments never appear among this problem's core entities; the search target is always the post.

q: FB 帖子搜索的 API 应该是什么形状？
q_en: What shape should the FB Post Search API have?
options: 单一搜索端点，写入直连数据库
全部收敛为一个 GraphQL 端点
搜索复用写入端点
写路径（发帖/点赞）+ 查询路径（搜索）两条腿
why: API 分两条腿：写入端点接帖子与点赞、搜索端点服务查询；并向面试官说明真实系统中写入多半来自事件总线，独立端点只是为了讲解清晰。
why_en: The system exposes a write path for posts and likes plus a search query path, and in production the writes would likely arrive via an event stream like Kafka.
options_en: A single search endpoint, with writes going straight to the database.
Everything collapsed into one GraphQL endpoint.
Search reuses the write endpoint.
A write path (create post / like) plus a query path (search) — two legs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让客户端按需声明字段的单端点查询语言。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GraphQL is a single-endpoint query language where clients request exact fields.

optionExplanations: 写入直连数据库跳过了摄取和索引构建这一整套流程。
GraphQL 收敛所有查询字段，跟这里读写分离的架构无关。
写入和搜索的负载特征完全不同，合用一个端点会互相拖累。
写路径喂事件建索引、查询路径服务搜索，各司其职最清晰。
optionExplanations_en: Writing straight to the database skips the whole ingestion and index-building pipeline this design needs.
GraphQL collapses query fields into one endpoint, which has nothing to do with separating reads from writes here.
Writes and searches have completely different load shapes; cramming them into one endpoint makes each worse.
The write path feeds events into the index while the query path serves search — a clean separation of concerns.

q: 设计只聚焦「搜索」时，对上游 Post Service / Like Service 的正确处理方式是？
q_en: If the design focuses only on search, how should you treat upstream Post and Like services?
options: 假设它们已存在且正常工作，只从它们接收事件
必须从零开始重新设计这两个服务
把它们合并进搜索服务统一实现
忽略它们，让客户端直连索引
why: 搜索只是整个社交产品的一部分，合理做法是假设上游发帖/点赞服务存在并工作正常，我们的摄取层从它们接事件；把边界说清楚能省下宝贵时间。
why_en: Since we are only designing search, we assume the upstream post and like services already exist and feed our ingestion pipeline.
options_en: Assume they already exist and work; just consume their events.
Design both services from scratch.
Merge them into the search service.
Ignore them and let clients hit the index directly.
optionExplanations: 搜索只是整个产品的一部分，划清边界后专心做摄取和索引。
重新设计发帖/点赞服务偏离了「只做搜索」的题目边界。
合并服务混淆了职责边界，搜索不该兼管发帖点赞的业务逻辑。
跳过上游服务，索引就没有数据来源，搜索无从谈起。
optionExplanations_en: Search is only one slice of the product, so drawing that boundary lets you focus on ingestion and indexing.
Redesigning the post and like services strays outside the 'search only' scope this problem sets.
Merging the services blurs ownership; search shouldn't also own posting and liking business logic.
Skip the upstream services and the index has no data source at all — there's nothing left to search.

q: 用这条 SQL 直接在 PB 级帖子表上做关键词搜索，最根本的问题是？
q_en: What is the fundamental problem with running this SQL keyword search directly on a PB-scale posts table?
options: 语法不合法，无法执行
没有索引，查询时要逐帖全表扫描，PB 级下太慢
返回的结果不正确
LIKE 这条语法本身并不支持中文内容匹配
why: 前置通配符的 LIKE 无法走索引，每次查询都要在查询时刻扫描每一帖；结果正确但在万亿帖、PB 级数据上是灾难——数据组织必须匹配请求模式。
why_en: A leading-wildcard LIKE cannot use an index, so every query scans every post at query time, which is hopeless at petabyte scale.
options_en: The syntax is invalid and won't run.
No index is usable, so every query scans all posts — hopeless at petabyte scale.
The returned results are incorrect.
LIKE doesn't support non-English text.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

optionExplanations: 这条 SQL 语法完全合法，能正常执行，只是慢到不可用。
前置通配符的 LIKE 走不了索引，每次查询都要扫全表。
结果本身是对的，问题出在扫描代价，不是结果错误。
LIKE 对语言无感知，真正的病根是缺索引而非语言支持。
optionExplanations_en: The SQL syntax is perfectly valid and runs fine; the problem is that it's unusably slow.
A leading-wildcard LIKE can't use an index, so every query scans the entire table.
The results themselves are correct; the issue is scan cost, not wrong output.
LIKE has no awareness of language at all; the real defect is the missing index, not text support.

q: 对全表扫描方案做分片/复制（M 个节点各扫 N/M 帖），结论是？
q_en: If you shard and replicate the full-table scan across M nodes, what is the conclusion?
options: 分片能彻底解决扫描慢的问题
只要把节点数 M 撑得足够大就能达标
只是边际改善：每节点仍要扫海量，依旧太慢，死路
分片反而会让结果不正确
why: 分片把扫描量从 N 降到 N/M，但面对万亿级帖子这只是把「不可能」变成「依然不可能」；正确出路是改变数据组织方式，而不是堆机器硬扫。
why_en: Sharding the naive scan only cuts each node's work to N over M posts, which is still far too slow and a dead end.
options_en: Sharding fully solves the slow-scan problem.
It's fine as long as the node count M is large enough.
Only a marginal gain: each node still scans a huge amount — still too slow, a dead end.
Sharding makes the results incorrect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据拆到多台机器，分摊写入和存储压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across machines by a key to spread load.

optionExplanations: 分片只是把慢均摊到多台机器，扫描这件事本身没有变快。
把 M 堆得再大，万亿级数据下每片仍是海量，撑不起亚秒级。
分片只把总扫描量摊薄成 N/M，量级依旧巨大，唯一出路是重新组织数据。
分片只影响谁去扫，不影响扫描逻辑本身，结果依旧正确。
optionExplanations_en: Sharding just spreads the slowness across machines; scanning itself doesn't get any faster.
However large M gets, each shard of a trillion-row table is still huge and can't hit sub-second latency.
Cutting N down to N/M only turns 'impossible' into 'still impossible' — the fix has to be reorganizing the data itself.
Sharding only changes who does the scanning, not the scan logic, so results stay correct.

scenario: 万亿级帖子，要求按关键词找出所有包含该词的帖子，查询延迟中位数 <500ms，且不允许使用现成搜索引擎。
scenario_en: Across trillions of posts, you need sub-500 ms keyword lookup without using an off-the-shelf search engine.
q: 应该采用的核心数据结构是？
q_en: What core data structure should you use?
options: 倒排索引：关键词 → 包含它的帖子 ID 列表
对 content 列建 B-tree 索引
分片后的并行全表扫描
用布隆过滤器直接返回结果
why: 倒排索引把工作移到写入时：发帖时拆词并把帖子 ID 挂到每个词的列表下，查询就变成一次按 key 取列表的快速查找，这是关键词搜索的教科书解法。
why_en: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of posts containing it, turning search into a fast key lookup instead of a scan.
whenOtherWins: 若查询是前缀或范围查询，B-tree 类索引才有用武之地；若允许用 Elasticsearch，直接用它内置的倒排索引省去自建成本。
diagram:
flowchart LR
    P["新帖: I saw Taylor"] --> T["拆词 tokenization"]
    T --> A["key: i ← post9"]
    T --> B["key: saw ← post9"]
    T --> C["key: taylor ← post9"]
    Q["搜索 taylor"] -. 直接取列表 .-> C
options_en: An inverted index: keyword → list of post IDs containing it.
A B-tree index on the content column.
Parallel full-table scan after sharding.
Use a Bloom filter to return results directly.
tradeoff: 写时预组织(倒排索引) vs 查询时扫描/过滤

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 数据库常用的按值排序索引，擅长前缀和范围查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A B-tree index sorts values for fast prefix and range lookups.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用位数组做概率性成员判断，只能答「可能存在/一定不存在」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Bloom filter probabilistically tests set membership with no false negatives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 开箱即用的分布式搜索引擎，内部本身就用倒排索引。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Elasticsearch is an off-the-shelf search engine built on inverted indexes.

optionExplanations: 把词到帖子的映射提前建在写入阶段，检索时只是一次哈希查找，天然扛得住亚秒级要求。
B-tree 擅长前缀和范围查询，但整词精确匹配靠它仍要扫描，帮不上这里的忙。
并行扫描把 N 降到 N/M，可万亿级数据下每片仍太大，赶不上 500ms。
布隆过滤器只能答「可能存在」，给不出完整的帖子列表，满足不了搜索需求。
optionExplanations_en: Pre-building the keyword-to-post mapping turns every query into a single key lookup, which is what makes sub-second latency possible.
A B-tree shines at prefix and range lookups, but exact whole-word matching still forces a scan, so it doesn't help here.
Parallel scanning cuts N down to N/M, but each shard of a trillion posts is still too large to hit 500ms.
A Bloom filter can only answer 'maybe present,' not hand back the actual list of matching posts search needs.

q: 补全倒排索引的写入流程：
q_en: Fill in the write flow for building an inverted index:
text: 帖子创建后，Ingestion 服务把内容拆解成一个个可匹配的关键词，这个过程叫 {{tokenization}}；随后把该帖的 {{post ID}} 追加到每个关键词对应的列表里。
why: 倒排索引的构建就是「拆词 + 挂 ID」：一帖可能含 10-1000 个词，意味着一次发帖触发多个 key 的写入，这也是后面写扩展问题的根源。
why_en: Ingestion tokenizes each post into keywords and appends the post ID to every keyword's list in the index.
diagram:
graph LR
    Post[New post] --> Tokenize[Tokenize text]
    Tokenize --> Terms[Terms]
    Terms --> Index[Update inverted index]
    Index --> Redis[(Redis lists or sets)]
    Post --> Store[(Post store)]

termDefinitions.meaning: 把帖子内容拆解成一个个可匹配关键词的过程，中文叫分词。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Tokenization breaks a post into individual searchable keywords.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

scenario: 倒排索引位于中位 <500ms 的核心查询路径上，需要极快的读取，同时你接受用替代方案弥补持久性短板。
scenario_en: The inverted index sits on the sub-500 ms query path, needs very fast reads, and can address durability through another option.
q: 这个倒排索引应该放在什么存储里？
q_en: Where should this inverted index live?
options: 磁盘上的 MySQL 表——最耐久但读取偏慢
本地文件——最简单但单机无法扩展
Redis 内存——查询极快，MemoryDB 补持久
S3 对象存储——最便宜但延迟太高
why: 索引放 Redis 内存里查询飞快，满足亚 500ms 的核心诉求；内存的持久性短板是可解的——换 MemoryDB 等持久化兼容方案或留到深挖处理。
why_en: The index lives in Redis for blazing-fast in-memory lookups, with durability concerns addressed by a persistent alternative like MemoryDB.
whenOtherWins: 若索引重建代价不可接受、持久性是硬约束，一开始就选 MemoryDB 或磁盘型存储；冷门关键词后面也会下沉到便宜的 blob 存储。
options_en: A MySQL table on disk — most durable but slow to read.
Local files — simplest but a single box that can't scale.
Redis in memory — blazing-fast reads, with MemoryDB covering durability.
S3 object storage — cheapest but latency is too high.
tradeoff: 内存读取速度 vs 持久性/成本

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 兼容 Redis 接口但带持久化的内存数据库，可弥补纯内存的易失性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MemoryDB is a durable, Redis-compatible in-memory database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按对象存取的廉价云存储，容量大但延迟高于内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Blob storage like S3 or R2 stores objects cheaply at higher latency than memory.

optionExplanations: MySQL 落盘最耐久，但磁盘读取撑不住亚 500ms 的核心查询路径。
本地文件简单直接，可惜是单机存储，没法随索引规模水平扩展。
内存读取满足亚 500ms 的核心诉求，持久性短板换成 MemoryDB 之类方案来补。
S3 便宜、容量大，但延迟太高，只适合放冷门数据而非热查询路径。
optionExplanations_en: MySQL on disk is the most durable option, but disk reads can't keep up with the sub-500ms query path.
Local files are simple, but they live on one box and can't scale horizontally as the index grows.
In-memory reads meet the sub-500ms requirement, and a durable variant like MemoryDB covers the persistence gap.
S3 is cheap and huge, but its latency is too high for the hot query path — better suited to cold data.

numberAnchors.risk: 单主写瓶颈、索引/事务变重

q: Redis 倒排索引方案从第一天起就自带哪些挑战？（多选）
q_en: Which challenges come with a Redis inverted-index design from day one?
options: 常见关键词的 post ID 列表会变得非常大
一帖含 10-1000 个关键词，每次发帖要写很多个 key
Redis 完全无法水平扩展
内存存储天生有持久性顾虑
why: 三大隐患：热词列表巨大（后面用截断+冷存储解决）、发帖写放大（用 Kafka+分片解决）、内存持久性（用 MemoryDB 解决）；Redis 本身完全可以通过分片水平扩展。
why_en: Common keywords produce huge ID lists, each post fans out into many key writes, and in-memory storage raises durability concerns.
options_en: Post-ID lists for common keywords grow very large.
A post has 10-1000 keywords, so each post writes many keys.
Redis can't scale horizontally at all.
In-memory storage inherently raises durability concerns.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写在底层被放大成多次物理写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification turns one logical write into many physical writes.

optionExplanations: 热词列表膨胀会拖慢读取、吃光内存，后面得靠截断和冷存储控制。
拆词后一帖变成几十上百次写，是写路径压力的直接来源。
Redis 完全可以按关键词分片水平扩展，这不是它的真实短板。
内存易失意味着宕机可能丢索引，必须换持久化方案兜底。
optionExplanations_en: Hot-keyword lists ballooning drags down reads and eats memory, which later forces caps and cold storage.
Tokenizing one post into dozens or hundreds of writes is the direct source of write-path pressure.
Redis actually scales out fine by sharding on keyword; horizontal scaling isn't its real weakness.
In-memory storage can lose the index on a crash, so it needs a durable fallback.

q: 把「选择倒排索引」的完整决策链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the full decision chain for choosing an inverted index in the correct order:
steps: 代价：每帖拆出几十上百个词、每个词都要写 key；热词的 postId 列表巨大
需求：万亿帖中按关键词亚秒级找到所有匹配帖子
缓解写放大：Kafka 缓冲写入 + 索引按关键词分片
决定性质：查询时全量扫描必死，必须在写入时按查询模式预组织数据
选型：Redis 内存倒排索引（关键词 → postId 列表）
缓解大列表：截断到 1k-10k 条 + 冷词下沉 blob 存储
why: 完整链条 = 需求 → 决定性质（写时预组织）→ 选型（Redis 倒排索引）→ 代价（写放大、大列表）→ 两条缓解各自对应一个代价；两个缓解之间先说哪个都成立。
why_en: The chain runs from the sub-second keyword search requirement, through organizing data at write time, to a Redis inverted index whose write amplification and huge lists are mitigated by buffering, sharding, capping, and cold storage.
diagram:
graph TD
    Scan[Full table scan too slow] --> Inverted[Use inverted index]
    Inverted --> Redis[Fast posting lists]
    Redis --> Challenges[Memory and ranking challenges]
    Challenges --> Tiering[Hot Redis plus cold storage]
tradeoff: 写时预组织 vs 查询时扫描

termDefinitions.meaning: 把每个关键词映射到「包含它的帖子 ID 列表」的字典结构。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inverted index maps each keyword to the list of post IDs that contain it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Redis is an in-memory key-value store used for very fast reads and writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分布式日志/流平台，可分区并行、缓冲突发、持久化事件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Kafka is a distributed log that partitions load and buffers event bursts.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某个键把数据拆到多台机器，分摊写入和存储压力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data across machines by a key to spread load.

q: 「请求时排序」（取出关键词全部 postId → 逐个查时间戳 → 内存排序）有哪些致命问题？（多选）
q_en: What fatal problems come from request-time sorting after fetching all post IDs and timestamps?
options: 热词可能有千万级 postId，索引返回的载荷可达数百 MB
每个 postId 都要一次查找，累计上千万次查询
请求时排序百万级条目，平添不必要的延迟
排序结果一定是错误的
why: 三重打击：网络传输巨量 ID、海量逐条查找、请求时全量排序，500ms 的 SLA 完全无望；结果本身是对的，但代价不可接受。
why_en: Request-time sorting suffers from hundreds of megabytes of IDs, tens of millions of lookups, and expensive in-memory sorts on every query.
options_en: Popular keywords can have tens of millions of post IDs, payloads up to hundreds of MB.
Each post ID needs a lookup — tens of millions of them.
Sorting millions of items at request time adds needless latency.
The sorted result is guaranteed to be wrong.
optionExplanations: 千万级 ID 的载荷光传输就吃掉大量带宽和时间预算。
上千万次逐条查找的延迟叠加起来，远超 500ms 的预算。
把百万条目的排序留到请求时做，等于每次查询都白白多花时间。
排序算法本身没有错，问题全在代价高昂，不在结果对不对。
optionExplanations_en: A payload of tens of millions of IDs alone burns through bandwidth and time budget just being transferred.
Tens of millions of individual lookups stack up latency far past the 500ms budget.
Leaving a million-item sort for request time means every query pays that cost for nothing.
The sorting logic itself isn't wrong; the entire problem is the cost, not correctness.

scenario: 搜索结果必须支持「按最新」和「按点赞数」两种排序，且查询时不能做大规模排序运算。
scenario_en: Search results must support recency and like-count sorting, but queries cannot perform large sorts at request time.
q: 怎么同时支持按时间和按赞数排序，又不在查询时做大排序？
q_en: How do you support both recency and like-count sorting without large query-time sorts?
options: 每次查询后在搜索服务里排序
只支持按时间排序，直接砍掉按赞排序功能
把排序交给客户端处理
每个关键词维护两份预排序索引：按时间、按赞数
why: 用空间换时间：每个关键词同时维护按时间和按赞数两份预排序索引，查询直接取已排序的头部；代价是索引存储翻倍，但换来查询性能的巨大提升。
why_en: Each keyword gets two pre-sorted indexes, one by creation time and one by like count, so queries read already-ordered results.
whenOtherWins: 若数据量小或查询稀少，请求时排序能省下一半索引存储；简单系统未必需要预排序双索引。
options_en: Sort in the search service after each query.
Support only recency sorting and drop like-count sorting.
Offload sorting to the client.
Keep two pre-sorted indexes per keyword: one by time, one by like count.
tradeoff: 索引存储翻倍 vs 查询时零排序

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的普通列表，只在两端追加/读取，天然保留插入顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis list preserves insertion order with cheap appends at the ends.

optionExplanations: 候选可能有百万条，查询时才排序会拖垮延迟。
砍掉按赞排序不满足需求，属于悄悄削减功能而非解决问题。
客户端既没有全量数据也没有算力，排不出正确结果。
空间换时间：查询直接取预排序好的头部，零排序开销。
optionExplanations_en: Candidates can run into the millions, so sorting them at query time wrecks latency.
Dropping like-count sorting fails the requirement — it's quietly cutting a feature, not solving the problem.
The client has neither the full dataset nor the compute to produce a correct order.
Trading space for time: queries just read the already-sorted head, with zero sort cost.

scenario: creation index 只会不断追加新帖，查询永远只取最新的若干条，需要为每个关键词选一个 Redis 结构。
scenario_en: The creation index only appends new posts and queries always take the newest few items, so choose a Redis structure per keyword.
q: 哪组命令符合 creation index 的正确用法？
q_en: Which command pattern is correct for the creation index?
codeSample:
# 发帖时间索引：按到达顺序追加
RPUSH kw:taylor:by_time post123
# 查询：只取列表尾部最新 10 条
LRANGE kw:taylor:by_time -10 -1
options: RPUSH 追加写入；LRANGE 取列表尾部最新 N 条
ZADD 按时间戳写入；ZRANGE 取全量再过滤
SET 每次覆盖写入最新一条
SADD 写入集合；SMEMBERS 全量取出
why: 发帖天然按时间到达，用普通 Redis list 尾部追加即可免费保持时间序；查询只读尾部最新元素，写入和读取都很便宜。
why_en: Posts arrive in time order, so a plain Redis list with tail appends and tail reads keeps the creation index sorted for free.
whenOtherWins: 需要按会变化的分数（点赞数）排序时 list 无能为力，必须换 sorted set 按 score 动态维序。
options_en: RPUSH to append; LRANGE to read the newest N from the tail.
ZADD keyed by timestamp; ZRANGE to read all then filter.
SET to overwrite with the latest one each time.
SADD into a set; SMEMBERS to read everything.
tradeoff: 追加即有序的 list vs 需按分数维序的 sorted set

termDefinitions.meaning: RPUSH 向列表尾部追加，LRANGE 按区间读取列表元素。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RPUSH appends to a list tail and LRANGE reads a range of elements.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的普通列表，只在两端追加/读取，天然保留插入顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis list preserves insertion order with cheap appends at the ends.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

optionExplanations: 发帖天然按时间到达，普通 list 尾部追加免费维持时间序。
sorted set 的按分数维序能力这里用不上，时间序不需要它。
SET 只能存一条，历史帖子全被覆盖丢失。
集合无序，取不出「最新 N 条」这种有顺序的结果。
optionExplanations_en: Posts arrive in time order naturally, so a plain list's tail append keeps that order for free.
A sorted set's score-based ordering is overkill here; time order doesn't need it.
SET holds only one value, so every earlier post gets overwritten and lost.
A set has no order, so it can't produce an ordered 'newest N' result.

scenario: likes index 需要按「会不断变化的点赞数」维持排序，要像优先队列一样支持按分数插入与按名次查询。
scenario_en: The likes index must maintain order by a constantly changing like count, like a priority queue with score updates and ranked reads.
q: 哪组命令符合 likes index 的正确用法？
q_en: Which command pattern is correct for the likes index?
codeSample:
# 点赞事件：给帖子的 score 加 1
ZINCRBY kw:taylor:by_likes 1 post123
# 查询：取点赞最高的前 10
ZREVRANGE kw:taylor:by_likes 0 9
options: RPUSH 命令负责把元素追加到普通列表的尾部
LPUSH 插到普通列表的头部
GET 直接读取一个字符串键
ZINCRBY 加分；ZREVRANGE 取最高前 N
why: Redis sorted set 按 score 维持有序，插入/更新/按名次查询的复杂度与优先队列相当，天然适合「按点赞数排序」的索引。
why_en: A Redis sorted set keeps posts ordered by like-count score, supporting priority-queue-like insertion and ranked queries.
whenOtherWins: 若排序键是不可变的到达时间，普通 list 追加更省内存也更简单。
options_en: RPUSH to append to the tail of a plain list.
LPUSH to prepend to the head of a plain list.
GET to read a single string key.
ZINCRBY to bump the score; ZREVRANGE to read the top-N.
tradeoff: 可变分数维序(sorted set) vs 固定顺序(list)

termDefinitions.meaning: ZINCRBY 给有序集合成员的分数加值，ZREVRANGE 取分数最高的前 N 个。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ZINCRBY increases a member score and ZREVRANGE reads the highest-scoring N.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的普通列表，只在两端追加/读取，天然保留插入顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis list preserves insertion order with cheap appends at the ends.

optionExplanations: 普通列表只能保留插入顺序，赞数一变就没法重新排序。
头插和尾插都只是顺序不同，同样解决不了「按分数排序」。
单个字符串键存不下一份排行结构。
sorted set 每次点赞都能重新排序，天然适合按赞数排名。
optionExplanations_en: A plain list only preserves insertion order; it can't reorder itself when a like count changes.
Head versus tail insertion is just direction — neither solves ordering by a changing score.
A single string key can't hold a ranked structure at all.
A sorted set re-orders on every like, making it the natural fit for ranking by like count.

q: 双索引方案下，发帖和点赞分别触发什么索引操作？
q_en: In the dual-index design, what index operations do posts and likes trigger?
options: 发帖只写 creation；点赞只新增 likes 条目
发帖和点赞都触发全量重建索引
发帖写两份索引(每词)；点赞更新 likes 的 score
发帖和点赞都只修改 likes index
why: 新帖要在它的每个关键词下同时进两份索引（时间序列表 + 赞数 sorted set）；点赞只需给 likes index 对应 score 加一，但高频点赞会带来巨大更新压力。
why_en: A new post is added to both indexes for every keyword it contains, while each like updates the post's score in the likes index.
options_en: A post writes only creation; a like just adds a likes entry.
Both a post and a like trigger a full index rebuild.
A post writes both indexes (per keyword); a like updates that post's score in likes.
Both posts and likes only modify the likes index.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的有序集合，按 score 维持排序，插入和按名次查询都很快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Redis sorted set keeps members ordered by a numeric score.

optionExplanations: 发帖同样要进 likes index（初始分数），漏写了这一份。
全量重建代价高得离谱，双索引方案从不需要整体重建。
新帖进两份索引各自的每个词下，点赞只改 likes 的 score。
发帖时 creation index 同样要写，不能只更新 likes。
optionExplanations_en: A post also needs an initial entry in the likes index, which this option skips.
A full index rebuild would be absurdly expensive; the dual-index design never needs one.
A new post lands in both indexes under every keyword, while a like only bumps the likes score.
Posting still has to write the creation index too — it can't touch only the likes index.

q: 双索引方案的两个代价是？
q_en: What are the two costs of the dual-index design?
options: 存储翻倍 + 高频点赞带来海量 score 更新
查询延迟会明显变慢，且返回结果还不正确
索引无法分片也无法缓存
只支持英文并有内存泄漏
why: 每个关键词存两份索引，存储直接翻倍——为查询性能付的合理学费；更麻烦的是 100k/s 的点赞每个都要更新多个 sorted set，写压力成为必须解决的深挖点。
why_en: The dual indexes double storage and, worse, the heavy stream of likes forces constant score updates that stress the system.
options_en: Storage doubles, and heavy likes cause a flood of score updates.
Queries get slower and results become incorrect.
The index can neither be sharded nor cached.
It only supports English and leaks memory.
optionExplanations: 每个词存两份索引存储直接翻倍，高频点赞还要频繁改分数。
双索引恰恰是为了让查询更快、结果依旧正确，代价不在这里。
分片和缓存跟维护两份索引没有冲突，这不是真实代价。
语言支持和内存泄漏跟这个设计选择完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: Storing two indexes per keyword doubles storage, and heavy likes force constant score updates.
The dual-index design exists precisely to keep queries fast and correct; that's not where the cost lands.
Sharding and caching aren't blocked by maintaining two indexes — that's not a real cost here.
Language support and memory leaks have nothing to do with this design choice.

scenario: 系统无个性化（同一查询人人结果相同），新帖可见性 SLA 为 1 分钟，搜索读流量 10k/s 且可能突发 10 倍。
scenario_en: The system has no personalization, a one-minute freshness SLA, about 10K searches/s, and possible 10x spikes.
q: 应对读流量的第一个显而易见的工具是？
q_en: What is the first obvious tool for handling read traffic?
options: 给每个用户建独立索引
升级更大内存的 Redis 机器
限流拒绝超额请求
结果缓存：先查缓存，未命中再搜索并回填
why: 判断缓存是否合适的两个信号在这全中：能容忍陈旧（1 分钟 SLA）+ 大量重复请求（无个性化），于是在搜索服务旁加分布式结果缓存。
why_en: With duplicate queries and a one-minute staleness budget, a distributed result cache in front of the search path is the obvious first tool.
whenOtherWins: 若结果因人而异（个性化）或必须秒级新鲜，查询级缓存的命中率和正确性都会崩，只能缓存更底层的数据。
options_en: Build a separate index per user.
Upgrade to a Redis box with more memory.
Rate-limit and reject excess requests.
Result cache: check the cache first, only search and backfill on a miss.
tradeoff: 容忍 1 分钟陈旧换高命中缓存 vs 每次实时搜索

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取或重建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL is how long a cached entry lives before it must be refetched.

termDefinitions.meaning: 常用的内存型 key-value 存储，读写在内存里完成、极快。

optionExplanations: 无个性化下人人查询结果相同，按用户建索引是白花的存储。

q: 搜索结果缓存的 TTL 应该设为多少，为什么？
q_en: What TTL should the search-result cache use, and why?
options: 小于 1 分钟——贴着新帖可见 SLA
24 小时——把命中率做到最高
1 秒——尽量保证结果最新鲜
永不过期——运维上最省事
why: TTL 由业务 SLA 反推：新帖必须 1 分钟内可见，缓存最长只能存活不到 1 分钟，这样即使命中旧缓存也不会违反可见性承诺。
why_en: Setting the cache TTL below one minute guarantees cached results never violate the one-minute searchability SLA for new posts.
scenario: 系统无个性化、同查询人人同结果，且新帖必须在 1 分钟内可被搜到。
scenario_en: The system has no personalization, identical results for identical queries, and new posts must be searchable within one minute.
options_en: Under one minute — hugging the new-post visibility SLA.
24 hours — to maximize the hit rate.
1 second — to keep results as fresh as possible.
Never expire — least operational effort.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存条目的存活时间，到期后必须重新获取或重建。

1 秒白白牺牲命中率，1 分钟内的陈旧本就被业务允许。

24 hours blows past the one-minute promise, so a cache hit could be badly out of date.
1 second sacrifices hit rate for nothing — staleness up to a minute is already allowed.
Never lapsing means a new post could stay unsearchable forever, breaking the SLA outright.

scenario: 全球用户都在搜索相同的热门查询，希望命中时几十毫秒返回，最好请求还没进你的机房就被消化掉。

q: 在 Redis 结果缓存之外还能加什么？
q_en: What can you add on top of the Redis result cache?
options: 再多加几台无状态的搜索服务实例做横向扩容
CDN 边缘缓存：就近节点缓存 /search 响应
让客户端不停地轮询并重试
给数据库多加几个只读副本
why: CDN 本质是一片地理分布的 HTTP 缓存：配好源站和 DNS，命中时用户在本地边缘节点几十毫秒拿到结果，未命中才回源走完整链路。

CDN edge cache: geographically local nodes cache the /search response.
Have clients keep polling and retrying.
Add several read replicas to the database.

scenario: 想让 CDN 缓存 /search 的响应以吸收重复查询，同时不能违反新帖 1 分钟可见的 SLA。

q: 下面哪个响应头设置是正确做法？
q_en: Which response-header setting is correct?
codeSample:
GET /search?q=taylor+swift&sort=likes

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Cache-Control: public, max-age=59
Content-Type: application/json

{ "results": ["..."] }

Cache-Control: public, max-age=59

why: public 允许共享缓存（CDN）存储，max-age=59 让缓存寿命 <1 分钟、贴着 SLA 上限拿最高命中率；no-store 直接放弃缓存，3600 秒则违反 SLA。
why_en: Marking the response public with a max-age just under sixty seconds lets the CDN cache aggressively while still honoring the one-minute freshness SLA.
whenOtherWins: 若响应包含用户私有数据应改用 private 或 no-store，宁可牺牲命中率也不能把私有结果发给别人。
options_en: Set Cache-Control: no-store.
Set Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600.
Set Cache-Control: public, max-age=59.
Set Expires: never.
tradeoff: public 高命中(共享缓存) vs private/no-store 保私密但少缓存

q: CDN 边缘命中 vs 完整回源链路（网关 → 搜索服务 → 结果缓存 → 返回）的延迟量级对比是？

options: 两者都在几毫秒级
边缘命中反而更慢
两者延迟都超过整整 1 秒钟
边缘命中几十毫秒，完整链路要几百毫秒
why: 边缘节点物理上离用户近，命中时几十毫秒返回；老老实实穿过 API 网关、搜索服务、结果缓存再回来则要几百毫秒——一个数量级的差距。
why_en: A CDN edge hit returns in tens of milliseconds versus the hundreds of milliseconds needed to traverse the full gateway, service, and cache path.
scenario: 一次搜索要么命中地理就近的 CDN 边缘，要么回源穿过网关→搜索服务→结果缓存再返回。
scenario_en: A search either hits a nearby CDN edge or goes back through gateway, search service, result cache, and response path.
options_en: Both are in the low-millisecond range.
An edge hit is actually slower.
Both exceed one second.
An edge hit is tens of ms; the full path is hundreds of ms.

termDefinitions.meaning: 地理分布的 HTTP 缓存网络，命中时在离用户最近的边缘节点返回。

q: 把「交集法」回答 Taylor Swift 短语查询的步骤排成正确顺序：
q_en: Put the intersection-method steps for answering a Taylor Swift phrase query in the correct order:
steps: 拉取候选帖原文，验证确实包含连续短语 Taylor Swift，而不是 Taylor made a swift exit 这种散装匹配
分别取出 Taylor 和 Swift 两个关键词的 postId 列表
把通过验证的帖子按排序要求返回
求两个列表的交集，得到同时含两个词的 postId
why: 交集法四步：取各词列表 → 求交 → 原文验证短语连续性（过滤「碰巧都含这两个词」的假阳性）→ 返回；不改索引结构，是侵入最小的多词方案。
why_en: Fetch each keyword's post list, intersect them, verify the actual phrase appears contiguously in the post text, and return the survivors in order.

graph LR
    Query[Taylor Swift] --> T1[term taylor]
    Query --> T2[term swift]
    T1 --> Intersect[Intersect postIds]
    T2 --> Intersect
    Intersect --> Verify[Fetch text and verify phrase]
    Verify --> Rank[Rank results]
tradeoff: 不改索引(交集法) vs 改索引(bigram)

q: 交集法处理短语查询的最大痛点是？
q_en: What is the biggest pain point when using intersection for phrase queries?
options: 无法返回正确结果
Redis 本身并不支持集合求交运算
热词集合极大，传输与求交贵，难赶 500ms
只能支持两个词的查询
why: 两个热词各有百万级 postId 时，光传输和求交就可能吃掉整个延迟预算；更糟的是若两词常同帖出现但不构成短语，过滤环节的计算全部白费。
why_en: Popular keywords yield huge ID sets that are expensive to transfer and intersect within the latency budget, and overlapping but nonadjacent words force wasteful filtering.
options_en: It can't return correct results.
Redis doesn't support set operations.
Popular keywords have huge sets — transfer and intersection are costly, hard within 500ms.
It only supports two-word queries.

Transferring and intersecting millions of post IDs alone eats the latency budget, putting 500ms at risk.

scenario: Taylor Swift 这类高频短语查询要避开昂贵的交集运算，希望一次索引查找直接命中。
scenario_en: For frequent phrase queries like Taylor Swift, you want one index lookup instead of expensive set intersection.
q: 应该怎么改进索引？
q_en: How should you improve the index?
options: 索引 bigram/shingle：相邻词对当 key
把一整句完整的话原样当成唯一的索引 key
改用正则表达式在查询时扫全表
缩短每个索引列表的最大长度

why_en: Indexing bigrams or shingles lets a phrase query hit the Taylor Swift key directly instead of intersecting two huge single-word lists.
whenOtherWins: 索引体积敏感、或短语查询占比很低时，交集法不增加任何索引膨胀，更划算。

q: 补全 bigram 切分示例：
q_en: Fill in the bigram tokenization example:
text: 句子 I saw Taylor Swift at the concert 会切出 I saw、saw Taylor、{{Taylor Swift}}、Swift at 等相邻词对；这种 token 在 Lucene 术语里叫 {{shingles}}。

q: 引入 bigram 索引的主要代价是？
q_en: What is the main cost of adding a bigram index?
options: 短语查询反而变得更慢
索引键爆炸：词对稀疏，key 可能涨一个数量级
bigram 索引无法与单词索引共存并用

why_en: Bigrams are far more unique than single words, so the index can balloon from ten million keys to over a hundred million.
options_en: Phrase queries actually get slower.
Key explosion: bigrams are sparse, so keys can grow by an order of magnitude.
Bigrams can't coexist with single-word indexes.
Like scores can no longer be updated.

scenario: bigram 索引膨胀太贵，你想只为「真的会被搜到」的短语付出索引成本。
scenario_en: A full bigram index is too expensive, so you only want to pay index cost for phrases people actually search.
q: 合理的折衷方案是？
q_en: What is a reasonable compromise?
options: 彻底放弃短语查询
把所有 bigram 都直接存 S3

每天全量重建一次索引

why_en: Index only the popular bigrams identified with a probabilistic counter like count-min sketch, and fall back to intersection for the rare ones.
whenOtherWins: 若存储预算充足且短语查询延迟至上，全量 bigram 索引更简单，也没有回退路径带来的复杂度。
options_en: Abandon phrase queries entirely.
Dump all bigrams straight into S3.
Index only popular bigrams; fall back to intersection for the rest.
Fully rebuild the whole index daily.
tradeoff: 索引膨胀 vs 命中率——只为高频短语付索引成本

q: 为什么说发帖在索引侧存在「写放大」？
q_en: Why does posting create write amplification on the index side?

Redis 会自动把数据复制成三份副本
每帖都要重建全量索引
每帖拆成 10-100+ 个词，每词一次索引写
why: 倒排索引把一次发帖放大成「每个关键词一次写」，双索引下还要乘 2；10k 帖/秒的创建流量在索引层就成了百万级写/秒的压力源。
why_en: Tokenization fans a single hundred-word post out into a hundred or more index writes, massively amplifying the write load.
options_en: Every post must be written synchronously to primary and replica.
Redis automatically replicates data three times.
Every post rebuilds the whole index.
Each post splits into 10-100+ keywords, one index write each.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一次逻辑写在底层被放大成多次物理写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification turns one logical write into many physical writes.
