把模糊死连接变成明确断线
补拉 Inbox 里仍 pending 的消息

codeSample:
serverDeliver(clientId, msg):
  ws.send(msg)
  if no ACK before timeout:
    retry a few times
  if still no ACK:
    ws.close()  # make the stale connection obvious

clientOnClose():
  reconnectWithBackoff()
  authenticate(userId, clientId)
  syncPendingFromInbox()
optionExplanations: 只等 TCP 超时是分钟级发现，跟这里想要的「投递当口就发现」目标不符。
盲发两遍掩盖不了死连接问题，还会让在线用户收到重复消息。
对：发消息后等 ACK，超时重试几次仍失败就断开逼客户端重连，复用了已有的 ack 机制。
把所有弱网用户都降级轮询，牺牲了这部分用户本该有的实时性，代价过大。
optionExplanations_en: Waiting only for TCP timeout means minute-scale detection, which doesn't match the goal of catching failures right when delivering.
Blindly sending twice doesn't fix stale-connection detection and also risks duplicate messages for online users.
Right: send, wait for ack, retry a few times on timeout, then close and force a reconnect — reusing the existing ack mechanism.
Downgrading every poor-network user to polling sacrifices real-time delivery for that whole group, too high a cost.

q: 「只靠投递 ACK 超时」检测死连接的盲区是？
q_en: What is the blind spot of detecting dead connections purely from delivery ACK timeouts?
options: ACK 报文太大浪费带宽
会频繁误杀健康连接
认为服务器内存不够存放大量定时器
安静期挂掉时发现不了，要等下条消息才暴露
options_en: The ACK payload is too large and wastes bandwidth
It frequently kills healthy connections by mistake
Assumes the server runs out of memory holding that many timers
A connection that dies during a quiet period goes unnoticed until the next message
why: 投递超时是「被动」检测：没有消息就没有探测。真正的时间上界要靠主动心跳来给。
why_en: Delivery-based detection only works while sending, so a connection that dies during a quiet period goes unnoticed until the next message.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ack is the confirmation signal a client sends back after receiving a message.

optionExplanations: ACK 报文本身很小，带宽不是这个机制的盲区所在。
超时阈值设置合理时不会频繁误杀，这不是「靠投递 ACK」这个机制固有的局限。
定时器占用内存很小，不是这个机制真正的瓶颈。
对：安静期没有消息可发就没有探测动作，死连接要等下一条消息才会暴露。
optionExplanations_en: The ACK payload itself is tiny; bandwidth isn't this mechanism's blind spot.
With a reasonable timeout it won't falsely kill healthy connections often — that's not this mechanism's inherent limitation.
A timer uses negligible memory, not the real bottleneck here.
Right: with no message to send during a quiet period, there's no probe at all, so a dead connection only surfaces when the next message arrives.

scenario: 需要给死连接检测一个有保证的时间上界，即使会话完全安静也能触发。
scenario_en: You need a guaranteed upper bound on dead-connection detection time, one that still fires even if the conversation is completely silent.
q: 标准方案是？
q_en: What is the standard solution?
options: 服务器定时 ping，超时不回 pong 即断开
每分钟强制重建所有连接
要求客户端每秒上报一次完整状态全量数据
依赖运营商网络事件通知
options_en: The server pings on a timer, and a missed pong closes it
Force-rebuild every connection once a minute
Requires the client to report its full state every second
Rely on carrier network failure notifications
why: 主动心跳把“等消息时才发现”改成定时探测，死连接可在秒级被关闭。它通常走同一条 WebSocket 的 ping/pong 控制帧或小型应用消息，不是额外 REST 调用；重连后仍靠 Inbox sync 兜底。
why_en: Active heartbeats probe on a timer over the existing WebSocket, so quiet dead sockets are closed within seconds and reconnect plus Inbox sync handles missed messages.
whenOtherWins: 如果能接受「只在发消息时才发现死连接」的弱实时场景，仅用投递 ACK 超时可以省掉这份心跳流量。
tradeoff: 有保证的检测时间上界 vs 心跳带来的额外探测流量
diagram:
graph LR
    Server[Chat server] --> Ping[WebSocket ping or app ping]
    Ping --> Client[Client]
    Client --> Pong[Return pong]
    Pong --> Alive[Keep connection]
    Ping --> Timeout[Timeout closes stale connection]

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测消息，用来确认对方仍然存活；在聊天系统里通常跑在现有 WebSocket/TCP 连接上。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small periodic probe message used to confirm the other side is still alive; in chat systems it usually runs over the existing WebSocket/TCP connection.

termDefinitions.meaning: WebSocket 协议自带的控制帧，不需要另开一个 HTTP/REST 请求。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: WebSocket ping/pong are protocol-level control frames and do not require a separate HTTP/REST request.

termDefinitions.meaning: 业务协议自己定义的小消息，例如 {type: "ping"} 和 {type: "pong"}；可以顺带携带 latestSeq 等业务字段。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Application-level ping/pong are small messages defined by the business protocol, such as {type: "ping"} and {type: "pong"}; they can carry business fields such as latestSeq.

termDefinitions.meaning: 通常是一来一回的 HTTP 请求/响应。WebSocket 长连接已经存在时，用 REST 做高频心跳通常更重。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A REST API is usually an HTTP request/response. When a WebSocket is already open, using REST for frequent heartbeats is usually heavier.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of messages that have not yet been delivered.

optionExplanations: 对：服务器定时 ping、超时不回 pong 就断开，把「等消息才发现」改成「定时探测」，给出确定的时间上界。
每分钟强制重建全部连接是粗暴的一刀切，代价远超它要解决的问题。
每秒全量上报状态的负载随在线人数线性增长，会自己先把系统压垮。
依赖运营商网络事件通知既不可控也不通用，不是可以设计进系统的机制。
optionExplanations_en: Right: the server pings on a timer and closes on a missed pong — turning "only discover when a message arrives" into "discover on a schedule," with a guaranteed upper bound.
Force-rebuilding every connection every minute is a blunt hammer whose cost far outweighs the problem it solves.
Full-state reporting every second from everyone scales load linearly with online users and would overload the system on its own.
Relying on carrier network notifications isn't controllable or portable — not something you can design into the system.

scenario: 心跳间隔设为 10 秒、pong 超时设为 5 秒。
scenario_en: The heartbeat interval is set to ten seconds and the pong timeout to five seconds.
q: 补全心跳检测上界的算式：
q_en: Fill in the formula for the heartbeat detection upper bound:
text: 心跳间隔 {{10}} 秒、pong 超时 {{5}} 秒时，任何死连接最迟 {{15}} 秒内被发现——心跳给出的是检测时间的保证上界。
why: 上界 = 间隔 + 超时(最坏是连接刚回完 pong 就死，要等近一个间隔才发下次 ping、再等满超时)。两个旋钮管不同的事：间隔换「检测速度↔ping 流量」，超时换「容忍网络抖动不误杀↔检测延迟」，所以超时通常明显小于间隔。10/5/15 是可调示例，不是圣旨。
why_en: Upper bound = interval + timeout (worst case: the connection dies right after a pong, so you wait nearly a full interval before the next ping, then the full timeout). Two knobs tune different things: interval trades detection speed vs ping traffic; timeout trades tolerating jitter (no false kills) vs detection delay — so timeout is usually well below the interval. 10/5/15 are tunable examples, not sacred.

rows: 死连接赖着占内存、presence 不新鲜
流量预算 + presence 新鲜度
误杀只是暂时慢的健康连接→重连风暴
最坏 RTT + 网络抖动(≈几倍 RTT)

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

termDefinitions.meaning: RTT=一个包往返一趟的时间;抖动=RTT 的忽大忽小。pong 超时必须吃得下最坏 RTT+抖动,否则会把「活着但暂时慢」的连接误判为死。移动网 RTT 可从几十 ms 抖到 1s+,所以 5s 超时是留了余量的。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RTT is the time for one packet to make a round trip; jitter is the variance in RTT. The pong timeout must absorb worst-case RTT+jitter, or it will misjudge a "live but slow" connection as dead. Mobile RTT can swing from tens of ms to 1s+, so a 5s timeout leaves headroom.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把一条其实还活着的连接判成死的、强行关掉。代价:客户端被迫重连 + 重新 sync Inbox,大量同时误杀会造成重连风暴/负载尖峰。所以 pong 超时宁可设宽一点也别贪快。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A false positive: declaring a still-alive connection dead and closing it. Cost: the client must reconnect and re-sync its Inbox; many simultaneous false kills cause a reconnect storm / load spike. So the pong timeout is set generously rather than aggressively short.

tradeoff: 间隔:小=检测快但 ping 流量大 / 大=省流量但死连接赖着; 超时:小=检测快但误杀慢连接 / 大=不误杀但确认死亡慢

scenario: 2 亿在线用户，心跳间隔设为 10 秒。
scenario_en: There are two hundred million online users, with a ten-second heartbeat interval.
q: 由此算出的 ping/pong 交换量级，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Which conclusion does the resulting ping/pong exchange rate most directly support?
options: 算下来约 20 亿次/秒，远超任何基础设施能承受的范围，心跳机制不可行
算下来小到可以忽略，不需要为心跳做任何容量规划
这个量级只取决于消息大小，与在线用户数无关
算下来约 2000 万次/秒——量大但每条都是几字节的小消息，实践中可以接受
options_en: It comes out to about two billion a second, far beyond what any infrastructure could bear, making heartbeats infeasible
It comes out small enough to ignore entirely, no capacity planning needed for heartbeats
The figure depends only on message size, not on the number of online users
It comes out to about twenty million a second — a big number, but each message is only a few bytes, which is acceptable in practice
why: 200M / 10s = 2000 万次/秒的 ping/pong。说出这个数字并解释「消息极小所以没问题」，比回避它更加分。
why_en: Two hundred million connections on a ten-second interval means about twenty million tiny ping-pong exchanges per second, which is acceptable in practice.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

optionExplanations: 20 亿次/秒的量级算错了单位换算，实际远没有这么夸张。
量级不能忽略——2 亿 / 10 秒是个真实需要评估的数字，不能跳过容量规划。
这个量级恰恰主要由在线用户数决定（除以心跳间隔），跟消息大小无关。
对：约 2000 万次/秒，量大但每条都是几字节的小消息，实践中可以接受。
optionExplanations_en: 20 billion/sec comes from a unit-conversion mistake; the real number is nowhere near that.
The magnitude can't be waved away — 200M / 10s is a real number that needs capacity planning, not something to skip.
This figure is mainly driven by online user count divided by heartbeat interval, not by message size.
Right: about 20 million/sec — large in count but each message is only a few bytes, which is acceptable in practice.

scenario: Pub/Sub 尽力而为可能漏推，需要给已连接客户端一个最朴素的兜底手段拿回漏掉的消息。
scenario_en: Pub/Sub's best-effort delivery can drop a push; connected clients need the simplest possible backstop for recovering a missed message.
q: 这个兜底方案是？
q_en: What is that backstop mechanism?
options: 客户端重启即可
直接信任 Pub/Sub 绝不会丢消息，跳过兜底设计
客户端定时发 sync 请求，服务器补发未投递消息
每天凌晨做一次全量同步
options_en: Just have the client restart
Simply trusts Pub/Sub to never lose a message and skips a fallback altogether
Clients periodically send a sync request and the server pushes undelivered messages
Run one full sync for everyone at midnight
why: Pub/Sub 丢的是实时提醒，不是消息本体。发送路径先写 Message+Inbox 再推送；没 ack 的 Inbox row 留着，之后由 sync、重连、序号缺口或心跳补回来。
why_en: Pub/Sub can lose a realtime notification, but Message and Inbox remain durable until ACK, so sync, reconnect, sequence gaps, or heartbeats can recover it.
codeSample:
sendMessage(msg):
  db.put(Message[msg.id] = msg)
  db.put(Inbox[receiverId, msg.id] = PENDING)
  pubsub.publish(userChannel(receiverId), msg.id)  # best effort

sync(receiverId):
  pending = db.query(Inbox where receiverId and status = PENDING)
  sendOverWebSocket(pending)

ack(receiverId, msgId):
  db.delete(Inbox[receiverId, msgId])  # or mark DELIVERED
whenOtherWins: 想要秒级发现丢失得靠序号 + 心跳组合；轮询间隔越短负载越高，它更适合当最后一道防线。
tradeoff: 轮询兜底覆盖全场景 vs 轮询间隔在延迟与负载之间的取舍

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个接收者保存未投递消息的持久化队列；没有收到 ack 前，记录会留在这里等待补发。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An inbox is a durable per-recipient queue of undelivered messages; until an ACK arrives, the row stays pending for redelivery.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端收到消息后回给服务器的确认信号；服务器据此删除或标记已投递的 Inbox 记录。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ACK is the client confirmation after receiving a message; the server uses it to delete or mark the inbox row as delivered.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端主动向服务器询问自己还有哪些未收到消息；它牺牲一点延迟和查询成本，换来漏推后的补发能力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sync is the client asking the server for messages it has not received; it trades extra latency and query load for recovery after a missed push.

rows: 无人订阅/故障时用户可能暂时看不到
未 ack 就保留，sync/重连时补发

optionExplanations: 客户端重启不会主动补回漏掉的消息，问题依旧存在。
信任 Pub/Sub 不会丢消息违背了它 at-most-once 的语义，风险仍在。
对：客户端定时发 sync 请求，服务器查 Inbox 补发未投递消息，是最朴素也最兜底的方式。
每天一次全量同步间隔太长，白天丢的消息要等到凌晨才补回，达不到兜底应有的及时性。
optionExplanations_en: Restarting the client doesn't actively pull back missed messages; the problem is still there.
Trusting Pub/Sub never to lose anything contradicts its at-most-once semantics — the risk is still real.
Right: the client periodically sends a sync request and the server checks the Inbox for anything undelivered — the simplest, most reliable fallback.
A once-a-day full sync is too infrequent; a message missed in the morning wouldn't be recovered until the next sync, too slow for a real fallback.

scenario: 2 亿在线用户，如果都采用每 30 秒一次的 sync 轮询兜底。
scenario_en: Two hundred million online users all use a thirty-second sync-polling backstop.
q: 由此算出的轮询负载量级，最支持下面哪个结论？
q_en: Which conclusion does the resulting polling load most directly support?
options: 算下来只有约 7 千次查询/秒，负载小到可以把轮询直接当主力投递机制
算下来约 700 万次查询/秒，轮询只能当兜底不能当主力，拉长间隔要用延迟换
算下来约 7 亿次查询/秒，说明这个方案在任何规模下都不可行
算出来的负载与在线用户数无关，只取决于消息大小
options_en: It comes out to only about seven thousand queries a second, small enough to make polling the primary delivery mechanism
About 7M queries/sec — polling can only be a fallback, not the primary path; lengthening the interval trades away latency
It comes out to about seven hundred million queries a second, meaning this approach is infeasible at any scale
The resulting load has nothing to do with the number of online users, only message size
why: 200M / 30s ≈ 700 万 QPS，全是「查一下有没有漏」的开销。这正是纯轮询只能做兜底、不能做主力的原因。
why_en: Two hundred million clients polling every thirty seconds adds about seven million sync queries per second, trading load against latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每秒查询/请求数，用来衡量系统吞吐的常用单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: QPS measures how many queries or requests a system handles each second.

optionExplanations: 7 千次/秒的量级算小了近千倍，不能把轮询直接当主力投递机制。
对：把在线人数除以轮询间隔，得到的量级只能当兜底，不能顶替主力投递路径。
7 亿次/秒把量级又算大了百倍，不是这道估算的正确结果。
负载明显取决于在线用户数和轮询间隔，跟消息大小无关这个说法不成立。
optionExplanations_en: 7k/sec understates this by nearly a thousand-fold; polling can't be treated as the primary delivery mechanism at that estimate.
Right: 200M / 30s ≈ 7M QPS — pure polling can only be a fallback; lengthening the interval trades latency for lower load.
700M/sec overstates this by roughly a hundred-fold — not the correct result of this estimate.
Load clearly scales with online user count and poll interval, so "independent of user count" doesn't hold.

q: 每个 chat 一个单调递增序号，客户端如何用它发现漏消息？
q_en: With one monotonically increasing sequence number per chat, how does the client use it to detect a missed message?
options: 序号用于端到端加密，和漏消息无关
认为序号只是驱动 UI 排序动画，纯展示层用途
服务器按序号做负载均衡，与客户端无关
客户端记本地最后序号，跳号即知有漏，立刻请求重新同步
options_en: The sequence number is used for end-to-end encryption, unrelated to missed messages
Treats the sequence number as purely a display-layer detail driving sort animation
The server load-balances based on the sequence number, unrelated to the client
The client tracks its last local sequence number; a gap means a miss, and it immediately requests a resync
why: 序号让「丢失」变得可观测：缺口即证据。生成端用 Redis INCR 这类原子自增即可，成本极低。
why_en: Clients track the last sequence number seen, so receiving number five right after three reveals the missing four and triggers a resync.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条消息带的单调递增编号，客户端靠比对编号发现是否漏收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number is a monotonically increasing id on each message that lets a client spot gaps by comparing numbers.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令，单步完成「读取当前值并加一」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is a Redis command that atomically reads a counter and increments it in a single step.

codeSample:
# Redis: atomic monotonically-increasing sequence per chat
INCR seq:chat:456          # returns the next sequence number, e.g. 42

# Client tracks lastSeq locally; a gap in incoming seq means a miss.
# lastSeq = 41, next message arrives with seq = 43 -> seq 42 is missing,
# so the client immediately requests a resync instead of waiting.
optionExplanations: 序号是明文的自增计数器，跟加密算法完全不搭边。
排序动画属于展示细节，序号真正的作用是让丢失变得可观测。
序号由生成端 INCR 得到，跟负载均衡策略是两回事。
对：客户端记 lastSeq，收到更大的 seq 却跳号，缺口本身就是「漏消息」的证据，立刻请求同步。
optionExplanations_en: The sequence number is a plain incrementing counter, unrelated to any encryption scheme.
Sort animation is a display detail; the real point of the sequence number is making loss observable.
The sequence number comes from an INCR at the sender side, a separate concern from load-balancing policy.
Right: the client tracks lastSeq, and a gap when a higher seq arrives is itself the evidence of a missed message, triggering an immediate resync.

q: 「靠序号缺口发现丢失」这个机制的固有局限是？
q_en: What is the inherent limitation of detecting loss purely from sequence-number gaps?
options: 序号很快就会溢出
INCR 不是原子操作
缺口要等下条消息才能发现，安静期会一直漏
认为客户端无法把序号持久化保存下来
options_en: The sequence number overflows quickly
INCR is not an atomic operation
A gap is only discovered when the next message arrives; a quiet period keeps leaking
Assumes the client has no way to persist the sequence number
why: 缺口检测是被动的：客户端要先看到更大的新序号，才知道中间漏了。若 lastSeq=3、seq=4 丢后一直安静，客户端不会发现；所以要用心跳带 latestSeq 或周期 sync 兜底。
why_en: Gap detection is passive because the client needs a later sequence to see the hole, so quiet periods require latestSeq in heartbeats or periodic sync.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条消息带的单调递增编号，客户端靠比对编号发现是否漏收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number is a monotonically increasing id on each message that lets a client spot gaps by comparing numbers.

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令，单步完成「读取当前值并加一」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is a Redis command that atomically reads a counter and increments it in a single step.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端和服务器定期互发的小消息，用来确认连接还活着；如果顺带携带最新序号，就能在没有新聊天消息时也发现客户端落后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small periodic ping between client and server to prove the connection is alive; if it carries the latest sequence number, the client can detect lag even when no new chat message arrives.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端发现自己序号落后或定时兜底时，请求服务器按 Inbox 补发未收到消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sync is the client asking the server to replay missing messages from the Inbox after it detects lag or as a periodic backstop.

rows: 要靠心跳带 latestSeq 或定时 sync

codeSample:
# Gap detection is passive: it only fires when a *later* message arrives.
# lastSeq = 3, seq 4 is lost, and the chat stays quiet -> no new seq ever
# arrives, so the client never learns seq 4 was missed.
INCR seq:chat:456   # seq 4 generated, published, then lost in transit
# ... silence ...    # client is stuck at lastSeq=3 with no trigger to resync
optionExplanations: 序号量级远小于溢出门槛，溢出不是这个机制的真正短板。
INCR 对单个 Redis key 恰恰是原子的，这不是缺口检测的问题所在。
对：缺口检测是被动的，客户端要先看到更大的新序号才知道中间漏了，安静期发现不了。
本地持久化 lastSeq 是实现细节，跟「缺口要靠后续消息触发」这个根本局限无关。
optionExplanations_en: Sequence numbers stay well below any overflow threshold, so overflow isn't this mechanism's real weakness.
INCR is in fact atomic for a single Redis key, so that isn't the flaw behind gap detection.
Right: gap detection is passive — the client only learns about a miss once a larger new sequence number arrives, so a quiet period hides it indefinitely.
Persisting lastSeq locally is an implementation detail, unrelated to the core limitation that a gap needs a later message to surface it.

scenario: 想在几乎不新增负载的前提下，把漏推检测的时间压进一个心跳周期。
scenario_en: You want to compress missed-push detection time down to roughly one heartbeat interval while adding almost no extra load.
q: 文中的组合方案是？
q_en: What is the article's combined solution?
options: 把心跳间隔缩短到 1 秒
维护每用户全局序号，捎带在心跳 ping 里发现落后
让 Redis Pub/Sub 升级成 at-least-once
取消轮询、全信心跳
options_en: Shorten the heartbeat interval to 1 second
Keep one global sequence per user and piggyback it on heartbeat pings to detect lag
Upgrade Redis Pub/Sub to at-least-once delivery
Drop polling entirely and trust heartbeats alone
why: 组合方案：每个 user 维护全局 seq，latestSeq 捎带进已有心跳。客户端发现 latestSeq > lastSeq 就 sync Inbox，额外负载只是心跳多一个数字。
why_en: Piggyback latestSeq on existing heartbeats; if it is greater than the client's lastSeq, the client syncs the Inbox, paying only one small payload field plus a per-user counter.
whenOtherWins: 没有心跳基础设施、或不想为原子计数器加依赖时，单纯拉长间隔的轮询更简单，只是发现丢失更慢。
tradeoff: 心跳捎带序号，近零额外成本 vs 引入原子计数器这个新依赖
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as Sender path
    participant R as Redis counter
    participant I as Message + Inbox
    participant P as Pub/Sub push
    participant C as Client
    S->>R: INCR seq:user:123 -> 42
    S->>I: store msgId with userSeq=42
    S-->>P: publish msgId, seq=42
    P--xC: realtime push may be missed
    Note over C: local lastSeq is still 41
    S-->>C: heartbeat ping { latestSeq: 42 }
    C->>C: latestSeq > lastSeq, detect lag
    C->>I: sync missing/pending messages
    I-->>C: msgId, seq=42, chatId, body
    C->>C: apply, persist lastSeq=42, ack
codeSample:
# Send path: assign one global sequence per recipient user
sendMessage(toUserId, chatId, body):
  seq = redis.incr(f"seq:user:{toUserId}")
  msgId = newId()
  Message.put(chatId=chatId, msgId=msgId, userSeq=seq, body=body)
  for clientId in Clients.query(toUserId):
    Inbox.put(clientId=clientId, msgId=msgId, chatId=chatId, userSeq=seq, status="PENDING")
  redis.publish(f"user:{toUserId}", { "msgId": msgId, "seq": seq })

# Existing heartbeat: add latestSeq to the ping payload
sendHeartbeat(userId, ws):
  latestSeq = getLatestSeq(userId)  # Redis GET, local cache, or replicated presence state
  ws.send({ "type": "ping", "latestSeq": latestSeq })

# Client side: detect missed pushes without waiting for the next chat message
onMessage(msg):
  if msg.seq > local.lastSeq + 1:
    syncInbox(fromSeq=local.lastSeq + 1, toSeq=msg.seq - 1)
  apply(msg)
  local.lastSeq = max(local.lastSeq, msg.seq)
  ack(msg.msgId)

onHeartbeatPing(latestSeq):
  if latestSeq > local.lastSeq:
    syncInbox(fromSeq=local.lastSeq + 1, toSeq=latestSeq)
  sendPong({ "lastSeq": local.lastSeq })

syncInbox(fromSeq, toSeq):
  rows = Inbox.query(clientId=local.clientId, userSeqBetween=[fromSeq, toSeq])
  for row in rows:
    msg = Message.get(row.chatId, row.msgId)
    apply(msg)
    ack(row.msgId)

termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small periodic probe used to confirm the other side is alive; here it also carries latestSeq so the client can detect missed pushes during quiet periods.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发给某个 user 的每条消息带的单调递增编号。客户端保存 lastSeq，和心跳里的 latestSeq 比较即可知道自己是否落后。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number is a monotonically increasing id on messages sent to a user. The client stores lastSeq and compares it with latestSeq in heartbeats to know whether it is behind.

termDefinitions.meaning: 服务端认为这个 user 最新应该看到的序号。它可以来自 Redis 计数器、连接状态缓存或专门的 presence/sequence 状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: latestSeq is the newest sequence the server believes this user should have seen. It can come from a Redis counter, connection-state cache, or dedicated presence/sequence state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端本地已经成功应用并持久化的最大序号。latestSeq 大于 lastSeq 时，说明有消息可能漏了，需要 sync。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: lastSeq is the largest sequence the client has successfully applied and persisted. If latestSeq is greater than lastSeq, some messages may be missing and the client should sync.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

optionExplanations: 缩短心跳间隔能加快发现，但代价是心跳负载线性上升，不是这里说的「组合方案」。
对：per-user 全局 seq 捎带进心跳的 latestSeq 字段，客户端一比较就知道该不该 sync。
Redis Pub/Sub 升级成 at-least-once 需要它自己持久化和重试，这不是本题给出的方案。
完全取消轮询会丢掉最后一道兜底，跟「组合」的意思相反——三种机制是互补而不是二选一。
optionExplanations_en: Shortening the heartbeat interval speeds up discovery but scales heartbeat load linearly — not what "the combined approach" means here.
Right: a per-user global sequence rides along in the existing heartbeat as latestSeq; the client just compares it against lastSeq to decide whether to sync.
Upgrading Redis Pub/Sub to at-least-once would need it to persist and retry on its own — not what this design does.
Dropping polling entirely removes the last-resort fallback, the opposite of "combined" — the three mechanisms complement each other rather than replace one another.

scenario: 要为每个用户维护全局单调递增的消息序号（发往该用户的每条消息 +1），用于漏消息检测，且并发下不能出错。
scenario_en: You need a globally monotonically increasing message sequence number per user (incremented for every message sent to them) for miss detection, and it must be correct under concurrency.
q: 用哪条 Redis 命令原子地生成下一个序号？
q_en: Which Redis command atomically generates the next sequence number?
options: GET seq:user:123 之后再 SET 加一
INCR seq:user:123
EXPIRE seq:user:123 60
PUBLISH seq:user:123 next
options_en: GET seq:user:123 and then SET it plus one
INCR seq:user:123
EXPIRE seq:user:123 60
PUBLISH seq:user:123 next
why: GET+SET 是两步读改写，并发下可能撞号；INCR 对单个 Redis key 原子自增并返回新值。它只保证单命令单 key，不等于多 key 事务，也不保证故障切换绝不回退。
why_en: GET plus SET can race, while INCR atomically increments one Redis key and returns a unique value; it is not a multi-key transaction or failover guarantee.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要会话内定序，可按 chat 计数（INCR seq:chat:456）；全局用户序号的优势是一个数字覆盖该用户所有会话的丢失检测。
tradeoff: INCR 单 key 原子自增 vs GET+SET 两步读改写的竞态风险
codeSample:
# 每有一条消息发往 user 123：
INCR seq:user:123    # 单 key 原子自增，返回新序号
# 并发调用会排队执行，不会返回同一个数字
# 心跳 ping 里捎带当前序号，客户端对比本地值，落后即请求同步

termDefinitions.meaning: Redis 的原子自增命令，单步完成「读取当前值并加一」。它保证单个 key 的并发自增不会撞号，但不负责多 key 原子事务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: INCR is a Redis command that atomically reads and increments one counter. It prevents duplicate numbers for concurrent increments on one key, but it is not a multi-key atomic transaction.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条消息带的单调递增编号，客户端靠比对编号发现是否漏收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number is a monotonically increasing id on each message that lets a client spot gaps by comparing numbers.

GET 后 SET 再加一
不保证；两步之间会竞态
同时更新 seq:user 和另一张表
不保证；需要事务、Lua 或换存储设计
Redis 主从切换后绝不回退
不单靠 INCR 保证；要看持久化和复制配置

optionExplanations: 先读一次再写回，中间有个窗口——两个请求都可能读到同一个旧值，各自加一后还是撞车。
对：这条命令把「取值」和「加一」压成一步，不给任何请求留下能插进来的窗口。
这条命令给 key 设一个存活时间，跟生成下一个序号完全是两件事。
这条命令是发布消息到频道，不会返回或递增任何序号。
optionExplanations_en: GET then SET is a two-step read-modify-write; under concurrency two requests can read the same old value and each add one, colliding.
Right: INCR atomically increments and returns the new value for a single Redis key, sidestepping the GET+SET race entirely.
This command puts a lapse timer on the key — a completely different concern from generating the next sequence number.
This command publishes a message to a channel; it doesn't return or increment any sequence number.

q: 生产系统实践中通常怎样组合可靠投递的三种机制？
q_en: How do production systems typically combine the three reliable-delivery mechanisms?
options: 只用轮询，简单可靠
认为只用心跳就能覆盖连接和消息两类故障
三者互补：心跳测连接，序号测漏消息，轮询兜底
只用序号，其余多余
options_en: Use polling alone, it is simple and reliable
Assumes a heartbeat alone covers both connection and message failures
The three complement each other: heartbeats catch dead sockets, sequence numbers catch drops, polling backstops
Use sequence numbers alone, the rest is redundant
why: 三种机制对应三类故障：连接死了靠心跳、消息漏了靠序号、以上都失灵还有轮询。关键盲区：序号只有「后面还有下一条」才暴露缺口，若最后一条丢了、又没有新消息，序号和心跳都发现不了——轮询定时主动问一遍 Inbox 兜住它。
why_en: Three mechanisms cover three failure modes: heartbeat for dead connections, sequence numbers for lost messages, polling as the last resort. Key blind spot: a sequence gap only shows when a later message arrives, so if the last message is lost and none follows, neither sequence nor heartbeat notices — periodic polling of the Inbox catches it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条消息带的单调递增编号，客户端靠比对编号发现是否漏收。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sequence number is a monotonically increasing id on each message that lets a client spot gaps by comparing numbers.

termDefinitions.meaning: 基于 TCP 的全双工长连接协议，一次握手后客户端与服务器可以随时双向收发消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A WebSocket is a persistent, full-duplex connection over TCP that lets client and server send messages to each other at any time after one handshake.

termDefinitions.meaning: 客户端不等服务器推，而是自己按固定间隔(如每 30s)主动去问服务器「有没有我没收到的消息」，服务器翻 Inbox 把未 ack 的行补推。是 pull 模型，与 push(服务器有事主动推)相对。可靠但贵又慢，所以在此当兜底而非主力。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Polling: instead of waiting for a server push, the client asks the server on a fixed interval (e.g. every 30s) "any messages I have not received?", and the server re-pushes un-acked Inbox rows. It is a pull model, opposite of push. Reliable but expensive and slow, so used here as a fallback, not the primary path.

termDefinitions.meaning: push=服务器一有事件就主动发给客户端(实时、省无谓请求，靠长连接)；pull/轮询=客户端定时主动来问(实现简单、不依赖连接状态，但有延迟且请求量大)。可靠投递里 push 做主力、pull 做兜底。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Push = the server sends to the client the moment an event happens (real-time, no wasted requests, needs a persistent connection). Pull/polling = the client asks on a timer (simple, connection-agnostic, but adds latency and heavy request volume). For reliable delivery, push is primary and pull is the fallback.

optionExplanations: 只用轮询意味着安静期和活跃期都靠固定间隔查询，死连接发现慢，还浪费大量无效请求。
只靠心跳能测连接死活，但测不出消息本身是否漏投，覆盖不了投递层的故障。
对：三者互补——心跳测连接是否还活着，序号测消息有没有漏，轮询兜底覆盖前两者都可能错过的场景。
只用序号能测出消息缺口，但测不出连接本身什么时候已经死了，覆盖不了连接层故障。
optionExplanations_en: Relying only on polling means every discovery, quiet or busy, waits for a fixed interval — slow detection and a lot of wasted requests.
A heartbeat alone tells you if the connection is alive, but not whether a message itself went missing — it doesn't cover delivery failures.
Right: the three complement each other — heartbeat checks the connection is alive, sequence numbers catch missed messages, and polling backstops whatever the other two might miss.
Sequence numbers alone catch message gaps but can't tell you when the connection itself died — they don't cover connection-layer failures.

scenario: 分布式系统里消息乱序不可避免；聊天用户更在乎「新消息尽快出现」而不是严格的全局顺序。
scenario_en: Out-of-order messages are unavoidable in a distributed system; chat users care more about seeing new messages fast than about strict global ordering.
q: 对乱序消息，文中的态度是？
q_en: What is the article's stance on out-of-order messages?
options: 不做严格重排，直接按服务器时间戳展示
用向量时钟实现全序广播
所有消息经单一队列串行化
统一延迟 5 秒再排序显示
options_en: Do not strictly reorder; just display by the server-received timestamp
Use vector clocks for total-order broadcast
Serialize every message through a single queue
Uniformly delay display by 5 seconds to let reordering happen
why: 严格保序要付出延迟与重排机制的复杂度，而聊天用户宁要快不要序——产品需求决定了不值得做。
why_en: The design deliberately does not enforce strict ordering because chat users prefer seeing new messages fast over guaranteed order.
whenOtherWins: 必须按事件时间严格处理的流计算才值得等迟到数据——如 Flink 的有界乱序水位线策略，先等待再处理。
tradeoff: 展示速度优先 vs 严格全局顺序需要的等待与重排复杂度

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台服务器把时钟对齐到同一参考时间的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes server clocks to a shared reference time.

optionExplanations: 对：不做严格重排、直接按服务器时间戳展示，用户要的是「新消息尽快出现」，不是绝对全局顺序。
向量时钟能给出因果序，但实现和判断成本远超聊天场景需要的收益。
单一队列串行化会把并发写入压成一条主路径，牺牲的吞吐和延迟都不划算。
统一延迟几秒排序是拿实时性换正确顺序，跟「用户更在乎新消息尽快出现」的前提正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: Right: skip strict reordering and show by server-received timestamp — users want new messages fast, not a strict global order.
Vector clocks give causal ordering, but the implementation and reasoning cost far outweighs what a chat app needs.
Funneling every write through a single serial queue crushes concurrency, trading away throughput and latency for little gain.
Delaying everything by seconds to sort trades real-time delivery for strict ordering — the opposite of what "users want new messages fast" implies.

scenario: 所有 Chat Server 需要给消息一个统一、可复现的展示顺序，即使到达顺序不同。
scenario_en: Every Chat Server needs to give messages one consistent, reproducible display order, even when they arrive in a different order.
q: 补全消息排序的实际做法：
q_en: Fill in the actual approach to message ordering:
text: 所有 Chat Server 经 {{NTP}} 同步时钟；消息到达时盖上{{服务器接收}}时间戳，客户端一律按此时间戳排序展示，从而让所有客户端看到{{一致}}的顺序。
why: NTP 把各 Chat Server 的钟拉齐到几毫秒内，「服务器接收时间」才成为跨服务器可比的全局排序键。不信客户端时间(可能错/被改)。排序键要用 (server_ts, server_id, message_id) 这种全序且确定的组合，相同戳也能被所有客户端排出逐字节相同的顺序——这才是「可复现」。NTP 够好但不完美，残留偏差导致偶发 pop-in(卡074)。
why_en: NTP aligns all Chat Server clocks to within a few ms, so "server-received time" becomes a cross-server-comparable global sort key. Client time is not trusted (may be wrong/spoofed). The sort key must be a total, deterministic tuple like (server_ts, server_id, message_id) so even equal timestamps order identically on every client — that is what makes it reproducible. NTP is good-enough but imperfect; residual skew causes occasional pop-in (card 074).

termDefinitions.meaning: 让一堆机器的时钟通过网络对齐到同一参考时间的协议(源头是原子钟/GPS，经 stratum 分层下发，还会扣掉网络往返延迟)。作用:把各 Chat Server 的钟拉齐到几毫秒内，使「服务器接收时间」成为跨服务器可比的排序键。它够好但不完美——残留几 ms~几十 ms 偏差，所以排序偶有 pop-in。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP (Network Time Protocol) synchronizes machine clocks over a network to a common reference (rooted at atomic/GPS clocks, distributed through strata, accounting for round-trip delay). Here it aligns Chat Server clocks to within a few ms so "server-received time" is a cross-server-comparable sort key. Good-enough but imperfect — residual ms-to-tens-of-ms skew causes occasional pop-in.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个「对任意两条消息都能分出先后、且在所有客户端上判定完全一致」的排序键。单用 server_ts 不够(可能相等)，要补确定性 tie-breaker：(server_ts, server_id, message_id)。这样相同时间戳也被所有端排出逐字节相同的顺序 = 可复现。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A total-order sort key can order any two messages and does so identically on all clients. server_ts alone is insufficient (values can tie); add a deterministic tie-breaker: (server_ts, server_id, message_id). Then even equal timestamps sort byte-identically everywhere = reproducible.

codeSample:
# —— 服务器端：收到即盖戳 ——
def on_message_received(msg, sender):
    msg.server_ts = now()       # NTP 同步过的本机时钟；各 server 差几 ms 内
    msg.server_id = SERVER_ID   # 平局时的 tie-breaker
    persist(msg)                # 写 Message 表，server_ts 当排序键
    fan_out(msg)                # 推给各接收者（到达顺序不保证）

# —— 客户端：展示时一律按戳排序 ——
def render(inbox):
    # 关键：排序键要"全序且确定"，所有客户端才排出完全相同的顺序
    msgs = sorted(inbox.all(),
                  key=lambda m: (m.server_ts, m.server_id, m.message_id))
    display(msgs)               # 新消息可能插到已显示消息上方 = pop-in（卡074）

q: 按服务器接收时间排序的可见副作用是什么？
q_en: What is the visible side effect of ordering messages by server-received time?
options: 部分消息会永久丢失
偶尔消息会插到发送更晚的消息上方，用户能接受
时钟漂移会让消息重复
认为客户端必须缓存全部历史消息才能排序
options_en: Some messages are permanently lost
Occasionally a message pops in above one sent later, and users find it acceptable
Clock drift causes duplicate messages
Claims the client must cache the entire message history just to sort it
why: 接收时间 ≠ 发送时间，偶发的 pop-in 在所难免；但这是拿微小的视觉瑕疵换实时性，用户买账。
why_en: Occasionally a message pops in above one that was actually sent later, and users find that acceptable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让多台服务器把时钟对齐到同一参考时间的协议。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: NTP synchronizes server clocks to a shared reference time.

optionExplanations: 消息本体仍然完整保存并展示，不会因为排序键选择而永久丢失。
对：排序键换成了服务器视角而不是发送方视角，两者出现分歧时用户看到的顺序会跳一下，但能接受。
时钟漂移影响的是排序先后，不会凭空复制出重复消息。
按接收时间排序不需要客户端缓存全部历史，跟这个副作用无关。
optionExplanations_en: The message body is still fully stored and displayed — nothing is permanently lost by this choice of sort key.
Right: received time isn't send time, so an occasional pop-in (a later-sent message appearing above an earlier one) is unavoidable but acceptable to users.
Clock drift affects ordering, not message duplication — it doesn't spawn extra copies.
Sorting by received time doesn't require the client to cache full history; that isn't this side effect.

q: 「用户每次发消息 / 收消息 / 回心跳都更新一次 lastSeen 字段」这个 naive 方案的问题？
q_en: What is the problem with the naive design of updating a lastSeen field every time a user sends a message, receives a message, or answers a heartbeat?
options: 读取延迟太高，其实读一条记录很快
巨大写放大：心跳把写入推到百万级/秒，且数据立刻过时
时间戳精度不够，这不是这里的真正问题
会暴露用户隐私 IP，其实字段里没有 IP
options_en: Read latency becomes too high, but reading one record is actually fast
Massive write amplification: heartbeats push writes to millions per second, and the data is stale the instant it lands
Timestamp precision is insufficient, but that is not the real problem here
It leaks user IP addresses, but the field never stores an IP
why: 每个活动都写库，写入量被心跳放大到数百万/秒，换来的却是「查到时已过时」的数据——成本与价值完全倒挂。
why_en: Updating last seen on every action creates millions of low-value writes per second that are stale the moment they land, paying for consistency nobody needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 连接双方按固定间隔互相发送的小探测包，用来确认对方仍然存活。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A heartbeat is a small probe message sent at a fixed interval to confirm the other side of a connection is still alive.

optionExplanations: 读一条记录本身很快，读取延迟不是这个 naive 方案的问题所在。
对：把高频活动直接变成写库操作，量级会被心跳持续放大，而查到的值本来就该是近似值。
时间戳精度足够表达秒级的在线状态变化，精度不是这里的真正问题。
字段里只存时间戳，没有 IP 信息，不存在隐私暴露的问题。
optionExplanations_en: Reading a single row is fast; read latency was never this naive design's problem.
Right: heartbeats push write frequency into the millions per second, and what you get back is already stale by the time you read it — cost and value are completely inverted.
Timestamp precision is more than enough to express second-level online-state changes; precision isn't the real issue.
The field only stores a timestamp, no IP — there's no privacy exposure here.

scenario: 要做「最后在线时间」，希望存储与写入都最小化。两个洞察：用户断连时服务器一定知道；用户在线时他自己能实时告诉你。
scenario_en: You want to build "last seen" while minimizing both storage and writes. Two insights: the server always knows when a user disconnects, and an online user can tell you about it in real time.
q: 文中的设计是？
q_en: What is the article's design?
options: 只在断连时写一条记录，查询时并行读表并经 Pub/Sub 探活，合并显示
每分钟对全体在线用户做快照，负载随在线人数线性增长
客户端之间 P2P 互相询问，对方离线时完全查不到结果，也没权限校验
在负载均衡器上采集日志离线分析，只能查历史查不了当下
options_en: Write one row only on disconnect; on query, read it in parallel with a Pub/Sub probe and merge the results
Snapshot every online user once a minute; load grows linearly with the number of online users
Clients query each other peer-to-peer; when the other side is offline there's no result at all, and it skips permission checks too
Collect logs on the load balancer and analyze offline; can only answer historical queries, never the current state
why: 最小写入方案是断连时写 LastSeen，查询时并行读 LastSeen 并经 Pub/Sub 探活目标 Chat Server。在线就显示 online；没响应才回退 lastDisconnect。
why_en: Write LastSeen only on disconnect, then answer reads by combining that durable row with a live Pub/Sub presence probe; load-balancer logs are analytics, not the presence source of truth.
whenOtherWins: 用户量小或需要完整在线历史审计时，按活动直接写库更简单、信息也更全。
tradeoff: 存储与写入最小化 vs 在线状态的实时精确性
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant A as Querying client
    participant API as Chat API
    participant LS as LastSeen table
    participant PS as Pub/Sub
    participant CS as Target Chat Server
    A->>API: getLastSeen(targetUserId)
    par historical fallback
      API->>LS: read lastDisconnect(targetUserId)
      LS-->>API: 10:32:05
    and live presence probe
      API->>PS: ask user:target are you online?
      PS->>CS: presence probe
      CS-->>API: online if connection exists
    end
    API-->>A: online OR last seen at 10:32:05
codeSample:
onDisconnect(userId):
  LastSeen.conditionalUpdate(
    key=userId,
    set={ "lastDisconnect": now() },
    condition="new timestamp is newer"
  )

getLastSeen(viewerId, targetUserId):
  historical = LastSeen.get(targetUserId)  # durable fallback
  live = pubsub.request(
    channel=f"user:{targetUserId}",
    message={ "type": "presenceProbe" },
    timeout_ms=150
  )

  if live == "ONLINE":
    return { "status": "online" }
  return { "status": "offline", "lastSeen": historical.lastDisconnect }

# Load-balancer logs may show that a socket/request existed earlier,
# but they are analytics/debug data, not the source of truth for presence.

rows: 历史断连时间+此刻在线

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用户此刻是否在线、在哪台 Chat Server 持有连接的状态。它是实时状态，不适合只靠离线日志回答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Presence is the realtime state of whether a user is online and which Chat Server owns their connection. It should not be answered only from offline logs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 userId 存最近断连时间的持久化表。它回答“最后一次离线是什么时候”，不直接证明“现在在线”。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The LastSeen table stores the latest disconnect time by userId. It answers when the user last went offline, not directly whether the user is online right now.

termDefinitions.meaning: LB 记录的连接或请求事件日志，适合审计、排障、流量分析；即使进入近实时分析系统，也不是聊天 presence 的权威读路径。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Load-balancer logs are connection or request event logs used for audit, debugging, and traffic analysis. Even if streamed into a near-real-time analytics system, they are not the authoritative read path for chat presence.

termDefinitions.meaning: 日志在几秒到几分钟内进入分析系统并可查询；它比离线批处理快，但仍不是毫秒级产品状态查询。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Near-real-time analytics means logs become queryable within seconds to minutes. It is faster than offline batch, but still not a millisecond-level product-state query.

optionExplanations: 对：只有断开这一个事件才落一次库，查的时候另开一路去问对方现在还在不在，两路结果合并展示。
按分钟给全体在线用户做快照，写入量直接跟在线人数挂钩，跟「最小写入」的目标相反。
对方离线时 P2P 完全查不到结果，也没有服务端权限控制这层保护，不满足查询需求。
负载均衡器日志适合事后趋势分析，但答不出「此刻在不在线」这种实时问题。
optionExplanations_en: Right: write LastSeen only on disconnect, then on query read it in parallel with a Pub/Sub probe and merge — minimal writes while covering both history and live state.
Snapshotting every online user each minute ties write volume directly to online headcount, the opposite of minimizing writes.
Peer-to-peer questioning returns nothing when the other side is offline, and it also bypasses server-side permission control.
Load-balancer log analysis is fine for after-the-fact trends but can't answer "is this person online right now."

q: 两台服务器可能先后为同一用户写断连时间戳，如何防止旧值覆盖更新的值？
q_en: Two servers might write a disconnect timestamp for the same user out of order — how do you stop a stale value from overwriting a newer one?
options: 写之前抢一把全局锁
随机退避后再写
只允许固定一台服务器负责写这个字段，其余全部转发
DynamoDB 条件写：新时间戳更大才更新
options_en: Grab a global lock before writing
Write after a random backoff delay
Only ever let one fixed server write this field and forward everything else to it
A DynamoDB conditional write that only updates when the new timestamp is greater
why: 条件写把「比较再更新」压进存储层原子完成：晚到的旧时间戳会条件失败，不会倒退覆盖更近的断连时间。
why_en: A DynamoDB conditional write that only updates when the new timestamp is greater prevents two servers from racing and clobbering a more recent disconnect time.
codeSample:
UpdateItem LastSeen
  Key: { userId: "u_42" }
  SET lastDisconnect = :new
  ConditionExpression: :new > lastDisconnect
# fails harmlessly if another server already wrote a newer timestamp

termDefinitions.meaning: AWS 提供的托管 NoSQL 键值/文档数据库，按分区键把数据水平分布到多个节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL key-value database that distributes data across nodes by partition key.

termDefinitions.meaning: 只有满足指定条件（如新值大于旧值）才提交的写操作，由存储层原子完成「比较并更新」。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A conditional write only commits when a stated condition holds, letting the store atomically compare and update in one step.

optionExplanations: 全局锁会把所有断连写入串行化，代价太大，也不是这里给出的方案。
随机退避降低碰撞概率，但不能保证旧值绝不覆盖新值，只是概率性缓解。
固定一台服务器负责写不现实——用户可能连在任意一台 Chat Server 上断开。
对：DynamoDB 条件写让「只有新时间戳更大才更新」在存储层原子完成，晚到的旧值会条件失败。
optionExplanations_en: A global lock would serialize every disconnect write — too costly, and not the mechanism actually used here.
Random backoff lowers the chance of a collision but doesn't guarantee an old value can never overwrite a newer one — only a probabilistic mitigation.
Pinning writes to one fixed server isn't realistic — a user can disconnect from whichever Chat Server they happened to be on.
Right: a DynamoDB conditional write makes "update only if the new timestamp is larger" atomic at the storage layer, so a late, stale write simply fails the condition.

q: 客户端查询他人 last seen 的完整流程是？
q_en: What is the full flow when a client queries someone else's last seen?
options: 直接读 LastSeen 表并原样返回，不会去问对方当前是否真的在线
服务器并行读 LastSeen 表，同时经 Pub/Sub 探活，合并结果显示
向全部 Chat Server 广播查询再投票，开销随集群规模线性增长
轮询目标用户直到回应，请求持续阻塞等待，没有并行的历史兜底路径
options_en: Read the LastSeen table directly and return it as-is, without asking whether they are actually online right now
The server reads the LastSeen table and probes via Pub/Sub in parallel, then merges the results
Broadcast the query to every Chat Server and vote, with cost scaling linearly with cluster size
Poll the target user until it responds; the request blocks the whole time with no parallel historical fallback
why: 一次查询、两路并行响应（数据库的历史值 + 实时的在线确认），由客户端合并——存储与实时各答各的强项。
why_en: The server checks the last-seen table and in parallel forwards the query to the target's channel, and the client merges the database answer with any live online reply.
diagram:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as 请求者客户端
    participant A as Chat Server A
    participant DB as LastSeen 表
    participant B as Chat Server B（目标所在）
    C->>A: getLastSeen(target)
    par 并行
        A->>DB: 读最后断连时间
        A-->>C: updateLastSeen($DATE)
    and
        A->>B: 经 Pub/Sub 转发 getLastSeen
        B-->>C: updateLastSeen(ONLINE)（若在线）
    end
    C->>C: 合并：ONLINE 则绿点，否则显示断连时间

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

optionExplanations: 直接读表返回历史值，不会去确认对方此刻是否真的在线，查询不完整。
对：服务器并行读 LastSeen 表和经 Pub/Sub 问对方是否在线，两路结果由服务器合并后返回。
向全部 Chat Server 广播投票的开销随集群规模线性增长，不是这里选用的路径。
轮询直到回应会让请求一直阻塞等待，没有并行的历史兜底路径，体验也差。
optionExplanations_en: Reading the table alone and returning the stored value never confirms whether the person is actually online right now — an incomplete query.
Right: the server reads the LastSeen table and probes via Pub/Sub in parallel, then merges the two results before responding.
Broadcasting a vote to every Chat Server scales cost with cluster size — not the path used here.
Polling until a response blocks the request with no parallel historical fallback, and it's a poor experience besides.

scenario: WhatsApp 要显示联系人是否在线或最后在线时间。为少写库，方案只在用户断连时写 LastSeen 表；查询时并行读表并经 Pub/Sub 问对方是否在线。
scenario_en: WhatsApp needs to show whether a contact is online or their last-seen time. To minimize writes, the design writes the LastSeen table only on disconnect, and a query reads that table while asking over Pub/Sub in parallel whether the target is online.
q: 这个 last-disconnect 方案还剩哪些风险和补强？（多选）
q_en: What risks and mitigations remain for this last-disconnect design? (select all)
options: 两路响应可能先后到达，客户端要能等待或平滑更新 UI
Chat Server 崩溃时可能来不及写断连时间
补强：连接建立时也写一次 LastSeen 表
必须每秒刷新所有用户的 last seen
options_en: The two responses may arrive apart, so the client must wait or update the UI smoothly.
A Chat Server crash may happen before it writes the disconnect time.
Mitigation: also write the LastSeen row when a connection is established.
Every user's last seen must be refreshed every second.
why: 这个方案用少量写入换取近似在线状态，所以剩余风险在合并两路响应和断连上报可靠性。连接时也写一次 LastSeen 是低成本加固；每秒全量刷新会把写入量打爆。
why_en: The design saves writes, but the client must merge two responses and the server may miss a disconnect, so writing on connect adds a cheap safety net.
tradeoff: 最小写入量 vs 在线状态鲁棒性

termDefinitions.meaning: 只记录用户最近一次断开连接的时间，用它近似表示最后在线时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Last-disconnect means storing only the most recent time a user disconnected, as an approximation of last seen.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按 userId 存最近断连或连接时间的表，用来回答最后在线时间。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A LastSeen table stores each user's latest connection-related timestamp for last-seen queries.

termDefinitions.meaning: 维护用户长连接、转发实时消息并上报连接事件的服务节点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Chat Server holds user connections, forwards realtime messages, and reports connection events.

termDefinitions.meaning: 发布-订阅消息模式：发布者把消息发到一个频道，所有订阅该频道的连接都会收到；Redis 的实现不持久化消息，无人订阅就丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pub/Sub is publish-subscribe messaging where a publisher sends to a channel and every current subscriber receives it; Redis does not persist these messages, so one with no subscriber is simply lost.

optionExplanations: 两路响应到达有先后，客户端要能等待或平滑更新 UI，否则会闪烁或短暂显示错误状态。
Chat Server 崩溃时可能来不及写断连时间戳，这条时间就会停留在更早的值上。
连接建立时也写一次 LastSeen，是用极小的额外写入换取断连上报失败时的兜底。
每秒全量刷新所有用户会把写入量打爆，跟这个方案「最小写入」的目标正好相反。
optionExplanations_en: The two responses can arrive at different times, so the client needs to wait or update smoothly, or the UI flickers or briefly shows the wrong state.
If Chat Server crashes, it may not get to write the disconnect timestamp in time, leaving that value stuck on an earlier one.
Also writing LastSeen on connect trades a tiny extra write for a safety net when the disconnect report itself fails to land.
Refreshing every user's status every second would explode write volume, the opposite of this design's minimal-write goal.

scenario: 面试官按候选人级别（中级 / 高级 / Staff+）调整对广度与深度的期望比例。
scenario_en: Interviewers adjust their breadth-versus-depth expectations by candidate level (mid-level, senior, staff-plus).
q: 补全各级别期望的广度 : 深度比例：
q_en: Fill in the expected breadth-to-depth ratio at each level:
text: 面试期望的广度 : 深度——中级约 {{80}}:20、高级约 60:{{40}}、Staff+ 约 40:{{60}}；级别越高，越要主动识别问题并引领 deep dive，而不是等面试官来驱动。
why: 中级重广度、把功能跑通即可；高级要讲透伸缩与鲁棒性、比较分区策略的利弊；Staff+ 要 2-3 层深入故障模式、瓶颈甚至区域化架构。
why_en: Expectations shift from eighty-twenty breadth versus depth at mid-level, to sixty-forty at senior, to forty-sixty at staff-plus where you proactively lead the deep dives.

q: Yelp 题的产品核心最准确地说是什么？
q_en: What is the core product being designed in the Yelp problem?
options: 本地商家搜索、浏览和评论平台
在线视频上传和播放平台
实时拼车调度系统
面向商家的广告竞价系统
options_en: A local business search, browsing, and review platform.
An online video upload and playback platform.
A real-time ride-hailing dispatch system.
A business-facing ad auction system.
why: 本题围绕本地商家发现和评论：用户搜索商家、查看商家和评论、留下评分和文字评论。广告、推荐和地图展示都不是主线。
why_en: The Yelp design centers on local business search, business detail viewing, and user reviews, not ads or recommendations.
optionExplanations: 本题从头到尾都在设计本地商家的搜索、浏览和评论闭环，这是唯一贴合的产品框架。
视频上传播放是 YouTube 类系统的核心机制，Yelp 不做内容托管。
拼车调度关心实时匹配和路径规划，和商家点评是两个完全不同的问题域。
广告竞价是变现功能，属于产品的另一层，不是这道题要设计的核心。
optionExplanations_en: The whole problem is scoping search, browsing, and reviews for local businesses — that's the only fit.
Video upload and playback defines a YouTube-style system, not what Yelp is designing.
Ride dispatch is about real-time matching and routing, a different problem domain from business reviews.
Ad auctions are a monetization feature layered on top, not the core product this problem asks for.

scenario: 面试官已经把 Yelp 定义为本地商家搜索与评论平台，要求你先划定 MVP 范围内的核心功能。
scenario_en: The interviewer defines Yelp as a local business search and review platform, and asks you to scope the MVP features first.
q: Yelp 本地商家点评网站的核心功能需求有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which core functional requirements belong in the MVP for a local business review site?
options: 为用户生成个性化推荐流
查看商家详情和评论
给商家留下 1-5 星评分和可选文字评论
按名称、经纬度位置和类别搜索商家
options_en: Generate a personalized recommendation feed for each user.
View business details and their reviews.
Leave a 1-5 star rating with optional text review.
Search businesses by name, lat/long location, and category.
why: 核心功能是商家搜索、详情+评论查看、写评论三件事；个性化推荐和地图展示属于范围外。
why_en: The core functions are searching businesses, viewing details with reviews, and creating reviews — not personalized recommendations.
optionExplanations: 个性化推荐要建用户行为模型和排序系统，超出了这版 MVP 划的搜索评论范围。
详情页要展示商家基本信息和已有评论，用户决定要不要去之前必须先看到它们。
1-5 星加可选文字是评论的最小闭环，也是后面维护平均分要用的数据源。
搜索要同时支持名称、位置和类别过滤，用户才能真正找到附近想去的商家。
optionExplanations_en: A personalized feed needs behavior modeling and ranking — well outside this MVP's search-and-review scope.
The detail page must show business info and existing reviews, which users need before deciding to visit.
A 1-5 star rating with optional text is the minimal review loop and feeds the rating aggregate later.
Search needs name, location, and category filters together so users can find nearby businesses.

q: Yelp 题的核心非功能需求包括哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which nonfunctional requirements matter most for the Yelp design?
options: 搜索延迟低于约 500ms
所有评论写入必须跨区域强一致同步
扩展到 100M 日活用户和 10M 商家
高可用，接受最终一致
options_en: Search latency under about 500 milliseconds.
All review writes must be strongly consistent across regions.
Scale to 100M daily active users and 10M businesses.
High availability, with eventual consistency accepted.
why: 核心是低延迟搜索、高可用和百万级规模；评论和搜索结果可接受最终一致，不要求跨区域强一致同步。
why_en: The key nonfunctional requirements are sub-500ms search, high availability with eventual consistency, and scale to 100M users and 10M businesses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入后短时间内副本可能不一致，但停止写入后会收敛到相同状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eventual consistency means replicas may briefly disagree after a write but converge once writes stop.

optionExplanations: 搜索延迟压在 500ms 内，是读路径设计必须达到的硬指标。
跨区域强一致同步会拖慢每次评论写入，评论数据完全不需要这么重的一致性。
百万级日活和千万商家规模，决定了后面要不要分片、要不要上专用搜索引擎。
高可用配最终一致：短暂读到旧评分能接受，但服务不能说挂就挂。
optionExplanations_en: Keeping search under about 500ms is the hard latency target the read path must meet.
Cross-region strong sync would slow every review write; review data doesn't need that heavy a guarantee.
100M daily users and 10M businesses are the scale numbers that drive sharding and search-engine decisions.
High availability with eventual consistency: a briefly stale rating is fine, but the service can't go down.

q: Yelp 题里，用来防止刷分和竞对恶意差评的核心业务约束是什么？
q_en: What business rule prevents rating spam and malicious competitor reviews in Yelp?
options: 每个商家最多只能有十条评论
每个用户对每个商家只能留一条评论
每个搜索请求必须返回全量商家
每个城市只能有一个类别
options_en: Each business may have at most ten reviews.
Each user may leave only one review per business.
Every search request must return the full business set.
Each city may only have one category.
why: 一人一商家一评是后续数据库约束深挖的基础，用来防止同一用户刷分或竞品恶意刷差评。
why_en: The key constraint is that each user may leave only one review per business, preventing rating manipulation.
optionExplanations: 限制评论总数堵不住刷分，恶意用户换个商家或账号照样能刷。
一人一商家一评从根上堵住了同账号反复刷分或竞对刷差评的漏洞。
强制返回全量商家跟防刷分无关，只会让搜索接口又慢又没用。
每城市限一个类别是荒谬的产品限制，和评论真实性毫不相干。
optionExplanations_en: Capping total reviews doesn't stop spam — the same bad actor can still hit a different business or account.
Limiting each account to a single review on a business closes the loophole for self-boosting or competitor spam.
Forcing every search to return the full business set has nothing to do with spam, just slower search.
One category per city is an absurd product rule with no connection to review authenticity.

q: 满足核心需求需要哪些核心实体？（多选）
q_en: Which core entities are needed for the main Yelp requirements?
options: Business
User
VideoSegment
Review
options_en: Business — the listed venue entity.
User — the person searching and reviewing.
VideoSegment — a video-platform entity, not part of Yelp.
Review — a rating and optional text tied to a user and business.
why: Business 存商家信息，User 是搜索/写评论的人，Review 连接两者并带评分与文字；VideoSegment 属于视频类系统，不在 Yelp 域内。
why_en: The core entities are Business, User, and Review; VideoSegment belongs to a video platform, not Yelp.
optionExplanations: Business 存商家名称、地址、类别这类展示必需的信息。
User 是发起搜索和写评论的人，评论必须能追溯到具体用户。
VideoSegment 只在视频类系统里才有意义，Yelp 不托管视频内容。
Review 把 User 和 Business 连起来，带评分和文字，是平均分聚合的数据源。
optionExplanations_en: Business holds the name, address, and category data a listing needs to render.
User is who searches and writes reviews — every review must trace back to a user.
VideoSegment only makes sense in a video platform; Yelp never hosts video content.
Review links User and Business with a rating and text, feeding the rating aggregate.

q: 补全 Yelp 核心 API 的形状：
q_en: Fill in the shape of the core Yelp APIs.
text: 搜索商家：{{GET /businesses?query&location&category&page}}；查看详情：{{GET /businesses/:businessId}}；写评论：{{POST /businesses/:businessId/reviews}}。
why: API 基本按功能需求一一映射。搜索需要分页，详情和评论可以合并或拆开，取决于评论分页需求。
why_en: The APIs map directly to search, business detail retrieval, and review creation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大结果集拆成多页返回，每次只传输一小部分数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pagination splits a large result set into pages so each request transfers only a small slice.

q: 为什么搜索接口需要 page 参数或其他分页机制？
q_en: Why does the business search API need a page parameter or another pagination mechanism?
options: 让写评论变成异步任务
保证每个商家只能有一条评论
避免单次返回结果集过大，拖慢响应
替代全文索引
options_en: Turn review writing into an async task.
Guarantee each business has only one review.
Avoid returning a huge result set at once, cutting payload size and latency.
Replace full-text indexing.
why: 搜索结果可能很大，分页可以限制单次 payload，提升响应速度和客户端体验。分页不是索引替代品，只是结果传输控制。
why_en: Pagination keeps search responses small and responsive when the result set may be large.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大结果集拆成多页返回，每次只传输一小部分数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pagination splits a large result set into pages so each request transfers only a small slice.

optionExplanations: 分页控制的是搜索结果传输量，跟评论写入是不是异步没有关系。
一人一评是数据库约束该管的事，分页参数管不了这件事。
分页把每次响应限制在一页大小内，热门搜索结果再大也不会拖垮延迟。
分页只是控制传输量，替代不了检索本身要用的索引结构。
optionExplanations_en: Pagination controls how much search data is transferred, unrelated to whether review writes are async.
One-review-per-user is a database constraint's job — a page parameter can't enforce it.
Pagination caps each response to one page, so even a huge result set won't blow up latency.
Pagination only limits transfer size; it can't replace the indexing that retrieval itself needs.

scenario: 商家详情页可能有成千上万条评论，用户只需要逐页滚动评论列表。
scenario_en: A business detail page may have thousands of reviews, and users only need to scroll the review list page by page.
q: 详情和评论 API 更合适怎样拆分？
q_en: How should the business detail and review APIs be split?
options: 写评论时顺便返回全站所有评论
只提供一个不分页的大接口
把所有评论嵌入搜索结果里
拆成两个 GET 接口，评论单独分页
options_en: Return all site-wide reviews whenever someone posts a review.
Provide one endpoint with no pagination at all.
Embed every review inside the search results.
Split into two GET endpoints: business detail, and a paginated review list.
tradeoff: 接口拆分带来的独立缓存与分页能力 vs 单接口的简单性
why: 拆分后商家详情可以快速返回，评论独立分页加载；评论量很少时也可以合并成一个接口。
why_en: Separating business details from paginated reviews keeps the detail endpoint fast while allowing large review lists to load incrementally.
whenOtherWins: 如果每个商家评论数量很少且页面总是一起展示，一个聚合详情接口更简单。

termDefinitions.meaning: 把大结果集拆成多页返回，每次只传输一小部分数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pagination splits a large result set into pages so each request transfers only a small slice.

optionExplanations: 写评论时顺带吐出全站评论完全跑题，跟拆分详情/评论接口没关系。
不分页的大接口在商家评论上千条时会让详情页一次性变得很重。
把评论塞进搜索结果会让搜索响应体膨胀，拖慢本该轻量的搜索路径。
读模式不同的两块拆开后，各自都能独立缓存和扩容，不必绑在一个响应里。
optionExplanations_en: Returning every review site-wide on a write is off-topic and doesn't address splitting the endpoints.
A single unpaginated endpoint gets heavy fast once a business has thousands of reviews.
Embedding reviews in search results bloats the search response and slows the path that should stay light.
Splitting two different read patterns lets each cache and scale independently instead of sharing one response.

q: 把基础商家搜索请求路径排成正确顺序。
q_en: Put the basic business search request path in the right order.
steps: Business Service 根据 query/location/category 查询商家数据
客户端发起 GET /businesses 请求
结果经 API Gateway 返回客户端
API Gateway 将请求路由到 Business Service
why: 基础路径是客户端到网关，网关到业务服务，业务服务查存储并返回。深挖前先有一条能工作的读路径。
why_en: The basic search path is client to API Gateway, then Business Service, then storage, and back to the client.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  A[Client] --> B[API Gateway]
  B --> C[Business Service]
  C --> D[(Business DB/Search Index)]
  D --> C
  C --> B
  B --> A

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求并路由到具体后端服务的统一入口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API Gateway is the single entry point that routes client requests to the right backend service.

q: 基础高层设计中的主要组件有哪些？（多选）
q_en: Which components belong in the basic high-level Yelp design?
options: Client
API Gateway
Business Service
Video Transcoder
Database
options_en: Client — the web or mobile app.
API Gateway — routes requests to services.
Business Service — handles search and business reads.
Video Transcoder — a video-platform component, not part of Yelp.
Database — stores business and review data.
why: 基础读路径由客户端、网关、Business Service 和数据库组成；Video Transcoder 属于视频类系统。
why_en: The simple Yelp architecture uses a client, API Gateway, Business Service, and database.

termDefinitions.meaning: 接收客户端请求并路由到具体后端服务的统一入口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API Gateway is the single entry point that routes client requests to the right backend service.

optionExplanations: Client 发起搜索和详情请求，是整条读路径的起点。
API Gateway 统一收请求再路由到具体服务，不用让客户端直连每个服务。
处理搜索和商家详情读取的这块业务逻辑，是整条路径的核心层。
视频转码相关组件只属于视频类系统，Yelp 读路径完全用不上。
Database 持久化商家和评论数据，是整条读路径最终查询的地方。
optionExplanations_en: Client is where search and detail requests originate, the start of the read path.
API Gateway is the single entry point that routes requests, so clients don't call each service directly.
Business Service handles search and detail reads, the core business layer on this path.
Video Transcoder only belongs in a video platform; Yelp's read path has no use for it.
Database persists business and review data — the final place this read path queries.

scenario: 搜索商家和查看商家详情都读取相似的商家数据，读模式接近，且二者强相关。
scenario_en: Business search and business detail pages read similar business data, have similar read patterns, and are tightly related.
q: 这两块逻辑初始应该如何放置？
q_en: Where should search and business-detail logic live at the start?
options: 先放在同一个 Business Service 中
强行拆成两个微服务和两个数据库
全部放进 Review Service
放到客户端直接查数据库
options_en: Start with both inside one Business Service.
Force a split into two microservices with two databases.
Put everything inside the Review Service.
Let the client query the database directly.
tradeoff: 服务内聚的简单性 vs 提前拆分带来的独立扩缩容
why: 功能强相关且读扩展模式类似，先放一个服务能减少复杂度。服务边界应由职责和扩缩容差异驱动，而不是机械拆分。
why_en: Search and business detail reads are closely related and scale similarly, so one Business Service is the simpler starting boundary.
whenOtherWins: 如果详情页产生完全不同的热点、权限或写入路径，拆服务才更有理由。

termDefinitions.meaning: 职责单一、可独立部署和扩展的小型服务。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A microservice is a small, independently deployable service with a single responsibility.

optionExplanations: 读模式和数据都高度重合时，先合在一个 Business Service 里能省掉跨服务调用。
在职责还没分化时硬拆两个服务两个库，只会平白多出运维和一致性成本。
把搜索也塞进 Review Service 会让评论写路径背上不相关的读流量。
客户端直连数据库绕过了业务层的校验和边界，扩展和权限都会失控。
optionExplanations_en: When read patterns and data overlap heavily, one Business Service avoids unnecessary cross-service calls.
Splitting into two services and databases before responsibilities diverge just adds ops and consistency cost.
Cramming search into the Review Service saddles the review write path with unrelated read traffic.
Letting clients query the database directly skips business-layer validation, breaking scaling and access control.

scenario: 用户搜索和浏览很多，但很少写评论；评论创建有独立校验和写路径。
scenario_en: Users search and browse much more often than they write reviews; review creation has its own validation and write path.
q: 为什么引入单独的 Review Service 是合理的？
q_en: Why is a separate Review Service reasonable in this design?
options: 所有微服务都必须一服务一库
评论写入模式与商家读取模式差异大，可以独立演进
搜索必须通过 Review Service 才能低延迟
Review Service 可以替代数据库
options_en: Every microservice must own exactly one database.
Review writes have a very different pattern from business reads and can evolve independently.
Search must go through the Review Service to stay low-latency.
The Review Service can replace the database.
tradeoff: 写路径独立演进 vs 额外服务和数据同步成本
why: 写评论和读商家的流量形态不同，评论还要处理一人一评和评分更新。单独服务让写路径职责更清晰。
why_en: A Review Service is useful because review creation has a very different write-heavy workflow from business search and viewing.
whenOtherWins: 如果产品规模很小，一个服务内模块化就够；如果读写差异不明显，拆服务会增加无谓成本。
diagram:
flowchart LR
Client[Client] --> Biz[Business Service]
Client --> Review[Review Service]
Biz --> BizDB[(Business DB)]
Review --> ReviewDB[(Review DB)]
Review --> Rating[Rating aggregate]
optionExplanations: 一服务一库是常见实践，不是拆 Review Service 的理由，本题看的是流量差异。
评论写入和商家读取的流量形态差很大，拆开后各自能独立扩容和演进。
搜索走的是商家读路径，绕道 Review Service 反而多一跳延迟。
服务是处理请求的进程，替代不了持久化数据的数据库。
optionExplanations_en: One-database-per-service is a common practice, not the reason to split here — the real driver is traffic shape.
Review writes and business reads have very different traffic shapes, so splitting lets each evolve independently.
Search belongs on the business read path; routing it through the Review Service just adds a hop.
A service processes requests; it can't replace a database that persists the data.

scenario: Business 和 Review 紧密关联，详情页经常一起读取；总数据约 1TB 量级，单库或简单复制可承受。
scenario_en: Business and Review are tightly related and often read together; about one terabyte of data can fit in one database with replication.
q: 初始数据库边界更务实的选择是什么？
q_en: What is the pragmatic initial database boundary?
options: 评论正文必须存进 Redis
拆成两个服务各自独占数据库
先共用同一个数据库
商家数据必须存进对象存储
options_en: Review text must be stored in Redis.
Split into two services, each owning its own database.
Start with one shared database for both.
Business data must be stored in object storage.
tradeoff: 共库省 join 的简单性 vs 服务独立数据库带来的故障隔离
why: 两者紧密关联、总量约 1TB，先共库能避免跨服务 join；故障隔离可靠复制等手段先缓解。
why_en: Keeping businesses and reviews in one database is practical because they are tightly coupled and the data volume is manageable.
whenOtherWins: 如果评论写入量巨大、团队所有权强隔离或故障域要求严格，拆库才更值得。

termDefinitions.meaning: 以对象为单位存放非结构化数据的存储服务，如图片和文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Object storage holds unstructured data such as files and images as discrete objects.

optionExplanations: Redis 是内存缓存，不是评论正文这种持久数据该待的地方。
数据量才 1TB 且两表强相关，现在拆库只会换来更多跨库 join 麻烦。
两表经常一起读、总量可控时，先共库能省掉跨服务 join，故障隔离靠复制先顶着。
商家是结构化记录，要按字段查询和更新，对象存储不适合这种访问模式。
optionExplanations_en: Redis is an in-memory cache, not where persistent review text should permanently live.
At only about 1TB with tightly coupled tables, splitting databases now just trades in more cross-database joins.
With tightly coupled tables and manageable volume, one shared database avoids cross-service joins for now.
Business data is structured and needs field-level queries and updates — not what object storage is built for.

scenario: 10M 商家、每家约 100 条评论，每条评论约 1KB，总评论数据量级约为 1TB。
scenario_en: Assume 10M businesses, about 100 reviews per business, and roughly 1KB per review, for about 1TB of review data.
q: 这个数据量级最支持下面哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this data size support?
options: 写入量已经大到必须上消息队列
必须立刻做水平分片
应该把评论正文都放进内存缓存常驻
单库 + 简单复制就能撑住，不必现在做分片
options_en: Write volume is already too high without a message queue.
You must shard horizontally right away.
All review text should live permanently in an in-memory cache.
A single database with simple replication is enough; no need to shard yet.
why: 1TB 级别的数据现代单实例数据库可轻松承载，不需要为规模本身引入分片；故障隔离可靠复制缓解。
why_en: About one terabyte of review data comfortably fits a single modern database instance, so sharding is not yet needed for scale alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把数据水平切分到多个数据库实例，突破单机容量或吞吐上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits data horizontally across multiple database instances to scale beyond one machine's limits.

optionExplanations: 1TB 是存量数据大小，不能直接说明写入速率已经高到要上队列。
单机数据库现在轻松装得下 1TB，光看规模还不到必须马上分片的地步。
把全部评论正文常驻内存缓存既没必要也浪费内存，多数评论很少被重复读。
1TB 量级配上简单复制就能稳稳扛住，分片留到真正的瓶颈出现再做。
optionExplanations_en: 1TB describes stored volume, not write rate — it doesn't by itself justify adding a queue.
A single database instance easily holds 1TB today, so scale alone doesn't force sharding yet.
Permanently caching all review text in memory is wasteful — most reviews are rarely re-read.
About 1TB fits comfortably on one database with simple replication; save sharding for a real bottleneck.

q: 为什么不能在每次搜索时实时 join reviews 并计算平均评分？
q_en: Why should search not join reviews and compute average ratings on every request?
options: 评论越多，join 聚合越慢，拖慢搜索
SQL 不能计算 AVG
平均评分不应该展示在搜索结果里
这样会违反一人一评约束
options_en: Real-time joins get slower as review counts grow, dragging down search reads.
SQL cannot compute AVG.
Average rating should not appear in search results.
This would violate the one-review-per-business rule.
why: 搜索是高频读路径，实时聚合会重复做相同计算，热门商家评论越多越慢；平均评分应预先或增量维护。
why_en: Computing average ratings during every search repeats expensive joins and aggregations on a high-read path.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库中把两张表按条件关联起来的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JOIN combines rows from two database tables based on a related condition.

optionExplanations: 商家评论越多，这条 join+聚合每次都要重新算一遍，热门商家最先被拖垮。
SQL 的 AVG 函数完全能算平均值，问题不在语法能力上。
平均分是搜索结果里很有用的排序/展示信号，不该被藏起来。
实时聚合和一人一评的写入约束是两回事，跟这条规则不冲突。
optionExplanations_en: The more reviews a business has, the more this join-and-aggregate repeats per search, hurting hot ones first.
SQL's AVG function computes averages just fine — the problem isn't syntax capability.
Average rating is a useful signal for ranking and display in search results — it shouldn't be hidden.
Real-time aggregation and the one-review-per-user write rule are unrelated issues.

scenario: 商家详情页需要展示平均评分；候选方案是每次搜索都用下面这段 SQL 现算。
scenario_en: The business detail page needs average ratings, and one proposal computes them with this SQL on every search.
q: 这类实时平均评分 SQL 的主要扩展性问题是什么？
q_en: What is the main scalability problem with this real-time average-rating SQL?
codeSample:
SELECT b.business_id, b.name, AVG(r.rating) AS average_rating
FROM businesses b
JOIN reviews r ON b.business_id = r.business_id
GROUP BY b.business_id;
options: 它无法返回 business_id
每次读都重新 join 和聚合，评论越多越慢
它会自动保证一人一评
它会把数据写入 Elasticsearch
options_en: It cannot return business_id.
Every read repeats the join and aggregation, getting slower as reviews grow.
It automatically enforces one review per user.
It writes data into Elasticsearch.
why: 这段查询适合理解逻辑，不适合高频搜索路径：它把每次搜索都变成一次聚合计算，而不是读一个预计算字段。
why_en: The query is logically simple but makes every search pay for a join and aggregation instead of reading a maintained rating field.

termDefinitions.meaning: 关系型数据库中把两张表按条件关联起来的操作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A JOIN combines rows from two database tables based on a related condition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按某一列的值分组后再做聚合计算（如求平均）的 SQL 子句。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GROUP BY is a SQL clause that groups rows by a column before applying an aggregate like AVG.

optionExplanations: 这条 SQL 明明 SELECT 了 b.business_id，返回不了这个说法不成立。
每次搜索都要重新 JOIN 和 GROUP BY 一遍，评论越堆越多，这条查询就越跑越慢。
这条查询只负责算平均分，跟一人一评的写入约束毫无关系。
这是一条只读的 SELECT，不会往 Elasticsearch 写任何东西。
optionExplanations_en: The query explicitly selects b.business_id, so saying it can't return it doesn't hold up.
Every search re-runs the JOIN and GROUP BY from scratch, so it gets slower as reviews pile up.
This query only computes averages; it has nothing to do with enforcing one review per user.
This is a read-only SELECT — it never writes anything into Elasticsearch.

q: Write-Through 与 Write-Behind 在「写延迟 vs 持久性」上的区别是？
q_en: How do write-through and write-behind differ on write latency versus durability?
options: 写穿透写更快但可能丢数据
两者写延迟和持久性完全一样
同步落库写更慢但更持久，写回更快但可能丢
写回更慢也更持久，写穿透更快
options_en: Write-through is faster but may lose data.
Both have identical write latency and durability.
Write-through is slower but more durable; write-behind is faster but may lose data.
Write-behind is slower and more durable.
tradeoff: 写延迟 vs 数据持久性
why: 写 DB 后删缓存是 cache-aside，不是 write-through。它同步写 DB 和缓存，确认持久化才返回，更慢但更安全；write-behind 先写缓存/队列就返回，异步刷 DB，更快但可能丢更新。
why_en: Strictly, writing the database and deleting the cache is cache-aside invalidation, not write-through. Write-through synchronously writes the database and cache before acknowledging, so it is slower but safer; write-behind acknowledges after a cache or queue write and flushes to the database later, so it is faster but can lose updates if the flush fails or the queue is not durable.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入时同步更新数据库和缓存，通常等数据库持久化、缓存也更新后才返回；不是简单删除缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through synchronously updates the database and cache and usually acknowledges only after the database is durable and the cache is updated; it is not simply deleting the cache.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写入先落到缓存或持久队列并快速返回，再由后台异步写数据库；如果后台写库失败且没有可靠队列、重试或 WAL，可能丢更新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-behind writes to the cache or durable queue first, acknowledges quickly, then flushes to the database asynchronously; if the flush fails without a reliable queue, retry, or WAL, updates can be lost.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用先写数据库，再删除或失效缓存；下一次读 miss 后从数据库回填缓存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cache-aside invalidation writes the database first, then deletes or invalidates the cache so the next cache miss reloads from the database.

optionExplanations: 说反了：write-through 恰恰是等持久化后才返回，慢但安全，不是快但丢数据。
二者正是要在延迟和持久性上分道扬镳，说完全一样就没法回答本题。
write-through 等 DB 落盘才应答，更慢也更保险；另一种模式应答快、落库靠后台补上，快但刷库失败会丢。
再说反一次方向：先返回、后台再落库的是快而有风险的那一种，不是更慢更持久的那一种。
optionExplanations_en: This reverses it — write-through waits for durability before returning, so it's the slower, safer one.
The whole point is that these two diverge on latency versus durability — calling them identical misses it.
Write-through acks only after the DB commits, slower but safer; write-behind acks first and flushes later, faster but riskier.
This flips the direction again — write-behind returns first and persists later, so the risk sits in the async flush.

q: 补全增量更新平均评分所需的字段和公式：
q_en: Fill in the fields and formula needed for incremental average-rating updates.
text: Business 表保存 {{average_rating}} 和 {{num_reviews}}；新评分到来时，新均值 = {{(old_rating * num_reviews + new_rating) / (num_reviews + 1)}}。
why: 维护评论数后，每次新评论只需常数时间更新平均分。这个更新可以和写评论在同一事务或受保护的写路径中完成。
why_en: Keeping average_rating and num_reviews lets each new review update the average in constant time.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每次只根据新数据小幅调整已有聚合结果，而不重新计算整体。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An incremental update adjusts an existing aggregate slightly for each new data point instead of recomputing everything.

q: 两个用户同时基于同一个 num_reviews 和 average_rating 更新评分，可能导致什么问题？
q_en: What can go wrong if two users update the same rating aggregate from the same old state?
options: 评论文本会被压缩成图片
数据库自动转成全文搜索
搜索延迟一定下降
后写覆盖先写，最终少算一条评论
options_en: Review text gets compressed into an image.
The database automatically switches to full-text search.
Search latency is guaranteed to drop.
The later writer overwrites the earlier one, so the final average and count miss a review.
why: 并发读旧状态后分别计算新均值，会产生 lost update。最终状态可能只反映其中一条评论，而不是两条。
why_en: Concurrent average-rating updates can cause a lost update when two writers calculate from the same old state.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个并发写入基于同一旧状态计算，后写覆盖先写导致一次更新丢失。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A lost update happens when two concurrent writers compute from the same old state and one overwrites the other.

optionExplanations: 评论文本变成图片跟并发覆盖评分毫无关系，纯属无关选项。
数据库不会因为并发写入自动切换成全文搜索模式，这不是它的行为。
并发覆盖是正确性问题，不是延迟问题，延迟不会因此确定下降。
两个写入都读到同一份旧状态再各自算新均值，后写盖掉先写，等于丢了一条评论的贡献。
optionExplanations_en: Compressing review text into an image has nothing to do with concurrent rating overwrites.
A database doesn't auto-switch into full-text search mode because of concurrent writes.
Concurrent overwrites are a correctness problem, not a latency one — latency won't drop because of it.
Both writers start from the same old state and compute independently, so the later write erases the earlier one's contribution.

scenario: 写评论时需要同步更新商家的 num_reviews 和 average_rating；同一商家可能同时收到多条评论，但总体写量很小。
scenario_en: When writing a review, the system synchronously updates num_reviews and average_rating; the same business may receive concurrent reviews, but total write volume is small.
q: 避免评分并发丢更新，最合适的方式是什么？
q_en: What is the best way to avoid lost rating updates under concurrency?
options: 乐观锁：更新前校验版本未变，冲突就重试
把所有评分更新放进每天一次的离线任务
允许覆盖，因为最终一致总会自动修复
把平均分存在客户端
options_en: Optimistic locking: verify the version is unchanged before updating, retry on conflict.
Batch all rating updates into a once-a-day offline job.
Allow overwrites since eventual consistency will fix it automatically.
Store the average rating on the client.
tradeoff: 同步更新加重试的简单性 vs 引入队列的额外运维
why: 乐观锁失败时重新读取并重算，可以避免覆盖另一个并发评论。写量很小，因此同步更新加重试比引入队列更简单。
why_en: Optimistic locking detects concurrent changes to the rating row and retries from the latest state.
whenOtherWins: 如果同一商家写入极热、冲突频繁，异步聚合或分片计数器可能更好；本题写量太小，不必复杂化。
diagram:
flowchart LR
Review[New review] --> Tx[DB transaction]
Tx --> Insert[Insert review unique user business]
Tx --> Update[Atomic rating update]
Update --> Commit[Commit]

termDefinitions.meaning: 先记录读到的版本，更新时校验版本未变才写入，否则重试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Optimistic locking checks that a record's version is unchanged before committing an update, retrying otherwise.

termDefinitions.meaning: 记录数据修改次数的字段，乐观锁靠它判断数据是否被并发修改。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A version field tracks how many times a row changed, letting optimistic locking detect concurrent edits.

optionExplanations: 更新前带版本校验，冲突就重读重算再重试，天然避免覆盖别的并发写。
评论量本就很小，攒到每天一次批处理反而让评分长时间不准确。
最终一致解决的是副本间同步延迟，解决不了同一份记录被覆盖丢更新。
平均分是服务端聚合出的共享状态，放在客户端既不同步也不可信。
optionExplanations_en: Checking the version before updating and retrying on conflict naturally avoids overwriting a concurrent write.
Write volume is already tiny; batching into a once-a-day job just leaves ratings stale for hours.
Eventual consistency fixes replica lag, not a lost update where one write overwrites another on the same row.
Average rating is server-computed shared state — storing it client-side makes it unsynced and untrustworthy.

scenario: 评论创建的读写比可达 1000:1，100M 日活用户下评论写入约为每秒 1 次。
scenario_en: Review creation can have a read-write ratio around 1000:1; at 100M daily active users, review writes are about one per second.
q: 这个写入量级最支持哪条设计判断？
q_en: What design judgment does this review-write volume support?
options: 写量已经超过数据库承载能力，必须分片
写量很小，同步更新加乐观锁就够
写量为零，可以完全不做并发控制
写量很大，必须引入消息队列削峰
options_en: Write volume already exceeds what the database can handle, so it must be sharded.
Write volume is tiny — synchronous updates with optimistic locking are enough, no queue needed.
Write volume is zero, so no concurrency control is needed.
Write volume is huge, so a message queue is required to absorb spikes.
why: 读写比约 1000:1，评论写入约 1/s，量级很小；用估算证明同步更新已经够用，是文章强调的 staff 信号。
why_en: With a read-write ratio around one thousand to one, review writes are roughly one per second — small enough that synchronous updates need no queue.
optionExplanations: 每秒 1 次写入连普通单库的零头都用不到，分片在这个量级毫无必要。
1000:1 的读写比换算下来评论写入量很小，同步更新已经够用，不用上队列。
约每秒一次不等于零，只要还有并发写入就仍需要处理丢更新的问题。
这个量级远没有大到需要队列削峰，加队列只是徒增运维复杂度。
optionExplanations_en: About one write per second barely touches a single database's capacity — sharding is unnecessary at this scale.
A roughly 1000-to-1 read-write ratio works out to a tiny write rate, small enough that sync updates need no queue.
About one write per second is not zero — any concurrent writes still risk a lost update without protection.
This volume is nowhere near large enough to need a queue for spikes — adding one just adds needless ops overhead.

scenario: 候选人想在 Review Service 和评分更新之间加消息队列；但估算后评论写入只有约 1/s，数据库可轻松承受。
scenario_en: A candidate wants to add a message queue between Review Service and rating updates, but estimated review writes are only about one per second.
q: 更成熟的取舍是什么？
q_en: What is the more mature tradeoff for rating updates at this write volume?
options: 完全不存平均分
必须引入 Kafka，否则不是高级设计
同步写评论并更新平均分，用乐观锁保护并发
把评论写入浏览器 localStorage
options_en: Don't store the average rating at all.
You must introduce Kafka, or it isn't a sophisticated design.
Write reviews synchronously and update the average rating with optimistic locking.
Write reviews into browser localStorage.
tradeoff: 同步更新的简单性 vs 队列带来的额外一致性和运维成本
